Use ofOtherthanFulland OpenCompetitionis authorizedby 10 U.S.C.2304(c)(1) andFAR

V. DEMONSTRATION THAT THE CONTRACTOR’S UNIQUE
QUALIFICATIONS OR NATURE OF THE ACQUISITION REQUIRES THE USE
OF THE AUTHORITY CITED ABOVE
The authority in paragraph IV above applies because UTC is the Original Equipment
Manufacturer (OEM) with design control, authorization, and documentation to overhaul and
manufacture the Wheel and Brake components. As per the 417 SCMS/GUEA Engineer
Group, each of the weapon systems’ components are considered highly specialized because the
geometry/materials and proprietary process requirements have been specifically designed by
UTCto meet the Government’s requirements. Each of the weapon systems’ wheels, brakes
SourceSelectionInformation–SeeFAR 2.101&3.104
Page3of9
UTCAerospace Systems Wheels and Brakes PBL Effort
and components are designed to allow heat to escape rapidly and in a specific manner to protect
the integrity of surrounding parts (seals, o-rings etc.). If the wrong materials, data, overhaul
processes, and geometry are used, theweapon system could becomeineffectiveand/or
unreliable. It should be noted that a fleet wide retrofit for each of the previously identified
weapon systems’, to include thewheel, brake and components, was awarded to UTCthrough
an Improved Item Replacement Programs(IIRP)or Wheels Brake System Improvement
(WBSI) redesign effort.The redesign effortswereawarded through full and open competition
toUTC. In order to have been selected as the redesignawardee or new OEM supplier, UTC
had to pass a number of critical design reviews and performance specification/parameters --
such as capability, reliability and safety improvements. All associated redesign engineering
and data was independently developed by UTC through its own financial resources.
Therefore, all redesigned wheels, brakes and consumable items are owned by the OEM:UTC.
The parts provided by UTCinclude critical machining, bonding, and post treating processes
which areproprietary andowned by the OEM. In order for the partsto perform properly,
maintain required friction parameters, temperature limits, and to preserve wear life, these
critical processes must be followed. The Government does not have the capability to perform
these processes organically and it has been deemed economically unfeasible(through the IIRP
& WBSI)to reverse engineer the wheels, brakes andcomponents. Since the data required to
properly support the wheels, brakes andcomponents is owned by UTC, interested vendors
would have to be willing to invest the time, funding, and manpower required to reverse
engineer the entire A10, F-16, C-130, C-5 and E-3 weapon systems’ wheel and brake assembly
at their own expense.
In order for another source to be qualified for this acquisition, the qualification process includes,
but is not limited to,the following: 1) Lab analysis which requires a dynamometer capableof
simulating max energy stop conditions,2)Destructive testing to determine max capability, 3)
Validation of proof drawings by the United States Air Force landing gear engineering office,
through collaboration with manufacturersand 4) Qualification testing and on-aircraft testing
which requires allocation of a dedicated test aircraft for the duration of the test. Ultimately,
multiple iterations of each step couldbe required --depending on each outcome. The Air Force
cannot afford to wait for other offerors to qualify new weapon system components without the
weapon system experiencing unacceptable delays,which include but are not limited to Global
multi-service failures (affecting Special Forces, Air Force, Navy, Marines, Coast Guard, and
Foreign Military allies).
As each weapon system plays akey role in the support of the Global War on Terrorismand the
overall mission of the Department of Defense, asset availability is criticalto interrupted logistical
support. Therefore the Air Forceis requesting that this requirement be awarded no later than
MAY 2018.
Accordingly, UTCis the only firm capable of providing the services and supplies described in
Section III above without the government experiencing delays in fulfilling its requirements.

2. Nature and Description of the Action Being Approved (RFO 6.104-1(a)(2)).
The MDA has a requirement for the purchase of four (4)ACU-808-DUP-150 Ton Diesel
Powered Trailer Mounted Commercial Flight Line Air Conditioners (ACU-808),manufactured
by TLD. TheGeneral Services Administration (GSA) has a contract (GS-30F-0030X) with Aero

the ability to orderACU-808units. The MDA utilizes the ACU-808 for
because it is the Air Transportability Test Loading Activity (ATTLA) certified Air Conditioning
Unit (ACU)capable of meeting mission requirements. The ACU-808 holds the required
certification for use which is essential to operational success.
As set forth below, based on market research, no other ACUs of this capacity are currently
known to meet both the ATTLA-certification standards and the MDA’s operational needs and
requirements.Therefore, the MDA is limited to the procurement of the ACU-808.The MDA
intends to fulfil this requirement though placing an order against the GSA Federal Supply
Schedule(FSS).

a) Reverse Engineer of Application Specific design: The U.S. Army Combat
Capabilities DEVCOM-AC Engineering estimates that the time to develop a
competitive technical data package for this item through reverse engineering
would take approximately 12 months. Reverse engineering includes, but is not
limited to, the following: identify all the deficiencies such as
conditions/characteristics that do not meet current approved configuration,
conduct market research on available parts and components, work in conjunction
with the M777A2 155MM Howitzer weapon system integrator to identify the
system’s components and their interrelationships, obtain existing parts, tear
down and understand the design, create representations of the system in another
form or a higher level of abstraction, create the physical representation of that
system and fully define functional parameters, generate Bill of Materials
documentation, build a prototype, and then draft a new TDP which would include
complete component drawings, performance specifications, and qualification
procedures. This could take at least 12 months to include fabrication and testing
of the prototype hardware and releasing a validated TDP.
b) Develop Qualification Procedures/Requirements: Since there are no qualification
procedures in place to determine whether other sources are qualified to meet
Government requirements, it would take an estimated 12 months for the U.S.
Army, DEVCOM-AC Engineers to develop the Government’s requirements
suitable for the prospective contractors to be able to manufacture and qualify
samples. The Engineers would also need to consider testing to the failure point
and beyond, to determine the qualifications that are best suited for the M777A2
155MM Howitzer.
c) Build Prototype Units: In this case, producing the prototype units is the long pole
of the reverse engineering effort, taking considerable effort and time, which is
estimated to be a minimum of 18 months. For the U.S. Army to acquire or build
prototypes, they must first solicit for and get estimates to produce the prototypes.
After accepting and starting work on this effort, the producer must review the
requirements, develop manufacturing processes and routes and plans, produce
3d models for Computer Numerical Control (CNC) programming and measuring,
produce fixturing for the manufacturing and testing processes, procurement of
materials required for production and then manufacture and measure the parts.
In some cases an on-site First Article Test analysis is warranted, which takes
further time to schedule and conduct. Shipping times are also included in the
prototyping effort as well as a full review of the manufacturability of the prototype
to the drawing and quality documents provided by the U.S. Army, DEVCOM-AC
Engineers.
d) Testing/Analysis of Application Specific Design: It would take an additional 8
months to conduct the actual engineering testing/analysis in collaboration
between the Government engineers and weapon system integrator to include the
time for any additional test equipment or fixtures; component, safety and system
level/ higher level assemblies testing or end item systems required to test the
Wheel Assembly, Pneumatic Tire, plus, any additional time for test facilities and

Motorola Hardware and Maintenance VA-26-00048856
JUSTIFICATION FOR AN EXCEPTION TO FAIR OPPORTUNITY
1. Contracting Activity: Department of Veterans Affairs (VA)
Office of Procurement, Acquisition, and Logistics
Technology Acquisition Center
23 Christopher Way
Eatontown, NJ 07724
2. Description of Action: The proposed action is for a Firm-Fixed Price (FFP) Task Order
(TO) that will be issued under the National Aeronautics and Space Administration
(NASA) Solutions for Enterprise-Wide Procurement (SEWP) Contract Number
NNG15SC67B with Cynergy Professional Systems to provide Veterans Affairs Medical
Center (VAMC) Las Vegas with Motorola APX N30 Radios, AXS Dispatch Consoles,
Radio Programming and the installation of the consoles.
3. Description of the Supplies or Services: The proposed action is to provide APX N30
Radios, AXS Dispatch Consoles, Radio Programming and the installation of the
consoles at the VA Southern Nevada Healthcare System, 6900 N. Pecos Road, North
Las Vegas, NV 89086. The Contractor shall also provide all additional equipment,
labor, supervision, and materials required to complete the project along with one year of
maintenance support. Once installation and configuration are complete, two one-hour
training sessions will be conducted on the AXS operation. The total estimated value of
the proposed action is
4. Statutory Authority: The statutory authority permitting an exception to fair opportunity
for this action is 38 U.S.C. 8127(c), known as the Veterans First Contracting Program
which provides the authority to directly contract with a Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned
Small Business (SDVOSB) or a Veteran-Owned Small Business (VOSB). This authority
is pursuant to the exception to the fair opportunity process at Revolutionary FAR
Overhaul VA Deviation 16.507-6(b)(5), which states that “For orders exceeding the
simplified acquisition threshold, a statute expressly authorizes or requires that the
purchase be made from a specified source.”
5. Rationale Supporting Use of Authority Cited Above: The proposed source is Cynergy
Professional Systems, 23187 La Cadena Drive, Laguna Hills, CA 92653. Cynergy
Professional Systems is a Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB)
that is fully authorized and certified to provide Motorola Solutions’ public safety
communications equipment, software, and integration services. As an original
equipment manufacturer (OEM)-authorized reseller with extensive experience
supporting mission-critical Land Mobile Radio and dispatch environments, Cynergy
Professional Systems is uniquely positioned to meet the agency’s requirements
effectively, efficiently, and economically, while ensuring compliance with federal
procurement preferences for SDVOSBs. The requirement includes procurement and
integration of Motorola’s CommandCentral AXS Dispatch Console, which is specifically
engineered to operate within Motorola’s public safety communications ecosystem. The
CommandCentral AXS platform provides capabilities and system-level functionality that
are critical to emergency communications operations and not available through
non-OEM solutions or generic dispatch platforms.
Page 1 of 5
Motorola Hardware and Maintenance VA-26-00048856
The CommandCentral AXS Dispatch Console is the only dispatch platform that provides
full and direct access to the agency’s Motorola mission-critical communications
environment without function loss or the need for unsupported integrations. Dispatchers
require immediate and uninterrupted access to alarms, talkgroup changes, emergency
notifications, and encrypted communications to coordinate timely responses. The AXS
console’s native interoperability ensures these functions are maintained without
additional middleware, increased latency, or loss of features, all of which would impose
unacceptable risks in emergency operations. Interoperability and System Compatibility
Research confirmed that regional public safety communications infrastructure is
predominantly Motorola, including dispatch console configurations, encryption key
management, ISSI/CSSI gateways, and subscriber programming templates. Motorola
CommandCentral AXS is the only dispatch console platform that integrates natively with
the region’s Motorola system core and provides full access to system-level controls and
talkgroup management. Interoperability with surrounding agencies—critical for joint
responses, mutual aid, and daily operational coordination—can only be fully achieved
through Motorola subscriber units and consoles. Performance and Reliability Data Field
operational feedback, system logs, and after-action reviews demonstrated that Non-
Motorola units experienced higher rates of dropped communications, loss of system
affiliation, and roaming instability when operating on the region’s Motorola-based
ASTRO 25 network. Motorola radios consistently demonstrated superior audio quality,
stable roaming, and uninterrupted connectivity, essential for officer and responder
safety.
Cynergy Professional Systems, as an authorized SDVOSB reseller and integrator of
Motorola technology, is uniquely qualified to deliver, configure, and support this
equipment. Their authorization ensures access to OEM-protected software, system
keys, interface protocols, firmware, and security updates that are not accessible through
non-authorized vendors. This protects system integrity, ensures proper lifecycle
support, and maintains warranty and cybersecurity compliance. For these reasons, the
combination of Motorola’s proprietary CommandCentral AXS platform and its
authorized, SDVOSB-certified role, Cynergy Professional Systems is uniquely capable
of meeting the agency’s operational, technical, and mission-critical requirements without
degradation of service or unacceptable risk to public safety operations and is in the best
interest of the Government.
6. Efforts to Obtain Competition: Market research was conducted, details of which are in
the market research section of this document. This effort did not yield any additional
sources that could meet the Government’s requirements. There is no competition
anticipated for this acquisition. In accordance with FAR 16.507-6(f)(1), the justification
will be made publicly available on the Contracting Opportunities Page within 14 days of
award.
7. Actions to Increase Competition: The Government will continue to conduct market
research to ascertain if there are changes in the marketplace that would enable future
actions to be completed.
Page 2 of 5
Motorola Hardware and Maintenance VA-26-00048856
8. Market Research: Market research efforts were conducted during January 2026 to
determine if competition was viable for this action. Specifically, the Government
technical experts reviewed multiple manufacturers including Harris, Kenwood Viking,
L3Harris, EF Johnson, and Motorola Solutions. While several vendors produce
P25-compliant radios, market research determined that Motorola is the dominant and
primary vendor in the region, with surrounding agencies—including law enforcement,
fire departments, emergency medical personnel, and regional interoperability groups—
operating on Motorola ASTRO 25 infrastructure and Motorola subscriber units. Only
Motorola subscriber units and dispatch solutions provide full feature compatibility with
local partner systems without the loss of mission-critical functionality. Harris subscriber
radios, although P25 compliant, have experienced consistent operational issues,
including dropped transmissions, roaming failures, and intermittent connectivity on
Motorola-based systems—issues acknowledged by both field operations and technical
staff. Based on these findings, alternative vendors were unable to provide the level of
interoperability, reliability, and system-native integration required for mission-critical
communications. Cynergy Professional Systems, an authorized Motorola reseller and
integrator with access to OEM-protected software, system keys, firmware, and
configuration tools, is the most effective, efficient, and economical solution for this
procurement.
The Small Business Administration certification database was accessed in August 2026.
This search concluded that Cynergy Professional Systems is registered, certified and
qualifies as a SDVOSB in accordance with the federal small business size standard for
the applicable North American Industry Classification System Code 541519. It was also
verified that Cynergy Professional Systems is registered in SAM.gov database and is
eligible to receive government contracts. The Contracting Officer reviewed NASA
SEWP V Program Performance Ratings and all ratings were Excellent, demonstrating
they are a responsible contractor with respect to performance.
9. Other Facts: The Procuring Contracting Officer has determined that this proposed
action meets all the requirements of 38 U.S.C. 8127(c) and VAAR 819.7008. This
acquisition is below the $5,000,000.00 threshold, Cynergy Professional Systems is a
responsible SDVOSB for performance of the services described herein, the
proposed contract can be awarded at a fair and reasonable price and is in the best
interest of the Government.
Page 3 of 5

Motorola Hardware and Maintenance VA-26-00048856
Advocate for Competition Approval
In my role as procuring activity Advocate for Competition, based on the foregoing
justification, I hereby approve the acquisition of Motorola APX N30 Radios, AXS
Dispatch Consoles, Radio Programming and the installation of the consoles at VAMC
Las Vegas on an other than fair opportunity basis pursuant to the authority cited in
Section 4 above, subject to availability of funds, and provided that the property and
services herein described have otherwise been authorized for acquisition.

Justification and Approval (J&A) for Other Than Full and Open Competition
I. Agency and Contracting Activity.
The Department of the Air Force, Air Force Material Command, Air Force Life Cycle Management Center, Presidential &
Executive Airpower Directorate, Program Office (PO) (AFLCMC/WVB) proposes to enter into a contract on a basis of
other than full and open competition for the program
II. Nature and/or description of the action being approved.
A new contract action will be awarded to CAE USA Inc. (CAE) under the authority of this J&A. The PO plans to use a
firm fixed price contract action for the following requirements: site survey, procurement of a commercial FAA Level D
certified 747-8i Full Flight Simulator (FFS), delivery, installation, operational hardware, software, cybersecurity, initial support
and maintenance, and initial training and courseware for flight instruction.
III. Description of supplies/services required to meet agency needs.
The ) has a critical and urgent requirement for one dedicated, commercial, FAA Level D
certified 747-8i FFS, expected to be The capability is mission-essential for flight
crews to achieve and maintain the mandatory proficiency required for Airlift operations. The 747-8i FFS is vital
for conducting initial pilot qualification, recurrent proficiency, as well as other aircrew training exercises.
The site survey will evaluate facility requirements for the FFS. The evaluation will determine if the facility has the required
space for Full Operational Capability (FOC) of the FFS and Instructor Operating Station (IOS), including requirements for
installation, support and maintenance, and training.
The newly manufactured commercial FAA Level D certified 747-8i FFS is anticipated to include, but not be limited to, the
following features and capabilities: Full motion system with aerodynamic modeling and performance data, visual system,
sound system, cockpit environment, aircraft systems simulation, and IOS. The contract CLIN structure is anticipated to
include separately priced CLINs for Intellectual property (IP) and IP rights. The PO anticipates acquiring all necessary
technical data and computer software to operate and maintain a Level D certified 747-8i FFS via the Contract Data
Requirements List (CDRLs) including, but not limited to, 747-8i performance data, high fidelity models of frequently visited
airports; acceptance test procedures to validate software models, and training and courseware documentation for operators
and maintenance personnel. The PO anticipates acquiring license rights necessary to allow for future competition of the
follow-on operation and maintenance of the Level D FFS. This includes technical data, computer software, and computer
software documentation in which the USG is entitled to unlimited or unrestricted rights (e.g. Operation Maintenance
Installation and Training (OMIT) data). The PO will also evaluate the commercial license rights typically provided with
purchase and operation of a Level D certified 747-8i FFS to see if the rights are sufficient to meet any portion of the
acquisition.
The Full Motion System will provide Six Degree of Freedom (6-DOF) motion for realistic aircraft movement and G-forces. The
FFS will incorporate aero model data to account for ground effect, flap settings, and other aerodynamic factors. The
simulator must accurately perform as the aircraft under various atmospheric conditions, including wind shear, turbulence,
and icing. The FFS will accurately reproduce the 747-8i performance data, including take-off and landing distances, climb
rates, and cruise speeds.
The Visual System will provide high-resolution, wide field-of-view (FOV) with realistic day, night, and adverse weather
conditions and will include detailed airport scenery, terrain, and atmospheric effects for minimum FOV to meet Level D
certification. The visual database will include high-fidelity models including accurate runway
markings, lighting, terminal buildings and any other possible obstacles and will have an easily updated and customizable
database. The Sound System will have realistic audio cues for all aircraft systems and environmental sounds and will
accurately simulate engine noise, aerodynamic sounds, and cockpit alerts.
The Cockpit Environment will be an accurate replica of the 747-8i cockpit, including all instruments, controls, and displays.
The Aircraft Systems Simulation will be an accurate and comprehensive simulation of all aircraft systems including: flight
controls, engines, hydraulic systems, electrical systems, fuel systems, environmental control systems, navigation systems,
autopilot and flight director systems, communications systems, warning and caution systems, ice and rain protections,

Justification and Approval (J&A) for Other Than Full and Open Competition
landing gear and braking systems, fire protection systems, flight management systems, and electronic flight bag integration.
The IOS will be intuitive and user-friendly to control all aspects of the simulation, including scenario management, weather/
time of day control, typical aircraft malfunctions, positioning and repositioning, student performance monitoring and data
recording, real-time performance analysis and feedback tools, and the ability to create custom training scenarios.
Delivery and installation of the 747-8i FFS will be required. The delivery and installation Period of Performance (PoP) is
estimated at contract award.
The FFS operational hardware, software, and cybersecurity will be fully developed and tested. The hardware architecture at
install will be the most current to support necessary computers, networking, and cybersecurity requirements. The software
will cover all aircraft systems necessary for a Level D FFS and include a complete set of acceptance test procedures to
validate the software models. All computer and operating system cybersecurity standards will be in full compliance with
DoD Instructions DoDI 8500.01 and DoDI 8510.01, Air Force Instructions AFI 17-101 and AFI 17-130 and DoD Manual 5200.01,
Vol 1-4.
The initial support and maintenance will consist of on-site maintenance and repair services for the FFS operations, spare
parts, software updates to maintain accuracy and address any issues, technical documentation and training for operators
and maintenance personnel, and a guaranteed uptime percentage. The initial support and maintenance is anticipated to
have a 12-18 month support PoP. The support PoP will also include the courseware and flight instruction to train pilots,
instructors, and aircrew personnel.
IV. Demonstration that the contractor's unique qualifications or the nature of the acquisition requires use of the
authority cited above.
This J&A supports the use of other than full and open competition to procure the supplies and services described in Section
III above via a sole source contract to CAE. CAE is the only responsible source and no other types of supplies or services will
satisfy agency requirements (see RFO 6.103-1, 10 USC 3204(a)(1)). CAE is the only contractor with the unique qualifications to
manufacture a commercial, FAA Level D certified 747-8i FFS.
CAE has manufactured all of the commercial Level D certified 747-8 simulators worldwide, including past contracts with
commercial airlines and Commercially, CAE has delivered a total of 747-8 simulators,
with in the last CAE is currently subcontracted for a future delivery of a 747-8i FFS for the
Historically, CAE has produced Level D certified simulators for the Air Force, Army,
Navy and Marine Corps branches, including the military platforms.
CAE's design for the 747-8i FFS will use a commercially available FFS platform, manufactured to meet FAA Level D
certification as outlined by Title 14 CFR Part 60. The platform will be further developed to meet the 747-8i requirements, as
described in Section III above. Successful manufacturing and delivery of previous 747-8 FFSs demonstrates CAE's ability to
perform the work required.
CAE maintains the appropriate security clearances to manage work , and will ensure employees
maintain appropriate clearances for the design, development, manufacturing and installation of the FFS.
CAE has the requisite personnel, technical expertise, and facilities to ensure the Government's delivery timeline is met. By
leveraging CAE's capabilities, the program can mitigate risk of significant schedule delays, increased lifecycle costs, and
critical gaps in mission-essential training for the by providing an all-inclusive package for the FFS. CAE is positioned as
the authoritative source for courseware and flight instruction supporting the FFS, making CAE the only responsible source to
deliver the program on time and within budget for all scoped requirements.
V. Description of efforts made to ensure that offers are solicited from as many potential sources as practicable,
including whether a notice was or will be publicized as required by subpart 5.2 and, if not, which exception under
FAR 5.202 applies.
A Sources Sought Notice (SSN) was released on SAM.gov on 22 December 2025, with a deadline for submissions of 16

January 2026 (SSN ID: F4FDWL-26-R-000). The SSN requested responses from qualified vendors capable of providing a new
(not an upgraded or refurbished system), commercial, FAA Level D certified 747-8i FFS. Responses were received from
vendors, and the results from the review are included in the attached market research report and Section VII of this form. The
pre-solicitation synopsis required per RFO 5.201 will be posted via a Notice of Contracting Action (NOCA) to SAM.gov. The
Request for Proposal (RFP) will be posted on SAM.gov per RFO 5.201 and a post-award Synopsis and the J&A will be posted
after award.
VI. Determination by the Contracting Officer that the anticipated cost to the Government will be fair and reasonable.
The efforts covered under this J&A will not be subject to the submission of certified cost and pricing data by the contractor
as this effort is commercial. The Contracting Officer (CO) will request other than certified cost or pricing data, such as sales
data, to accomplish the price analysis. The PO has also accomplished budget estimates of the commercial FFS and initial
support. The CO expects to determine that the anticipated cost to the Government will be fair and reasonable.
VII. Description of the market research conducted and the results, or a statement of the reasons market research was
not conducted.
As described in Section V, an SSN was released on SAM.gov on 22 December 2025, with a deadline for submissions of 16
January 2026. The SSN requested responses from qualified vendors capable of providing a new (not an upgraded or
refurbished system), commercial, FAA Level D certified 747-8i FFS, meeting all applicable regulatory requirements, and
providing realistic, immersive training for pilots transitioning to, or maintaining currency in the 747-8i aircraft. The
respondents included CAE. stated in
writing that they expressed interest, but did not provide a follow-up statement of their capabilities, limiting the Government
to reviewing the company's profile online for the analysis and concluded that was not an adequate vendor.
CAE provided complete SSN responses prior to the due date. The PO reviewed the submissions, conducted One-on-One
Industry Sessions to review RFIs with the potential vendors, and the PO conducted additional research via Internet searches
and Government Contacts to finalize the Market Research Report. Based on the market research report, asserted they
would act as an integrator for the FFS procurement, partnering with an OEM to produce the FFS. The Government concluded
this would pose a significant risk to the program's cost and schedule, as the Government did not request a procurement
integrator in the SSN. The only manufacturer of 747-8 FFS

1. Background
Naval Construction Training Center (NCTC) Port Hueneme conducts advanced
Construction Mechanic (CM) “C” School training in support of U.S. Navy Seabee
readiness. The CM transmission curriculum requires hands-on instruction utilizing
current-generation heavy-duty automatic transmissions representative of fleet platforms.
Existing training transmissions require factory-certified overhaul and replacement to
maintain alignment with current fleet configuration and manufacturer performance
standards.
2. Scope
The contractor shall provide six (6) Allison 4700SP_P (4th Generation) Factory ReTran
automatic transmissions and coordinate the pickup, packaging, and transportation of six
(6) Government-owned transmissions for overhaul exchange.
3. Requirements
The contractor shall provide:
• Six (6) Allison 4700SP_P 4th Generation Factory ReTran transmissions (P/N 29572129
or current OEM superseding part).
• Factory-certified remanufactured units built to OEM performance standards.
• Full Allison factory warranty documentation.
• Manufacturer certification of remanufacture and testing.
Instructional Durability Requirements:
Due to repetitive disassembly and reassembly in a controlled instructional environment,
all external threaded mounting holes, service access points, and repeatedly used fastener
interfaces shall be reinforced with Keenserts, hardened steel thread inserts, replaceable
threaded studs, or equivalent OEM-approved reinforcement solutions.
Reinforcement shall be limited to external, serviceable threaded locations and shall not
alter internal transmission components, affect OEM configuration, or void the Allison
factory warranty.
Government Furnished Property (GFP) – Pickup and Packaging:
The contractor will provide (6) new transmissions that shall be properly secured to
pallets, shrink-wrapped or otherwise protected, and prepared to prevent damage during
loading and transportation for delivery to Naval Construction Training Center, 363 White
House Way, Port Hueneme, CA 93043. Additionally, on the same day of initial delivery
contractors will pick up the (6) used core charge transmissions. Palletizing, shrink-wrap
or otherwise protect, to prevent damage during loading and transportation back to point
of origin.
The contractor shall provide all labor, materials, palletization, crating (if required), and
packaging necessary to transport the core charge (used) transmissions to their location for
processing.
Risk of loss or damage shall be transferred in accordance with contract terms upon
pickup from Government location.
4. Warranty Requirements
All transmissions shall include the full Allison Factory ReTran Limited Warranty in
effect at time of award.
Warranty shall begin upon Government acceptance at destination.
The contractor shall assist with warranty registration and coordinate any warranty claims
through authorized service channels.
5. Delivery Requirements
Delivery shall be Destination to:
Naval Construction Training Center
363 White House Way
Port Hueneme, CA 93043
The contractor shall coordinate delivery with the designated Government Point of
Contact prior to shipment.
All items shall be properly packaged, palletized, and protected against damage during
shipment.
6. Inspection and Acceptance
Government inspection and acceptance shall occur at destination. Acceptance will be
based on verification of correct part numbers, serial numbers, manufacturer certification,
and warranty documentation.
7. Period of Performance
Pickup of Government-owned transmissions and delivery of replacement ReTran units
shall be completed within the contractor’s quoted lead time after contract award.

Description: Notice of Intent to Award a Sole Source Contract The US Army Corps of Engineers, Rock Island District, intends to procure and enter into a firm-fixed-price purchase order with Schoellhorn-Albrecht Machine Co., Inc. of St. Louis, MO, for the purchase and delivery of one (1) Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) Chanoine Winch (Part ID: SA-CP10000-30-DC-BB). This procurement is being conducted on a sole-source basis in accordance with the authority at FAR 13.106-1(b)(1), as only one source is reasonably available. The Peoria Lock and Dam requires this genuine OEM winch to ensure operational compatibility with a vessel specifically engineered by the Marine Design Center (MDC). Due to proprietary engineering data, unique physical dimensions, and specific integration requirements, Schoellhorn-Albrecht is the only source capable of providing a winch that is physically and functionally interchangeable with existing assets. This sole-source requirement is based on the need for a direct, bolt-in replacement that matches the vessel's pre-fabricated foundation, drum geometry, line pull capacity, and integrated Direct Torque Control (DTC) system, thereby ensuring operational safety and leveraging the Government's existing spare parts inventory. This is a supply-only requirement; installation is not included. THIS NOTICE IS NOT A REQUEST FOR COMPETITIVE QUOTES and no solicitation will be issued. However, any firm that believes it can meet the requirement may give written notification to the Contracting Officer in the form of a capability statement. Supporting evidence must be furnished in sufficient detail to demonstrate the ability to comply with the requirement listed and must be furnished to the point of contact listed below by the response date and time. Solicitation number: FA487726QA217

Description: This is not a solicitation, and quotes are not being accepted at this time. The 355th Contracting Squadron intends to issue a sole-source contract action for procurement of the following items: - CLIN 0001 - Rigged Alternate Method-Tandem (RAM-T) 40s - QTY 18 - CLIN 0002 - RAM-T 40 Accessory Kits - QTY 9 Commercial Market Research & Distribution Strategy: Open market research, past procurement reviews, and technical reviews confirmed that while other tethered-tandem cargo systems exist, none match the proprietary geometry, dimensions, and rigging integration tested and approved in TB 25-16. Furthermore, communications with the manufacturer (Onyx Industries) confirmed that for stateside procurements, they sell direct to the Government or through prime vendors for the Defense Logistics Agency (DLA). As this requirement is not being procured through DLA, a direct sole-source award to the Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) is the most efficient and practical acquisition strategy. Sole Source / Small Business Determination: Onyx Industries is confirmed as the manufacturer and sole supplier of the certified RAM-T 40 system outside of DLA channels.0 The requested items will enable 304 RQS pararescue teams to safely conduct C-130 aircraft Military Tandem Tethered Bundle (MTTB) aerial insertion operations for boats assigned to the unit. These operations are conducted using pre-established Combat Ready Insertion Barrel (CRIB) procedures in conjunction with the Onyx RAM-T 40 modular air delivery solution which increases the unit's ability to conduct maritime rescue and Isolated Personnel recovery missions. CRIB (Onyx RAM-T 40) is a commercial-off-the-shelf (COTS) product providing for standardized rigging and deployment procedures that are used during maritime recovery missions of Isolated Personnel. CRIB (Onyx RAM-T 40) has been fully tested on the C-130 airframe and equipment preparation procedures are described in USAF Tactics Bulletin (TB) 25-16, dated 3 March 2026. Additionally, this testing and evaluation performed by the 88th Test and Evaluation Squadron has resulted in the development of the Tactics, Techniques, and Procedures (TTP) documentation specific to the Onyx RAM-T 40 product and outlined in TB 25-16. All interested/capable parties should respond no later than 9/03/2026 at 11:00am PDT to the POCs identified within this notice. Department of the Air Force: Justification for Other Than Full and Open Competition
I. Agency and Contracting Activity (RFO 6.104-1(a)(1)):
Agency: ACC
Contracting Activity: 355 Contracting Squadron
II. Nature and/or description of the action being approved (RFO 6.104-1(a)(2)):
This justification supports the award of a sole-source acquisition to Onyx Versatile Innovation for the procurement of the
Onyx RAM-T 40 (Rigged Alternate Method-Tandem) Modular aerial-delivery system in support of the 304th Rescue Squadron
(RQS).
III. Description of supplies/services required to meet agency needs (RFO 6.104-1(a)(3)):
The Government requires commercial aerial delivery hardware and accessories corresponding exactly to the tested and
fielded Combat Ready Insertion Barrel (CRIB) configuration supporting training and real-world maritime rescue and
Isolated Personnel recovery operations:
- 0001 - Onyx RAM-T 40 (Rigged Alternate Method-Tandem) Modular aerial-delivery system supporting tethered-tandem,
conventional-parachute, and guided-parachute configurations; includes carriage assembly, roller track, and rigging
components.
- 0002 - Onyx RAM-T 40 Accessory KitAccessory kit for RAM-T 40C/B & RAM-T 40L containing inflatable barrel, ballast system,
protective liner, filler, and restraint hardware.
Estimated Delivery: 120 - 180 Days After Receipt of Order (ARO), FOB Destination to 304 RQS, Portland, OR (DoDAAC:
DODF1PTR7).
IV. Statutory Authority Permitting Other Than Full and Open Competition (RFO 6.104-1(a)(4)):
10 U.S.C. 3204(a)(1), Only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements.
V. Rationale for Use of Authority (RFO 6.104-1(a)(5)):
304 RQS has an urgent operational requirement for the CRIB (Onyx RAM-T 40), a specialized aerial delivery assembly used to
conduct Military Tandem Tethered Bundle (MTTB) insertion of maritime equipment specifically a deflated Combat Rubber
Raiding Craft (CRRC) with outboard motor, fuel bladders, and accessories from C-130 aircraft.
Operational Test Baseline: The 88th Test and Evaluation Squadron (88 TES) conducted comprehensive operational testing of
the Guardian Angel (GA) CRIB from 14–18 April 2025, executing six (6) daytime airborne water jumps to validate C-130 exit
characteristics, parachute deployment, high-speed water impact, release sequences, and post-insertion boat inflation.
Authoritative Tactics, Techniques, and Procedures (TTP): Testing established the tactics and safety parameters published in
USAF Warfare Center Tactics Bulletin 25-16 (TB 25-16, dated 3 March 2026), Guardian Angel Combat Ready Insertion Barrel.
TB 25-16 specifies the exact dimensional tolerances, roller carriage geometry, Z/B/C/D strap configurations, Quick Ejector
Snap (QES) release steps, and aerodynamic end-cap rigging unique to the Onyx RAM-T 40.
Safety & Interoperability Impact: Procuring an alternate, untested aerial insertion system would require extensive new
airworthiness engineering reviews, C-130 wind tunnel / flight exit evaluations, live parachute airdrop testing, and full
rewrites of approved Air Force TTPs. Introducing unvalidated hardware into high-risk tandem parachute jumps poses
unacceptable life-safety risks to Pararescue personnel, risks catastrophic damage to aircraft and payload, and disrupts cross-
squadron interoperability across the 920th Rescue Wing (304 RQS, 306 RQS, and 308 RQS).
MMaayy 22002266 PPaaggee 33 ooff 44
CUI
Department of the Air Force: Justification for Other Than Full and Open Competition
Accordingly, Onyx Industries, LLC is the only responsible source capable of providing the tested and certified RAM-T 40
configuration that satisfies the Government's minimum operational and safety requirements.
VI. Integrated Market Analysis and Efforts to Solicit Competition (RFO 6.104-1(a)(6), (8), and (10)):
Mandatory and Strategic Sources Review: In accordance with RFO Part 8, mandatory sources (Air Force Strategic Vehicles,
AbilityOne, UNICOR/FPI, and GSA/AF Advantage) were reviewed. No mandatory source or GSA schedule vendor provides the
specialized CRIB RAM-T 40 system or meets the required technical specifications.
Commercial Market Research & Distribution Strategy: Open market research, past procurement reviews, and technical
reviews confirmed that while other tethered-tandem cargo systems exist, none match the proprietary geometry,
dimensions, and rigging integration tested and approved in TB 25-16. Furthermore, communications with the manufacturer
(Onyx Industries) confirmed that for stateside procurements, they sell direct to the Government or through prime vendors
for the Defense Logistics Agency (DLA). As this requirement is not being procured through DLA, a direct sole-source award
to the Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) is the most efficient and practical acquisition strategy.
Sole Source / Small Business Determination: Onyx Industries is confirmed as the manufacturer and sole supplier of the
certified RAM-T 40 system outside of DLA channels.
Notice of Intent to Sole Source: A Notice of Intent to Sole-Source Contract Action will be posted to SAM.gov allowing any
interested parties (including authorized DLA primes) to demonstrate capability.
VII. Determination of Fair and Reasonable Cost (RFO 6.104-1(a)(7)):
The Contracting Officer is responsible for evaluating, determining, and documenting the anticipated contract cost/price is
fair and reasonable in accordance with RFO Subpart 15.4, Contract Pricing.
VIII. Any Other Facts Supporting the Justification (RFO 6.104-1(a)(9)):
Utilizng the Onyx RAM-T 40 across the 304th, 306th, and 308th Rescue Squadrons ensures unified training, common tactics,
interchangeable rigging parts, and seamless integration of personnel and equipment during joint personnel recovery
contingency deployments.
Life Cycle & Logistics Efficiency: Fielded familiarization with the Onyx carriage system and harness components avoids
redundant training pipelines and reduces maintenance overhead across the Guardian Angel enterprise.
IX. Actions to Overcome Barriers to Competition (RFO 6.104-1(a)(11):
The Government will continue to monitor industry developments for other commercial-off-the-shelf (COTS) aerial delivery
insertion systems. If/When receiving future procurements, market research will be re-conducted to determine if alternative
manufacturers have developed comparable systems that have undergone Department of the Air Force test, evaluation, and
airworthiness certification. If alternative systems achieve operational qualification under applicable AFTTP / Tactics Bulletins,
future requirements will be competed to the maximum extent practicable.

matters.text:
Federal notice (Special Notice), DEPT OF DEFENSE.US SPECIAL OPERATIONS COMMAND (USSOCOM).HQ USSOCOM
Title: Notice of Intent to Award a Sole Source Contract under NAICS Code 334515
Solicitation number: H9240326RKCCharon
PSC: 6625; NAICS: 334515
Description: 1. Description This is a notice of intent to award a sole-source contract and is not a request for competitive proposals. HQUSSOCOM intends to negotiate and award a contract on a sole-source basis to Charon Technologies, LLC (CAGE: 5GRT9, DUNS: 078525181) for the procurement of the following items: Product: Spectrum Guard 2 Remote Kit (SG2 + Resource Manager) Part Number: P16A-K Quantity: 3 Estimated Total Value: $272,280.00 2. Authority This acquisition is being conducted under the authority of Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 6.302-1, "Only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements." Charon Technologies, LLC is the original equipment manufacturer (OEM) and sole developer, producer, and distributor of the proprietary Spectrum Guard 2 system. No other source has the technical data, proprietary rights, or expertise required to provide these specific items. The Government does not possess the data rights to solicit this requirement competitively from other sources. 3. Purpose The purpose of this is to notify potential sources of the Government's intent to award a sole-source contract. This notice is not a request for competitive quotes. However, all responsible sources may submit a capability statement, proposal, or quotation, which shall be considered by the agency. A determination by the Government not to compete this proposed contract based upon responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. 4. Submission of Information Interested parties who believe they can meet the requirement must submit a capability statement to the Point of Contact listed above no later than 15 calendar days from the date of this notice's publication. The statement must provide clear and convincing evidence that the respondent has the necessary technical capability and resources to provide the specified equipment.

PREPARATION FOR DELIVERY (COMMERCIALLY PACKAGED ITEMS)
(a) Preservation, packaging, and packing shall be in accordance with ASTM-D-3951 (most current edition), "Standard for Commercial Packing." The
unit pack quantity that applies to items under this contract is "Industry Standard".
(b) Prohibited Packing Materials. The use of asbestos, excelsior, loose fill polystyrene, newspaper or shredded paper (all types including waxed paper,
computer paper and similar hydroscopic or non-neutral material) is prohibited.
(c) Non-Manufactured Wood Packing. All non-manufactured wood utilized in wood pallets and wood containers shall be heat treated to a minimum
core temperature of 56 degrees centigrade for 30 minutes and certified by an accredited agency recognized by the American Lumber Standards
Committee (ALSC). Refer to https://www.aphis.usda.gov/aphis/ourfocus/planthealth/import-information/wood-packaging-material for wood packing
policy, enforcement regulations and accredited agencies. Non-coniferous (hardwood) and manufactured wood, such as particleboard and plywood, are
exempt from this requirement.
(d) Manufactured wood, such as particleboard and plywood, are exempt from this requirement.
(e) Packing must be sufficient to ensure safe delivery to the final destination without the need for additional repackaging or repair.
(f) All materials shall be packed to withstand multiple modes of transport (truck, rail, sea, or air) and handling by forklifts or cranes.
(g) Heavy items must be crated or skid-mounted to distribute weight evenly and ensure lifting point are accessible and marked.

FLCPS SRF 006 FLCPS_SRF_SHIPPING (Aug 2025)
I. INTRODUCTION
For this FOB Origin procurement, the Government will arrange for transportation and pay all associated transportation costs through the NAVSUP
WSS Shipment Processing (SP) office (aka NAVSUP GLS, NAVSUP LOC or NOLSC). NAVSUP WSS will process shipments of materials from
within the United States to CONUS (Continental United States)/OCONUS (Outside Continental United States) consignees with delivery terms Free
On-Board (FOB) Origin.
Contractors/vendors shall complete the Naval Supply Systems Command automated Ready-to-Ship (RTS) web form by accessing the link provided
below in Section II. By completing the form on line, the NAVSUP WSS at Norfolk, VA will receive an email of the shipment request immediately
and will act on it as soon as possible during their normal working hours of 7:30 AM to 6:00 PM Eastern Time Monday through Friday. In response,
NAVSUP WSS will provide MANDATORY USE shipping labels to the contractor/vendor. The contractor/vendor will arrange for shipment with the
NAVSUP WSS designated carrier IMMEDIATELY upon receipt of the shipping labels. If the NAVSUP WSS provided shipping labels are not used,
the contractor/vendor will experience delays and additional work to reconcile the transportation payment under the NAVSUP WSS tracking number
and possible additional costs not covered under the contract or NAVSUP WSS Transportation. If the contractor/vendor turns an ordered vehicle away
and a vehicle furnished not used charge is incurred the contractor/vendor is responsible for payment. If the contractor/vendor detains the vehicle and
incurs a detention charge the contractor/vendor is responsible for payment. International small parcel shipment documents are invalid after five
business days. If the vendor incurs any extra costs with the carrier outside of the CBL/GBL it is the vendors responsibility for payment. NAVSUP
WSS does not accept hazardous or explosive shipments.
CONTRACTORS/VENDORS ARE NOT AUTHORIZED TO ARRANGE FOR TRANSPORTATION OR PAY TRANSPORTATION COSTS FOR
SHIPMENT OF FOB ORIGIN PROCUREMENT.
II. PROCEDURES FOR CONTRACTORS TO REQUEST READY-TO-SHIP (RTS) NOTICES
When the cargo is ready for shipment, the contractor/vendor will submit their shipping request to NAVSUP WSS using the following procedures:
Click on the link at https://mynavsup-public.nag.navy.mil/public/ops$mailer.ready_to_ship_form to open the NAVSUP WSS RTS Web Form. The
contractor/vendor is required to fill in all data fields marked with a red asterisk under the headings "Vendor Information" and "Package Information."
The fields not marked with a red asterisk and the heading "Additional Notes" are optional fields to be filled in at the contractor's/vendor's discretion.
Click on the blue question mark at the right of each data field to access "On-line Data Element Help" which explains the data required in that field. If
shipping labels are being requested for multiple packages, enter the data for the first package under "Package Information" then click the "Store Pkg
Info" button. Repeat this procedure for each package. When all data has been entered on the electronic form, click the "Submit" button.
Container Shipments: containers take longer to book and arrange for loading. If you can provide reliable dimensions and weight estimates for the
cargo, send the initial shipping request THREE WEEKS before your requested container load date.
If you have any questions regarding the web form, contact NAVSUP WSS Transportation directly at (757) 443-5449 or usn.norfolk.navsupwssnorf.

Description: The Defense Logistics Agency Weapons Support Richmond issues this Sources Sought for potentially adding a population of 1 NSNs identified as sole source via modification. This agency proposes adding 353 items to the existing TF33 Pacer Phoenix Contract. These will be added to the contract SPE4AX-24-D-9000, awarded to Pratt and Whitney/CAGE 52661 in accordance with the originally approved J&A. However, the NSNs identified here were not included in the list of original items synopsized for this effort. The contract has 8 potential years remaining. This contract requires supply of parts, as well as other functions including but not limited to planning and forecasting, reliability improvements, engineering maintenance, and design control affecting these parts. A Letter Request for Proposal (RFP) will be issued to the awardee to request addition of the items as sole source. Contact the Contracting Officer listed to obtain a copy of the Letter RFP. Solicitation Number: To Be Determined DISCLAIMER: THE GOVERNMENT DOES NOT INTEND TO AWARD A CONTRACT ON THE BASIS OF THIS SOURCES SOUGHT OR TO OTHERWISE PAY FOR THE INFORMATION SOLICITED. This Sources Sought is issued for information and planning purposes only and does not constitute a solicitation. The Government requires that only non-proprietary information be submitted in response to this Sources Sought Notice. The Government shall not be liable for or suffer any consequential damages for the use of any proprietary information submitted. Responses to the Sources Sought will not be returned. The responses to this notice are not an order and cannot be accepted by the Government to form a binding contract. The Government reserves the right to reject, in whole or in part, any contractor's input resulting from this Sources Sought. Responders are solely responsible for all expenses associated with responding to this Sources Sought. Purpose: This agency proposes this Sources Sought as a means of conducting market research to determine if other companies can provide any items that have been determined to be sole source to Pratt & Whitney. The list of NSNs is attached to this notice. Objective: The Government intends to solicit and negotiate with only one source under authority of FAR 6.302. Interested parties may identify their interest and capability to support the objectives by responding to this notice. The proposed sole source Letter RFP will be issued to Pratt & Whitney, CAGEs 52661/77445. All responses received by the notice response date of September 3, 2026 will be considered by the Government. Title: Intent to Sole Source - SMASH 2000LE

Description: The 14th Contracting Squadron at Columbus AFB, MS hereby gives NOTICE OF INTENT TO AWARD A SOLE SOURCE to SmartShooter Inc., 13405 Elevation Lane, Herndone, VA 20171, to provide all products/support IAW the Statement of Work for SMASH 2000LE fire control optics. Description of Requirement: This acquisition is a strict sole-source procurement to fill an immediate capability gap identified by the Department of War (DoW) Joint C-sUAS Office (JCO) and recognized under the DAF FM 679 waiver. The "capability gap" refers to the critical point defense shortfall for a dismounted kinetic effects capability, specifically against small, unmanned aerial systems (sUAS). The SMASH 2000LE system is required to fill this immediate capability gap by providing a predictive tracking and fire control solution that enhances marksmanship, reduces the risk of collateral damage, and serves as a force-multiplier against fast-moving aerial and ground targets. Deliverables: 6ea SMASH 2000LE System � Each SMASH 2000 ENHANCED is provided with a 12-months warranty and includes Sighting unit (including Lock button), Fire Block Mechanism (replaceable hand grip), (3) rechargeable batteries, (1) battery charger, cables & accessories, case and operational guide. 1ea Spare Parts Kit This is not a solicitation for competitive quotes; however, if any interested party believes they can provide this service without compromising manufacturing, delivery, warranty, system integrity, or proprietary software licensing constraints, you may submit a statement of capabilities to be considered. A determination by the Government not to compete this proposed requirement is based upon responses to this notice and is solely within the discretion of the Government. Information received will be considered solely for the purpose of determining whether to conduct a competitive procurement in the future. The capability statement, a price list, and any other information furnished must be sent via email only and must contain material in sufficient detail to allow the Government to determine if the vendor can meet the requirements without violating SmartShooter Inc.'s exclusive software and hardware ownership. Capability statements and related materials must be e-mailed directly to SrA Holly Walters at holly.walters.2@us.af.mil and Jones, Nina M at nina.jones.2@us.af.mil no later than 12:00 PM Central Daylight Time on 28 August 2026.

DEPARTMENT OF THE AIR FORCE
14TH FLYING TRAINING WING (AETC)
COLUMBUS AIR FORCE BASE MISSISSIPPI
18 August 2026
MEMORANDUM FOR RECORD
FROM: 14 CONS/PKB
SUBJECT: Sole Source Justification Memorandum for Smart Shooter SMASH 2000LE Fire
Control System
1. This memorandum serves to document the decision and justification to award a sole-source
contract directly to Smart Shooter Inc. This is a request from the 14th Security Forces Squadron for
the acquisition of a SMASH 2000LE to use as a proprietary "one shot, one kill" fire control
technology. The SMASH 2000 family of optics is a fire-control system, designed to equip onto
existing USAF M4 and M4A1 carbines, intended to serve as an interim solution to address an
urgent C-UxS capability gap.
2. HQ AETC/A4S requires the use of a rapid, man-portable C-UxS targeting solution. The
SMASH 2000LE system is uniquely qualified to satisfy the acquisition requirements due to the
distinct operational and technical capabilities listed below:
• Assisted Aiming Technology: The SMASH 2000LE features a computerized sight that
tracks targets in real-time. The internal computer, aided by image processing, calculates
the ballistic firing solution to ensure first round accuracy, and depresses the plunger to
enable the operator to fire.
• Proven Operational Effectiveness: PACAF/A4SO conducted field testing at Schofield
Barracks on 1 May 2024. PACAF/A4SO mirrored Joint C-sUAS University’s (JCU)
SMASH 2000L (3000) test by suspending a balloon from a sUAS utilizing a steel cable.
The test itself consisted of engaging multiple ground targets and aerial targets utilizing
multiple flight patterns at various distances. 10 different courses of fire were used, with
an average accuracy of 65%. The conclusion noted that the SMASH 2000L provides an
inexpensive, highly deployable, kinetic kill option as a last resort against the emergent
sUAS threat, therefore, benefiting the Security Forces enterprise.
3. Market research indicated that other operational bases are using this exact product, such as
Maxwell AFB in Alabama, Laughlin AFB in Texas, and Spangdahlem AFB in Germany. The
DAF FM 679 waiver request for USAFE-AFAFRICA for this exact system confirms that a
command-level decision has been made to standardize this capability to fill a "critical point
defense shortfall." Procuring a different system would invalidate established doctrine and require
developing entirely new training and safety protocols, causing unacceptable delays.

Description: NWFSC SptTech BioMicroLab VC100 Instrument NOTICE OF INTENT TO NEGOTIATE A SINGLE-SOURCE CONTRACT Special Notice: FD-2026-523 NOAA/NMFS/SEFSC The U.S. Department of Commerce (DOC), National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA), Northwest Fisheries Science Center (NWFSC), Office of Management and Budget (OMB) intends to negotiate, on a sole source basis, under the authority of FAR 12.102(a), to SPT Labtech Inc. This requirement is for: Services, non-personal, to provide all labor, equipment and materials (unless otherwise provided herein) necessary for SptTech BioMicrolab VC100. The applicable Size Standard is North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) Code 334516 with a Small business size standard of 1000 employees. This Sole Source Determination is based on NOAAA's requirement for SPT Tech BioMicrolab VC100; SptTech is the sole manufacturer and supplier of the BioMicrolab VC100 and the only vendor capable of servicing and repairing the instrument using required OEM parts. While there are other liquid measuring instruments, none have been found that meet our technical specifications required to support robust, reproducible molecular genetic data generation other than the BioMicroLab VC100. TECHNICAL SPECIFICATIONS: The BioMicrolab VC100/384 instruments feature a proprietary ultrasonic sensor that uses distance measurements and a standard curve to determine sample liquid levels in various laboratory consumables (labware), extrapolating the liquid volume from distance in a calibration table created by the user and outputs the volume for each well position. The VC100 replaces visual or manual inspection of well plates to verify sample volume before and after liquid handling operations, or to provide a QC step for assay plate creation. 1. Functional & Operational Performance Technology: Patented, non-contact ultrasonic distance-to-meniscus sensor. Primary Application: Automated sample volume verification and quality control (QC) for microplates and tube racks (replaces manual/visual inspection). Labware Compatibility: Uncapped or unsealed standard ANSI/SLAS 96, 48, and 24-format well plates and tube racks (including shallow, deep-well, and PCR plates). Liquid/Solution Compatibility: Water, alcohols, buffers, DMSO, and other common laboratory solvents. Throughput Speed: Scans and detects sample volumes across a full 96-well plate in 1 minute. Sensitivity/Accuracy: Liquid level sensors detect volume changes down to the sub-10 $\mu$L range (tested on 96-well formats). Consumables Required: None (operates directly on existing compatible labware without specialized adapters). 2. Physical & Environmental Specifications Dimensions (W � D � H): 11.5" � 26.5" � 12.5" / 29.5 cm � 68 cm � 32 cm (depth specification includes required cable clearance and full tray extension). Weight: 33.25 lbs / 15.0 kg. Operating Temperature: 10�C to 40�C. Operating Humidity: 10% to 90% RH (Non-condensing). Placement Requirement: Level, vibration-free laboratory benchtop space. 3. Electrical & Power Requirements Input Voltage: 100�240 VAC universal power supply. Frequency: 50/60 Hz. Connectivity: Powered/controlled via a single dedicated USB port connection to a host PC. 4. Software & System Requirements Operating System Compatibility: Windows 10 or Windows 11 (supports both 32-bit and 64-bit systems). Hardware Prerequisites: Minimum 2 GB RAM laptop PC. Data Output Format: Automatically generates comma-separated values (.csv) file outputs mapping volume metrics on a well-by-well basis; native utility for printing or generating PDF plate reports. Automation Integration: ActiveX toolkit available to support integration with downstream liquid handlers and robotic platforms. SPECIAL REQUIREMENTS: On site BioMicroLab VC Remote Installation & Training required (Period of Performance, DOA - 12/1/2026). Twelve month BioMicroLab VC100 reliance complete Service Contract as extended warranty required to support instrument performance. (Period of Performance, DOA - 8/31/2028). DELIVERY SCHEDULE: The SptTech BioMicroLab VC100 must be delivered by 11/1/2026. On site training to be completed by 12/1/2026. 12 month extended warranty/service contract valid through 8/31/2028. matters.text:
Federal notice (Special Notice), DEPT OF DEFENSE.DEPT OF THE AIR FORCE.FA7000  10 CONS LGC
Title: NOI to Sole Source - Frequency Comb System Upgrade
Solicitation number: FA700026NOIFCS
PSC: 6650; NAICS: 334516
Description: The 10th Contracting Squadron at the United States Air Force Academy (USAFA) intends to solicit and award a firm-fixed-price (FFP) commercial purchase order on a sole-source basis to Vescent Technologies, Inc. (DBA Vescent Photonics, LLC), Golden, CO (UEI: JDCKBJDFLLL5) for a proprietary laser frequency comb system upgrade and expansion. The Physics Department's Laser and Optics Research Center (LORC) requires specialized wavelength extension modules, optical frequency references, phase-lock servos, temperature controllers, and data acquisition hardware to expand its pre-existing, government-owned Vescent RubriComb frequency comb system (originally purchased under Contract FA700025P0122). This acquisition includes the following proprietary components (or exact equivalents engineered specifically for physical and electronic docking within the pre-existing Vescent architecture): Stabilaser 1542E: 1542 nm Stabilized Laser Optical Frequency Reference. RUBRICOMB-100-RHT1542: Core platform exchange upgrade for optical locking at 1542.4 nm. RUBRIColor Chassis & 4 Wavelength Extension Modules: Configured specifically for target atomic transition wavelengths: 780.2 nm (EXT-HS780), 882.2 nm (EXT-HS882), 993.4 nm (EXT-HS993), and 1009.9 nm (EXT-H1010). 4 SLICE-OPL Offset Phase Lock Servos: Fast analog PID loops with >8 MHz bandwidth. SLICE-QTC Temperature Controller & Slide Rackmounts: Four-channel thermal controller. Quarto-101 Data Acquisition Controller: High-speed experimental controller. On-site Training & Installation: Direct technical OEM integration support at USAFA. The government-owned frequency comb operating at the USAFA LORC is a proprietary, closed-architecture platform designed and manufactured exclusively by Vescent Technologies, Inc. The requested hardware modules must physically slide into, optically seed from, and electronically loop-lock with the pre-existing Vescent core architecture. Hardware and modules from alternative manufacturers operate on incompatible optical repetition rates, distinct fiber interconnect types, and non-interoperable closed-loop feedback card protocols. These alternative systems are physically and electronically incompatible with the existing Vescent infrastructure. A competitive award to any other vendor would require the government to completely abandon its pre-existing investment and purchase a completely new system plus additional costs in auxiliary technical labor, fiber splicing, and custom software rebuilding. Consequently, a competitive procurement would result in a substantial, unrecoverable duplication of costs and an unacceptable delay of 6 to 12 months to active, federally-funded cadet atomic research programs. Response Instructions for Interested Parties This notice of intent is not a request for competitive quotes, and no solicitation document is currently available. However, the Government will consider written capability statements from any interested vendor that believes it can satisfy this requirement. To be considered, a capability statement must clearly demonstrate the vendor's ability to provide high-precision wavelength expansion modules, master reference lasers, and phase-lock electronics that can physically, optically, and electronically integrate with USAFA's pre-existing Vescent RubriComb system without requiring a replacement of the core laser chassis. All capability statements must include: Company Name, Address, CAGE Code, and UEI Number. Business size standard under NAICS 334516. Detailed technical documentation proving complete physical, optical, and software compatibility with the pre-existing Vescent architecture. JUSTIFICATION FOR BRAND NAME COMMERCIAL PRODUCTS/SERVICES OVER THE SIMPLIFIED
ACQUISITION THRESHOLD (SAT) USING SIMPLIFIED PROCEDURES (REVOLUTIONARY FAR
OVERHAUL (RFO))
REFERENCE: SOL 68HERW26R0031, “Beckman Coulter Automated Liquid Handler System
(B87585): Biomek i7 Hybrid (MC + Span-8) with a basic warranty, pipefitting, software,
customer training and application support options”
1. The Environmental Protection Agency’s Water, Tribal, and Science Division (WTSD)
proposes to restrict competition for this commercial acquisition as authorized by RFO
12.102(b).
2. Nature and/or description of the action being approved: New equipment acquisition using
commercial procedures.
Purchase of the Beckman Coulter Automated Liquid Handler System (B87585): Biomek i7
Hybrid (MC + Span-8) with a basic warranty, pipefitting, software, customer training and
application support options best meets the needs of the government. The government will
award a Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) contract resulting from this combined synopsis/solicitation
to the responsible offeror whose offer, conforming to the synopsis/solicitation, will be most
advantageous to the government (as determined by the solicitation evaluation criteria).
3. Description of the supplies and/or services required to meet the agency’s needs (including
the estimated value): One (1) Beckman Coulter Automated Liquid Handler System (B87585)
with a basic warranty, pipefitting, software, customer training and application support
options with a total cost of approximately [REDACTED].

Technical Specifications for Automated Liquid Handling System to be used for the generation
of transcriptomic data supporting OCSPP chemical risk assessment
BASE INSTRUMENT:
A work surface that can be configured with a variety of passive holders for
o
microplates, reservoirs and tip boxes. System must also support:
 Placement of functional components such as plate heating or
shaking.
 On-deck and peripheral device integrations to increase capacity
for microplate and tip box storage, and add functionality (e.g.,
heating, cooling, stirring, washing, plate reading).
 Framing of work surface for accurate 3-dimensional
positioning—including an optical framing tool.
A grid-based deck for flexible positioning of holders and
o
functional accessories, providing for up to 45 deck positions.
 Passive deck positions must be useable to store microplates and
tip boxes.
A Multichannel head and an 8-Channel Dispense head that can work in
o
parallel, sharing most positions on the work surface.
Two integrated grippers for efficient transportation of
o
microplates, microplate lids and tip boxes. Grippers must:
 Rotate 360° for microplate reorientation or for accessing
integrated devices with different microplate nest orientations.
 Be equipped with downward-pointing offset fingers that
maximize accessible deck positions and provide access to
peripheral integrated devices. Gripper force must be software
controlled and dependent on transported microplate, reservoir,
or tip box.
An integrated front light curtain and safety side shields to protect
o
operator from interfering with the system while pipetting arms are
moving.
 It must be possible to resume method after tripping light curtain.
A status light with four different colors and light patterns to indicate
o
stand-by, operation, user intervention required, and error condition.
 Status light must be visible from all sides of the instrument.
An LED-illuminated work surface for optimum visibility when accessing
o
the instrument.
 Switch for LED light must be positioned outside of work surface.
Integrated cameras that enable system monitoring from
o
networked devices.
 System cameras must be able to record/store video of unexpected
error conditions to support efficient/timely error diagnosis.
Software and hardware must support stacking of microplates and
o
microplate lids, including support of mixed stacks of different microplates,
if possible, by microplate geometry.
System must be upgradeable to include multiple integrated devices,
o
optional transportation robot, and planning/optimizing/scheduling
software.
System must support remote service by providing a secure infrastructure for
o
desktop and file sharing.
 Remote desktop and file access must be configurable and must
be granted by the user.
Vendor must have a qualification program for service and application
o
support personnel accessing the system.
PIPETTING:
Instrument must have an 8 Channel Dispensing Head with each channel
o
independently controlled, and with Variable Span to process 384-, 96-, 48-,
24- and 6-well plates, and tube sizes ranging from a PCR tube up to a 50 mL
bottle.
8 Channel Dispensing Head must support:
o
Calibration of individual channels to allow for optimization of
o
pipetting performance in low-volume range.
Individual capacitive liquid level sensing for all channels.
o
System must be user configurable to allow for exchange of 96-channel
o
and 384-channel heads. Standard-volume Multichannel head must
provide 300 µL working volume and enable use of large-volume filter
tips.
Large-volume Multichannel head must provide for 1200 µL air
o
displacement to effectively enable transfer of 1000 µL with filter tips, and
including sufficient blowout volume of >10% target transfer volume.
Multichannel head must support working with individual tips, columns, rows
o
and patterns to increase flexibility for applications such as tube-to-plate
transfer, addition of control reagents, and serial dilution.
System software must support volume and liquid-level tracking to
o
avoid repeat sensing for known volumes and volume changes.
Pipetting tips must be:
o
Provided in individual tip boxes that separate tips in
o
individual compartments to reduce contamination risk.
Provided in gripper-transportable tip boxes to move tips from
o
storage positions to tip loading.
Certified free of DNAse, RNAse, DNA (human and mouse),
o
PCR inhibitors, endotoxins and trace metals.
Pre-sterile tips must be sterilized with ethylene oxide to avoid use of
o
electron beam irradiation.
Tip boxes must be color-coded, with colors duplicated in instrument
o
software to reduce user error when loading the system.
SOFTWARE:
System must operate under the latest version of Microsoft Windows operating
o
system.
System software must:
o
Provide an interface that supports operators with instructions for
o
system setup, selection of desired protocol, monitoring of runs in
progress, and performing basic system tasks, as well as protecting
validated methods from inadvertently being altered.
Support remote monitoring of the system from networked devices.
o
Provide visual method authoring interface with drag & drop
o
functionality as well as the ability to copy/paste method items,
transfer steps, or method sections.
Offer a set of pre-configured basic pipetting operations such as
o
plate transfer, plate replication, combining plates, and serial
dilution. Standard method steps must be user-configurable for
method items and pipetting actions. Software should also present
plain text summary of settings for pipetting operations.
Aid method authoring with real-time, step-by-step validation. This
o
includes checking for logical errors, assisting error resolution with plain
text instructions, and providing estimated time to completion for the
entire methods.
Enable full control over 3D motion path of tips in wells when
o
moving, dispensing or aspirating. User must be able to define
complex pipetting patterns such as X-pattern for aspirating content
of a flat-bottom microplate.
Be able to automatically split volumes that exceed usable pipette
o
tip or pipetting head/probe volumes.
Support re-use of tips by assigning individual tip boxes to specific
o
reagent reservoirs.
Include an integrated SQL database for integrity of sample/process data.
o
Support recording, tracking, copying and pooling of sample IDs
o
following pipetting procedures.
Support liquid level tracking to calculate volume changes and
o
well/tube fill heights from initial volumes based on pipetting steps.
Support using sample data (e.g., sample ID, volume, concentrations,
o
OD readings) for data-driven pipetting operations such as hit picking
or normalization.
Visualize protocols in 3D simulation for faster method development.
o
Allow for different user roles to manage operations in a multi-
o
user environment. Access restrictions must be available to limit
method development and validation to user-qualified
application developers.
User must be able to easily define new microplate and reservoir definitions
o
based on existing definitions or on actual measurement of the microplate or
reservoir.
Controlled access must provide functions for multiple user access levels,
o
method version control, and system audit trail to support 21 CFR Part 11
requirements for electronic signatures.
CUSTOMER TRAINING AND APPLICATION SUPPORT OPTIONS:
Basic operation instructions must be provided upon system installation.
o
Online training classes must be available to help expedite initial training
o
Classroom trainings at vendor site must be available for method authoring and
o
method adaptation.
Optional customer-site training must be available on request.
o
Optional on-site field application support must be available to implement
o
required protocols or to assist with customer site method development.
Pre-defined methods must be available for
o
Lexogen Quant-seq 3’ FWD v2 w/UDI
o
Magmax-96 Total RNA Isolation Kit
o

Funding:
2. Brief Description of Supplies/ Services required and the intended
use/Estimated Amount:
The Truman VA Open Field Blast Core (OFBC) requires acquisition of a
Hi-Techniques Synergy P16U-T Data Acquisition System (DAS), hardened transport
case, four signal conditioning breakout interfaces, and shipping, totaling $38,099.42.
The system provides sixteen high-speed input channels capable of streaming 500
kS/s per channel and digitizing signals up to 1 MHz bandwidth, supporting voltage,
bridge, accelerometer, thermocouple, and infrasound sensor inputs. The OFBC will
use the system to expand its blast-exposure data collection capacity for
VA-approved traumatic brain injury (TBI) research. The additional DAS will allow
connection of new infrasound sensors and additional pressure sensors required for
expanded open-field blast studies, ensuring complete multi-aspect blast
characterization.
3. Unique characteristics that limit availability to only one source, with the
reason no other supplies or services can be used:
The Hi-Techniques Synergy P16U-T system is uniquely required because it must
match the existing Synergy systems already in use at the OFBC blast site. The
current system operates with fifteen pressure sensors using proprietary
Hi-Techniques input modules, signal conditioning interfaces, and data formatting.
Only the Synergy P16U-T provides complete compatibility with these existing
modules, cables, connectors, sampling rates, transient memory architecture, and
data processing/software workflows. Substituting a different manufacturer would
require replacing or reconfiguring the entire existing DAS infrastructure, would break
compatibility with currently deployed pressure sensors, and would compromise
uniformity and reproducibility of blast-exposure data. For expanded capacity—
