Federal notice (Combined Synopsis/Solicitation), DEPT OF DEFENSE.DEPT OF THE AIR FORCE.FA9302  AFTC PZZ
Title: Brand Name SLICE IP68 Data Acquisition System
Solicitation number: F1S0AY6202A003
PSC: 6610; NAICS: 334111
Description: This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial items prepared in accordance with the format in the Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO) policies and procedures, as supplemented with additional information included in this notice. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation; quotes are being requested and a formal written solicitation document will not be issued. BRAND NAME ONLY REQUIREMENT: This is a brand-name-only requirement for Diversified Technical Systems (DTS) SLICE IP68 parts. The specific form, fit, and function of the SLICE IP68 product line are essential to the Government's minimum needs and are required for compatibility and interoperability with existing government-owned equipment and test infrastructure. An approved Determination & Findings (D&F) for a brand-name acquisition is on file. Quotes for "or equal" items will not be considered. AUTHORIZED RESELLER PROOF REQUIRED: To be considered for award, quotes MUST be accompanied by formal, verifiable documentation directly from the Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM), Diversified Technical Systems (DTS), establishing that the bidding vendor is an Authorized Reseller/Distributor in good standing. Failure to provide this proof of authorized reseller status with the initial quote submission will result in the quote being deemed technically unacceptable and excluded from award consideration. REQUIREMENT: The Air Force Test Center (AFTC) at Edwards Air Force Base has a requirement to procure new, brand-name Diversified Technical Systems (DTS) SLICE IP68 data acquisition system components to support critical testing for the B-1 Bomber S.I. Data Lab. SET-ASIDE: This acquisition is a 100% Small Business Set-Aside. NAICS Code: 334111 - Electronic Computer Manufacturing (Size Standard: 1,250 Employees) Product Service Code (PSC): 6610 - Flight Instruments LINE ITEMS (CLINs): The specific part numbers, quantities, and descriptions are detailed in the attached solicitation document (SF1449 and/or attachments). BASIS FOR AWARD: The Government intends to award a single Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) purchase order to the responsible vendor whose quote conforms to the solicitation and is determined to be the Lowest-Priced Technically-Acceptable (LPTA). Technical acceptability is contingent upon the vendor's ability to provide the exact brand-name items and their verified DTS Authorized Reseller Proof. SUBMISSION INSTRUCTIONS: All interested small businesses must review the attached solicitation documents in their entirety and submit their quotes alongside the required OEM Authorized Reseller Proof in accordance with the instructions provided. All quotes must be received by the date and time specified in this notice. QUESTIONS: All questions regarding this solicitation must be submitted in writing to the Contract Specialist and Contracting Officer, Josiah Broadway, at josiah.broadway@us.af.mil, Terence Vickers at terence.vickers@us.af.mil no later than August 19, 2026, by 2:00 PM EST.

22 July 2026
Ruggedized Data Acquisition System (DAS)
Requirements Document
for
704th Test Group/846th Test Squadron
1.0 PURPOSE
The 704th Test Group (704 TG) mission is to be the premier provider of unique test and evaluation
capabilities relevant to tomorrow’s warfighter through world-class people improving technical excellence,
cost-effectiveness, and agility. The 846th Test Squadron (846 TS) is one of the units assigned to the
704 TG. The 846 TS’s primary test capability is the Holloman High Speed Test Track (HHSTT) where
they utilize rocket powered sled trains to simulate flight like environments and scenarios with the control
and recovery of a ground-based system. In order to collect data from these systems, a robust data
acquisition system is required. These tests are required for the test mission and validation of various
avionics platforms, payloads, and equipment for the Department of Defense in conjunction with its
partners over a number of differing rocket sled configurations. The 846 TS has purchased nine DTS
Slice6 AIRs systems and requires an add-on data acquisition system that will interface directly with DTS
for additional collection capability, to continually meet customer requirements.
2.0 SCOPE
The Contractor shall deliver two hardened DAS systems with the option to purchase an additional two in
the future. The hardened DAS systems should meet the following requirements:
2.1 Operational requirements:
2.1.1 System Control:
2.1.1.1 DAS shall have a single controlling module capable of operating up to 6 channels of analog data
2.1.1.2 System shall be capable of communicating to a PC over ethernet at a distance of 350 feet without
external aid and to a distance of 1000 feet with an ethernet extender
2.1.1.3 System shall be capable of being networked together or centralized to increase the number of
analog channels
2.1.2 Data Acquisition Parameters:
2.1.2.1 For Bridge and IEPE signal conditioning, DAS must provide the following signal conditioning
characteristics:
2.1.2.1.1 Bridge input range of 0 to 5 V
2.1.2.1.2 Bandwidth of DC to 50 kHz
2.1.2.1.3 Software programmable gain range of 1.0 to 1280
2.1.2.1.4 Auto offset range with 100% of effective input range at gain >2
2.1.2.1.5 Automatically calculated emulation method shunt check
2.1.2.1.6 Linearity ≤0.1% (for gain setting of 1 to 320), and ≤0.5% (for gain setting ≥640)
2.1.2.1.7 Accuracy of ≤0.5% typical
2.1.2.1.8 IEPE Singal range 0.5 to 23.5 V
2.1.2.2 DAS must contain anti-aliasing capability with the following specifications:
2.1.2.2.1 Fixed 4-pole butterworth low pass filter with 50 kHz knee frequency
2.1.2.2.2 Programmable 5-pole butterworth low pass filter, configurable between 1 Hz and 35 kHz and
bypass-able for maximum bandwidth
2.1.2.3 DAS shall contain one 16-bit SAR (Successive Approximation Register) ADC per channel, with
simultaneous sampling of all channels.
2.1.3 Triggers (DAS unit will provide the following triggering capability):
2.1.3.1 Triggering by means of:
2.1.3.1.1 Contact closure & TTL logic-level (active low)
2.1.3.1.2 Positive and/or negative level on any active sensor channel
2.1.3.2 Software triggering shall be available for daisy-chained systems
2.1.4 Power (DAS shall have the following power characteristics):
2.1.4.1 Operate on 9 to 30 VDC
2.1.4.2 Maximum current draw ≤ 3 W with full sensor load
2.1.4.3 Remote power control input for on/off
2.1.4.4 Reverse current and electrostatic discharge protection
2.1.5 Data Recording and Streaming:
2.1.5.1 Minimum of 16 GB of non-volatile system memory
2.1.5.2 Must include multiple data recording modes:
2.1.5.2.1 Recorder
2.1.5.2.2 Circular buffer
2.1.5.2.3 Multiple event
2.1.5.3 Maximum sample rate per channel shall be no less 400,000 samples / second
2.1.5.4 Must stream in IRIG Chapter 10 and TmNS (but not simultaneous)
2.1.5.5 Must stream no less than 20,000 samples / second
2.1.5.6 DAS shall except IRIG-B122 time source
2.1.6 Excitation (DAS unit will provide the following excitation capability):
2.1.6.1 Independently regulated channels
2.1.6.2 Supply 5 V and up to 20 mA per channel
2.1.6.3 Include short circuit protection with recovery ≥1 msec
2.1.6.4 IEPE current 5 mA per channel (24 V source)
2.1.6.5 DAS shall shut down excitation when not armed or recording
2.1.7 Hardware Interface:
2.1.7.1 DAS must directly interface with:
2.1.7.1.1 Minimum of 6 piezo-resistive or voltage input sensors
2.1.7.1.2 Minimum of 6 piezo-electric sensors
2.1.7.3 Allow for connection to multiple data acquisition systems including:
2.1.7.3.1 A minimum of 3 DTS SLICE6 Air daisy chained
2.1.7.3.2 Two additional data acquisition systems with no more than 5 meter separation
2.1.7.4 DAS shall have electronic ID interface to automatically read and determine what sensor is
attached to each sensor input channel
2.1.8 Physical and Environmental:
2.1.8.1 Mounting shall be accomplished with no less than two bolts through the face of the machined
case
2.1.8.2 Interfacing connectors shall be mounted on the face of the machined aluminum case
2.1.8.3 System shall not be larger than 1.65”L x 1.65”W x 0.51”H
2.1.8.4 System shall not exceed 55 grams
2.1.8.5 Operational Temperature range of -40 to 176°F
2.1.8.6 Operational Humidity of 95% RH non-condensing
2.1.8.7 Shock on all axis ± 5000 g, 0.1 msec half sine
2.1.8.8 Vibration on all axis shall meet MIL-STD-810G and MIL-STD-461G
2.1.8.9 Survival at minimum vibration of 12 grms, 3 to 2k Hz
2.2 Documentation and Support:
2.2.1 An operations manual for the unit will be provided
2.2.2 DAS control software shall be provided
3.0 MILESTONES
The contractor shall deliver two 6-channel ruggedized data acquisition systems no later than 35 days
ARO.
4.0 DELIVERABLES
The contractor shall deliver all hardware and documentation to 846 TS, Attn: Brent Kolste at 1521 Test
Track Road, Holloman Air Force Base, New Mexico 88330-7850.

DEPARTMENT OF THE AIR FORCE

COMBINED SYNOPSIS/SOLICITATION_FA910126QB067
This is a sole source solicitation for a commercial product. As such, this solicitation is prepared in
accordance with (IAW) the format in the Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO) 12.201-1, as supplemented
with additional information included in this request. This solicitation is not authorization to begin
performance, and in no way obligates the Government for any costs incurred by the offeror associated
with developing an offer. The Government reserves the right not to award a contract in response to this
RFP.
Solicitation Number: FA910126QB067
Solicitation Type: Request for Quote (RFQ)
North American Industry NAICS code 334515 - Instrument Manufacturing for Measuring
Classification System (NAICS) and Testing Electricity and Electrical Signals
Code:
Federal Supply Code (FSC): 6625 - Electrical and Electronic Properties Measuring and Testing
Instruments
Size Standard: 750 Employees
Set-Aside Status: None - Unrestricted
Nonmanufacturer Rule (NMR) Not Applicable
Description of Requirement:
The Government requires a quantity of two (2) brand-name only DTS SLICE6 AIR Modules (P/N:
13006-90910) to be delivered to Holloman Air Force Base, New Mexico, with an option to purchase an
additional two (2) identical modules within 12 months of contract award. This is purely a supply
procurement with no "or equal" products or incidental services. All items must be factory-new, carrying
the full manufacturer's warranty, and provided by the OEM, Diversified Technical Systems, Inc. (DTS).
See "Attachment 1 - Specifications" for full details.
Justification for Limiting Competition (Brand-Name Only):
The 846th Test Squadron (846 TS) operates the Holloman High Speed Test Track (HHSTT) and
currently utilizes the proprietary DTS Slice6 AIRs system as its primary data acquisition architecture.
The ruggedized Data Acquisition Systems (DAS) being procured must physically and electrically daisy-
chain with this existing network. Due to proprietary communication protocols, pinout configurations,
and sub-millisecond synchronization requirements during high-speed track testing, introducing an
alternative manufacturer's hardware would result in catastrophic data failure and inability to integrate.
Therefore, "equal" products are technically unacceptable. In accordance with RFO 12.102(a),
competition is restricted to a single-source brand-name supply directly with the OEM, Diversified
Technical Systems, Inc. (DTS).
Non-Applicability of NMR:
The Nonmanufacturer Rule (NMR), as outlined in RFO 19.505 and 13 CFR § 121.406, is not applicable
to this acquisition. The NMR applies strictly to competitive acquisitions that have been set aside (fully or
partially) for small business concerns. Because this requirement is being solicited as an Unrestricted
single-source action directly to the OEM, the NMR does not apply.
One AFMC…Powering the World’s Greatest Air Force
DPAS Priority Rating:
DO-C9 in accordance with RFO 52.211-15. The "DO" rating ensures the manufacturer gives this order
preferential lead-time treatment over unrated commercial orders. The "C9" program identification
symbol was selected because the 846th Test Squadron conducts testing and evaluation that directly
supports miscellaneous national defense and Research & Development (R&D) programs, aligning with
the "Miscellaneous / Testing" designation under DPAS Schedule I (15 CFR Part 700).
CMMC Exemption:
The Government has determined that the product required under this solicitation is a Commercially
Available Off-the-Shelf (COTS) item. Because this procurement is exclusively for a COTS product, the
Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification (CMMC) requirements are not applicable. Offerors are not
required to hold or demonstrate a CMMC certification level to be eligible for award under this
solicitation.
Basis for Award:
The Government intends to award a single, firm-fixed-price purchase order on a sole-source basis to the
responsible offeror, Diversified Technical Systems, Inc. (DTS), whose quote conforms to all solicitation
requirements and represents the overall best value to the Government, technical acceptability and price
considered.
The evaluation process will be conducted in the following sequential steps:
1. Technical Validation: Verify that the proposed item is the exact brand-name DTS SLICE6 AIR
Module (P/N: 13006-90910) in new condition, carries the full manufacturer's warranty, and matches
the physical, functional, and performance requirements specified in Attachment 1.
2. Responsibility Determination: The Government will evaluate the apparent successful offeror to
determine responsibility in accordance with RFO Subpart 9.1. This includes verifying that the offeror
has an active registration in the System for Award Management (SAM.gov), does not have any active
exclusions or suspensions, and possesses a satisfactory record of performance, integrity, and business
ethics.
3. Determination of Price Reasonableness: Evaluate and establish price reasonableness in accordance
with RFO 12.204(a) (Commercial Items Price Evaluation) utilizing the price analysis techniques
defined in RFO 15.404-1(b).
Instructions to Offeror:
Offerors must submit a complete quote that conforms to all solicitation requirements. Quotes must be
valid for a minimum of 60 days from the submission deadline.
Submission Method
The quote must be submitted electronically via email to the Contracting Officer, Bethany Hill
(bethany.hill.3@us.af.mil), no later than 1:00 PM Central Time on 14 August 2026. Late quotes will
not be accepted.
Quote Format and Content
To facilitate a timely and efficient evaluation, quotes must be organized into two distinct sections:
Administrative/Price and Technical.
Section I: Administrative & Price
One AFMC…Powering the World’s Greatest Air Force
This volume must contain all pricing information and required administrative representations.
• Company Information: Provide the Company Name, Point of Contact (Name, Phone, Email),
Unique Entity ID (UEI), and CAGE Code.
• System for Award Management (SAM): Confirm active registration in SAM.gov.
• Price Schedule: Submit a total Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) quote for all requested items. The total
FFP must include all applicable costs, including shipping/freight (FOB Destination) to
Holloman AFB, NM:
LIN 0001 (Base): 2 EA - DTS SLICE6 AIR Modules (P/N: 13006-90910), inclusive of
o
standard manufacturer's warranty and shipping.
LIN 1001 (Option): 2 EA - DTS SLICE6 AIR Modules (P/N: 13006-90910), pricing
o
held firm for 365 days post-award.
• Delivery Schedule: State the proposed delivery timeframe in number of Weeks After Receipt of
Order (ARO) for the Base LIN and Option LIN.
Section II: Technical Capability
This volume must include sufficient documentation to verify compliance with the physical and
functional parameters of the requirement:
• OEM Warranty Statement: Confirm that the quoted modules are factory-new and carry the
standard, active manufacturer's product warranty.
• Product Specifications: Submit standard product literature, cut sheets, or technical specification
documents demonstrating that the quoted product meets all physical, functional, and
performance requirements outlined in Attachment 1.
Note: .zip files are not an acceptable format for the Air Force Network and will not go through our email
system.
Attachments:
• Attachment 1 – Specification
• Attachment 2 – SF 1449
BETHANY R. HILL
Contracting Officer

Operating Capacity (FOC). Selecting Eurotech is essential because its advanced
automation delivers equivalent production output using fewer machines.
Alternative solutions requiring more machines necessitate a larger facility
footprint, which would result in an estimated one-time cost of $50,000 for 1,000
sq. ft. of additional floor space and negate the efficiencies of TYAD's planned
layout. The Eurotech solution strictly fits within TYAD's physical space limitations
while preserving crucial room for future expansion.
2. Fleet Commonality, Maintenance, and Sustainment:
TYAD currently possesses an established fleet of Eurotech CNC machines.
Introducing a different brand would break fleet commonality, creating operational
inefficiencies, requiring significant retraining, and increasing the overall
maintenance burden. Conversely, the Eurotech solution's lower machine count
inherently reduces the ongoing maintenance burden, downtime, and lifecycle
costs for TYAD. The quantifiable costs associated with duplicating efforts for a
mixed-brand fleet include:
• One-time retraining for four employees, estimated at $32,000.
• A 4-month delay for implementation and retraining, resulting in a time-
delay impact to the government monetized at $190,000.
• Ongoing annual costs, including an additional $573,000 for two extra
employees required to manage a mixed-brand fleet, and $3,000 for
additional service contracts.
3. Operational Flexibility and Future Capacity: The specific Eurotech combination of
the 20mm Swiss Lathe and the Turning Center provides critical flexibility. This
specific configuration best positions TYAD for advanced, flexible production work
beyond just sUAS motors, ensuring the facility can adapt to future capability
needs.
4. Total Quantifiable Impact: The total estimated dollar impact of selecting an
alternative vendor is approximately $845,000 in the first year alone. Over a five-
year period, the duplicated costs are estimated to be $3,137,000, which will not
be recovered through new competition.

$576,000 (as stated above in Summary of duplicated costs).
2. Use of In-house Resources: TYAD does not currently possess the organic
manufacturing capability, specialized high-speed Swiss lathe machinery, or
automated turning centers required to execute this high-precision micro-
machining requirement internally.
3. Capacity & Throughput Constraints: To meet the program’s critical mission-
essential throughput of units per month at FOC for sUAS motors,
specialized multi-axis automation is mandatory. TYAD's existing in-house
machine shop is fully committed to active depot-level repair and sustainment
missions; attempting to absorb this high-volume production line would
exhaust current organic capacity, create severe bottlenecking, and
compromise the readiness of other high-priority U.S. Army Communications
Electronics Command programs.
4. Alta Enterprises is the authorized representative and exclusive distributor of
Eurotech products in Eastern Pennsylvania. Eurotech utilizes an authorized
regional distribution model for all U.S. Government procurements, which is
pricing-neutral compared to a direct manufacturer purchase as both channels
build in identical baseline costs for training, service, and support. While some
competitors offer centralized "direct" government channels, these divisions
lack localized support structures and function less efficiently than a regional
network. Procuring through Eurotech's authorized local distributor is
operationally critical for the U.S Government, securing a guaranteed 24-hour
on-site technical response time that minimizes production downtime on the
sUAS motor line without the delay or cost of flying in a factory engineer
5. The selection of Alta Enterprises to support the Eurotech machining
infrastructure is justified by the following operational and economic factors:
6. Infrastructure Continuity: TYAD has a well-established Eurotech machining
infrastructure primarily supported by Alta Enterprises. This existing fleet has
allowed TYAD to build a deep, robust baseline of internal expertise in
specialized operations and maintenance.
7. Operational Disruption: Introducing unique, mixed-brand equipment into this
established workflow would disrupt existing shop-floor operations and
severely degrade technical continuity and mission readiness.
8. Non-Recoverable Lifecycle Costs: Open Market alternatives for this action
would duplicate operational and training costs already invested, ultimately

forcing TYAD to accept a solution with higher overall lifecycle costs that
cannot be recovered through competition.
c. Impact/Risks if not approved: Disapproval would result in:
1. Significant program delays while the Government duplicates a costly
comprehensive market intelligence-gathering process already completed by
MxD. A transition to any alternative CNC vendor will introduce an immediate,
non-recoverable four (4) month delay in establishing Tobyhanna Army
Depot’s (TYAD) organic manufacturing capability. This four-month schedule
slippage is the absolute minimum timeline required for the Government to
duplicate the costly and comprehensive market intelligence-gathering,
technical validation, and engineering compatibility assessments already
completed for the Eurotech solution.
2. Duplicating the completed market survey and technical validation process for
an alternative vendor will introduce an immediate four-month production
capability delay at TYAD, directly violating the HQAMC high-rate
manufacturing directive. This 120-day production freeze results in a severe
supply bottleneck of critical sUAS components, directly decreasing combat
mission readiness by delaying the fielding of tactical reconnaissance drones
to deployed units. Ultimately, forcing frontline units to operate without these
organic aerial assets in contested environments creates a critical intelligence
gap, significantly increasing the risk to warfighter life, safety, and operational
survivability.
3. TYAD suffering a loss of efficiency by having to operate and maintain a
mixed-brand fleet, completely duplicating training, setup, and support
expenditures.
4. Approving this justification is essential to maintaining fleet commonality and
successfully meeting the Army's critical, increased production goals for the
sUAS program.
7. Efforts to Obtain Competition: On 18 May 2026, the Tobyhanna Division
contracting officer posted to the governmentwide point of entry a notice of intent to
award a sole source contract to Alta Enterprises and invited interested parties to submit
information regarding their capability to satisfy this requirement. To date, only Alta
Enterprises responded, confirming that they are capable and willing to supply the
machines for the requirement. No other responses were received to the notice of intent
to award a sole source contract. The Contracting Officer has published the notices
required by RFO 5.101 and any bids or proposals received shall be considered.

Advance notice will not be published per 41 U.S.C. § 6101; see attached deviation from the FAR per LCR 7-210 § 3.A.
We made the following efforts to interest potential sources in this award:
This procurement was competed by issuing a solicitation (Solicitation 030ADV26Q0154) to four vendors which the COR identified as
likely able to provide the projector which meets the Library’s requirements. The four vendors were: B&H Foto and Electronics Corp.,
Digital Video Group, Buy Direct & Save, and Proven Projectors.
9. Listing of Sources That Expressed Interest in Writing
The following sources expressed interest in this award:
The Library received one timely proposal from B&H Foto and Electronics Corp.
10. Additional Information
The following additional information is relevant to this justification and approval:
The one proposal received in response to Solicitation 030ADV26Q0154 was evaluated, per the solicitation requirements, to determine
if it met the lowest price technically acceptable evaluation requirements. The Subject matter expert reviewed the proposal from the
only offeror, B&H Foto and Electronics Corp. and determined the proposal to be technically acceptable.
11. Contracting Officer Determination that Price Is Fair and Reasonable
As explained in detail below, I have determined that the prices for this contracting action are fair and reasonable based on comparison of the
prices to the following (see FAR 15.404-1(b)(2)):
Historical prices paid by the Government Published competitive price lists
Library’s Independent Government Estimate Prices obtained through market research
Other: FAR 15.403-1(c)(1)(ii)(A) and FAR 15.403-1(c)(1)(ii)(A)(1) Prices obtained through competitive proposals
The following analysis (based on attached pricing information) supports my determination:
There was adequate price competition, as the Library submitted the solicitation to multiple reputable vendors and received one quote.
By submitting the solicitation to multiple potential offerors, there was a reasonable expectation, that two or more responsible offerors,
competing independently would submit priced offers in response to the requirement, even though only one offer was received (See
FAR 15.403-1(c)(1)(ii)(A). In addition, the CO concluded that the offeror believed at least one other offeror was capable of submitting
a meaningful offer and the offeror had no reason to believe that other potential offerors did not intend to submit an offer, as such the
price is fair and reasonable (See FAR 15.403-1(c)(1)(ii)(A)(1).

Description: 1. ANNOUNCEMENT The United States Coast Guard (USCG), Surface Forces Logistics Center (SFLC), announces its intent to award a sole-source purchase order to Alfa Laval Inc. for an original equipment manufacturer (OEM) operating water cover and driving device vertical for FOP. This action is being conducted under Simplified Acquisition Procedures. 2. Balint Email Address: karla.p.balint@uscg.mil Email Subject Line: Response to Notice of Intent - OEM Fuel Oil Purifier parts Oral submissions will not be accepted. 6. DISCLAIMER The information in this notice is current as of the publication date but is subject to change and is not binding on the government. The government reserves the right to ask clarifying questions to individual companies based on proprietary information submitted without posting those questions publicly.

JUSTIFICATION FOR OTHER THAN FULL AND OPEN COMPETITION (JOFOC)
FOR COMMERCIAL PRODUCTS/SERVICES OVER THE SIMPLIFIED
ACQUISITION THRESHOLD (SAT) USING SIMPLIFIED PROCEDURES
(REVOLUTIONARY FAR OVERHAUL (RFO))
REFERENCE: PR-OCSPP-26-00252; High-resolution accurate mass liquid
chromatography/orbitrap mass spectrometer
1. The EPA – Analytical Chemistry Laboratory, Fort Meade, MD and WTSD - Water and OITA
Branch proposes to restrict competition for this commercial acquisition as authorized by RFO
12.102(b).
2. Nature and/or description of the action being approved: New action using commercial
procedures under GSA schedules to acquire a high-resolution accurate mass liquid
chromatography/orbitrap mass spectrometer.
Item: BRE725572 - Orbitrap Excedion Pro MS system
Vendor: Thermo Electron North American LLC
GSA Contract: 47QSWA21D0055
3. Description of the supplies and/or services required to meet the agency’s needs (including the
estimated value):
High-resolution accurate mass liquid chromatography/orbitrap mass spectrometer that meets
the minimum specifications to provide measurement capabilities for targeted analytes in
supporting their environmental mission. (See Specifications attached below).
The Thermo Scientific™ Orbitrap™ Excedion Pro with EASY-IC is a high-performance,
small-footprint benchtop quadrupole Orbitrap hybrid system that combines a high-capacity
transfer tube capillary, an electrodynamic ion funnel, the most advanced quadrupole
technology, an ion routing multipole, and Orbitrap analyzer. The high field Orbitrap mass
analyzer features high-resolution accurate mass analysis, with and without HCD
fragmentation. The instrument includes the Thermo Scientific™ EASY-IC™ Ion Source
which generates internal calibrant ions for realtime mass calibration of any mass spectrum.
The instrument contains the following:
• OptaMax Plus ion source API inlet source housing with x, y, and z probe positioning,
integrated APCI compatibility, a fixed on-axis view port, and automatically connected
gas and voltage connections ensuring seamless performance and ultimate reliability.
• OptaMax Plus ion source housing includes one HESI spray insert and a calibration
probe.
• Vacuum system pumped by a 6-stage split-flow turbomolecular pump one single stage
turbo pump.
• High-Capacity Transfer Tube and an Electrodynamic Ion Funnel to capture and
efficiently focus ions in a tight beam.
• Resolving injection filter and bent trap to improve robustness and to reduce noise by
preventing neutral and high-velocity clusters from entering the quadrupole mass filter.
• Segmented quadrupole mass filter with rod-switching capabilities for increased
robustness in front of the curved ion trap (C-Trap) with a hyperbolic surface, which
provides excellent peak shape and transmission with a minimum resolution of 0.4
FWHM.
• High-field Orbitrap Mass Analyzer with enhanced FT transient processing resulting in
resolving power from 3,750 up to 480,000 FWHM at m/z 200 and isotopic fidelity, m/z
range of 40-6000 (up to 12,000 with Biopharma edition), and with up to 70 Hz
acquisition speed. Enhanced Dynamic Range (eDR) mode enabling up to 5 orders of
magnitude of intra-scan dynamic range. A TurboTMT mode ions are detected with Phi
SDM processing.
• Ion routing multipole for trapping of ions and higher-energy collisional dissociation.
• Thermo Scientific™ EASY-IC™ Ion Source which generates internal calibrant ions
for real-time mass calibration of any mass spectrum.
• Independent syringe pump which is controlled via the data station for maximum
flexibility.
4. Identification of the statutory authority permitting other than full and open competition:
This noncompetitive action is conducted pursuant to the authority of 41 USC 1901, as
implemented by FAR 12.102(b).
5. Demonstration that the proposed contractor’s unique qualifications or nature of the action
requires use of the authority cited:
The instrument from Thermo Electron North America LLC has patented technology and is the
only instrument on the market capable of generating high-resolution measurements of up to
500,000 FWHM (full width at half maximum) with the option of achieving up to 1,000,000
FWHM at m/z 200 and a sub-1 ppm mass accuracy. The high resolution and accuracy in mass
in sample analysis are essential for reliable identification and confirmation of target pesticides
and environmental contaminants in complex sample metrices. Current analytical instruments
at ACB could not produce high confidence in the sample analyses.
In addition, it is the only instrument that provides high mass resolution and accuracy over a
wide mass range including the small molecule mass range for non-targeted analyses, that are
essential in the screening for and identifying of unknown compounds present in samples. The
detection and identifying of unknown compounds in samples with high confidence would
greatly enhance ACB’s analytical capabilities and benefit the OPP’s missions in general. The
instrument also provides quantitative and qualitative analytical capability in a single platform
and often in a single run while also reliably and routinely delivers sub-ppb sensitivity and sub-
ppm mass accuracy.
6. Description of efforts made to ensure offers are solicited from as many potential sources as is
practicable, including whether a notice was or will be publicized as required by RFO 5 and, if
not, which exception applies:
There is only one responsible source available for the instrument required given the
specifications – Exemption: RFO FAR 5.101(b)(2).
7. Determination by the CO that the anticipated cost to the government will be fair and
reasonable:
The CO determines the anticipated price will be fair and reasonable because the equipment
will be purchased using commercial acquisition procedures for an item that is widely available
in the marketplace to both Government and non-Government customers. The CO will also rely
on the subject matter expertise of the program office’s evaluation team, whose experience,
market research, and general knowledge of the marketplace will allow for an opinion as to
price fairness and reasonableness for this piece of equipment.
8. A description of the market research conducted and results, or the reason market research was
not conducted.
Several research techniques used:
• Researched instruments available through vendors (see market research memo)
No other vendors, except Thermo Electron, were found with an instrument that
o
meets the specifications needed
• Past purchases of mass spectrometers used for similar testing
• Consulted with other federal agencies with similar projects
9. Any other facts supporting using other than full and open competition:
None.
10.A listing of the sources, if any, that expressed in writing an interest in the acquisition:
Only responsible source identified – Thermo Electron summitted a quote.
11.A statement of any actions the agency will take to remove or overcome any future barriers to
competition before any subsequent acquisition for the supplies or services required:
No other actions are available to remove or overcome the barriers to competition given that
only one responsible source has been identified and the vendor holds a patent to the technology
that allows for the specifications needed for the instrument.
12.CO certification:
I certify that this justification is accurate and complete to the best of my knowledge and belief.
Since this effort does not exceed $900,000, this certification serves as approval.

matters.text:
Federal notice (Presolicitation), COMMERCE, DEPARTMENT OF.NATIONAL OCEANIC AND ATMOSPHERIC ADMINISTRATION.DEPT OF COMMERCE NOAA
Title: SOLE SOURCE: YSI Nile Water Level Sensors for the National Ocean Service Engineering Division in Chesapeake, VA.
Solicitation number: 141016-26-0093
PSC: 6640; NAICS: 334513
Description: The National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration�s (NOAA) Acquisition and Grants Office, Eastern Acquisition Division-Kansas City intends to negotiate and award, on a sole source basis, under authority of RFO FAR 6.103-1, with YSI Inc.for Nile custom water level sensors (P/N: 203360) and associated cables as required replacements for the National Ocean Service Engineering Division in Chesapeake, VA. Sole Source Justification: The sole source determination is based on NOAA�s Sole Source Justification. Only one source is capable- The NOAA Nile, FMR51 Design Analysis radar water level sensor, Part Number: 203360 (Formally Series 3611) is CO-OPS standard noncontact primary water level sensor used at environmental monitoring stations on the Atlantic coast, the Gulf of America coast, throughout the Pacific, the Great Lakes, the Caribbean, and in coastal areas of Alaska. The NOAA Nile is a lineof-sight microwave radar instrument that measures range to a target by transmitting a series of pulses, detecting the resulting return echoes, and then using the time of flight of the return pulse to calculate a range to the target. YSI/xylem is the sole manufacturer and sole distributor of the equipment in this purchase. As the manufacture only YSI/xylem has the proprietary rights and knowledge to produce the specialized oceanographic equipment in this purchase. Significant engineering effort was utilized to ensure these sensors not only provide the precise measurements required but also are capable of withstanding the harsh marine environments they are deployed in for extended periods of time and that the power consumption, size, and other characteristics are appropriate for the specialized data acquisition and logging system to which it is connected. This purchase is for spare parts to support monitoring station stations within PORTS� throughout the United States. Implementing different components will result in additional cost and resources. Also, there will be resulting delay for testing, training, and purchase of support equipment. Under the current CO-OPS operating system any environmental monitoring equipment that has not previously been approved must be subjected to a series of tests to ensure the quality of the data and the durability of the equipment for the intended use. These tests usually include bench testing using controlled conditions and physical measurement, controlled environmental testing to check a sensor's reliability under different conditions, and long-term comparison testing with accepted equipment at multiple real-world locations. These tests and the analysis of the resulting data take a large amount of time, money, and resources to conduct. CO-OPS environmental monitoring systems are designed to operate with the components in this purchase. Implementing different components will result in compatibility issues and require extensive system integration efforts. Modifications to the existing infrastructure of the stations would also be necessary to accommodate the new equipment, requiring additional funding and engineering resources. Currently CO-OPS field personal and contractors are trained in the use and maintenance of the systems and components in this purchase. Additional cost will incur from having to train field personal and contractors on the use and maintenance of new equipment. CO-OPS also has the ability and equipment to test, calibrate, and repair the sensors in this purchase. If new sensors are purchased additional parts and equipment will need to be purchased to support the new equipment. Additional training will also be required for those tasked with calibrating and repairing this equipment. This pre-solicitation notice is not a request for competitive proposals and no solicitation package is available. However, firms that believe they can fully meet the government�s requirements may submit substantiating documentation or a request for additional information in writing to the (Contract Specialist) within 15 days after publication of this pre-solicitation notice. Such requests and documentation will be evaluated solely for the purpose of determining whether or not to conduct this procurement on a competitive basis. A determination by the government not to conduct a competitive procurement, based upon responses to this notice, is solely within the discretion of the government. Oral communications are not acceptable in response to this pre-solicitation notice.

2. CONTRACT TITLE: Irradiator for Humanized Mice Core
BACKGROUND:
The VA Maryland Health Care System (VAMHCS) Research and Development (R&D)
Service has received FY26 Lab Animal Major equipment (LAM) funding to establish a
colony of ~400 mice with humanized immune systems. This will allow VAMHCS
scientists to create more relevant animal models for preclinical biomedical research.
Humanized mice enable the study of human immune mechanisms that underlie
diseases disproportionately affect Veterans, including chronic viral infections (e.g, HIV),
cancer, neuroinflammation, age-associated immune dysfunction, Gulf War Illness (GWI)
and PTSD. Thus, humanized mice are crucial for bridging the gap between animal
research and human clinical application, allowing for more accurate, "personalized"
testing of treatments for Veteran-specific health challenges.
4. SCOPE: To create humanized mice, immunodeficient newborn pups will be exposed
to x-ray radiation to irradicate their immune systems. Human CD34+ Hematopoietic
Stem Cells (HSCs), isolated from human cord blood, will then be injected into mice and
this will develop into immune systems which will have 30-70% human characteristics.
Treatments will then be trialed to better understand the molecular scientific mechanisms
of how the disease interacts with the treatment.

matters.text:
Federal notice (Special Notice), DEPT OF DEFENSE.DEPT OF THE AIR FORCE.FA4654 434 CONF LGC
Title: Notice of Intent to Sole Source: Testforce TF300 DOD ATG and TF300 DOD ATG ILS
Solicitation number: F5D0016205A002
PSC: 4920; NAICS: 334515
Description: The 434th Contracting Flight intends to award a firm-fixed-price sole-source contract to Testforce USA Inc. (CAGE: 4L0V9) under the authority of FAR 13.106-1(b)(1), soliciting from a single source for a requirement with an estimated value of $70,000. The Government intends to procure a quantity of Testforce TF-300 DoD Automated Test Generator (ATG) for Instrument Landing Systems (ILS). This includes the test system, proprietary software/procedures, and the associated hardware interface kit. Justification for Sole Source: The Testforce TF-300 is the only system that can meet the Government's requirement. Market research has indicated that Testforce is the only source capable of providing this highly customized equipment for the following reasons: Proprietary Software and Procedures: The required test procedures and specialized setup files were developed by Testforce in direct partnership with the Air Force Flight Standards Agency (AFFSA). These files are proprietary to Testforce, reside on the test unit itself, and are not available from any other vendor, including the original equipment manufacturer (Viavi). Testforce is the only entity that controls and provides required updates to these systems. Unique Hardware Interface Kit: The procurement requires a specific hardware "kit" containing proprietary cables and adapters necessary to interface the test set with the Air Force's CM300/350 and URC-300 radios. This hardware kit was designed by and is exclusively provided by Testforce. System Integration and Standardization: This system is the approved and standardized solution for replacing 8 to 12 obsolete instruments with a single integrated test solution, which is critical for reducing calibration costs, training time, and maintenance complexity in alignment with official Air Force Technical Orders (TOs). This Notice of Intent is not a request for competitive proposals or quotations. A formal solicitation will not be posted. However, all responsible sources may submit a capability statement, proposal, or quotation, which shall be considered by the agency if received by August 25, 2026, at 1:59 PM EDT. Capability statements must provide clear and convincing evidence of the vendor's ability to provide a solution that is 100% compatible with existing Air Force airfield navigational systems and meets the precise specifications of the TF-300 DoD ATG ILS, including the proprietary software and hardware interface kits. Information received will be considered solely for the purpose of determining whether to conduct a competitive procurement. A determination by the Government not to compete this proposed contract based upon responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. Responses must be submitted via email to the Contracting Officer, Jason A. Hahn, jason.hahn.4@us.af.mil, no later than the closing date and time specified above.

2. Description of the Action Being Approved.
Award of a five (5) year firm-fixed-price, Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) contract
for the procurement and sustainment of Inertial Measurement Units (IMU), on a sole source basis to
Northrop Grumman (NG), 21240 Burbank Blvd, Woodland Hills, CA, 91367-6675.
3. Description of Supplies/Services.
The IMU component supports the Raytheon (RTX) family of Electro Optic/Infrared (EO/IR)
Systems, also known as Multi-Spectral Targeting Systems (MTS). NG is the original equipment
manufacturer (OEM) of the IMU. The supplies and services include the procurement of test,
teardown/inspection and evaluation (TT&E), failure analysis and repairs; engineering services;
technical data to support factory repair; and spare assemblies in direct support of MTS,
As MTS OEM,
RTX, subcontracted design and production of the cited components to the respective
developer/manufacturer NG. The anticipated supplies and services will be utilized in the repair and
sustainment support of MTS,
, hereafter referred to as EO/IR
Systems. These systems provide Intelligence Surveillance and Reconnaissance, Detection,
Identification and Targeting capability in day/night operations for both manned and unmanned
platforms. These internal components are key elements of the MTS and have been integrated, tested
and documented as part of the MTS approved configuration by RTX. The procurement of new
IMUs to support upgrades and spares, as well as the TT&E and repairs of these components will
facilitate a shortened overall repair turn-around time of the overarching MTS to increase
availability.

6. Description of Efforts Made to Solicit Offers from as Many Offerors as Practicable.
Informal market research continues to be conducted by NSWC-CR. Market research includes
contacting knowledgeable individuals in the Government and industry, reviewing previous
procurements and in-house contracts, review of catalogs and other product literature, internet
searches and attendance at Industry Trade shows. NSWC-CR representatives maintain a close
working relationship with the Electro-Optics industries throughout the world. This working
relationship with industry provides a base of knowledge as extensive as would normally be obtained
through a formal market survey and facilitates continuous knowledge of the available technologies
and manufacturing capabilities throughout the industry. Based upon the aforementioned background
and working relationship with industry, it is the technical representatives' judgment that there are no

B.3 STATEMENT OF WORK
STATEMENT OF WORK (SOW)
SECTION 1: BACKGROUND
1.1
The U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs and VA Maryland Adaptive Sports programs are
committed to increasing access to recreational and therapeutic activities for Veterans with
disabilities. Participation in adaptive water sports, including kayaking, has been shown to
improve physical health, enhance psychological well-being, and foster social connection.
However, our current water access lacks accessible infrastructure, creating barriers for
individuals with mobility impairment to safely enter and exit watercraft. An adaptive kayak
launch system addresses this gap by providing a stable, user-friendly transfer platform
that promotes independence and safety.
SECTION 2: II PURPOSE
2.1 PRODUCT, SERVICE OR OUTCOME NEEDED.
What will the vendor do? Delivery, installation, assembly, start up?
The purpose of this project is to procure and install an adaptive kayak launch system that
ensures equitable access to kayaking opportunities for Veterans and other individuals with
disabilities.
This initiative aims to:
• Increase participation in adaptive sports and outdoor recreation
• Promote physical rehabilitation and mental health recovery
• Enhancing independence and confidence among participants
• Support inclusive programming aligned with VA Adaptive Sports objectives
The contractor/vendor shall provide a fully functional adaptive kayak launch system,
including all necessary components for safe and accessible water entry and exit. The
system should be compliant with Americans with Disabilities Act standards and
suitable for use by individuals with varying levels of mobility.
The adaptive kayak launch system shall include, at a minimum:
• Transfer bench or seating system designed for lateral transfers
• Stabilized kayak support structure to prevent tipping during entry/exit
• Handrails and support features for safety and independence
• Adjustable or floating dock compatibility (if applicable)
• Durable, weather-resistant materials suitable for long-term outdoor use
• Weight capacity sufficient to accommodate diverse users and adaptive equipment
• Compatibility with multiple kayak types, including adaptive kayaks
INSTALLATION & SITE PREPARATION
The contractor shall:
• Provide all labor, materials, and equipment necessary for installation
• Ensure integration with existing dock or shoreline infrastructure
• Comply with all local, state, and federal safety and environmental regulations
TRAINING & DOCUMENTATION
The contractor shall provide:
• On-site training for staff on safe operation and participant assistance
• User manuals and maintenance guidelines
• Safety protocols and recommended usage procedures
MAINTENANCE & WARRANTY
• Provide manufacturer warranty information
• Outline recommended maintenance schedule
• Offer optional service agreement for ongoing maintenance and repairs
2.2 SCOPE OF THE PRODUCT, SERVICE, OR OUTCOME.
• Increased Veteran participation in adaptive kayaking programs
• Improved accessibility to waterfront recreational activities
• Enhanced therapeutic outcomes related to physical and mental health
• Strengthened community partnerships and inclusive recreation opportunities
• The ADA-accessible EZ Dock kayak launch will benefit a wide range of veterans
with spinal cord injuries, amputations, multiple sclerosis, stroke, traumatic brain
injury, Parkinson’s disease, balance disorders, chronic pain, arthritis, joint
replacements, and other service-connected disabilities to participate in adaptive
kayaking. The launch also supports aging veterans and those who use
wheelchairs, walkers, canes, or prosthetic limbs by reducing transfer challenges
and fall risk. By improving accessibility and independence, the ADA-compliant EZ
Dock kayak launch enables more veterans to safely engage in therapeutic
recreation, physical activity, and social participation, regardless of their functional
limitations while also updating the VA equipment to be ADA Compliant
3. VA POINT OF CONTACT FOR TECHNICAL QUESTIONS:
• VA POC: Lauren Buckingham – Email: Lauren.Buckingham@va.gov.
• VA POC: Jeter Francine – Email: Frencine.Jeter@va.gpov.
4. PLACE OF PERFORMANCE.
Perry Point VA Medical Center
Avenue D & 8th Street
Perry Point, MD 21902
5. PERIOD OF PERFORMANCE: Delivery is expected within 60 days ARO.
6. INVOICING: Contractor shall submit a consolidated invoice monthly in arrears of the
month for which services are being billed. One all-inclusive monthly invoice shall be
provided, which shall contain an invoice number, contract number, obligations order
number, and an itemized list of services provided. An acceptable master (all-inclusive)
itemized list of services shall be agreed to between the Contractor and the COR prior to
submission of the first invoice.
All invoices from the contractor shall be submitted electronically in accordance with VAAR
Clause 852.232-72 Electronic Submission of Payment Requests.

Services Center (FSC) uses a third-party contractor, Tungsten, to transition vendors from
paper to electronic invoice submission. Please go to this website to begin submitting

http://www.tungsten-network.com/US/en/veterans-affairs/.
More information on the VA FSC is available at: http://www.fsc.va.gov/einvoice.asp.

Mice Core
3. BACKGROUND: The VA Maryland Health Care System (VAMHCS) Research and
Development (R&D) Service has received FY26 Lab Animal Major equipment
(LAM) funding to establish a colony of ~400 mice with humanized immune
systems. This will allow VAMHCS scientists to create more relevant animal models
for preclinical biomedical research. Humanized mice enable the study of human
immune mechanisms that underlie diseases disproportionately affect Veterans,
including chronic viral infections (e.g, HIV), cancer, neuroinflammation, age-
associated immune dysfunction, Gulf War Illness (GWI) and PTSD. Thus,
humanized mice are crucial for bridging the gap between animal research and
human clinical application, allowing for more accurate, "personalized" testing of
treatments for Veteran-specific health challenges.
4. SCOPE: To house immunodeficient humanized mice, rooms BB-117 and BB-113
within the former Bio Safety Level III area of the Research and Development
Veterinary Medical Unit will be operating as a Bio Safety Level II unit with positive
air pressure and house 2 Individually Vented Cage (IVC) Rack Systems. IVCs pull
air from the room passing it through HEPA filters and then through hoses to each
individual animal cage. The purpose of these systems is to ensure a high level of
biological containment by preventing cross contamination and disease transmission
between animals. Commercially available IVCs contain anywhere from 120-160
cages each with 60-80 cages on each side. Cages house 1-3 mice each depending
on the operating procedures of the animal facility.
The VAMHCS R&D humanized mice core will house ~400 necessitating 2 IVC
racks with 120-160 cages each (racks with 60 cages on each side will total 120 per
rack, racks with 80 cages per side will total 160).

to the Allentown NexGen Mouse IVCs:

N. Green Street – BB-117 and BB-113, Baltimore, MD 21201
5. PERFORMANCE MONITORING: COR will inspect the cage rack system upon delivery
with the animal facility manager and the subject matter expert and inform the vendor of
any deficiencies.
6. SECURITY REQUIREMENTS: N/A
No special security requirements are necessary
7. GOVERNMENT-FURNISHED EQUIPMENT (GFE)/GOVERNMENT-FURNISHED
INFORMATION (GFI). No special security requirements are necessary.
8. OTHER PERTINENT INFORMATION OR SPECIAL CONSIDERATIONS.
a. Identification of Possible Follow-on Work. N/A

c. Identification of Non-Disclosure Requirements. N/A
d. Packaging, Packing and Shipping Instructions.
The COR and vendor will discuss any special requirements for shipping and set up. Items
will be packaged and itemized on all invoices. The equipment will be delivered to the main
receiving dock at 10 N Greene St, the dock is approximately 4 feet high, 10 feet deep, and
20 feet wide-
A box truck is recommended for delivery rather than a semi-trailer because of the
navigation to the dock from the street. Upon delivery the components of the IVC Rack
Systems will be unloaded and unpacked, positioned in rooms BB-117 and BB-113 then
assembled. Usage training will then be provided.
e. Inspection and Acceptance Criteria.

(NBK) Environmental that lists all hazardous materials (HM) being used on the installation for the project and an
estimated quantity of each amount being used. The CHMI shall be accompanied by all relevant Safety Data Sheets
(SDSs). Once approved by NBK Environmental, the HM is authorized for use on the installation. The Contractor
must keep the CHMI and associated SDSs with them on-site where the work is being performed. All containers of

agent), Class I and II Ozone Depleting Substances (ODS), radioactive materials or instruments capable of producing

3.2.1. The Government shall determine if waste is hazardous or non-hazardous. A Waste Information Sheet (WIS)
will be completed for each hazardous waste prior to start of work.
3.2.2. A trained individual from the Government shop with a current Waste Originator certification must be present,
during normal business hours for any hazardous waste produced.

PREPARATION FOR DELIVERY (COMMERCIALLY PACKAGED ITEMS)
(a) Preservation, packaging, and packing shall be in accordance with ASTM-D-3951 (most current edition), "Standard for Commercial Packing." The
unit pack quantity that applies to items under this contract is "Industry Standard".
(b) Prohibited Packing Materials. The use of asbestos, excelsior, loose fill polystyrene, newspaper or shredded paper (all types including waxed paper,
computer paper and similar hydroscopic or non-neutral material) is prohibited.
(c) Non-Manufactured Wood Packing. All non-manufactured wood utilized in wood pallets and wood containers shall be heat treated to a minimum
core temperature of 56 degrees centigrade for 30 minutes and certified by an accredited agency recognized by the American Lumber Standards
Committee (ALSC). Refer to https://www.aphis.usda.gov/aphis/ourfocus/planthealth/import-information/wood-packaging-material for wood packing
policy, enforcement regulations and accredited agencies. Non-coniferous (hardwood) and manufactured wood, such as particleboard and plywood, are
exempt from this requirement.
(d) Manufactured wood, such as particleboard and plywood, are exempt from this requirement.
(e) Packing must be sufficient to ensure safe delivery to the final destination without the need for additional repackaging or repair.
(f) All materials shall be packed to withstand multiple modes of transport (truck, rail, sea, or air) and handling by forklifts or cranes.
(g) Heavy items must be crated or skid-mounted to distribute weight evenly and ensure lifting point are accessible and marked.
(h) Packages must be stable, not exceed safe stacking limits, and be secured against movement in transit.
MARKING OF SHIPMENTS (COMMERCIALLY PACKAGED ITEMS)
(i) Marking shall be in accordance with ASTM-D-3951 (most current edition) and with the information set forth in paragraph (ii) below. Unless
specified elsewhere in this contract/order, bar coding is not required.
(ii) All unit and exterior containers/packs shall, as a minimum, be marked as follows:
1. National stock number (NSN), when available, or
Federal stock number (FSN), when NSN is not available, or
part number when neither NSN or FSN are available.
2. Noun nomenclature cited on contract or order.
3. Quantity and unit of issue.
4. Contract, or order number.
5. From:_______________________________________________
(Contractor's Name)
_______________________________________________
(Address)
6. To: (See delivery address on page 3-4 or in Section F)
(iii) Markings may be applied by any means which provide legibility.
TRACEABLE FREIGHT
The Contractor shall assume all responsibility for shipment to the specified destination. Shipment must be via a fully traceable commercial freight
method. Traceable freight means that the shipment is registered upon shipment with an identifying number. The number is for location of the
shipment at any point in transit, including final destination, and verifies shipment arrival at the specified destination. If a shipping method does not
provide traceability as defined above, it shall not be used.
INSPECTION AND ACCEPTANCE (DESTINATION)
Inspection and acceptance of the supplies or services to be furnished hereunder shall be made at destination by the receiving activity.
PROOF OF DELIVERY
If United Parcel Service (UPS) or Federal Express services are used for transportation, each package must have a unique package identification
number. The Government will not consider the manifest as proof of delivery unless each package can be uniquely identified. Acceptance will occur
only after the Government can verify actual receipt of the contract items--packaged, marked and labeled as required elsewhere in this contract.

Title: Intent to Sole Source � Fairbanks Morse LLC � LT Water Connecting Box Assembly
Solicitation number: N0040626Q0448
PSC: 1610; NAICS: 336413
Description: Fleet Logistics Center Puget Sound (FLCPS) intends to solicit on a sole source basis for LT Water Connection Assembly (OEM Fairbanks Morse, LLC P/N PA12650721). This requirement is a sole source procurement to Fairbanks Morse, LLC, the Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM), for a direct replacement LT Water Connection Assembly. The required part is proprietary to the OEM and must maintain the original form, fit, and function of the existing system. The use of substitute or non-OEM parts could adversely affect the reliability, performance, and operational readiness of the equipment. Accordingly, only Fairbanks Morse, LLC can provide the required OEM part that meets the Government's minimum technical requirements. Interested entities may identify their interest and capability to respond to the requirement, which will be considered solely for the purpose of determining whether to conduct a competitive procurement. A determination not to compete this action based upon responses received to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. Quotes will be evaluated in accordance with RFO 12.203. The Government will select the most advantageous offer based on the following evaluation factors: technical including delivery date, price, and past performance in no order of relative importance. Anticipated Award Date: August 2026 Contracting Officer: Anna Rose M. Fulton annarose.m.fulton.civ@us.navy.mil

matters.title: Notice of Intent to Sole Source USAFA Autoclave System and Reverse Osmosis System
matters.text:
Federal notice (Special Notice), DEPT OF DEFENSE.DEPT OF THE AIR FORCE.FA7000  10 CONS LGC
Title: Notice of Intent to Sole Source USAFA Autoclave System and Reverse Osmosis System
Solicitation number: USAFAAutoclaveSystemandReverseOsmosisSystem 
PSC: 6640; NAICS: 339113
Description: The United States Air Force Academy (USAFA) intends to award a sole-source, Firm-Fixed-Price contract to Getinge USA Sales, LLC (Getinge) under the simplified procedures for commercial products in accordance with RFO Part 12. The proposed North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) Code is 339113 (Surgical Appliance and Supplies Manufacturing). Requirement: The USAFA Dean of Faculty Department of Biology (DFBI) requires the lifecycle replacement of one Autoclave System and one Reverse Osmosis (RO) System for use by over 800 Cadets per year for critical daily operations, including sterilizing materials for classes and research and processing biohazardous waste. The systems must meet the following salient characteristics: Steam Sterilizer System (Autoclave) Quantity: One (1) new system Chamber volume: At least 275L Gravity Cycles: Capable of 110C � 135C temperatures Vacuum Cycles: Capable of 110C � 135C temperatures Liquid Cycles: Capable of 104C � 135C temperatures Exterior Dimensions (W x H x D): Close to 30� x 74� x 48� Configuration: Freestanding unit Utilities: Integrated electric steam generator with 480V AC, 60Hz, 3-phase electrical requirements; sterilizer control with 115V AC, 60Hz, 1-phase electrical requirements Control Interface: Touchscreen interface and a PACS 3500 Programmable Logic Controller with preprogrammed cycles Safety Features: Chamber safety interlock and steam safety valves to protect against over pressurization Reverse Osmosis (RO) Water Treatment System Quantity: One (1) new system Configuration: Wall-mounted system with associated bladder tank Utilities: 115V, 60Hz, 1-phase electrical requirements Capacity: Capability to produce up to 400 gallons per day of RO water Rough Dimensions (L x W x D): Close to 38� x 26� x 7� Filter Elements: 3 pre-filters and single membrane Bypass: Manual bypass capability Feeder: Polyphosphate feeder cartridge Removal and Installation Services Deinstallation, removal, and complete haul-away of the Department's existing Autoclave and RO systems. Turnkey installation, final utility connections, calibration, and startup testing of the new system. Justification: In accordance with RFO 12.102(a), the Government has determined that only one source is reasonably available to fulfill this requirement. Market research and responses to a prior Request for Information (RFI) confirmed that alternative manufacturer models that meet the minimum 275L chamber volume are physically too large to fit into the laboratory room�s highly restricted, pre-built spatial footprint. Getinge is the only known manufacturer whose 275L unit complies with the strict physical room dimensions. Additionally, DFBI currently has an active preventative maintenance and service contract with Getinge for other departmental laboratory autoclaves. Standardizing on Getinge equipment allows the Government to integrate this new system under the existing active maintenance contract immediately. This standardizes training for laboratory technicians and biological safety personnel, ensures immediate compatibility of replacement parts, and reduces administrative and logistical overhead by avoiding the management of multiple service contracts. To prevent unacceptable supply chain, installation, and biological safety certification risks, the Government requires this procurement to be executed directly with Getinge USA Sales, LLC to guarantee OEM-certified utility connections, check-out, and warranty integration. Disclaimer: This notice of intent is not a request for competitive quotations, and a formal solicitation will not be issued. However, any responsible source that believes it can meet these requirements may submit a capability statement. Information received will be considered solely for the purpose of determining whether to conduct a competitive procurement. A determination not to compete this action is solely within the discretion of the Government. Responses: Submit capability statements electronically to Nicole Cibula at nicole.cibula@us.af.mil and Amy Krause at amy.krause.1@us.af.mil by 11:00 AM (MDT) on 7 August 2026.

No BAA price penalties or restrictions will be applied to UK-origin bids. Refer to the attached solicitation PDF for all applicable foreign-acquisition clauses. Offerors must declare their product's country of origin in their quote. 5. matters.title: Notice of Intent to Sole Source Gasmet
matters.text:
Federal notice (Special Notice), DEPT OF DEFENSE.DEFENSE HEALTH AGENCY (DHA).DEFENSE HEALTH AGENCY
Title: Notice of Intent to Sole Source Gasmet
Solicitation number: HT9427-26-JC-8426
PSC: 6640; NAICS: 334516
Description: The Defense Health Agency Contracting Activity (DHACA) intends to award a Firm Fixed Price (FFP) sole source contract on behalf of the Defense Health Agency (DHA) Defense Centers for Public Health � Aberdeen (DCPH-A) to Gasmet for a Model GT5000 Terra Portable multi-gas analyzer, under the authority GSAR 538.7104-3(b)(1)(ii): Only one source is capable of providing the products, services, or solution required at the level of quality required because the products, services or solutions are unique or highly specialized. The Gasmet Model GT5000 Terra Portable multi-gas analyzer possesses patented and proprietary features that are functionally essential to the DHA and Department of War (DoW) industrial hygiene mission, and these features are exclusively available from Gasmet. The proposed contractor is uniquely qualified because they are the sole developer and Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) of the patented GICOR interferometer and non-hygroscopic optical systems used in this device. There are no authorized third-party manufacturers that can produce or modify competing equipment to replicate Gasmet�s specific zero-purge and active-movement capabilities. Gasmet is the only reasonable source because the GT5000 Terra is the only commercially available, backpack-portable Fourier Transform Infrared (FTIR) analyzer that can be operated while actively moving without signal degradation or requiring logistical tail support. The lack of competition is supported by the following proprietary capability, patented vibration resistance and zero-purge logistics. The proprietary GICOR interferometer utilizes a highly symmetric mirror layout that eliminates interference from physical vibration. Competing FTIR systems require the operator to remain completely stationary to achieve accurate readings. Market research indicates that while other companies manufacture portable FTIR analyzers, their products lack essential features such as portability and zero field-purging. Competing brands either weigh significantly more, reducing the time a responder can operate in heavy Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) or utilize standard interferometers that lose calibration when bumped or moved. Since Gasmet holds the patents on the specific hardware geometry and coatings that solve these operational problems, competing products cannot be physically modified to meet the agency's field operation needs. The DoW/DHA currently utilizes Gasmet's proprietary Calcmet software ecosystem and its extensive library of chemical spectra. Procuring the Gasmet GT5000 Terra ensures 100% data interoperability with existing Gasmet systems, such as the legacy DX4040 or stationary units that are already fielded across the enterprise. Procuring a different brand would force the Government to forego its established baseline of spectral data, invest in entirely new software requiring approval, and spend critical financial resources retraining industrial hygienists and first responders on a non-standardized platform. Failure to approve this sole source justification will result in a direct and severe degradation of the DHA�s emergency response and industrial hygiene field survey capabilities, potentially increasing health and safety risks to the warfighter. If forced to procure a competing system without Gasmet's proprietary technology, DoW personnel will face detrimental effects to include, delayed triage and response and logistical vulnerabilities. This is a notice of intent to issue a contract on a sole source basis. This notice of intent is NOT a request for quotations (RFQ). Any other firms desiring consideration must fully identify their interest in and capability to provide these services to the individual listed below. A determination by the Government not to compete this proposed contract based upon responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. Interested persons may identify their interest in writing, to the Government point of contact. Responses to this notice must be received no later than 3:00 PM Eastern Standard Time, 19 August 2026. The point of contact for this action is James Cheng, james.cheng1.civ@health.mil.

matters.title: Notice of Intent to Sole Source and Sources Sought: Counter-small Unmanned Aerial Systems (C-sUAS) for the Amphibious Combat Vehicle (ACV)
matters.text:
Federal notice (Combined Synopsis/Solicitation), DEPT OF DEFENSE.DEPT OF THE NAVY.COMMANDER
Title: Notice of Intent to Sole Source and Sources Sought: Counter-small Unmanned Aerial Systems (C-sUAS) for the Amphibious Combat Vehicle (ACV)
Solicitation number: M67854-26-I-0225
PSC: 5810; NAICS: 334511
Description: NOTICE OF INTENT TO SOLE SOURCE AND SOURCES SOUGHT Portfolio Acquisition Executive � Marine Corps Program Manager Advanced Amphibious Assault M67854-26-I-0225 03 August 2026 Program Manager Advanced Amphibious Assault (PM AAA), within the Portfolio Acquisition Executive � Marine Corps (PAE-MC), intends to negotiate and award on a sole-source basis in accordance with 10 United States Code (U.S.C.) �3204 (a)(1), as implemented by the Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 6.103-1, for Non-kinetic Attack Counter-small Unmanned Aerial Systems (C-sUAS) Packages developed by Anduril Industries, Inc. (Anduril), 1400 Anduril, Costa Mesa, CA 92626, which will be incorporated into the Amphibious Combat Vehicle (ACV) Fleet of Vehicles (FoV). The Government seeks to acquire the Pulsar Lite MKI- RX/TX 4CH (Pulsar-L) and required accessories for its operation, including the Anduril Control Station Interface, Omnidirectional Antenna Array, Standard EW Software License, and Warranty and Support, through the ACV C-sUAS Contract. In addressing the Marine Corps requirement for an ACV C-sUAS Package, the Marine Corps Capabilities Development Directorate (MCCDC) directs that �Enclosure (1) provides the materiel requirement, concept of employment, and distribution plan.� That enclosure identifies the Anduril Pulsar-L as the only viable solution to meet the requirements established in the Urgent Statement of Need (USON), implementing the Urgent Universal Needs Statement (UUNS). The MCCDC states that the Marine Corps� use of the Anduril Pulsar-L will mitigate and close several capability gaps posed by current ACV FOV. Part of the ACV C-sUAS requirement is to provide a mobile and organic means to detect, track, identify, and defeat of Group 1 and 2 sUAS threats, to complement existing enterprise C-sUAS systems, and coordinate with Service-level capabilities to support a layered defense approach reliability in a deployed environment. The Army�s existing contracts for vehicular C-sUAS solutions incorporates the Anduril Pulsar-L Packages to support the stated threshold and objective requirements with an Other Than Full and Open Competition Justification and Approval (JA-26-DC3oE-0038) dated 05 March 2026. In its solicitation for the ACV C-sUAS, the Marine Corps will require Offerors to propose a C-sUAS Compliance Roadmap, with a clear path to meet the implementation and certification of the ACV C-sUAS solution, currently specified as threshold and objective requirements. The Government intends to procure ACV C-sUAS Packages through a Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) Delivery Order issued under an Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) contract for Non-Developmental Items. The Government requires the following for the ACV C-sUAS threshold capability: A platform-integrated omni-directional ES/EA based C-sUAS combined sensor/jammer package to detect, track, identify, and defeat radio frequency dependent (GNSS and RF�controlled) Group 1 and Group 2 UAS. Detection at long ranges, from two (2) to five (5) kilometers (km). Provide a trigger signal to externally enable jamming of sUAS at a range of two (2) km. Ability to simultaneously engage multiple UASs and execute the full kill-chain (detect, track, identify, and defeat) while the ACV is static or on the move. Ability to rapidly identify and respond to emerging UAS technologies and tactics without frequent updates to predefined threat analysis libraries. Ability to reliably operate and survive in both land and maritime/littoral environments. Ability to integrate onto the ACV platform, addressing Size, Weight, and Power considerations. The solution must not exceed the limited amount of space claim nor weight claim available in the ACV FoV which has been allotted for a C-sUAS solution. The Government will not disclose the threshold requirements of either the space claim or weight claim. Possess a Ground Control System (GCS) that is intuitive, lightweight, and resilient. The vendor must process the ability to manufacture the requirement of over fifty (50) C-sUAS Packages within twelve (12) months, and the ability to regularly deliver units to support the Government�s rapid integration schedule of the ACV FoV beginning in first quarter Fiscal Year 2027. The Government requires the following for the ACV C-sUAS objective capability: Commercial or non-developmental solution. Provide a trigger signal to externally enable jamming of sUAS at ranges farther than two (2) km, with GNSS jamming. The objective space claim requirement is one (1) box when fully integrated. The objective weight claim requirement is 35 lbs or less when fully integrated. The GCS should be compatible or configurable to operate using pre-existing ACV displays or devices via plugin, application, or software installation. Interested vendors possessing the requisite skills, resources, and capabilities necessary to meet the stated requirements are invited to respond to this SSN via a submission of an executive summary on 8-1/2 x 11 in paper, no more than five (5) pages in length (including cover pages), using 12-point font describing product summary, complete technical characteristics, and spare parts support capability. Respondents are requested to provide information that fully demonstrates their ability to manufacture and deliver an ACV C-sUAS capability which meets or exceeds the specifications stated above. This response shall include a product summary and any currently available technical data and reports to support the capability statement. Interested Offerors should describe their ability to meet the anticipated requirements in support of this effort. All responses shall include the following information: a) Company name, address, email, telephone number, point(s) of contact; b) Commercial and Government Entity (CAGE) Code and Unique Entity Identifier (UEI); c) Size of business pursuant to North American Industrial Classification System (NAICS) code 334511; d) Vendor�s response to all information stated herein and describing all capabilities and relevant past performance; e) The current availability of commercial and non-developmental solutions, or, if none exist, estimated lead times to design, manufacture, test, and deliver a solution, including timelines for these major categories of activity; f) A list of Government contracting vehicles (if available); g) Any relevant testing data and supporting documents for available solutions submitted as attachments to the executive summary (does not count towards the page limit stated above); and h) Identification of any unique requirements anticipated to provide these supplies to the Government (e.g. financing terms; availability of essential raw materials; requirements for efficient manufacturing during production of the supplies; the use of advanced manufacturing technology, processes and systems; special equipment or use of modern technology production equipment; use of commercial manufacturing processes; expanded use of commercial items or non-developmental items; technical data and computer software deliverables and associated license rights). Please be advised that any proprietary information must be marked as such on a page-by-page basis. The Government will not assume that any of the information provided by a respondent is proprietary unless it is conspicuously marked on each page containing proprietary information. Moreover, the Government does not assume any duty to contact a respondent and inquire whether any unmarked information submitted in response to this SSN is proprietary. Responses shall be submitted via e-mail to Jessica Hathaway Contracting Officer at jessica.hathaway@usmc.mil and Matthew Mercer, Contract Specialist at matthew.mercer@usmc.mil, no later than 10:00 AM local time Quantico, VA on 18 August 2026, 1500 Local Time, Quantico, Virginia, with the subject line �NOI and SSN � PM AAA C-sUAS � M67854-26-I-0225.� Inquiries by telephone will not be accepted.

including delivery date, price, and past performance in no order of relative importance.

performance work statement, if any. It will be assumed that any quote without mention of any exceptions will take no exception from all
specifications, terms and conditions, clauses, or provisions within the solicitation."
6. SINGLE AWARD FOR ALL ITEMS: Due to the interrelationship of supplies and/or services to be provided hereunder, the Government
reserves the right to make a single award to the quoter whose quote is considered in the best interest of the government, price and other factors
considered. Therefore, quoters who quote less than the entire effort specified herein may be determined to be unacceptable.
