Description: Page 1 of 5 DEPARTMENT OF VETERANS AFFAIRS Justification and Approval For Exception to Fair Opportunity Memo Acquisition Plan Action ID: 36C245-26-AP-4181 Contracting Activity: Department of Veterans Affairs VA Maryland Health Care System (VAMHCS) 10 N. Greene Street Baltimore, MD 21201 2237#512-26-3-056-0269 Description of Action: The VA Maryland Health Care System needs to procure a new Command & Control Audio-Visual system to support their critical Emergency Management obligations. This justification supports a new sole-source procurement for the acquisition through Thundercat Technologies, integration, and installation of audiovisual, video-wall, routing, collaboration, control, and emergency operations technology for the Baltimore VA Emergency Operations Center (Room 3A-300). This purchase will also include diagram system drawings, system testing and all training support and maintenance. This A/V system must also be integrated with the Facility Notification System for Emergency broadcast capabilities within conference room (3A-300). This system is crucial for first touch to host and interface with dignitaries, medical staff, lifesaving and life safety training and education operations. Description of Supplies or Services: The VA seeks to procure and integrate a comprehensive, mission-critical audiovisual and command-and-control system upgrade for the Baltimore VA EOC. The work includes design, installation, programming, commissioning, and sustainment of: A 19 x 5.5 dvLED video wall Three 86" displays Haivision Alpha Core processing and routing architecture Crestron-based control systems Integrated audio systems (BiAmp Tesira) VTC infrastructure, KVM systems, workstations, tuners, and associated equipment Equipment racks, lecterns, and supporting components These requirements are fully defined in the Statement of Work Baltimore VA EOC.pdf, including detailed technical specifications, room configurations, media routing dependencies, audio system requirements, and integration constraints. The procurement estimate is $466,798.71. The projected POP will be 1 August 2026 Through 31 Dec 2026. Statutory Authority: The statutory authority permitting an exception to fair opportunity is Section 41 U.S.C. 4106(c) as implemented by the Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 16.505(b)(2)(i): ( ) FAR 16.505(b)(2)(i)(A): The agency need for the supplies or services is so urgent that providing a fair opportunity would result in unacceptable delays. ( X ) FAR 16.505(b)(2)(i)(B): Only one awardee is capable of providing the supplies or services required at the level of quality required because the supplies or services ordered are unique or highly specialized. ( ) FAR 16.505(b)(2)(i)(C): The order must be issued on a sole-source basis in the interest of economy and efficiency because it is a logical follow-on to an order already issued under the contract, provided that all awardees were given a fair opportunity to be considered for the original order. ( ) FAR 16.505(b)(2)(i)(D): It is necessary to place an order to satisfy a minimum guarantee. ( ) FAR 16.505(b)(2)(i)(E): For orders exceeding the simplified acquisition threshold, a statute expressly authorizes or requires that the purchase be made from a specified source . The statutory authority permitting an exception to fair opportunity for this action is 38 U.S.C. 8127(c), known as the Veterans First Contracting Program which provides the authority to directly contract with a Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB) or a Veteran-Owned Small Business (VOSB). Rationale Supporting Use of Authority Cited Above: Thundercat Technology can also meet the following system requirements: Demonstrate the capability to provide Command and Control system that will conform and align with technology standards established by the VA Cyber Security Operations Centers (CSOC) located in Martinsburg, WV, Hines, IL, and Austin, TX. Provide proof that their proposed system meets and integrates with the standards and operational practices used by the EOCs/ICCs in Tampa and Orlando (and the Electronic Health Records Management System (EHRMS) Command Center at VACO). Supplied Command and Control A/V system must contain an architecture that allows for the real time collaboration of the Common Operating Picture from EOC/ICC space to other locations within the medical centers or to other hospitals with in the VISN and/or across the country (including VACO IOC as needed) using the Haivision Network Site-Sharing package. Vendor must be able to provide Seamless integration with facility-wide emergency notification and messaging systems, including BrightSign-based workflows already deployed in other VA environments Using them exclusivity, ensures that the VA Maryland Health Care System receives the exact same proprietary soft/hardware programming and updates and support directly from the vendor. Using Thundercat Technologies prevents substantial duplicate costing as another vendor would be required to completely start over to research, program, and re-implement the highly Specialized infrastructure. Efforts to Obtain Competition: A description of efforts made to ensure that offers are solicited from as many potential sources as is practicable. Review of Prior Market Research and Historical Purchasing Data Program personnel evaluated historical VA procurements of similar audiovisual, command-and-control, and EOC technology systems. Review of internal documentation, including prior sole source justifications located in Atch 1 Open Market Sole Source Justification, demonstrated that only highly specialized integrators with Haivision, Crestron, BiAmp, and dvLED engineering credentials have successfully delivered comparable systems at VA sites. Consultation With Technical Experts and Contracting Personnel Internal coordination with technical experts and Contracting Office staff (referenced in communications such as the email from FW: ThunderCat Technology's MRR to VA Baltimore for EOC/ICC and Technology Modernization Project) confirmed that no additional SDVOSB vendors had expressed capability or interest in performing a project of this complexity or scale. Engineering and program personnel reviewed ThunderCat s unique OEM partner ecosystem, prior VA EOC installations, and system architecture dependencies documented in the SOW. Assessment of Potential SDVOSB Alternatives The VA evaluated whether other SDVOSB firms possessed: Required Haivision Alpha Core processor expertise Crestron Certified Programmer capabilities Proven past performance integrating multi-vendor routing, A/V, KVM, VTC, and audio DSP systems Prior VA emergency operations center deployment experience No alternative SDVOSB source met these combined technical thresholds. Conclusion All reasonable efforts were made to solicit interest and assess potential competition. Market research, historical data, internal SME review, and prior justification materials confirm that only ThunderCat Technology can meet the Baltimore VA EOC s specialized technical, operational, and compatibility requirements. Efforts to broaden future competition are documented in Atch 1 Open Market Sole Source Justification.docx, which notes VA s commitment to reviewing OEM ecosystems, market capabilities, and opportunities for competitive follow-on acquisitions. Actions to Increase Competition: Describe actions taken, or that will be taken, to remove or overcome any barriers to competition before initiating any subsequent acquisitions for the supplies, or services required, including challenges to restrictive data markings, data rights, preparation of a performance-based work statement, and etc. The VA will continue to: Review evolving OEM partner ecosystems Evaluate potential open competition for future lifecycle refreshes Reassess market capabilities at each procurement stage This sole-source is limited strictly to the minimum required to meet urgent operational needs. Title: 6520-3D Shape Scanner (Brand Name or Equal)

PSC: 6520; NAICS: 339114
Award:
Description: 1. Title: Dental 3D Shape Scanner (Brand name or Equal) 2. Purpose: The Network Contracting Office (NCO) 16, located at Galleria Financial Center, 5075 Westheimer Rd, Ste 750, Houston, TX 77030, hereby issues the following Sources Sought to Request Information (RFI) with the intent of determining the contractor interest, capabilities, qualifications of potential businesses, nonmanufacturer rule compliance, Buy American Act compliance, Trade Agreement compliance and estimated industry pricing information for market research and estimated budgetary purpose to provide the Dental 3D Shape Scanner. Contractor shall provide all necessary labor, materials, supplies, equipment, and transportation to provide the Dental 3D Shape Scanner in accordance with the Draft SOW. This Sources Sought is published for market research purposes. This Sources Sought will be used to determine if a set-aside for any small business program is appropriate. Government anticipates competitive, firm fixed price task order if on a Federal Supply Schedule (FSS) or firm fixed price purchase order if �open market�. Please review this announcement, respond to questions below and review all attachments in their entirety. Government requests that interested offerors complete all questions below, provide required documentation, descriptive literature and/or authorization letter as described below. The Government is in no way obligated to do business with or to enter any form of contract with any person, firm or other entity that receives or responds to this announcement. 3. Objective: To find qualified contractors with the capability to provide the Dental 3D Shape Scanner for the Michael E. DeBakey VA Medical Center located in Houston, TX. 4. Place of Performance: Michael E DeBakey VA Medical Center 2002 Holcombe Blvd Houston, TX 77030 5. Responses Requested: The NCO 16 requires all the following information and questions answered 5a through 5i in this RFI/SS: Questions and information that are not provided shall be considered nonresponsive to the Request for Information and contractor shall not be considered as part of the market research. a. Do you (contractor) possess the capability to meet the government requirements listed in the Draft SOW? b. Do you (contractor) possess the capability to meet the government requirements of place of performance and distance from the Micheal E. Debakey VA Medical Center of the Draft SOW? c. Do you (contractor) possess the capability to meet the government requirements Period of Performance and Schedule in of the Draft SOW (30 Days from date of Award)? d. Contractors shall provide their point(s) of contact name, address, telephone number, and email address; and the company's business size, and SAM Unique Entity Identification Number. e. Is your company a small business, SDVOSB, VOSB, SDBs, HUBZone, or 8A concern? Please provide proof of qualifications. f. Is your company considered small under the NAICS code 339114? g. Do you (Contractor) have the ability to meet the requirements in SOW itself or will subcontracting be required for you to meet requirements in SOW? h. Are you an authorized Service Provider? Provide evidence from original equipment manufacturer (OEM). Please indicate if you are the OEM. If not applicable for this requirement state N/A. i. For the service required, Is your company available under any; Government Wide Agency Contract (GWAC) General Services Administration Schedules (GSA) Veterans Affairs (VA) NAC Federal Supply Schedules Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) Blanket Purchase Agreement (BPA) If so, please list the contract number for service. 6. Opportunity: The NCO 16 is seeking information from potential contractors on their ability to provide this service. THIS IS A SOURCES SOUGHT FOR REQUEST INFORMATION (RFI) ONLY. Small Business Concerns are encouraged to provide responses to this Sources Sought in order to assist the NCO 16 in determining potential levels of competition available in the industry. Contractor shall possess the capability to provide all requirements and objectives. 7. Instructions and Response Guidelines: Sources Sought responses are due by August 6th, 2026, at 12:00 PM (CST) via email to eugene.jackson2@va.gov. Telephone requests or inquiries will not be accepted. Public Information will not be provided and shall be utilized to the full extent possible. The subject line shall read: 36C25626Q1159 - Sources Sought � Dental 3D Shape Scanner � Houston, TX. NO SOLICITATION EXISTS AT THIS TIME. There is no page limitation on subparagraphs 5(a) - 5(i). Please provide the information you deem relevant to respond to the specific inquiries of the Sources Sought. Information provided will be used solely by NCO 16 as "market research" and will not be released outside of the NCO 16 Purchasing and Contract Team. This Sources Sought notice does not constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP), Invitation for Bid (IFB), or Request for Quotation (RFQ), and it is not to be construed as a commitment by the Government to enter into a contract, nor will the Government pay for the information submitted in response to this request. All information contained in this Sources Sought is preliminary as well as subject to modification and is in no way binding on the Government. In accordance with FAR 15.101(c)(2), responses to this notice are not offers and cannot be accepted by the U.S. Government to form a binding contract. If a solicitation is released, it will be synopsized on Contracting Opportunities (https://beta.sam.gov/) website or GSA e-buy. It is the responsibility of the interested parties to monitor these sites for additional information pertaining to this Sources Sought, or future RFP/RFQ. 8. Contact Information: Contract Specialist, Eugene Jackson Email address: eugene.jackson2@va.gov Your responses to this notice are appreciated. THIS NOTICE IS NOT A REQUEST FOR COMPETITIVE QUOTES/PROPOSALS; however, any firm that believes it can meet the requirements may provide answers, responses and give written notification prior to the response due date and time. Supporting evidence and responses must be furnished in enough detail to demonstrate the ability to perform the requirements.

Federal notice (Special Notice), COMMERCE, DEPARTMENT OF.COMMERCE, DEPARTMENT OF
Title: Notice of Intent to Sole Source Wirebond Pull Tester
Solicitation number: NB687000-26-02180
PSC: 6640; NAICS: 334515
Description: The National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) Acquisition Management Division intends to negotiate with K&R Next Generation Bonding Inc., located in Santa Ana, CA, on a sole source basis under the authority of FAR Subpart 6.302-1, soliciting from a single source, for a Wirebond Pull Tester. Specific Requirements are as follows: The unit shall be a new West Bond 70PTE Wire Pull Tester, �E� Series, with A-1 Tweezer Feature, with the following specifications: binocular microscope with 10x eyepieces. LED Illuminator: Twin Array. z Tool Range: at least 9/16�. z Encoder Resolution: 0.002�. Test Force Range: 100 g minimum. Test Range: at least 1/8� depth with 360? rotation. Force Resolution: 0.1 g or better. Force Accuracy: +/� 0.2 g or better. ESD Protection: yes. (x, y, z) micromanipulator of pull hook and swap-in tweezer attachment: single-lever, dual-counter counterbalanced with 8:1 motion-reduction ratio. The contractor shall supply a one-year warranty on all parts. NAICS Code is 334515 �Instrument Manufacturing for Measuring and Testing Electricity and Electrical Signals, with a Size Standard of 750 employees. NIST anticipates negotiating and awarding a firm-fixed-price purchase order to K&R Next Generation Bonding for this requirement. Interested parties that can demonstrate they could satisfy the requirement listed above for NIST must clearly and unambiguously identify their capability to do so in writing on or before the response date for this notice. This notice of intent is not a solicitation. Information submitted in response to this notice will be used solely to determine whether competitive procedures could be used for this acquisition. If competitive procedures are not used it is estimated that an award will be issued by August 28, 2026. Any questions regarding this notice must be submitted in writing via email to lisa.stevens@nist.gov. All responses to this notice of intent must be submitted to lisa.stevens@nist.gov no later than the date and time provided herein this posting. JUSTIFICATION FOR OTHER THAN FULL AN OPEN COMPETITION: The NIST Quantum Sensors Division (QSD) is contracted by NASA to provide flight hardware for the Athena X-ray-astronomy satellite mission. As part of this work, the QSD team will be wirebonding to flight parts. The team needs to be able to measure the pull strength of the wirebonds. The team also needs to be able to remove wirebonds in a highly controlled way. This purchase is for a dual-use benchtop unit: a manual wirebond-pull tester that also has a swap-in tweezer attachment to remove wirebonds. The new unit will be sited in the QSD's new �flight lab� that is being commissioned to handle, test, and store Athena flight parts. To support its general mission to assemble and test detector and readout hardware, the QSD already operates and maintains a fleet of wirebonders (to apply wirebonds) and diebonders with tweezers (to remove wirebonds) that were all made by the same manufacturer, West Bond. Wirebond-pull testers share many operating features with wirebonders and diebonders and are built from many of the same types of mechanical, optical, and electronic components. Thus, to maintain intercompatibility with its existing stock of spare West Bond parts and to avoid the need to re-train its large user base that already knows how to operate, trouble-shoot, and repair West Bond wirebonders and diebonders, the QSD is requesting to purchase a specific West Bond model (the 70PTE Wire Pull Tester, �E� Series, with A-1 Tweezer Feature) from a specific company (K&R Next Generation Bonding, Inc.). The QSD presently operates and maintains 6 West Bond wirebonders and diebonders. All of these units use the same optic (binocular microscope with 10x eyepieces) that are also present in the new wirebond-pull tester. All but one use the same (x, y, z) single-lever, dual-counterbalanced micromanipulator with 8:1 motion-reduction ratio that is also present in the new wirebond-pull tester. All but one use the same mechanical stage and the same control electronics that are also present in the new wirebond-pull tester. Two use the same tweezers and actuator that are also present in the new wirebond-pull tester. The QSD keeps an inventory of spare parts and has super-users for each machine that have been trained by West Bond technicians to repair them. A sole-source purchase of the specified West Bond 70PTE-A-1 wirebond-pull tester with tweezers guarantees intercompatibility with QSD�s spare parts and the ability of QSD�s already-trained super-users to service and repair the new machine. The present QSD user base for the existing West Bond machines is about 35 people. The user base for the new wirebond-pull tester is expected to be about 6 to 8 people, all of whom are present users of QSD�s other West Bond machines. A sole-source purchase of the specified West Bond 70PTE-A-1 guarantees interoperability by the existing QSD user base without the need for re-training. West Bond, Inc. went out of business at the end of 2025. The remaining stock of new West Bond wirebonders, diebonders, and wire-pull testers was transferred to a new company, K&R Next Generation Bonding, Inc. This company is the only authorized seller of new (manufacturer original) West Bond machines. Thus, QSD is requesting to purchase the 70PTE-A-1 (the only wire-pull tester with tweezer attachment that fulfills QSD�s technical needs) from K&R Next Generation Bonding, Inc. (the only company authorized to sell it).

Statement of Requirements
Wire-Pull Tester with Tweezer Attachment
NB687000-26-02180
1. Background Information:
The NIST, Physical Measurements Laboratory, Quantum Sensors Division, Quantum
Microcalorimeter Group (QMG) is contracted by NASA to provide flight hardware for the Athena
X-ray-astronomy satellite mission. As part of this work, the QMG will be wirebonding to flight
parts. The team needs to be able to measure the pull strength of the wirebonds and also needs to
be able to remove wirebonds in a highly controlled way.
This purchase is for a dual-use benchtop unit: a manual wirebond-pull tester that also has a swap-
in tweezer attachment to remove wirebonds. The new unit will be sited in the QMG’s new “flight
lab” that is being commissioned to handle, test, and store Athena flight parts.
To support its general mission to assemble and test detector and readout hardware, the QMG
already operates and maintains a fleet of wirebonders (to apply wirebonds) and diebonders with
tweezers (to remove wirebonds) that are all made by the same manufacturer. Wirebond-pull testers
share many operating features with wirebonders and diebonders, and are built from many of the
same types of mechanical, optical, and electronic components.
2. Scope of Work:
a. Objectives:
The goal of this purchase is to supply a dual-use benchtop system: a manual wirebond-pull
tester that also has a tweezer attachment to remove wirebonds.

i. Provide a new unit. Prototypes, demonstration models, or used or refurbished
instruments will not be considered for award.
ii. Supply the installation and user manual(s), including utility requirements.

1. binocular microscope with 10x eyepieces.
2. LED Illuminator: Twin Array.
3. z Tool Range: at least 9/16”.
4. z Encoder Resolution: 0.002”.
5. Test Force Range: 100 g minimum.
6. Test Range: at least 1/8” depth with 360⁰ rotation.
7. Force Resolution: 0.1 g or better.
8. Force Accuracy: +/– 0.2 g or better.
9. ESD Protection: yes.
10. (x, y, z) micromanipulator of pull hook and swap-in tweezer attachment:
single-lever, dual-counter counterbalanced with 8:1 motion-reduction ratio.
ii. The contractor shall supply a one-year warranty on all parts.
3. Period of Performance:
Readiness of unit for shipment to NIST shall be four (4) weeks ARO, with early readiness
allowable.
The government’s planned acceptance-testing period is seven (7) business days after receipt of the
shipped unit at NIST.

I. Agency and Contracting Activity.
This Justification and Approval (J&A) request authority for Other Than Full and Open
Competition to support requirements generated for the Air Force Life Cycle Management
Center (AFLCMC)/Common Avionics Branch (AFLCMC/WNY) in conjunction with the
Air Force Sustainment Center (AFSC)/Common Avionics Supply Chain Management
Squadron (AFSC/407 SCMS). The contracting agency for this requirement and
Justification for Other Than Full and Open Competition is the Defense Logistics Agency
Aviation (DLA). The purchase request number supporting this contracting action is
FD2060-22-32030 (Production) and FD2060-23-00009 (Repair).
II. Nature and/or description of the action being approved.
This J&A is being submitted to establish a follow-on contracting vehicle to procure and
repair Joint Helmet Mounted Cueing System (JHMCS). This J&A is to support United
States Air Force (USAF), Navy, and Foreign Military Sales (FMS) customer
requirements for the Joint Helmet Mounted Cueing System (JHMCS) components
including consumable and Depot Level Reparable (DLR) spares. Due to the
circumstances described herein, the activity requests authority to acquire the supplies
listed and services in this document using Other Than Full and Open Competition as
prescribed by Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 6.302-1, Only One Responsible
Source and No Other Supplies or Services Will Satisfy Agency Requirements. This
action will result in the award of a new contract, which will be a Indefinite
Delivery/Requirements, FAR 16.503, type contract. Performance period for this contract
will be 72 months (plus a six-month extension), which includes one three (3) year Basic
Ordering Period plus three (3) one-year Ordering Periods. In addition, contract clause
FAR 52.217-9, “Option to Extend the Term of the Contract” will be included to allow up
to a maximum 6-month extension to the period of performance.
This sole source requirement will be purchased from the following company:
Collins Elbit Vision Systems, LLC (CEVS)
4700 Marine Creek Parkway
Fort Worth TX 76179-3505
CAGE: 6VSE4

This contract will be awarded as a Single Award Task Order/Delivery Order Contract.
DFARS 216.504(c)(3) states, “In accordance with Section 816 of the National Defense
Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2020 (Pub. L. 116-92), the determination at FAR
16.504(c)(1)(ii)(D) is not required if a justification has been executed, in accordance with
FAR subpart 6.3 and subpart 206.3.
III. Description of supplies/services required to meet agency needs (including the
estimated value).
DLA Aviation Warner Robins is proposing a joint opportunity contract between DLA
Aviation and the USAF to acquire JHMCS consumable and depot level reparable (DLR)
spares sole sourced to Collins Elbit Vision Systems (CEVS), formerly Rockwell Collins
ESA Vision Systems, LLC and before that Vision International, LLC (VSI). This
contract will support continuing requirements and provide sustainment support until the
end of the contract performance periods. This contract will establish an agreement
between the Government and CEVS that provides on-demand, performance-based repair,
hardware deliveries and manufacturing that are sole source to CEVS. This contract will
foster comprehensive supplier relationships by engaging both of CEV’s fifty percent
(50%) business partners in conversations about costs and pricing, parts obsolescence, and
schedules for repair performance; provide certainty to the supply chain by providing
monthly demand needs and conducting monthly performance reviews; and enable
efficiencies in the delivery of materials and repair services to support the Warfighter. The
current contract will expire 30 August 2023. The period of performance will be for six
years after the date of award and will include an option for a six-month extension.
This production and repair contract effort will provide all of the necessary parts and labor
to manufacture and repair JHMCS items. All items covered by this contract will be
military unique and sole-sourced to CEVS, who is the Original Equipment Manager
(OEM) for the JHMCS components. The contract will be used to acquire manufacturing
and repair services where the supplier is the only responsible source, to support
sustainment of the JHMCS weapon system, platforms, Shop Replacement Units (SRUs),
and Line Replacement Units (LRUs). There are 47 items included in the initial population
which consists of: 29 consumable and 18 depot level repair (DLR) items. Additional
items may be added if replacements are identified as obsolete items or additional sole
source items are identified. The estimated value for this contract effort is
$ and the performance period for this contract will be 72 months (plus an
option for a six-month extension) which includes one three (3) Basic Ordering Period
plus three (3) one-year Ordering Periods. The projected quantities, referenced in
Attachment 1: Table 2: Production NSNs and Table 4: Repair NSNs, will be Best
Estimated Quantities (BEQ) per year.

extension(s) utilizing range pricing from the latest priced ordering period until negotiated
prices are incorporated by contract modification.

10 U.S.C. 3204 (a)(1), as implemented by FAR 6.302-1, Only One Responsible Source

V. Demonstration that the contractor's unique qualifications or the nature of the
acquisition requires use of the authority cited above (applicability of authority).
The JHMCS is a highly sophisticated and specialized human mounted avionics system
designed to provide the aircraft fire control systems aircrew with the combat advantage of
first look, first shot capability in the air-to-air, within visual range combat arena. It has a
magnetic helmet-mounted tracker that determines where the pilot's head is pointed,
combined with a miniature display system that projects information onto the pilot's visor.
The head tracker and visor display act as a targeting device that can aim sensors and
weapons wherever the pilot is looking. JHMCS is installed on USAF F-15 and F-16
aircraft, United States Navy F-18 aircraft, and all the aforementioned platforms for FMS.
There are twenty-three (23) countries flying JHMCS configured jets. CEVS is the
original OEM for the JHMCS components covered by this acquisition and includes
various pieces mounted to the pilot’s helmet.
As the OEM, CEVS is the only source that has met the requirements and been approved
as a source of supply for the military unique items covered under this acquisition since
the calendar year (CY) 2000. Currently, there are still no commercial market sources for
these JHMCS components outside of CEVS. The only viable alternative the Government
has in production of the JHMCS spares is to attempt reverse engineering. Given the
advanced technologies and high voltage aspects of JHMCS, it is considered high risk to
reverse engineer. There are 47 items; 33 consumable and 14 depot level repair items
included in the market research supporting this J&A. The USAF does not own the
technical data to any of these items.
For our effort, there is a limited amount of capability and funding available to redesign
obsolete parts (along with no bid from the OEM and any other potential manufacturing
sources). These particular Next Higher Assembly (NHAs) NSNs are not considered
obsolete at this point and would fall towards the bottom of the priority list to redesign
and/or reverse engineer. In conclusion, the cost and time associated with reverse
engineering these NSNs would cost the USAF an excess of and 8-10 years. This

is a very optimistic forecast. If reverse engineering is attempted, a full First Article
qualification, sled testing, and ejection testing would also need to be conducted. Based on
past similar engineering acquisitions, the cost is prohibitive as is the acquisition time to
POM for funding, negotiate/award a contract, perform reverse engineering, build first
articles and test/evaluate.
For the subassemblies, within the NHA, with higher failure and replacement rates, the
government has no proprietary rights on any data associated with these and is not
authorized to do repairs in house. Reverse engineering or attainability of piece parts is
futile since the government does not have the capability to do repairs without contractor
supplied data via the Public Private Partnership with the Warner Robins Air Loistics
Complex. Since the government has no data on reverse engineering JHMCS equipment,
similar avionics items can be compared for cost analysis. Currently, the Microphone
Station on the E-3 aircraft is in process of being reverse engineered. The Period of
Performance (PoP) was initially two years and is continuing to be extended. The cost of
this reverse engineering process has already exceeded Averaging a repair
cost range of and a 25% reduction in repair costs, due to reverse
engineering, and averaging a subassembly needs to be replaced 10 times a month, the
fastest return on investment (ROI) would take more than 40 years. Since the current
subassemblies are not becoming obsolete, there is no monetary or mission capability
benefit in reverse engineering JHMCS system subassemblies since the ROI would extend
far pass the retirement set for Calendar Year 2040.
For the consumable items, many of these components are low-cost to the government.
The monetary cost and time it takes to reverse engineer these items are not only high risk
to the government, but uneconomical. Similar avionics items (the module and variable
attenuator, and the APY ½ Push Button Switch) are currently reverse engineered and take
upwards of two years and at a price point ranging from for the
first phase of reverse engineering development. The total reverse engineering process,
testing, and implementation takes on average three to five years. Assumning an initial
investment of for a reverse engineering effort on the Visor Day Anti Scratch 25%/
NSN: 8475-01-475-4702, it would take approximately 42 years for the government to see
a return on investment, which would be calander year 2065. The JHMCS system is slated
to be retired in calander year 2040 and therefore would be uneconomical for the
government to pursue.
Accordingly, an award to any other source would result in substantial duplication of cost
to the Government that is not expected to be recovered through competition and
unacceptable delays in fulfilling the Government’s requirements, per the AFLCMC
JHMCS Program Management Office.

The statutory authority which permits other than full and open competition for this acquisition is 10 U.S.C. � 3204(a)(1), as implemented by Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO) 6.103-1. Therefore, a Request for Quotation (RFQ) solicitation from a single source, will be issued to Compunetix Inc to provide EPOS HME-130 headset systems for Mission Voice Platform systems at Joint Base Pearl Harbor-Hickam. The required EPOS HME-130 headset systems are vital components of the proprietary Compunetix Mission Voice Platform (MVP), a system for which Compunetix, Inc. is the Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM). The MVP system requires a specific polarized, dual-prong connector and a unique electronic interface that is not available in standard Commercial-Off-The-Shelf (COTS) products. The vendor, Compunetix, Inc., has certified in writing that the EPOS HME-130 is the sole compatible replacement for the unit's legacy headsets, which are now discontinued. As the OEM, Compunetix is the only source with the proprietary technical knowledge and authority to guarantee system compatibility and interoperability. Procuring from any other source would introduce unacceptable mission risk and void the warranty and support for the existing mission-critical MVP system. The designated North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) Code is 334310, Audio and Video Equipment Manufacturing, with a size standard of 750 employees. SCOPE OF WORK 

1.0 Introduction

This Statement of Work (SOW) defines the requirements of the Harry S Truman VA Medical Center - Multi-Specialty CBOC – Rolla in establishing a fixed-price order for Ice Makers & Medical Grade Ref./Freezers. 

1.1 Background

Harry S Truman VA Medical Center - Multi-Specialty CBOC – Rolla requires Ice Makers & Medical Grade Ref./Freezers to outfit the new facility and provide services for the VA.


1.2 Scope

The scope of this purchase order is to provide Harry S Truman VA Medical Center - Multi-Specialty CBOC – Rolla with the products outlined for delivery to the Harry S Truman VA Medical Center - Multi-Specialty CBOC – Rolla location. Contractors shall furnish all requirements. 

The initial delivery will be to an offsite warehouse to support installation time lines. The warehouse location has yet to be determined. The warehouse will be available June 1st, 2026 – May 31st,2027. Initial Outfitting Transition and Activation team will be responsible for delivery to Rolla Super CBOC with estimated delivery dates are November 2nd, 2026 – January 8th, 2027. Specific installation dates will be defined upon award.

The delivery schedule is based upon the current construction schedule, which is subject to change. The vendor shall not increase prices for a change in delivery date due to construction delays. The awardees actual delivery dates will be confirmed by VA upon award.

The Contractor shall provide services and support at the locations identified in this Statement of Work. The Government reserves the right to add, remove, or modify locations and facilities as mission requirements evolve across the current and future operational footprint. The Contractor shall accommodate these changes within the scope of the contract without disruption to services. Any adjustments to pricing, schedule, or resources resulting from such changes shall be addressed through the appropriate contractual modification process in accordance with the applicable Changes clause.

2.0 General Requirement 

All equipment to be supplied under the specifications shall be the newest and the most current model of a standard product of a manufacturer of record. The products provided must meet or exceed the specifications laid out in the sections. A manufacturer of record is defined as a company whose main occupation is the manufacture for sale of the items of equipment and which:

a. Maintains a factory production line.
b. Maintains a stock of replacement parts for the item.
c. Maintains engineering drawings, specifications, operating manuals and maintenance manuals.
d. Has published and distributed descriptive literature and equipment specifications on the equipment.

Any equipment or service as applicable must be in compliance with the Memorandum dated March 6th 2025 Subject: Electronic Health Record Modernization Standardization (VIEWS 12862405).

Description: This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial products prepared in accordance with the format in FAR Subpart 12.6, as supplemented with additional information included in this notice. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation; a quotation is being requested, and a separate written solicitation will not be issued. The solicitation number is HFP-OLOAS-26-C-B029, issued as a Request for Quotations (RFQ). NOTICE OF INTENT TO SOLICIT SINGLE SOURCE: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA), Atlanta Human and Animal Food Laboratory (ATLHAFL), Nutrient Analysis Branch, intends to solicit and award a firm-fixed-price purchase order to Leco Corporation, St. Joseph, MI (CAGE OJ626), on a brand-name, single-source basis for one (1) Leco FP928 Boom-Mounted Touchscreen/Autoloader PC Macro Nitrogen Determinator (combustion/Dumas protein analyzer) with delivery, installation, IQ/OQ, operator training, minimum 12-month warranty, and an OEM Gold Maintenance Plan (base period plus four one-year options; period of performance 8/1/2026 through 7/31/2031 if all options are exercised). attachments.text:
STATEMENT OF WORK
Combustion Protein Analyzer Brand
Name (Leco FP928) – Sole Source
Background
The Food and Drug Administration (FDA) Atlanta Human and Animal Food Laboratory (ATLHAFL)
Nutrient Analysis Branch (NAB) require replacement of an existing obsolete Nitrogen Determinator system
used to analyze infant formula, medical foods, food, dietary and feed samples for the analysis of protein
utilizing the Dumas method. The NAB performs nutrient analysis on food products, animal feed and dietary
supplements. This includes infant formula and medical foods which have stricter guidelines because they
may serve as a sole source of nutrition for the consumer. The system must maintain compliance with
cGMP/cGLP/ISO/IEC 17025-2017, ISO 9001:2008, and 21 CFR part 11 standards as required under current
laboratory accreditation.
Purpose/Scope
The current nitrogen determinator system has become obsolete and the manufacturer cannot provide
service or replacement parts. The purpose of this acquisition is to replace the existing nitrogen
determinator system with a new, fully serviceable unit to ensure uninterrupted protein analysis of high-
priority infant formula and medical food samples.
The Contractor shall provide all resources necessary to accomplish the tasks and deliverables described in this
Statement of Work (SOW), specifically:
▪ System A: One (1) FP928 model Boom Mounted Touchscreen/Autoloader PC Macro Nitrogen
Determinator (Brand Name: Leco FP928)
▪ Part B: A Gold Maintenance Agreement for one (1) base period plus four (4) option years.
Minimum Required Technical/Performance Specifications
The instrument shall meet the following minimum requirements:
I. System A
• Shall be a Model FP928 Boom Mounted Touchscreen with Autoloader PC Macro Nitrogen
Determinator (Leco FP928, brand name/sole source), meeting all specifications outlined in
this SOW.
• This is a brand-name (sole-source) requirement for the Leco FP928; “or equal” substitutes will not
be evaluated. See the sole-source justification and market research.
• The system shall comply with the approved methods of analysis: ISO, AOAC, AACC, AOCS, and
ASBC.
• Shall include Horizontal ceramic furnace design with exclusive oxygen environment ensuring
complete oxidation of macro samples.
• Maximum operating temperature of 1450°C (minimum requirement)
• Shall accommodate large, open and reusable ceramic sample boats that facilitate the handling and
combustion of macro samples ranging from 1 to 3 grams.
• Shall have sample ash retention in boat for post-analysis removal, eliminating furnace tube
maintenance requirements.
• Thermal conductivity cell shall support the flexibility of using helium or argon as a carrier gas
without hardware change.
• Shall have rapid analysis times that are low-cost with instrument designs with reagent-free furnaces.
• Shall have long lifetimes with the model FP928 featuring a combustion gas aliquot system that
provides extended and consistent reagent lifetime including a 4000-sample reduction tube reagent
lifetime.
• Shall have a dual loop aliquot doser provided with the flexibility to optimize methods based upon
sample element concentration (low/high) or analysis cost and uptime.
• The instrument shall have the Cornerstone software on a Boom-Mounted Touchscreen which
enables the operator to have a more efficient workflow (operator-centered design).
• Shall have extended reagent lifetimes which contribute to a low cost-per-analysis
• Shall have expanded furnace efficiency and reliability with a reagent-free design – with a reagent-
free, high-efficiency furnace with intelligent control that expands the heating element and ceramic
lifetime.
• Shall have a thermoelectric cooler which eliminates the use of chemicals desiccant reagents for the
removal of combustion gas moisture in the Nitrogen/Protein model.
• Shall have 100-sample position autoloader for sequential and non-sequential analysis
• Shall have a rapid cycle-time of 5 minutes
• Shall have an ergonomic, operator-centered design with boom-mounted touch-screen interface
which introduces all operations on one screen.
• Shall have a SmartLine remote diagnostics that can allow for plots of ambience or multiple
ambiences at the same time to optimize time frame.
• Shall have a SmartLine that includes advance Leak Check Diagnostics to help the operator diagnose
a problem or find a potential leak in the system.
• Shall have the Cornerstone software that can perform advanced diagnostics, monitor the instrument
and furnace, perform calibrations divided into four parts: Analysis, Diagnostics, Settings and
Instrument – for simplified navigation and organization.
• Shall have advance interactive diagnostic features that include a digital on-board manual,
maintenance animations, photo-illustrations, and screen capture that provides direction needed.
• Shall have live screens that will show color-coded tubing inside the instrument, and an automated
system will check for verification of operational systems.
• Shall have easy access to all reagent tubes and common maintenance areas for simplified
maintenance
• Shall be reliable with a knowledgeable, state-of-the-art technical service (experienced application
chemists to assist in method development).
• Shall provide a global and regional service network with regional support centers dedicated to
providing service and support.
• The determination of protein is conducted in accordance with Official AOAC Method 990.03 and
LIB 4635, specifically applicable to infant formula analysis. These methods require nitrogen
determination via combustion using a Leco nitrogen/protein analyzer. To support this analytical
capability, we are seeking to procure the Series FP928 model with boom-mounted touchscreen and
autoloader PC macro system, designed for accurate and efficient nitrogen and protein determination
through combustion.
Installation Requirements
• The Contractor shall provide on-site installation and setup—including delivery, set-up, installation,
clean-up of installation area and training—within 2 weeks of receipt of equipment.
• The contractor shall provide installation qualification (IQ) and Operational Qualification (OQ)
performed by a certified employee who can provide proof of IQ/OQ certification.
Initial Training
• The Contractor shall provide comprehensive operator training at the time of installation for up to
four (4) users. Onsite location will be provided at time of installation or shortly thereafter (within 30
days), such that operators may independently operate the instrument and with increased familiarity
and proficiency.
• The training shall include manuals and consumables for use during training.
• Training Location: FDA/ATLHAFL Nutrient Analysis Branch (NAB), 1777 Hardee Avenue SW
Atlanta, GA 30310, Room 2333, Protein Laboratory.
Trade and Service Specifications
• The instruments shall be newly manufactured units, not used and refurbished or previously used for
demonstrations. The Contractor shall provide routine customer service and technical support to be
available from the vendor during its lifecycle.
• The system shall include at least a one (1) year warranty and shall include at a minimum: coverage
on all non-consumable items and parts supplied including base instrument, computer, monitor,
factory-certified replacement parts, engineer labor and travel costs. This requirement does not
obligate the Government to purchase an extended warranty. However, the entire system(s) must be
covered on a manufacturer warranty for parts and labor for a minimum of 12 months to start after the
completion of installation, training, and formal government acceptance, and include preventative
maintenance. The vendor must also be capable of servicing the instrument through an extended
warranty service (See Item II Options).
• Instrument operators shall have access to a technical representative call center, for technical
assistance and troubleshooting, which is staffed by senior engineers to provide a high level of
expertise for troubleshooting the instrument.
• At least one preventative maintenance (PM) visit shall be included per contract year. This visit shall
be inclusive of all parts, labor, travel, consumables, and supplies which are necessary to complete
the OEM’s suggested PM protocol. Trained OEM engineers shall perform service.
• System shall be delivered no later than 30 days after award.
Warranty period
The Contractor shall provide a comprehensive manufacturer's warranty covering all parts, labor, and travel
for a minimum period of twelve (12) months from the date of final acceptance.
The warranty period shall run concurrently with the first year of the maintenance agreement.
Minimum Required Maintenance Agreement Specifications
The contractor shall perform the following minimum tasks:
II. Gold Maintenance Agreement:
• Provide a timeline for instrument approximate date of delivery, installation, qualification.
• Provide “One KIT PMA Gold Maintenance Plan” required for first preventative maintenance visit.
• Perform one (1) preventative regular preventive maintenance call annually from the effective date of the
Contract. The contractor shall document the final state of the instrument at each of these calls.
• Perform two (2) emergency maintenance visits from the effective date of the Contract. The contractor
shall document the final state of the instrument at each of these calls
• Inspect the equipment at each visit and make the necessary adjustments or repairs.
• Emergency maintenance shall begin within forty-eight hours of a maintenance request.
• Maintenance shall be provided by maintenance engineers who are trained and certified by the original
manufacturer of this instrument. Maintenance engineers shall have access to the manufacturer's latest
technical developments, repair procedures, application updates, and diagnostic software and planned
maintenance procedures.
• The contractor shall perform the adjustment and alignments to original factory specification or better, to
meet the manufacturer’s performance specifications.
• The contractor shall perform software upgrades to the most current version, to meet the manufacturer’s
performance specifications.
• All software updates to the scientific equipment and/or software and related installation of such
instrument updates and /or software during the Agreement Term.
• Upon the preventative maintenance on-site visit, the contractor shall assess the scientific equipment and
determine if the repairs needed to the scientific equipment are covered under the maintenance agreement.
If the repairs are not covered under the maintenance agreement and are deemed necessary to complete the
preventative maintenance, the contractor shall submit a quote to the Government for review, and approval
or negotiation, which shall include travel costs, parts costs and labor costs.
• Warranty on parts and labor for any repairs completed during the maintenance period is for the term of
the contract.
• Unlimited telephone support during regular business hours, 8:00 AM-5:00 PM ET. for instrument support
and applications at no additional charge
• The contractor shall perform all non-emergency work during FDA’s regular business hours on regular
business days.
• Unlimited use of Smartline remote diagnostic tool.
III. Maintenance Calls:
• The Contractor shall respond within two (2) business days after receipt of a maintenance call from
the TPOC.
• The Contractor shall provide unlimited telephone and email access to instrument technical support
Monday – Friday between the hours of 8-5 p.m. EST.
• All repairs shall result in system maintenance meeting the original equipment manufacturer
specifications. All repairs shall use factory, new replacement parts.
• The Contractor shall perform a diagnostic test and document results and provide a narrative summary
demonstrating that the system is meeting the original equipment manufacturer’s specifications.
Any parts or components removed for repl

Commercial Single-Source Justification
(Open Market, RFO Part 12 Exceeding MPT, Not Exceeding
SAT)
Section 1 General Information
Requiring Activity: FDA / HFP / OLOAS / ORTS / Atlanta Human and Animal Food Laboratory
(ATLHAFL), Nutrient Analysis Branch (NAB)
Program / Project Title: Combustion Protein Analyzer (CIN HFP-OLOAS-26-C-B029; ALP HFP-2026-
134729)
Proposed Contractor: Leco Corporation, 3000 Lakeview Avenue, St. Joseph, MI 49085 (CAGE OJ626)
NAICS Code: 334516 - Analytical Laboratory Instrument Manufacturing (size standard 1,000
employees)
Estimated Total Value: $[REDACTED] (base equipment $[REDACTED] plus four one-year Gold
Maintenance option periods)
Period of Performance: August 1, 2026 through July 31, 2027 (base period; plus four one-year
option periods through July 31, 2031 if exercised)
Description of Products or Services: Purchase of one (1) Leco FP928 Boom-Mounted
Touchscreen/Autoloader PC Macro Nitrogen Determinator (combustion/Dumas protein analyzer) with
a five-year Gold Maintenance Plan (Leco SVC-800-GLD-FP928). Used for protein/nitrogen determination
under AOAC Official Method 990.03 and LIB 4635 on infant formula, medical foods, foods, and dietary
supplements. Replaces an obsolete, unserviceable Leco TruMac; the laboratory capability is currently
down.
Section 2 Authority and Determination
Authority: This single-source justification is executed under RFO 12.102(a), which authorizes
the contracting officer, for acquisitions valued at or below the SAT, to restrict competition by
documenting the decision that only one source is available and the basis for that decision. The
competition standard being limited is at RFO 12.201-1(c), which directs the contracting officer to
promote competition to the maximum extent practicable when acquiring commercial products or
commercial services at or below the SAT and sets a default of soliciting quotations from at least
three sources (RFO 12.201-1(c)(2)). Where the requirement specifies a brand name or a product
or feature peculiar to one manufacturer, RFO 11.204 applies and the brand-name documentation
in Section 4.3 is required.
Determination: The Contracting Officer determines in writing that only one source is reasonably
available for the products or services identified in Section 1 and that providing for competition to
the maximum extent practicable is not feasible. The basis is identified in Section 3 and supported
by the narrative in Section 4.
Section 3 Basis for Single Source
Page 1 of 4
☒ A. Items particular to one manufacturer (brand name)
☐ B. Exclusive licensing agreement
☐ C. Urgency
☐ D. Other circumstances making only one source reasonably available
Summary: N/A — basis is 3.A (brand name); see Section 4.3.
Section 4 Justification
4.1 Agency Need
The ATLHAFL Nutrient Analysis Branch (NAB) tests and verifies the declared nutritional claims of
domestic and imported products, including infant formula, medical foods, foods, and dietary supplements.
Protein is a key regulated nutrient historically subject to economic adulteration (dilution or filler/solvent
substitution), and infant formula and medical foods carry stricter requirements because they may serve
as a consumer's sole source of nutrition. Protein is determined by combustion (Dumas) nitrogen analysis
under AOAC Official Method 990.03 and LIB 4635. The laboratory's existing Leco TruMac analyzer has
been designated obsolete by the manufacturer and is unserviceable, leaving this capability down; a
replacement combustion protein analyzer is required to restore and sustain it.
4.2 Why Only One Source Is Reasonably Available
The requirement is met only by the Leco FP928, a proprietary combustion nitrogen/protein analyzer
manufactured by Leco Corporation. The laboratory's validated methods (AOAC 990.03 and LIB 4635)
require nitrogen determination by combustion on a Leco nitrogen/protein analyzer, and the FP928
embodies proprietary Leco technology - including the Cornerstone control and diagnostic software,
boom-mounted touchscreen interface, dual-loop aliquot doser, reagent-free furnace, and SmartLine
remote diagnostics - that is not available from any other manufacturer. Because the action also replaces
an obsolete Leco TruMac and must preserve continuity with the laboratory's validated Leco-based
methods, no other source can furnish an acceptable instrument without full, costly method re-validation.
4.3 Brand Name Addendum (RFO 11.204)
4.3.1 Essential Brand-Specific Feature(s):
(1) The Leco FP928 combustion (Dumas) nitrogen/protein analyzer architecture; (2) Leco Cornerstone
control and diagnostic software; (3) compatibility with the laboratory's validated AOAC 990.03 and LIB
4635 methods developed on the Leco platform; (4) the Leco Gold Maintenance Plan (SVC-800-GLD-
FP928) for OEM-certified service, parts, and software updates.
4.3.2 Why Each Feature Is Essential:
The FP928's proprietary combustion furnace and Cornerstone software produce the nitrogen/protein
results the validated methods depend on; AOAC 990.03 and LIB 4635 specify combustion determination
on a Leco analyzer. Substituting another platform would require costly re-validation of accredited
methods and would jeopardize continuity of results for infant formula and medical foods, where protein
content is safety-critical. Only Leco can furnish the FP928 and the OEM Gold Maintenance needed to keep
the instrument qualified.
4.3.3 Market Research Showing No Equal:
Page 2 of 4
Per the Market Research Report (Combustion Protein Analyzer), prepared by Rossana Kelton, Biologist,
ATLHAFL, and completed April 20, 2026, only Leco Corporation was identified as capable, owing to its
proprietary technology and unique expertise; no two capable small businesses and no equivalent
alternative were found. Research included GSA Advantage, the Leco online catalog (leco.com), internet
searches, and review of prior purchases of similar items.
4.3.4 Equivalent Products Considered and Rejected:
No equivalent instrument was identified. Other nitrogen/protein analyzers cannot run the laboratory's
validated Leco-based methods without full re-validation and do not provide the proprietary Leco FP928
architecture or Cornerstone software; accordingly, no alternative was acceptable.
Section 5 Fair and Reasonable Price
Per RFO 12.204(a), the Contracting Officer must determine the price to be fair and reasonable.
Where competitive quotations are not available because the acquisition is single-source, the
determination is based on price analysis.
Price analysis method and result: Price analysis will be performed by comparing Leco Corporation's
quotation to the Independent Government Cost Estimate ($[REDACTED] base; $[REDACTED] total
including options) and to Leco's published commercial catalog and GSA pricing for the FP928 and the Gold
Maintenance Plan. Because no prior award for this instrument exists and no competitive quotations are
available (single source), the determination rests on this price analysis. Upon receipt of the quotation, the
quoted price of $[quote] will be documented as within [X]% of the IGCE, and the Contracting Officer will
determine the price fair and reasonable.
Section 6 Posting / Publication
For acquisitions involving a brand name or item peculiar to one manufacturer, the documentation
must be posted for acquisitions over $25,000 (RFO 11.204(a)(3)). For other single-source
actions, post a presolicitation notice in the Governmentwide Point of Entry under subpart 5.1
unless an exception at 5.101(b) applies. State which applies:
Page 3 of 4
This is a brand‑name single‑source action (Section 3.A) with an estimated value exceeding $25,000. The
justification will be posted in the Governmentwide Point of Entry (SAM.gov) as required by RFO
11.204(a)(3).
Section 7 Contracting Officer Certification
I, the undersigned Contracting Officer, having considered the agency's need and the facts set
forth in this justification, determine in writing that only one source is reasonably available for the
products or services identified in Section 1 and that competition to the maximum extent
practicable is not feasible. This justification is executed in accordance with RFO 12.201-1(c) and
RFO 13.101(b), and, where Section 3.A is selected, RFO 11.204.

1. Contracting Agency: The Army Contracting Command-Detroit Arsenal (ACC-DTA)
is the contracting activity.
2. Description of Action: ACC-DTA proposes to award a new five-year, Firm-Fixed-

Government Entity (CAGE) 11384, for National Stock Number (NSN) 3010-01-373-
5945, Actuator, Electro-Mechanical, Linear, (Travel Lock Actuator), using Army Working

3. Description of Supplies/Services: The service repair to be performed under the
proposed contract is on a Travel Lock Actuator used on the M109A6 Paladin and
M109A7 Self-Propelled Howitzer.
Equipment capabilities, limitations, and vulnerabilities
Repair
may include unpacking, disassembly, inspection, diagnosis, removal and replacement
of subassemblies and component parts, reassembly, cosmetic work (i.e. paint touch ups
or replacement of cable ports to prevent further deterioration or functionality
interference), calibration, final testing and inspection, and packing for shipment.
The total
Readiness and vulnerability assessment
contract value is estimated at $2,777,922.00 for the service repair of an estimated
maximum quantity of 425 EA. The deliverables for this contract are as follows:
a. Noun: Actuator, Electro-Mechanical, Linear, (Travel Lock Actuator)
b. National Stock Number: 3010-01-373-5945
c. Manufacturer Part Number: 12361513
d. Initial Repair Quantity: 30 EA
e. Estimated Maximum Quantity: 425 EA

4. Authority Cited: The statutory authority permitting other than full and open
competition for this action is Title 10 United States Code (USC), Section 3204(a)(1), as
implemented by Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 6.302-1(a)(2), which provides,
“When the supplies or services required by the agency are available from only one
responsible source, or, for DoD, NASA, and the Coast Guard, from only one or a limited
number of responsible sources, and no other type of supplies or services will satisfy
agency requirements, full and open competition need not be provided for.” In
accordance with 6.302-1(a)(2)(iii), “services may be deemed to be available only from
the original source in the case of follow-on contracts for the continued provision of
highly specialized services when it is likely that award to any other source would result
in - (A) Substantial duplication of cost to the Government that is not expected to be
recovered through competition; or (B) Unacceptable delays in fulfilling the agency’s
1
OPSEC
OPSEC
CMO Control #: 2023-009
requirements.”
5. Reason for Authority Cited: Kollmorgen is the only source approved to repair the
Travel Lock Actuator. Kollmorgen has a confidential proprietary validated repair process
and is the only entity with that repair process technical data. The Government does not
have possession of the Travel Lock Actuator technical data to enable a competitive
procurement.
On 13 April 2022, Kollmorgen was contacted to request consideration for the U.S.
Government to purchase the intellectual property, but they refused.
The Travel Lock Actuator is a critical component of the M109 system.
Equipment capabilities, limitations, and vulnerabilities
Kollmorgen has a
confidential proprietary validated repair process which meets all unique characteristics
in the areas of performance, design, construction, operations in various environmental
conditions, and vehicle system testing.
readiness and vulnerability assessment
As authorized by FAR 6.302-1(a)(2)(ii)(A),(B), procurement by other than full and open
competition is necessary because Kollmorgen is the only source with a proven process
to repair the Travel Lock Actuator. Funding another company to develop another repair
process for the Travel Lock Actuator will be cost prohibitive and cause undue delay.
Substantial Duplication of Cost: To compete this service, the Government would need to
provide Travel Lock Actuator technical data. The Government requested to purchase
the technical data and associated rights for the Actuator, Electro-Mechanical, Linear,
(Travel Lock Actuator) from Kollmorgen, and Kollmorgen declined. The below table
shows the activities required, along with their associated timing/costs for a new vendor
to be validated as a source for competitive procurement. These are engineering
estimates based on previous efforts of this nature performed by the Government.
These include but are not limited to cost estimates to develop TDPs, historical data of
vehicle/component testing, and time/cost to acquire parts for said testing. Due to the
function of the part, on-vehicle testing is required. Testing would require scheduling a
window of time at an Army test center and must meet all requirements on the part
drawing.
Reverse Engineering 6 Months $300K
Obtain part samples 2 Months $20K
Develop Repair Process 6 Months $250K
Repair of parts 2 Months $100K
Component testing 4 Months $250k
2

Vehicle testing 12 Months $1M
TOTAL 32 Months $1.92M
The Government would not be expected to recover, through subsequent competition,
the costs involved in either procuring the proprietary data or reverse engineering the
item to create a competitive build to print technical data package and repair process
within a reasonable time frame. At the current usage rate of 120 units per year, at the
current unit repair cost of $6,536.29, and assuming the 25% saving achieved through
competition, the $196,088.70 annual savings would take 10 years to offset the
estimated $1.92M cost of developing a repair process.
Unacceptable Delays: As identified in the chart above, developing a new repair process
would take six months, whereas the entire process for a new source to be validated
would take 32 months. The vehicle level testing would be conducted at an Army test site
due to the limited availability of test vehicles and expenses associated with performing
such tests, which adds significant schedule delays. We need the item immediately since
there are zero on hand with 55 backorders and a current average monthly demand of
10. If these M109A6 Paladins and M109A7 Self-Propelled Howitzers cannot be
repaired, it will bring harm to the solider since these vehicles will remain Non-Mission
Capable without the Travel Lock Actuator and will cause a delay in fielding making it
impossible for the soldier to properly train and adequately prepare for field use.
Moreover, multiple depot programs will be negatively affected. If the depot cannot
obtain Travel Lock Actuators for their vehicle programs, it will cause a production
shutdown.
6. Efforts to Obtain Competition:
a. Effective competition: Due to the reasons cited in section 5 above we are not
pursuing competition for this item. This action will be synopsized in accordance
with FAR 5.201 any bids or proposals will be considered.
b. Subcontracting competition: The solicitation and resulting contract will include
FAR clauses 52.219-8, "Utilization of Small Business Concerns"; 52.244-5,
"Competition in Subcontracting"; 52.219-16, "Liquidated Damages--
Subcontracting Plan";" and Defense Federal Acquisition Regulation Supplement
(DFARS) 252.219-7003, "Small Business Subcontracting Plan (DoD Contracts),"
to maximize small business opportunities and utilization.
7. Actions to Increase Competition: There are no plans to increase competition for
future procurements due to the reasons cited above. However, the marketplace will
continue to be surveyed in search of competitors who can perform this same type of
work.

Title: Three (3) Rigaku Icon-X Handheld 1064nm Raman Spectrometers - Brand Name

Description: This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial products prepared in accordance with the format in FAR Subpart 12.6, as supplemented with additional information included in this notice and the attached documents. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation; quotations are being requested, and a separate written solicitation will not be issued. Solicitation number OC-OCS-26-C4920 is issued as a Request for Quotations (RFQ). The incorporated provisions and clauses are those in effect through the most current Federal Acquisition Circular. The associated NAICS code is 334516 (small business size standard: 1,000 employees); PSC 6640. This acquisition is unrestricted. The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA), National Forensic Chemistry Center (NFCC), Cincinnati, OH, requires three (3) new Rigaku IconX handheld 1064nm Raman spectrometers, including all standard features and accessories, CommandSuite software, familiarization training for up to six (6) users per instrument, and a three (3) year manufacturer's warranty, in accordance with the attached Statement of Work. Delivery is F.O.B. Destination to Cincinnati, OH 45237, no later than ninety (90) days after award. This is a brand-name requirement pursuant to FAR 13.106-1(b); "or equal" products will not be evaluated. The Brand-Name Justification is posted with this notice in accordance with FAR 5.102(a)(6). Quotations will be accepted from the OEM or from dealers/resellers currently authorized by Rigaku Analytical Devices; quoters other than the OEM shall submit evidence of current authorization with their quotation. The attached Combined Synopsis/Solicitation document constitutes the complete RFQ, including line items, instructions to quoters, and applicable provisions and clauses. attachments.text:
BRAND-NAME JUSTIFICATION
Limiting the Requirement to the Rigaku Icon-X — FAR 13.106-1(b); FAR 11.105
Action / Order Title Three (3) Rigaku Icon-X Handheld 1064nm Raman Spectrometers
Center Item Number (CIN) OC-OCS-26-C-4920
Requiring Activity OC / OCS / OSLES / NFCC — National Forensic Chemistry Center,
Cincinnati, OH
Contracting Office OAGS / Division DAP / Branch FSB
Estimated Value [Redacted] – below the Simplified Acquisition Threshold
NAICS / PSC 334516 (Analytical Laboratory Instrument Manufacturing) / 6640
(Laboratory Equipment and Supplies)
Date July 10, 2026
Competition Brand-name; unrestricted as to source/business size (resellers may
compete)
1. Requirement and Nature/Description of the Acquisition
The NFCC requires three (3) Rigaku Icon-X handheld 1064nm Raman spectrometers, including on-
instrument commercial spectral libraries and a three-year manufacturer warranty, for field/mail-facility
identification of narcotics, precursors, cutting agents, and related substances. This justification supports
specifying the Rigaku Icon-X by brand name; award will be made for the Icon-X, with competition
permitted among any responsible sources (e.g., authorized resellers) offering that brand.
2. Authority
This brand-name justification is prepared under FAR 13.106-1(b) (soliciting on a limited/brand-name
basis for acquisitions at or below the Simplified Acquisition Threshold) and FAR 11.105 (use of brand-
name in requirements). It documents why only the Rigaku Icon-X will satisfy the Government's need,
consistent with the market research.
3. Salient Characteristics Unique to the Rigaku Icon-X
Market research evaluated fourteen handheld Raman instruments. Only the Rigaku Icon-X meets every
mandatory salient characteristic. The distinguishing requirements, and why competing products fail
them, are:
• 1064 nm laser wavelength — required to suppress fluorescence on dark/colored/mixed samples
common in mail-facility casework. Thermo Fisher (TruScan/TruNarc/Gemini), Agilent (Resolve, 830
nm), and several Metrohm units are 785 nm and cannot meet this.
• 490 mW maximum laser power — Thermo Defender Omega (480 mW), Metrohm TacticID-1064 ST
(450 mW), and TacticID-Mobile (220 mW) fall short.
• 6-13 cm-1 spectral resolution — the only small-business option, SIMTRUM, reaches only 10 cm-1
and does not meet the requirement.
• Interoperability and mission continuity — the Icon-X uses a 13,200+ entry commercial library and
NFCC's established Rigaku workflow, requires no user calibration (polystyrene-rod verification,
eliminating benzonitrile), and offers a higher operating-temperature threshold and faster scan
processing suited to IMF satellite-lab and field conditions. These characteristics, taken together, are
met only by the Icon-X.
4. Market Research Supporting the Brand-Name Basis
The Market Research Memorandum documents the fourteen-instrument evaluation (Rigaku Icon-X and
CQL Max-ID, Rigaku Progeny ResQ, Thermo Fisher TruScan/TruNarc/Gemini/Defender Omega, Agilent
Resolve, Metrohm TacticID-N Plus/Mobile/1064 ST/MIRA XTR, SIMTRUM, and Detectachem Apex R7).
Each alternative fails one or more mandatory salient characteristics (wavelength, power, or resolution)
or is end-of-life/withdrawn. The Icon-X is the only product that satisfies all requirements at a fair and
reasonable price ([unit price redacted]).
5. Efforts to Promote Competition
Restricting to the Icon-X brand does not eliminate competition: the requirement will be solicited on an
unrestricted basis, and any responsible source able to furnish the Rigaku Icon-X (including the
manufacturer's authorized resellers) may compete on price. The solicitation will be publicized as
required, and the salient characteristics will be stated so the basis for the brand-name restriction is
transparent.
6. Determination
I determine that only the Rigaku Icon-X handheld 1064nm Raman spectrometer will meet the
Government's minimum need, for the reasons stated above, and that specifying this item by brand
name under FAR 13.106-1(b) and FAR 11.105 is justified. Competition will be sought among all
responsible sources offering the specified brand.
______James P. Jenrette III___________________________________
James Jenrette
Contracting Officer / Contract Specialist, OAGS/DAP/FSB
Date: _7/10/2026______________

Federal notice (Justification), STATE, DEPARTMENT OF.STATE, DEPARTMENT OF.U.S. EMBASSY PANAMA CITY
Title: NEC - Embassy Switch Gear Breaker Replacement
Solicitation number: 19PM0726Q0014
PSC: 5925; NAICS: 335313
Description: The requirement is to provide REPLACEMENT AND RETROFIT OF THE EMBASSY's MAIN ELECTRICAL SERVICE DISTRIBUTION SWITCHGEAR at COMPOUND AND CHANCERY BUILDING. The estimated value for the entire period of performance is $202,000.00, including options. These supplies/services require the emergency replacement of obsolete main power system breakers that are 20 years old and have reached end-of-life status. The existing Siemens 480-volt breakers can no longer be procured or repaired due to obsolescence and pose an imminent risk of catastrophic failure. The retrofit requires the supply and installation of genuine OEM Schneider Electric Square D breakers, which are the only components compatible with the Embassy's existing proprietary electrical distribution infrastructure. The work includes removal of obsolete breakers, installation of new Schneider Electric breakers, system integration, testing, and commissioning to ensure full operational capability while maintaining the manufacturer's warranty on the electrical distribution system. This will allow the Office of Facilities Management to accomplish the critical mission objective of maintaining continuous, reliable electrical power to all Embassy operations, including security systems, communications infrastructure, and life-safety equipment. Failure to complete this retrofit immediately creates an unacceptable risk of complete electrical system failure, which would result in a total shutdown and cessation of all Embassy operations. Additional Pertinent Information: The Embassy's electrical distribution system is classified as mission-critical security infrastructure. The existing system utilizes Schneider Electric's proprietary Square D breaker technology throughout the main distribution panels. Due to the age and obsolescence of the current breakers, there is an imminent risk of failure that could cause a complete power outage affecting all Embassy operations. The breakers have exceeded their rated service life, and replacement parts are no longer available from the original manufacturer (Siemens). Only Schneider Electric Centro America, as the sole authorized distributor and service provider for Schneider Electric products in Panama, can provide the genuine OEM components, technical expertise, and warranty-compliant installation services required for this time-sensitive emergency retrofit. The use of non-OEM or adapted components is prohibited under USG safety and security standards for sensitive infrastructure.

SCHNEIDER ELECTRIC CENTRO AMERICA is the only responsible source capable of
meeting the Embassy's requirements for this mission-critical electrical infrastructure
retrofit. The sole source determination is based on the following factors:
I. Proprietary Equipment and Patent Protection
The Embassy's electrical· distribution system is built exclusively on Schneider Electric's
proprietary Square D breaker technology. Schneider Electric manufactures and owns the
patents on Square D breaker products, which are the only breakers compatible with the
Embassy's existing main electrical distribution panels. This is a product-specific retrofit
requiring proprietary components that cannot be substituted with alternative brands. No
other manufacturer can legally produce compatible components for this patented system.
2. Exclusive Authorized Distributor Status
SCHNEIDER ELECTRIC CENTRO AMERICA is the sole authorized distributor and
service provider for Schneider Electric products in Panama. Only this vendor has:
• Factory authorization to distribute genuine OEM Schneider Electric components
• Access to proprietary technical specifications and installation software
• Factory-trained and certified technicians qualified to work on Schneider Electric

• Authorization to perform warranty-compliant installations on Schneider Electric

• Local presence in Panama for immediate emergency response and ongoing technical

3. Warranty Preservation Requirements
The Embassy's existing electrical distribution system is covered under manufacturer's
warranty. Only installations performed by authorized Schneider Electric service providers
using genuine OEM components maintain this warranty coverage. Use of any other vendor
or non-genuine components would immediately void the manufacturer's warranty, exposing
the USG to significant financial risk and potential liability in the event of system failure.
4. USG Security and Safety Compliance
The Embassy's electrical distribution system is classified as sensitive security infrastructure

genuine Schneider Electric components installed by authorized technicians meet these
stringent security and safety requirements.

catastrophic system failure.

Description: The Government requires an integrated core laboratory solution acquired under a cost?per?reportable?result (CPRR) model, in which VHA is invoiced solely based on the number of reported patient test results rather than capital equipment purchases. The solution must provide high?throughput chemistry and immunoassay testing, vendor?neutral track automation, and unified middleware/analytics within the physical constraints of Rooms 2B?174 and 2B?170, while embedding all equipment, service, reagents, consumables, middleware, and automation costs into a single CPRR rate. The requirement covers end?to?end core lab operations: pre?analytic processing (centrifugation, decapping/recapping, aliquoting, routing), analytic testing (Chem/IA/ID), and post?analytic archiving, including Indexor?based tracking at phlebotomy and outreach sites to provide true collection?to?result visibility from specimen draw through result release. The digital ecosystem must support high auto verification rates, rules?based QC management, real?time turnaround?time and workload dashboards, and integrated inventory management, all within the CPRR commercial structure so that AVAHCS pays only for verified reportable patient results rather than discrete hardware or service line items. The selected platform also uniquely offers an FDA?cleared lab?based TBI blood test panel on the core Alinity i analyzer, supporting rapid, objective concussion evaluation for Veterans within the same automated ecosystem. Services required include installation, configuration of all required interfaces (including VistA and DI?IM), validation, staff training, and relocation of the Phase?2 solution into the permanent core lab in Phase 3, with these implementation and support activities treated as covered deliverables under the CPRR agreement. Essential physical characteristics include the ability to fit a near?complete automation line into ?765 sq ft in Room 2B?174 during Phase 2 and a high?density integrated solution into Room 2B?170 in Phase 3, while meeting power, HVAC, and utility constraints and avoiding major structural renovation in the temporary space.
