2237: 508-27-1-2043-0002
2. Description of Action: This acquisition is conducted under the authority of the Multiple-
Award Schedule Program (41 U.S.C. 152(3) and 40 U.S.C. 501).
The AVAHCS Pathology & Laboratory Medicine Service (PLMS), in coordination with
Facilities, Biomedical Engineering, and Health Informatics, is undertaking a multi-phase
modernization of the core laboratory to address aging instrumentation, manual pre-analytic
workflows, space constraints, and growing test volumes. The project covers three phases:
Phase 1 infectious disease transition, Phase 2 Chem/IA/ID automation in temporary Room
2B-174, and Phase 3 relocation into a new permanent core lab in Room 2B-170.
This is a follow-on requirement to task order 36C24722N0054 which ends September 2026.
This task order will be Firm-Fixed Price (FFP) for a base year and 4 one-year option periods.
Order against: FSS Contract Number: 36F797-19-D0024
Name of Proposed Contractor: Abbott Laboratories Inc.
Street Address: 100 Abbott Park Rd D934
City, State, Zip: Abbott Park, IL 60064
3. Description of Supplies or Services:
.
The Government requires an integrated core laboratory solution acquired under
a cost-per-reportable-result (CPRR) model, in which VHA is invoiced solely based on the
number of reported patient test results rather than capital equipment purchases. The solution
must provide high-throughput chemistry and immunoassay testing, vendor-neutral track
automation, and unified middleware/analytics within the physical constraints of rooms
2B-174 and 2B-170, while embedding all equipment, service, reagents, consumables,
middleware, and automation costs into a single CPRR rate.

determination: Price/costs are determined fair and reasonable as this award will be issued
under the GSA FSS. All prices have been negotiated by GSA and were found fair and
reasonable at time of award. Options will also be priced in accordance with FSS pricing.
6. Describe the Market Research Conducted among schedule holders and the results or a
statement of the reason market research was not conducted:
Market research for this acquisition included: review of prior AVAHCS and VA contracts for
core lab and IVD equipment; release and analysis of an RFI to five major vendors (Abbott,
Siemens, Roche, Beckman Coulter, Ortho); vendor-submitted technical proposals and CAD
layouts; and internal site visits/virtual sessions focused on space and workflow feasibility. The
team also reviewed published product literature, industry documentation on analyzer/track
performance, and VA/VHA experience with digital middleware platforms.
The Contracting Officer and Small Business Specialist conducted database checks (SAM,
VetCert, DSBS) to identify VetCert-certified SDVOSB/VOSB and other small business
distributors; however, the underlying Chem/IA/ID automation systems and middleware are
OEM-controlled solutions not developed or manufactured by small businesses. No
AbilityOne, FPI, or mandatory Government sources were identified that could provide a
comparable integrated core lab automation ecosystem.
7. Any Other Facts Supporting the Justification:
The proposed vendor is currently providing multiple systems to provide diagnostics for our
Veterans. This requirement provides additional equipment to provide seamless
collection/diagnostics/reportables across the facility thus enhancing veteran experience while
saving time and money of consolidating results.

that led to the restricted consideration before any subsequent acquisition for the supplies or
services is made: At this time the requirement cannot be satisfied through competitive
methods. However, for future requirements thorough market research shall again be
conducted to ensure, if possible, the requirements will be competed if viable.

(2) Description of Action The procurement is to procure Fecal Immunochemical Test (FIT) collections kits to Veterans to screen for colorectal cancer (CRC). This acquisition supports the Veterans Affairs CRC Screening outreach program. The action will be awarded as a new requirement under Federal Supply Schedule (FSS) 36F79720D0016. Order against: FSS Contract Number: 36F79720D0016 Name of Proposed Contractor: Polymedco, LLC DBA: Polymedco Cancer Diagnostic Pro Street Address: 510 FURNACE DOCK ROAD City, State, Zip: CORTLANDT MANOR, NY 10567 Phone: 914-930-3223 (3) Description of Supplies or Services: The estimated value of the proposed action is $500,000.00 Proposed action: FSS BPA with a five (5) year ordering period. The service includes assembling the FIT collection kits, mailing the kits, conducting prenotification and follow-up communication with Veterans. It requires approximately 6,000 FIT collection kits to be mailed annually. (4) Identify the Authority and Supporting Rationale (see below and if applicable, a demonstration of the proposed contractor s unique qualifications to provide the required supply or service. FAR 8.405-6(a)(1)(A): An urgent and compelling need exists and following the ordering procedures would result in unacceptable delays: RFO FAR 8.4: Ordering under the Federal Supply Schedule Only one source is capable of providing the supplies or services required at the level of quality required because the supplies or services are unique or highly specialized; Polymedco Cancer Diagnostic Products LLC is the sole manufacturer and distributor of the required FIT kits and the only source that can provide FIT kits. Since there are no authorized distributors of the required FIT kits, Polymedco Cancer Diagnostic Products LLC is the only contractor capable of performing the mailing and notification service required for colorectal cancer screening. The current FIT kit used for colorectal cancer screening is provided to Washington DC VAMC. This service will also provide the instrumentation to analyze the samples collected returned by Veterans. The required collection kits have a 14-day inoculated stability and are compatible with the existing instrumentation, OC-Auto Sensor Diana, and OC-Auto Sensor iO. FAR 8.405-6(a)(1)(C): In the interest of economy and efficiency, the new work is a logical follow-on to an original Federal Supply Schedule order provided that the original order was placed in accordance with the applicable Federal Supply Schedule ordering procedures. The original order must not have been previously issued under sole source or limited source procedures. FAR 8.405-6(b): Items peculiar to one manufacturer: A patent, copyright or proprietary data limits competition. The proprietary data is: These are direct replacements parts/components for existing equipment. The material/service must be compatible in all aspects (form, fit and function) with existing systems presently installed/performing. (5) Describe Why You Believe the Order Represents the Best Value consistent with FAR 8.404(d) to aid the contracting officer in making this best value determination: The order from Polymedco represents the best value as it combines competitive pricing with a high-quality, clinically validated FIT product that meets industry standards for colorectal cancer screening. The mail-in format reduces overhead costs associated with in-office testing while improving patient compliance and accessibility. When evaluated against comparable alternatives, Polymedco s offering delivers a strong balance of cost-effectiveness, reliability, and ease of use, making it the most practical and economical. (6) Describe the Market Research Conducted among schedule holders and the results or a statement of the reason market research was not conducted. Polymedco, LLC. DBA Polymedco Cancer Diagnostic is a small business vendor with FSS Contract #: 36F79720D0016. Market research for the Polymedco mail-in FIT was conducted using industry-standard methodologies, including analysis of existing market data, competitive benchmarking, and evaluation of colorectal cancer screening tends. Additional market research on sam.gov, via contracting displayed contracts awards dating back as far as 10 years from today. An intent to Sole Source was posted on sam.gov (Notice ID: 36C24526Q0535) 5/14/2026 6/1/2026. The were no challenges to the proposed method of a sole source procurement. (7) Any Other Facts Supporting the Justification: Polymedco Cancer Diagnostic Products, LLC is a primary contractor for Federal Supply Schedule (FSS) VA contracts for Fecal Immunochemical Test (FIT) kits, often supporting colorectal screening initiatives. Switching vendors would require replacement of analyzers, revalidation, staff retraining, IT/LIS changes, and updated clinical pathways, resulting in substantial additional cost and unacceptable delay in screening services. This includes mailer kits, lab services, and automated analysis systems under VISN-level procurement. Polymedco FIT kits and analyzers are already provided to VA under Federal Supply Schedule VA FSS contracts, and VA has repeatedly determined they are a reasonably available source for compatible supplies and services throughout multiple VISNs dating back more than 10 years per Sam.gov search history. (8) A Statement of the Actions, if any, the agency may take to remove or overcome any barriers that led to the restricted consideration before any subsequent acquisition for the supplies or services is made: N/A (9) Requirements Certification: I certify that the requirement outlined in this justification is a Bona Fide Need of the Department of Veterans Affairs and that the supporting data under my cognizance, which are included in the justification, are accurate and complete to the best of my knowledge. I understand that processing of this limited sources justification restricts consideration of Federal Supply Schedule contractors to fewer than the number required by FAR Subpart 8.4.

SCOPE OF WORK 

1.0 Introduction

This Statement of Work (SOW) defines the requirements of the Harry S Truman VA Medical Center - Multi-Specialty CBOC – Rolla in establishing a fixed-price order for Ice Makers & Medical Grade Ref./Freezers. 

1.1 Background

Harry S Truman VA Medical Center - Multi-Specialty CBOC – Rolla requires Ice Makers & Medical Grade Ref./Freezers to outfit the new facility and provide services for the VA.


1.2 Scope

The scope of this purchase order is to provide Harry S Truman VA Medical Center - Multi-Specialty CBOC – Rolla with the products outlined for delivery to the Harry S Truman VA Medical Center - Multi-Specialty CBOC – Rolla location. Contractors shall furnish all requirements. 

The initial delivery will be to an offsite warehouse to support installation time lines. The warehouse location has yet to be determined. The warehouse will be available June 1st, 2026 – May 31st,2027. Initial Outfitting Transition and Activation team will be responsible for delivery to Rolla Super CBOC with estimated delivery dates are November 2nd, 2026 – January 8th, 2027. Specific installation dates will be defined upon award.

The delivery schedule is based upon the current construction schedule, which is subject to change. The vendor shall not increase prices for a change in delivery date due to construction delays. The awardees actual delivery dates will be confirmed by VA upon award.

The Contractor shall provide services and support at the locations identified in this Statement of Work. The Government reserves the right to add, remove, or modify locations and facilities as mission requirements evolve across the current and future operational footprint. The Contractor shall accommodate these changes within the scope of the contract without disruption to services. Any adjustments to pricing, schedule, or resources resulting from such changes shall be addressed through the appropriate contractual modification process in accordance with the applicable Changes clause.

2.0 General Requirement 

All equipment to be supplied under the specifications shall be the newest and the most current model of a standard product of a manufacturer of record. The products provided must meet or exceed the specifications laid out in the sections. A manufacturer of record is defined as a company whose main occupation is the manufacture for sale of the items of equipment and which:

a. Maintains a factory production line.
b. Maintains a stock of replacement parts for the item.

d. Has published and distributed descriptive literature and equipment specifications on the equipment.

Any equipment or service as applicable must be in compliance with the Memorandum dated March 6th 2025 Subject: Electronic Health Record Modernization Standardization (VIEWS 12862405).

Federal notice (Justification), VETERANS AFFAIRS, DEPARTMENT OF.VETERANS AFFAIRS, DEPARTMENT OF.257-NETWORK CONTRACT OFFICE 17 (36C257)
Title: 6640--Seahorse XF Pro Analyzer
Solicitation number: 36C25726Q0696

Award: AGILENT TECHNOLOGIES, INC. LEXINGTON 02421 295169.60000000
Description: Agency: Department of Veterans Affairs Contracting Activity: RPO West | NCO 17 | Lab Services Support (LSS), purchasing on behalf of Central Texas Veterans Health Care System (CTVHCS) / VISN 17 Center of Excellence Requirement Title: Seahorse XF Pro Analyzer Purchase Request: 674-26-4-998-0295 JOFOC Number: FY26 - NCO 17 - 1694 Prepared By: Ognian D. Ivanov, Contracting Officer Date: July 7, 2026 Contract Type: Firm-Fixed-Price Purchase Order Estimated Value: $295,169.60 Current Simplified Acquisition Threshold: $350,000.00 NAICS: 334516 Analytical Laboratory Instrument Manufacturing PSC: 6640 1. Identification of the Agency and Contracting Activity This sole source justification supports a commercial product acquisition by the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), Regional Procurement Office (RPO) West, Network Contracting Office 17 (NCO 17), Lab Services Support (LSS), purchasing on behalf of the Central Texas Veterans Health Care System (CTVHCS) / VISN 17 Center of Excellence. 2. Nature and Description of the Action Being Approved The Government intends to solicit from and award to a single source, Agilent Technologies, Inc., for one (1) Seahorse XF Pro Analyzer, including proprietary software, installation, operator training, and a 5-year extended warranty, on a firm-fixed-price basis. 3. Description of Supplies Required to Meet the Agency Need The VISN 17 Center of Excellence requires a live-cell metabolic analysis platform capable of simultaneous real-time measurement of oxygen consumption rate (OCR) and proton efflux rate (PER) in a 96-well format to support biomedical research. The required item is the Agilent Seahorse XF Pro Analyzer, Stock No. S7855A / SYS-SE-XFPRO, including Wave Pro Controller software, Seahorse Analytics, installation, training, and extended warranty coverage. The estimated total value is $295,169.60. 4. Authority Permitting Solicitation From a Single Source This requirement is a commercial product acquisition under FAR Part 12 as revised under the Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO). The estimated value of $295,169.60 is at or below the current Simplified Acquisition Threshold of $350,000. Accordingly, consistent with FAR 12.102(a), the Contracting Officer is documenting the decision that only one source is available and the basis for that decision. FAR Part 13 does not apply because the requirement is for a commercial product, not a noncommercial acquisition. 5. Demonstration That the Proposed Contractor s Unique Qualifications Require Use of the Authority Cited Agilent Technologies, Inc. is the only responsible source capable of meeting the Government s minimum needs. The Seahorse XF Pro Analyzer is a proprietary commercial product uniquely capable of simultaneous OCR and PER measurement in live cells in a 96-well microplate format with integrated reagent injection, proprietary sensor cartridge technology, and the required Wave Pro and Seahorse Analytics software environment. Only licensed Agilent technicians are authorized to install, service, and train users on the system. No alternative source was identified that could provide a functionally equivalent system meeting all technical requirements. 6. Efforts Made to Ensure That Offers Are Solicited From as Many Potential Sources as Practicable The contracting activity conducted extensive market research and public notice efforts. On June 24, 2026, Notice of Intent to Sole Source Notice ID 36C25726Q0645 was posted on SAM.gov for 13 calendar days, closing on July 7, 2026. No responses, objections, or capability statements were received. Additional market research included VetCert/SBA searches, GSA eLibrary review, AbilityOne review, FPI/UNICOR review, and review of recent federal procurement history. These efforts identified no additional capable sources. 7. Determination That the Anticipated Cost to the Government Will Be Fair and Reasonable The anticipated cost of $295,169.60 is determined fair and reasonable based on the commercial nature of the product, comparison to recent federal acquisitions for similar Seahorse analyzer systems, and the proprietary status of the required item and support package. The acquisition includes hardware, proprietary software, installation, training, and a 5-year extended warranty. 8. Description of Market Research Conducted and Results Market research was conducted in accordance with FAR Part 10 and VA acquisition procedures. The research included searches of VetCert/SBA for SDVOSB/VOSB sources under NAICS 334516, SAM.gov public notice, GSA eLibrary, AbilityOne, FPI/UNICOR, and review of federal procurement history. Results showed zero verified SDVOSB/VOSB sources, no other capable small business sources, no AbilityOne or FPI source, no GSA Schedule source for the analyzer itself, and no responses to the SAM.gov notice. Federal acquisition history for the Seahorse analyzer family reflected awards to Agilent Technologies, Inc. 9. Other Facts Supporting the Use of Sole Source Procedures The Government s minimum needs are based on unique research capabilities required by the CTVHCS / VISN 17 Center of Excellence. The required features are not unduly restrictive; rather, they reflect legitimate minimum needs that are only met by the Agilent Seahorse XF Pro platform. Proprietary software, manufacturer-authorized service, and compatibility requirements are integral to successful performance and cannot be separated from the supply requirement. 10. Listing of Sources That Expressed, in Writing, an Interest in the Acquisition No sources expressed interest in writing in response to the public notice. No capability statements were received during the notice period. 11. Actions the Agency May Take to Remove or Overcome Barriers to Competition Before Subsequent Acquisitions Prior to future acquisitions for similar research instrumentation, the Government will reassess the marketplace to determine whether additional commercial products or responsible sources become available. The requiring activity and contracting office will continue to monitor industry developments and procurement history. At present, the lack of competition is attributable to the proprietary nature of the required commercial product, not to any Government-created barrier. 12. Contracting Officer Certification I certify that this justification is accurate and complete to the best of my knowledge and belief.

DESCRIPTION
Agency: Department of Veterans Affairs
Contracting Activity: RPO West | NCO 17 | Lab Services Support (LSS), purchasing on behalf of Central Texas Veterans Health Care System (CTVHCS) / VISN 17 Center of Excellence
Requirement Title: Seahorse XF Pro Analyzer
Purchase Request: 674-26-4-998-0295
JOFOC Number: FY26 - NCO 17 - 1694
Prepared By: Ognian D. Ivanov, Contracting Officer
Date: July 7, 2026
Contract Type: Firm-Fixed-Price Purchase Order
Estimated Value: $295,169.60
Current Simplified Acquisition Threshold: $350,000.00
NAICS: 334516 – Analytical Laboratory Instrument Manufacturing
PSC: 6640
1. Identification of the Agency and Contracting Activity
This sole source justification supports a commercial product acquisition by the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), Regional Procurement Office (RPO) West, Network Contracting Office 17 (NCO 17), Lab Services Support (LSS), purchasing on behalf of the Central Texas Veterans Health Care System (CTVHCS) / VISN 17 Center of Excellence.
2. Nature and Description of the Action Being Approved
The Government intends to solicit from and award to a single source, Agilent Technologies, Inc., for one (1) Seahorse XF Pro Analyzer, including proprietary software, installation, operator training, and a 5-year extended warranty, on a firm-fixed-price basis.
3. Description of Supplies Required to Meet the Agency Need
The VISN 17 Center of Excellence requires a live-cell metabolic analysis platform capable of simultaneous real-time measurement of oxygen consumption rate (OCR) and proton efflux rate (PER) in a 96-well format to support biomedical research. The required item is the Agilent Seahorse XF Pro Analyzer, Stock No. S7855A / SYS-SE-XFPRO, including Wave Pro Controller software, Seahorse Analytics, installation, training, and extended warranty coverage. The estimated total value is $295,169.60.
4. Authority Permitting Solicitation From a Single Source
This requirement is a commercial product acquisition under FAR Part 12 as revised under the Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO). The estimated value of $295,169.60 is at or below the current Simplified Acquisition Threshold of $350,000. Accordingly, consistent with FAR 12.102(a), the Contracting Officer is documenting the decision that only one source is available and the basis for that decision. FAR Part 13 does not apply because the requirement is for a commercial product, not a noncommercial acquisition.
5. Demonstration That the Proposed Contractor’s Unique Qualifications Require Use of the Authority Cited
Agilent Technologies, Inc. is the only responsible source capable of meeting the Government’s minimum needs. The Seahorse XF Pro Analyzer is a proprietary commercial product uniquely capable of simultaneous OCR and PER measurement in live cells in a 96-well microplate format with integrated reagent injection, proprietary sensor cartridge technology, and the required Wave Pro and Seahorse Analytics software environment. Only licensed Agilent technicians are authorized to install, service, and train users on the system. No alternative source was identified that could provide a functionally equivalent system meeting all technical requirements.
6. Efforts Made to Ensure That Offers Are Solicited From as Many Potential Sources as Practicable
The contracting activity conducted extensive market research and public notice efforts. On June 24, 2026, Notice of Intent to Sole Source Notice ID 36C25726Q0645 was posted on SAM.gov for 13 calendar days, closing on July 7, 2026. No responses, objections, or capability statements were received. Additional market research included VetCert/SBA searches, GSA eLibrary review, AbilityOne review, FPI/UNICOR review, and review of recent federal procurement history. These efforts identified no additional capable sources.
7. Determination That the Anticipated Cost to the Government Will Be Fair and Reasonable
The anticipated cost of $295,169.60 is determined fair and reasonable based on the commercial nature of the product, comparison to recent federal acquisitions for similar Seahorse analyzer systems, and the proprietary status of the required item and support package. The acquisition includes hardware, proprietary software, installation, training, and a 5-year extended warranty.
8. Description of Market Research Conducted and Results
Market research was conducted in accordance with FAR Part 10 and VA acquisition procedures. The research included searches of VetCert/SBA for SDVOSB/VOSB sources under NAICS 334516, SAM.gov public notice, GSA eLibrary, AbilityOne, FPI/UNICOR, and review of federal procurement history. Results showed zero verified SDVOSB/VOSB sources, no other capable small business sources, no AbilityOne or FPI source, no GSA Schedule source for the analyzer itself, and no responses to the SAM.gov notice. Federal acquisition history for the Seahorse analyzer family reflected awards to Agilent Technologies, Inc.
9. Other Facts Supporting the Use of Sole Source Procedures
The Government’s minimum needs are based on unique research capabilities required by the CTVHCS / VISN 17 Center of Excellence. The required features are not unduly restrictive; rather, they reflect legitimate minimum needs that are only met by the Agilent Seahorse XF Pro platform. Proprietary software, manufacturer-authorized service, and compatibility requirements are integral to successful performance and cannot be separated from the supply requirement.
10. Listing of Sources That Expressed, in Writing, an Interest in the Acquisition
No sources expressed interest in writing in response to the public notice. No capability statements were received during the notice period.
11. Actions the Agency May Take to Remove or Overcome Barriers to Competition Before Subsequent Acquisitions
Prior to future acquisitions for similar research instrumentation, the Government will reassess the marketplace to determine whether additional commercial products or responsible sources become available. The requiring activity and contracting office will continue to monitor industry developments and procurement history. At present, the lack of competition is attributable to the proprietary nature of the required commercial product, not to any Government-created barrier.
12. Contracting Officer Certification
I certify that this justification is accurate and complete to the best of my knowledge and belief.
See attached document: Sole_Source_Justification_Seahorse_XF_Pro. CO signed.

1. Contracting Activity
Marine Corps Systems Command (M67854)

2. Description of the Action Being Approved
This Justification and Approval (J&A) authorizes and approves,
on a noncompetitive basis, award of a sole source contract to
Polaris Government and Defense (G&D) for the procurement of up
to 580 Ultra-Light Tactical Vehicles (ULTVs)comprised of ULTV
Logistics (ULTV-L) and ULTV High Power (ULTV-HP) variants.
3. Description of Supplies/Services
This J&A is to procure up to 580 ULTVs, spare repair parts, tool
kits, and field service representative support to meet Force
Design 2030 priority integration and fielding of systems in
accordance with fielding schedules of III Marine Expeditionary
Force (MEF), II MEF, supporting establishments, and integrated
programs.
The Program Manager Motor Transport (PM MT) has a requirement to
provide the operational forces with ULTV-L and ULTV-HP variants
capable of internal transport on MV-22 tilt rotor and CH-53
rotary wing aircraft for employment during littoral operations.
The ULTV improves operational capabilities for both infantry
logistics, long-range intelligence, surveillance, and
reconnaissance missions, as well as other designated missions in
support of distributed heliborne operations. The primary role of
the ULTV is as a logistics vehicle to transport ammunition and
other break bulk cargo and execute casualty evacuation missions.
DISTRIBUTION: DoW COMMUNITY ONLY
Estimated Dollar Value
The Independent Government Cost Estimate for the procurement is
$98M.
The funding table below shows the funding profile in millions of
dollars by FY and appropriation type.
Funding by FY and Appropriation ($M)
FY25 FY26 FY27 FY28 FY29 Total
PMC $12.04 $5.32 $21.13 $21.45 $10.91 $70.85
RDTE $0.04 $0.23 $0.24 $0.24 $0.25 $1.00
*Total $12.08 $5.55 $21.37 $21.69 $11.16 $71.85
*Due to budget cuts during Program Objective Memorandum FY26 (POM-26), PM
MT submitted a POM-27 decision package to provide funding for ULTV
procurement to reach full operational capability (FOC). Other Program
Management Offices (PMOs) requiring the ULTV as their prime mover have
also submitted POM decision packages to ensure procurement of the ULTV
supports reaching their FOC.
4. Statutory Authority Permitting Other Than Full and Open
Competition
The statutory authority permitting other than full and open
competition is 10 U.S.C. Section 3204(a)(1), “Only One
Responsible Source and No Other Supplies or Services Will
Satisfy Agency Requirements.”
5. Rationale Justifying Use of Cited Statutory Authority
In accordance with Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR)
6.302-1(a)(2)(ii)(A) and(B)and FAR 6.302-1(A)(2)(iii)(B),
award to a source other than Polaris G&D would result in
unacceptable delays and significant duplication of costs in
fulfilling the agency’s requirements for highly specialized
equipment and services in support of the ULTV program.
The ULTV was previously procured through a competitively
awarded General Services Administration (GSA) contract
47QFSA20D0005 which will expire in 2027. The contract ceiling
will be increased by $20M in 2025, and a follow-on contract
is not planned to be awarded. The remaining ceiling is
insufficient to cover PM MT’s required procurements and does
not include the ULTV-HP variant. Polaris G&D is the sole
designer, developer, and manufacturer of the ULTV-HP variant
and the only source with the requisite knowledge, experience,
and technical expertise to manufacture the ULTV-L and ULTV-HP
within the required scheduled delivery parameters.
2
DISTRIBUTION: DoW COMMUNITY ONLY
To meet fielding objectives, PM MT requires a production
capacity of thirty vehicles per month upon contract award.
Based on recent market research, only Polaris G&D can
immediately meet this requirement without causing a minimum
twelve-month in delay in production. In addition, several
critical Force Design Marine Corps systems dependent upon
integration onto the ULTV platform, such as the Light Marine
Air Defense Integrated System and the Common Aviation Command
and Control System, would be subjected to unacceptable delays
in providing these critical capabilities to deployed Marines.
Polaris G&D is also the only vendor with a current MV-22
internally transportable certification for both the ULTV-L
and ULTV-HP. This is a unique Marine Corps requirement for
the ULTV. Air certification of a like vehicle would take a
new vendor a minimum of twelve months to achieve.
The procurement of ULTVs from a new source would require
duplication of ULTV-HP variant research and development
efforts recently completed, some of which was government-
funded. In addition, associated operations and maintenance
manuals, a weapon’s mount engineering change proposal and
recently conducted studies for vehicle service life and
corrosion assessments have been conducted on the currently
fielded ULTV. Transitioning to another ultra-light tactical
vehicle at this stage of the program would require
significant redesign, integration, and testing of the ULTV-HP
variant. In addition, the currently approved gun mount would
have to undergo review, testing, and approval by the U.S Navy
Weapons Systems Explosive Safety Review Board prior to use
with a different base vehicle, adding additional expense and
schedule delays. The duplicative development cost of
transitioning to a different base vehicle as a replacement to
the currently fielded ULTV is estimated at $25M over a two-
year period.
Based on the current ULTV production schedule, high-power
development and testing, and MV-22 certification, it would
take another contractor a minimum of two years to meet the
contract requirements and require additional research and
development funding. Moreover, additional delay and costs
would be incurred to train personnel to maintain four (two
ULTV-L and two ULTV-HP variants) ultra-light vehicle
platforms as well as to provision parts and maintain a supply
system for the four variants. Introducing additional ultra-
light vehicle variants would cause unacceptable and costly
schedule delays and negatively impact United States Marine
Corps manpower and infrastructure. This would jeopardize both
the current ULTV fielding schedule and the critical Force
3
DISTRIBUTION: DoW COMMUNITY ONLY
Design systems that rely on the ULTV as a prime mover. Given
the recently completed market research, the substantial
duplication of costs would not be recovered through any type
of competition for this procurement.
6. Description of Efforts Made to Solicit Offers from as Many
Offerors as Practicable
A sources sought notice, M67854-24-I-0128, was issued on 15
July 2024 to assess industry’s capability to manufacture and
provide ULTVs, as well as associated special tooling, training,
operations/maintenance manuals, and field service
representative capability. Ten responses were received by 13
September 2024, one of which was from Polaris G&D. Of the
request for information (RFI) responses, three vendors were
deemed minimally viable to meet all Marine Corps requirements.
Of these three, Polaris G&D was deemed to be the most viable
vendor to meet all performance and production requirements in
the RFI. The other two vendors were assessed to require 18-24
months to establish high-power variant development, MV-22
internally transportable certification, and production
capacity.
Based on the assessment of the responses received, the
Government determined Polaris G&D to be the only identified
source able to fulfill the requirement for the procurement of
the ULTV-L and ULTV-HP, as well as associated special tooling,
training, and field service representatives for fielding to the
integrating programs.
In accordance with FAR 5.201, a notice of the proposed contract
action will be made through SAM.gov prior to solicitation.
7. Determination of Fair and Reasonable Cost
The Contracting Officer has determined the anticipated cost to
the Government of the supplies/services covered by this J&A will
be fair and reasonable.
8. Actions to Remove Barriers to Future Competition
For the reasons set forth in Paragraph 5, PM MT has no current
plan to compete future contracts for the types of
supplies/services covered by this document. If another potential
source emerges, PM MT will assess whether competition for future
requirements is feasible.
4
DISTRIBUTION: DoW COMMUNITY ONLY
If the Marine Corps decides to increase the acquisition
objective of the ULTVs beyond the initial 580 vehicles, PM MT
will assess whether competition for future requirements is
feasible. Any future actions will be reviewed by PM MT to
offer competition to the greatest extent possible.
5
DISTRIBUTION: DoW COMMUNITY ONLY

Federal notice (Justification), TRANSPORTATION, DEPARTMENT OF.FEDERAL AVIATION ADMINISTRATION.6973GH FRANCHISE ACQUISITION SVCS
Title: ASR-8 1618 to 1625 Conversion Kit
Solicitation number: 6973GH-26-J-ASR8
PSC: 4940; NAICS: 334511
Description: SINGLE SOURCE JUSTIFICATION FOR PRODUCTS, SERVICES AND CONSTRUCTION 1. Title of Procurement Procurement of ASR-8 1618 to 1625 Conversion Kit 2. Nature of Procurement Action The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) has identified a requirement to convert existing Airport Surveillance Radar (ASR-8) rotary joints from the Model 1618 configuration, designed for use with the Air Traffic Control Beacon Interrogator (ATCBI-5), to the Model 1625 configuration used with the Mode Select Beacon System (Mode-S). This effort supports the Brand-New Air Traffic Control System (BNATCS) under the Radar System Replacement (RSR) Program. Most ASR-8 sites currently employ the Model 1618 rotary joint; however, this configuration is not compatible with the RSR system that will replace the ASR-8 and ATCBI-5 systems. To ensure compatibility with the RSR architecture, the FAA has determined that existing Model 1618 rotary joints must be converted to the Model 1625 configuration utilized by ASR-8 and Mode-S systems. Frontgrade, the Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM), has developed a conversion kit to accomplish this modification. 3. Description of Supplies/Services The FAA proposes acquiring seventeen 1618 to1625 Conversion Kits to convert existing rotary joints and prevent any delays or loss of critical functions essential to the Radar System Replacement (RSR) Program. These kits are required for RSR to be completed at ASR-8 sites with an ATCBI-5 Secondary System. Without the converted joint, the radar cannot operate or be placed into service following RSR installation. 4. Authority Authority for single source procurement is provided by AMS policy section 3.2.2.4. 5. Market Analysis During RSR development, commercial off-the-shelf (COTS) solutions were evaluated for use across the ASR-8 and ASR-9 platforms to reduce sustainment complexity through common baseline management and address obsolescence concerns. Frontgrade�s 1618-to-1625 Conversion Kit was determined to be the solution that best met both current operational needs and Radar System Replacement (RSR) requirements. Consequently, the kit was approved for use within the National Airspace System (NAS). Frontgrade has also been the historical supplier of individual rotary joint components throughout the system's service life. 6. Rationale Supporting Use of a Single Source Frontgrade is the OEM for both the Model 1618 and Model 1625 rotary joints and is the proprietary owner and sole approved source for more than half of the components required for the conversion kit. The only alternative source for these components is operational stock currently reserved for the repair of existing Model 1625 rotary joints. Diverting these assets would degrade the FAA Logistics Center�s repair capability, reduce rotary joint availability, increase lead times, and elevate the risk of equipment shortages and potential NAS service impacts.

Federal notice (Special Notice), ENERGY, DEPARTMENT OF.ENERGY, DEPARTMENT OF
Title: Notice of Intent to Sole Source - Wolverine Escort Vehicle Light Chassis (W-EVLC)
Solicitation number: NAPAS315WEVLC

Description: This is a Notice of Intent to sole source to Wulco Inc. doing business as: NextGen Armor (NextGen), for the design and build of the First Article of Wolverine Escort Vehicle Light Chassis (W-EVLC) and development and delivery of Office of Secure Transportation�s (OST/NA-15) next generation W-EVLCs. NextGen owns the original EVLC proprietary design and complete technical data package (TDP) utilizing highly specialized Government-Furnished equipment (GFE). NextGen�s proprietary EVLC design is critical to the success of the new and modern W-EVLC. The current design includes a DoT compliant sleeper berth, safety-compliant equipment storage areas, and an OST Advanced Radio Enterprise System (ARES) communication suite incorporated into a specialized custom enclosure. The TDP encompasses all OST directed EVLC design changes, modifications, and engineered enhancements captured in tens of thousands of proprietary Computer-Aided Design (CAD) drawings dating back to 2010. NextGen is the only vendor with an in-depth knowledge and understanding of the complexities of the electrical, mechanical, internal cabling, power systems requirements, and integration of the ARES communications suite that has been fully tested to be forward and backwards compatible with the Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) vehicle chassis and electrical harnesses of the EVLC platform. The ARES communication suite will be an important component of the new W-EVLC design. NextGen owns all proprietary EVLC testing data, including how this data has changed due to OEM changes in order to meet stringent OST off-road and highway requirements. Leveraging this foundational dataset within the W-EVLC design-build phase minimizes engineering risk and eliminates redundant cycles by directly applying proven historical baselines to the new system configuration. NextGen is the only manufacturer capable of dismantling an EVLC and then reconstituting and re-engineering the re-usable �Aft-Body� into a new W-EVLC. NexGen�s manufacturing facility (on-site tooling, fabrication/testing stations, and disassemble line) has been optimally and efficiently configured to take an aging EVLC where it will be dismantled as follows: (1) removing the Aft-Body and then reconstituting it into the new W-EVLC build; (2) removing all exterior panels; (3) tearing down the engine and transmission; (4) removing all interior components; (5) creating a bill of materials for salvage or re-use; and (5) dismantling the chassis and suspension components. Though other vendors may be able to dismantle an EVLC, they will not be as efficient or effective since they may not know what part(s) should be marked for salvage, disposition or reconstitution into the new W-EVLC. NextGen is International Organization for Standardization (ISO) 9000/9001 and Association Connecting Electronics Industries (formerly known as Institute for Interconnecting and Packaging Electronic Circuits) (IPC) 610/620 certified and has an approved OST Site Security Plan designed to protect sensitive but unclassified information that requires safeguarding and dissemination controls (Controlled Unclassified Information). A new vendor would have to demonstrate that it meets the ISO 9000/9001 and IPC 610/620 certifications, including meeting OST�s Site Security Plan requirements. If a vendor does not meet either requirement, OST will experience delays that will significantly impact and disrupt its mission. NextGen on-site tooling, fabrication facilities/testing stations, and assembly line are pre-configured to mass produce the W-EVLC once the prototype is built, tested, and accepted by OST. It would be extremely challenging and difficult for another vendor to build or attempt to reverse-engineer the steps needed to build the next W-EVLC prototype using the re-usable Aft Body when the vendor�s production facility is not setup to mass produce the W-EVLC without years of pre-planning, trial and error, and a substantial investment of time and resources from OST personnel. This substantial duplication of cost, testing, and Government involvement is not only cost prohibitive, but it also has high likelihood to significantly delay and disrupt OST�s mission-critical schedule as more EVLCs approach and/or exceed their life cycle. Additionally, this could also result in an alternate system design, thereby creating unnecessary challenges and costs related to vehicle maintenance and fleet sustainment.

4. Description of Services or Supplies: This acquisition is for the procurement of two
(2) Creaform HandySCAN Pro handheld three-dimensional laser scanner package,
along with associated proprietary software licenses, hardware accessories, and multi-
year technical support agreements.
In layman's terms, a three-dimensional laser scanner is a highly specialized metrology
device that projects multiple blue laser lines onto a physical object to rapidly capture its
exact physical geometry and dimensions. The scanner translates this physical object
into a highly accurate digital "point cloud" or mesh model.
This digital data is then utilized for reverse engineering (recreating three-dimensional
models of legacy military parts that no longer have active supply chains) and high-
precision inspection (verifying that manufactured or repaired components perfectly
match their original blueprint specifications to prevent part failure).

accredit, and maintain a separate, parallel software ecosystem and forces operators to
undergo duplicate training protocols. This fragmentation creates a substantial
duplication of cost to the Government—including software licensing, Authority to
Operate (ATO) cybersecurity accreditation for new software, and specialized personnel
training—that is not expected to be recovered through competition. Therefore, Creaform
is the only brand capable of ensuring seamless workflow continuity and interoperability
without introducing unacceptable delays and unrecoverable costs.
b. Failure to approve this justification will result in unacceptable delays and a substantial
duplication of costs to the Government that cannot be recovered through competition.
Procuring a non-interoperable scanner forces the Government to abandon its
standardized digital engineering ecosystem, resulting in immediate operational
fragmentation. Specifically, the Government will incur unrecoverable financial and
temporal costs required to procure, accredit (including mandatory Authority to
Operate/Risk Management Framework cybersecurity approvals), and sustain a
redundant, parallel software architecture. Furthermore, introducing a disparate system
creates a critical, ongoing training burden. Given the high operational tempo and
frequent personnel turnover within the requiring activity, forcing operators to master
multiple, non-integrated metrology platforms severely degrades mission readiness and
creates unacceptable delays in establishing technical proficiency. Ultimately, this
fragmented workflow directly compromises the Government's ability to execute essential
dimensional validation and formal quality assurance, thereby degrading the immediate
mission capabilities and readiness of the requiring activity.

8. Market Research: Market research was conducted between 4 June and 23 June
2026 by , with technical input from , to identify all
qualified sources for a high-precision portable 3D scanning system. The research
confirmed that only the Creaform HandySCAN Pro meets the Government’s essential

requirements for interoperability, technical performance, and offline software
functionality.
The market research process included a comprehensive review of mandatory sources,
industry outreach, and an analysis of the commercial marketplace.
a. Mandatory Source Review (Conducted 10 June 2026): In accordance with FAR
Part 8, the AbilityOne Program, Federal Prison Industries (FPI/UNICOR), and
Army Computer Hardware, Enterprise Software and Solutions (CHESS) were
reviewed. None could provide the required equipment. A formal Statement of
Non-Availability (SoNA) was obtained from CHESS, authorizing an open market
procurement.
b. Industry Outreach:
• A Sources Sought notice posted to the Government Point of Entry (GPE)
from 4-11 June 2026 .
• A Request for Information (RFI) posted to GSA eBuy from 11-17 June
2026 to identify Federal Supply Schedule holders yielded zero responses.
c. Commercial Market Analysis: Research included direct review of Original
Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) and authorized distributor websites (
). This analysis confirmed the Creaform HandySCAN
Pro is a Commercial-Off-The-Shelf (COTS) item with a mature market.
Results and Conclusion: The combined results of this market research unequivocally
support a brand-name specification. The research demonstrates that other companies’
similar products do not meet, and cannot be modified to meet, the Government's critical
needs for interoperability and data continuity with identical systems already in use at
sister depots and engineering directorates. The outreach efforts failed to identify any
small businesses capable of providing the required brand-name product, making a small
business set-aside inappropriate as the "Rule of Two" cannot be met. Therefore, this
acquisition must proceed as a brand-name requirement competed among authorized
Creaform distributors to ensure technical compliance, warranty, and interoperability.

matters.title: Award to Florida Floats, Inc. DBA: Bellingham Marine
matters.text:
Federal notice (Justification), HOMELAND SECURITY, DEPARTMENT OF.US COAST GUARD.BASE MIAMI(00028)
Title: Award to Florida Floats, Inc. DBA: Bellingham Marine
Solicitation number: 70Z02826PMIAM0028
PSC: 6145; NAICS: 541330
Description: Notice of Intent to Award a Sole-Source Purchase Order U.S. Coast Guard Office of Procurement & Contracting (LOG-931) Summary of Requirement The U.S. Coast Guard (USCG) Office of Procurement & Contracting (LOG-931) Miami Detachment, on behalf of USCG Sector St. Petersburg, FL, intends to award a sole-source, firm-fixed-price purchase order to Florida Floats, Inc. (DBA: Bellingham Marine). The contractor shall furnish all materials, equipment, and services required to complete critical floating dock electrical repairs at USCG Sector St. Petersburg. Proposed Awardee: Florida Floats, Inc. (DBA: Bellingham Marine) Anticipated Award Value: $34,785.00 Contract Type: Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) Applicable NAICS Code: 541330 - Engineering Services Scope of Supplies & Services The contractor is required to deliver and install the following specific electrical components: 350 Linear Feet: New 200 AMP Power Cable to service the North and South Docks. As Required: 4C #1/0 Copper Portable Power Cable to re-feed the North and South Docks. Integration: Tie-in of new cabling to existing circuit breakers (previously feeding the North and South Docks) to power two (2) newly installed pedestals. Regulatory Authority & Justification Because this procurement is valued at $34,785.00, which falls below the Simplified Acquisition Threshold (SAT), this sole-source action is conducted under the authority of: FAR 13.106-1(b)(1) � Soliciting from a Single Source "Contracting officers may solicit from one source if the contracting officer determines that the circumstances of the contract action deem only one source reasonably available..." Technical & Operational Justification ? Project Linkage & Technical Continuity This electrical work is directly tied to Defense Logistics Agency (DLA) Project Number 22960286 (Replace Floating Dock Sector St. Pete). Bellingham Marine is the active on-site contractor executing the primary floating dock replacement. Performing this electrical work under the current work scope ensures a seamless structural and utility integration, avoiding divided operational liability between separate vendors. ? Operational Impact & Urgency Restoring power to the North and South docks is a direct prerequisite for establishing full immediate mission readiness for active boat crews stationed at Sector/Station St. Petersburg. ? Administrative & Fiscal Efficiency Procuring this cabling through a separate solicitation or a complex contract modification would introduce substantial administrative delays. Given the modest $34,785.00 project scale, a separate competitive procurement would result in duplicative mobilization costs and delay critical mission operations. Response Instructions & Disclaimer This notice is not a request for competitive quotes or proposals. However, interested parties may submit responses. To be considered, responses must demonstrate clear and convincing evidence that: Competition would be advantageous to the Government. A competitive procurement would not be cost or time-prohibitive. Conducting a competition would not hinder the mission objective of completing the floating dock repairs needed for active boat crews. The determination not to compete this proposed contract action based on responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. The Government is not responsible for any costs incurred by parties responding to this notice.

matters.text:
Federal notice (Presolicitation), DEPT OF DEFENSE.DEFENSE LOGISTICS AGENCY.DLA AVIATION
Title: Parker Hannifin Sole Source Parts
Solicitation number: SPE4A526R0250
PSC: 1560; NAICS: 336412
Description: Defense Logistics Agency (DLA) Aviation, Richmond proposes to issue a Letter Request for Proposal (RFP) to support a DLA Strategic Initiative. This strategic effort includes multiple NSNs to support various sole source weapon systems / operational platforms. A total of 32 NSNs for various platforms / weapon systems are targeted for this RFP and contract action. OEM Parker Hannifin Corporation (59211) has been identified as the approved source of supply for the listed items; therefore, the proposed action is intended to be awarded on a sole source basis to the OEM. It is anticipated that 32 items will be awarded and priced with lead-times as add-ons to the OEM's existing Long-Term Contracts (LTCs): Captains of Industry (COI) Supplier Capabilities Contract (SCC) SPE4AX-21-D-9402 for commercial items and SPE4AX-21-D-9403 for military unique items (Parker Hannifin Commercial Subsumable Contract). It is the Government's intent to use a letter solicitation format to the sole source Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM); therefore, if a non-OEM source is interested in any of the NSNs, please notify the Contracting Officer prior to the synopsis closing date. These items have been identified as sole source; however, some items may have history showing awards to other than the OEM. Surplus dealers are also invited to respond to this synopsis. The response should include a completed surplus certificate, DLA Procurement Note 04, Government Surplus Property Material or adequate traceability documentation to show that the product is acceptable. (Note: DLA Procurement Note M05 Evaluation Factor for Unused Former Government Surplus Property, will apply and other Aviation sites will provide their equivalent surplus documentation, as applicable). Responses to this announcement from other than the OEM should identify items of interest and include evidence of ability to supply the items in accordance with the aforementioned acquisition strategy. In addition, respondents should identify the available quantities, prices, and lead-times. DLA will consider all such responses and may alter the acquisition strategy if purchase of existing surplus or newly manufactured inventory is in the best interest of the government. Responses to this announcement from other than the OEM are required by Thursday, July 23, 2026. A copy of the letter of interest should be forwarded to the contracting officer identified. If your company desires to be reviewed and qualified as an "Approved Source" for any of the items listed, submit an application package through the Source Approval Request (SAR) Program as outlined in the attached SAR document. A SAR package contains all of the technical data needed to demonstrate that the prospective contractor can competently manufacture the product to the same level of quality, or better, than the Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM). The onus is on the contractor to document and demonstrate their product is equal to, or better, than the currently approved item which DLA Aviation is procuring. (Note: To submit your SAR please send an email to: dlaavnsmallbus@dla.mil, subject� request a SAR drop off�. After we receive your email request a �request for drop off� will be returned, where you can download your file. Include CAGE code, the NSN, and the email address where you want to receive the link. For guidance on completing a SAR package, please review the Source Approval Handbook. Current procurements will not be held pending review; therefore, any actions will be for future procurements or strategic efforts.) Export Control: Items cited require data which is restricted to contractors certified by DoD to access unclassified data per DoD 5220.22M. Certification is obtained by submitting DD Form 2345, Military Critical Technical Data Agreement, to the Defense Logistics Information Services. Additionally, letters expressing interest in subcontracting provided to the Contracting Officer will be forwarded to the identified Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM). FAR Parts 12 / 15 procedures may apply. The attached 32 NSNs have been identified for the current procurement. If other NSNs are subsequently added, as defined by this strategic initiative and contract terms, they will be synopsized separately. The anticipated closing date August 31, 2026. If you are interested in this opportunity, you may contact Kenya Allamby at kenya.allamby@dla.mil.

matters.title: Justification for other than full and open competition for UV printer
matters.text:
Federal notice (Justification), STATE, DEPARTMENT OF.STATE, DEPARTMENT OF.US EMBASSY BANGKOK
Title: Justification for other than full and open competition for UV printer
Solicitation number: 19TH2026P1318
PSC: 3610; NAICS: 3231
Description: The Roland VersaObject MO-240 UV printer is the only market solution capable of meeting all technical and operational agency requirements within budget. Alternative brands and models evaluated either failed to support core project requirements or substantially exceeded the necessary scope at a prohibitive price point. Additionally, operational constraints require a localized vendor to eliminate customs clearance delays, international freight surcharges, and extended transport timelines, ensuring a strict 5-day delivery window post-purchase order issuance. The equipment must natively feature a built-in 220V power supply to match Embassy infrastructure, and the vendor must guarantee 24-hour supply replenishment alongside complimentary, in-person training and on-site warranty servicing. If this hardware is not procured urgently through this vendor, the Embassy will lose the capability to complete the project work in-house. Forcing this project to an outside contractor will result in significantly higher outsourced labor and material costs. Furthermore, outsourcing introduces severe operational risks, including missed milestones, unless substantial expedited processing fees and overtime labor costs are incurred.

matters.title: Troll Systems Equipment
matters.text:
Federal notice (Justification), TRANSPORTATION, DEPARTMENT OF.FEDERAL AVIATION ADMINISTRATION.6973GH FRANCHISE ACQUISITION SVCS
Title: Troll Systems Equipment
Solicitation number: 6973GH-26-S-Troll
PSC: 5820; NAICS: 334220
Description: SINGLE SOURCE JUSTIFICATION FOR PRODUCTS, SERVICES AND CONSTRUCTION 1. Title of Procurement Customs and Border Protection (CBP) Air and Marine Operations (AMO) procurement of Troll branded equipment in Support of the Aircraft Video Downlink (AVDL) system. Purchase request number AC-26-03727 2. Nature of Procurement Action The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) proposes the acquisition of Troll Systems equipment through Single Source procedures. The proposed vendor is Troll Systems, 24950 Anza Drive, Valencia, CA 91355 (SAM UEID NKHRJR5PMKL3). Troll Systems is the only known source that can provide the equipment necessary for the AMO AVDL system that can satisfy this requirement. 3. Description of Supplies/Services Under an inter-agency agreement with DHS, the FAA is responsible for lifecycle support of Air and Marine Operations (AMO) Aircraft Video Downlink (AVDL) ground receive stations. The aircraft transmitting video to these stations has undergone a technical refresh and now are being delivered with Troll Systems video equipment. The existing terrestrial site receiving equipment is required to maintain serviceability. For this effort, the FAA is looking to process an Indefinite Delivery / Indefinite Quantity (ID/IQ) type contract to support the required system upgrade. As the AVDL program is expected to utilize the Troll Systems equipment into the foreseeable future, it would be most effective to put the ID/IQ contract in place to provide more efficiency for future efforts, including the procurement of spares and repairs. 4. Authority Authority for single source procurement is provided by AMS policy section 3.2.2.4. 5. Market Analysis A formal public announcement was posted to the System for Award Management website (SAM.gov) on March 30, 2026, with a response due date of April 6, 2026. Troll Systems (the OEM) was the only vendor that responded to the Market Survey. No other entity responded to the posting. The Notice ID for the posting is 6973GH26CBPTROLLRADIOEQUIPMENT. Additional Market research was performed using the Internet, which helped determine the estimated amounts required for this effort. Based upon Troll Systems being the OEM of the system and provided the only response to the formal Market Survey along with additional market research, Troll Systems is the only source that can provide the required equipment and services to meet the need for this effort. 6. Rationale Supporting Use of a Single Source Troll Systems is the Original Equipment Manufacturer for the Troll X750 Remote Site Controllers. Troll Systems does not have any resellers or distributors for their equipment. For the AMO Terrestrial Sites to serve their intended purpose, the configuration must be the same across the ground stations in the field. As the aircraft are now equipped with the Troll Linkbox, the optimal receive site configuration (antenna controllers and receivers) must be Troll. There is not another government contract that can satisfy this requirement. Troll does not have a network of distributors and is the sole source of this equipment. This award is being processed under Single Source Procedures, based upon the vendor�s knowledge and experience in this type of equipment and configuration as the Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM). The current request is also urgent in that, without a contract vehicle in place, the AVDL system is not operating at full capacity. It is expected that in the Base Year, several systems will be procured and deployed across the AVDL program. Specialized Expertise. Troll Systems is the only known vendor that can provide the appropriate parts and services to ensure a proper fit and function for the AVDL system, ensuring proper operation for the end user. Due to the uniqueness of the components of AVDL, Troll Systems knowledge and expertise is the only known source that will satisfy the needs of the Government. As the OEM of the design and maintenance of the tracking system, Troll Systems� expertise is needed to ensure proper configuration. Without acquiring these parts and services, AVDL systems would be inoperable and the CBP Agents will be unable to surveil in sensitive operational areas. Time Constraints. The equipment and configuration services are needed immediately to support the CBP AVDL system for many special events. The equipment is deployed on CBP aircraft (fixed wing and helicopters) to surveil special events including sporting events such as the Super Bowl and other high-profile events. The previous equipment has become obsolete, and the Troll equipment is the upgrade replacing the older system. Thus, this contract is needed to ensure these systems remain in operational status. Without this effort, illegal threats will continue to enter the United States undetected and cause harm to the United States and citizens. This includes the smuggling of people (e.g. � human trafficking with examples shown below), deaths caused by drugs (e.g. � fentanyl deaths as stated below) or harm from weapons (e.g. � information on weapons as shown below). In the case of weapons smuggling, the threat is greater for weapons to be trafficked from the United States. Patents, Proprietary Data, and Unique Items. Troll Systems is the only known source that can provide the required parts and repair services as parts are proprietary to Troll Systems and only Troll Systems has the specifications information. When these systems were procured, the Government did not purchase all necessary technical, logistics, and maintenance data needed to support this requirement. The data and knowledge necessary to manufacture and repair these parts are the exclusive proprietary property of Troll Systems. Troll Systems has not licensed this data or knowledge to any other vendors. Troll Systems will not sell or otherwise provide data, knowledge, or other intellectual property necessary to compete the required support. The proprietary nature of this requirement was confirmed through a proprietary letter from Troll Systems dated June 17, 2026. 7. Other Facts Supporting Use of Single Source At this time and due to configuration requirements, the Troll Systems brand equipment is the only equipment that will satisfy the need of the CBP AMO program. If CBP revises the system in the future, the FAA will support through proper Acquisition Management System (AMS) procedures to ensure competition is utilized to maximum extent.

Workbook Tabs: Initial SLTCs � Items intended to be awarded with or shortly after the basic contract(s). All Consumables � Items that may be considered for award over the life of the contract(s). DLRs � Service managed items that may be considered for award either initially or over the life of the contract(s). THIS SOURCES SOUGHT IS FOR INFOMATIONAL PURPOSES ONLY. THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL. IT DOES NOT CONSTITUE A SOLICITATION AND SHALL NOT BE CONSTRUED AS A COMMITMENT BY THE GOVERNMENT. RESPONSES IN ANY FORM ARE NOT OFFERS AND THE GOVERNMENT IS UNDER NO OBLIGATION TO AWARD A CONTRACT AS A RESULT OF THIS ANNOUNCEMENT. NO FUNDS ARE AVAILABLE TO PAY FOR PREPARATION OF RESPONSES TO THIS ANNOUNCEMENT. ANY INFORMATION SUBMITTED BY RESPONDENTS TO THIS TECHNICAL DESCRIPTION IS STRICTLTY VOLUNTARY. Current Collins Contracts with the Defense Logistics Agency (DLA) Aviation acquire sole source consumable parts and depot-level reparables (DLR) for aircraft and systems supporting worldwide DLA direct (DD) & Customer Direct (DVD) shipments under Federal Acquisition Regulations (FAR) Part 12 and Part 15. Collins� current contract (SPE4AX18D9402) was issued May 01, 2018, as a 5-year, fixed-price, requirements type contract (RTC) with one five-year option period. The contract is structured as an �Umbrella� with numerous �Subsumable� contracts issued to Collins individual business units. The contract is currently within the third year of the option period. DLA aims to initially maintain the scope of the subsumable contracts, by issuing separate contracts to each business unit under a Basic Agreement (yet to be negotiated) for which the Government intends to solicit and negotiate with only one source as authorized by 10 U.S.C. 3204(a)(1) and FAR 6.302-1. The basic agreement and individual contracts will support DLA-Direct (stock) purchases. Any future performance-based projects may incorporate the basic agreement as a baseline but will be separately solicited and negotiated on an as-needed basis. If any such projects relating to the Collins-DLA relationship are identified, market research will be performed to ensure these subsequent phases are sole source to Collins. Market research techniques will include, but are not limited to, industry feedback, synopses, Requests for information (RFI), technical reviews and information obtained from the applicable Services regarding drawings and technical data rights. Interested persons may identify their interest and capability to respond to this requirement or submit proposals. This notice of intent is not a request for competitive proposals. However, all proposals received by the synopsis response date will be considered by the Government. A determination by the Government not to compete this proposed contract based upon responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. Information received will normally be considered solely for the purpose of determining whether to conduct a competitive procurement. RESPONSES: DLA requires that only non-proprietary information be submitted in response to this Sources Sought Notice. DLA shall not be liable for or suffer any consequential damages for the use of any proprietary information submitted. 1. Responses are required no later than August 30, 2026. 2. Respondents shall provide the following company information: Company Name / Address Contractor and Government Entity (CAGE) Code Data Universal Numbering System (DUNS) Number Point of Contact Phone / Fax Number Email Address Web Page URL Size of Business relative to North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) Code (Small Business Size Standard employees or less), and the socioeconomic category of your company, if applicable United States (U.S.) or Foreign Owned Entity Please indicate whether your interest is as a prime contractor or as a subcontractor 3. Respondents must address Their capability to supply the items listed in the attachment and indicate what prior experience they have on efforts that are similar in nature and scope. The date by which they will submit a Source Approval Request (SAR) for approval of an alternate source. Willingness to provide up front pricing for the total validity period of the contract(s). SUBMISSION OF INFORMATION: Responses to this Sources Sought Notice must be readable by Microsoft Office or Adobe software. Responses to this Sources Sought Notice shall be unclassified and should not exceed 20 pages in length. Please note: Emails containing file types such as .zip, .xlsx, docx, or other macro-enabled extensions, may not be delivered to the intended recipient. All responses and questions under this Sources Sought Notice must be transmitted electronically via e-mail to John Whaley at john.whaley@dla.mil. Prior to the response date, if necessary, potential respondents may request clarifications by email. Significant responses to a potential respondent's request for clarification will be posted to FedBizOpps under this Sources Sought Notice. This effort has been identified as sole source to Collins Aerospace. Responses to this announcement from other than the original equipment manufacturer (OEM) are required by August 30, 2026 and should identify areas of interest and include evidence of ability to perform. A copy of the letter of interest should be forwarded to the Contracting Officer identified herein and Small Business Administration (SBA) Procurement Center Representative (PCR) (steven.powell@sba.gov). Any alternate source must submit the appropriate data and receive approval by the cognizant Government engineering support activity (ESA). The Government may alter the acquisition strategy if it is in the best interest of the Government. If your company desires to be reviewed and qualified as an �Approved Source� for the item in the Sources Sought Workbook, submit an application package through the Source Approval Request (SAR) Program as outlined in the attached SAR document. A SAR package contains all of the technical data needed to demonstrate that the prospective contractor can competently manufacture the product to the same level of quality, or better, than the Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM). The onus is on the contractor to document and demonstrate their product is equal to, or better, than the currently approved item, which DLA Aviation is procuring. If there is an open solicitation for a NSN, to which you want to submit a SAR, please submit the SAR directly to the buyer noted on the solicitation. If you are submitting a SAR for a NSN with no open solicitation, please send it to the Competition Advocate SAR Program Office address below: SAR Program DLA Aviation Attn: DLA AVN-DU (SAR Program Manager) 6090 STRATHMORE ROAD Richmond, VA 23297-5100 See attached SAR guidelines for additional information. matters.title: Videographer and a photographer for Freedom 250 Events
matters.text:
Federal notice (Justification), STATE, DEPARTMENT OF.STATE, DEPARTMENT OF.U.S. EMBASSY ZAGREB
Title: Videographer and a photographer for Freedom 250 Events
Solicitation number: PR16093765
PSC: 5836; NAICS: 
Description: The Department of State requires the services of a qualified videographer and photographer to provide comprehensive documentation coverage of all Freedom 250 events over a 10-day period. Services include, but are not limited to: On-site video recording and photography at all Freedom 250 event venues Editing and delivery of final video and photographic products in formats specified by the Government Availability for the full duration of all scheduled and unscheduled Freedom 250 events across the 10-day period The proposed contractor has demonstrated unique qualifications that make them the only viable source capable of fulfilling this requirement. Specifically: Established Familiarity with Freedom 250 Events: The proposed contractor has developed an in-depth understanding of the Freedom 250 event structure, key personnel, operational tempo, and logistical requirements. This institutional knowledge is critical to ensuring seamless, uninterrupted visual documentation across all events during the 10-day period. Specialized Technical Capability: The proposed contractor possesses specialized equipment, technical expertise, and production capabilities tailored to the specific visual documentation standards required for Freedom 250 events. Continuity of Visual Record: The proposed contractor will be involved in all Freedom 250 documentation efforts, providing an unbroken visual record that is essential for historical, archival, and communications purposes. Introducing a new vendor would create inconsistency in style, quality, and contextual understanding of the subject matter. The requirement demands a single, cohesive team of videography and photography professionals who can provide consistent, coordinated coverage across all Freedom 250 events. Splitting this requirement among multiple vendors or conducting a phased competition would result in fragmented deliverables and undermine the integrity of the final product. Visual documentation of Freedom 250 events serves a critical public diplomacy and strategic communications function for the Department of State. Any gap in coverage or degradation in quality resulting from a vendor transition would directly harm the Department's ability to communicate key messages to domestic and international audiences.

matters.text:
Federal notice (Presolicitation), DEPT OF DEFENSE.DEFENSE LOGISTICS AGENCY.DLA AVIATION
Title: Moog, Inc. Requirements Type LTC for Sole Source Consumable Spare Parts
Solicitation number: SPE4AX26R0010
PSC: 5977; NAICS: 336413
Description: The Defense Logistics Agency (DLA) Weapons Support Richmond, VA intends to issue a solicitation for consumable and Depot Level Reparable (DLR) spare part support for sole source items assigned to Moog, Inc. facility CAGE 99932 located in Blacksburg, VA. This acquisition intends to renew the Moog Joint Opportunity Contract SPE4AX-17-D-9415 that expires on August 24, 2027. Moog, Inc. is currently the sole source manufacturer for the parts scheduled for solicitation and the acquisition will be conducted using other than full and open competition procedures in accordance with10 U.S.C 2304 (c)(1) and FAR 6.103-1 (Class Deviation 2026-O0017), Only One Responsible Source and No Other Supplies or Services Will Satisfy Agency Requirements. The government procures these items on a part number basis and does not possess any technical data. The solicitation will be for a ten-year requirements type long-term contract. There will be one five-year base period and one five-year option period. Pricing terms will be firm fixed price with a price redetermination conducted concurrently when exercising the option period. An Economic Price Adjustment clause is also likely to be used for price adjustments. Once items are added, they will remain on contract with Moog, Inc. until the final expiration of the contract unless they become competitive items. The eventual contract is intended to be awarded as non-commercial using FAR Part 15 (Class Deviation 2026-O0048) procedures. The items support various weapon systems. Shipments will be made on a DLA direct basis. The estimated solicitation issue date for the Request for Proposal is August 14, 2026. It is the Government�s intent to conduct a sole source acquisition with the Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM); therefore, if any non-OEM source is interested in the NSNs listed in the attachment to this synopsis, please notify the Contracting Officer prior to the synopsis closing date. Surplus dealers are also invited to respond to this synopsis. The response should include a completed surplus certificate, DLA Procurement Note 04, Unused Former Government Surplus Property or adequate traceability documentation to show that the product is acceptable. (Note: DLA Procurement Note M05 Evaluation Factor For Unused Former Government Surplus Property will apply and other Aviation sites will provide their equivalent surplus documentation, as applicable). Responses to this announcement from other than the OEM should identify items of interest and include evidence of ability to supply the items for the contract period as identified. In addition, respondents should identify the quantity available and price. A copy of the letter of interest should be forwarded to the contracting officer identified herein and SBA PCR (Steven.Powell@sba.gov). The Government may alter the acquisition strategy if purchase of existing surplus or newly-manufactured inventory is in the best interest of the Government. Synopsis contains an attachment with the NSN, Part Number, CAGE, Nomenclature, and Estimated Annual Demand Quantity (EAQ). All responses received by the response date will be considered by the Government. A determination by the Government not to compete this proposed contract based upon responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. Information received will normally be considered solely for the purpose of determining whether to conduct a competitive procurement. This synopsis is for informational purposes only. This is not a Request for Proposal. It does not constitute a solicitation and shall not be construed as a commitment by the government. Responses in any form are not offers and the government is under no obligation to award a contract as a result of this announcement. No funds are available to pay for preparation of responses to this announcement. Any information submitted by respondents is strictly voluntary.
