NAVSEA CONTRACTS HANDBOOK
JUSTIFICATION AND APPROVAL
FOR USE OF
OTHER THAN FULL AND OPEN COMPETITION
N0016425RWP18
J&A Number: CR-24033
DEPARTMENT OF THE NAVY
NAVAL SURFACE WARFARE CENTER
CRANE DIVISION
300 HIGHWAY 361 IN REPLY REFER TO:
CRANE INDIANA 47522-5001 J&A Number: CR-24033
Code: 0241
P.R.: N0016425RWP18
JUSTIFICATION AND APPROVAL
FOR USE OF OTHER THAN FULL AND OPEN COMPETITION
1. Contracting Activity
Naval Sea Systems Command (NAVSEA), Naval Surface Warfare Center, Crane Division
(NSWC Crane), Spectrum Warfare Contracts Division, (024).
2. Description of the Action Being Approved
Award of a Firm-Fixed Price (FFP), Indefinite Delivery, Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ), supply
contract with an ordering period of five (5) years on a sole source basis for the repair, upgrade,
and/or manufacture of Solid State High Voltage Switches (SSHVS) and 2kV Bias Power Supplies
(BPS), in support of AN/SPS-49A(V)1 series of radar systems to Polarity, Inc., 11294 Sunshine
Park Drive, Rancho Cordova, CA 95742 (CAGE 1KQE1).
3. Description of Supplies/Services
The requirement is for repair, upgrade, and/or manufacture of SSHVS and 2kV BPS. The SSHVS
and 2kV BPS are used in a Solid-State Modulator (SSM) for the AN/SPS-49A(V)1 series of radar
systems to manufacture the existing switch tube modulator design used to pulse modulate a
Varian/CPI VA-889F Klystron. The SSMs are part of Field Change Kit (FC5) for installation
aboard Navy ships. This requirement will also include Engineering Services to support
Engineering Investigations and redesign efforts for replacement of Diminishing Manufacturing
Sources and Material Shortages (DMSMS) components identified and confirmed by the
Government to be critical parts in the SSHVS and BPS assemblies. It is anticipated that this will
be a cost-plus-fixed-fee (CPFF) CLIN; however, the preponderance of the contract will be a firm
fixed supply contract.
Award of a 5-year supply FFP IDIQ contract is intended. This IDIQ will be for a maximum of
$6,600,000 over a 5-year period and will be funded with appropriations from Navy Working
Capital Funds (WCF), Operations and Maintenance Navy Funds (OM&N), and Foreign Military
Sales (FMS). An estimate of the proposed contract utilization is listed in the following table.
J&A Number: CR-24033
Estimated Dollar Value
FY25 – FY29
Total
Supply WCF $ 5,900,000.00
O&MN $ 300,000.00
FMS $ 400,000.00
Total $ 6,600,000.00
4. Statutory Authority Permitting Other Than Full and Open Competition
10 U.S.C. 3204(a)(1), as implemented by FAR 6-302.1, only one responsible source or only a
limited number of responsible sources and no other type of property or services will satisfy the
needs of the agency.
5. Rationale Justifying Use of Cited Statutory Authority
The Government has a requirement to repair failed SSHVSs and repair and/or upgrade
(Engineering Change Proposal (ECP) 0049-065) 2kV BPS within the SSM of the AN/SPS-49
Radar System. The Government also has a requirement to manufacture the failed SSHVSs and
2kV BPS when repair efforts fail in order to maintain the capability of the AN/SPS-49 Radar
System within the US Navy’s Fleet.
The Government previously issued three separate contracts with two different vendors, DTI
Incorporated and Raytheon Electronic Systems, to develop SSHVSs and 2kV BPS that meet the
Government's requirements. DTI was tasked to deliver a prototype solid state modulator under
phase II SBIR contract N00014-99-C-0234 and two (2) pre-production kits under N00164-02-C-
6002. Raytheon was tasked to build an SSM kit (FC 5) under contract N00024-01-C-5254. Both
companies failed to provide an acceptable product.
After those failures, NSWC Crane, Code WXP tasked Technology Service Corporation (TSC) to
pursue this effort under engineering support contract, N00164-01-D-0039. TSC subcontracted to
Polarity, Inc. to design/develop a switch and bias supply that would meet the Government's
requirements. Polarity developed engineering developmental models (EDMs) that passed
engineering design verification testing and acceptance testing, and was subsequently awarded a
one-time, sole-source production contract for the SSHVSs and 2kV BPS, N00164-07-D-8916.
Polarity was awarded second and third sole-source contracts, N00164-13-R-GR23 & N00164-20-
D-WP53, to continue repair and manufacturing SSHVS and BPS.
Requirements have arisen for the procurement of new production units, as well as the capability
to repair and upgrade the SSM units that were not originally accounted for on contract N00164-
13-R-GR23. The original production units have been installed in 31 ships in the Fleet, as well as
six (6) land-based sites. Due to the high operational tempo of the radar system running 24 hours a
day/7 days a week at high temperatures, these switches and bias supplies are beginning to fail,
and require repair and/or replacement by newly manufactured units. These units are made with
multiple electronic components that will reach the end of their life cycle due to its continuous
operation within the AN/SPS-49 Radar System.
J&A Number: CR-24033
Utilizing any source other than Polarity for repair or manufacture efforts would result in
substantial duplication of cost. It is estimated that the development of another source would create
a delay of 18-24 months, which would cost the Government, at a minimum, an additional
$11,064,102. Failure to provide a SSHVS or 2kV BPS in the most expedient way will leave these
ships without a functioning AN/SPS 49 Radar System which would jeopardize the defense of the
ship. Due to funding constraints, developing an alternative source cannot be economically or
technically supported.
Additionally, the investment the Navy has already made (over $5M on contracts N00164-01-D-
0039, N00164-07-D-8916, and N00164-13-R-GR23) towards development and production of the
SSHVSs and 2kV BPS that are currently installed on 31 U.S. Navy Ships, would not be recouped
through competition.
Utilizing any source other than Polarity would also result in unacceptable delays in the agency’s
requirements. Based on the Fleet costs that would be incurred during the time involved to re-
qualify and perform compatibility testing on a competitor’s product, it would not be in the best
interest of the Government to duplicate this effort. Such a delay in schedule and cost would result
in increased risks and seriously jeopardize the US Navy’s Fleet
6. Description of Efforts Made to Solicit Offers from as Many Offerors as Practicable
The Government has attempted to repair SSHVS and BPS on a limited basis with the approval of
the In-Service Engineering Agent (ISEA). These efforts were similar to reverse engineering
efforts. The Government was unsuccessful in reverse engineering both the SSHVS and BPS, and
without a detailed Technical Data Package (TDP), there is nothing for other vendors to base their
proposals on. Furthermore, companies performing similar repairs were contacted during market
research but stated that without a complete TDP, they would not be able to perform the required
manufacturing and repairs.
The proposed contract sources sought was posted on the Government Point of Entry (GPE)
SAM.gov website on 04 June 2024. One interested party, Telecommunication Support Services,
Inc. (dba: TSS Solutions), expressed interest and provided a capability statement concerning this
requirement. The capability statement was reviewed by the RTA, and determined that TSS
Solutions is capable of doing this work and providing the SSHVS and BPS. Although TSS
Solutions is capable of performing the requirement, due to the Government not owning the data
rights and the time and cost detriment it would be to the Government, the Government’s position
is to keep this requirement as sole source. Changing to a different vendor at this point in time
would cause an unacceptable time delay due to having to start the acquisition process completely
over and having new prototypes made, and adding time to get the new data rights qualified. This
would also cause a cost detriment to the Government in duplicating the work and qualifying the
data rights.
TSS Solutions was notified of the Government’s findings on 12 August 2024 and responded on
12 August 2024 concurring and accepting the Government’s basis for the sole source.
J&A Number: CR-24033
In accordance with DFARS 205.205-71 the proposed contract was synopsized on the Government
Point of Entry (GPE) SAM.gov website on 12 August 2024. To date, no interested parties have
expressed interest or provided feedback.
7. Determination of Fair and Reasonable Costs
The Contracting Officer has determined the anticipated cost to the Government of the
supplies/services covered by this J&A will be fair and reasonable.
8. Actions to Remove Barriers to Competition
For the reasons set forth in Section 5 and Section 6, NSWC Crane has no plans at this time to
compete future contracts for the types of supplies covered by this contract. Market conditions are
continuously being monitored, and if another potential source emerges, NSWC Crane will assess
whether competition for a future requirement is feasible.
J&A Number: CR-24033

matters.title: Senegal MILES IWS 2 Notice of Intent to Sole Source
matters.text:
Federal notice (Special Notice), DEPT OF DEFENSE.DEPT OF THE ARMY.W6QK ACC-APG-ORLANDO
Title: Senegal MILES IWS 2 Notice of Intent to Sole Source
Solicitation number: PANORL-26-P-0000-026741
PSC: 6920; NAICS: 333310
Description: The Army Contracting Command-Orlando (ACC-ORL) intends to solicit and award a Firm-Fixed-Price contract on an Other Than Full and Open Competition basis to Cubic Defense Applications, Inc., (Cubic) CAGE 94987, 9233 Balboa Avenue, San Diego, CA 92123 for the procurement of Multiple Integrated Laser Engagement System - Individual Weapon System 2 (MILES-IWS2) kits and associated New Equipment Training (NET) for the country of Senegal. The applicable North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code is 333310 (Commercial and Service Industry Machinery Manufacturing) with a small business size standard of 1,000 employees, and the Product Service Code (PSC) is 6920 (Armament Training Devices). Requirement Description: The Government requires the production and delivery of fifty-five (55) MILES IWS2 kits (to include harnesses, halos, and Small Arms Transmitters), and the execution of a five (5) day New Equipment Training (NET) event in Senegal. Period of Performance & Funding: The Period of Performance for this effort is anticipated to be 01 October 2026 through 31 December 2027. This execution window accommodates hardware production, extended Defense Transportation System (DTS) shipping transit times, and the subsequent execution of the NET event. This effort utilizes 10 United States Code (U.S.C.) Section 333 Building Partner Capacity (BPC) funds which will be obligated prior to their statutory expiration on 30 September 2026. Statutory Authority: The proposed contract action is for supplies/services for which the Government intends to solicit and negotiate with one source, Cubic Defense Applications, Inc., under the authority of 10 U.S.C. � 3204(a)(1), as implemented by FAR 6.103-1 (Only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements). This equipment is proprietary to Cubic, the Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM). Cubic possesses unique qualifications that include proprietary hardware and software architectures, knowledge of the equipment�s design, and the technical data required to ensure mission-critical interoperability with U.S. and Allied forces during joint training exercises. Market Research: The requirement is being solicited on a sole-source basis. The Government conducted market research in accordance with FAR Part 10. Sources Sought Notice, PANORL-26-P-0000-026741, was posted to SAM.gov on 13 May 2026 and closed on 26 May 2026. Market research concluded that Cubic is the only responsible source that possesses the intellectual property rights and engineering capabilities to independently manufacture and meet the technical specifications for the MILES-IWS2 system. Submission Instructions: THIS NOTICE OF INTENT IS NOT A SOLICITATION, REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL, OR A REQUEST FOR QUOTATION. A solicitation package will NOT be issued, and requests for copies of a solicitation will not be honored or acknowledged. However, the Government will consider all responses received within 10 days of the publication of this notice. Firms who want to challenge the sole-source determination must submit an interest letter that clearly demonstrates their firm's ability to manufacture and meet all original OEM specifications without requiring reverse-engineering, acting as a non-manufacturing pass-through reseller, or causing unacceptable mission delays. Information received in response to this notice will be considered solely for the purpose of determining whether conducting a competitive procurement in the future is in the best interest of the Government. All information submitted should support the offeror's capability to provide the supplies required and shall be furnished at no cost or obligation to the Government. Responses or questions must be in writing and transmitted via email referencing "ACC-ORL_NOI_SS_SENEGAL_MILES_[Your Company Name]". Send email no later than [Insert Date 10 days from Posting], 12:00 p.m. (EDT) to: Contract Specialist Sherrie.r.moore.civ@army.mil and George.c.coker2.civ@army.mil.

Description: This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial items prepared in accordance with the format in FAR subpart 12.6, as supplemented with additional information included in this notice. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation; quotations are being requested and a written solicitation will not be issued. Solicitation number 70Z03826QB0000146 is issued as a request for quotation (RFQ). This solicitation document and incorporated provisions and clauses are those in effect as of November 28, 2025, IAW the Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO). The applicable North American Industry Classification Standard Code is 336413. The small business size standard is 1,250 employees. This is a restricted requirement. All responsible sources may submit a quotation which shall be considered by the agency. It is anticipated that a firm-fixed price purchase order will be awarded on a brand name basis as a result of this synopsis/solicitation. All parts must have clear traceability to the Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM), Kulite Semiconductor Products Inc (Cage Code 34345). Traceability means a clear, complete, documented, and auditable paper trail which traces each step from an OEM or approved source. See attached documents titled: �Requirements � 70Z03826QB0000146,� �Terms and Conditions � 70Z03826QB0000146�, and �Redacted J and A � 70Z03826QB0000146� 52.217-6 Option for Increased Quantity (MAR 1989) applies to this acquisition and is tailored as follows: The Government may increase the quantity of supplies called for in the Schedule, by up to a quantity of Fifteen (15), at the unit price specified, up to a maximum quantity of Thirty-Six (36). The Contracting Officer may exercise the option by written notice to the Contractor within one calendar year after Purchase Order award. Delivery of the added items shall continue at the same rate as the like items call for under the Purchase Order, unless the parties otherwise agree. ***Please note that if the USCG chooses to exercise any optional quantity modification, such modifications will be issued unilaterally to the contractor. (End of Clause) Concerns having the expertise and required capabilities to provide these items are invited to submit offers in accordance with the requirements stipulated in this solicitation. The Government shall ensure all procurements are awarded without jeopardizing quality or safety of flight. No alternate part numbers will be accepted. Parts must be approved in accordance with Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) guidelines to ensure safety of our aircrew. Best value to the Government is always the goal, but without jeopardizing quality or safety of flight. Only the use of airworthy commercial specifications or standard military specifications/military standard parts will be utilized and approved from this solicitation. Newly manufactured commercial items will only be procured from sources able to provide a certificate of conformance (COC). The Federal Aviation Regulation, Part 21, outlines certification procedures. Description: THIS IS A PRESOLICITATION NOTICE The Department of Veterans Affairs, Network Contracting Office 9, located at 1639 Medical Center Parkway, Suite 204, Murfreesboro, TN, 37129, anticipates issuing a solicitation Request for Quotation (RFQ) on or about 06/23/2026 for two EQUAL or better semi-instantaneous vertical CEMLINE hot water heaters on behalf of the James H. Quillen VA Medical Center, located in Mt. Home, Tennessee. Situation: The two hot water heaters in building 005 MTN Home VAMC have failed due to being at their end-of-life cycle and require replacement. These are specialty semi-instantaneous vertical hot water heaters fabricated in accordance with ASME codes and stamped for 150 psi working pressure. The packaged water heater will be constructed with a Stainless-steel tank and Stainless-steel threaded openings. Heater will be mounted on a steel support skid and will have lifting lugs. Heater will be insulated with foam insulation and protected by an enameled metal jacket, 20-gauge thickness. These water heaters are specialty units that must function within the existing mechanical room space. Intra tank circulator. ASME pressure- temperature relief valve. Water pressure gauge and steam pressure gauge. Solid State Control module that includes the following functions with individual pilot lights: On-off switch, remote start-stop, alarm horn with alarm silence button, power on, primary high limit, and secondary high limit. Module will have built in PIO Control signal with LED display of set point and operating temperature read out and contacts for BACnet and Computrol Compatible (Front -End capability). Double solenoid safety system. Vacuum Breaker. Heater shall be rated to heat 27 G.P.M. of water from 40 F. to 140 F. and control the outlet within 5 degrees of the selected temperature when supplied with 15 PSIG of saturated steam to the control valve. Heater will be mounted vertically. attachments.text:
TITLE: Single Source Acquisition for GSB-2501 Airfield Lighting Control System
(ALCMS) Upgrade
The 4th Contracting Squadron, Seymour Johnson AFB, NC intends to award a sole source
contract to ADB SAFEGATE Americas LLC (CAGE: 5ED70) for a proprietary technology
upgrade.
This procurement is for a proprietary hardware and software technology upgrade to the existing
GSB-2501 Airfield Lighting Control and Monitoring System (ALCMS) at Seymour Johnson
AFB. Specifically, this requirement includes replacing existing unmanaged network components
with a new, fully managed system based on the Cisco IE3300 switch platform. The procurement
will include all proprietary hardware for the Air Traffic Control Tower, Airfield Electrical Vault,
and Maintenance Center, as well as the necessary professional services for project submittals,
factory acceptance testing, and on-site system commissioning to ensure a fully functional,
integrated system.
APPLICABILITY OF AUTHORITY:
This contract action is for supplies and services for which the Government intends to solicit and
negotiate with only one source under the authority of R-DFARS 206.103-170, Only one
responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements. Market
research confirms the ALCMS is a proprietary system, and only the Original Equipment
Manufacturer, ADB SAFEGATE Americas LLC, possesses the requisite proprietary data,
software, and expertise to perform the upgrade without causing unacceptable risk to airfield
safety and operations.
This notice of intent is not a request for competitive proposals. A determination by the
Government not to compete this proposed contract lies solely within the discretion of the
Government. Information received will be considered solely for the purpose of determining
whether to conduct a competitive requirement.
The closing date for responses to this synopsis is 30 June 2026 at 3:00 PM EST. The anticipated
award date is unknown. For information regarding this purchase, please contact Brooke Shenk at
brooke.shenk@us.af.mil. All responses must be submitted via email to the point of contact.
Telephone inquiries will not be accepted.

This is a sole-source action issued to Lockheed Martin Corporation (CAGE 64059) pursuant to the authority of Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) FAR 6.103-1(b); ��only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements.� NOUN NSN PART NUMBER QUANTITY CONTROL SECTION, GUI 1420-01-540-8608 13540365 35 The Government contemplates a Firm-Fixed-Pricing (FFP) single purchase effort. Responses shall be provided to the contracting team identified above. 2. Your response is requested as soon as possible. If you choose to submit a proposal in response to this RFP it shall be submitted on/or before 5:00 P.M. Central Standard Time (CST) October 30, 2026. B. Instructions for the proposal: 1. attachments.text:
ORIENTATION ON
FIRST ARTICLE TESTING (FAT)
(CONTRACTOR TESTING)
Aviation and Missile Center (AvMC)
Systems Readiness Directorate (SRD)
Sustainment Division
26 April 2023
INTRODUCTION
This document is provided as an orientation to familiarize the Contractor with the purpose and
scope of the First Article Test, Contractor Tested, as performed on this contract. It provides a
detailed review of the processes, controls, and procedures described in the first article approval
clause of the contract, FAR 52.209-3. Moreover, it is provided for informational purposes only
and is not part of the terms and/or conditions of the contract. The contents of this orientation
document shall not be construed or interpreted as direction to perform tasks, work, or labor
which could result in a monetary charge to the U.S. Government. Additionally, the contents of
this document shall not be used as direction to modify any existing contract between vendors and
the U.S. Government. For questions regarding contracts and changes to contracts, consult your
contracting officer. The contracting officer is the approving authority for all matters related to
contracts.
TESTING
The purpose of the first article test and approval process are to assure that the Contractor has the
capability to manufacture a product that conforms to all contract requirements. Per FAR 52.209-
3, participation in the FAT is an option available to the Government. It is imperative that the
local Defense Contract Management Agency (DCMA) Quality Assurance Representative (QAR)
participate in the test, whether or not other government representatives attend. The on-site test
participants should communicate expectations for the First Article Test Report (FATR), possibly
preventing delays in approval.
The FAT normally begins with a meeting between all cognizant government and contractor
personnel. The purpose of this meeting is to review the scope of the FAT and to agree upon the
manner in which it will be conducted. A contractor representative is normally designated as a
focal point of contact for government participants to coordinate actions and to obtain
authoritative responses to issues that may arise. Prior to the meeting, a thorough review of the
procurement package is completed to determine the technical scope involved and to ensure that
participating personnel are intimately familiar with overall requirements. Additional meetings
are held as often as necessary, and a final critique is conducted upon completion of the test. The
FAT process will neither exceed nor modify the contract requirements in any way. Any
contract modifications, if required, will be through the Contracting Officer.
The test of the first article candidate is the responsibility of the Contractor; however, the
government representatives may, at their option, perform any of the required inspections and/or
tests with assistance from any specially trained Contractor personnel necessary to operate unique
or complex special inspection and test equipment. The on-site FAT consists of, but is not limited
to, a thorough examination of certifications; employee training records (where certifications are
required); material; processes, procedures; item characteristics; manufacturing, inspection and
test equipment calibration records; dimensions; marking; preservation, packaging, packing
operations; and special and/or functional testing, necessary to assure compliance. This
information should be included in the FATR. The Contractor is responsible for providing the
facilities and test equipment and any additional administrative or technical support personnel
necessary to assist in conducting the FAT. The product of this process is the FATR, which must
include all of the information required by the contract. The importance of the test report cannot
be underestimated, as it is the deliverable which forms the basis of acceptability of the FAT,
notwithstanding the observations of government representatives while on-site. Any questions
related to the content of the FATR may be submitted to the Government though the contracting
officer. Deficiencies are defined as any nonconformance or departure from any contractually
required material; physical, operational, functional, or special characteristics; processes; and/or
procedures. To increase the likelihood of a successful first-time submission of the FATR, the
Contractor may request a courtesy review of the draft report by the government Quality
Assurance Specialist (QAS) prior to formal submission to identify any possible causes for
eventual rejection (A list of common causes for FATR rejection is provided below). This is not a
guarantee that the FATR will be accepted; it is only a courtesy offered to increase that
likelihood. Please note that if the procured item is highly complex (e.g., an engine transmission)
and performing a courtesy review could significantly extend the length of the FAT visit, time for
a complete courtesy review may not be permitted.
Upon completion of the FAT, an exit brief will be conducted on-site. Findings and/or results of
the FAT will be discussed and differences resolved. As the FATR is a contractual line item with
inspection at origin, the test report must be annotated by the DCMA QAR recommending
approval/disapproval. The Contractor will finalize the report and forward it through the
Administrative Contracting Officer (ACO) to the Procurement Contracting Officer (PCO) who
will provide it to the SRD for review. In the event that a FATR is disapproved, another FAT may
be scheduled depending on the number and complexity of the issues involved. Any second FAT
should be scheduled after the Contractor has implemented the appropriate actions to determine
the cause of the nonconformance, taken required corrective actions, and presented a reworked or
replacement first article test piece. With PCO concurrence, it is appropriate to contact the QAS
to seek clarity on FAT findings, but all official FAT/FATR corrective actions must be routed
through the DCMA QAR to the PCO. Purchase of materials, components, and /or
commencement of production for the balance of the contract quantity is at the sole risk of the
Contractor unless the PCO grants specific written authorization (see paragraph (g) of FAR 52-
209-3 Alt 2).
SUMMARY
There may be variations in the basic guidance presented herein, based on the peculiarities of
specific products. The FAT is a thorough assessment to determine the ability of the Contractor to
produce conforming material on a repetitive basis and to ascertain the adherence to product
specifications and adequacy of operational requirements. When fully supported by contractor and
government personnel, FATs play an extremely important role in the overall objective to provide
quality materiel to the Warfighter.
COMMON CAUSES OF FATR REJECTIONS
No indication of DCMA participation in first article testing process (e.g., missing DD Form 1222
and/or DD Form 250)
No evidence that contractor has a quality program as required by contract. (FAR 52.246-11)
Missing material/process certifications
Lack of traceability for material process/certifications showing requirements are flowed to
subcontractors
Missing special process certifications for personnel (e.g., NDT, welding)
Wrong material used
A 100% dimensional characteristics check taken during first article test in-process and final
inspections not recorded on appropriate documentation
No part marking or bar code label verification
Packaging/packing requirements not verified
Functional test not performed/documented as required
Lack of required calibration data
No certification the first article and production quantity will be produced in the same facility
Non-conforming characteristics not approved under waiver/deviation process
Lack of traceability for material process/certifications showing requirements are flowed to
subcontractors

attachments.text:
BAR CODE MARKING REQUIREMENTS
Bar Code Markings are required in accordance with the latest revision of MIL-STD-129 and ISO/IEC
16388 - Information Technology - Automatic Identification and Data Capture Techniques - Bar Code
Symbology Specification - Code 39
CALIBRATION REQUIREMENTS
The calibration of Test, Measurement and Diagnostic Equipment shall be in accordance with
American National Standards Institute/National Conference of Standards Laboratories
(ANSI/NCSL) Z540-3-2006 (General Requirements for Calibration Laboratories and Measuring and
Test Equipment) or ISO 10012:2003 (Quality Assurance Requirements for Measuring Equipment).
Terminology shall be as defined by International Organization for Standardization (ISO) 8402,
Quality Management and Quality Assurance – Vocabulary.
ELECTRONIC FABRICATION: REQUIREMENTS FOR ELECTRICAL AND ELECTRONIC ASSEMBLIES
1. Notwithstanding any other provision contained in any part of this contract to the contrary, the
minimum requirements/standards for soldering electrical and electronic assemblies shall be the
non-military joint industry standard, ANSI/J-STD-001, Class 3. The revision of ANSI/J-STD-001 in
effect on the effective date of the contract shall govern the hardware produced hereunder. A copy
of ANSI/J-STD-001 may be obtained from the Institute for Interconnecting and Packaging Electronic
Circuits (IPC), 3000 Lakeside Drive, 105N, Bannockburn, IL, 60015, https://www.ipc.org.
2. The contractor shall establish and maintain an electronic/electrical parts control program and
shall maintain and make available to the Government records and data which will provide visibility
and traceability of all parts used in the production of the equipment under this contract. This
selection of parts shall not be construed to relieve the contractor of meeting specified performance
of the end item in which the part is used.
3. The Technical Data Package (TDP) shall serve as the baseline Program Parts Selection List (PPSL)
and the parts and sources listed therein are the standard parts and sources. A Non Standard Part is
defined as a part or source other than that cited in the PPSL. When the contractor desires to use a
part or source other than those cited in the PPSL, the change must be approved by the Government
via a Request for Deviation (RFD) as defined elsewhere in this contract. Failure on the part of the
contractor to submit such RFDs may result in the replacement of the nonstandard part with the
standard part by the Government at the contractor’s expense for all affected items.
4. The contractor shall provide objective evidence such as form, fit, function, and interchangeability
data that shows the proposed part complies with the requirements of applicable parts
documentation. The RFD shall detail the technical justification for the use of the part and
advantages of the nonstandard part, if any. Compare the nonstandard part to the standard part
whose characteristics are nearest to those required for the application. Include, when applicable:
a. Part Number and Source
b. Size and weight data.
c. Electrical and mechanical characteristics
d. Reliability (with data if requested)
e. Availability of the standard part (delivery schedules, still available etc.)
f. Supplemental data such as existing control drawings, specifications, vendor data sheets, and
other pertinent data. Data need not be furnished for nonstandard parts covered by documents
listed in the Department of Defense Index of Specifications and Standards (DoDISS) or
Standardized Military Drawings (SMD).
5. The Contractor shall maintain a Lead Free Control Plan (LFCP) and make available to the
Government upon request. The requirement for a Lead Free Control Plan shall be flowed down to
suppliers of equipment that may include lead-free materials. The LFCP shall follow the guidelines
set forth in GEIA-STD-0005-1, "Performance Standard for Aerospace and High Performance
Electronic Systems Containing Lead- Free Solder" or its equivalent. In addition, the LFCP shall also
include tin whisker mitigation plans in accordance with GEIA-STD-0005- 2, "Standard for Mitigating
the Effects of Tin Whiskers in Aerospace and High Performance Electronic Systems" or its
equivalent, at control level 2C or equivalent. The Contractor should include in the LFCP any special
design considerations, manufacturing process controls, test and qualification requirements,
quality inspection and screening, marking and identification, maintenance and repair processes,
and other steps taken to mitigate risk.
6. The Contractor shall prepare, or update existing, Counterfeit Risk Management Plan and make
available to the Government upon request. The Plan shall meet the requirements of SAE AS5553 for
electronic items. The Contractor shall procure parts from original manufacturers or the original
manufacturers’ franchised distributors. Contractors shall report counterfeits and suspected
counterfeits to the Government and in the Government Industry Data Exchange Program (GIDEP), in
accordance with the GIDEP Operations Manual, SO300-BT-PRO- 010.
ENGINEERING CHG PROPOSAL, VALUE ENG CHG PROPOSAL, REQUEST FOR VARIANCE, ENG
RELEASE RECORDS, NOTICE OF REVISION, AND SPECIFICATION CHG NOTICE PREPARATION
AND SUBMISSION INSTRUCTIONS
1. Contractor initiated Engineering Change Proposals (ECPs), Value Engineering Change Proposals
(VECPs), and Request for Variance (RFVs), collectively referred to as "proposals", shall be prepared,
submitted and distributed in accordance with paragraphs 2, 3 and 4 below except as specified in
paragraph 5 below.
2. Format.
a. Class I ECPs require the "Long Form Procedure" for documenting the change and describing the
effects of the change on the suitability and supportability of the Configuration Item (CI). Class I
ECPs should be limited to those that are necessary or offer significant benefit to the Government.
Class I ECPs are those that affect the performance, reliability, maintainability, survivability, weight,
balance, moment of inertia, interface characteristics, electromagnetic characteristics, or other
technical requirements in the specifications and drawings. Class I ECPs also include those
changes that affect Government Furnished Equipment, safety, compatibility, retrofit, operation and
maintenance manuals, interchangeability, substitutability, replaceability, source control
specifications and drawings, costs, guarantees or warranties, deliveries, or schedules. Class II
ECPs are those that do not affect form, fit and function, cost, or schedule of the system CI and do
not meet the other criteria described above for Class I ECPs.
b. Long Form Procedure: Class I changes to the CI require that DD Form 1692, pages 1
through 7 (as applicable), be prepared. Use of this procedure assures that all effects of the change
on the CI are properly addressed and documented to the necessary detail to allow proper
evaluation of the proposed change.
c. Short Form Procedure: ECPs and VECPs , which meet the requirements of Class II
ECPs, shall be prepared using DD Form 1692 (page 1 only). Supplemental pages may be used with
the form as necessary. The responsible Defense Contract Management Agency (DCMA) Contract
Management Office (CMO) will validate data entries in Block 5 "Class of ECP", Block 6 "Priority", and
Block 8 "Justification Codes."
d. The Contractor shall not manufacture items for acceptance by the Government that
incorporate a known departure from requirements, unless the Government has approved an RFV.
RFVs shall be prepared using DD Form 1694.
e. Each ECP and RFV shall be accompanied by a written and signed evaluation prepared by
the responsible Defense Contract Management Agency (DCMA) technical representative. The
DCMA written evaluation shall be considered part of the ECP/RFV proposal.
f. Classification of RFVs.
(1) Major RFVs. RFVs written against CIs shall be designated as major when the
RFV consists of acceptance of an item having a nonconformance with contract or configuration
documentation involving health; performance; interchangeability; reliability; survivability;
maintainability; effective use or operation; weight; appearance (when a factor); or when there is a
departure from a requirement classified as major in the contractual documentation.
(2) Critical RFVs. RFVs written against CIs shall be designated as critical when the RFV consists
of acceptance of an item having a nonconformance with contract or configuration documentation
involving safety or when there is a departure from a requirement classified as critical in the
contractual documentation.
(3) Minor RFVs. RFVs written against CIs shall be designated as minor when the RFV consists of
acceptance of an item having a nonconformance with contract or configuration documentation
which does not involve any of the factors listed above in paragraphs f(1) or g(2), or when there is a
departure from a requirement classified as minor in the contractual documentation.
g. Proposals shall include sufficient technical data to describe all changes from existing
contract requirements.
h. Proposals shall include sufficient justification for making the change, including a
statement of contract impact, if the change is not authorized.
i. Proposals for ECPs shall set forth a "not to exceed" price and delivery adjustment
acceptable to the Contractor if the Government subsequently approves the proposal. If approved,
the equitable increase shall not exceed this amount.
j. Times allowed for technical decisions for ECP and RFV proposals will be worked out via
mutual agreement between the Contractor and the Government.
k. Proposals for VECPs shall set forth a "not less than" price and delivery adjustment
acceptable to the Contractor if the Government subsequently approves the proposal. If approved,
the savings shall not be less than this amount.
l. The Contractor shall utilize DD Form 2617, "Engineering Release Record" (ERR) to release
new or revised configuration documentation to the Government for approval.
m. The Contractor shall utilize DD Form 1695, "Notice of Revision" (NOR) to describe the
exact change(s) to configuration documentation specified as a data requirement in the contract.
The Contractor shall describe the change using sub-sections entitled "WAS" to describe the current
contractual technical requirement and "IS" to describe the proposed new requirement.
3. Submittal. The preferred method of submittal is digitally as a single file in Adobe Acrobat
Portable Document Format (PDF). Unless otherwise specified, alternate methods of submittal
shall be proposed to and authorized by the PCO prior to submittal. If the hardcopy method is
requested and approved, the Contractor shall submit two (2) copies of each proposal to the
responsible Administrative Contracting Officer (ACO). One (1) copy of each proposal shall be
returned to the Contractor within (5) working days after receipt by the ACO, stating whether or not
the proposal is in compliance with this provision. Any unresolved differences between the ACO and
the Contractor concerning ECPs, VECPs, or RFVs will be submitted to the PCO for resolution.
4. Distribution.
a. Electronic Distribution. The preferred method of distribution for unclassified is through
the email or DOD safe site (https://safe.apps.mil) addressed to the PCO. Classified material shall
be distributed via SIPERNET or by classified email as determined by the PCO. Microsoft Word is
required for use with the transmittal letter (E-mail). Required forms will be attached to the E-mail.
All forms may be obtained from the Office of the Secretary of Defense Executive Services
Directorate DoD Directives Division website (http://www.esd.whs.mil/DD/) via the DoD Forms
menu. The forms are provided in fillable Adobe Acrobat Portable Document Format (PDF). In order
to access and use the forms, the user must have the "Adobe Acrobat" software installed on their
computer. Drawings may be scanned and sent as an attachment. In some cases, because of s

ORIENTATION ON
FIRST ARTICLE TESTING (FAT)
(CONTRACTOR TESTING)
Aviation and Missile Center (AvMC)
Systems Readiness Directorate (SRD)
Sustainment Division
26 April 2023
INTRODUCTION
This document is provided as an orientation to familiarize the Contractor with the purpose and
scope of the First Article Test, Contractor Tested, as performed on this contract. It provides a
detailed review of the processes, controls, and procedures described in the first article approval
clause of the contract, FAR 52.209-3. Moreover, it is provided for informational purposes only
and is not part of the terms and/or conditions of the contract. The contents of this orientation
document shall not be construed or interpreted as direction to perform tasks, work, or labor
which could result in a monetary charge to the U.S. Government. Additionally, the contents of
this document shall not be used as direction to modify any existing contract between vendors and
the U.S. Government. For questions regarding contracts and changes to contracts, consult your
contracting officer. The contracting officer is the approving authority for all matters related to
contracts.
TESTING
The purpose of the first article test and approval process are to assure that the Contractor has the
capability to manufacture a product that conforms to all contract requirements. Per FAR 52.209-
3, participation in the FAT is an option available to the Government. It is imperative that the
local Defense Contract Management Agency (DCMA) Quality Assurance Representative (QAR)
participate in the test, whether or not other government representatives attend. The on-site test
participants should communicate expectations for the First Article Test Report (FATR), possibly
preventing delays in approval.
The FAT normally begins with a meeting between all cognizant government and contractor
personnel. The purpose of this meeting is to review the scope of the FAT and to agree upon the
manner in which it will be conducted. A contractor representative is normally designated as a
focal point of contact for government participants to coordinate actions and to obtain
authoritative responses to issues that may arise. Prior to the meeting, a thorough review of the
procurement package is completed to determine the technical scope involved and to ensure that
participating personnel are intimately familiar with overall requirements. Additional meetings
are held as often as necessary, and a final critique is conducted upon completion of the test. The
FAT process will neither exceed nor modify the contract requirements in any way. Any
contract modifications, if required, will be through the Contracting Officer.
The test of the first article candidate is the responsibility of the Contractor; however, the
government representatives may, at their option, perform any of the required inspections and/or
tests with assistance from any specially trained Contractor personnel necessary to operate unique
or complex special inspection and test equipment. The on-site FAT consists of, but is not limited
to, a thorough examination of certifications; employee training records (where certifications are
required); material; processes, procedures; item characteristics; manufacturing, inspection and
test equipment calibration records; dimensions; marking; preservation, packaging, packing
operations; and special and/or functional testing, necessary to assure compliance. This
information should be included in the FATR. The Contractor is responsible for providing the
facilities and test equipment and any additional administrative or technical support personnel
necessary to assist in conducting the FAT. The product of this process is the FATR, which must
include all of the information required by the contract. The importance of the test report cannot
be underestimated, as it is the deliverable which forms the basis of acceptability of the FAT,
notwithstanding the observations of government representatives while on-site. Any questions
related to the content of the FATR may be submitted to the Government though the contracting
officer. Deficiencies are defined as any nonconformance or departure from any contractually
required material; physical, operational, functional, or special characteristics; processes; and/or
procedures. To increase the likelihood of a successful first-time submission of the FATR, the
Contractor may request a courtesy review of the draft report by the government Quality
Assurance Specialist (QAS) prior to formal submission to identify any possible causes for
eventual rejection (A list of common causes for FATR rejection is provided below). This is not a
guarantee that the FATR will be accepted; it is only a courtesy offered to increase that
likelihood. Please note that if the procured item is highly complex (e.g., an engine transmission)
and performing a courtesy review could significantly extend the length of the FAT visit, time for
a complete courtesy review may not be permitted.
Upon completion of the FAT, an exit brief will be conducted on-site. Findings and/or results of
the FAT will be discussed and differences resolved. As the FATR is a contractual line item with
inspection at origin, the test report must be annotated by the DCMA QAR recommending
approval/disapproval. The Contractor will finalize the report and forward it through the
Administrative Contracting Officer (ACO) to the Procurement Contracting Officer (PCO) who
will provide it to the SRD for review. In the event that a FATR is disapproved, another FAT may
be scheduled depending on the number and complexity of the issues involved. Any second FAT
should be scheduled after the Contractor has implemented the appropriate actions to determine
the cause of the nonconformance, taken required corrective actions, and presented a reworked or
replacement first article test piece. With PCO concurrence, it is appropriate to contact the QAS
to seek clarity on FAT findings, but all official FAT/FATR corrective actions must be routed
through the DCMA QAR to the PCO. Purchase of materials, components, and /or
commencement of production for the balance of the contract quantity is at the sole risk of the
Contractor unless the PCO grants specific written authorization (see paragraph (g) of FAR 52-
209-3 Alt 2).
SUMMARY
There may be variations in the basic guidance presented herein, based on the peculiarities of
specific products. The FAT is a thorough assessment to determine the ability of the Contractor to
produce conforming material on a repetitive basis and to ascertain the adherence to product
specifications and adequacy of operational requirements. When fully supported by contractor and
government personnel, FATs play an extremely important role in the overall objective to provide
quality materiel to the Warfighter.
COMMON CAUSES OF FATR REJECTIONS
No indication of DCMA participation in first article testing process (e.g., missing DD Form 1222
and/or DD Form 250)
No evidence that contractor has a quality program as required by contract. (FAR 52.246-11)
Missing material/process certifications
Lack of traceability for material process/certifications showing requirements are flowed to
subcontractors
Missing special process certifications for personnel (e.g., NDT, welding)
Wrong material used
A 100% dimensional characteristics check taken during first article test in-process and final
inspections not recorded on appropriate documentation
No part marking or bar code label verification
Packaging/packing requirements not verified
Functional test not performed/documented as required
Lack of required calibration data
No certification the first article and production quantity will be produced in the same facility
Non-conforming characteristics not approved under waiver/deviation process
Lack of traceability for material process/certifications showing requirements are flowed to
subcontractors

BAR CODE MARKING REQUIREMENTS
Bar Code Markings are required in accordance with the latest revision of MIL-STD-129 and ISO/IEC
16388 - Information Technology - Automatic Identification and Data Capture Techniques - Bar Code
Symbology Specification - Code 39
CALIBRATION REQUIREMENTS
The calibration of Test, Measurement and Diagnostic Equipment shall be in accordance with
American National Standards Institute/National Conference of Standards Laboratories
(ANSI/NCSL) Z540-3-2006 (General Requirements for Calibration Laboratories and Measuring and
Test Equipment) or ISO 10012:2003 (Quality Assurance Requirements for Measuring Equipment).
Terminology shall be as defined by International Organization for Standardization (ISO) 8402,
Quality Management and Quality Assurance – Vocabulary.
ELECTRONIC FABRICATION: REQUIREMENTS FOR ELECTRICAL AND ELECTRONIC ASSEMBLIES
1. Notwithstanding any other provision contained in any part of this contract to the contrary, the
minimum requirements/standards for soldering electrical and electronic assemblies shall be the
non-military joint industry standard, ANSI/J-STD-001, Class 3. The revision of ANSI/J-STD-001 in
effect on the effective date of the contract shall govern the hardware produced hereunder. A copy
of ANSI/J-STD-001 may be obtained from the Institute for Interconnecting and Packaging Electronic
Circuits (IPC), 3000 Lakeside Drive, 105N, Bannockburn, IL, 60015, https://www.ipc.org.
2. The contractor shall establish and maintain an electronic/electrical parts control program and
shall maintain and make available to the Government records and data which will provide visibility
and traceability of all parts used in the production of the equipment under this contract. This
selection of parts shall not be construed to relieve the contractor of meeting specified performance
of the end item in which the part is used.
3. The Technical Data Package (TDP) shall serve as the baseline Program Parts Selection List (PPSL)
and the parts and sources listed therein are the standard parts and sources. A Non Standard Part is
defined as a part or source other than that cited in the PPSL. When the contractor desires to use a
part or source other than those cited in the PPSL, the change must be approved by the Government
via a Request for Deviation (RFD) as defined elsewhere in this contract. Failure on the part of the
contractor to submit such RFDs may result in the replacement of the nonstandard part with the
standard part by the Government at the contractor’s expense for all affected items.
4. The contractor shall provide objective evidence such as form, fit, function, and interchangeability
data that shows the proposed part complies with the requirements of applicable parts
documentation. The RFD shall detail the technical justification for the use of the part and
advantages of the nonstandard part, if any. Compare the nonstandard part to the standard part
whose characteristics are nearest to those required for the application. Include, when applicable:
a. Part Number and Source
b. Size and weight data.
c. Electrical and mechanical characteristics
d. Reliability (with data if requested)
e. Availability of the standard part (delivery schedules, still available etc.)
f. Supplemental data such as existing control drawings, specifications, vendor data sheets, and
other pertinent data. Data need not be furnished for nonstandard parts covered by documents
listed in the Department of Defense Index of Specifications and Standards (DoDISS) or
Standardized Military Drawings (SMD).
5. The Contractor shall maintain a Lead Free Control Plan (LFCP) and make available to the
Government upon request. The requirement for a Lead Free Control Plan shall be flowed down to
suppliers of equipment that may include lead-free materials. The LFCP shall follow the guidelines
set forth in GEIA-STD-0005-1, "Performance Standard for Aerospace and High Performance
Electronic Systems Containing Lead- Free Solder" or its equivalent. In addition, the LFCP shall also
include tin whisker mitigation plans in accordance with GEIA-STD-0005- 2, "Standard for Mitigating
the Effects of Tin Whiskers in Aerospace and High Performance Electronic Systems" or its
equivalent, at control level 2C or equivalent. The Contractor should include in the LFCP any special
design considerations, manufacturing process controls, test and qualification requirements,
quality inspection and screening, marking and identification, maintenance and repair processes,
and other steps taken to mitigate risk.
6. The Contractor shall prepare, or update existing, Counterfeit Risk Management Plan and make
available to the Government upon request. The Plan shall meet the requirements of SAE AS5553 for
electronic items. The Contractor shall procure parts from original manufacturers or the original
manufacturers’ franchised distributors. Contractors shall report counterfeits and suspected
counterfeits to the Government and in the Government Industry Data Exchange Program (GIDEP), in
accordance with the GIDEP Operations Manual, SO300-BT-PRO- 010.
ENGINEERING CHG PROPOSAL, VALUE ENG CHG PROPOSAL, REQUEST FOR VARIANCE, ENG
RELEASE RECORDS, NOTICE OF REVISION, AND SPECIFICATION CHG NOTICE PREPARATION
AND SUBMISSION INSTRUCTIONS
1. Contractor initiated Engineering Change Proposals (ECPs), Value Engineering Change Proposals
(VECPs), and Request for Variance (RFVs), collectively referred to as "proposals", shall be prepared,
submitted and distributed in accordance with paragraphs 2, 3 and 4 below except as specified in
paragraph 5 below.
2. Format.
a. Class I ECPs require the "Long Form Procedure" for documenting the change and describing the
effects of the change on the suitability and supportability of the Configuration Item (CI). Class I
ECPs should be limited to those that are necessary or offer significant benefit to the Government.
Class I ECPs are those that affect the performance, reliability, maintainability, survivability, weight,
balance, moment of inertia, interface characteristics, electromagnetic characteristics, or other
technical requirements in the specifications and drawings. Class I ECPs also include those
changes that affect Government Furnished Equipment, safety, compatibility, retrofit, operation and
maintenance manuals, interchangeability, substitutability, replaceability, source control
specifications and drawings, costs, guarantees or warranties, deliveries, or schedules. Class II
ECPs are those that do not affect form, fit and function, cost, or schedule of the system CI and do
not meet the other criteria described above for Class I ECPs.
b. Long Form Procedure: Class I changes to the CI require that DD Form 1692, pages 1
through 7 (as applicable), be prepared. Use of this procedure assures that all effects of the change
on the CI are properly addressed and documented to the necessary detail to allow proper
evaluation of the proposed change.
c. Short Form Procedure: ECPs and VECPs , which meet the requirements of Class II
ECPs, shall be prepared using DD Form 1692 (page 1 only). Supplemental pages may be used with
the form as necessary. The responsible Defense Contract Management Agency (DCMA) Contract
Management Office (CMO) will validate data entries in Block 5 "Class of ECP", Block 6 "Priority", and
Block 8 "Justification Codes."
d. The Contractor shall not manufacture items for acceptance by the Government that
incorporate a known departure from requirements, unless the Government has approved an RFV.
RFVs shall be prepared using DD Form 1694.
e. Each ECP and RFV shall be accompanied by a written and signed evaluation prepared by
the responsible Defense Contract Management Agency (DCMA) technical representative. The
DCMA written evaluation shall be considered part of the ECP/RFV proposal.
f. Classification of RFVs.
(1) Major RFVs. RFVs written against CIs shall be designated as major when the
RFV consists of acceptance of an item having a nonconformance with contract or configuration
documentation involving health; performance; interchangeability; reliability; survivability;
maintainability; effective use or operation; weight; appearance (when a factor); or when there is a
departure from a requirement classified as major in the contractual documentation.
(2) Critical RFVs. RFVs written against CIs shall be designated as critical when the RFV consists
of acceptance of an item having a nonconformance with contract or configuration documentation
involving safety or when there is a departure from a requirement classified as critical in the
contractual documentation.
(3) Minor RFVs. RFVs written against CIs shall be designated as minor when the RFV consists of
acceptance of an item having a nonconformance with contract or configuration documentation
which does not involve any of the factors listed above in paragraphs f(1) or g(2), or when there is a
departure from a requirement classified as minor in the contractual documentation.
g. Proposals shall include sufficient technical data to describe all changes from existing
contract requirements.
h. Proposals shall include sufficient justification for making the change, including a
statement of contract impact, if the change is not authorized.
i. Proposals for ECPs shall set forth a "not to exceed" price and delivery adjustment
acceptable to the Contractor if the Government subsequently approves the proposal. If approved,
the equitable increase shall not exceed this amount.
j. Times allowed for technical decisions for ECP and RFV proposals will be worked out via
mutual agreement between the Contractor and the Government.
k. Proposals for VECPs shall set forth a "not less than" price and delivery adjustment
acceptable to the Contractor if the Government subsequently approves the proposal. If approved,
the savings shall not be less than this amount.
l. The Contractor shall utilize DD Form 2617, "Engineering Release Record" (ERR) to release
new or revised configuration documentation to the Government for approval.
m. The Contractor shall utilize DD Form 1695, "Notice of Revision" (NOR) to describe the
exact change(s) to configuration documentation specified as a data requirement in the contract.
The Contractor shall describe the change using sub-sections entitled "WAS" to describe the current
contractual technical requirement and "IS" to describe the proposed new requirement.
3. Submittal. The preferred method of submittal is digitally as a single file in Adobe Acrobat
Portable Document Format (PDF). Unless otherwise specified, alternate methods of submittal
shall be proposed to and authorized by the PCO prior to submittal. If the hardcopy method is
requested and approved, the Contractor shall submit two (2) copies of each proposal to the
responsible Administrative Contracting Officer (ACO). One (1) copy of each proposal shall be
returned to the Contractor within (5) working days after receipt by the ACO, stating whether or not
the proposal is in compliance with this provision. Any unresolved differences between the ACO and
the Contractor concerning ECPs, VECPs, or RFVs will be submitted to the PCO for resolution.
4. Distribution.
a. Electronic Distribution. The preferred method of distribution for unclassified is through
the email or DOD safe site (https://safe.apps.mil) addressed to the PCO. Classified material shall
be distributed via SIPERNET or by classified email as determined by the PCO. Microsoft Word is
required for use with the transmittal letter (E-mail). Required forms will be attached to the E-mail.
All forms may be obtained from the Office of the Secretary of Defense Executive Services
Directorate DoD Directives Division website (http://www.esd.whs.mil/DD/) via the DoD Forms
menu. The forms are provided in fillable Adobe Acrobat Portable Document Format (PDF). In order
to access and use the forms, the user must have the "Adobe Acrobat" software installed on their
computer. Drawings may be scanned and sent as an attachment. In some cases, because of s

Description: N0016426Q0189 � SOLE SOURCE � DATRON NEO PLUS PRO � FSG 3417 - NAICS 333517 ISSUE DATE 18-JUN-2026 � CLOSING DATE 01-JUL-2026 � 11:00 PM Eastern Time ITEM DESCRIPTION- Naval Surface Warfare Center (NSWC) Crane has a requirement for the purchase of a DATRON Neo plus Pro Computer Numerical Control (CNC) Machine, all components to properly configure the CNC machine, along with set-up and training. This acquisition is in support of SPY-6 Depot activation/SPY to replace aging equipment and for direct fleet support and is considered mission-critical equipment. The effort has a required delivery time of ten (10) weeks after date of award. SOLE SOURCE PROCUREMENT- The proposed contract action is for the supplies or services for which the Government intends to solicit and negotiate with one source only DATRON USA, INC. of Milford, New Hampshire, Cage Code 7CRQ0, under the authority of FAR 12.201-1 for Commercial items using simplified procedures. This is being solicited on a sole source only basis because DATRON USA, Inc., of Milford, New Hampshire, Cage Code 7CRQ0, is the Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) of the DATRON Neo plus Pro CNC machine. The Neo plus Pro machine is required to provide compatibility and interoperability with existing equipment, processes, and software configurations currently established for the SPY-6 depot operations. Purchasing from the OEM provides comprehensive operational training and engineering support, which other suppliers are not able to provide. Only a purchase directly from DATRON will ensure the CNC machine is installed to the standards required. Purchase of another CNC machine would cost the government in excess of $70,000 to configure another machine into the existing inventory of CNC machines, due to reconfiguration of software and workflows. In addition, the purchase of another machine would require the complete re-engineering of established repair procedures and extensive retraining of qualified personnel, leading to delays more than one to three months for active engineering projects and SPY-6 fleet support schedules. All responsible sources may submit a capability statement, which shall be considered by the agency. However, a determination by the Government not to compete with this proposed contract based upon responses to this solicitation is solely within the discretion of the Government. Information received will normally be considered solely for the purpose of determining whether to conduct a competitive procurement. Contractors must be properly registered in the System for Award Management (SAM). Offerors may obtain information on SAM registration and annual confirmation requirements by calling 866-606-8220 or via the internet at https://sam.gov. This solicitation is being issued pursuant to the procedures at FAR 12.201-1 as a written Firm Fixed Priced Request for Quotes . Synopsis exception FAR 5.202(a)(13) applies and Solicitation Number N0016426Q0189 is hereby issued as an attachment hereto. All changes to the requirement that occur prior to the closing date will be posted to Contract Opportunities on https://sam.gov/. It is the responsibility of interested vendors to monitor https://sam.gov/ for any amendments, which may be issued to this solicitation. For changes made after the closing date, only those offerors that provide a quote will be provided any changes/amendments and considered for future discussions and/or award. Offers shall be e-mailed to rose.m.brown44.civ@us.navy.mil. All required information must be received on or before 01-JUL-2026 � 11:00 PM Eastern Time.

matters.title: Creaform HandySCAN Pro 3D Scanner (Brand Name Only)
matters.text:
Federal notice (Presolicitation), DEPT OF DEFENSE.DEPT OF THE ARMY.0418 AQ HQ     CONTRACTING SUP
Title: Creaform HandySCAN Pro 3D Scanner (Brand Name Only)
Solicitation number: W91151-26-Q-A056
PSC: 6635; NAICS: 334519
Description: The IIIAC has a requirement for the procurement of two (2) Creaform HandySCAN Pro (Brand Name Only), along with required software licenses, calibration accessories, and initial operator training. The Government's overarching need is to establish an organic, point-of-need metrology and reverse-engineering capability to rapidly digitize legacy components. The required hardware must utilize blue laser triangulation technology capable of capturing complex metallic surfaces with a volumetric accuracy of up to 0.020 mm + 0.060 mm/m. The system must feature a highly portable footprint (weighing under 1.0 kg). Crucially, the associated processing software must be fully functional offline within secure environments, requiring no continuous internet connection. Furthermore, the system must be 100% interoperable with existing hardware and Technical Data Packages (TDPs) currently utilized by sister depots to ensure the seamless sharing of 3D point cloud data without incurring data-translation errors. (ii) Procedures for Award & Anticipated Date: This requirement will be solicited using the commercial product acquisition procedures of RFO FAR Part 12. The Government anticipates issuing a formal Request for Quotations (RFQ) directly to at least three vendors on or about 01 July 2026, with an anticipated award date on or about 8 July 2026. Award will be made on a competitive basis to the responsible vendor whose quotation conforms to the solicitation and provides the most advantageous overall value to the U.S. Government. Quotes will be evaluated based on the following criteria: Technical Acceptability: The vendor must demonstrate the ability to provide the exact Creaform HandySCAN Pro (Brand Name Only) model, including the associated offline software (VXelements), manufacturer warranty, and on-site training/support. OEM Certification: The vendor must provide verifiable documentation (e.g., a letter from the manufacturer) confirming they are an Authorized Value-Added Reseller (VAR) or distributor for Creaform products, ensuring the Government receives full OEM support and warranties. Past Performance: The vendor must provide a brief statement of past performance or references demonstrating a history of successfully delivering similar metrology equipment and training to Government or commercial clients. Price: The total evaluated cost must be determined fair, reasonable, and the most advantageous to the U.S. Government. Please note: This is a Presolicitation notice only. This is not a request for quotes or proposals. All responsible sources may submit a quotation in response to the forthcoming solicitation, which will be considered by the agency.

matters.text:
Federal notice (Combined Synopsis/Solicitation), DEPT OF DEFENSE.DEPT OF THE AIR FORCE.FA8641 PRES ALFT DIR AFLCMC WVBK
Title: Combined Synopsis/Solicitation - Sole Source - Acquisition of a Level D 747-8i Full Motion Simulator
Solicitation number: FA8641-26-R-B001
PSC: 6930; NAICS: 336413
Description: Synopsis/Solicitation Statement (i) This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial products or commercial services prepared in accordance with the format in RFO Part 12, as supplemented with additional information included in this notice. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation; a formal, separate written solicitation document will not be posted publicly. (ii) The solicitation number is FA8641-26-R-B001 and is issued as a Request for Proposal (RFP). (iii) The solicitation document and incorporated provisions and clauses are those in effect through the most recent Federal Acquisition Circular / RFO Deviation Guide updates. (iv) Set-Aside Status: This requirement is not set aside for small business. This is a sole-source solicitation directed to CAE USA Inc., Orlando, Florida (CAGE: 1FNV1). (v) Contract Line Item Numbers (CLINs): Specific line item structures, quantities, and units of measure are omitted from this public notice and will be provided directly in the RFP to the sole-source vendor. (vi) Description of Requirements: AFLCMC/WVB has a critical, urgent, and mission-essential requirement for one (1) dedicated, commercial, FAA Level D certified 747-8i Full Flight Simulator (FFS). The FFS will be located at Joint Base Andrews (JBA). The required scope includes: Hardware & Systems: Procurement, delivery, and installation of the FFS, including 6-DOF motion, visual system, sound system, and an exact 747-8i cockpit replica. Cybersecurity: All operational hardware, software, and networking must be fully compliant with DoDI 8500.01/8510.01 and applicable AFI/DoD Manuals. Support: Initial support and maintenance, including spare parts and necessary software updates. Training: Initial courseware development and flight instruction for designated personnel. (vii) Delivery and Period of Performance (PoP): Delivery/Installation: Estimated at 24-36 months from contract award. Support/Maintenance: Estimated at 12-18 months following successful installation and acceptance. Place of Performance/Delivery: Joint Base Andrews (JBA), Maryland. FOB: Destination. (viii) Justification for Sole Source: CAE USA Inc. is the only responsible source capable of fulfilling this requirement. Extensive market research, including a Sources Sought Notice (SSN ID: F4FDWL-26-R-0001) posted in December 2025, confirmed that CAE is the sole manufacturer of commercial Level D certified 747-8 simulators globally. Procuring through a third-party integrator poses unacceptable risks to the program's cost, schedule, and mission. By utilizing the only proven Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) of the 747-8i FFS, the Government mitigates the risk of significant schedule delays, increased lifecycle costs, and critical gaps in mission-essential training. In accordance with RFO 6.305, the Justification and Approval (J&A) document supporting this sole-source action will be published to SAM.gov within 14 days after contract award. (ix) Provisions and Clauses: The standard commercial provisions and clauses apply to this acquisition, including, but not limited to, the equivalents of FAR 52.212-1 (Instructions to Offerors - Commercial Products and Commercial Services), FAR 52.212-4 (Contract Terms and Conditions), and FAR 52.212-5 (Contract Terms and Conditions Required To Implement Statutes or Executive Orders). Specific clauses will be detailed in the direct RFP sent to CAE USA Inc. (x) Proposal Submission: While this solicitation is directed as a sole-source procurement to CAE USA Inc. and is not a request for competitive proposals, all responsible sources may submit a capability statement, proposal, or quotation, which shall be considered by the agency. A determination by the Government not to compete this proposed contract based upon responses to this solicitation is solely within the discretion of the Government.
