CUI
Department of the Air Force: Justification for Other Than Full and Open Competition
I. Agency and Contracting Activity (RFO 6.104-1(a)(1)):
Agency: USAF F-15EX (AFLCMC/WAQK)
II. Nature and/or description of the action being approved (RFO 6.104-1(a)(2)):
This initiative aims to develop a self-sufficient, organic maintenance and repair capability for the F-15EX aircraft at the Air
Logistics Complex (ALC). A primary goal is to maximize the reuse of existing F-15 legacy capability and capacity to ensure
cost-effectiveness and efficiency.
To achieve this, a sole-source Indefinite Delivery/Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) contract will be awarded to the ITT Aerospace
Controls LLC. This action is justified under FAR 6.302-1 as they are the only responsible source for the Flow Control Valve, a
key component integrated into the F-15EX's baseline design. The contract will facilitate Depot Activation (DA), a process to
establish the capability for comprehensive overhaul, upgrading, or rebuilding of parts and subassemblies, along with
necessary equipment testing and reclamation, as defined in 10 USC Section 2460. This process involves identifying the
necessary facilities, equipment, materials, and certified personnel to perform depot-level maintenance. Depot activation is a
strategic, long-term investment aimed at ensuring a ready and controlled source of technical competence and resources to
respond to national defense contingencies and other emergency requirements.
This contract covers the procurement of essential parts and associated Depot Activation actions for the Flow Control Valve,
supporting both current and future F-15EX sustainment needs.
Due to cost and schedule constraints, the IDIQ contract will have a three-year base ordering period with an additional one-
year option. The total ceiling for this Justification and Approval (J&A) is set at $ which is based on a Rough Order of
Magnitude (ROM) estimate for the depot-level repair capability required for Flow Control Valve repairs.
III. Description of supplies/services required to meet agency needs (RFO 6.104-1(a)(3)):
Establishing an organic, depot-level repair capability requires the strategic delivery of a complete product support package
to the designated ALC(s). This consists of acquiring the required hardware, software, test, technical publication, training,
supply support, packaging, support equipment and data for the designated ALC to repair the depot level repairable(s). To
establish the organic repair capability, delivery of the core infrastructure for depot-level hardware testing and repair is
required. This includes the identification of requirements for, and the subsequent design, build, or purchase of, the
following components: Specialized Test Equipment (STE), Test Program Sets (TPS), and Interface Test Adapters (ITAs).
The United States Air Force (USAF) will provide all common support equipment for this activation effort. Due to proprietary
restrictions stemming from private investment in the development of F-15/F-15EX Line Replaceable Units (LRU), the
government's current ability to establish organic repair of the LRU is not possible. Technical data is restricted by the
manufacturer's intellectual property rights constraints. Therefore, to establish organic repair of the Flow Control Valve,
the USAF needs to negotiate licenses for only the sensitive data needed to repair the LRU. The repair and maintenance of
Flow Control Valves requires not only the Flow Control Valve itself but all associated parts/spares and the rights in
technical data necessary to maintain and ensure the software used in the displays functions correctly to support
verification of repairs at designated ALC.
Flow Control Valves manage, regulate, and shut off fuel, hydraulic, pneumatic, and coolant fluids in aircraft systems. They
provide high-reliability, low-weight solutions designed for severe operating conditions. They regulate the flow rate of
compressed air in pneumatic systems or fluids, directly affecting the speed of actuators. Flow control valves are used in fluid
systems, including fuel pumps and brake controls, to maintain consistent pressure. These valves are designed to withstand
high pressure, high heat, and EMI (electromagnetic interference), often utilizing aluminum or stainless steel materials.
Primary Contract Purpose
Primarily, this IDIQ will be a contract focused on ensuring the USAF can repair the current and future Flow Control Valve
specs authorized to be installed on F-15EX aircraft. Incidental to the provision of Flow Control Valves are field and depot-
MMaarrcchh 22002266 PPaaggee 22 ooff 77
CUI
Department of the Air Force: Justification for Other Than Full and Open Competition
level support, engineering necessary to implement future variants within the EX-airframe, provisioning and support
equipment. Section IV of this document explains these requirements in greater detail.
Contract Framework and Competition This IDIQ will allow efficient award of depot activation capabilities associated with
the Flow Control Valve. The CLIN structure may include separately priced CLINs for intellectual property (IP) rights as
negotiated with the Contractor. The Contract will be asked to include a data rights assertion list which will be provide as part
of the RFP Package sent to the OEM.
Cost Ceiling Justification The requested $ individual J&A ceiling is based on the PO's estimate for the entire Flow
Control Valve DA IDIQ ordering period, assuming each option is exercised. This ceiling was derived from current
programmatic activities based on in-house cost estimates for future projected DA requirements as explained above.
Cost Exclusions In keeping with the programmatic need to leverage legacy EX hardware, the cost ceiling for this IDIQ
excludes costs associated with qualifying an entirely new Flow Control Valve solution, implementing that new solution onto
existing EX airframes, altering the production line to install that new solution on future EX airframes, and the stand up of new
DA capabilities for any Flow Control Valve solution other than the one being awarded under this contract. These duplicative
costs have been excluded for reasons explained in Section IV below.
IV. Statutory Authority Permitting Other Than Full and Open Competition (RFO 6.104-1(a)(4)):
10 U.S.C. 3204(a)(1), Only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements.
V. Rationale for Use of Authority (RFO 6.104-1(a)(5)):
Background
Currently, ITT Aerospace Controls LLC produces the Flow Control Valves installed on every F-15EX through sole-source
procurement and integration by The Boeing Company (Boeing). ITT Aerospace Controls LLC is the only responsible Original
Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) capable of providing the Flow Control Valve and associated technical data rights necessary
for Depot Activation of the Flow Control Valves. Historically, repairs have been contracted to Boeing, who subcontracted
with ITT Aerospace Controls LLC for Flow Control Valve repairs and maintenance.
ITT Aerospace Controls LLC Flow Control Valve is fully developed, integrated, and has been certified/qualified for use on all
F-15EX aircraft. The Flow Control Valve further meets all safety, suitability, and effectiveness requirements necessary for
fielding EX aircraft. As the OEM of the only compliant Flow Control Valve available to the USAF, ITT Aerospace Controls LLC is
the only source in possession of the technical expertise, technical data, source code, proprietary engineering
documentation, and knowledge necessary to fulfill the delivery and DA requirements the USAF requires to continue fielding
EX aircraft without substantial impacts to cost and schedule.
The risk factors associated with procuring a new organic maintenance repair solution for an Flow Control Valve that is not
the current Flow Control Valve provided by ITT Aerospace Controls LLC are as follows:
Integration Complexity
A new OEM must design and qualify a part, requiring the USAF to act as integrator while Boeing incorporates that part into
the aircraft. This process involves drawing updates, technical order updates, and training updates. The complexity increases
if, as is the case with Flow Control Valve, the part contains software that interfaces with the mission computer, requiring
additional integration activities and a direct contract with Boeing for Operational Flight Program (OFP) updates to achieve
flight clearance.
Interim Support Degradation
The existing OEM has no incentive to continue maintaining OEM Specialized Test Equipment (STE) needed to repair existing
parts under Interim Contractor Support (ICS) or Contractor Logistics Support (CLS) while the USAF waits for new parts to
complete the design, qualification, and integration cycle. This results in degraded performance for maintaining existing
MMaarrcchh 22002266 PPaaggee 33 ooff 77
CUI
Department of the Air Force: Justification for Other Than Full and Open Competition
hardware during the transition period.
Depot Activation Continuity
New OEM selection must include the assumption that the new part will undergo depot activation. Otherwise, the USAF will
face the same OEM limitations with the new supplier as currently experienced with existing OEMs.
The challenges above present considerable cost, schedule, and budgetary risks that the USAF cannot expect to overcome via
the issuance of a competitive source selection for a new Flow Control Valve OEM.
Cost Prohibitions
Procuring and qualifying a new Flow Control Valve solution would result in substantial cost duplication that the Government
cannot expect to recover by conducting a competitive source selection.
Schedule Constraints
The schedule impacts associated with new Flow Control Valve qualifications and implementation are unacceptable. The
timeline to award and qualify a new Flow Control Valve solution includes: 1-2 years for a source selection, 3-5 years for
qualification, and an additional 2-4 years to qualify a new Flow Control Valve source's facilities, personnel, processes, and
procedures.
This entire 6-11 year process would be required if a new Flow Control Valve OEM is selected. With existing contractual
support for inorganic Depot Activation expiring at the end of FY 2026, any solution other than sole-source award to ITT
Aerospace Control LLC will result in EX aircraft being grounded during this extended timeline.
ITT Aerospace Control LLC's Unique Position
ITT Aerospace Control LLC Flow Control Valve is fully developed, integrated, and has been certified/qualified for use on all
F-15EX aircraft. The Flow Control Valve further meets all safety, suitability, and effectiveness requirements necessary for
fielding EX aircraft. As the OEM of the only compliant Flow Control Valve available to the USAF, ITT Aerospace Controls LLC is
the only source in possession of the technical expertise, technical data, source code, proprietary engineering
documentation, and knowledge necessary to fulfill the delivery and DA requirements the USAF requires to continue fielding
EX aircraft without substantial impacts to cost and schedule.
Accordingly, ITT Aerospace Control LLC is the only viable OEM capable of providing the supplies and services identified in
Section III above without the cost, schedule and budgetary risks explained in this section.
VI. Integrated Market Analysis and Efforts to Solicit Competition (RFO 6.104-1(a)(6), (8), and (10)):
In accordance with FAR Subpart 5.2, a synopsis of the proposed contract action was published on SAM.gov.
Furthermore,market research was conducted to identify all potential sources for this requirement, consistent with the
procedures outlined below.
Regulatory Requirement
DFARS PGI 206.302-1(d) states that "When utilizing the authority at FAR 6.302-1, the Contracting Officer shall post a request
for information or a sources sought notice, and shall include the results of this inquiry in the justification required by FAR
6.303.

Federal notice (Combined Synopsis/Solicitation), DEPT OF DEFENSE.DEPT OF THE NAVY.NAVAL SURFACE WARFARE CENTER
Title: Sole Source to EOLA Power for the replacement and installation services of three UPS units at the Navy Experimental Diving Unit, As Requested, See All Attachments.
Solicitation number: N61331-26-Q-JC17
PSC: 6150; NAICS: 221118
Description: Sole Source to EOLA Power for the replacement and installation services of three UPS units at the Navy Experimental Diving Unit, As Requested in the Attachments. Description This action will award a firm fixed price purchase order, on a sole source basis, to EOLA Power, located at 8782 NW 18th Terrace, Miami, FL 33172 for the replacement of three UPS units at the Navy Experimental Diving Unit. QTY: 3 EACH Additional Details The contractor shall provide replacement and installation services to NEDU and as requested in the Sole Source Justification. Refer to All Attachment for complete details. EOLA Power is qualified and has historically supplied NEDU our UPS maintenance needs (most recently 5 year option contract N61331-26-P-0125) which are critical to ensuring our divers� life support systems stay online during power outages NEDU. The replacement UPSes will be included under the maintenance contract, offering continuity and saving the government time and money. These UPS systems are written into our Scope of Certification boundary and are the only allowable systems that can replace our obsolete units. To use another company to conduct the maintenance would require additional knowledge of the system during the removal and replacement of the legacy UPS systems that EOLA Power has historically maintained. Use of another vendor may change or introduce new parameters that may be harmful to all diving systems tested and maintained at NEDU and negatively affect the electrical life support systems that are vital components of the OSF. Therefore, it is imperative that EOLA Power be used to limit the risk of NEDU personnel working within the systems that utilize the various equipment protected under these UPS systems. As such, the Government does not expect significant savings through competition and does not expect significant and unacceptable delays that will negatively impact this requirement. Therefore, it is in the Governments� best interest to acquire the replacement services with EOLA Power who currently and historically provide maintenance services of EOLA Power to support the NEDU mission. For questions or comments email jessica.d.clark27.civ@us.navy.mil on or before the closing date and time of Thursday, 18 June 2026, 3pm Central Time. Email subject line must include Solicitation Number and Vendor Name at beginning of subject line.

matters.text:
Federal notice (Justification), DEPT OF DEFENSE.DEPT OF THE AIR FORCE.FA8634 AFLCMC WAQK F15
Title: Request for Information - F-15 EX Flow Control Valve - Redacted
Solicitation number: FA8634-26-RB009-5
PSC: 1510; NAICS: 336413
Description: Please see the attached.

attachments.name: justification_and_approval_document ITT Aerospace_EMM Signed redact_Redacted.pdf
attachments.text:
CUI
Department of the Air Force: Justification for Other Than Full and Open Competition
I. Agency and Contracting Activity (RFO 6.104-1(a)(1)):
Agency: USAF F-15EX (AFLCMC/WAQK)
II. Nature and/or description of the action being approved (RFO 6.104-1(a)(2)):
This initiative aims to develop a self-sufficient, organic maintenance and repair capability for the F-15EX aircraft at the Air
Logistics Complex (ALC). A primary goal is to maximize the reuse of existing F-15 legacy capability and capacity to ensure
cost-effectiveness and efficiency.
To achieve this, a sole-source Indefinite Delivery/Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) contract will be awarded to the ITT Aerospace
Controls LLC. This action is justified under FAR 6.302-1 as they are the only responsible source for the Flow Control Valve, a
key component integrated into the F-15EX's baseline design. The contract will facilitate Depot Activation (DA), a process to
establish the capability for comprehensive overhaul, upgrading, or rebuilding of parts and subassemblies, along with
necessary equipment testing and reclamation, as defined in 10 USC Section 2460. This process involves identifying the
necessary facilities, equipment, materials, and certified personnel to perform depot-level maintenance. Depot activation is a
strategic, long-term investment aimed at ensuring a ready and controlled source of technical competence and resources to
respond to national defense contingencies and other emergency requirements.
This contract covers the procurement of essential parts and associated Depot Activation actions for the Flow Control Valve,
supporting both current and future F-15EX sustainment needs.
Due to cost and schedule constraints, the IDIQ contract will have a three-year base ordering period with an additional one-
year option. The total ceiling for this Justification and Approval (J&A) is set at $ which is based on a Rough Order of
Magnitude (ROM) estimate for the depot-level repair capability required for Flow Control Valve repairs.
III. Description of supplies/services required to meet agency needs (RFO 6.104-1(a)(3)):
Establishing an organic, depot-level repair capability requires the strategic delivery of a complete product support package
to the designated ALC(s). This consists of acquiring the required hardware, software, test, technical publication, training,
supply support, packaging, support equipment and data for the designated ALC to repair the depot level repairable(s). To
establish the organic repair capability, delivery of the core infrastructure for depot-level hardware testing and repair is
required. This includes the identification of requirements for, and the subsequent design, build, or purchase of, the
following components: Specialized Test Equipment (STE), Test Program Sets (TPS), and Interface Test Adapters (ITAs).
The United States Air Force (USAF) will provide all common support equipment for this activation effort. Due to proprietary
restrictions stemming from private investment in the development of F-15/F-15EX Line Replaceable Units (LRU), the
government's current ability to establish organic repair of the LRU is not possible. Technical data is restricted by the
manufacturer's intellectual property rights constraints. Therefore, to establish organic repair of the Flow Control Valve,
the USAF needs to negotiate licenses for only the sensitive data needed to repair the LRU. The repair and maintenance of
Flow Control Valves requires not only the Flow Control Valve itself but all associated parts/spares and the rights in
technical data necessary to maintain and ensure the software used in the displays functions correctly to support
verification of repairs at designated ALC.
Flow Control Valves manage, regulate, and shut off fuel, hydraulic, pneumatic, and coolant fluids in aircraft systems. They
provide high-reliability, low-weight solutions designed for severe operating conditions. They regulate the flow rate of
compressed air in pneumatic systems or fluids, directly affecting the speed of actuators. Flow control valves are used in fluid
systems, including fuel pumps and brake controls, to maintain consistent pressure. These valves are designed to withstand
high pressure, high heat, and EMI (electromagnetic interference), often utilizing aluminum or stainless steel materials.
Primary Contract Purpose
Primarily, this IDIQ will be a contract focused on ensuring the USAF can repair the current and future Flow Control Valve
specs authorized to be installed on F-15EX aircraft. Incidental to the provision of Flow Control Valves are field and depot-
MMaarrcchh 22002266 PPaaggee 22 ooff 77
CUI
Department of the Air Force: Justification for Other Than Full and Open Competition
level support, engineering necessary to implement future variants within the EX-airframe, provisioning and support
equipment. Section IV of this document explains these requirements in greater detail.
Contract Framework and Competition This IDIQ will allow efficient award of depot activation capabilities associated with
the Flow Control Valve. The CLIN structure may include separately priced CLINs for intellectual property (IP) rights as
negotiated with the Contractor. The Contract will be asked to include a data rights assertion list which will be provide as part
of the RFP Package sent to the OEM.
Cost Ceiling Justification The requested $ individual J&A ceiling is based on the PO's estimate for the entire Flow
Control Valve DA IDIQ ordering period, assuming each option is exercised. This ceiling was derived from current
programmatic activities based on in-house cost estimates for future projected DA requirements as explained above.
Cost Exclusions In keeping with the programmatic need to leverage legacy EX hardware, the cost ceiling for this IDIQ
excludes costs associated with qualifying an entirely new Flow Control Valve solution, implementing that new solution onto
existing EX airframes, altering the production line to install that new solution on future EX airframes, and the stand up of new
DA capabilities for any Flow Control Valve solution other than the one being awarded under this contract. These duplicative
costs have been excluded for reasons explained in Section IV below.
IV. Statutory Authority Permitting Other Than Full and Open Competition (RFO 6.104-1(a)(4)):
10 U.S.C. 3204(a)(1), Only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements.
V. Rationale for Use of Authority (RFO 6.104-1(a)(5)):
Background
Currently, ITT Aerospace Controls LLC produces the Flow Control Valves installed on every F-15EX through sole-source
procurement and integration by The Boeing Company (Boeing). ITT Aerospace Controls LLC is the only responsible Original
Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) capable of providing the Flow Control Valve and associated technical data rights necessary
for Depot Activation of the Flow Control Valves. Historically, repairs have been contracted to Boeing, who subcontracted
with ITT Aerospace Controls LLC for Flow Control Valve repairs and maintenance.
ITT Aerospace Controls LLC Flow Control Valve is fully developed, integrated, and has been certified/qualified for use on all
F-15EX aircraft. The Flow Control Valve further meets all safety, suitability, and effectiveness requirements necessary for
fielding EX aircraft. As the OEM of the only compliant Flow Control Valve available to the USAF, ITT Aerospace Controls LLC is
the only source in possession of the technical expertise, technical data, source code, proprietary engineering
documentation, and knowledge necessary to fulfill the delivery and DA requirements the USAF requires to continue fielding
EX aircraft without substantial impacts to cost and schedule.
The risk factors associated with procuring a new organic maintenance repair solution for an Flow Control Valve that is not
the current Flow Control Valve provided by ITT Aerospace Controls LLC are as follows:
Integration Complexity
A new OEM must design and qualify a part, requiring the USAF to act as integrator while Boeing incorporates that part into
the aircraft. This process involves drawing updates, technical order updates, and training updates. The complexity increases
if, as is the case with Flow Control Valve, the part contains software that interfaces with the mission computer, requiring
additional integration activities and a direct contract with Boeing for Operational Flight Program (OFP) updates to achieve
flight clearance.
Interim Support Degradation
The existing OEM has no incentive to continue maintaining OEM Specialized Test Equipment (STE) needed to repair existing
parts under Interim Contractor Support (ICS) or Contractor Logistics Support (CLS) while the USAF waits for new parts to
complete the design, qualification, and integration cycle. This results in degraded performance for maintaining existing
MMaarrcchh 22002266 PPaaggee 33 ooff 77
CUI
Department of the Air Force: Justification for Other Than Full and Open Competition
hardware during the transition period.
Depot Activation Continuity
New OEM selection must include the assumption that the new part will undergo depot activation. Otherwise, the USAF will
face the same OEM limitations with the new supplier as currently experienced with existing OEMs.
The challenges above present considerable cost, schedule, and budgetary risks that the USAF cannot expect to overcome via
the issuance of a competitive source selection for a new Flow Control Valve OEM.
Cost Prohibitions
Procuring and qualifying a new Flow Control Valve solution would result in substantial cost duplication that the Government
cannot expect to recover by conducting a competitive source selection.
Schedule Constraints
The schedule impacts associated with new Flow Control Valve qualifications and implementation are unacceptable. The
timeline to award and qualify a new Flow Control Valve solution includes: 1-2 years for a source selection, 3-5 years for
qualification, and an additional 2-4 years to qualify a new Flow Control Valve source's facilities, personnel, processes, and
procedures.
This entire 6-11 year process would be required if a new Flow Control Valve OEM is selected. With existing contractual
support for inorganic Depot Activation expiring at the end of FY 2026, any solution other than sole-source award to ITT
Aerospace Control LLC will result in EX aircraft being grounded during this extended timeline.
ITT Aerospace Control LLC's Unique Position
ITT Aerospace Control LLC Flow Control Valve is fully developed, integrated, and has been certified/qualified for use on all
F-15EX aircraft. The Flow Control Valve further meets all safety, suitability, and effectiveness requirements necessary for
fielding EX aircraft. As the OEM of the only compliant Flow Control Valve available to the USAF, ITT Aerospace Controls LLC is
the only source in possession of the technical expertise, technical data, source code, proprietary engineering
documentation, and knowledge necessary to fulfill the delivery and DA requirements the USAF requires to continue fielding
EX aircraft without substantial impacts to cost and schedule.
Accordingly, ITT Aerospace Control LLC is the only viable OEM capable of providing the supplies and services identified in
Section III above without the cost, schedule and budgetary risks explained in this section.
VI. Integrated Market Analysis and Efforts to Solicit Competition (RFO 6.104-1(a)(6), (8), and (10)):
In accordance with FAR Subpart 5.2, a synopsis of the proposed contract action was published on SAM.gov.
Furthermore,market research was conducted to identify all potential sources for this requirement, consistent with the
procedures outlined below.
Regulatory Requirement
DFARS PGI 206.302-1(d) states that "When utilizing the authority at FAR 6.302-1, the Contracting Officer shall post a request
for information or a sources sought notice, and shall include the results of this inquiry in the justification required by FAR
6.303.

To achieve this, a sole-source Indefinite Delivery/Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) contract will be awarded to the ITT Aerospace
Controls LLC. This action is justified under FAR 6.302-1 as they are the only responsible source for the Flow Control Valve, a
key component integrated into the F-15EX's baseline design. The contract will facilitate Depot Activation (DA), a process to
establish the capability for comprehensive overhaul, upgrading, or rebuilding of parts and subassemblies, along with
necessary equipment testing and reclamation, as defined in 10 USC Section 2460. This process involves identifying the
necessary facilities, equipment, materials, and certified personnel to perform depot-level maintenance. Depot activation is a
strategic, long-term investment aimed at ensuring a ready and controlled source of technical competence and resources to
respond to national defense contingencies and other emergency requirements.
This contract covers the procurement of essential parts and associated Depot Activation actions for the Flow Control Valve,
supporting both current and future F-15EX sustainment needs.
Due to cost and schedule constraints, the IDIQ contract will have a three-year base ordering period with an additional one-
year option. The total ceiling for this Justification and Approval (J&A) is set at $ which is based on a Rough Order of
Magnitude (ROM) estimate for the depot-level repair capability required for Flow Control Valve repairs.
III. Description of supplies/services required to meet agency needs (RFO 6.104-1(a)(3)):
Establishing an organic, depot-level repair capability requires the strategic delivery of a complete product support package
to the designated ALC(s). This consists of acquiring the required hardware, software, test, technical publication, training,
supply support, packaging, support equipment and data for the designated ALC to repair the depot level repairable(s). To
establish the organic repair capability, delivery of the core infrastructure for depot-level hardware testing and repair is
required. This includes the identification of requirements for, and the subsequent design, build, or purchase of, the
following components: Specialized Test Equipment (STE), Test Program Sets (TPS), and Interface Test Adapters (ITAs).
The United States Air Force (USAF) will provide all common support equipment for this activation effort. Due to proprietary
restrictions stemming from private investment in the development of F-15/F-15EX Line Replaceable Units (LRU), the
government's current ability to establish organic repair of the LRU is not possible. Technical data is restricted by the
manufacturer's intellectual property rights constraints. Therefore, to establish organic repair of the Flow Control Valve,
the USAF needs to negotiate licenses for only the sensitive data needed to repair the LRU. The repair and maintenance of
Flow Control Valves requires not only the Flow Control Valve itself but all associated parts/spares and the rights in
technical data necessary to maintain and ensure the software used in the displays functions correctly to support
verification of repairs at designated ALC.
Flow Control Valves manage, regulate, and shut off fuel, hydraulic, pneumatic, and coolant fluids in aircraft systems. They
provide high-reliability, low-weight solutions designed for severe operating conditions. They regulate the flow rate of
compressed air in pneumatic systems or fluids, directly affecting the speed of actuators. Flow control valves are used in fluid
systems, including fuel pumps and brake controls, to maintain consistent pressure. These valves are designed to withstand
high pressure, high heat, and EMI (electromagnetic interference), often utilizing aluminum or stainless steel materials.
Primary Contract Purpose
Primarily, this IDIQ will be a contract focused on ensuring the USAF can repair the current and future Flow Control Valve
specs authorized to be installed on F-15EX aircraft. Incidental to the provision of Flow Control Valves are field and depot-

CUI
Department of the Air Force: Justification for Other Than Full and Open Competition
level support, engineering necessary to implement future variants within the EX-airframe, provisioning and support
equipment. Section IV of this document explains these requirements in greater detail.
Contract Framework and Competition This IDIQ will allow efficient award of depot activation capabilities associated with
the Flow Control Valve. The CLIN structure may include separately priced CLINs for intellectual property (IP) rights as
negotiated with the Contractor. The Contract will be asked to include a data rights assertion list which will be provide as part
of the RFP Package sent to the OEM.
Cost Ceiling Justification The requested $ individual J&A ceiling is based on the PO's estimate for the entire Flow
Control Valve DA IDIQ ordering period, assuming each option is exercised. This ceiling was derived from current
programmatic activities based on in-house cost estimates for future projected DA requirements as explained above.
Cost Exclusions In keeping with the programmatic need to leverage legacy EX hardware, the cost ceiling for this IDIQ
excludes costs associated with qualifying an entirely new Flow Control Valve solution, implementing that new solution onto
existing EX airframes, altering the production line to install that new solution on future EX airframes, and the stand up of new
DA capabilities for any Flow Control Valve solution other than the one being awarded under this contract. These duplicative
costs have been excluded for reasons explained in Section IV below.
IV. Statutory Authority Permitting Other Than Full and Open Competition (RFO 6.104-1(a)(4)):
10 U.S.C. 3204(a)(1), Only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements.
V. Rationale for Use of Authority (RFO 6.104-1(a)(5)):
Background
Currently, ITT Aerospace Controls LLC produces the Flow Control Valves installed on every F-15EX through sole-source
procurement and integration by The Boeing Company (Boeing). ITT Aerospace Controls LLC is the only responsible Original
Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) capable of providing the Flow Control Valve and associated technical data rights necessary
for Depot Activation of the Flow Control Valves. Historically, repairs have been contracted to Boeing, who subcontracted
with ITT Aerospace Controls LLC for Flow Control Valve repairs and maintenance.
ITT Aerospace Controls LLC Flow Control Valve is fully developed, integrated, and has been certified/qualified for use on all
F-15EX aircraft. The Flow Control Valve further meets all safety, suitability, and effectiveness requirements necessary for
fielding EX aircraft. As the OEM of the only compliant Flow Control Valve available to the USAF, ITT Aerospace Controls LLC is
the only source in possession of the technical expertise, technical data, source code, proprietary engineering
documentation, and knowledge necessary to fulfill the delivery and DA requirements the USAF requires to continue fielding
EX aircraft without substantial impacts to cost and schedule.
The risk factors associated with procuring a new organic maintenance repair solution for an Flow Control Valve that is not
the current Flow Control Valve provided by ITT Aerospace Controls LLC are as follows:
Integration Complexity
A new OEM must design and qualify a part, requiring the USAF to act as integrator while Boeing incorporates that part into
the aircraft. This process involves drawing updates, technical order updates, and training updates. The complexity increases
if, as is the case with Flow Control Valve, the part contains software that interfaces with the mission computer, requiring
additional integration activities and a direct contract with Boeing for Operational Flight Program (OFP) updates to achieve
flight clearance.
Interim Support Degradation
The existing OEM has no incentive to continue maintaining OEM Specialized Test Equipment (STE) needed to repair existing
parts under Interim Contractor Support (ICS) or Contractor Logistics Support (CLS) while the USAF waits for new parts to
complete the design, qualification, and integration cycle. This results in degraded performance for maintaining existing
MMaarrcchh 22002266 PPaaggee 33 ooff 77
CUI
Department of the Air Force: Justification for Other Than Full and Open Competition
hardware during the transition period.
Depot Activation Continuity
New OEM selection must include the assumption that the new part will undergo depot activation. Otherwise, the USAF will
face the same OEM limitations with the new supplier as currently experienced with existing OEMs.
The challenges above present considerable cost, schedule, and budgetary risks that the USAF cannot expect to overcome via
the issuance of a competitive source selection for a new Flow Control Valve OEM.
Cost Prohibitions
Procuring and qualifying a new Flow Control Valve solution would result in substantial cost duplication that the Government
cannot expect to recover by conducting a competitive source selection.
Schedule Constraints
The schedule impacts associated with new Flow Control Valve qualifications and implementation are unacceptable. The
timeline to award and qualify a new Flow Control Valve solution includes: 1-2 years for a source selection, 3-5 years for
qualification, and an additional 2-4 years to qualify a new Flow Control Valve source's facilities, personnel, processes, and
procedures.
This entire 6-11 year process would be required if a new Flow Control Valve OEM is selected. With existing contractual
support for inorganic Depot Activation expiring at the end of FY 2026, any solution other than sole-source award to ITT
Aerospace Control LLC will result in EX aircraft being grounded during this extended timeline.
ITT Aerospace Control LLC's Unique Position
ITT Aerospace Control LLC Flow Control Valve is fully developed, integrated, and has been certified/qualified for use on all
F-15EX aircraft. The Flow Control Valve further meets all safety, suitability, and effectiveness requirements necessary for
fielding EX aircraft. As the OEM of the only compliant Flow Control Valve available to the USAF, ITT Aerospace Controls LLC is
the only source in possession of the technical expertise, technical data, source code, proprietary engineering
documentation, and knowledge necessary to fulfill the delivery and DA requirements the USAF requires to continue fielding
EX aircraft without substantial impacts to cost and schedule.
Accordingly, ITT Aerospace Control LLC is the only viable OEM capable of providing the supplies and services identified in
Section III above without the cost, schedule and budgetary risks explained in this section.
VI. Integrated Market Analysis and Efforts to Solicit Competition (RFO 6.104-1(a)(6), (8), and (10)):
In accordance with FAR Subpart 5.2, a synopsis of the proposed contract action was published on SAM.gov.
Furthermore,market research was conducted to identify all potential sources for this requirement, consistent with the
procedures outlined below.
Regulatory Requirement
DFARS PGI 206.302-1(d) states that "When utilizing the authority at FAR 6.302-1, the Contracting Officer shall post a request
for information or a sources sought notice, and shall include the results of this inquiry in the justification required by FAR
6.303.

Description: THIS SYNOPSIS IS FOR INFORMATIONAL PURPOSES ONLY. The Program Executive Officer Land Systems (PEO-LS), Ground Base Air Defense (GBAD) Marine Corps, Quantico, VA 22134 intends to enter into sole source negotiations and subsequently award a Cost Plus Fixed Fee (CPFF) contract to CACI, Inc. � Federal (CACI) 14370 Newbrook Dr, Chantilly, VA 20151 USA (Cage Code: 1QU78). CACI is the Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) of the CM-262 optic systems modified and integrated into the Marine Air Defense Integrated System (MADIS) program. CACI holds the modification rights to the CM-262 source code and remains the only source available to provide the hardware and software lifecycle support. The proposed contract action provides the required supplies and services including the continued software lifecycle management support activities needed to test and sustain the optic systems and associated software applications within the MADIS software baseline; continued procurement of necessary licenses; software maintenance; and provides updates and modifications to the core optic software for integration, test, and evaluation program events. Additionally, this requirement includes services for the repair and maintenance of optic component hardware in support of the MADIS Family of Systems as well as options to procure additional optic systems if existing program approved acquisition objective quantities increase. The software applications must maintain interoperability with the associated information systems as they continue to upgrade and refresh over time. The Government does not possess the required rights to the source code necessary to support a competitive procurement for the hardware and software lifecycle management effort. THIS NOTICE IS NOT A REQUEST FOR COMPETITIVE PROPOSALS. This acquisition is being pursued on a sole source basis under the statutory authority of 10 U.S.C. 2304(c)(1), as implemented by Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 6.302-1(a)(2)(ii)(A) "Only One Responsible Source and No Other Supplies or Services Will Satisfy Agency Requirements". The North American Industry Classification System code is 333310, Commercial and Service Industry Machinery Manufacturing. The Product or Service Code is 1240, Optical Sighting and Ranging Equipment. The Government has not made a commitment to procure any of the items discussed and should not be construed as a commitment or as authorization to incur cost for which reimbursement would be required or sought. All responses to this notice shall be submitted to Mr. Kyle Bond at kyle.r.bond.civ@usmc.mil and Ms. Megan Brady at megan.brady.civ@usmc.mil . Description: Intent to sole source to NexTech Solutions (NTS). This is not a solicitation and quotes are not being accepted at the moment. The 355th Communication Squadron requires eight (8) High Assurance Internet Protocol Encryptor (HAIPE) systems to establish a mobile Mission Planning Cell (MPC) capable of supporting Expeditionary operations and Mission Generation Force Element (MGFE) deployments during contingencies and exercises. The Government intends to solicit and negotiate with only one source under the authority of FAR 6.302-1. Government intends to solicit to procure the below listed item. The Government does not possess or cannot provide the data necessary to manufacture the item: - Must provide both NIPRNet and SIPRNet connectivity, enabling access to essential mission?planning and execution products (e.g., ATO, ACO, AOD, SPINS) from any austere global location. - Small?form?factor configuration capable of providing NIPRNet and SIPRNet services via a U.S. Government transport provider (e.g., DISA, SNOC, JCSE). - Minimum 8 NIPRNet and 8 SIPRNet ports per system. - Ruggedized construction capable of withstanding drops and environmental exposure outside a protective case. - Internal battery power using replaceable MIL?STD radio batteries, plus external AC power capability. Integrated crypto sled supporting small?form?factor encryption devices. - Multiple dirty?internet integration options including:Built?in 5G SIM card port. - Ability to ingest wired internet from a Starshield terminal or other Ethernet?based solution. - Single?person portability with no palletization required. - Setup/teardown under 10 minutes. All responsible sources may identify their interest and provide capability statements in response to this notice. This notice of intent is not a request for competitive proposals. However, all responses received within 3 work days after date of publication of this sources sought notice will be considered by the Government. A determination by the Government not to compete with this proposed contract based upon responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. Approval of a source is required. 355 CONS will not delay award while Source Approval is pending. The time required for approval of a new source is normally such that an award cannot be delayed pending approval of a new source. This notice serves as the synopsis and notice of intent to sole-source. attachments.text:
CONTROLLED UNCLASSIFIED INFORMATION
Single Source Justification (Simplified Acquisition)
Section A: General Contract Information
Is this a Bridge Action as defined in the AF Bridge Action Reduction Plan? Yes No
Contracting Activity: 355th CONS PKP
Project/Program Name: Tuck-19 (HAIPE ) TAC Kits (Sole Source to NexTech Solutions (NTS))
Purchase Request / Local ID Number: F1P3XP6092AC01
Estimated Contract Cost (including Options): $0.00
Section B: Description of the Supplies/Services Required
355th Wing requires eight (8) Rebel Systems TUCK‑19 High Assurance Internet Protocol Encryptor (HAIPE) systems to establish a
mobile Mission Planning Cell (MPC) capable of supporting expeditionary operations and Mission Generation Force Element
(MGFE) deployments during contingencies and exercises. While Rebel Systems manufactures the hardware, NexTech Solutions
(NTS) provides the proprietary software integration that makes the TUCK‑19 uniquely capable. Therefore, 355th Wing must limit
competition because competing solutions would require multiple systems and lack seamless transport switching, resulting in
unacceptable mission‑critical connectivity gaps. As a result, the requirement is being prepared as a Sole Source procurement to NTS.
Procuring these four systems will allow the Wing to support simultaneous ATO execution and MGFE operations at up to two
geographically separated locations when tasked.
Requirements:
- Must provide both NIPRNet and SIPRNet connectivity, enabling access to essential mission‑planning and execution products (e.g.,
ATO, ACO, AOD, SPINS) from any austere global location.
- Small‑form‑factor configuration capable of providing NIPRNet and SIPRNet services via a U.S. Government transport provider
(e.g., DISA, SNOC, JCSE).
- Minimum 8 NIPRNet and 8 SIPRNet ports per system.
- Ruggedized construction capable of withstanding drops and environmental exposure outside a protective case.
- Internal battery power using replaceable MIL‑STD radio batteries, plus external AC power capability. Integrated crypto sled
supporting small‑form‑factor encryption devices.
- Multiple dirty‑internet integration options including:Built‑in 5G SIM card port.
- Ability to ingest wired internet from a Starshield terminal or other Ethernet‑based solution.
- Single‑person portability with no palletization required.
- Setup/teardown under 10 minutes.
Section C: Justification for Soliciting from a Single Source or Brand Name
Market research identified at least four HAIPE‑capable solutions; however, the Rebel Systems TUCK‑19 is the only unit found that
meets the full combination of operational, environmental, and integration requirements.
April 2021 CONTROLLED UNCLASSIFIED INFORMATION Page 1 of 3
CONTROLLED UNCLASSIFIED INFORMATION
Single Source Justification (Simplified Acquisition)
Tuck-19 system provides all of the below:
- Mobile networking platform that delivers fully integrated, automated PACE failover across 5G, Wi‑Fi, and transport services
within a single, ultra‑rugged, smallest‑in‑class chassis.
- Automated switching that requires no operator action, ensuring uninterrupted connectivity during mission‑critical operations and
rapid deployment in contested or austere environments.
- Ruggedized operation outside a Pelican case.
- Small form factor and true man‑portability.
- Integrated small‑form‑factor crypto sled
- Native 5G SIM card integration.
- MIL‑STD replaceable battery power.
- NIPRNet/SIPRNet‑only connectivity.
- Simplified operation suitable for non‑communications personnel.
- No end‑of‑life or legacy hardware concerns.
NTS integration of the following:
- MANTLE automation suite - GUI‑driven configuration enabling full system setup within minutes.
- Virtualized routing environment - dynamic, software‑defined routing across multiple transports.
- Embedded HyperVisor architecture - secure virtualization for routing and network management.
No other vendor found provides this combination of rugged hardware, automated failover, integrated routing, and simplified
configuration in a single deployable platform. Without NTS's integration, the TUCK‑19 would not meet 355 WG requirements for
AEW 2.0 deployment. Alternative solutions would require multiple devices, increase system complexity, and introduce unacceptable
connectivity gaps during transport transitions.
Section D: Efforts to Obtain Competition
Cubic and Curtiss‑Wright were evaluated but could not meet the full requirement identified. Strategic sourcing channels were
reviewed with no viable alternatives identified. Additionally, a Request for Quotation (RFQ) was posted on NASA SEWP, allowing
127 companies the opportunity to bid. The notice remained open for one week. NexTech Solutions, a large business, has previously
been awarded two sole‑source contracts (FA441821F0160 and FA570225F0115) through NASA SEWP platform.
Section E: Steps to Preclude Future Single Source or Brand Name Awards
For future purchases or technology refreshes, the 355 WG will reassess all available solutions to determine whether multiple vendors
can meet mission requirements. If more than one system is capable, open competition will be pursued. Additionally, the Wing will
April 2021 CONTROLLED UNCLASSIFIED INFORMATION Page 2 of 3
CONTROLLED UNCLASSIFIED INFORMATION
Single Source Justification (Simplified Acquisition)
continue monitoring the market for emerging technologies that replicate or exceed the TUCK‑19's integrated capabilities. Although
the specialized nature of this requirement suggests NexTech Solutions may remain the only viable provider in the near term, periodic
market research will be conducted to identify potential competitors as technology evolves. Finally, to encourage future competition,
the Wing will also broadcast requirements and engage with industry partners, particularly within the defense IT sector, to stimulate
innovation in rapidly deployable C2 solutions for austere environments.
Section F: Contracting Officer's Determination
I have determined, in accordance with FAR 13.106-1(b)(1), that the circumstances of this contract action deem only a
single source is reasonably available.

Description: N00164-26-Q-0153 � SOLE SOURCE - Keysight Electrical and Electronic Equipment � FSG 5963 � NAICS 334515 ISSUE DATE 04-JUN-2026 � CLOSING DATE 16-JUN-2026 � 11:00 PM Eastern Time ITEM DESCRIPTION- Naval Surface Warfare Center (NSWC) Crane has a requirement for Sole Source procurement through Keysight Technology Inc for electrical and electronic equipment SOLE SOURCE PROCUREMENT- The proposed contract action is for the supplies or services for which the Government intends to solicit and negotiate with one source only KEYSIGHT TECHNOLOGIES INCof Colorado Springs, Colorado, Cage Code 7ZXR5, under the authority of FAR 12.201-1 for Commercial using simplified procedures. This is being solicited on a sole source only basis because This equipment is a cornerstone for the SPY-3 TRIMM program, a new developmental effort to establish an organic capability to test and repair SPY-3 TRIMM antenna modules returning from the fleet. The program is presently relying on loaned equipment tied to another program, which is not a sustainable or reliable solution for meeting developmental deadlines. The acquisition of this dedicated equipment is a critical and urgent step to complete the Automated Test Equipment (ATE) test set, which is required to enter the depot timeline and achieve necessary depot certifications. The requested equipment from Keysight Technologies forms a uniquely integrated and proprietary modular system. The N6700C/N6702C mainframes and the corresponding power modules are designed by the Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) to work as a single, cohesive unit. The hardware, firmware, communication protocols, and software are proprietary to Keysight, and for this reason, there are no "or-equal" components from other manufacturers that are compatible or can provide the same integrated functionality. All responsible sources may submit a capability statement, which shall be considered by the agency. However, a determination by the Government not to compete with this proposed contract based upon responses to this solicitation is solely within the discretion of the Government. Information received will normally be considered solely for the purpose of determining whether to conduct a competitive procurement. Description: NO TELEPHONE REQUESTS WILL BE ACCEPTED. DIRECT YOUR REQUESTS AND COMMUNICATION TO: ATTN: DLA-AHCA, MARI BRETZ, CONTRACT SPECIALIST; VIA EMAIL HECMARI.BRETZ@DLA.MIL. SOLICITATION WILL BE PUBLISHED IN SAM.GOV, FOR ALL OTHER INQUIRIES, IN THE EMAIL SUBJECT LINE ENTER SPRRA2-26-R-0083, PROVIDE YOUR NAME, THE COMPANY NAME AND CAGE CODE AND A TELEPHONE NUMBER AND EMAIL ADDRESS. IN SUPPORT OF THE MULTIPLE LAUNCH ROCKET SYSTEM (MLRS), THE GOVERNMENT PROPOSES TO ACQUIRE THE FOLLOWING ON A FIRM FIXED PRICE (FFP) SINGLE PURCHASE CONTRACT. PRON: D16T0126D1, CONTROL SECTION,GUI, NSN: 1420-01-540-8608, PART#: 13540365, AN ESTIMATED QUANTITY OF 35 EACH. THE ESTIMATED PRODUCTION LEAD TIME (PLT) WITH FIRST ARTICLE TESTING (FAT) IS 675 DAYS AFTER CONTRACT AWARD (DACA), AND WITHOUT FIRST ARTICLE TESTING (FAT) IS 450 DAYS AFTER CONTRACT AWARD (DACA) AND WITH DELIVERIES TO CHAMBERSBURG, PA, 17201-4150. THIS ITEM IS RESTRICTED TO: LOCKHEED MARTIN CORPORATION MISSILES AND FIRE CONTROL, CAGE: 64059. THE TECHNICAL DATA FOR THIS PART HAS UNDERGONE FULL SCREENING PER THE DFARS PGI 217.7506, SPARE PARTS BREAKOUT PROGRAM. THIS ITEM HAS BEEN ASSIGNED AMC/AMSC CODE 3B. PART# 13540365 HAS BEEN ASSIGNED AMC/AMSC CODE 3B AND MUST BE ACQUIRED, FOR THE SECOND OR SUBSEQUENT TIME, DIRECTLY FROM THE ACTUAL MANUFACTURER. THIS PART MUST BE ACQUIRED FROM A MANUFACTURING SOURCE(S) SPECIFIED ON A SOURCE CONTROL OR SELECTED ITEM DRAWING AS DEFINED BY THE CURRENT VERSION OF DOD-STD-100. SUITABLE TECHNICAL DATA, GOVERNMENT DATA RIGHTS, OR MANUFACTURING KNOWLEDGE ARE NOT AVAILABLE TO PERMIT ACQUISITION FROM OTHER SOURCES, NOR QUALIFICATION TESTING OF ANOTHER PART, NOR USE OF A SECOND SOURCE PART IN THE INTENDED APPLICATION. ALTHOUGH, BY DOD-STD-100 DEFINITION, ALTERED AND SELECTED ITEMS SHALL HAVE AN ADEQUATE TECHNICAL DATA PACKAGE, DATA REVIEW DISCLOSES THAT REQUIRED DATA OR DATA RIGHTS ARE NOT IN GOVERNMENT POSSESSION AND CANNOT BE ECONOMICALLY OBTAINED. IF ONE SOURCE IS AVAILABLE, AMCS 3, 4, OR 5 ARE VALID. IF AT LEAST TWO SOURCES EXIST, AMCS 1 OR 2 ARE VALID. AS A RESULT, THIS ACQUISITION IS CURRENTLY BEING PROCURED UNDER FEDERAL ACQUISITION REGULATION (FAR) 6.302-1(A)(2) HAVING ONLY A LIMITED NUMBER OF RESPONSIBLE SOURCES. THE GOVERNMENT IS INTERESTED IN ALL BUSINESSES TO INCLUDE 8(A), SMALL BUSINESS AND SMALL DISADVANTAGED BUSINESS, SERVICE-DISABLED VETERAN-OWNED, HUBZONE, AND WOMEN-OWNED SMALL BUSINESS CONCERNS. ALL OFFERORS MUST MEET PREQUALIFICATION REQUIREMENTS IN ORDER TO BE ELIGIBLE FOR AWARD. THE U.S. ARMY COMBAT CAPABILITIES DEVELOPMENT COMMAND AVIATION & MISSILE CENTER�S (AVMC DEVCOM) SYSTEM READINESS DIRECTORATE (SRD), SUSTAINMENT DIVISION (SD) IS THE ENGINEERING SOURCE AUTHORITY (ESA). FIRMS THAT RECOGNIZE AND CAN PRODUCE THE REQUIRED ITEM DESCRIBED ABOVE ARE ENCOURAGED TO IDENTIFY THEMSELVES. FIRMS ARE ENCOURAGED TO SEEK SOURCE APPROVAL IN ORDER TO COMPETE FOR FUTURE SOLICITATIONS BY CONTACTING THE CONTRACT TEAM. THE CLOSING DATE ANNOTATED IS AN ESTIMATED DATE AND MAY BE ADJUSTED DEPENDENT UPON THE DATE OF RELEASE FOR SOLICITATION; HOWEVER, THE SOLICITATION WILL NOT CLOSE PRIOR TO THE DATE STATED ABOVE. FOREIGN FIRMS ARE REMINDED THAT ALL REQUESTS FOR SOLICITATION MUST BE PROCESSED THROUGH THEIR RESPECTIVE EMBASSIES. THE CONTRACTOR SHALL BE CAPABLE OF SUCCESSFULLY PERFORMING AND COMPLYING WITH ANY AND ALL SPECIAL REQUIREMENTS IN ACCORDANCE WITH THE TERMS AND CONDITIONS SET FORTH IN THE SOLICITATION ANNOTATED ABOVE, AT THE UNIT PRICES ESTABLISHED AT TIME OF A CONTRACT AWARD. THE CONTRACTOR WILL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR RECURRING AND NONRECURRING ENGINEERING SERVICES ASSOCIATED WITH BECOMING A QUALIFIED SOURCE. THE CONTRACTOR WILL ALSO BE RESPONSIBLE FOR ALL ASPECTS OF THE MANUFACTURING/PRODUCTION PROCESS, INCLUDING BUT NOT LIMITED TO - SUPPLY CHAIN MANAGEMENT, LOGISTICS, FORECASTING OF PARTS, LONG-LEAD PARTS PROCUREMENT, MATERIAL FORECASTING, OBSOLESCENCE ISSUES AND FINAL DELIVERY OF ASSETS AS WELL AS ANY AND ALL ADDITIONAL COSTS INCURRED RESULTING FROM CONTRACT PERFORMANCE. PROCUREMENT CONSISTS OF TWO OR MORE REQUIREMENTS FOR SUPPLIES, BASED ON FORECASTED DEMANDS. THE SUBSEQUENT SOLICITATION SHALL INCLUDE A REQUEST FOR ECONOMIC ORDER QUANTITIES (EOQS) TO ENSURE OPTIMAL ORDERING QUANTITIES. THE EOQ REQUEST, IS TO AVOID ACQUISITIONS IN DISADVANTAGEOUS QUANTITIES AND TO ASSIST THE GOVERNMENT IN DEVELOPING DATA FOR CURRENT AND FUTURE ACQUISITIONS OF THIS ITEM/THESE ITEMS. THE GOVERNMENT ANTICIPATES THE OFFEROR�S PROPOSAL (IN VIEW OF MARKET RESEARCH, HISTORICAL AWARDS, THE NATURE OF THE ITEM(S) BEING SOLICITED, AND THE CURRENT ECONOMIC ENVIRONMENT) WILL INCLUDE QUANTITIES/RANGES THAT WILL VARY FROM THOSE BEING SOLICITED. THE SOLICITED QUANTITIES ARE BASED ON ESTIMATED ANNUAL DEMANDS AND AS SUCH GOVERNMENT RESERVES THE RIGHT TO AWARD THE MOST ADVANTAGEOUS QUANTITIES &/OR RANGES. THE GOVERNMENT RETAINS THE RIGHT TO CANCEL THIS PROCUREMENT, PARTIALLY OR IN ENTIRETY BEFORE AWARD. IN THE EVENT THE GOVERNMENT CANCELS THIS ACQUISITION (PARTIALLY OR IN ENTIRETY) BEFORE AWARD, THE GOVERNMENT HAS NO OBLIGATION TO REIMBURSE AN OFFEROR FOR ANY COSTS. THIS ACQUISITION MAY CONTAIN TECHNICAL DATA WHOSE EXPORT IS RESTRICTED BY THE ARMS EXPORT CONTROL ACT (TITLE 22, USC., SEC 2751 ET SEQ) OR THE EXPORT ADMINISTRATION ACT (TITLE 50, USC., APP 2401-2402) EXECUTIVE ORDER 12470. Section A: General Contract Information
Section A: General Contract Information

Section B: Description of the Supplies/Services Required
Section B: Description of the Supplies/Services Required

A quantity of 1 asset will be procured. The item will be purchased using FMS funds. This purchase is intended to provide the asset necessary to support the current mission requirements of the FMS F-16 aircraft. The procurement will be a total of 1ea with an estimated unit price of $126,505.00 and an estimated total contract price of
$126,505.00.

NSN: 5895-01-567-7326
Part Number: 8010000806-4
Quantity: 1 each

Section C: Justification for Soliciting from a Single Source or Brand Name
Section C: Justification for Soliciting from a Single Source or Brand Name

The agency's minimum needs can only be satisfied by the unique supplies or services available from Symetrics Industries L.L.C dba Extant Aerospace (Extant) or via their agreement with Integrated Procurement Technologies dated 25 August 2020. The CARA system technical data rights were purchased by Extant from NavCom Defense Electronics, Inc., the Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM), in Oct 2018. A

The last buy was a sole source to NavCom under contract SPRWA112D0004. Period of performance was from 20 Sept 2012 to 19 Sept 2014. NavCom completed the entirety of this contract.

The Government does not possess the complete technical data package (TDP). The complete TDP for manufacture of the Signal Data Converter (SDC) is now owned by Extant. A complete engineering data package is not available for competitive solicitation due to proprietary rights claimed by the manufacturer. The SDC requires highly specialized technical skills, use of Extant proprietary data, and specialized equipment and facilities to manufacture these items. This data is proprietary and the contractor refuses to release the rights or sell the data.

The CARA system is military unique and must meet form, fit, function, interface (F3I) requirements, military standards, and pass applicable inspection and acceptance processes. Extant possesses the unique skill, equipment, facilities, and production data necessary to perform SDC production.

The assigned AMC/AMSC code is 5/P and was established on 31 October 2024. AMC "5" indicates acquire directly from a sole source contractor which is not the actual manufacturer. AMSC "P" indicates that the rights to use the data needed to purchase this item from additional sources are not owned by the Government and cannot be purchased.


Section D: Efforts to Obtain Competition
Section D: Efforts to Obtain Competition

A Sources Sought Synopsis (SSS) was posted to Sam.gov on 19 March 2024 with a response date of 2 April 2024 under Notice ID SPRWA1-00318. The SSS requested responses from interested vendors that possess the expertise, capabilities, and experience to meet qualification requirements for this effort. Integrated Procurement Technologies, on behalf of Extant, was the only source that expressed an interest and submitted a response.

Extant and IPT are the only sources identified through the market research that possesses the technical data, facilities, test equipment, and expertise required to manufacture and repair the CARA SDC. Extant and IPT are the sole source manufacture for the CARA SDC. The Government does not possess a technical data package to support a competitive award, nor does the Government have the capability to independently validate the operational capability range of end repair or production items. The incumbent, Extant was determined to be the only capable vendor.


Section E: Steps to Preclude Future Single Source or Brand Name Awards
Section E: Steps to Preclude Future Single Source or Brand Name Awards

To preclude single source awards for future procurements the Integrated Product Team will continue to conduct AMC/AMSC screening analysis, publish a Sources Sought Synopses to the SAM.gov website to determine industry interest.
While the current market research indicates limited competition to approved sources for the CARA system, the Government will engage Extant on an annual basis to determine the feasibility of procuring the TDP.


Section F: Contracting Officer's Determination
Section F: Contracting Officer's Determination

I have determined, in accordance with FAR 13.106-1(b)(1), that the circumstances of this contract action deem only a single source is reasonably available.

technical data, tooling, and configuration specifications. No other source is legally or technically capable of
producing, modifying, or supplying this engine in a manner that meets the agency’s operational, safety, and
compatibility requirements. Because the OEM is the sole entity with the legal authority and technical
capability to provide this engine, restricting competition is necessary and fully supported by the statutory
framework governing commercial item acquisitions and simplified acquisition procedures.
5. Rationale Supporting Use of Cited Authority
The equipment specified in this Contract is original to the Gladding Hearn designed and built 64-foot Patrol
Boat (64PB), as procured by Government Contract N00024-07-F-2213, Modification 3.
Sole Source OEM: MTU Friedrichshafen GmbH is the original equipment manufacturer (OEM) of the SV-64
engine. As the OEM, MTU is the sole designer, developer, and producer, and possesses the exclusive proprietary
technical data, specialized tooling, and manufacturing expertise required to produce this engine. No other source
has access to the necessary drawings or intellectual property.
Item Obsolescence: The SV-64 engine is obsolete and no longer in serial production. MTU has agreed to re-
establish a production line for the express purpose of this single production run for the U.S. Navy. This is a unique,
one-time opportunity to fulfill the Government's total life-cycle requirement. Non-Severable Requirement: The
significant, one-time cost and logistical effort for MTU to re-establish the obsolete production line make it
prohibitive to conduct smaller, recurring procurements. The cost to the Government to reopen the production line
annually would be vastly expensive and fiscally irresponsible. Therefore, a single, one-time life-cycle purchase is
the only viable acquisition strategy.
6. Market Research Conducted
In accordance with RFO 12.102, market research has confirmed that only one responsible source is capable
of meeting the Government’s minimum requirements, supporting the restriction of competition and the use
of a brand-name description without allowing for “equal” products. No synopsis was published as this is a
purchase of a supply for which there is only one responsible source; market research (detailed in paragraph
8) has definitively confirmed that MTU is the only entity with the capability to produce new SV-64 engines.
Therefore, soliciting offers from other sources would serve no purpose and would only result in unnecessary
delay to a critical procurement. Consistent with RFO 5.101(b)(2), when the Government has established that
only one source is available, a synopsis is not required, and public notice is not necessary for this action.
7. Description of Efforts Made to Solicit Offers from as Many Potential Sources as Practicable
The Contracting Officer will determine the final negotiated price to be fair and reasonable prior to award. A
detailed cost and price analysis will be conducted upon receipt of the contractor's certified proposal to ensure
the final price is fair and reasonable.
8. Fair and Reasonable Determination
Market research was conducted to identify alternative solutions and potential sources. This research
confirmed that no other manufacturer has the capability to produce the required SV-64 engine. Furthermore,
research and analysis were conducted on the alternative of rebuilding existing engines. This alternative was
deemed not viable due to two primary factors:
No Cost or Schedule Advantage: Rebuilding existing engines does not provide a meaningful cost or time
savings compared to procuring newly manufactured engines.
Material Scarcity: A severe and growing scarcity of existing engine blocks, a critical component for rebuilds,
makes this alternative logistically unsupportable for the full lifecycle requirement. The program has already
exhausted its on-hand inventory of rebuilt engines to avoid a , highlighting the
unsustainability of this approach.
This research conclusively demonstrates that a sole-source, one-time purchase from the OEM is the only
course of action that satisfies the Government's need.

attachments.text:
DRAFT Statement of Work
Silane Distribution System
Background Information: 

The National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST)-Boulder has a state-of-the-art research laboratory (the Katharine Blodgett Gebbie Building) to support the most sensitive research done at NIST. Included in this building is a Class 100 microelectronics fabrication facility, called the Boulder Micro-Fabrication Facility (BMF). Among the many critical pieces of equipment in this laboratory is equipment that uses the process gasses silane (SiH4). Silane is a toxic and pyrophoric gas and needs to be stored in and outside bunker using a gas rack and is delivered to tools through a specialized gas valve manifold box (VMB). Recently, the BMF has learned that their existing system has reached end of life and the system needs to be replaced for safety and operational reasons. The Government requires a new silane delivery system that is compatible with its existing life safety equipment, such as the toxic gas monitoring system and other gas cabinets to continue to use silane as process gasses.

Scope of Work:

Objectives: 

The goal of this contract is to provide the Government with a new silane distribution system consisting of a gas rack and VMB to meet the needs of the NIST Boulder community.

General:
The contractor shall:
Provide personnel that pass required government background checks to be issued badges for work on site.
Provide all new items. Prototypes, one-off systems, demonstration models, used instruments, or refurbished instruments are unacceptable.

Specifications for the Work:
All staff must be badged by NIST Security. No one may enter the site without a badge.
The work and badging shall be scheduled with the Contracting Officer’s Representative (COR) and/or Technical Point of Contact (TPOC) prior to arrival to do the work.

Specific Requirements:

The contractor shall provide the Government with a silane distribution system that is compatible with the Governments existing SDC CiphercoNTM gas delivery infrastructure. To maintain critical life-safety continuity, the new system shall utilize identical spare parts, safety interlock mechanisms, and software architecture as the existing SDC gas delivery infrastructure.
System Requirements:
The silane distribution system shall consist of a silane gas rack and a silane VMB.
The new gas rack shall be a CiphercoN™ 1500 Gas Rack or equivalent with the following specifications:
Be able to be repaired using spare parts from the Government’s existing stock of spare parts for a SDC CiphercoNTM 1500 cabinet.
Be constructed of materials that are compatible for use with silane.
Meet all applicable code for delivering silane such as SEMI S2 and/or CGA-13 standards.
Be able to deliver Ultra High Purity (UHP) silane to a VMB in a manner that is consistent with semiconductor industry standards.
Be able to deliver silane to each system in a fully automated, computer-controlled method using a touch screen.
Be a two-cylinder system with one cylinder being an independent out, configured for silane, and the other as an onboard purge system, configured as nitrogen.
The gas Rack shall meet all CGA-13 requirements, including but not limited to:
High pressure test circuit
Vent purge trickle
Reduced flow orifice (RFO)
Have a Z-purge system.
Be able to be used outdoors in Boulder, Colorado, USA year-round.
The system shall include a control heater system if required.
Any weather proofing required to operate year-round.
Have an appropriate integrated UVIR detection and safety shutoffs.
Have an adjustable cylinder shelf to accommodate standard size gas cylinders.
Have the ability to accommodate gas cylinders with an industry standard automatic pneumatic valve and a manual hand valve. 
Have dual stage regulators.
Have CGA standard DISS fittings for the lines that connect to both the silane and nitrogen gas cylinders.
Have a process gas out line filter appropriate to industry standards for the semiconductor industry.
Have a purge inlet filter appropriate to industry standards for the semiconductor industry.
Have an EMO button.
Have an evacuate system that is able to independently evacuate the delivery line, purge line, and the inlet line of the system to vacuum pressures that is consistent with semiconductor industry standards.
Have the ability to communicate with the Government’s existing Toxic Gas Monitoring System (TGMS) where it can send and receive signals including but not limited to: the gas rack is ready to deliver gas, the gas rack is not able to deliver gas, and can receive and shut down signal to shut down the system.
Have an excess flow switch that can shut down the line delivery in case of a large change in flow signifying a leak.
Have a manual isolation valve on the output that has the ability to be locked out with a lock for standard LOTO procedures.
The new gas rack shall be a FlexGas™ VMB or equivalent with the following specifications:
Be able to receive gas from the gas rack and deliver UHP silane to up to 8 process tools in a manner that is consistent with semiconductor industry standards.
Be constructed of materials that are compatible for use with silane.
Meet all applicable code for delivering silane such as SEMI S2 and/or CGA-13 standards.
Be able to deliver silane to each system in a fully automated, computer-controlled method using a touch screen.
Be able to deliver silane to each system in a fully automated, computer controlled method.
Be able to independently deliver silane to 6 systems with the ability to expand the system to 8 delivery lines.
Have a nitrogen purge system that is able to independently purge each delivery line and the inlet line of the system.
A manual input isolation valve that has the ability to be locked out with a lock for standard LOTO procedures.
Have an evacuate system that is able to independently evacuate each delivery line, purge line, and the inlet line of the system to vacuum pressures that is consistent with semiconductor industry standards.
Have an inlet manifold electronic shut off valve
Have an appropriate integrated UVIR detection and safety shutoffs.
Have an EMO button.
Each of the 6 delivery lines shall have:
 An automated line isolation valve with contacts for a tool to call gas or to signal that gas is available.
A manual input isolation valve that has the ability to be locked out with a lock for standard LOTO procedures.
A manual outlet isolation valve that has the ability to be locked out with a lock for standard LOTO procedures.
An automatic purge isolation valve
A pressure regulator to regulate pressure for pressures consistent with semiconductor industry standards for the use of silane.
An electronic pressure transducer to measure each line’s delivery pressure.
An excess flow switch that can shut down the line delivery in case of a large change in flow signifying a leak.
An automated evacuation isolation valve
Have the ability to communicate with the Government’s existing TGMS where it can send and receive signals including but not limited to: the gas rack is ready to deliver gas, the gas rack is not able to deliver gas, and can receive and shut down signal to shut down the system and each silane stick individually.
Be expandable to include 2 more spare user configurable gas delivery lines that meet the same requirements listed in REF _Ref226621060 \w \h 2.c.ii.3.l.

Delivery and Installation:
The contractor shall be responsible for delivering the silane gas rack and VMB to the Government. After the gas rack and VMB are delivered, the Government will then be able to facilitize the system for a period between system delivery and site commissioning. This time period shall be at least 1 month and will not exceed 1 year, and the actual time period will be agreed upon between the Government and the contractor. If facilitization occurs faster than the agreed upon time period, then the contractor may start the commissioning on a date that is mutually agreeable between the Government and the contractor.

Commissioning and acceptance:
After the gas rack and VMB are facilitized, the contract shall commission the gas rack and VMB using a standard site acceptance test. The system will be accepted by the Government after the system passes the site acceptance test.
After completing the site acceptance test, the contractor shall assist the Government in introducing gas back to all of the process lines. Additionally, the contractor shall provide written directions on how to perform a cylinder change, pumping out the delivery line to the VMB, and introducing process gas to the VMB.
The contractor shall be responsible for all travel expenses.

NIST-SS26-133 Amendment 01 - Silane Distribution System
June 1, 2026
Questions & Answers (Q&A)

Q1.SOW c.ii.2.a. – We do not believe we can do this, we don’t know enough about the Stainless Design product to determine what might be re-usable.A1.We have two spare CipherCon 1500 gas rack systems. Roughly ~$40k-$50k worth of spare parts.
Q2.SOW c.ii.2.i. – Will the outdoor system be under a roof, or in a lean-to? If its will be completely exposed, we will have to use only stainless steel. A2.The system is under a roof that is about 12’4” high. However, the edge of the roof is about 4’6” away so it does get a fair amount of weather. Additionally, we’re in Boulder, CO with mean winter temperatures of 21F to 48F with a record low of -33F in 1930.
Q3.SOW c.ii.2.l. – how do you intend to control the change from pneumatic to manual regarding the system software?A3.We should be able to change between the two in software.
Q4.SOW c.ii.2.p – What is the purpose of the purge inlet filter? Do you possible mean purifier?A4. This is a particulate filter to make sure no particles go from the cylinder into the line.
Q5.SOW c.ii.3.a – what is the flow rate required if all eight tools are in use? Please provide a per line flow.A5. 800 sccm total (100 sccm per tool)
Q6.SOW c.ii.3.f – contrast line f with c.ii.3.a.A6.a. is the requirement that the system is able to have 8 lines, f. says that only 6 lines need to be populated with the valves, gauges, regulators, etc with the ability to field add two more lines.
Q7.SOWc.ii.3.j. – is a pneumatic shut off valve acceptable, we believe this is what most semiconductor silane processes use. A7.Pneumatic valve is acceptable to meet the requirement of c.ii.3.j
Q8.SOW c.ii.3.m.i. – we don’t understand this requirementA8.Each line needs to be able to interact with our toxic gas monitoring system so that we can independently control and shutdown delivery lines tool by tool depending on tool status.
Q9.SOW c.ii.3.m.ii. / c.ii.3.m.iii. – why are both of these required? IS either / or acceptable?A9.We require both input and output valves to be able to isolate the system on both the input and output for both safety and troubleshooting reasons.
