matters.title: Notice of Intent to Sole Source - Acquisition of a Level D 747-8i Full Motion Simulator
matters.text:
Federal notice (Special Notice), DEPT OF DEFENSE.DEPT OF THE AIR FORCE.FA8641 PRES ALFT DIR AFLCMC WVBK
Title: Notice of Intent to Sole Source - Acquisition of a Level D 747-8i Full Motion Simulator
Solicitation number: FA8641-26-R-B001
PSC: 6930; NAICS: 336413
Description: 1. Statement of Intent & Authority The United States Air Force (USAF), AFLFMC/WVB intends to award a sole source, firm-fixed-price contract to CAE USA Inc. (CAE), Orlando, Florida, CAGE: 1FNV1. This action is being executed under the authority of 10 U.S.C. 3204(a)(1) as implemented by RFO 6.103-1, Only One Responsible Source and No Other Supplies or Services Will Satisfy Agency Requirements. 2. Description of Requirement AFLCMC/WVB has an critical, urgent, and mission-essential requirement for one (1) dedicated, commercial, FAA Level D certified 747-8i Full Flight Simulator (FFS) to be located at Joint Base Andrews (JBA). The procurement includes: Site survey and facility evaluation. Procurement, delivery, and installation of the FFS (including 6-DOF motion, visual system, sound system, and exact 747-8i cockpit replica). Operational hardware, software, and cybersecurity compliant with DoDI 8500.01/8510.01 and applicable AFI/DoD Manuals. Initial support and maintenance, including spare parts and software updates. Initial training, courseware, and flight instruction. The Government intends to procure this requirement using Commercial procedures in accordance with RFO Part 12. Period of Performance (PoP): Delivery and installation is estimated at 24-36 months from contract award, followed by a 12-18 month support and maintenance PoP. 3. Justification for Sole Source CAE is the only responsible source capable of fulfilling this requirement. Extensive market research, including a Sources Sought Notice (SSN ID: F4FDWL-26-R-0001) posted in December 2025, confirmed that CAE is the sole manufacturer of commercial Level D certified 747-8 simulators globally. Procuring through a third-party integrator poses unacceptable risks to the program's cost, schedule, and mission. By utilizing the only proven Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) of the 747-8i FFS, the Government mitigates the risk of significant schedule delays, increased lifecycle costs, and critical gaps in mission-essential training. In accordance with RFO 6.305, the Justification and Approval (J&A) document supporting this sole-source action will be published to SAM.gov within 14 days after contract award. 4. Demonstration of Capability This notice of intent is not a request for competitive proposals. However, all responsible sources may submit a capability statement, proposal, or quotation, which shall be considered by the agency. A determination by the Government not to compete this proposed contract based upon responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. Information received will normally be considered solely for the purpose of determining whether to conduct a competitive procurement. 5. Submission Instructions for Capability Statements Deadline: Responses must be received no later than 17 June 2026 at 1700 Eastern Time. Format: Capability statements must be submitted via email to the points of contact below. Point of Contact (POC): Justin Ternent-Wittenbach, justin.ternent-wittenbach@us.af.mil Point of Contact (POC): James Eric, james.eric@us.af.mil

CONTROLLED UNCLASSIFIED INFORMATION
Justification and Approval (J&A) for Other Than Full and Open Competition
I. Agency and Contracting Activity.
This Justification and Approval is to request authority for Other Than Full and Open Competition
supporting requirements generated for the Receiver Transmitter (RT) that is installed in the Combined
Altitude Radar Altimeter (CARA), AN/APN-232. This requirement is a Foreign Military Sales (FMS)
procurement for 11 each supporting requisition numbers DCIF5433105600, DTWM2550137500, and
DPLZ5443465504. The contracting activity for this requirement is SPRWA1 DLA/AWB. The purchase
request number supporting this contracting action is FD2060-24-00419.
II. Nature and/or description of the action being approved.
Due to the circumstances described herein, the activity requests authority to acquire the supplies listed in
the document using Other Than Full and Open Competition as prescribed by FAR 6.302-1. Only One
Responsible Source and No Other Supplies or Services Will Satisfy Agency Requirements. This action will
result in the award of a Firm-Fixed Price contract. The period of performance for manufacture production
on this contract will be one year.
This sole source requirement will be purchased from the following company:
Symetrics Industries, LLC dba Extant Aerospace
1615 W NASA Blvd
Melbourne, FL 32901
CAGE Code: 22830
III. Description of supplies/services required to meet agency needs.
This acquisition is for the procurement of the AN/APN-232 CARA (Combined Altitude Radar Altimeter)
assemblies. These AN/APN-232 CARA assemblies are utilized in conjunction with the AN/APN-232
Electronic Altimeter Radar Set. This requirement provides the material for the National Stock Number
(NSN) listed below:
Buy requirements for NSN: 5841-01-349-9175 P/N 8010000788-1 are as follows:
CLIN Noun NSN P/N Est Unit Cost Total
0001 RT 5841-01-349-9175 8010000788-1 $ 11 EA
Total: $
This Line Replaceable Unit (LRU), CARA Receiver Transmitter (RT), is installed in the F-16 platform.
The CARA RT consists of nine (9) circuit card assemblies, two (2) regulated power suppliers, switch filter
assembly, mother board, and RFA. Typical system installation consists of a CARA RT and two antennas
(transmitting and receiving), one or more Height Indicators.
The estimated acquisition cost of $ is based on quote from Symetrics Industries, LLC dba

CONTROLLED UNCLASSIFIED INFORMATION
Justification and Approval (J&A) for Other Than Full and Open Competition
Extant Aerospace (Extant). Payment for this procurement if funded using the country's funds. The NSNs
have been screened and assigned the following Acquisition Method Code (AMC)/Acquisition Method
Suffix Code (AMSC) (AFMC Form 761).
AMC/AMSC Codes of 5/P applies to the RT NSN: 5841-01-349-9175
AMC: 5, Acquired directly from a sole source contractor which is not the actual manufacturer
AMSC: P, The rights to use the data needed to purchase this item from additional sources are not owned by
the Government and cannot be purchased.
NAVCom (CAGE: 57057) sold CARA technical data rights to Symetrics Industries, LLC dba Extant
Aerospace (Extant) in Oct 2018. The 407th Engineer approved Extant (CAGE: 22830) as a procurement
source in February 2021. Past contracts with NavCom (CAGE: 57057) are identified on the AFMC Form
761 for the RT.
IV. Demonstration that the contractor's unique qualifications or the nature of the acquisition requires use of the
authority cited above.
The agency's minimum needs can only be satisfied by the unique supplies or services available from
Extant. The CARA system technical data rights were purchased by Extant from NavCom Defense
Electronics, Inc., the Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM), in Oct 2018.
The last buy contract was sole source to NavCom under contract SPRWA112D0004. Period of
performance was from 01 Nov 2012 to 30 Oct 2013. NavCom completed the entirety of this contract.
The Government does not possess the complete technical data package or Government purpose data rights
to pursue a full and open competition manufacture strategy for this LRU. The Government owns Technical
Order (TO) 12P5-2APN232-13, which is used to test and maintain a number of CARA RT SRUs. The
complete Technical Data Package (TDP) for manufacture of the RT is now owned by Extant. A complete
engineering data package is not available for competitive solicitation due to proprietary rights claims by the
manufacturer. This data is proprietary and the contractor refuses to release the rights or sell the data. No
further breakout effort will be made at this time.
Since NavCom sold the CARA system to Extant, the Government reached out to Extant on 5 February
2025 to request a quote to purchase the technical data rights for the RT. On 11 February 2025 the
contractor declined to provide a quote and stated they were not willing to sell the data.
The RT requires highly specialized technical skills, use of Extant proprietary data, and specialized
equipment and facilities to manufacture these items. Due to limited availability of packaged Mil-Spec solid
state microwave components in the restricted 4.2 to 4.4 GHz radar altimeter band, a unique and highly
specialized RF module was developed by NavCom during the 1980's. The manufacture efforts require the
use of proprietary processes, procedures, and critical RF tuning to match impedance.
The CARA system is military unique and must meet form, fit, function, and interface (F3I) requirements,
military standards, and pass applicable inspection and acceptance processes according to Extant's
engineering drawing design. Extant possesses the unique skill, equipment, facilities, and production data

CONTROLLED UNCLASSIFIED INFORMATION

necessary to perform RT production.
Reverse engineering to obtain data to support a competitive award was considered. However, this buy
requirement is for a FMS country that is unwilling to wait the minimum 2 years that reverse engineering
would require in order to potentially obtain manufacture data to support a competitive acquisition.
Therefore, reverse engineering is not practical or feasible for this requirement.
Accordingly, Extant is the only firm capable of providing the requirements described in Section III above
without the United States Air Force (USAF) experiencing an unacceptable delay in fulfilling its
requirements.
V. Description of efforts made to ensure that offers are solicited from as many potential sources as practicable,
including whether a notice was or will be publicized as required by subpart 5.2 and, if not, which exception under
FAR 5.202 applies.
A Sources Sought Synopsis (SSS) was posted to Sam.gov on 19 March 2024 with a response date of 2
April 2024 under Notice ID SPRWA1-00419. The SSS requested responses from interested vendors that
possess the expertise, capabilities, and experience to meet qualification requirements for this effort.
Integrated Procurement Technologies, on behalf of Extant, was the only source that expressed an interest
and submitted a response.
Extant is the only source identified through the market research that possesses the technical data, facilities,
test equipment, and expertise required to manufacture and repair the CARA RT. The Government does not
possess a technical data package to support a competitive award, nor does the Government have the
capability to independently validate the operational capability range of end repair or production items. The
incumbent, Extant was determined to be the only capable vendor.
A pre-solicitation notice of the requirement will be synopsized on the Sam.gov in accordance with FAR
5.201(b), citing conditions which preclude Full & Open Competition. Sources expressing an interest as a
result of the synopsis will be investigated for their capabilities to perform on this and/or future
requirements. Any source(s) that expressed interest as a result of this synopsis will be identified to the
prime contractor as a potential for subcontracting possibilities.
VI. Determination by the Contracting Officer that the anticipated cost to the Government will be fair and reasonable.
Based upon (1) certified cost or pricing data provided in the offeror's proposal in accordance with FAR
15.403-4; (2) the program office or expert technical personnel analysis of the offeror's Basis of Estimates;
(3) inputs from the Defense Contract Management Agency, the contracting officer expects to determine the
anticipated cost to the Government to be fair and reasonable.
VII. Description of the market research conducted and the results, or a statement of the reasons market research was
not conducted.
Market research was conducted 3 April 2024 through 27 March 2025 in accordance with FAR Part 10.001
and 10.002. The market research report was completed on 20 May 2025. The market research techniques
used included SSS, searches on Purchase Request Process System (PRPS), Air Force stock number search
in D043A, Haystack search using Robins PDM Gateway, review of NavCom website, and query using
Small Business Administration Dynamic Small Business Search (DSBS) engine.

March 2024 with a response date of 2 April 2024. Integrated Procurement Technologies, on behalf of
Extant, was the only source that expressed an interest and submitted a response.
Searches on PRPS, D043A, Haystack, NavCom website, and DSBS query utilizing NSNs, part numbers,

NavCom was the only company with valid procurement history for the CARA system. All drawings in our

Extant.
Commercial Opportunities: The RT is not a commercial item. The item is peculiar for military application
and the manufacturing processes and components used in the manufacture are unique to the avionics
industry; therefore, these items do not meet the commercial definition in FAR Part 2.101. There are no
commercial items or non-development items available to meet this requirement.
The market research concluded Extant is the only manufacturer/repair source of supply for the AN/
APN-232 CARA RT systems in the current market. Extant is the only source that possesses the unique
skills, equipment, facilities, TDP, and processes necessary to perform these manufactures.
VIII. Any other facts supporting the use of Other Than Full and Open Competition.
None.
IX. List of any sources that expressed, in writing, an interest in the acquisition.
See Section VI above
X. A statement of the actions, if any, the agency may take to remove or overcome any barriers to competition before
any subsequent acquisitions for the supplies or services required.
While the current market research indicates a sole source environment for the CARA system, the
Government will engage Extant on an annual basis to determine the feasibility of procuring the TDP.
The plan to break barriers to competition in the prior J&A was to continue engaging NavCom on selling the
RT TDP. NavCom subsequently sold the RT TDP to Extant in Oct 2018. The Government reached out to
Extant on their interest in selling the RT TDP or partnering with the Depot. Extant expressed they are not
willing to discuss any type of partnership with the Depot or sell of technical data until the Government has

15.403-4; (2) the program office or expert technical personnel analysis of the offeror's Basis of Estimates;
(3) inputs from the Defense Contract Management Agency, the contracting officer expects to determine the
anticipated cost to the Government to be fair and reasonable.
VII. Description of the market research conducted and the results, or a statement of the reasons market research was
not conducted.
Market research was conducted 3 April 2024 through 27 March 2025 in accordance with FAR Part 10.001
and 10.002. The market research report was completed on 20 May 2025. The market research techniques
used included SSS, searches on Purchase Request Process System (PRPS), Air Force stock number search
in D043A, Haystack search using Robins PDM Gateway, review of NavCom website, and query using
Small Business Administration Dynamic Small Business Search (DSBS) engine.

Commercial Opportunities: The RT is not a commercial item. The item is peculiar for military application
and the manufacturing processes and components used in the manufacture are unique to the avionics
industry; therefore, these items do not meet the commercial definition in FAR Part 2.101. There are no

APN-232 CARA RT systems in the current market. Extant is the only source that possesses the unique

Description: 6/1/26 Amendment 01: Notice amended to provide responses to questions received. See attached 'Amendment 01 Q and A 6-1-26.' ***THIS IS A COMBINED SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE AND NOTICE OF INTENT TO SOLE SOURCE*** The purpose of this sources sought notice is to conduct market research and identify potential sources of commercial products/services that satisfy the Government�s anticipated needs. If no alternate sources are identified, the Government intends to issue a Sole Source Award to CVD Equipment Corporation, 355, South Technology Drive, Central Islip, NY 11722, US, under the authority of FAR 12.102(a). The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for this acquisition is 333242, Semiconductor Machinery Manufacturing. BACKGROUND The National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) has a state-of-the-art research laboratory (the Katharine Blodgett Gebbie Building) in Boulder, CO to support the most sensitive research done at NIST. Included in this building is a Class 100 microelectronics fabrication facility, called the Boulder Micro-Fabrication Facility (BMF). Among the many critical pieces of equipment in this laboratory is equipment that uses the process gasses silane (SiH4). Silane is a toxic and pyrophoric gas and needs to be stored in and outside bunker using a gas rack and is delivered to tools through a specialized gas valve manifold box (VMB). Recently, the BMF has learned that their existing system has reached end of life and the system needs to be replaced for safety and operational reasons. The Government requires a new silane delivery system that is compatible with its existing life safety equipment, such as the toxic gas monitoring system (TGMS) and other gas cabinets to continue to use silane as process gases. The NIST BMF has many toxic gases that it uses in the process of making its NIST mission critical devices. Among these gases is silane which, for safety reasons, is sourced out of a single bottle in an outside gas bunker. Further distribution through the BMF requires the use of a Valve Manifold Box (VMB). Due to the life safety hazards associated with the toxic gas systems, the BMF has standardized to the Ciphercon platform to ensure it ensuring operators only need to interact with a single, familiar control interface during high-stress emergencies and allows the BMF to have a stable of spare parts to use for the systems. The BMF currently has an installed base of six SDC Ciphercon 1500 toxic gas cabinets, which are fully integrated into our facility's TGMS. Procuring this replacement directly from CVD Equipment Corp is the only way to ensure a seamless platform for safe operation and allow for a clean, straightforward integration with the existing TGMS. NIST conducted market research from March through May 2026 by performing internet searches, reviewing past awards for commissioning of previous systems in the BMF, and speaking with vendors to determine what sources could meet NIST�s minimum requirements. The results of that market research revealed that only CVD Equipment Corporation (UEI: PHV4F6NMWQQ4) appears to be capable of meeting NIST�s requirements. attachments.text:
DRAFT Statement of Work
Silane Distribution System
Background Information: 

The National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST)-Boulder has a state-of-the-art research laboratory (the Katharine Blodgett Gebbie Building) to support the most sensitive research done at NIST. Included in this building is a Class 100 microelectronics fabrication facility, called the Boulder Micro-Fabrication Facility (BMF). Among the many critical pieces of equipment in this laboratory is equipment that uses the process gasses silane (SiH4). Silane is a toxic and pyrophoric gas and needs to be stored in and outside bunker using a gas rack and is delivered to tools through a specialized gas valve manifold box (VMB). Recently, the BMF has learned that their existing system has reached end of life and the system needs to be replaced for safety and operational reasons. The Government requires a new silane delivery system that is compatible with its existing life safety equipment, such as the toxic gas monitoring system and other gas cabinets to continue to use silane as process gasses.

Scope of Work:

Objectives: 

The goal of this contract is to provide the Government with a new silane distribution system consisting of a gas rack and VMB to meet the needs of the NIST Boulder community.

General:
The contractor shall:
Provide personnel that pass required government background checks to be issued badges for work on site.
Provide all new items. Prototypes, one-off systems, demonstration models, used instruments, or refurbished instruments are unacceptable.

Specifications for the Work:
All staff must be badged by NIST Security. No one may enter the site without a badge.
The work and badging shall be scheduled with the Contracting Officer’s Representative (COR) and/or Technical Point of Contact (TPOC) prior to arrival to do the work.

Specific Requirements:

The contractor shall provide the Government with a silane distribution system that is compatible with the Governments existing SDC CiphercoNTM gas delivery infrastructure. To maintain critical life-safety continuity, the new system shall utilize identical spare parts, safety interlock mechanisms, and software architecture as the existing SDC gas delivery infrastructure.
System Requirements:
The silane distribution system shall consist of a silane gas rack and a silane VMB.
The new gas rack shall be a CiphercoN™ 1500 Gas Rack or equivalent with the following specifications:
Be able to be repaired using spare parts from the Government’s existing stock of spare parts for a SDC CiphercoNTM 1500 cabinet.
Be constructed of materials that are compatible for use with silane.
Meet all applicable code for delivering silane such as SEMI S2 and/or CGA-13 standards.
Be able to deliver Ultra High Purity (UHP) silane to a VMB in a manner that is consistent with semiconductor industry standards.
Be able to deliver silane to each system in a fully automated, computer-controlled method using a touch screen.
Be a two-cylinder system with one cylinder being an independent out, configured for silane, and the other as an onboard purge system, configured as nitrogen.
The gas Rack shall meet all CGA-13 requirements, including but not limited to:
High pressure test circuit
Vent purge trickle
Reduced flow orifice (RFO)
Have a Z-purge system.
Be able to be used outdoors in Boulder, Colorado, USA year-round.
The system shall include a control heater system if required.
Any weather proofing required to operate year-round.
Have an appropriate integrated UVIR detection and safety shutoffs.
Have an adjustable cylinder shelf to accommodate standard size gas cylinders.
Have the ability to accommodate gas cylinders with an industry standard automatic pneumatic valve and a manual hand valve. 
Have dual stage regulators.
Have CGA standard DISS fittings for the lines that connect to both the silane and nitrogen gas cylinders.
Have a process gas out line filter appropriate to industry standards for the semiconductor industry.
Have a purge inlet filter appropriate to industry standards for the semiconductor industry.
Have an EMO button.
Have an evacuate system that is able to independently evacuate the delivery line, purge line, and the inlet line of the system to vacuum pressures that is consistent with semiconductor industry standards.
Have the ability to communicate with the Government’s existing Toxic Gas Monitoring System (TGMS) where it can send and receive signals including but not limited to: the gas rack is ready to deliver gas, the gas rack is not able to deliver gas, and can receive and shut down signal to shut down the system.
Have an excess flow switch that can shut down the line delivery in case of a large change in flow signifying a leak.
Have a manual isolation valve on the output that has the ability to be locked out with a lock for standard LOTO procedures.
The new gas rack shall be a FlexGas™ VMB or equivalent with the following specifications:
Be able to receive gas from the gas rack and deliver UHP silane to up to 8 process tools in a manner that is consistent with semiconductor industry standards.
Be constructed of materials that are compatible for use with silane.
Meet all applicable code for delivering silane such as SEMI S2 and/or CGA-13 standards.
Be able to deliver silane to each system in a fully automated, computer-controlled method using a touch screen.
Be able to deliver silane to each system in a fully automated, computer controlled method.
Be able to independently deliver silane to 6 systems with the ability to expand the system to 8 delivery lines.
Have a nitrogen purge system that is able to independently purge each delivery line and the inlet line of the system.
A manual input isolation valve that has the ability to be locked out with a lock for standard LOTO procedures.
Have an evacuate system that is able to independently evacuate each delivery line, purge line, and the inlet line of the system to vacuum pressures that is consistent with semiconductor industry standards.
Have an inlet manifold electronic shut off valve
Have an appropriate integrated UVIR detection and safety shutoffs.
Have an EMO button.
Each of the 6 delivery lines shall have:
 An automated line isolation valve with contacts for a tool to call gas or to signal that gas is available.
A manual input isolation valve that has the ability to be locked out with a lock for standard LOTO procedures.
A manual outlet isolation valve that has the ability to be locked out with a lock for standard LOTO procedures.
An automatic purge isolation valve
A pressure regulator to regulate pressure for pressures consistent with semiconductor industry standards for the use of silane.
An electronic pressure transducer to measure each line’s delivery pressure.
An excess flow switch that can shut down the line delivery in case of a large change in flow signifying a leak.
An automated evacuation isolation valve
Have the ability to communicate with the Government’s existing TGMS where it can send and receive signals including but not limited to: the gas rack is ready to deliver gas, the gas rack is not able to deliver gas, and can receive and shut down signal to shut down the system and each silane stick individually.
Be expandable to include 2 more spare user configurable gas delivery lines that meet the same requirements listed in REF _Ref226621060 \w \h 2.c.ii.3.l.

Delivery and Installation:
The contractor shall be responsible for delivering the silane gas rack and VMB to the Government. After the gas rack and VMB are delivered, the Government will then be able to facilitize the system for a period between system delivery and site commissioning. This time period shall be at least 1 month and will not exceed 1 year, and the actual time period will be agreed upon between the Government and the contractor. If facilitization occurs faster than the agreed upon time period, then the contractor may start the commissioning on a date that is mutually agreeable between the Government and the contractor.

Commissioning and acceptance:
After the gas rack and VMB are facilitized, the contract shall commission the gas rack and VMB using a standard site acceptance test. The system will be accepted by the Government after the system passes the site acceptance test.
After completing the site acceptance test, the contractor shall assist the Government in introducing gas back to all of the process lines. Additionally, the contractor shall provide written directions on how to perform a cylinder change, pumping out the delivery line to the VMB, and introducing process gas to the VMB.
The contractor shall be responsible for all travel expenses.

NIST-SS26-133 Amendment 01 - Silane Distribution System
June 1, 2026
Questions & Answers (Q&A)

Q1.SOW c.ii.2.a. – We do not believe we can do this, we don’t know enough about the Stainless Design product to determine what might be re-usable.A1.We have two spare CipherCon 1500 gas rack systems. Roughly ~$40k-$50k worth of spare parts.
Q2.SOW c.ii.2.i. – Will the outdoor system be under a roof, or in a lean-to? If its will be completely exposed, we will have to use only stainless steel. A2.The system is under a roof that is about 12’4” high. However, the edge of the roof is about 4’6” away so it does get a fair amount of weather. Additionally, we’re in Boulder, CO with mean winter temperatures of 21F to 48F with a record low of -33F in 1930.
Q3.SOW c.ii.2.l. – how do you intend to control the change from pneumatic to manual regarding the system software?A3.We should be able to change between the two in software.
Q4.SOW c.ii.2.p – What is the purpose of the purge inlet filter? Do you possible mean purifier?A4. This is a particulate filter to make sure no particles go from the cylinder into the line.
Q5.SOW c.ii.3.a – what is the flow rate required if all eight tools are in use? Please provide a per line flow.A5. 800 sccm total (100 sccm per tool)
Q6.SOW c.ii.3.f – contrast line f with c.ii.3.a.A6.a. is the requirement that the system is able to have 8 lines, f. says that only 6 lines need to be populated with the valves, gauges, regulators, etc with the ability to field add two more lines.
Q7.SOWc.ii.3.j. – is a pneumatic shut off valve acceptable, we believe this is what most semiconductor silane processes use. A7.Pneumatic valve is acceptable to meet the requirement of c.ii.3.j
Q8.SOW c.ii.3.m.i. – we don’t understand this requirementA8.Each line needs to be able to interact with our toxic gas monitoring system so that we can independently control and shutdown delivery lines tool by tool depending on tool status.
Q9.SOW c.ii.3.m.ii. / c.ii.3.m.iii. – why are both of these required? IS either / or acceptable?A9.We require both input and output valves to be able to isolate the system on both the input and output for both safety and troubleshooting reasons.

DRAFT SOW: Procurement and Installation of ProCuity Beds
1. Purpose
The purpose of this SOW is to define the requirements for the procurement, delivery, installation, and support of hospital beds to enhance patient care, safety, and clinical efficiency across inpatient care settings. The requested equipment must support patient safety initiatives, reduce fall risk, improve caregiver ergonomics, and integrate with existing clinical workflows and technologies. This acquisition is intended to replace or supplement existing bed inventory with modern systems that meet current healthcare standards
2. Scope of Work
The contractor shall provide all labor, materials, equipment necessary to furnish, deliver, assemble, install, test, and provide training for the beds at 2200 Fort Roots Dr. Bld 170. This shall include Hospital bed frames, compatible mattresses, all required accessories and components, on-site installation, functional testing of all beds, user training for clinical support staff, and warranty and support services.
3. Requirements
3.1 Product Specifications
Each bed must include the following features:
Low Height: Uncompromised low height of 11.5 inches (14 inches with Zoom motorized drive), enabling advanced fall and injury prevention without compromising stability or clearance; 6” double casters for ease of transport; 5.75 inches underbed clearance for lifts and overbed tables.
Headboard with Caregiver Cut-out: Allows enhanced head-end patient access for procedures such as intubation/extubation and boosting.
One-touch/Any Position Scale: Integrated scale enables weighing the patient in any position, stores up to 40 weights per stay, and operates with a single touch.
Secure Adaptive Bed Alarm: Innovative weight-based system provides three sensitivity zones, intuitive zone adjustment when side rails are altered, and multiple alarm disarm points (foot end, siderail).
iBed Watch: Continuous electronic monitoring of side rail, head-of-bed, bed height, and bed-flat positions; provides alerts via icons and optional EHR and nurse call integration.
12” Integrated Bed Extender: Built-in extender increases surface area from 84 to 96 inches.
One-touch Electric Brakes: Manual and electric brakes with multi-point access, visual brake status alerts on footboard and siderails.
Foot End Advanced Controls: Advanced caregiver controls placed at the foot for uninterrupted patient care.
USB Port and Device Holder: Open-face patient device holder with integrated USB charging, designed for easy cleaning and patient convenience.
Integrated Footboard Pump Holder/Accessory Outlets: Built-in pump rack and 120V accessory outlets located away from patient entry/egress.
Zoom Drive System: Motorized bed drive system for improved mobility and caregiver efficiency.
iBed Wireless Capability: Wireless connectivity enables bedside data collection, open architecture for integration, and supports cost-effective custom solutions.
Secure Connect: Cable-free, three-anchor nurse call connectivity for consistent nurse communication.
3.2 Quantity
20 Hospital beds with compatible mattresses and components. 
3.3 Delivery and Installation
Contractor shall coordinate delivery and installation with the Community Living Center personnel. Veronica Hawkins 501-257-2261 or Angela McLaurin 501-257-2786. Beds and mattresses will be delivered to Building 170 ward C
3.4 Training
Within 30 days after delivery, the Contractor shall provide on-site in-service training for clinical, nursing, and technical staff in the use, cleaning, and maintenance of beds. At least 1 on-site training is required. 
Training materials and quick-start guides shall be provided.
3.5 Warranty and Support
Shall include a minimum 1 year warranty for manufacturing defects, seam failures, fluid ingress, loss of pressure redistribution performance. Includes replacement or repair at no cost and the turnaround time is 30 days from day of filed claim. 
Support shall include: remote support (phone/email) during normal business hours, on-site support when issues cannot be resolved remotely, preventative maintenance guidance, troubleshooting and repair services. Initial response is within 24 hours. On-Site service to be held within 72 hours for unresolved issues. 
4. Period of Performance
The period of performance shall be from 90 days of award.
5. Government Furnished Property/Space
The facility will provide contractor access to the areas designated for bed placement, as well as reasonable access required for installation and training activities.
RECORDS MANAGEMENT OBLIGATIONS
A.  Applicability
This clause applies to all Contractors whose employees create, work with, or otherwise handle Federal records, as defined in Section B, regardless of the medium in which the record exists.  
B.  Definitions
“Federal record” as defined in 44 U.S.C. § 3301, includes all recorded information, regardless of form or characteristics, made or received by a Federal agency under Federal law or in connection with the transaction of public business and preserved or appropriate for preservation by that agency or its legitimate successor as evidence of the organization, functions, policies, decisions, procedures, operations, or other activities of the United States Government or because of the informational value of data in them.  
The term Federal record:
includes [Agency] records. 
does not include personal materials.
applies to records created, received, or maintained by Contractors pursuant to their [Agency] contract.
may include deliverables and documentation associated with deliverables.
C.  Requirements
Contractor shall comply with all applicable records management laws and regulations, as well as National Archives and Records Administration (NARA) records policies, including but not limited to the Federal Records Act (44 U.S.C. chs. 21, 29, 31, 33), NARA regulations at 36 CFR Chapter XII Subchapter B, and those policies associated with the safeguarding of records covered by the Privacy Act of 1974 (5 U.S.C. 552a). These policies include the preservation of all records, regardless of form or characteristics, mode of transmission, or state of completion. 
In accordance with 36 CFR 1222.32, all data created for Government use and delivered to, or falling under the legal control of, the Government are Federal records subject to the provisions of 44 U.S.C. chapters 21, 29, 31, and 33, the Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) (5 U.S.C. 552), as amended, and the Privacy Act of 1974 (5 U.S.C. 552a), as amended and must be managed and scheduled for disposition only as permitted by statute or regulation. 
In accordance with 36 CFR 1222.32, Contractor shall maintain all records created for Government use or created in the course of performing the contract and/or delivered to, or under the legal control of the Government and must be managed in accordance with Federal law. Electronic records and associated metadata must be accompanied by sufficient technical documentation to permit understanding and use of the records and data. 
[Agency] and its contractors are responsible for preventing the alienation or unauthorized destruction of records, including all forms of mutilation. Records may not be removed from the legal custody of [Agency] or destroyed except for in accordance with the provisions of the agency records schedules and with the written concurrence of the Head of the Contracting Activity. Willful and unlawful destruction, damage or alienation of Federal records is subject to the fines and penalties imposed by 18 U.S.C. 2701. In the event of any unlawful or accidental removal, defacing, alteration, or destruction of records, Contractor must report to [Agency]. The agency must report promptly to NARA in accordance with 36 CFR 1230.
The Contractor shall immediately notify the appropriate Contracting Officer upon discovery of any inadvertent or unauthorized disclosures of information, data, documentary materials, records or equipment. Disclosure of non-public information is limited to authorized personnel with a need-to-know as described in the [contract vehicle]. The Contractor shall ensure that the appropriate personnel, administrative, technical, and physical safeguards are established to ensure the security and confidentiality of this information, data, documentary material, records and/or equipment is properly protected. The Contractor shall not remove material from Government facilities or systems, or facilities or systems operated or maintained on the Government’s behalf, without the express written permission of the Head of the Contracting Activity. When information, data, documentary material, records and/or equipment is no longer required, it shall be returned to [Agency] control or the Contractor must hold it until otherwise directed. Items returned to the Government shall be hand carried, mailed, emailed, or securely electronically transmitted to the Contracting Officer or address prescribed in the [contract vehicle]. Destruction of records is EXPRESSLY PROHIBITED unless in accordance with Paragraph (4).
The Contractor is required to obtain the Contracting Officer's approval prior to engaging in any contractual relationship (sub-contractor) in support of this contract requiring the disclosure of information, documentary material and/or records generated under, or relating to, contracts. The Contractor (and any sub-contractor) is required to abide by Government and [Agency] guidance for protecting sensitive, proprietary information, classified, and controlled unclassified information.
The Contractor shall only use Government IT equipment for purposes specifically tied to or authorized by the contract and in accordance with [Agency] policy. 
The Contractor shall not create or maintain any records containing any non-public [Agency] information that are not specifically tied to or authorized by the contract. 
The Contractor shall not retain, use, sell, or disseminate copies of any deliverable that contains information covered by the Privacy Act of 1974 or that which is generally protected from public disclosure by an exemption to the Freedom of Information Act. 
The [Agency] owns the rights to all data and records produced as part of this contract. All deliverables under the contract are the property of the U.S. Government for which [Agency] shall have unlimited rights to use, dispose of, or disclose such data contained therein as it determines to be in the public interest. Any Contractor rights in the data or deliverables must be identified as required by FAR 52.227-11 through FAR 52.227-20.
Training.  All Contractor employees assigned to this contract who create, work with, or otherwise handle records are required to take [Agency]-provided records management training. The Contractor is responsible for confirming training has been completed according to agency policies, including initial training and any annual or refresher training. 
[Note: To the extent an agency requires contractors to complete records management training, the agency must provide the training to the contractor.] 
D.  Flowdown of requirements to subcontractors
The Contractor shall incorporate the substance of this clause, its terms and requirements including this paragraph, in all subcontracts under this [contract vehicle], and require written subcontractor acknowledgment of same. 
Violation by a subcontractor of any provision set forth in this clause will be attributed to the Contractor.

matters.title: Notice of Intent to Sole Source for Hydrogen Chloride Detectors
matters.text:
Federal notice (Presolicitation), DEPT OF DEFENSE.DEPT OF THE AIR FORCE.FA6800 AFICC 767 ESF
Title: Notice of Intent to Sole Source for Hydrogen Chloride Detectors
Solicitation number: FA680026R0008
PSC: 6665; NAICS: 334519
Description: The Air Force Global Strike Command (AFGSC) intends to award a sole source, firm-fixed-price contract to RKI Instruments, Inc. for the procurement of the RKI Instruments Model GD-70D-HCL-15E Hydrogen Chloride (HCl) Gas Detection System. This requirement is for the procurement, delivery, and documentation of approximately 86 brand-name HCl gas detection systems to be used in Missile Alert Facilities (MAFs) across three Intercontinental Ballistic Missile (ICBM) wings: 90th Missile Wing (F.E. Warren AFB, WY), 341st Missile Wing (Malmstrom AFB, MT), and 91st Missile Wing (Minot AFB, ND). These detectors provide critical, real-time monitoring to protect personnel and sensitive Nuclear Command, Control, and Communications (NC3) equipment from HCl gas exposure. This acquisition is being conducted on a sole-source basis in accordance with the authority at FAR 6.302-1, "Only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements." This specific brand and model are required for the following reasons: Interoperability and Configuration Control: The RKI Instruments GD-70D HCL 15E is the only system that is fully compatible with the existing facility infrastructure, including annunciator panels, monitoring systems, wiring harnesses, and power supply interfaces currently fielded in AFGSC missile wings. Utilizing any other system would break the required configuration control mandated under the Air Force Nuclear Surety Program. Nuclear Certification: The existing RKI detectors are part of a certified system baseline for nuclear environments. Introducing a different brand would necessitate a complete and costly recertification process, including extensive environmental, safety, and electromagnetic interference (EMI) testing, which would introduce unacceptable operational risk and delays. Standardization: Procuring the same brand-name detectors ensures consistency in performance, calibration, and maintenance procedures across all three missile wings. This standardization is critical for operational efficiency, reduces the training burden for missile combat crews and maintenance personnel, and simplifies logistics through common spare parts management. The contractor shall procure and deliver new, fully functional RKI Instruments GD-70D-HCL-15E detection systems, along with all associated manuals, warranty documentation, calibration kits, and consumables, to the three specified Air Force Bases. Government personnel will be responsible for installation. This notice of intent is not a request for competitive proposals. However, all responsible sources may submit a capability statement, proposal, or quotation, which shall be considered by the agency. A determination by the Government not to compete this proposed contract action based upon responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. Information received will normally be considered solely for the purpose of determining whether to conduct a competitive procurement.

Description: MARKET RESEARCH PURPOSES ONLY NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL OR SOLICITATION The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA), Office of Acquisitions and Grants Services (OAGS) is issuing this source sought announcement on behalf of the Office of Pharmaceutical Quality Research (OPQR), in order to determine if there are existing small business sources capable of providing a �Brand Name or Equal� Nanalysis AUTOsample-100 autosampler. Other than small business concerns, especially vendors who may be able to offer domestic products are also encouraged to submit a capability statement that provides company information, as well as information demonstrating that it can meet all of the minimum requirements included below, to include the country of manufacture of products offered. If your firm is considered a small business source under North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) Code 334516 - Analytical Laboratory Instrument Manufacturing; with a Small Business Size Standard of 1,000 employees and you believe that your firm would be able to provide the FDA with the supplies/services described below, please submit an email to Warren.Dutter@fda.hhs.gov. Background: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA), Office of Pharmaceutical Quality Research (OPQR) in Saint Louis, MO (OPQR-STL), is a laboratory-based office focused on the quality assessment of drug products. OPQR conducts research to support the establishment of scientific standards for product quality, performance, and the therapeutic equivalence of generic drug products. The purpose of this acquisition is to procure a �Brand Name or Equal� Nanalysis AUTOsample-100 autosampler for use with an existing Nanalysis 100 MHz benchtop NMR system. Benchtop NMR systems utilize low magnetic field strength permanent magnets, which are more cost-effective per MHz than traditional high-field NMR systems and require less maintenance. These systems are well suited for high-throughput screening applications. The addition of an autosampler will significantly improve laboratory efficiency by automating sample handling, eliminating the need for analysts to manually exchange samples between runs. It will also enable unattended operation, including overnight experiment execution, thereby increasing throughput and optimizing staff time efficiency. This is a Brand Name or Equal requirement. Products other than the specified Nanalysis AUTOsample-100 autosampler are acceptable but shall meet all the salient characteristics contained in the Minimum Technical Requirements below. Minimum Technical Requirements (Salient Characteristics): The autosampler shall be compatible with and capable of full integration with the existing Government-owned Nanalysis 100-PRO benchtop NMR system (magnet), Serial Number C109122022. The autosampler shall support automated queuing and execution of multiple NMR experiments. The autosampler shall support automated queuing and processing of multiple samples without operator intervention between runs. The autosampler shall enable automated execution of queued experiments without requiring manual sample exchange between analyses. The autosampler shall support automated magnetic field shimming adjustments between queued experiments and samples. The autosampler shall support automated lock adjustments between queued experiments and samples. The autosampler shall operate using the existing Nanalysis software and control environment without requiring custom third-party integration or modification to the existing Government-owned Nanalysis 100-PRO system. Additional System Requirements: The components and equipment shall be newly manufactured, not used or refurbished, or previously used for demonstration. Offered systems shall be a turn-key solution i.e., the contractor shall be responsible for providing all hardware, components, instruments, computers, software, and that otherwise required to meet these specifications and the FDA�s stated need. The systems shall be delivered with all necessary supplies and accessories required for installation and start-up. The system and associated accessories shall include operations and maintenance manuals covering proper operation, routine maintenance, and troubleshooting for the system and controlling software. All manuals and documentation shall be provided in hard copy and/or electronic format. The Contractor shall provide all labor, travel, and tools to install the equipment at the address provided below, to include shipping. The contractor shall demonstrate upon installation that the item meets or exceeds all performance specifications. Upon acceptance of the system, the contractor shall provide on-site operator training/familiarization. Such familiarization shall include system operations, calibration, optimization, troubleshooting and basic operational maintenance procedures. Systems shall be warranted for not less than one (1) year from FDA acceptance of the system(s). Warranty service shall include troubleshooting capabilities based on complete knowledge of the entire system, and immediate access to replacement parts. Phone and email technical support shall be included for a minimum of one (1) year. Place of Performance: FOB Point Destination. All items shall include shipping, handling, installation, and inside delivery to the destination identified herein. FDA/CDER/OPQR 645 Newstead Ave., St Louis, MO 63110 Period of Performance: Delivery shall occur within 60 calendar days from date of award. Responses to this Sources Sought shall unequivocally demonstrate that the respondent is regularly engaged in the sale of same or substantially similar product/service. (DSI) Modumax/Moducore - Custom Supply Storage System that meets the salient characteristics and performance requirements listed below. VA Pittsburgh Healthcare System (VAPHS) SCOPE OF WORK AND GENERAL DESCRIPTION Distribution Systems International, Inc. (DSI) Modumax/Moducore - Custom Supply Storage System Introduction Pittsburgh s supply room for the Operating Room will be moving locations, and the complete conversion from current wire track shelving to a Custom High Density Basket System. Fully compatible with Operating Room clean central core, sub sterile, and supply room workflows. Must integrate with existing VAPHS storage layouts without structural modification. Construction & Materials Frame and shelving constructed of medical grade, corrosion resistant steel or anodized aluminum suitable for high humidity and high turnover Operating Room settings. All components must withstand frequent cleaning with VA approved disinfectants. Smooth, non porous surfaces that comply with infection prevention standards. Description: ***THIS IS A COMBINED SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE AND NOTICE OF INTENT TO SOLE SOURCE*** The purpose of this sources sought notice is to conduct market research and identify potential sources of commercial products/services that satisfy the Government�s anticipated needs. If no alternate sources are identified, the Government intends to issue a Sole Source Award to CVD Equipment Corporation, 355, South Technology Drive, Central Islip, NY 11722, US, under the authority of FAR 12.102(a). The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for this acquisition is 333242, Semiconductor Machinery Manufacturing. BACKGROUND The National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) has a state-of-the-art research laboratory (the Katharine Blodgett Gebbie Building) in Boulder, CO to support the most sensitive research done at NIST. Included in this building is a Class 100 microelectronics fabrication facility, called the Boulder Micro-Fabrication Facility (BMF). Among the many critical pieces of equipment in this laboratory is equipment that uses the process gasses silane (SiH4). Silane is a toxic and pyrophoric gas and needs to be stored in and outside bunker using a gas rack and is delivered to tools through a specialized gas valve manifold box (VMB). Recently, the BMF has learned that their existing system has reached end of life and the system needs to be replaced for safety and operational reasons. The Government requires a new silane delivery system that is compatible with its existing life safety equipment, such as the toxic gas monitoring system (TGMS) and other gas cabinets to continue to use silane as process gases. The NIST BMF has many toxic gases that it uses in the process of making its NIST mission critical devices. Among these gases is silane which, for safety reasons, is sourced out of a single bottle in an outside gas bunker. Further distribution through the BMF requires the use of a Valve Manifold Box (VMB). Due to the life safety hazards associated with the toxic gas systems, the BMF has standardized to the Ciphercon platform to ensure it ensuring operators only need to interact with a single, familiar control interface during high-stress emergencies and allows the BMF to have a stable of spare parts to use for the systems. The BMF currently has an installed base of six SDC Ciphercon 1500 toxic gas cabinets, which are fully integrated into our facility's TGMS. Procuring this replacement directly from CVD Equipment Corp is the only way to ensure a seamless platform for safe operation and allow for a clean, straightforward integration with the existing TGMS. NIST conducted market research from March through May 2026 by performing internet searches, reviewing past awards for commissioning of previous systems in the BMF, and speaking with vendors to determine what sources could meet NIST�s minimum requirements. attachments.name: DRAFT Statement of Work.docx
attachments.text:
DRAFT Statement of Work
Silane Distribution System
Background Information: 

The National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST)-Boulder has a state-of-the-art research laboratory (the Katharine Blodgett Gebbie Building) to support the most sensitive research done at NIST. Included in this building is a Class 100 microelectronics fabrication facility, called the Boulder Micro-Fabrication Facility (BMF). Among the many critical pieces of equipment in this laboratory is equipment that uses the process gasses silane (SiH4). Silane is a toxic and pyrophoric gas and needs to be stored in and outside bunker using a gas rack and is delivered to tools through a specialized gas valve manifold box (VMB). Recently, the BMF has learned that their existing system has reached end of life and the system needs to be replaced for safety and operational reasons. The Government requires a new silane delivery system that is compatible with its existing life safety equipment, such as the toxic gas monitoring system and other gas cabinets to continue to use silane as process gasses.

Scope of Work:

Objectives: 

The goal of this contract is to provide the Government with a new silane distribution system consisting of a gas rack and VMB to meet the needs of the NIST Boulder community.

General:
The contractor shall:
Provide personnel that pass required government background checks to be issued badges for work on site.
Provide all new items. Prototypes, one-off systems, demonstration models, used instruments, or refurbished instruments are unacceptable.

Specifications for the Work:
All staff must be badged by NIST Security. No one may enter the site without a badge.
The work and badging shall be scheduled with the Contracting Officer’s Representative (COR) and/or Technical Point of Contact (TPOC) prior to arrival to do the work.

Specific Requirements:

The contractor shall provide the Government with a silane distribution system that is compatible with the Governments existing SDC CiphercoNTM gas delivery infrastructure. To maintain critical life-safety continuity, the new system shall utilize identical spare parts, safety interlock mechanisms, and software architecture as the existing SDC gas delivery infrastructure.
System Requirements:
The silane distribution system shall consist of a silane gas rack and a silane VMB.
The new gas rack shall be a CiphercoN™ 1500 Gas Rack or equivalent with the following specifications:
Be able to be repaired using spare parts from the Government’s existing stock of spare parts for a SDC CiphercoNTM 1500 cabinet.
Be constructed of materials that are compatible for use with silane.
Meet all applicable code for delivering silane such as SEMI S2 and/or CGA-13 standards.
Be able to deliver Ultra High Purity (UHP) silane to a VMB in a manner that is consistent with semiconductor industry standards.
Be able to deliver silane to each system in a fully automated, computer-controlled method using a touch screen.
Be a two-cylinder system with one cylinder being an independent out, configured for silane, and the other as an onboard purge system, configured as nitrogen.
The gas Rack shall meet all CGA-13 requirements, including but not limited to:
High pressure test circuit
Vent purge trickle
Reduced flow orifice (RFO)
Have a Z-purge system.
Be able to be used outdoors in Boulder, Colorado, USA year-round.
The system shall include a control heater system if required.
Any weather proofing required to operate year-round.
Have an appropriate integrated UVIR detection and safety shutoffs.
Have an adjustable cylinder shelf to accommodate standard size gas cylinders.
Have the ability to accommodate gas cylinders with an industry standard automatic pneumatic valve and a manual hand valve. 
Have dual stage regulators.
Have CGA standard DISS fittings for the lines that connect to both the silane and nitrogen gas cylinders.
Have a process gas out line filter appropriate to industry standards for the semiconductor industry.
Have a purge inlet filter appropriate to industry standards for the semiconductor industry.
Have an EMO button.
Have an evacuate system that is able to independently evacuate the delivery line, purge line, and the inlet line of the system to vacuum pressures that is consistent with semiconductor industry standards.
Have the ability to communicate with the Government’s existing Toxic Gas Monitoring System (TGMS) where it can send and receive signals including but not limited to: the gas rack is ready to deliver gas, the gas rack is not able to deliver gas, and can receive and shut down signal to shut down the system.
Have an excess flow switch that can shut down the line delivery in case of a large change in flow signifying a leak.
Have a manual isolation valve on the output that has the ability to be locked out with a lock for standard LOTO procedures.
The new gas rack shall be a FlexGas™ VMB or equivalent with the following specifications:
Be able to receive gas from the gas rack and deliver UHP silane to up to 8 process tools in a manner that is consistent with semiconductor industry standards.
Be constructed of materials that are compatible for use with silane.
Meet all applicable code for delivering silane such as SEMI S2 and/or CGA-13 standards.
Be able to deliver silane to each system in a fully automated, computer-controlled method using a touch screen.
Be able to deliver silane to each system in a fully automated, computer controlled method.
Be able to independently deliver silane to 6 systems with the ability to expand the system to 8 delivery lines.
Have a nitrogen purge system that is able to independently purge each delivery line and the inlet line of the system.
A manual input isolation valve that has the ability to be locked out with a lock for standard LOTO procedures.
Have an evacuate system that is able to independently evacuate each delivery line, purge line, and the inlet line of the system to vacuum pressures that is consistent with semiconductor industry standards.
Have an inlet manifold electronic shut off valve
Have an appropriate integrated UVIR detection and safety shutoffs.
Have an EMO button.
Each of the 6 delivery lines shall have:
 An automated line isolation valve with contacts for a tool to call gas or to signal that gas is available.
A manual input isolation valve that has the ability to be locked out with a lock for standard LOTO procedures.
A manual outlet isolation valve that has the ability to be locked out with a lock for standard LOTO procedures.
An automatic purge isolation valve
A pressure regulator to regulate pressure for pressures consistent with semiconductor industry standards for the use of silane.
An electronic pressure transducer to measure each line’s delivery pressure.
An excess flow switch that can shut down the line delivery in case of a large change in flow signifying a leak.
An automated evacuation isolation valve
Have the ability to communicate with the Government’s existing TGMS where it can send and receive signals including but not limited to: the gas rack is ready to deliver gas, the gas rack is not able to deliver gas, and can receive and shut down signal to shut down the system and each silane stick individually.
Be expandable to include 2 more spare user configurable gas delivery lines that meet the same requirements listed in REF _Ref226621060 \w \h 2.c.ii.3.l.

Delivery and Installation:
The contractor shall be responsible for delivering the silane gas rack and VMB to the Government. After the gas rack and VMB are delivered, the Government will then be able to facilitize the system for a period between system delivery and site commissioning. This time period shall be at least 1 month and will not exceed 1 year, and the actual time period will be agreed upon between the Government and the contractor. If facilitization occurs faster than the agreed upon time period, then the contractor may start the commissioning on a date that is mutually agreeable between the Government and the contractor.

Commissioning and acceptance:
After the gas rack and VMB are facilitized, the contract shall commission the gas rack and VMB using a standard site acceptance test. The system will be accepted by the Government after the system passes the site acceptance test.
After completing the site acceptance test, the contractor shall assist the Government in introducing gas back to all of the process lines. Additionally, the contractor shall provide written directions on how to perform a cylinder change, pumping out the delivery line to the VMB, and introducing process gas to the VMB.
The contractor shall be responsible for all travel expenses.

JUSTIFICATION FOR OTHER THAN FULL AND OPEN COMPETITION

II. NATURE AND/OR DESCRIPTION OF THE ACTION BEING PROCESSED
Due to the circumstances described herein, this activity requests authority to acquire the items/spares listed in
this document using Other Than Full and Open Competition as prescribed by FAR 6.302-1, Only One
Responsible Source and No Other Supplies or Services Will Satisfy Agency.
This action will result in the award of a new contract, which will be a firm-fixed price. This sole source
requirement will be purchased from the following company.
BAE Systems
10920 Technology Pl
San Diego, CA 92127-1874
Cage Code: 12436
Large Business
III. DESCRIPTION OF THE SUPPLIES/SERVICES REQUIRED TO MEET THE AGENCY’S
NEEDS
The requirement is for Enhanced Microwave Unit (EMU) sub-assemblies. The acquisition will be funded with
FY26 working capital funds.
Under the contemplated contract, BAE Systems (BAE) will provide the following supplies which are required
to support the VXI-IAIS test stations in support of F-16 weapon system program. The EMU subassembly
provides Radio Frequency (RF) stimulus and measurement capabilities for VXI-IAIS test stations. These test
stations are used for the testing and repair of F-16 avionics Line Replaceable Units (LRUs).
Basic Requirement

TOTAL POTENTIAL CONTRACT VALUE: $
Estimated delivery completion is 42 months after receipt of contract.
The AMC Code is 3/R meaning the manufacturing data is proprietary to the OEM.

Solicitation Number: SPRHA4-26-R-0041
IV. STATUTORY AUTHORITY PERMITTING OTHER THAN FULL AND OPEN COMPETITION
10 U.S.C. 3204(a)(1) , as implemented by FAR 6.302-1, Only One Responsible Source and No Other Supplies
or Services Will Satisfy Agency Requirements.
V. DEMONSTRATION THAT THE CONTRACTOR’S UNIQUE QUALIFICATIONS OR NATURE
OF THE ACQUISITION REQUIRES THE USE OF THE AUTHORITY CITED ABOVE
From the inception of the F-16 aircraft, BAE has been the Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) for the AIS
series of test stations, to include the VXI-IAIS. BAE is the Engineering authority for all generations of test
stations, supplying the Government with a cradle-to-grave approach in support of production, repair, and
sustainment requirements for both legacy and new production test stations.
As the Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM), BAE possesses the critical engineering, manufacturing, and
repair capabilities to maintain the EMU and its subcomponents. BAE provides the Government with system
and sub-system level support for every aspect of AIS test stations in order to ensure operational capability for
the USAF as well as FMS F-16 customers throughout the world.
BAE recently completed a project to re-design the EMU for the VXI-IAIS test station. The three-year effort
resolved Diminishing Manufacturing Sources and Material Shortage (DMSMS) issues the legacy microwave
unit was experiencing and provided the Government with a long-term solution to radio frequency testing
capability. No other vendor has the proprietary data required to re-deign/re-engineer and integrate another
solution that will work with the F-16 AIS test systems.
The EMU maintains an AMC/AMSC of 3/R, meaning the manufacturing data is proprietary to BAE and
therefore the government does not possess sufficient data to establish additional sources of supply. The
Government contacted BAE via email on 12 June 2025 to see if they would be interested in selling their
proprietary data. BAE responded the same day indicating they would not be interested in selling their data
rights.
VI. DESCRIPTION OF EFFORTS MADE TO ENSURE THAT OFFERS ARE SOLICITED FROM AS
MANY POTENTIAL SOURCES AS DEEMED PRACTICABLE
This requirement will be synopsized on Contract Opportunities as required by FAR 5.201. It is anticipated that
sources having an interest in subcontracting may be identified through synopsis. Although the Government
does not own data to support acquisition of this EMU from any other source, any source who responds to the
Government as a result of this synopsis will be identified to the prime contractor as a potential source for
subcontracting possibilities.
A combined Request for Information and Sources Sought Synopsis was posted to Sam.gov on 21 October 2025.
The solicitation number is SPRHA1-26-R-0041. No additional sources have expressed interest in the pending
acquisition. Any new or additional information related to interested suppliers will be documented in the official
contract file.
VII. DETERMINATION BY THE CONTRACTING OFFICER THAT THE ANTICIPATED COST
TO THE GOVERNMENT WILL BE FAIR AND REASONABLE
2
Solicitation Number: SPRHA4-26-R-0041
The following steps will be taken to ensure that the anticipated cost of this acquisition will be fair and
reasonable. The Contracting Officer will comply with the procedures and criteria contained in Federal
Acquisition Regulation (FAR) under Part 30 - Cost Accounting Standards, Part 31 - Contract Cost Principles
and Procedures, Subparts 15.4 - Contract Pricing; to include technical evaluations and audits, as appropriate.
Additional steps to ensure price reasonableness will be under the guidance of the Contract Pricing Reference
Guides, jointly developed by the Federal Acquisition Institute and the Air Force Institute of Technology. The
Contracting Office will obtain certified cost and pricing data IAW FAR Subpart 15.403, when required. The
final step is to include the Price Negotiation Memorandum (PNM). This detailed documentation and
justification of price reasonableness will be disclosed in the official PNM, to be prepared upon completion of
negotiations.
VIII. DESCRIPTION OF THE MARKET RESEARCH CONDUCTED AND THE RESULTS, OR
STATEMENT OF THE REASONS MARKET RESEARCH WAS NOT CONDUCTED
The Government does not possess the data rights to the set of technical drawings and performance
specifications required to procure these parts from sources other than BAE Systems (CAGE 12436).
In accordance with the FAR and to ensure Market Research is both continuous and relevant, a Combined
Request for Information and Sources Sought Synopsis was issued by the contracting officer, any new or
additional information related to interested suppliers will be documented in the official contract file.
Internet searches were performed as well as queried government databases, vendor surveys, and correspondence
with Subject Matter Experts (SMEs) and other individuals that are knowledgeable within the industry were
performed, including contacting known sources of supply. There was no conclusive evidence that another
source, other than the OEM, can satisfy this requirement.
Based on the research conducted and due to the highly specialized and unique nature of the complex redesign of
the F-16 EMU subassembly, no viable substitute system/component could be identified to support this
immediate requirement. There are no identified commercial/non-commercial alternatives currently on the
market that will satisfy this requirement.
Based on the research conducted and due to the highly specialized and unique nature of the F-16 EMU, it is
recommended that this spares acquisition be awarded to BAE as it determined; no other vendor has the
proprietary data required to re-deign/re-engineer and integrate another solution that will work with the F-16 AIS
test systems.

COMPETITION

Single Source Justification (Simplified Acquisition)
Section A: General Contract Information
Is this a Bridge Action as defined in the AF Bridge Action Reduction Plan? Yes No
Contracting Activity: 355 CONS

Purchase Request / Local ID Number:

Section B: Description of the Supplies/Services Required
CYPRES (ECC) Automatic Activation Device (AAD) and associated cost.
Section C: Justification for Soliciting from a Single Source or Brand Name
The CYPRES (ECC), NSN 1670-12-422-1310, is a proprietary Automatic Activation Device (AAD) manufactured by SSK Industries
and approved for use under the Air Force Personnel Parachute Program (PPP) Approved for Use List (AUL) in accordance with
AFI 10-3503. The AUL establishes standardized, mandatory equipment for military parachute operations to ensure safety,
compatibility, and airworthiness.
Due to the life-saving function of the AAD and its integration with certified parachute systems, only AUL-approved devices are
authorized for use. The CYPRES system utilizes proprietary technology, components, and software that are not interchangeable
with other manufacturers’ devices, and substitution is not permitted without formal PPP evaluation and approval.
As a result, SSK Industries (or its authorized distributors) is the only responsible source capable of providing this specific item in
compliance with Air Force requirements. Soliciting from other sources or considering alternate products would introduce
unacceptable safety and certification risks and would not meet PPP standards.
Section D: Efforts to Obtain Competition
Market research was conducted using available government and commercial sources, including NSN lookup and GSA platforms,
to identify potential vendors capable of providing the required item. Results confirmed that the CYPRES (ECC), NSN
1670-12-422-1310, is a proprietary product manufactured by SSK Industries and distributed only through authorized sources.
Due to its inclusion on the Air Force Personnel Parachute Program (PPP) Approved for Use List (AUL) in accordance with AFI
10-3503, no alternate manufacturers or equivalent items are authorized for substitution. As such, competition is not feasible for
this requirement.
Efforts to identify additional sources did not yield any vendors capable of providing an equivalent, compliant product,
reinforcing that this acquisition must be limited to the original manufacturer or its authorized distributors.
Section E: Steps to Preclude Future Single Source or Brand Name Awards
Efforts to obtain competition will continue through ongoing market research and monitoring of future AUL updates.

Federal notice (Sources Sought), HEALTH AND HUMAN SERVICES, DEPARTMENT OF.FOOD AND DRUG ADMINISTRATION.FDA OFFICE OF ACQ  GRANT SVCS
Title: �Brand Name or Equal� Nanalysis AUTOsample-100 autosampler
Solicitation number: FDA-SSN-133966

Description: MARKET RESEARCH PURPOSES ONLY NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL OR SOLICITATION The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA), Office of Acquisitions and Grants Services (OAGS) is issuing this source sought announcement on behalf of the Office of Pharmaceutical Quality Research (OPQR), in order to determine if there are existing small business sources capable of providing a �Brand Name or Equal� Nanalysis AUTOsample-100 autosampler. Other than small business concerns, especially vendors who may be able to offer domestic products are also encouraged to submit a capability statement that provides company information, as well as information demonstrating that it can meet all of the minimum requirements included below, to include the country of manufacture of products offered. If your firm is considered a small business source under North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) Code 334516 - Analytical Laboratory Instrument Manufacturing; with a Small Business Size Standard of 1,000 employees and you believe that your firm would be able to provide the FDA with the supplies/services described below, please submit an email to Warren.Dutter@fda.hhs.gov. Background: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA), Office of Pharmaceutical Quality Research (OPQR) in Saint Louis, MO (OPQR-STL), is a laboratory-based office focused on the quality assessment of drug products. OPQR conducts research to support the establishment of scientific standards for product quality, performance, and the therapeutic equivalence of generic drug products. The purpose of this acquisition is to procure a �Brand Name or Equal� Nanalysis AUTOsample-100 autosampler for use with an existing Nanalysis 100 MHz benchtop NMR system. Benchtop NMR systems utilize low magnetic field strength permanent magnets, which are more cost-effective per MHz than traditional high-field NMR systems and require less maintenance. These systems are well suited for high-throughput screening applications. The addition of an autosampler will significantly improve laboratory efficiency by automating sample handling, eliminating the need for analysts to manually exchange samples between runs. It will also enable unattended operation, including overnight experiment execution, thereby increasing throughput and optimizing staff time efficiency. This is a Brand Name or Equal requirement. Products other than the specified Nanalysis AUTOsample-100 autosampler are acceptable but shall meet all the salient characteristics contained in the Minimum Technical Requirements below. Minimum Technical Requirements (Salient Characteristics): The autosampler shall be compatible with and capable of full integration with the existing Government-owned Nanalysis 100-PRO benchtop NMR system (magnet), Serial Number C109122022. The autosampler shall support automated queuing and execution of multiple NMR experiments. The autosampler shall support automated queuing and processing of multiple samples without operator intervention between runs. The autosampler shall enable automated execution of queued experiments without requiring manual sample exchange between analyses. The autosampler shall support automated magnetic field shimming adjustments between queued experiments and samples. The autosampler shall support automated lock adjustments between queued experiments and samples. The autosampler shall operate using the existing Nanalysis software and control environment without requiring custom third-party integration or modification to the existing Government-owned Nanalysis 100-PRO system. Additional System Requirements: The components and equipment shall be newly manufactured, not used or refurbished, or previously used for demonstration. Offered systems shall be a turn-key solution i.e., the contractor shall be responsible for providing all hardware, components, instruments, computers, software, and that otherwise required to meet these specifications and the FDA�s stated need. The systems shall be delivered with all necessary supplies and accessories required for installation and start-up. The system and associated accessories shall include operations and maintenance manuals covering proper operation, routine maintenance, and troubleshooting for the system and controlling software. All manuals and documentation shall be provided in hard copy and/or electronic format. The Contractor shall provide all labor, travel, and tools to install the equipment at the address provided below, to include shipping. The contractor shall demonstrate upon installation that the item meets or exceeds all performance specifications. Upon acceptance of the system, the contractor shall provide on-site operator training/familiarization. Such familiarization shall include system operations, calibration, optimization, troubleshooting and basic operational maintenance procedures. Systems shall be warranted for not less than one (1) year from FDA acceptance of the system(s). Warranty service shall include troubleshooting capabilities based on complete knowledge of the entire system, and immediate access to replacement parts.
