Description: Limited Sources Justification Format >SAT Vocera Badges and Licensing VHAPG Part 808.405-6 Limiting Sources Page 1 of 4 Revision: 02 Effective Date: 03/02/2026 Acquisition ID#: 36C250-26-AP-2508 LIMITED SOURCES JUSTIFICATION ORDER >SAT GSAR 538.7104-3 Acquisition Plan Action ID: 36C250-26-AP-2508 (1) Contracting Activity: Department of Veterans Affairs, Network Contracting Office 10, located at 5500 Armstrong Rd, Battle Creek MI 49037, in support of VISN 10 VA Health Care System at 17273 State Route 104, Chillicothe, OH 45601. PR: 538-26-3-087-0064 (2) Description of Action: This acquisition is conducted under the authority of the Multiple-Award Schedule Program (41 U.S.C. 152(3) and 40 U.S.C. 501). Order against: FSS Contract Number: 47QTCA22D006J Name of Proposed Contractor: ALVAREZ LLC Street Address: 161 FORT EVANS RD NE, STE 335 City, State, Zip: LEESBURG, VA 20176 Phone: 877-739-7289 FSS Contract Number: GS-07F-187GA Name of Proposed Contractor: GOVERNMENT MARKETING AND PROCUREMENT, LLC Street Address: 13350 RANCH RD 12 City, State, Zip: WIMBERLEY, TX 78676 Phone: 703-349-2990 (3) Description of Supplies or Services: The estimated value of the proposed action is $__________. Vocera Voice and Messaging V5000 Smart badges and Vocera software facilitates communication between staff members within the Medical Center. The current fleet of Vocera devices is at end of life and requires hardware replacements. This request is to purchase V5000 devices to replace the current fleet of B3000N devices that are end of life/end of support. The scope of this acquisition is for Contractor to provide new V5000 devices, licensing, and associated accessories to include: Qty: 500 Model # 220-02100 Product: V5000, Smart badge Qty: 500 Model # 261-01950 Product: V5000,FIPS 140-2 Device License Ver 1.0 Qty: 1000 Model # 230-02150 Product: V5000, Battery Qty: 72 Model # 230-02158 Product: V5000, Charger, 8-Bay, Universal Qty: 28 Model # 230-02155 Product: V5000, Clip, Grip, 25-Pack Qty: 5 Model #230-02200 V5000, Training Kit, 100 users Professional Services and Extended Warranty: Qty 500 Product #920-05002 Product Warranty, V5000, Smart badge, Qty 72 Product # 920-05082 Product Warranty, V5000, 8-Bay Charger, Qty 22 Product # 240-01361 Product Service, Workflow, Implementation and Training Services (per hour) Qty 866 Product # 240-01239 Product Service, Reimbursable Expenses This is a Brand Name Only procurement, as items are currently in use at Chillicothe VA Medical Center. There are no Option Years for this procurement; this is one-time purchase for Firm-Fixed Priced items. This is not a modification for an already existing order. (4) Identify the Authority and Supporting Rationale (see below and if applicable, a demonstration of the proposed contractor s unique qualifications to provide the required supply or service. GSAR 538.7104-3(b)(1)(i): An urgent and compelling need exists and following the ordering procedures would result in unacceptable delays: GSAR 538.7104-3(b)(1)(ii): Only one source is capable of providing the supplies or services required at the level of quality required because the supplies or services are unique or highly specialized; GSAR 538.7104-3(b)(1)(iii): In the interest of economy and efficiency, the new work is a logical follow-on to an original Federal Supply Schedule order provided that the original order was placed in accordance with the applicable Federal Supply Schedule ordering procedures. The original order must not have been previously issued under sole source or limited source procedures. GSAR 538.7104-4: Items peculiar to one manufacturer: A patent, copyright or proprietary data limits competition. The proprietary data is: These are direct replacements parts/components for existing equipment. This request is to purchase V5000 devices to replace the current fleet of B3000N devices that are end of life/end of support. The Chillicothe VA Medical Center currently uses the Vocera Brand Name Smart Badges and software, switching to an alternate brand Smart Badges would make the current badges unable to connect to the badges already in use. Additionally: The badge hardware is custom-built to work with Vocera s software, including advanced features like context-aware routing, staff assignment, and location tracking. Substituting with another device would break these critical functions. Vocera Smart Badges meet specific healthcare communication standards for infection control, durability, and usability in clinical settings. Generic devices or smartphones cannot meet these requirements without compromising patient safety and compliance. Vocera Smart Badges are uniquely designed to integrate with electronic health records (EHR), nurse call systems, and alarm management tools. No other vendor offers this level of native integration and real-time alerting within the same ecosystem. The badges operate exclusively on the Vocera Communication Platform, which ensures end-to-end encryption and compliance with HIPAA regulations. Other devices cannot connect to this proprietary platform, making interoperability impossible. Vocera Smart Badges provide hands-free, voice-activated communication, which is critical in clinical environments where staff cannot use traditional handheld devices. Competing products do not offer the same level of natural language voice commands integrated with healthcare workflows. The material/service must be compatible in all aspects (form, fit and function) with existing systems presently installed/performing. (5) Describe Why You Believe the Order Represents the Best Value consistent with GSAR 538.7102-2(b)(4) to aid the contracting officer in making this best value determination: The pricing is based on FSS pricing and therefore is already deemed fair and reasonable. Vocera brand name only is required to prevent substantial duplication of costs. (6) Describe the Market Research Conducted among schedule holders and the results or a statement of the reason market research was not conducted. Searched SBA SBS database with NAICS 334511 and VOSB selected and received 933 results. In addition, keywords smart badges was also used in the search engine, with the same NAICS code, and this search provided no available vendors. Reviewed action 36C25026F0354 awarded by CO LouAnn Gilliland and competed as a brand name only action on GSA eBuy where two quotes were received and the award was made to GMP for $235,961.50 on March 11, 2026. Searched GSA Advantage! With keyword V5000 and received applicable results from Alvarez LLC (SDVOSB) and GMP (SDVOSB). Waiver for NAICS 334516 but the descriptor doesn t match our requirement. OEM, Vocera, is a large business. Two SDVOSBs were located on GSA. The VA rule of two cannot be met due to the NMR. The SBA rule of two is applicable. Therefore; CO recommends SB set-aside on GSA ebuy to be posted alongside the Brand Name Only Justification. Buy America act is applicable. The product is made in the USA. (7) Any Other Facts Supporting the Justification: There are no other facts supporting the justification. (8) A Statement of the Actions, if any, the agency may take to remove or overcome any barriers that led to the restricted consideration before any subsequent acquisition for the supplies or services is made: Should a requisition of this nature recur, the market will be surveyed. (9) Requirements Certification: I certify that the requirement outlined in this justification is a Bona Fide Need of the Department of Veterans Affairs and that the supporting data under my cognizance, which are included in the justification, are accurate and complete to the best of my knowledge. I understand that processing of this limited sources justification restricts consideration of Federal Supply Schedule contractors to fewer than the number required by RFO FAR 6.103-1(d). (This signature is the requestor s supervisor, fund control point official, chief of service or someone with responsibility and accountability.)

This request is to purchase V5000 devices to replace the current fleet of B3000N devices that are end of life/end of support. The Chillicothe VA Medical Center currently uses the Vocera Brand Name Smart Badges and software, switching to an alternate brand Smart Badges would make the current badges unable to connect to the badges already in use. Additionally:
The badge hardware is custom-built to work with Vocera’s software, including advanced features like context-aware routing, staff assignment, and location tracking.
Substituting with another device would break these critical functions.
Vocera Smart Badges meet specific healthcare communication standards for infection control, durability, and usability in clinical settings.
Generic devices or smartphones cannot meet these requirements without compromising patient safety and compliance.
Vocera Smart Badges are uniquely designed to integrate with electronic health records (EHR), nurse call systems, and alarm management tools.
No other vendor offers this level of native integration and real-time alerting within the same ecosystem.
The badges operate exclusively on the Vocera Communication Platform, which ensures end-to-end encryption and compliance with HIPAA regulations.
Other devices cannot connect to this proprietary platform, making interoperability impossible.
Vocera Smart Badges provide hands-free, voice-activated communication, which is critical in clinical environments where staff cannot use traditional handheld devices.
Competing products do not offer the same level of natural language voice commands integrated with healthcare workflows.

CUI
Department of the Air Force: Justification for Other Than Full and Open Competition
I. Agency and Contracting Activity (RFO 6.104-1(a)(1)):
Agency: USAF F-15EX (AFLCMC/WAQK)
II. Nature and/or description of the action being approved (RFO 6.104-1(a)(2)):
This initiative aims to develop a self-sufficient, organic maintenance and repair capability for the F-15EX aircraft at the Air
Logistics Complex (ALC). A primary goal is to maximize the reuse of existing F-15 legacy capability and capacity to ensure
cost-effectiveness and efficiency.
To achieve this, a sole-source Indefinite Delivery/Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) contract will be awarded to the Telspan Data LLC.
This action is justified under FAR 6.302-1 as they are the only responsible source for the Modular Instrumentation Traffic
Analysis Point Recorder (MITR) Digital Video Recorder (DVR) - MITR-DVR, a key component integrated into the F-15EX's
baseline design. The contract will facilitate Depot Activation (DA), a process to establish the capability for comprehensive
overhaul, upgrading, or rebuilding of parts and subassemblies, along with necessary equipment testing and reclamation, as
defined in 10 USC Section 2460. This process involves identifying the necessary facilities, equipment, materials, and certified
personnel to perform depot-level maintenance. Depot activation is a strategic, long-term investment aimed at ensuring a
ready and controlled source of technical competence and resources to respond to national defense contingencies and other
emergency requirements.
This contract covers the procurement of essential parts and associated Depot Activation actions for the MITR-DVR,
supporting both current and future F-15EX sustainment needs.
Due to cost and schedule constraints, the IDIQ contract will have a three-year base ordering period with an additional one-
year option. The total ceiling for this Justification and Approval (J&A) is set at $ which is based on a Rough Order of
Magnitude (ROM) estimate for the depot-level repair capability required for MITR-DVR repairs.
III. Description of supplies/services required to meet agency needs (RFO 6.104-1(a)(3)):
Establishing an organic, depot-level repair capability requires the strategic delivery of a complete product support package
to the designated ALC(s). This consists of acquiring the required hardware, software, test, technical publication, training,
supply support, packaging, support equipment and data for the designated ALC to repair the depot level repairable(s). To
establish the organic repair capability, delivery of the core infrastructure for depot-level hardware testing and repair is
required. This includes the identification of requirements for, and the subsequent design, build, or purchase of, the
following components: Specialized Test Equipment (STE), Test Program Sets (TPS), and Interface Test Adapters (ITAs).
The United States Air Force (USAF) will provide all common support equipment for this activation effort. Due to proprietary
restrictions stemming from private investment in the development of F-15/F-15EX Line Replaceable Units (LRU), the
government's current ability to establish organic repair of the LRU is not possible. Technical data is restricted by the
manufacturer's intellectual property rights constraints. Therefore, to establish organic repair of the MITR-DVR, the USAF
needs to negotiate licenses for only the sensitive data needed to repair the LRU. The repair and maintenance of MITR-
DVRs requires not only the MITR-DVR itself but all associated parts/spares and the rights in technical data necessary to
maintain and ensure the software used in the displays functions correctly to support verification of repairs at designated
ALC.
MITR-DVRs are high-definition systems that capture, store, and analyze multiple, synchronized video streams from sensors
and cockpits. These systems enhance situational awareness, provide security monitoring, and aid in incident investigation.
Primary Contract Purpose
Primarily, this IDIQ will be a contract focused on ensuring the USAF can repair the current and future MITR-DVR specs
authorized to be installed on F-15EX aircraft. Incidental to the provision of MITR-DVRs are field and depot-level support,
engineering necessary to implement future variants within the EX-airframe, provisioning and support equipment. Section IV
MMaarrcchh 22002266 PPaaggee 22 ooff 77

CUI
Department of the Air Force: Justification for Other Than Full and Open Competition
Depot Activation Continuity
New OEM selection must include the assumption that the new part will undergo depot activation. Otherwise, the USAF will
face the same OEM limitations with the new supplier as currently experienced with existing OEMs.
The challenges above present considerable cost, schedule, and budgetary risks that the USAF cannot expect to overcome via
the issuance of a competitive source selection for a new MITR-DVR OEM.
Cost Prohibitions
Procuring and qualifying a new MITR-DVR solution would result in substantial cost duplication that the Government cannot
expect to recover by conducting a competitive source selection.
Schedule Constraints
The schedule impacts associated with new MITR-DVR qualifications and implementation are unacceptable. The timeline to
award and qualify a new MITR-DVR solution includes: 1-2 years for a source selection, 3-5 years for qualification, and an
additional 2-4 years to qualify a new MITR-DVR source's facilities, personnel, processes, and procedures.
This entire 6-11 year process would be required if a new MITR-DVR OEM is selected. With existing contractual support for
inorganic Depot Activation expiring at the end of FY 2026, any solution other than sole-source award to Telspan Data LLC
will result in EX aircraft being grounded during this extended timeline.
Telspan Data LLC's Unique Position
Telspan Data LLC MITR-DVR is fully developed, integrated, and has been certified/qualified for use on all F-15EX aircraft. The
MITR-DVR further meets all safety, suitability, and effectiveness requirements necessary for fielding EX aircraft. As the OEM of
the only compliant MITR-DVR available to the USAF, Telspan Data LLC is the only source in possession of the technical
expertise, technical data, source code, proprietary engineering documentation, and knowledge necessary to fulfill the
delivery and DA requirements the USAF requires to continue fielding EX aircraft without substantial impacts to cost and
schedule.
Accordingly, Telspan Data LLC is the only viable OEM capable of providing the supplies and services identified in Section III
above without the cost, schedule and budgetary risks explained in this section.
VI. Integrated Market Analysis and Efforts to Solicit Competition (RFO 6.104-1(a)(6), (8), and (10)):
In accordance with FAR Subpart 5.2, a synopsis of the proposed contract action was published on SAM.gov.
Furthermore,market research was conducted to identify all potential sources for this requirement, consistent with the
procedures outlined below.
Regulatory Requirement
DFARS PGI 206.302-1(d) states that "When utilizing the authority at FAR 6.302-1, the Contracting Officer shall post a request
for information or a sources sought notice, and shall include the results of this inquiry in the justification required by FAR
6.303. This requirement to post may be waived by the Head of the Contracting Activity, or designee. The waiver authority
may not be delegated lower than a general or flag officer or a member of the Senior Executive Service."
Market Research Conducted
In fulfillment of this requirement, the Government conducted two separate market research inquiries via SAM.gov to identify
sources capable of meeting the full scope of the Government's needs.
Broad-Scope RFI: A Request for Information (RFI) was posted for 60 days (1 May - 28 June 2025) to identify sources capable
of providing depot-level maintenance and repair services for a variety of F-15EX components, including the MITR-DVR.
Targeted RFI: A second, more targeted RFI was posted for 14 days (3 Dec - 16 Dec 2025) specifically seeking sources for the
integrated MITR-DVR requirement, encompassing both immediate depot repair services and the elements required for a full
Depot Activation.

Results of Market Research
The comprehensive market research effort confirmed that no viable alternative sources exist.
No respondent to either RFI was able to demonstrate the existing capability to perform depot-level repair of the F-15EX
MITR-DVR. Further, no respondent could demonstrate possession of, or a viable path to obtaining, the necessary proprietary
technical data, OEM-certified engineering expertise, and source code required to establish an organic DA capability.
The results of this inquiry affirm that Telspan Data LLC as the OEM, is the only source with the unique qualifications,
proprietary data, and technical expertise required to perform both the immediate depot repair services and to provide the
essential support needed to establish a permanent, organic government depot solution.
VII. Determination of Fair and Reasonable Cost (RFO 6.104-1(a)(7)):
The Contracting Officer is responsible for evaluating, determining, and documenting the anticipated contract cost/price is
fair and reasonable in accordance with RFO Subpart 15.4, Contract Pricing.
VIII. Any Other Facts Supporting the Justification (RFO 6.104-1(a)(9)):
Contracting Officer Assessment
The F-15EX Contracting Officer has determined that the Government can obtain and negotiate a fair and reasonable price for
the MITR-DVR requirement defined in Section III above if acquired from Telspan Data LLC on a sole-source basis.
Analysis and Evaluation Support
Thorough technical, price, and cost analyses will be performed as necessary by the F-15 System Program Office (SPO) with
assistance from the Air Force Life Cycle Management Center (AFLCMC) Pricing Division, the Defense Contract Audit Agency
(DCAA), and the Defense Contract Management Agency (DCMA). The F-15EX program may utilize the DCMA Integrated Cost
Analysis Team (ICAT) for technical evaluation, pricing evaluation, and negotiation support, if warranted.
The undersigned Contracting Officer has determined that the anticipated cost to the Government for this acquisition of full
DA capability will be determined fair and reasonable.
This determination will be based on a comprehensive analysis of the contractor's proposal, as outlined below:
Comprehensive Government Cost Analysis
The SPO, with expert support from the Air Force Life Cycle Management Center (AFLCMC) Pricing Division, the Defense
Contract Audit Agency (DCAA), and the Defense Contract Management Agency (DCMA), will perform a thorough technical
and cost analysis of the contractor's proposal. This analysis will evaluate the reasonableness of all proposed costs for both
the recurring depot repair services and the non-recurring engineering and data deliverables associated with the Depot
Activation effort.
Final Negotiation and Verification
The Contracting Officer will use the results of the comprehensive government cost analysis as the primary basis for
negotiating a final, binding price.

In accordance with DFARS PGI 206.302-1(d), the Program Office conducted comprehensive market research to identify all

operational reliability.

2025. All notices required by FAR 5.201 will be published and any proposals received
will be considered.

competition is not anticipated.

“Competition in Subcontracting” and DFARS clause 252.219-7003, entitled “Small
Business Subcontracting Plan (DoD Contracts)” to ensure that all subcontracts are
awarded on a competitive basis to the maximum extent possible.

Federal notice (Special Notice), TRANSPORTATION, DEPARTMENT OF.FEDERAL AVIATION ADMINISTRATION.6973GH FRANCHISE ACQUISITION SVCS
Title: 6973GH-26-R-00121 - CBP WILL-BURT FOLLOW ON - NOTICE OF INTENT TO SINGLE SOURCE
Solicitation number: 6973GH-26-R-00121
PSC: 5999; NAICS: 811210
Description: The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) intends to award a single source contract to Will-Burt Company, 401 Collins Boulevard Orrville, OH for the repair, acquisition, and engineering services for the Will-Burt Mast System Assembly mounted on the Mobile Video Surveillance System (MVSS). In accordance with the FAA Acquisition Management System Paragraph 3.2.2.4, the purpose of this announcement is to inform industry of the basis of the FAA's decision to contract with a selected source via single source procedures. Will-Burt Company is the only known source that can provide the repair and services to Will-Burt Mast assembly and associated components. Will-Burt Company is the Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) of this equipment. Will-Burt is the sole proprietary source for the technical data and drawings necessary to repair and/or replace the Mast Assembly. The proposed principle North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for this effort is 811210 Electronic and Precision Equipment Repair and Maintenance, with a size standard of $34 million. This announcement is for informational purposes only, not a Solicitation/Request for Proposal. Competitive solicitation is not available for this procurement. All questions pertaining to this announcement should be addressed in writing to the contracting Officer, Tamara Maxwell at tamara.m.maxwell@faa.gov. No phone calls will be accepted.

“STATEMENT of OBJECTIVES”
For
Hot Water Tank
Procurement Request: 2126406Y61J5596001
USCG 270’ Campbell
Yard POC: James Johnston; (410) 636-3461 
Ship Superintendent
Required Delivery Date: 9/20/26 (or A.S.A.P)

Please Provide the following Item detailed below:
Description: Hubbell Marine Electric Water Heater
Model Number# MSH320-0-30SLT4
Packaged Hubbell marine electric water heater with Cement Lined vessel ASME Section IV stamped and registered with the National Board of Boiler and Pressure Vessel Inspectors. Complete with all electrical operating controls including the following: power distribution block, magnetic contactor(s), power circuit fusing, immersion heating element(s), fused low voltage transformer, operating thermostat, safety hi-temperature cut out with manual reset, safety door interlock switch, and an ASME rated combination temperature and pressure relief valve. Unit is factory assembled, insulated, jacketed, painted, wired, and tested. Unit is ready for electrical and plumbing service connections.
Cement Lined construction to ASME Section IV and stamped as such for 125 psig maximum allowable working pressure. 
Tank is 48 Diameter by 66 Overall Length with angle legs
Tank water capacity is 320 gallons -Unit is designed and constructed for shipboard installation including both deck and bulkhead mounting Supports
Tank to have ASME relief valve set at 75 psig, shipped loose for field installation
Tank to have one 12 X 16 inspector port -2 ANSI Flange inlet and outlet connections
One electric coil complete with-30 kW capacity for 460/3/60 power and capable of heating 400 gph of 40 degrees F water to 140 degrees F
Complete water heater package is factory assembled with 1 1/2 insulation, jacketed, wired and tested



The objective of this procurement is to acquire 1(ea.) Hubbell Marine Electric Water Heater as outlined by MECPL PDM that would be installed on board USCGC 270’ Campbell here by production forces at United States Coast Guard Yard. The current one being used is old and Bonding agent between copper lining of vessel has failed, CGY does not have the copper-smithing capacity to perform permanent repairs to copper lining. The item shall meet all applicable Coast Guard specifications, including material durability, pressure ratings, and compatibility with the existing conditions set up on the ship. This procurement aims to secure a high-quality component delivered by [9/20/26] to support scheduled maintenance and sustain the cutter’s mission readiness. Coordination with (James Johnston; (410) 636-3461)



FAR 52.237-1 Site Visit: Offerors or quoters are urged and expected to inspect the site where services are to be performed and to satisfy themselves regarding all general and local conditions that may affect the cost of contract performance, to the extent that the information is reasonably obtainable. In no event shall failure to inspect the site constitute grounds for a claim after contract award.

Controlled Unclassified Information: JCP certification is required for United States (U.S.) or Canadian contractors who wish to obtain access to unclassified technical data disclosing militarily critical technology with military or space application that is under the control of, or in the possession of the U.S. Department of Defense (DOD) or the Canadian Department of National Defense (DND).

ORAL MODIFICATION: No oral statement of any person other than the contracting officer shall in any manner or degree, modify, or otherwise affect the terms of this contract.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA: Criteria evaluated for payment approval. The government will review work in its entirety prior to issuing invoice approval.

GOVERNMENT FURNISHED ITEMS AND SERVICES: 
Services: The Government shall provide material handling services to load and unload Contractor machinery and for the set up of equipment. The Coast Guard Yard shall provide timely assistance as requested by the Contractor. The Contractor shall provide 48-hour notice to the Government when there is a need for material handling services. 

Utilities: The Government will provide water, compressed air, and electricity for the Contractor as defined herein. The Contractor shall instruct employees in utilities conservation practices. The Contractor shall be responsible for operating in such a manner that precludes the waste of utilities, for example turning off the water faucets or valves after using the required amount to accomplish assigned work.

Compressed Air: The Government shall provide a source of compressed air for Contractor machinery. The Contractor shall be responsible for ensuring that their compressed air hookup connections are compatible with the Yard’s compressed air sources.
Electricity: The Government shall provide up to 200 amps and up to 480 volts of electrical services. 
CONTRACTOR FURNISHED ITEMS, SERVICES AND RESPONSIBILITIES: 
General: The Contractor shall furnish all equipment and services required to perform work under this SOW, other than those explicitly addressed in government furnished services. 
The Contractor shall report to the designated work site on the date specified on the written notification by the Contracting Officer in the form of a signed order. No other individual has the authority to direct the Contractor to begin work, other than a warranted Contracting Officer. Pending Coast Guard Yard production schedules, services may be required on an intermittent basis within the period and quantity specified. 
Contractor Equipment: vehicles and tanks which holds or can hold hazardous materials that is left on CG Yard premises must have the Contractor’s contact information placed in the driver’s side window indicating the Emergency Contact Number (answered 24/7/365) for the owner/operator of the vehicle.  If a tank is left on the premises, the Emergency Contact Number (answered 24/7/365) for the owner/operator of the tank must be painted on the tank in a prominent location.  The government will not assume liability for any vehicles/tanks left on CG YARD property.  The COR/SS will coordinate the location with the Yard Environmental/Security/Materials Handling. 
RAPID GATE SECURITY REQUIREMENTS:  Effective September 1, 2016, all contractors and subcontractors performing on this contract/purchase order/task order must utilize the RAPIDGate Program and/or Transportation Worker Identification Credentials (TWIC) if repeat access to the CG Yard is required for seven (7) or more days annually. RAPIDGate manages the non-Common Access Credential (CAC) eligible vendor/contractor companies and their employees who require access to Coast Guard Yard, Baltimore. Vendor/contractor CAC eligibility has been restricted to only those who require physical access to Coast Guard Yard AND logical access to a DoD or DHS network or system.  
Vendor/contractor companies that require repeat (7 or more days annually) access to the CG Yard, pay an annual company enrollment subscription to participate in the RAPIDGate Program and an annual employee registration subscription for each employee to participate in the program. The company enrollment fee is waived for sole proprietors. Vendor/contractor companies must be approved by a government sponsor at each DoD and DHS installation where their employees require access. Vendor/contractor employees who are registered, undergo initial and regular vetting and are issued a single credential, which is valid for perimeter access to those DoD and DHS installations where access privileges have been granted. All company enrollments are submitted via the web at www.rapidgate.com and managed by phone or email. Initial employee registrations take place at a Program Registration Kiosk, typically located at participating DoD and DHS Installation Pass & ID Offices. The CG Yard’s Registration Kiosk is located at 2401 Hawkins Point Road, Baltimore, MD 21226, BLDG. 144, Security [brick building adjacent to the main gate]. Credentials will be available for pick-up at BLDG. 144 fourteen (14) days after the employee’s initial registration. Costs incurred for delays at the gate due to the contractor’s failure to comply with this requirement or to provide qualified, authorized personnel will not be reimbursed by the Government. Your tenant sponsor is, the Yard POC or Ship Superintendent listed at the beginning of this document. This sponsor will need a list of individual employee names and DOB’s with your quotation. Any RAPIDGate program questions should be directed to: 1-877-727-4342 
General: The Contractor will be required to follow 29 CFR 1915 (OSHA Shipyard Industry Standard), 16 CFR1303, 29 CFR 1910, 29 CFR 1915.1025, 29 CFR 1926.62, 15 U.S.C. 2601, while performing this work at the U.S. Coast Guard Yard. 
Safety Equipment: The area where this work taking place requires hard hats, safety harnesses and safety glasses at all times. The Contractor will provide all required personnel safety equipment for their employees, including, but not limited to, safety helmet and safety glasses with side shields. All safety equipment shall meet OSHA standards. The Contractor shall follow all applicable OSHA guidelines and regulations. It is also required that all COVID safety practices are followed. 
ISO Qualifications:  Contractor shall comply with all the U.S. Coast Guard Yard International Organization for Standardization (ISO) 9001 Quality Management and ISO 14001 Environmental Management Systems. The Contractor may be periodically audited to ensure conformity to these standards.  If the contractor fails to perform as specified, the contracting officer may direct that employees be replaced or suspend work. 
EMERGENCY SERVICES: The U.S. Coast Guard Yard has 24-hour first aid, spill response and fire protection available.  If necessary, the Contractor may call 410-636-3993 from non-Yard phones and extension 3000 from Yard phones for emergency situations. Injuries shall be reported immediately and followed up with a written report to the COR.  

ENVIRONMENTAL PROTECTION REQUIREMENTS: All contractors working on CG Yard shall abide by all federal, state, and local environmental regulations as published by the Environmental Protection Agency, 40 CFR (series) and the following Yard Environmental plans/policies:  
CG Yard Environmental Management Systems (EMS) 
CG Yard Storm Water Pollution and Prevention Plan (SWPPP) 
CG Yard Spill Prevention Control and Counter Measure Plan (SPCC) 
  
Transport and Disposal:  All material removed from tanks shall be taken off CG Yard property immediately after cleaning operations are complete.  Material shall be processed in accordance with Section 10.2.2 before leaving the Yard.  Prior to removing material, the Government environmental dept. reserves the right to inspect the transport vehicle status of contents, to ensure accurate quantities being removed from the CG Yard.   

The Contractor must properly remove and dispose of all materials in compliance with applicable Federal, state, and local environmental laws and regulations.  Contractor assumes all responsibility and liability for the transport and proper disposal of materials and in particular the following requirements: 
 
If a spill occurs, the CG Yard Environmental Branch shall be immediately notified and can be reached at (410) 636-3111. The Contractor must also report the spill to the USCG Yard Main Gate (410) 636-3993 or YARD extension 3000 IMMEDIATELY.  A letter describing the incident shall be submitted within 24 hours after the spill.  During a spill, the Contractor will receive direction from the Yard Incident Commander/ Firehouse / Environmental or YARD/Vessel OOD.  
 
The Contractor MUST follow the USCG Yard Facilities Response Plan, when operating on USCG Yard property.

Title: 6530--EQUIPMENT - GULDMANN PATIENT CEILING LIFT SYSTEMS BRAND NAME ONLY

Award:
Description: This is a SOURCES SOUGHT ANNOUNCEMENT ONLY.� � It is neither a solicitation announcement nor a request for proposals or quotes and does not obligate the� Government to award a contract.� Requests for a solicitation will not receive a response.� Responses to this Sources Sought must be in writing.� The purpose of this Sources Sought Announcement is for market research to make appropriate acquisition decisions and to gain knowledge of potential qualified businesses interested in and capable of providing the requested commodities. The NAICS Code is 339113; size standard is 800 employees; PSC is 6530. Unrestricted no set-aside Responses to this notice shall include the following: (a) company name� � b) address (c) socio-economic status, (d) point of contact (e) phone, fax, and email (f) SAM UEI number (g) Cage Code� (h) Tax ID Number (i) and must� � provide a capability statement that addresses the organizations qualifications and ability� to perform as a contractor and provide the commodities described below.� � BRAND NAME ONLY GULDMANN, INC. OBJECTIVE: James J. Peters VA Medical Center is replacing their outdated patient lifts that have exceeded their end-of-life. This project involves the deinstallation of the old units, procurement, installation, inspection, and staff training on the Guldmann GH3+ lifts, in coordination with Safe Patient Handling (SPH), Facilities Management Service (FMS), and Healthcare Technology Management (HTM). STANDARDS AND SPECIFICATIONS: Ceiling Lifts shall meet the latest versions of NFPA 13, NFPA 101, NFPA 70, NFPA 99, and all other applicable federal, state and local codes. Appropriate documentation should be provided. Ceiling Lifts shall comply with ISO 10535: Hoists for the transfer of disabled persons Requirements and test methods . Ceiling lifts must include a 2-point hangar bar, and manufacturers must allow and warrant the use of their lifts with the full range of manufacturer loop slings. The lifts shall be mounted (using ceiling support as determined by building structure and room covering layout needs) to provide lifting capability for the maximum area possible within each room which means wall to wall. The contractor shall offer both traverse and straight track options for the ceiling mounted lifts. Lifts must be capable of picking patients up off the floor. Scales must be internal; with patient weight displayed on LCD screen located on the hand control and must not decrease the lifting height of the system. Hoist must not have an external scale attachment. The lift hand control must be attached to the lift in a way that allows it not to be lost. Ceiling lift motors shall be capable of lifting at least 600 pounds for standard lifts and 880 pounds for bariatric lifts, as specified. Ceiling lifts vertical motion must be motorized. Motors shall be GFCI protected. Lift must charge automatically anywhere on the track via continuous AC charging. Ceiling lifts must include safeguards to prevent patients from being trapped or hurt, such as emergency stop buttons or emergency lowering devices in case of power failure. Use of emergency lowering devices must not require tools or ladders and easily accessible to patient care personnel (i.e. Nursing). Contractor shall not interfere with operations of existing sprinkler heads, lights, HVAC grills, curtain tracks, IV tracks, televisions, permanent furniture, or other permanent structures. Contractor shall not breach any firewalls during the installation of these lifts. Any fire barrier that must be penetrated must be discussed with VA safety personnel and must immediately have fire barrier repaired. An Above Ceiling Permit must be filled out before ceiling work, and the COR will check the ceiling after ceiling work, to make sure any fire barrier penetration was repaired. Each room where lifts are installed shall be returned to its original condition, excluding the newly installed ceiling lift. Holes in the wall or ceiling tile must be patched with appropriate materials. Ceilings must not be slotted exposing space above ceiling to the room below. Rail system and Patient Lift Motor must be provided by the same manufacturer. Place of Delivery: James J Peters VA Medical Center 130 W Kingsbridge Rd Bronx, NY 10468 The Government is not obligated to, nor will it pay for or reimburse any costs associated with responding to this Sources Sought request. BRAND NAME ONLY – GULDMANN, INC.

OBJECTIVE:

James J. Peters VA Medical Center is replacing their outdated patient lifts that have exceeded their end-of-life. This project involves the deinstallation of the old units, procurement, installation, inspection, and staff training on the Guldmann GH3+ lifts, in coordination with Safe Patient Handling (SPH), Facilities Management Service (FMS), and Healthcare Technology Management (HTM).

STANDARDS AND SPECIFICATIONS:
Ceiling Lifts shall meet the latest versions of NFPA 13, NFPA 101, NFPA 70, NFPA 99, and all other applicable federal, state and local codes. Appropriate documentation should be provided.
Ceiling Lifts shall comply with ISO 10535: “Hoists for the transfer of disabled persons – Requirements and test methods”.
Ceiling lifts must include a 2-point hangar bar, and manufacturers must allow and warrant the use of their lifts with the full range of manufacturer loop slings.
The lifts shall be mounted (using ceiling support as determined by building structure and room covering layout needs) to provide lifting capability for the maximum area possible within each room which means wall to wall.
The contractor shall offer both traverse and straight track options for the ceiling mounted lifts.
Lifts must be capable of picking patients up off the floor.
Scales must be internal; with patient weight displayed on LCD screen located on the hand control and must not decrease the lifting height of the system.
Hoist must not have an external scale attachment.
The lift hand control must be attached to the lift in a way that allows it not to be lost.
Ceiling lift motors shall be capable of lifting at least 600 pounds for standard lifts and 880 pounds for bariatric lifts, as specified.
Ceiling lifts’ vertical motion must be motorized.
Motors shall be GFCI protected.
Lift must charge automatically anywhere on the track via continuous AC charging.
Ceiling lifts must include safeguards to prevent patients from being trapped or hurt, such as emergency stop buttons or emergency lowering devices in case of power failure. Use of emergency lowering devices must not require tools or ladders and easily accessible to patient care personnel (i.e. Nursing).
Contractor shall not interfere with operations of existing sprinkler heads, lights, HVAC grills, curtain tracks, IV tracks, televisions, permanent furniture, or other permanent structures.
Contractor shall not breach any firewalls during the installation of these lifts. Any fire barrier that must be penetrated must be discussed with VA safety personnel and must immediately have fire barrier repaired. An Above Ceiling Permit must be filled out before ceiling work, and the COR will check the ceiling after ceiling work, to make sure any fire barrier penetration was repaired.
Each room where lifts are installed shall be returned to its original condition, excluding the newly installed ceiling lift. Holes in the wall or ceiling tile must be patched with appropriate materials.
Ceilings must not be slotted exposing space above ceiling to the room below.
Rail system and Patient Lift Motor must be provided by the same manufacturer.

130 W Kingsbridge Rd
Bronx, NY 10468

JUSTIFICATION
1. Contracting Activity.
The Naval Sea Systems Command, Naval Surface Warfare Center Indian Head
Division (NSWC IHD), Contracts Office Code 02.
2. Description of the Action Being Approved.
This action seeks to award a follow-on sole-source contract for 1,100 CCU-
189/B Impulse Cartridges (DODIC JP40) in support of EA-18G aircraft to
Applied Energetic Technology Corp (AETC).
3. Description of Supplies/Services.
NSWC IHD requires a contract for fabrication, acceptance inspection, and
delivery of JP40 impulse cartridges, with limited install life, for use in
EA-18G aircraft and for additional testing for service life extension. The
JP40 cartridge is a Hazards of Electromagnetic Radiation to Ordnance (HERO)
Safe version of an existing cartridge used in the Fleet. The ignition
element in the cartridge has been modified with a capacitor to make it
HERO-Safe and allow aircraft to avoid flying at an At-Risk status. The
Fleet requires delivery of these units no later than the end for calendar
year 2026.

AETC is the current and only source with the proven and currently validated

all government performance and safety requirements, including HERO-Safe
standards, within the timeframe dictated by operational necessity. The

For the reasons set forth in Paragraph 5, NSWC IHD has no plans at this

This requirement includes the provision of proprietary SOS hardware, software licensing exclusively authorized under CRADA CR-188, and specialized technical installation utilizing the patented Alignment Pro system. The project also involves ancillary facility improvements (site preparation) necessary to support the exhibit environment. Awardee: B/W Color Prints LLC (dba BWC Visual Technology). attachments.text:
Version 4.0
SOLE SOURCE
FOR AN ACTION EXCEEDING THE SIMPLIFIED ACQUISITION THRESHOLD
USING SIMPLIFIED PROCEDURES FOR CERTAIN COMMERCIAL ITEMS
(AUTHORITY: FAR 12.102(b), 41 U.S.C. 1901)
Request For Quote (RFQ) 1332KP26Q0009
1. Agency and contracting activity. Department of Commerce, NOAA Acquisition and Grants
Office (AGO), Satellite and Information Acquisition Division (SIAD) and National Environmental
Satellite, Data, and Information Service (NESDIS), Office of Projects, Planning, and Analysis
(OPPA).
2. Nature and/or description of the action being approved.
This is a sole source justification to support the award of a new firm-fixed-price turnkey installation
contract. The Government has solicited with the single source, B/W Color Prints LLC (dba BWC
Visual Technology), based on the proprietary nature of the requirement.
3. Description of supplies or services required to meet the agency’s needs (including the total
estimated value).
The NOAA Satellite Operations Facility (NSOF) requires a turnkey installation of a Science on a
Sphere (SOS) exhibit. The SOS is a specialized visualization system utilizing computers and four
video projectors to display animated environmental data onto a 60-inch diameter sphere. The SOS
exhibit is a mission-essential requirement for NSOF to fulfill NOAA’s statutory mandate under the
America COMPETES Reauthorization Act (33 U.S.C. § 893a) to improve public environmental
literacy. As the national command center for environmental satellite operations, NSOF requires a
high-fidelity visualization platform to translate complex, real-time data from the GOES-R and JPSS
constellations into intuitive, global formats for visiting policymakers, international scientific
partners, and the public. Unlike traditional flat-screen displays, the SOS provides a distortion-free,
360-degree representation of Earth, which is required for the accurate visualization of planetary-
scale phenomena such as atmospheric rivers, ocean currents, and global climate trends, core
mission areas for NESDIS.
Requirements include proprietary SOS hardware and software (Operating System, Wibu Dongle,
and "SOS RoboGuide" suite), specialized technical services (Remote Alignment Management and
API support), and ancillary site preparation including glass double doors, wall murals, and sphere
mounting points.
(cid:120) Period of Performance: 12 months from Notice to Proceed (NTP).
(cid:120) Total Estimated Value:
4. Statutory authority permitting the sole source (including brand name) acquisition.
The authority for this justification is Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO) 12.102, Restricting
Competition, and 41 U.S.C. 1901, and is based on only one responsible source and no other
supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements. The applicable procedures are in RFO
12.201-1 Simplified Procedures, as implemented by Department of Commerce Class Deviation to
FAR Parts 1 through 53 (PM 2026-06)
Page 1 of 3
1332KP26Q0009
5. Demonstration that the proposed contractor’s unique qualifications or the nature of the
acquisition requires use of the authority cited. The contracting officer has determined the
following circumstances justify the use of a sole source as supported below:
Exclusive Licensing Agreement/Restrictive Rights/Authorized Reseller - BWC Visual
Technology is the sole authorized partner for the SOS system in North America under CRADA
CR-188 (active through March 2029) and holds exclusive rights to the "Alignment Pro" system
(U.S. Patent No. 18/188,075).
Technical Necessity: This requirement involves the proprietary SOS codebase and the Wibu
Dongle hardware key, both of which are exclusively distributed and supported by BWC in
North America. No other company can satisfy the Government’s needs because a third-party
installation lacks the legal authority to utilize the proprietary alignment software suite.
Inseparability of Services: The ancillary site preparation, including the installation of glass
double doors and specialized structural mounting points, is technically inseparable from the
technical installation. The 60-inch sphere must be suspended with millimeter precision to
ensure the four projectors can seamlessly stitch images via BWC's proprietary software.
Splitting this work between multiple vendors would create a "liability gap" and void
manufacturer warranties as defined under the CRADA.
Mission Impact: Failure to award to BWC would prevent the successful deployment of the
SOS exhibit at NSOF. No other North American entity possesses the legal or technical
authority to install and certify the proprietary hardware and software suite required for this
mission-critical visualization tool.
6. Description of efforts made to ensure that offers are solicited from as many potential
sources as practicable, including whether a notice was or will be publicized as required by
FAR Subpart 5.2 and, if not, which exception under FAR 5.202 applies.
A Notice of Intent to Sole Source was published to SAM.gov on February 6, 2026, for 15 days
(Notice ID: REQUIREMENTS-25-5029). No responses were received from vendors capable of
meeting the technical and proprietary requirements.
7. Determination by the contracting officer that the anticipated cost to the Government will be
fair and reasonable.
The Contracting Officer will determine that the negotiated price of is fair and
reasonable. This determination will be based on a detailed price analysis comparing BWC’s
proposal to verified commercial pricing data.
This evaluation included an analysis
Page 2 of 3
1332KP26Q0009
Based on this information, the Contracting Officer determines that the anticipated price will be fair
and reasonable.
8. Description of the market research conducted (see Part 10) and the results or a statement
of the reason market research was not conducted.
Market research was conducted in February 2026 via SAM.gov, GSA, and internet searches.
Firms such as IM Systems Group (IMSG) and VizLab Protech were identified; however, they
lack the proprietary hardware rights and CRADA authorization required for physical SOS
installation. Globoccess AG was identified but disqualified as a German-based entity without
authorized distribution/installation rights in North America.
9. Any other facts supporting the use of a sole source (including brand name), such as:
All supporting facts have been documented herein.
10. List of the sources that expressed a written interest in the acquisition.
No sources expressed an interest in writing after the required notification on SAM.gov.
11. A statement of the actions, if any, the agency may take to remove or overcome any
barriers to competition before any subsequent acquisition for the supplies or services
required.
NOAA will continue to monitor the status of CRADA CR-188 and any future licensing changes.
If the proprietary rights or exclusive North American partnership status changes prior to
subsequent requirements, NOAA will pursue a full and open competition.
12. Technical/Requirements Representative Certification
I certify that this requirement constitutes the Government’s minimum needs and the
supporting data provided herein is accurate and complete to the best of my knowledge and
belief.
13. Contracting Officer’s Certification and Approval
I certify this justification is accurate and complete to the best of my knowledge and belief.

matters.title: Amended 01 Hybrid Enhanced Ballistic Protection System BPA
matters.text:
Federal notice (Justification), GENERAL SERVICES ADMINISTRATION.FEDERAL ACQUISITION SERVICE.GSA/FAS/GSS/QSCBD/ASSISTED CONTRACTING BRANCH B
Title: Amended 01 Hybrid Enhanced Ballistic Protection System BPA
Solicitation number: 47QSWC22A0010
PSC: 1680; NAICS: 332999
Description: PEO Aviation requires a sole source Blanket Purchase Agreement (BPA) for replacement Hybrid Enhanced Ballistic Protection System (HEBPS) components. These components are critical for CH-47 Chinook helicopters, enabling PEO Aviation to maintain 'Condition A' for deployable units and ensure continuous ballistic protection for pilots and soldiers during combat missions. This procurement is essential to restore damaged or non-functional HEBPS kits to full serviceability. This sole source action is justified under GSAR 538.7104-3(b)(ii) (GSA Class Deviation RGO-2026-01), citing that only one source is capable of providing these unique or highly specialized products. The Protective Group (TPG) manufactures HEBPS components and has confirmed Atlantic Diving Supply, Inc. (ADS) as their exclusive authorized distributor, both open market and on Schedule. TPG does not sell directly to the Government. A TPG letter of certification verifies ADS as the sole authorized distributor, making ADS the only capable source for these items.

Description: THERE IS NO SOLICITATION AVAILABLE AT THIS TIME. A REQUEST FOR A SOLICITATION WILL NOT RECEIVE A RESPONSE. THIS SOURCES SOUGHT SYNOPSIS (SSS) IS IN SUPPORT OF MARKET RESEARCH BEING CONDUCTED BY THE DEFENSE LOGISTICS AGENCY (DLA) TO IDENTIFY POTENTIAL SOURCES FOR THE SPARE PARTS LISTED BELOW, WHICH SUPPORT THE AH-64 APACHE MODERNIZED TARGET ACQUISITION DESIGNATION SIGHT/PILOT NIGHT VISION SENSOR (MTADS/PNVS). THE GOVERNMENT IS SEEKING QUALIFIED SOURCES FOR THE ACQUISITION OF THESE SPARE MISSILE PARTS TO ADD TO THE LOCKHEED MARTIN CAPTAIN OF INDUSTRIES (COI) SUPPLIER CAPABILITY CONTRACT (SCC) SPE4AX-22-D-9000. THIS REQUIREMENT SUPPORTS THE ROYAL NETHERLANDS LAND AIR & SPACE FORCE (RNLASF) UNDER FOREIGN MILITARY SALES (FMS) CASE NE-B-YCE. THE REQUIREMENT WILL BE FOR A ONE (1) YEAR PERIOD OF PERFORMANCE FOR THE FOLLOWING ITEMS. PSC NSN Part Number NAICS Size AMRC 1240 1240-01-518-3638 79760505-009 333310 1000 3/Q 1240 1240-01-589-5433 79760230-019 333310 1000 4/D 1240 1240-01-676-4038 79722960-009 333310 1000 TBD (TO BE DETERMINED) 1240 1240-01-687-6187 79787541-002 333310 1000 4/D 1240 1240-01-687-6785 79763030-009 333310 1000 4/P 1270 1270-01-535-8920 79760015-019 334511 1350 3/D 1270 1270-01-547-7770 79745095-001 334511 1350 TBD 1270 1270-01-547-7773 79718560-001 334511 1350 TBD 1680 1680-01-516-6818 79760545-009 336413 1250 3/Q JUSTIFICATION FOR SOLE SOURCE: THESE ITEMS HAVE BEEN ASSIGNED AMC/AMSC CODE 3, &/OR 4 WHICH REQUIRES THE GOVERNMENT TO ACQUIRE FOR THE FIRST, SECOND OR SUBSEQUENT TIME DIRECTLY FROM THE ACTUAL MANUFACTURER. THE DATA NEEDED TO ACQUIRE THIS PART COMPETITIVELY IS NOT PHYSICALLY AVAILABLE, IT CANNOT BE OBTAINED ECONOMICALLY, NOR IS IT POSSIBLE TO DRAFT ADEQUATE SPECIFICATIONS OR ANY OTHER ADEQUATE, ECONOMICAL DESCRIPTION OF THE MATERIAL FOR A COMPETITIVE SOLICITATION. AS A RESULT, THIS ACQUISITION IS CURRENTLY BEING PROCURED UNDER FEDERAL ACQUISITION REGULATION (FAR) ONLY ONE RESPONSIBLE SOURCE AND NO OTHER SUPPLIES OR SERVICES WILL SATISFY AGENCY REQUIREMENTS. THE GOVERNMENT IS INTERESTED IN ALL BUSINESSES TO INCLUDE 8(A), SMALL BUSINESS AND SMALL DISADVANTAGED BUSINESS, SERVICE-DISABLED VETERAN-OWNED, HUBZONE, AND WOMEN-OWNED SMALL BUSINESS CONCERNS. ALL OFFERORS MUST MEET PREQUALIFICATION REQUIREMENTS IN ORDER TO BE ELIGIBLE FOR AWARD. THE U.S. ARMY COMBAT CAPABILITIES DEVELOPMENT COMMAND AVIATION & MISSILE CENTER�S (AVMC DEVCOM) SYSTEM READINESS DIRECTORATE (SRD), SUSTAINMENT DIVISION (SD) IS THE ENGINEERING SOURCE AUTHORITY (ESA). FIRMS THAT RECOGNIZE AND CAN PRODUCE THE REQUIRED ITEM DESCRIBED ABOVE ARE ENCOURAGED TO IDENTIFY THEMSELVES. FIRMS ARE ENCOURAGED TO SEEK SOURCE APPROVAL IN ORDER TO COMPETE FOR FUTURE SOLICITATIONS BY CONTACTING THE CONTRACT TEAM. THE CLOSING DATE ANNOTATED IS AN ESTIMATED DATE AND MAY BE ADJUSTED DEPENDENT UPON THE DATE OF RELEASE FOR SOLICITATION; HOWEVER, THE SOLICITATION WILL NOT CLOSE PRIOR TO THE DATE STATED ABOVE. FOREIGN FIRMS ARE REMINDED THAT ALL REQUESTS FOR SOLICITATION MUST BE PROCESSED THROUGH THEIR RESPECTIVE EMBASSIES. THE CONTRACTOR SHALL BE CAPABLE OF SUCCESSFULLY PERFORMING AND COMPLYING WITH ANY AND ALL SPECIAL REQUIREMENTS IN ACCORDANCE WITH THE TERMS AND CONDITIONS SET FORTH IN THE SOLICITATION ANNOTATED ABOVE, AT THE UNIT PRICES ESTABLISHED AT TIME OF A CONTRACT AWARD. THE CONTRACTOR WILL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR RECURRING AND NONRECURRING ENGINEERING SERVICES ASSOCIATED WITH BECOMING A QUALIFIED SOURCE. THE CONTRACTOR WILL ALSO BE RESPONSIBLE FOR ALL ASPECTS OF THE MANUFACTURING/PRODUCTION PROCESS, INCLUDING BUT NOT LIMITED TO - SUPPLY CHAIN MANAGEMENT, LOGISTICS, FORECASTING OF PARTS, LONG-LEAD PARTS PROCUREMENT, MATERIAL FORECASTING, OBSOLESCENCE ISSUES AND FINAL DELIVERY OF ASSETS AS WELL AS ANY AND ALL ADDITIONAL COSTS INCURRED RESULTING FROM CONTRACT PERFORMANCE. PROCUREMENT CONSISTS OF TWO OR MORE REQUIREMENTS FOR SUPPLIES, BASED ON FORECASTED DEMANDS. THE SUBSEQUENT SOLICITATION SHALL INCLUDE A REQUEST FOR ECONOMIC ORDER QUANTITIES (EOQS) TO ENSURE OPTIMAL ORDERING QUANTITIES. THE EOQ REQUEST, IS TO AVOID ACQUISITIONS IN DISADVANTAGEOUS QUANTITIES AND TO ASSIST THE GOVERNMENT IN DEVELOPING DATA FOR CURRENT AND FUTURE ACQUISITIONS OF THIS ITEM/THESE ITEMS. THE GOVERNMENT ANTICIPATES THE OFFEROR�S PROPOSAL (IN VIEW OF MARKET RESEARCH, HISTORICAL AWARDS, THE NATURE OF THE ITEM(S) BEING SOLICITED, AND THE CURRENT ECONOMIC ENVIRONMENT) WILL INCLUDE QUANTITIES/RANGES THAT WILL VARY FROM THOSE BEING SOLICITED. THE SOLICITED QUANTITIES ARE BASED ON ESTIMATED ANNUAL DEMANDS AND AS SUCH GOVERNMENT RESERVES THE RIGHT TO AWARD THE MOST ADVANTAGEOUS QUANTITIES &/OR RANGES. THE GOVERNMENT RETAINS THE RIGHT TO CANCEL THIS PROCUREMENT, PARTIALLY OR IN ENTIRETY BEFORE AWARD. IN THE EVENT THE GOVERNMENT CANCELS THIS ACQUISITION (PARTIALLY OR IN ENTIRETY) BEFORE AWARD, THE GOVERNMENT HAS NO OBLIGATION TO REIMBURSE AN OFFEROR FOR ANY COSTS. DISCLAIMER: THIS SSS IS ISSUED SOLELY FOR INFORMATIONAL AND PLANNING PURPOSES. IT DOES NOT CONSTITUTE A SOLICITATION (REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL OR REQUEST FOR QUOTATION) OR A PROMISE TO ISSUE A SOLICITATION IN THE FUTURE AND SHALL NOT BE CONSTRUED AS A COMMITMENT BY THE GOVERNMENT. RESPONSES IN ANY FORM ARE NOT OFFERS AND THE GOVERNMENT IS UNDER NO OBLIGATION TO AWARD A CONTRACT AS A RESULT OF THIS ANNOUNCEMENT. statute expressly authorizes or requires that the acquisition be made through another
agency or from a specified source.” Public Law No. 108-136, National Defense
Authorization Act (NDAA) Fiscal Year 2004, Section 802, Quality Control Procurement of
Aviation Critical Safety Items and Related services, as implemented by Defense
Federal Acquisition Regulation Supplement (DFARS) 209.270-3(a).
5. Reason for Authority Cited: The proposed acquisition requires the use of the cited
statutory authority because the Connecting Link, Rig is an aviation Critical Safety Item
(CSI) as defined by DFARS 209.270-2. As such, this procured item can only be
performed by sources approved by the Systems Readiness Directorate
(SRD). The CSI classification means that, should the Connecting Link, Rig fail to
function properly, the result could be catastrophic, or cause a critical failure resulting in
the loss of, or serious damage to, the aircraft or weapon system; an unacceptable risk
of personal injury or loss of life; or an un-commanded engine shutdown that
jeopardizes safety. Pursuant to the provisions of Public Law No. 108-136, National
Defense Authorization Act Fiscal Year 2004, Section 802, Quality Control in
Procurement of Aviation Critical Safety Items and Related Services, as implemented by
DFARS 209.270-3(A), contracts for modification, repair, or purchase of CSI items can
only be awarded to a source approved by Systems Readiness Directorate (SRD), which
is the Army’s aviation design control activity.
The technical data for the Connecting Link, Rig has undergone full screening
per the DFARS PGI 217.7506, Spare Parts Breakout Program. The assigned
Acquisition Method Code / Acquisition Method Suffix Code (AMC/AMSC) is
1C, with AMC “1” meaning the item is suitable for competitive acquisition for
the second or subsequent time and AMSC “C” meaning this part must be
acquired from a manufacturing source(s) specified on a source control or
selected item drawing. Suitable technical data, Government data rights, or
manufacturing knowledge are not available to permit acquisition from other
sources, nor qualification testing of another part nor use of a second source
part in the intended application.
The only approved sources for the spare, Connecting Link, Rig are PCX
AeroSystems – Manchester and Sikorsky. However, Sikorsky does not intent

52.209-1, Qualification Requirements, will be included in the solicitation to advise

all subcontractors, except small businesses, that receive subcontracts more

Description: This is a Pre-solicitation Notice, as required by FAR 5.201 (RFO 5.101), regarding a proposed contract action. The Commander Fleet Readiness Centers (COMFRC) Procurement Group, Patuxent River, MD 20670 hereby gives notice of their intent to award a contract to The Boeing Company (Cage Code: 0PXV4) on a sole source basis in accordance with the Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Subpart 6.103-1, only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements. Fleet Readiness Center Southwest (FRCSW) has been tasked to procure a replacement Windscreen Repair Fixture system. The Windscreen Repair Fixture system is specifically designed for the F/A-18 E/F/G platform. Market research confirms that the Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM), The Boeing Company, manufacture�s the F/A-18 platform and is the only known qualified source capable of satisfying the Government�s specific requirements and mission for this procurement. The OEM of the Windscreen Repair Fixture system does not utilize third party vendors to manufacture this specific non-commercial equipment. Any liability to procure this equipment would cause an unacceptable delay in the F/A-18 platform maintenance cycle. For this reason, the Government intends to procure this equipment on a sole source basis from The Boeing Company (Cage Code: 0PXV4). THIS NOTICE OF INTENT IS NOT A REQUEST FOR COMPETITIVE PROPOSALS. However, all responsible sources may submit a capability statement, which, if received within fifteen (15) calendar days after the date of publication of this synopsis, will be considered. Any capability statement shall include the following information: 1) information showing responsibility in accordance with FAR Part 9, 2) specific exception to the intent to procure on a sole source basis; 3) technical data showing the capabilities of the respondent to perform the work listed above; and 4) past performance information on similar projects. The capability statement must provide clear and unambiguous evidence to substantiate the capability of the party to meet the requirement as listed above without substantial duplication of costs not expected to be recovered through competition or unacceptable delays in meeting the Government�s requirement. Information received will be considered solely for the purpose of determining whether to conduct a competitive procurement. A determination by the Government not to compete this requirement based upon responses received as a result of this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. A request for documentation, or additional information or submissions that only ask questions will not be considered an affirmative response to this notice. The Government does not intend to award a contract on the basis of this notice nor will it reimburse firms for any costs associated with preparing or submitting a response to this notice. Capability statements are due no later than the closing date and time of this notice. It is the responsibility of the respondent to contact the Government to confirm receipt prior to the due date and time. Primary Point of contact for this requirement is Kristin Randall at kristin.randall.civ@us.navy.mil Secondary Point of contact for this requirement is Tiffany Crayle at tiffany.l.crayle.civ@us.navy.mil

STATEMENT OF WORK (SOW) for
Peculiar Support Equipment Windscreen Repair Tooling Fixture

SCOPE:
This Statement of Work (SOW) is for the procurement, production and delivery of Peculiar Support Equipment (PSE) end item part numbers listed in Section 3.1.1 of this order. The PSE supports the F/A-18 E/F & E/A-18G Aircraft Depot level (D-Level) for maintenance and repair of the windscreen.

APPLICABLE DOCUMENTS: 
Government Documents: 

Specification, Standards, and Handbooks
The following specifications, standards, and handbooks form a part of this document to the extent specified herein. Unless otherwise specified, the issues of these documents are those listed in the latest issue of the Department of Defense Index of Specifications and Standards (DoDISS) and supplement thereto.

Standards – U.S. Navy

FED-STD-H28B – Screw Thread Standards for Federal Services (1994 edition)
MIL-STD-130N – Identification Marking of U.S. Military Property (2007 Island, Navy Primary Standards Lab (NPSL), North Island, 01 September 2020
MIL-STD-31000C – DoD Standard Practice, Technical Data Packages
MIL-S-8512 – Support Equipment, General Specification for Design

Local Documents

B250 CANOPY SHOP COURTESY LAYOUT, Distribution A

Non-Government Documents:

The product supplied shall comply with the following codes and specifications. The latest edition of the referenced publications shall be used. In case of a conflict between the requirements in this specification and those listed in the references, the Contractor shall notify the Technical Point of Contact (TPOC).

American Society of Mechanical Engineers (ASME)

ASME Y14.100 – Engineering Drawing Practices (2017 edition). Application for copies shall be addressed to the ASME International, Three Park Avenue, M/A 10 E, New York, NY 10016-5990.
REQUIREMENTS:
Manufacture: The contractor shall provide materials and services to manufacture, assemble, inspect, ship, and deliver to the government the PSE part numbers in Section 3.1.1 of this order. The manufacturing, assembly, and the inspection of the PSE end items shall be accomplished at the contractor’s facility.
Part Numbers:
 ▪ RE174350002-5 - Windscreen Fixture - QUANTITY (1)
 ▪ AK174350002-5 - Alignment Set - QUANTITY (1)
 ▪ RE274350002-5 - Tool Kit - QUANTITY (1)
 ▪ RE474000002-1 - Maintenance Stands - QUANTITY (2)

Note: The requirements in DFARS 252.211-7003, Item Identification, and Valuation, are applicable for this line item. The contractor shall provide DoD unique identification, or a DoD recognized unique identification equivalent.

Serialization: End item part numbers that have not been assigned serial numbers under previous Boeing procurement contracts for the same part numbers shall be assigned sequential serial numbers starting with 001. End item part numbers that have been previously procured under earlier Boeing contracts shall be sequentially serialized, starting with the next sequential serial number in the production history of that end item.

 Data: (CLIN 0005; CDRL A0001-A0004)
Technical Data Package: The contractor shall deliver a Technical Data Package for each end item part number listed in Section 3.1.1. in accordance with MIL-STD-31000C (CDRL A001; TDP) 3.3.1.1 Manuals/Drawings. The Contractor shall provide all prints, drawings per ASME reference in section REF _Ref128666407 \r \h 2.2.1a, specifications, and documentation to complete this project in digital format (.pdf) and three (3) hard copy sets to FRCSW TPOC before the final completion date and not later than five (5) working days after completion of all work. The digital manuals and drawings shall be organized, indexed and referenced similar to the equivalent hardcopy format (i.e. volume, manual, section, etc.)
3.3.1.2 Maintenance Manuals: Shall properly identify in detail the extent of preventive maintenance, materials, liquids, substances, parts, and chemicals, used during preventive maintenance, repair, and/or troubleshooting of equipment. A complete list of all materials, chemicals, substances, and parts used for the maintenance and operation of the equipment shall be provided to the TPOC. 
Fixture Alignment Data: The contractor shall provide fixture alignment data and instructions for each end item part number listed in Section 3.1.1 that requires periodic alignment, calibration, or adjustment in accordance with the Contractor’s established requirements for such fixtures (CDRL A002; TDP). For each fixture that requires alignment, the contractor shall recommend a fixture alignment interval or specify the conditions upon which alignment is recommended. The fixture alignment data shall be incorporated into the end item part number technical data package.

Tool Usage Instructions: The contractor shall provide Tool Usage Instructions (TUI) for each Part Number in accordance with the list below. The TUIs shall be delivered in accordance with CDRL A003; TDP.▪ RE174350002-5 ▪ Windscreen Fixture ▪ AK174350002-5 ▪ Alignment Set 
Facility Requirements: The contractor shall provide facility requirements information for each end item part number in Section 3.1.1 (CDRL A004; FRD). The information should include, as applicable, fixture space and footprint requirements, floor loads and surface finish, anchors or tie downs, electrical and hydraulic power, mechanical interfaces, ventilation, climate control, fire suppression, and noise attenuation. FRCSW will remove any current equipment to accommodate new PSE.
Cybersecurity Compliance:
 Requirements for Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification (CMMC) Status:
The contractor shall achieve and maintain CMMC Level 1 or above in accordance with DFARS 252.204-7021 and FAR 52.204-21 for each Contractor information system that will process, store, or transmit Federal Contract Information (FCI) used in performance of the contract.
Contractor shall provide, in its offer, the CMMC Unique Identifier (CMMC UID) issued by SPRS for each contractor information system that will process, store, or transmit FCI or CUI during performance of the contract.
Subcontractor Flowdown: The prime contractor must flow down the required CMMC level to subcontractors that will process, store, or transmit FCI. Prime contractors are responsible for ensuring subcontractors have a current CMMC status before awarding subcontracts.
The Government shall check the SPRS for each CMMC UID to verify the Contractor’s CMMC status. The Government shall not award a contract to a Contractor that does not have a current CMMC status posted in SPRS at the specified CMMC level or higher required by the solicitation.
INSPECTION/ACCEPTANCE
The Contractor shall self-inspect all equipment and develop deliverable end items at the Contractor’s facility. Final acceptance sign-off of Fixture and associated equipment will be conducted by the TPOC at destination and to confirm data defined in Section 3.3.2 Fixture Alignment Data is within acceptable values.

SHIPMENT
The contractor shall ship to the address below by traceable means. The contractor shall notify TPOC prior to shipment for coordination and escort at destination.
TPOC: joseph.m.omana.civ@us.navy.mil 619-545-9162TPOC Alt: raquel.l.wise.civ@us.navy.mil 619-545-7719Inventory Management Specialist: earl.d.fishell.civ@us.navy.mil 619-545-2947Shipping Address: FRCSW NASNI Quentin Roosevelt Blvd. Bldg. 36 North Bay San Diego, CA 92135 Attention: Joe Omana (5-9162) Earl Fishell (5-2947)

SECURITY AND BASE ACCESS: 
Security Forms. The Contractor shall coordinate with the TPOC to obtain, complete and submit SECNAV Form(s) 5512/1 and FRCSW Form 5512/5.
SECNAV Form 5512/1. Contractor shall submit one SECNAV Form 5512/1 for each individual Contractor personnel requiring base access.
FRCSW Form 5512/5. Contractor shall submit one FRCSW Form 5512/5 listing all Contractor personnel.
Upon arrival, all Contractor personnel shall report to the Visitor Control Center (VCC) Bldg.680, which is located near the Main Gate to Naval Base Coronado (NBC), NAS North Island, San Diego, CA. Contractor personnel shall check in and request a Defense Biometric Identification System (DBIDS) card. Only personnel in compliance with Section 6.1.1 will receive a DBIDS. Contractor personnel that do not possess a DBIDS will be refused entry to NBC.
Following receipt of a DBIDS, Contractor personnel shall coordinate with the TPOC to obtain visitor badges through the FRCSW Quarterdeck, located in Building 94. Contractor personnel shall submit a federally issued identification card to obtain a Visitor badge.
Contractor personnel shall report to FRCSW Quarterdeck at Building 94 before start of daily work to obtain visitor badges. Visitor badges shall be worn and visible at all times while on FRCSW work site.
After completion of daily work Contractor personnel shall return visitor badges to FRCSW Quarterdeck at Building 94.

7. Installation: The Govt. shall be responsible for installation, including floor-anchoring, and fixture leveling.

8.Warranty

Upon final acceptance, an industry standard warranty shall be provided, that follows “start-up, system(s) testing, and acceptance/recognition of project completion,” by the Government/FRCSW and final payment acceptance by the Contractor. The warranty shall cover all parts/labor accepted system and equipment. This means, parts will be defect free for one-year under normal operating conditions from the date of final acceptance, not the manufacturing or installation date. Replacement parts under warranty shall be provided to the Government/FRCSW whenever applicable. This shall include: shipping, handling, and, where Technical Support allows, any removal or installation involved in the replacement of said parts. In general, Return Material Authorization (RMA) commercial standard practices shall apply, on the understanding that provided equipment’s failure is catastrophic to FRCSW operations. Additionally, the warranty shall name FRCSW as the owner of the equipment and/or related structures.

Department of the Air Force: Justification for Other Than Full and Open Competition
I. Agency and Contracting Activity (RFO 6.104-1(a)(1)):
Agency: USAF F-15EX (AFLCMC/WAQK)
II. Nature and/or description of the action being approved (RFO 6.104-1(a)(2)):
This initiative aims to develop a self-sufficient, organic maintenance and repair capability for the F-15EX aircraft at the Air
Logistics Complex (ALC). A primary goal is to maximize the reuse of existing F-15 legacy capability and capacity to ensure
cost-effectiveness and efficiency.
To achieve this, a sole-source Indefinite Delivery/Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) contract will be awarded to the PneuDraulics Inc.
This action is justified under FAR 6.302-1 as they are the only responsible source for the Priority Valve, a key component
integrated into the F-15EX's baseline design. The contract will facilitate Depot Activation (DA), a process to establish the
capability for comprehensive overhaul, upgrading, or rebuilding of parts and subassemblies, along with necessary
equipment testing and reclamation, as defined in 10 USC Section 2460. This process involves identifying the necessary
facilities, equipment, materials, and certified personnel to perform depot-level maintenance. Depot activation is a strategic,
long-term investment aimed at ensuring a ready and controlled source of technical competence and resources to respond to
national defense contingencies and other emergency requirements.
This contract covers the procurement of essential parts and associated Depot Activation actions for the Priority Valve,
supporting both current and future F-15EX sustainment needs.
Due to cost and schedule constraints, the IDIQ contract will have a three-year base ordering period with an additional one-
year option. The total ceiling for this Justification and Approval (J&A) is set at $ which is based on a Rough Order of
Magnitude (ROM) estimate for the depot-level repair capability required for Priority Valve repairs.
III. Description of supplies/services required to meet agency needs (RFO 6.104-1(a)(3)):
Establishing an organic, depot-level repair capability requires the strategic delivery of a complete product support package
to the designated ALC(s). This consists of acquiring the required hardware, software, test, technical publication, training,
supply support, packaging, support equipment and data for the designated ALC to repair the depot level repairable(s). To
establish the organic repair capability, delivery of the core infrastructure for depot-level hardware testing and repair is
required. This includes the identification of requirements for, and the subsequent design, build, or purchase of, the
following components: Specialized Test Equipment (STE), Test Program Sets (TPS), and Interface Test Adapters (ITAs).
The United States Air Force (USAF) will provide all common support equipment for this activation effort. Due to proprietary
restrictions stemming from private investment in the development of F-15/F-15EX Line Replaceable Units (LRU), the
government's current ability to establish organic repair of the LRU is not possible. Technical data is restricted by the
manufacturer's intellectual property rights constraints. Therefore, to establish organic repair of the Priority Valve, the
USAF needs to negotiate licenses for only the sensitive data needed to repair the LRU. The repair and maintenance of
Priority Valves require not only the Priority Valve itself but all associated parts/spares and the rights in technical data
necessary to maintain and ensure the software used in the displays functions correctly to support verification of repairs at
designated ALC.
The Priority Valve is a hydro-mechanical flow control device that manages hydraulic fluid distribution to ensure the
operational integrity of primary flight control systems. The valve senses the main hydraulic system's flow rate and pressure.
Under normal system operation, the Priority Valve directs the specified flow rate to the primary flight control circuit. Any
flow exceeding the primary circuit demand is passed downstream to operate secondary, non-flight-critical systems. In the
event of a hydraulic pump failure, line rupture, or a excessive system demand, the valve automatically modulates or
completely shuts off hydraulic flow to the secondary circuits to ensure that that the available hydraulic fluid is dedicated
exclusively to the primary flight control circuit, guaranteeing the pilot retains essential control of the aircraft during low-
pressure or emergency situations.
