Department of the Air Force: Justification for Other Than Full and Open Competition
Primary Contract Purpose
Primarily, this IDIQ will be a contract focused on ensuring the USAF can repair the current and future Priority Valve specs
authorized to be installed on F-15EX aircraft. Incidental to the provision of Priority Valves are field and depot-level support,
engineering necessary to implement future variants within the EX-airframe, provisioning and support equipment. Section IV
of this document explains these requirements in greater detail.
Contract Framework and Competition This IDIQ will allow efficient award of depot activation capabilities associated with
the Priority Valve. The CLIN structure may include separately priced CLINs for intellectual property (IP) rights as negotiated
with the Contractor. The Contract will be asked to include a data rights assertion list which will be provide as part of the RFP
Package sent to the OEM.
Cost Ceiling Justification The requested $ individual J&A ceiling is based on the PO's estimate for the entire Priority
Valve DA IDIQ ordering period, assuming each option is exercised. This ceiling was derived from current programmatic
activities based on in-house cost estimates for future projected DA requirements as explained above.
Cost Exclusions In keeping with the programmatic need to leverage legacy EX hardware, the cost ceiling for this IDIQ
excludes costs associated with qualifying an entirely new Priority Valve solution, implementing that new solution onto
existing EX airframes, altering the production line to install that new solution on future EX airframes, and the stand up of new
DA capabilities for any Priority Valve solution other than the one being awarded under this contract. These duplicative costs
have been excluded for reasons explained in Section IV below.
IV. Statutory Authority Permitting Other Than Full and Open Competition (RFO 6.104-1(a)(4)):
10 U.S.C. 3204(a)(1), Only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements.
V. Rationale for Use of Authority (RFO 6.104-1(a)(5)):
Background
Currently, PneuDraulics Inc. produces the Priority Valves installed on every F-15EX through sole-source procurement and
integration by The Boeing Company (Boeing). PneuDraulics Inc. is the only responsible Original Equipment Manufacturer
(OEM) capable of providing the Priority Valve and associated technical data rights necessary for Depot Activation of the
Priority Valves. Historically, repairs have been contracted to Boeing, who subcontracted with PneuDraulics Inc. for Priority
Valve repairs and maintenance.
PneuDraulics Inc. Priority Valve is fully developed, integrated, and has been certified/qualified for use on all F-15EX aircraft.
The Priority Valve further meets all safety, suitability, and effectiveness requirements necessary for fielding EX aircraft. As the
OEM of the only compliant Priority Valve available to the USAF, PneuDraulics Inc. is the only source in possession of the
technical expertise, technical data, source code, proprietary engineering documentation, and knowledge necessary to fulfill
the delivery and DA requirements the USAF requires to continue fielding EX aircraft without substantial impacts to cost and
schedule.
The risk factors associated with procuring a new organic maintenance repair solution for an Priority Valve that is not the
current Priority Valve provided by PneuDraulics Inc. are as follows:
Integration Complexity
A new OEM must design and qualify a part, requiring the USAF to act as integrator while Boeing incorporates that part into
the aircraft. This process involves drawing updates, technical order updates, and training updates. The complexity increases
if, as is the case with Priority Valves, the part contains software that interfaces with the mission computer, requiring
additional integration activities and a direct contract with Boeing for Operational Flight Program (OFP) updates to achieve
flight clearance.
MMaarrcchh 22002266 PPaaggee 33 ooff 77
Department of the Air Force: Justification for Other Than Full and Open Competition
Interim Support Degradation
The existing OEM has no incentive to continue maintaining OEM Specialized Test Equipment (STE) needed to repair existing
parts under Interim Contractor Support (ICS) or Contractor Logistics Support (CLS) while the USAF waits for new parts to
complete the design, qualification, and integration cycle. This results in degraded performance for maintaining existing
hardware during the transition period.
Depot Activation Continuity
New OEM selection must include the assumption that the new part will undergo depot activation. Otherwise, the USAF will
face the same OEM limitations with the new supplier as currently experienced with existing OEMs.
The challenges above present considerable cost, schedule, and budgetary risks that the USAF cannot expect to overcome via
the issuance of a competitive source selection for a new Priority Valve OEM.
Cost Prohibitions
Procuring and qualifying a new Priority Valve solution would result in substantial cost duplication that the Government
cannot expect to recover by conducting a competitive source selection.
Schedule Constraints
The schedule impacts associated with new Priority Valve qualifications and implementation are unacceptable. The timeline
to award and qualify a new Priority Valve solution includes: 1-2 years for a source selection, 3-5 years for qualification, and an
additional 2-4 years to qualify a new Priority Valve source's facilities, personnel, processes, and procedures.
This entire 6-11 year process would be required if a new Priority Valve OEM is selected. With existing contractual support for
inorganic Depot Activation expiring at the end of FY 2026, any solution other than sole-source award to PneuDraulics Inc.
will result in EX aircraft being grounded during this extended timeline.
PneuDraulic's Unique Position
PneuDraulics Inc. Priority Valve is fully developed, integrated, and has been certified/qualified for use on all F-15EX aircraft.
The Priority Valve further meets all safety, suitability, and effectiveness requirements necessary for fielding EX aircraft. As the
OEM of the only compliant Priority Valve available to the USAF, PneuDraulics Inc. is the only source in possession of the
technical expertise, technical data, source code, proprietary engineering documentation, and knowledge necessary to fulfill
the delivery and DA requirements the USAF requires to continue fielding EX aircraft without substantial impacts to cost and
schedule.
Accordingly, PneuDraulics Inc. is the only viable OEM capable of providing the supplies and services identified in Section III
above without the cost, schedule and budgetary risks explained in this section.
VI. Integrated Market Analysis and Efforts to Solicit Competition (RFO 6.104-1(a)(6), (8), and (10)):
In accordance with FAR Subpart 5.2, a synopsis of the proposed contract action was published on SAM.gov.
Furthermore,market research was conducted to identify all potential sources for this requirement, consistent with the
procedures outlined below.

Department of the Air Force: Justification for Other Than Full and Open Competition
I. Agency and Contracting Activity (RFO 6.104-1(a)(1)):
Agency: USAF F-15EX (AFLCMC/WAQK)
II. Nature and/or description of the action being approved (RFO 6.104-1(a)(2)):
This initiative aims to develop a self-sufficient, organic maintenance and repair capability for the F-15EX aircraft at the Air
Logistics Complex (ALC). A primary goal is to maximize the reuse of existing F-15 legacy capability and capacity to ensure
cost-effectiveness and efficiency.
To achieve this, a sole-source Indefinite Delivery/Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) contract will be awarded to the Aerosonic LLC.
This action is justified under FAR 6.302-1 as they are the only responsible source for the Angle of Attack Transmitter (AoA) -
(LH/RH), a key component integrated into the F-15EX's baseline design. The contract will facilitate Depot Activation (DA), a
process to establish the capability for comprehensive overhaul, upgrading, or rebuilding of parts and subassemblies, along
with necessary equipment testing and reclamation, as defined in 10 USC Section 2460. This process involves identifying the
necessary facilities, equipment, materials, and certified personnel to perform depot-level maintenance. Depot activation is a
strategic, long-term investment aimed at ensuring a ready and controlled source of technical competence and resources to
respond to national defense contingencies and other emergency requirements.
This contract covers the procurement of essential parts and associated Depot Activation actions for the AoA, supporting
both current and future F-15EX sustainment needs.
Due to cost and schedule constraints, the IDIQ contract will have a three-year base ordering period with an additional one-
year option. The total ceiling for this Justification and Approval (J&A) is set at $ which is based on a Rough Order of
Magnitude (ROM) estimate for the depot-level repair capability required for AoA repairs.
III. Description of supplies/services required to meet agency needs (RFO 6.104-1(a)(3)):
Establishing an organic, depot-level repair capability requires the strategic delivery of a complete product support package
to the designated ALC(s). This consists of acquiring the required hardware, software, test, technical publication, training,
supply support, packaging, support equipment and data for the designated ALC to repair the depot level repairable(s). To
establish the organic repair capability, delivery of the core infrastructure for depot-level hardware testing and repair is
required. This includes the identification of requirements for, and the subsequent design, build, or purchase of, the
following components: Specialized Test Equipment (STE), Test Program Sets (TPS), and Interface Test Adapters (ITAs).
The United States Air Force (USAF) will provide all common support equipment for this activation effort. Due to proprietary
restrictions stemming from private investment in the development of F-15/F-15EX Line Replaceable Units (LRU), the
government's current ability to establish organic repair of the LRU is not possible. Technical data is restricted by the
manufacturer's intellectual property rights constraints. Therefore, to establish organic repair of the AoA, the USAF needs
to negotiate licenses for only the sensitive data needed to repair the LRU. The repair and maintenance of AoAs requires
not only the AoA itself but all associated parts/spares and the rights in technical data necessary to maintain and ensure
the software used in the displays functions correctly to support verification of repairs at designated ALC.
The AoAs are critical aerodynamic sensors that measure the angle between the wing's chord line and oncoming airflow to
prevent stalls and ensure flight safety. These sensors, often utilizing heated, pivoting vanes or probes on the fuselage,
transmit real-time data to flight computers, stall warnings, and cockpit displays.
Primary Contract Purpose
Primarily, this IDIQ will be a contract focused on ensuring the USAF can repair the current and future AoA specs authorized
to be installed on F-15EX aircraft. Incidental to the provision of AoAs are field and depot-level support, engineering
necessary to implement future variants within the EX-airframe, provisioning and support equipment. Section IV of this
document explains these requirements in greater detail.

Department of the Air Force: Justification for Other Than Full and Open Competition
Contract Framework and Competition This IDIQ will allow efficient award of depot activation capabilities associated with
the AoA. The CLIN structure may include separately priced CLINs for intellectual property (IP) rights as negotiated with the
Contractor. The Contract will be asked to include a data rights assertion list which will be provide as part of the RFP Package
sent to the OEM.
Cost Ceiling Justification The requested $ individual J&A ceiling is based on the PO's estimate for the entire AoA DA
IDIQ ordering period, assuming each option is exercised. This ceiling was derived from current programmatic activities based
on in-house cost estimates for future projected DA requirements as explained above.
Cost Exclusions In keeping with the programmatic need to leverage legacy EX hardware, the cost ceiling for this IDIQ
excludes costs associated with qualifying an entirely new AoA solution, implementing that new solution onto existing EX
airframes, altering the production line to install that new solution on future EX airframes, and the stand up of new DA
capabilities for any AoA solution other than the one being awarded under this contract. These duplicative costs have been
excluded for reasons explained in Section IV below.

10 U.S.C. 3204(a)(1), Only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements.

Description: This is a presolicitation notice of intent to award a sole-source contract. No reimbursement will be made for any costs associated with providing information in response to this posting. The purpose of this notification is to inform industry of the Government's intent and to gain knowledge of other potentially qualified sources. These adapters are mission-essential hardware required to interface with the government's OEM Instron calibration machine, for which the government does not possess the proprietary technical data package. prospective contractors to qualify Skate Mount Assembly samples.

Giulinistraße 2, S07 67065 Ludwigshafen, Germany, BPA number W912PB-26-A-A002.
The order will be awarded under the authority of the 41 U.S.C. 1901, as implemented in

3. Description of Supplies/Services: Endurance: ≥90 minutes, Range: 15–40 km
Payloads: EO/IR/Thermal, optional EW collect, Frequencies: Documented, encrypted
Portability: ≤3 Soldiers, Cost: ≤$50,000, Compliance: DIU Blue List required
4. Key Features and Capabilities: Fill the ISR gap between short-range FPV and
Brigade ISR assets · Sustain ≥90 minutes of endurance and ≥15 km range Operate on
non-PRC encrypted frequencies (900 MHz, 2.4 GHz) Be three-Soldier portable and cost
less than $50K Carry EO, IR, thermal, and optional EW payloads
5. Development and Availability The drone's development incorporated direct input
from real-world combat experiences, including testing prototypes under battlefield
conditions in Ukraine. It is compliant with Blue UAS and NDAA requirements, ensuring it
meets strict cybersecurity and supply chain standards without components of Chinese
origin. As a direct result of this urgency, and confirmed through extensive market
research, DRONIVO GmbH is the only responsible source capable of satisfying the
agency's requirements. This is based on the convergence of three unavoidable
constraints:
a. A Specific Technical Requirement: The mission requires the salient characteristics
of the EAGLE NXT eBee VISON model. Alternative models offered by other vendors
(e.g., the VESPER) were deemed technically unacceptable, and others (e.g., the
SKYDIO) are on the prohibited list with OMA funds.
b. An Unacceptable Delivery Delay from All Other Sources: Other vendors capable
of sourcing the correct model quoted a excessive lead time of four (4) to five (5) months
due to the requirement to secure export licenses for delivery to Germany. This delay
would directly result in mission failure.

c. A Unique Logistical Advantage: DRONIVO, as an authorized dealer for eBee
VISION systems located in Germany, is the only vendor that can provide the specific,
technically acceptable system within the mission's critical timeline without being subject
to the multi-month export delay.
Disapproval of this justification would force the agency to either procure an unsuitable
system or endure an unacceptable delay that would negatively impact operational
readiness and the execution of the mission.
6. Authority Cited: The statutory authority permitting other than full and open
competition for this acquisition is 41 U.S.C. 1901, as implemented by FAR 12.102
(Restricting competition) under the authority of the simplified acquisition threshold
(SAT). This authority applies to acquisitions of contracted support services / items
valued up to $9 million where limiting competition is justified. Accordingly, the Blanket
Purchase Agreement (BPA) order will be awarded as a sole-source requirement under
the authority of the FAR 12.102 (Restricting competition) and 12.201-1 (Simplified
procedures).
7. Reason for Authority Cited: The agency has an unusual and compelling urgent
need to procure the EAGLE NXT eBee VISON sUAS to support a critical and time-
sensitive mission. A delay in equipping our forces would result in an unacceptable
operational readiness gap and cause serious injury to the Government's mission. The
normal procurement and delivery cycle, estimated at four to five months through
standard competition, is unacceptable.
8. DRONIVO is the only identified source capable of providing the specific Ebee Vision
model that meets the Government's technical requirements and urgent delivery
schedule. Other vendors contacted either offered different drone models that are
unsuitable for the mission or quoted unacceptable delivery times of four to five months.
DRONIVO has the required item available for prompt delivery, making it the only source
that can satisfy this requirement in the required timeframe.
a. Background: The requiring activity has an urgent need for ebee Vision to support
its mission. The specific specifications of this model are essential for operational
success. Market research identified several potential drone suppliers, but upon inquiry,
it was determined that none could meet the Government's specific needs except for
DRONIVO. It is noted that Steven D. Mathias VP Global Sales and Business
Development EagleNXT, provided written confirmation, Subject: Manufacturer
Authorization – Exclusive Dealer for eBee VISION in Germany, that DRONIVO, located
at Giulinistraße 2, S07, 67065 Ludwigshafen, Germany, is hereby authorized as the
exclusive dealer and distributor for eBee VISION systems in Germany. Other vendors
either did not carry the specific Ebee Vision model or were not considered as having
exclusive rights to distribute the supplies. DRONIVO is the only identified vendor that
can provide the exact model required within the Government's delivery timeline.

3
JUNE 2025
CUI//SP-PROCURE//FEDCON
Control Number: G 26-012
b. Alternatives: The primary alternative considered was procuring a similar system
from other vendors. This was deemed not viable for the following reasons:
c. Unsuitable Products: Other vendors offered different drone systems that do not
meet the salient technical characteristics and specifications required for the mission.
d. Unacceptable Delays: Vendors who could potentially source the correct model
quoted delivery timelines of four to five months. Such a delay is unacceptable and
would negatively impact mission readiness.
e. In-house development is not an option due to the lack of technical expertise and
the urgent need for the equipment.
Impact if not approved: Disapproval of this justification would result in an
unacceptable delay of four to five months in acquiring mission-essential equipment. This
would force the agency to either procure an unsuitable system that fails to meet critical
needs or endure a significant delay that would negatively impact operational readiness
and the execution of the mission
9. Efforts to Obtain Competition: Efforts to solicit offers from as many sources as

Procurement Program (S2P2). This market research confirmed that no other source

confirmed DRONIVO is the only source capable of satisfying the Government's urgent
requirement. The research revealed:
a. Unsuitable Alternatives: Vantage Robotics offered their VESPER drone, which
does not meet the salient technical characteristics required.
b. The Astro Max sUAS was considered but does not meet the minimum
specifications required by the MRR ONS. It is a shorter-range quadcopter option suited

JUSTIFICATION AND APPROVAL FOR RESTRICTING COMPETITION (J&A)
FAR 12.102(b)(GSA Class Deviation RFO-2025-12)
1. IDENTIFICATION OF THE AGENCY AND CONTRACTING ACTIVITY

2. NATURE AND/OR DESCRIPTION OF THE ACTION BEING APPROVED
This action is to request the approval of a sole source Purchase Order for the supply of Av-DEC’s antenna gaskets to support
the production of the P-8A Poseidon aircraft.
This Justification and Approval serves to support the procurement as a sole source award for deliverables manufactured by
Av-DEC in accordance with FAR 12.102(b) (GSA Class Deviation RFO-2025-12), Restricting competition.
3. A DESCRIPTION OF THE SUPPLIES OR SERVICES REQUIRED TO MEET THE AGENCY’S NEEDS
(INCLUDING THE ESTIMATED VALUE)

4. AN IDENTIFICATION OF THE STATUTORY AUTHORITY PERMITTING OTHER THAN FULL
AND OPEN COMPETITION
This acquisition will be conducted under 10 U.S.C. 3204(a)(4) and the authority of FAR 12.102(b)(2) (GSA Class Deviation
RFO-2025-12), restricting competition and in accordance with FAR 12.201-1 Simplified procedures (GSA Class Deviation RFO-
2025-12), which allows restricting competition for the purchase of the P-8A spare part components in amounts greater than the
simplified acquisition threshold but not exceeding $9,000,000.00. Each spare part component meets the definition of a
commercial product in accordance with FAR 2.101 (GSA Class Deviation RFO-2025-02) as these items are generally available
for public use with a minor modification not customarily available in the commercial marketplace made to meet Federal
Government requirements.
For restricting competition exceeding the simplified acquisition threshold, the requirements at FAR 12.201-1 (GSA Class
Deviation RFO-2025-12) apply. The need to restrict competition is justified in writing utilizing the format at FAR 6.104-1 (GSA
Class Deviation RFO-2025-06) in accordance with 41 U.S.C. 1901. This justification will be approved at the levels specified in
accordance with FAR 6.104-2(a) (GSA Class Deviation RFO-2025-06) and posted to SAM.gov within fourteen (14) days of
contract award in accordance with FAR 6.301(b) (GSA Class Deviation RFO-2025-06).
5. A DEMONSTRATION THAT THE PROPOSED CONTRACTOR’S UNIQUE QUALIFICATIONS OR THE
NATURE OF THE ACQUISITION REQUIRES USE OF THE AUTHORITY CITED
NAVAIR has a need for the procurement of antenna gaskets for the P-8A Poseidon aircraft, modified from the commercial
aircraft Boeing 737-800ERX. The P-8A Poseidon is the latest maritime, patrol and reconnaissance aircraft designed to secure
the Navy’s future in long-range maritime patrol capability. NAVAIR’s PMA 290 holds the responsibility of maintaining,
repairing, and implementing new aircraft capabilities to the P-8A aircraft fleet for operational use. The P-8A aircraft antenna
gasket was developed for, integrated into, and tested on the P-8A during an extensive, competitively awarded P- 8A system
development and demonstration phase. AvDEC is the sole designer, developer, and manufacturer of the aircraft antenna
gasket for use in the P-8A. AvDEC’s design is proprietary and not based on any generic specification design. Av-DEC is the
only known source with the requisite knowledge of the design, technical data, instruction manuals, installation procedures, and
maintenance data necessary to support/sustain the whole system, fabrication, performance, and operational characteristics of
the antenna gasket capable of meeting the P-8A requirements, and is therefore uniquely qualified to perform the efforts
contemplated under this J&A. Any other supplier would need to have their parts certified, which requires testing and analysis.
Awarding to any other source would disrupt on-going P-8A production and maintenance by delaying the delivery of qualified
and properly integrated antenna gaskets to the P-8A line. The timeline to compete and qualify a second source to fulfill the P-
8A production weapon system requirements is estimated to be approximately four years.
The Department of the Navy issued ‘Authorization of AvDEC Polyurethane Conductive Gaskets on Aircraft Communication /
Navigation Antennas and Static Wick Mounting Bases to Aircraft Aluminum Surfaces to Eliminate Corrosion and Related
Precipitation Static Issues’ dated December 18, 2003, authorizing the use of AvDEC’s antenna gaskets for installation on Navy
and Marine Corps aircraft antenna and static dischargers located on aluminum substrates. The authorization letter further
states the antenna gasket that AvDEC provides is a polyurethane conductive gasket that provides electrical bonding between
aircraft aluminum substrate and the mounting base of aircraft antenna and static discharge mounting bases. This technology
is used to seal and protect components against moisture and subsequent corrosion while at the same time providing a
mechanism for bonding and grounding, eliminating airborne communication precipitation static (P-static) discrepancies caused
by corrosion.
6. A DESCRIPTION OF EFFORTS MADE TO ENSURE THAT OFFERS ARE SOLICITED FROM AS MANY
POTENTIAL SOURCES AS IS PRACTICABLE, INCLUDING WHETHER A NOTICE WAS OR WILL BE
PUBLICIZED AS REQUIRED BY SUBPART 5.2 AND, IF NOT, WHICH EXCEPTION UNDER 5.202
APPLIES DESCRIPTION OF EFFORTS TO ENSURE THAT OFFERS ARE SOLICITED FROM AS MANY
POTENTIAL SOURCES AS PRACTICABLE, INCLUDING IF A NOTICE WILL BE PUBLICIZED AS
REQUIRED BY SUBPART 5.2
The market research conducted by the Contracting Officer and information submitted by the customer for review indicates that only
one (1) source is available. Additionally, the Contracting Officer posted a notice of proposed contract action on December 8, 2025,
to SAM.gov, in which the Government intends to solicit and negotiate with only one (1) source; and no responses were received.
The notice was open for two (2) weeks and closed on December 22, 2025. Also, an email was sent to AvDEC on November 20,
2025, to see if they had any authorized distributors for the P-8A antenna gaskets. On the same day, AvDEC responded that it does
not have any authorized distributors for direct U.S. military sales.
7. A DETERMINATION BY THE CONTRACTING OFFICER THAT THE ANTICIPATED COST TO THE
GOVERNMENT WILL BE FAIR AND REASONABLE
Because this requirement is being restricted, the Government will be utilizing at least two (2) price analysis techniques outlined in
FAR 15.404-1(b) (GSA Class Deviation RFO-2025-15) by which to determine pricing submitted by AvDEC to be fair and
reasonable. These techniques include, but are not limited to the following:

8. A DESCRIPTION OF THE MARKET RESEARCH CONDUCTED (SEE PART 10) AND THE RESULTS OR A
STATEMENT OF THE REASON MARKET RESEARCH WAS NOT CONDUCTED
In accordance with FAR Part 10 (GSA Class Deviation RFO-2025-10), Market research was conducted to evaluate the availability
of AvDEC gaskets in meeting the Government’s need. Based on the NAVAIR’s input, a Notice of Intent (NOI) to negotiate on a
sole-source basis was published to SAM.gov on December 8, 2025, for fourteen (14) days to solicit industry feedback regarding
the gasket requirement. The NOI closed on December 22, 2025, with no responses received. The Contracting Officer also
contacted AvDEC, through email on November 20, 2025, to inquire whether authorized distributors were available for the gaskets.
AvDEC confirmed that it does not have any authorized distributors and that they will quote directly.
9. ANY OTHER FACTS SUPPORTING THE USE OF OTHER THAN FULL AND OPEN COMPETITION
All facts supporting this justification have been provided above.
10. A LISTING OF THE SOURCES, IF ANY, THAT EXPRESSED, IN WRITING, AN INTEREST IN THE
ACQUISITION
The AvDEC antenna gasket is the only product that has been rigorously tested and determined to meet the Government's needs.
There were no responses to the NOI that was posted or inquiries submitted by industry concerning the Government’s intent to sole
source this requirement to AvDEC.
11. STATEMENT OF ACTIONS, IF ANY, THE AGENCY MAY TAKE TO REMOVE BARRIERS TO
COMPETITION
Increasing concerns have emerged regarding potential barriers to competition when access to design, knowledge, and
technical data is required. However, AvDEC is currently the only source capable of meeting the Government’s needs. Prior to
any subsequent procurement, the Government will once again review the market using various methods to assess whether
any other qualified sources are available and are able to meet the Government's requirements.

4. Statutory Authority Permitting Other Than Full and Open
Competition
In accordance with 10 U.S.C. § 3204(a)(1), the supplies
required by NAVSEA are available from only one responsible
source (brand name or equal) and no other type of supplies
will satisfy the requirements.
5. Rationale Justifying Use of Cited Statutory Authority
10 U.S.C. 3204(a)(1) authorizes an agency to use other than
competitive procedures when the supplies needed by the agency
are available from only one responsible source and no other
type of property or services will satisfy the needs of the
agency. As implemented by FAR 6.302-1(c), an agency may
utilize this authority to acquire name brand equipment when
such name brand equipment is essential to the Government’s
requirements, thereby precluding consideration of a product
manufactured by another company. The name brand equipment
covered under this CJ&A is essential to the Navy’s
requirement to maximize fleet-wide commonality across the LSM
class. Procuring alternate equipment would result in
substantial duplication of cost to the Government and
unacceptable delays in fulfilling the Navy’s requirements for
2
CJ&A Number: 22,597
operational readiness, personnel interoperability, and
reduced total ownership cost.
The LSM class will be constructed concurrently across
multiple shipyards using Damen Shipbuilding & Cooperation
B.V. (Damen)’s Landing Ship Transport 100 (LST 100) design.
The LST 100 design is a mature commercial/non-developmental
item (CNDI) design that the Navy selected as the baseline for
the LSM class to avoid unnecessary delays and additional
costs associated with changes to ship designs during
construction. Although some changes during construction are
unavoidable, especially to account for variance across
shipyards, it is imperative that the Navy require specific
brand-name components for critical systems to minimize
changes to the design and provide capability to the fleet as
quickly as possible.
The LST 100 design calls out the specific equipment listed in
Section 3. Requiring use of this equipment during
construction avoids the additional engineering costs for
selection and redesign of major systems within the ship that
using alternative equipment would necessitate. These items
will be considered Class Standard Equipment and common across
all shipbuilders of the LSM, thereby limiting unnecessary
variance between ships and establishing a single, class-wide
logistics and supply chain for the most critical machinery.
Class commonality in this equipment will dramatically reduce
the required variety and volume of spare parts inventory that
the Navy must procure, warehouse, and manage globally. This
directly lowers supply chain complexity, avoids duplicative
procurement actions, and ensures the right parts are
available for the entire fleet, regardless of which shipyard
built the ship.
Furthermore, a common equipment baseline ensures seamless
interoperability of maintenance personnel and procedures
across the entire fleet. Sailors and technicians trained on
one vessel’s propulsion and power systems are immediately
qualified to service any other ship in the class. This
eliminates the significant cost and complexity of developing,
managing, and delivering shipyard-specific training programs,
specialized tools, and unique technical documentation,
thereby increasing crew flexibility and mission readiness.
The long-term savings derived from standardized logistics and
training far outweigh any potential short-term procurement
3
CJ&A Number: 22,597
savings from sourcing alternate components. By minimizing
expenditures on duplicative training pipelines, avoiding a
vastly expanded spare parts inventory, and increasing
operational availability through a proven, globally supported
system, the Navy will achieve a significantly lower total
ownership cost over the lifecycle of the entire ship class.
For these reasons, the Navy has determined that the name
brand equipment listed in Section 3 is essential to the
Government’s requirements and no other equipment can satisfy
the requirement.
6. Description of Efforts Made to Solicit Offers from as Many
Offerors as Practicable
Pursuant to DFARS PGI 206.302-1 the contracting officer
obtained a waiver for the pre-award requirement of a request
for information or a sources sought notice when utilizing FAR
6.302-1 authority. That waiver is a based on the
understanding that multiple offerors may be able to supply
brand name or equal equipment achieved through publicly
disclosing the redacted version of this CJ&A that lists those
brand name or equal items and therefore it is intended to
function as a market survey for subcontracting opportunities.
7. Determination of Fair and Reasonable Costs
The Contracting Officer has determined that the anticipated
cost to the Government for the supplies/services covered by
the brand name or equal CJ&A will be fair and reasonable.
8. Actions to Remove Barriers to Competition
For the reasons set forth in Paragraph 5, NAVSEA intends to
specify the brand name or equal equipment for LSMs under
these contract vehicles. The Government will continue to
monitor sources for the brand name and brand name or equal
items, and if another potential source emerges, will assess
whether the requirements can be competed.

Description: Sources Sought Notice Sources Sought Notice Page 3 of 7 Sources Sought Notice *= Required Field Sources Sought Notice Page 1 of 7 DESCRIPTION This Sources Sought Notice is for informational and planning purposes only and shall not be construed as a solicitation or as an obligation or commitment by the Government. This notice is intended strictly for Market Research. This is a Request for Information only. This is NOT a solicitation for proposals, proposal abstracts, or quotations. The Department of Veterans Affairs Olin E. Teague Veterans Medical Center Surgical Service in Temple, Texas intends to award a BRAND NAME OR EQUAL contract award for the purchase of ENTURO Scope Consumables. The Government is conducting a market survey to help determine the availability and technical capability of qualified service-disabled veteran-owned small businesses, veteran-owned small businesses, small businesses, HUBZone small businesses and/or other large businesses capable of serving the needs identified below. This notice of intent is for open market as well as Federal Supply Schedule items. The purpose of this notice is to gain knowledge of potential qualified sources and their size classification/socioeconomic status (service-disabled veteran owned small business, veteran owned small business, women owned small business, HUB Zone, 8(a), small business or large business, relative to NAICS 334510 Electromedical and Electrotherapeutic Apparatus Manufacturing with a size standard of 1,250 Employees. Responses to this notice will be used by the Government to make appropriate acquisition decisions. A solicitation is not currently available. STATEMENT OF WORK
SURGICAL SERVICES ENDOSCOPE EQUIPMENT AND CONSUMABLES

(BRAND NAME OR EQUAL)
Introduction/Background

The Central Texas Veterans Healthcare System (CTVHCS) requires the purchase of specialized endoscopy equipment and consumables for use with its leased medical scope equipment. This equipment supports diagnostic and therapeutic procedures in the Surgical Services departments, including urology (URO), ear-nose-throat (ENT), and general surgical endoscopy (SE). These consumables are required for facilities in Temple and Austin.  This procurement is crucial for ensuring the uninterrupted and safe performance of medical procedures by providing essential, compatible, and often single-use, accessories. This procurement shall be brand-name or equal in an attempt to maintain compatibility with the leased equipment across multiple CTVHCS facilities. 

The base period for this purchase is for one year, with no optional years to extend the period of performance. 

Statement of Need
To ensure the safe and effective operation of its newly leased scope equipment, the Central Texas Veterans Healthcare System (CTVHCS) must procure additional specialized endoscopy equipment and consumables that are compatible with VA- owned Olympus endoscope lithotripters and flush pumps. Without these specific, often single-use, items—such as specialized forceps, sterilization accessories, and system-compatible components—the advanced equipment would be rendered inoperable, directly jeopardizing patient care and procedural workflows. The objective is to establish a readily available supply chain for these consumables through a competitive process that maximizes participation from Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Businesses (SDVOSBs), thereby ensuring uninterrupted service, upholding the highest standards of patient safety, and promoting seamless interoperability across all relevant CTVHCS facilities.

CLASS JUSTIFICATION AND APPROVAL
FOR USE OF OTHER THAN FULL AND OPEN COMPETITION
1. Contracting Activity
The Naval Sea Systems Command, Shipbuilding Contracts Division (SEA 022).
2. Description of the Action Being Approved
Modification to Contract No. N00024-25-C-2414 with Damen Naval (Damen), De Willem
Ruysstraat 99, 4381 NK, Vlissingen, The Netherlands, to increase the scope of work to include
engineering support for the Medium Landing Ship (LSM) Program and award of a directed
subcontract by the Navy’s Vessel Construction Manager (VCM) for engineering and design
agent support for the future LSM Block 1 procurements. Both the Navy and the Navy’s Vessel
Construction Manager (VCM) have authority to act under this CJ&A. This authority expires on
30 September 2031.
3. Description of Supplies/Services
The proposed class of contract actions will procure engineering and design agent support from
Damen as needed for all LSM Program acquisition efforts. Such efforts include special studies
and engineering changes conducted under Contract No. N00024-25-C-2414 and the Navy’s
VCM contract, which will direct the VCM to subcontract with Damen as the Design and
Configuration Agent for the construction subcontracts awarded by the VCM.
The scope of services to be provided by Damen under this CJ&A includes, but is not limited to:
(cid:120) Design Baseline Management: Establishing and maintaining the authoritative Allocated
Baseline for the McClung-class LSM. This includes managing the Technical Data
Package (TDP) acquired by the Navy and ensuring all design documentation is current
and accurate.
(cid:120) Configuration Control: Serving as the central authority for managing and controlling
the LSM configuration. This involves evaluating, documenting, and approving all
engineering changes, modifications, and deviations from the baseline design to ensure
interoperability and consistency across all vessels built by various U.S. shipyards.
(cid:120) Engineering and Technical Support: Providing subject matter expertise to NAVSEA,
the VCM, and contracted shipyards on all aspects of the LST 100 design. This support is
critical for integrating U.S.-specific command, control, communications, computer, and
combat systems, as well as other government-furnished equipment, into the baseline
design while maintaining the vessel's performance characteristics.
(cid:120) Support to Production: Assisting U.S. shipbuilders in interpreting the LST 100 design,
resolving technical issues, and ensuring that construction methods adhere to the design's
specifications and quality standards.
CJ&A No. 22,569
The total estimated value in the table below includes cost of royalty fees for 15 ships, the cost for
the increased scope under Contract No. N00024-25-C-2414 for Damen to perform special studies
and engineering changes, and the effort to be performed by Damen as the directed Design and
Configuration Agent for the construction subcontracts awarded by the VCM. The Navy’s
minimum needs have been verified by certifying technical and requirements personnel.

4. Statutory Authority Permitting Other Than Full and Open Competition.
10 U.S.C. § 3204(a)(1), only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy
agency requirements.
5. Rationale Justifying Use of Cited Statutory Authority
The Navy has determined that only Damen can provide the required engineering support for the
LST 100 design because it is the original source of the design, and an award to any other
company would result in both a substantial duplication of the cost to the Government and
unacceptable delays in construction of LSM vessels based on the LST 100 design. 10 U.S.C. §
3204(a)(1), as implemented through FAR 6.302-1, authorizes a defense agency to use other than
full and open competition procedures when the supplies or services required by the agency are
only available from one or a limited number of responsible sources, and no other type of supplies
or services will satisfy the agency’s requirements. Per FAR 6.302-1(a)(2)(ii), supplies may be
deemed available only from the original source for follow-on contracts for the continued
development or production of a major system when it is likely that award to any other source
would result in “[s]ubstantial duplication of cost to the Government that is not expected to be
recovered through competition” or “[u]nacceptable delays in fulfilling the agency’s
requirements.” Use of this authority is appropriate when “[t]he existence of limited rights in
data, patent rights, copyrights, or secret processes; the control of basic raw material; or similar
circumstances, make the supplies and services available from only one source.” FAR 6.302-
1(b)(2).
The acquisition strategy for the LSM Block 1 requires a commercial/non-developmental item
(CNDI) design to significantly reduce the risk of cost and schedule growth associated with
design immaturity typically found in new shipbuilding programs. Accordingly, the Navy
conducted extensive market research to identify potential sources for a CDNI design and assess
U.S. shipyard capacity to produce vessels from an “as-designed” configuration. Through this
market research, the Navy identified two viable CNDI vessel designs that would meet the Top-
Level Requirements (TLRs) for LSM Block 1: (1) Non-Development Logistics Support Vessel
2
CJ&A No. 22,569
(NDLSV) (Ref J&A No. 22,216), designed by Bollinger Shipyards Lockport, L.L.C. (Bollinger),
and (2) Damen’s LST 100 (Ref J&A No. 22,217). To determine which design should serve as
the official design basis for the LSM Block 1, the Navy procured the TDPs for both designs (Ref
Contract Nos. N00024-25-C-2413 and N00024-25-C-2414, respectively). Subsequently, on 19
November 2025, the Under Secretary of the Navy for Research, Development, and Acquisition
(ASN (RD&A) selected the LST 100 design as the official design basis for the LSM Block 1 to
enable rapid fielding of a critical warfighting asset and enhance the Navy’s littoral maneuver and
logistics support capabilities.
Although the Navy has already procured the “as-designed” LST 100 TDP and the licensing
agreements necessary to construct vessels based on the design, the TDP will require updates
prior to and throughout the construction process. Accordingly, the Navy requires additional
engineering support to identify elements of the "as-designed" LST 100 design that pose a
material sourcing risk to the build strategy or that are not in compliance with American
regulatory and/or statutory requirements to ensure that the design is as close to production ready
as possible to support the construction of LSMs in American shipyards. Additionally, the Navy
anticipates that the next block of LSM vessels will need design changes to support the Navy and
Marine Corps’ long-term littoral maneuver and logistics support capability requirements, and
therefore, the Navy requires special studies and engineering support to evaluate and update the
LST 100 design for future LSM procurements. Furthermore, because the Navy anticipates that
multiple shipyards will be constructing LSMs concurrently, the design will need continuous
configuration management to reflect the yard-to-yard variations inherent to multi-yard vessel
construction in addition to incorporating standard “as-built” production data. Timely execution
of these engineering services is directly linked to upcoming production readiness activities,
VCM subcontract awards, and initial ship construction milestones. Any delay in design agent
support would have a cascading impact on material procurement, production sequencing, and
shipyard readiness across multiple yards, thereby delaying first ship delivery and degrading the
Navy’s ability to field LSM capability within required operational timelines.
The proposed class of contract actions will provide the necessary expert services to establish,
maintain, and control the LSM's design and configuration baseline throughout the program's
lifecycle. The ultimate deliverable is a stable, mature, and fully documented LSM Block 1
design, enabling multiple U.S. shipyards to proceed with efficient, low-risk production. These
services are essential for the successful execution of the Navy's VCM and multi-shipyard
production strategy.
As the originator, owner, and design agent for the LST 100, Damen is best suited to analyze,
update, and modify the design quickly, both during the production of the LSM Block 1 vessels
and for future LSM procurements. However, the Navy conducted additional market research to
assess whether other companies could provide the required engineering support without
substantial cost duplication or unacceptable delays. Based on this market research, the Navy
determined that using any other design agent would substantially delay the LSM Block 1
construction schedule and cost vastly more than acquiring the engineering support directly from
Damen. Because Damen originated and built the LST 100, the current design is configured for
3
CJ&A No. 22,569
the software and processes used in-house by Damen. Any other company would need to become
familiar with and adapt the design to its own software and processes before beginning the
required engineering support work thereby creating substantial delay to the LSM Block 1 and
duplicative costs for the additional work necessary to adapt the design.
For these reasons, the Navy has decided to award the required engineering support work to
Damen under the authority provided in § 3204(a)(1) to provide the capabilities of the LSM
Block1 to the Fleet as quickly as possible to support the Marine Corps’ operational requirements
without incurring the substantially duplicative costs and unacceptable delays associated with
awarding this work to any other source.
6. Description of Efforts Made to Solicit Offers from as Many Offers as Practicable
The Navy conducted extensive market research to identify potential sources for a non-
developmental landing ship design and assess U.S. shipyard capacity to produce vessels from an
“as-built” configuration. In support of its market research, the Navy released an industry-wide
RFI on 7 January 2025, seeking information on commercially available designs and shipyard
capabilities. The Navy received 14 responses, 13 of which included production recommendations
using nine distinct landing ship designs. However, only two of those identified designs, the
Bollinger’s ND-LSV and Damen’s LST 100 are mature designs that meet the LSM Block 1
TLRs and have already been successfully constructed.
On 19 November 2025, the Under Secretary of the Navy for Research, Development, and
Acquisition selected the LST 100 design as the official design basis for the Medium Landing
Ship (LSM) Block 1 to enable rapid fielding of a critical warfighting asset and enhance the
Navy’s littoral maneuver and logistics support capabilities. The Navy conducted further market
research into companies that could provide engineering support needed through analysis and
production of the LST 100 design. As described in Section 5, the Navy determined that
contracting these services outside of Damen would delay the construction schedule and cost
vastly more than the services provided directly from Damen. The amount of time any other

CONTROLLED UNCLASSIFIED INFORMATION
Single Source Justification (Simplified Acquisition)
Section D: Efforts to Obtain Competition
Market research was conducted to identify sources for the required X-ES chassis. Similar products for the following alternate
sources were evaluated for technical acceptance: Abaco, Annapolis Micro systems, Wakefield Thermal, Elma, Vadatech, Aitech,
and Amphenol. Most chassis do not support the correct Vita standard with several being the older standard(Vita 42) or too new
(Vita 67 & 68). Searches were performed across all mandatory government -wide acquisition contracts, including Quarterly
Enterprise Buy catalog, 2GIT, GSA Advantage, and NASA SEWP. None of these searches yielded positive results. Subsequently,
the program manager contacted the Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM), who confirmed that their products are sold
exclusively through a direct single source channel and are not available via resellers. No Request For information were posted,
due to lack of authorized resellers available. Based on this research, it is determined that a single source procurement is the only
viable method to acquire this product.
Section E: Steps to Preclude Future Single Source or Brand Name Awards
For reasons stated above, it is not anticipated that future acquisitions supporting the F-35 JPO equipment currently in use by the
Air Force could allow for competitive acquisition. However, the government continuously monitors advances in technology. If
changes in the marketplace reveal alternative products capable of satisfying the government's requirements, the government
will write future requirement description suitable for full and open competition.
Section F: Contracting Officer's Determination
I have determined, in accordance with FAR 13.106-1(b)(1), that the circumstances of this contract action deem only a
single source is reasonably available.

Veteran’s Affairs Medical Center in Washington DC (VAMCDC) located at 50 Irving
Street, N.W. Washington D.C. 20422. The 3DE nurse call system will not be integrated
with the facility’s existing nurse call system. The existing system consists of 14 call
buttons in 3 bathrooms. The expansion will include a 4th bathroom along with six
additional calls buttons that will require rough-ins and cable runs to the panel.
LOCATIONS AS SHOWN:
3D-112 (Unisex)
• Replace: 3 call buttons, dome light
• Add: 1 call button
3D-114 (Male)
• Replace: 6 call buttons, dome light
• Add: 3 call buttons

• Add: 1 call button, dome light

• Add: 1 call button

Contractor provides a proposal to include all the necessary materials, labor, and
equipment to complete all required work within all documented areas. Contractor to
reuse existing conduit/penetrations when able and when suitable for the functionality
required by the Government. All existing nurses call cables and equipment to be
removed by Contractor.
This work includes but is not limited to installation of rough ins in tiled bathrooms,
patching walls and ceilings, pulling cables and sealing of hardware necessary to
complete the nurse call system.
The contractor shall provide and install all parts, materials, labor, resources, and
training required to implement and utilize the equipment/system to their fullest
capacity. All items must be covered by manufacturer’s warranty and procured through
a manufacturer-approved distribution channel. A workmanship warranty for a minimum
of 3 years shall be included. A manufacturer parts warranty for a minimum of 1 year
shall be included. Distributers and resellers must be able to document ability to provide
items through manufacturer-approved distribution channels upon request.
4. SPECIFICATIONS.
4.1 EQUIPMENT
Line-Item Description Quantity
Call Buttons 1919
Panels 3
Dome Lights 11 1
4.2 REQUIRED FEATURES:
• All products must meet VHA Mental Health Facilities Design Guide and Mental
Health Environment of Care Checklist (MHEOCC) requirements
• Call buttons must be waterproof and have a gasket within the backplate.
• Dome lights and panels must be flush trim anchored with tamper resistant screws
• All hardware must be anti-ligature
5. SPECIFIC TASKS.
5.1 DELIVERY.
i. All equipment shall be delivered to:
Washington DC VA Medical Center
50 Irving St NW
Washington, DC 20422
ATTN: VHAWAS Equipment Committee
ii. Contract VA Purchase Order (PO) number shall be included with delivery
information (e.g., packing slip).
Note: PO number starts with station code 688 followed by a letter and 5 digits
(e.g., 688A12345)
iii. Delivery Hours: The Warehouse is open to receive deliveries Monday through
Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m., excluding holidays.
iv. Contractor shall coordinate delivery with the on-site Point of Contact (POC) and
provide shipment tracking information.
v. Contractor shall verify delivery date and time with the on-site POC at least 3
business days prior to scheduled delivery.
vi. Delivery is required within 90 days from award of the contract.
5.2 ON SITE PROCEDURES.
i. COVID-19 Screening: All people entering the facility shall be subject to
screening for COVID-19 per the current CDC (Center for Disease Control)
guidelines.
ii. Mask Requirement: All contractors shall wear masks while indoors.
iii. Contract personnel are required to identify themselves as such to avoid creating
an impression in the minds of members of the public that they are Government
Officials.
iv. Time spent on site shall be for a period sufficient to complete the work set forth
in the statement of work.
v. On-site visits shall be scheduled in advance with the designated on-site POC.
vi. Contractors shall check in and out with Biomedical Engineering prior to visiting
the worksite for each day of work.
vii. The VA campus is non-smoking. Contractor personnel are required to comply
with this policy.
viii. Parking: it is the responsibility of the Contractor to park in the appropriate
designated parking areas.
ix. Contractor personnel’s tool bags are subject to inspection.
5.3 INSTALLATION/IMPLEMENTATION.
i. Installation/Implementation will be completed by personnel certified and
knowledgeable with the designated equipment/system.
ii. Installation shall be completed within the period of performance.
iii. Contractors shall be responsible for any Personal Protection Equipment (PPE)
required when performing work on site.
iv. Contractor shall submit all removable media to be used on a VA system to
Biomedical Engineering for scanning with anti-virus software prior to use.
v. In the case of turn-in, exchange, repair, or replacement of equipment containing
hard drives used by the VA, the hard drives shall be removed from the
equipment and remain in possession of the VA (this includes loaned or rented
equipment).
vi. The contractor shall take all necessary precautions to prevent damage to any
government property. The contractor shall report any damage immediately and
shall be assessed current replacement costs for property damaged by the
contractor, unless corrective action is taken. Any damaged material (i.e., trees,
shrubs, lawn/turf, curbs, gutters, sidewalks, etc.) will be replaced in a timely
manner or corrected by the contractor with like materials, at no extra cost to the
government, upon approval of the Contracting Officer.
5.4 TRAINING.
i. Contractor shall be responsible for providing training to clinical staff/users.
ii. Training is to be scheduled in advance with the designated on-site POC.
iii. Education shall be provided prior to and/or at time of installation.
iv. Education professionals shall be certified to provide instruction on the
designated equipment/system.
v. Education curriculum must include operations and set-up, user maintenance,
safety, and user troubleshooting tips.
5.5 INSPECTION AND ACCEPTANCE.
i. Contractor shall conduct a joint inspection with the on-site POC upon
completion of installation.
ii. In the event deficiencies are identified, the contractor shall provide the date
when the identified deficiencies will be addressed if not addressed on the date
of installation. The Contractor shall conduct a joint inspection with the on-site
POC after addressing all deficiencies. All deficiencies identified in the joint
inspections shall be corrected by the Contractor prior to Government
acceptance of the item. Any disputes shall be resolved by the Contracting
Officer.
5.6 DELIVERABLES.
The Contractor shall provide the below documentation for the proposed equipment to
VHAWASEquipmentRequests@va.gov within 10 business days of work completion:
i. Service report.
ii. Warranty information.
iii. Electronic copy of the Operators Manual.
iv. Electronic copies of the complete technical service manuals, including
troubleshooting guides, necessary diagnostic software and equipment
information, schematic diagrams, and parts lists.
6. HOURS OF OPERATION.
DC VAMC’s normal business hours are Monday-Friday, 8:00 am to 4:30 pm, excluding
the Federal holidays observed:
New Year’s Day Labor Day
Martin Luther King’s Birthday Columbus Day
President’s Day Veterans Day
Memorial Day Thanksgiving Day
Juneteenth Christmas Day
Independence Day Any other national holiday as declared by
the President of the United States
7. PERIOD OF PERFORMANCE. Delivery is expected within 90 days of contract award.
8. SAFETY PRECAUTIONS.
a. The Contractor shall comply with all applicable Federal, State and Local legal
requirements regarding workers health and safety. The requirements include, but
are not limited to, NFPA, EPA, and those found in Federal and State Occupational
Safety and Health Act (OSHA) statutes and regulations, such as applicable
provision of Title 29, Code of Federal Regulations (CFR) Parts 1910 and 1926.
Contractor is solely responsible for following/complying with the legal requirements
that apply to activities and shall ensure safe and healthy working conditions for its
employees.
b. Contractor shall assume the responsibility to guard against causing fires and/or
explosions and to protect Government Property, reference NFPA 241 and OSHA
29 CFR 1926.
c. Follow Interim Life Safety Measures (ILSM). Any series of Operational Actions
taken to temporarily reduce hazards posed by Life Safety deficiencies which have
been created by demolition, renovation, or construction works, and which are to
remain in place and in effect for duration of Contract work. Provide interim life
safety measures (ILSM) where fire protection, fire suppression and/or smoke/fire
partitions will be shut down or rendered ineffective during construction. Coordinate
with the VA safety Office through COR. ILSM must be posted outside work area at
all times.
d. The Contractor shall perform the work in a manner consistent with the area security
and fire safety regulations especially with regard to exits and exit way access. All
utility shutdowns shall be coordinated through the COR and not compromise
security, communication or fire safety for occupants.
e. Once construction barriers are in place, Safety & Infection Control will inspect with
the CO/COR to ensure all protective measures are in place to start. After all
Safety, Infection Control, Security, and other things are in place a “Pre-
Construction Checklist Assessment” will be signed by Safety, Infection Control, and
COR. Then the document shall be posted outside of the main entrance door
throughout the duration of the project.
f. The necessary number and appropriate types of portable fire extinguishers are
required per National Fire Protection Association (NFPA) 10 and NFPA 41 must be
provided and be operational.
g. The Contractor must obtain a burn permit from VA Safety Office thru the COR prior
to any cutting, welding, brazing, grinding, and soldering. All permits shall be
prominently displayed outside of the entrance door(s) during all construction.
h. The Contractor shall notify the COR of any Utility Outages, and a Utility Outage
request must be completed by FMS prior to taking any Utilities out of service.
Contractor shall allow ample time for FMS to coordinate and schedule such events.
i. All necessary precautions shall be taken by the contractor to prevent activation of
any existing smoke detectors or sprinkler heads.
j. The Contractor shall at all times keep the work area free from accumulation of
waste materials. Contractor is responsible for the removal of all materials and
debris from the premises utilizing Contractor’s waste bin under the guidance of
state, federal, and local laws and regulations. Use of owner’s waste bins is
prohibited. Upon completing construction, the Contractor shall remove all
temporary facilities and leave the project site in a clean and orderly condition
acceptable to the COR.
k. Any repair of damage caused as a result of this project will be the responsibility of
the Contractor.
9. SECURITY REQUIREMENTS.
All staff that are to work on-site must attend a safety briefing prior to starting work. Staff
must also maintain possession and accountability for all parts and tools brought into
this area at all times. The recommendation is to minimize entry and exit of unit when
possible.

United States Department of Agriculture
Decision to Restrict Competition under the Simplified Acquisition Threshold
Identification Number: 1202SA26Q9001
In accordance with the Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul (RFO) part
12.102 (a), the following documents the decision to restrict competition for this acquisition.
(1) Mission Area and Contracting Activity.
Requisition Number: Pending
Requesting Activity Agency: United Stated Department of Agriculture, Forest Service (FS),
National Technology & Development Program (NTDP)
Contracting Activity: National Interagency Fire Center (NIFC), Incident Procurement Operations
(2) Estimated Value
Less than Simplified Acquisition Threshold (SAT)
(3) Brief Description of Supplies or Services
The DC-7 main parachute is one of the currently approved and required main parachutes for FS
Smokejumper operations as per the FS Standards for Smokejumper Operations. The smoke jumper
program ensures that proficiency is kept on two types of main parachutes to safeguard against the
possibility of having an issue arise with one parachute type and being solely reliant on a single failure
point. Different sizes and types of approved parachutes in the system also provide a mix of flight
characteristics and capabilities which can be more favorable for different size and experience levels of
smoke jumpers.
NTDP requires a one-year replenishment of proprietary parachute components to maintain the
Smokejumper Ram Air Delivery System:
• DC-7 Main Canopy (P/N 811406-0): A 7-cell ram-air canopy.
• MT1S Reserve Canopy (P/N 811306-0): A 5-cell ram-air canopy.
• MT1S Deployment System (P/N 886452-0): Pilot chute and free bag assembly.
A. Suggested Source
Airborne Systems North America of NJ Inc.
5800 Magnolia Ave, Pennsauken, NJ 08109
Unique Entity ID (UEI) WEYALM4WUT46
CAGE Code: 57172
(4) Justification for Restricting Competition and the Basis for that Decision.
A. Explain the unique qualifications/characteristics of the proposed contractor or product and why
no other contractor or product/service can meet the Government's need.
Airborne Systems North America is the sole owner of the proprietary technical data and
manufacturing rights for the DC-7 and MT1S systems. No other domestic source can provide
these specific, safety-certified components. Given the life-safety nature of smokejumper
Page 1 of 2
Rev. 3/4/26
United States Department of Agriculture
Decision to Restrict Competition under the Simplified Acquisition Threshold
Identification Number: 1202SA26Q9001
operations and the lack of authorized alternatives on the FS Approved Equipment List,
Airborne Systems is the only responsible source capable of fulfilling this requirement without
causing a catastrophic delay in mission readiness and an unacceptable risk to personnel.
B. Describe market research conducted and the results or the reason why no market research was
conducted.
Market research included a review of GSA Advantage and general internet searches, which
confirmed other parachute manufacturers exist, none produce the DC-7 or MT1S proprietary

CONTROLLED UNCLASSIFIED INFORMATION
Single Source Justification (Simplified Acquisition)
Section D: Efforts to Obtain Competition
Market research was conducted to identify sources for the required X-ES chassis. Similar products for the following alternate
sources were evaluated for technical acceptance: Abaco, Annapolis Micro systems, Wakefield Thermal, Elma, Vadatech, Aitech,
and Amphenol. Most chassis do not support the correct Vita standard with several being the older standard(Vita 42) or too new
(Vita 67 & 68). Searches were performed across all mandatory government -wide acquisition contracts, including Quarterly
Enterprise Buy catalog, 2GIT, GSA Advantage, and NASA SEWP. None of these searches yielded positive results. Subsequently,
the program manager contacted the Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM), who confirmed that their products are sold
exclusively through a direct single source channel and are not available via resellers. No Request For information were posted,
due to lack of authorized resellers available. Based on this research, it is determined that a single source procurement is the only
viable method to acquire this product.
Section E: Steps to Preclude Future Single Source or Brand Name Awards
For reasons stated above, it is not anticipated that future acquisitions supporting the F-35 JPO equipment currently in use by the
Air Force could allow for competitive acquisition. However, the government continuously monitors advances in technology. If
changes in the marketplace reveal alternative products capable of satisfying the government's requirements, the government
will write future requirement description suitable for full and open competition.
Section F: Contracting Officer's Determination
I have determined, in accordance with FAR 13.106-1(b)(1), that the circumstances of this contract action deem only a
single source is reasonably available.

Description: NOTICE OF INTENT TO AWARD SOLE SOURCE The Air Force Life Cycle Management Center, C-130J Program Branch (AFLCMC/WLNK), intends to award a sole source, Firm-Fixed-Price contract to BAE Systems, located in Austin, TX. This action will be for the manufacture and delivery of the Sanders Technology and Advanced Reduced Instruction Set (STAR) XIII Mission Computers (MCs) in support of the C-130J fleet. The Government requires the procurement of approximately 829 STAR XIII Mission Computers to meet agency requirements and mitigate operational readiness risks associated with the obsolescence of the legacy STAR VII and STAR IX MCs. National Stock Number (NSN): 6610-01-723-6214. Part Number: 697960-13 BAE Systems is the original equipment manufacturer (OEM) and the only known source with the requisite knowledge, experience, and technical data to produce the STAR XIII MCs. The STAR XIII MC hardware is a proprietary system owned and controlled by BAE Systems. The U.S. Government does not possess the technical data, intellectual property, or license rights necessary to support a competitive procurement. Awarding the contract to any other source would result in unacceptable delays in fulfilling the agency's requirements. It is estimated that developing a replacement would take approximately 10 years and cost upwards of $325M, creating a critical capabilities gap and leading to the grounding of C-130J aircraft. BAE Systems maintains the only validated and operational production line for the STAR XIII MCs and possesses an established supply chain, mitigating the risk of production delays. The statutory authority permitting other than full and open competition is 10 U.S.C. 3204(a)(1), as implemented by RFO 6.103-1(b), which states that supplies or services may be procured from only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements. In accordance with DFARS 205.205-71, a Sources Sought Synopsis (Notice ID: STARXIIIMC2025) was posted to SAM.gov from August 18, 2025, to October 3, 2025. No responses indicating an ability to perform the requirement were received from any source other than BAE Systems. This notice of intent is not a request for competitive proposals. However, all responsible sources may submit a capability statement, proposal, or quotation, which shall be considered by the agency. A determination by the Government not to compete this proposed contract based upon responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. Responses must be received within fifteen (15) calendar days of this notice's publication date. Any questions regarding this acquisition should be directed to the Contract Specialists, Tyran Knaff at e-mail: tyran.knaff@us.af.mil or Contracting Officer, Danielle Weeks at e-mail: danielle.weeks@us.af.mil.

STATEMENT OF REQUIREMENTS
Title: Mass Comparator for CHIPS 1.02 - Gas Flow and Properties: Standards and models for flow
metering semiconductor gases at flows from 10 μL/min to 1 L/min
Requiring Lab: Physical Measurement Laboratory (PML)
I. BACKGROUND INFORMATION
The NIST Sensor Science Division’s (SSD) mission is to advance the next genera(cid:415)on of SI-traceable
measurements in dimensional metrology, thermodynamics, op(cid:415)cal radia(cid:415)on, and fluid flow. The Fluid
Metrology Group (FMG) maintains standards for realizing gas flow. This procurement supports CHIPS
project 1.02 for grand challenge 1, where a main deliverable is a “low” flow standard for semiconductor
process gases that will be used to support U.S. manufacturer’s that produce mass flow controllers (MFCs).
The standard will be used to provide physical models for how mass flow controllers behave across various
semiconductor gas species. MFCs measure gas quan(cid:415)(cid:415)es that are delivered to reac(cid:415)on chambers for
surface deposi(cid:415)on or etching reac(cid:415)ons that produce chips. Therefore, the correct stoichiometry is cri(cid:415)cal
to the successful produc(cid:415)on of semiconductor chips. Currently there are no non-commercial labs that
provide SI-traceable flow for semiconductor gases.
To develop best-in-the-world gas flow standards, we need to determine the volumes of gas collec(cid:415)on
vessels with low uncertainty. We do this by weighing the vessel with a fluid that has a known, low-
uncertainty density. Therefore, we need to realize mass with high accuracy through SI-traceable masses
and a best-in-the-world mass comparator. To meet our mission, we need to procure a mass comparator
from the sole source of Me(cid:425)ler Toledo. Without the acquisi(cid:415)on of this laboratory grade mass comparator,
we cannot con(cid:415)nue our mission for SSD or CHIPS.
II. PURPOSE
The purpose of this acquisition is to purchase a 10 kg capacity, 1 mg readability mass comparator of
laboratory grade. We are seeking to sole source a Mettler Toledo brand mass comparator to replace our
30+ year old version that has failed and cannot be repaired. The application of this instrument is in the
chain of SI-traceable measurements that give the volume of gas collection vessels used in gas flow
standards.
III. MINIMUM REQUIREMENTS
The Contractor shall provide a system that meets all technical specifications identified below. All items
shall be new. Used or remanufactured equipment will not be considered for award. Experimental,
prototype, or custom items will not be considered. The use of “gray market” components are not
acceptable. All line items shall be shipped in the original manufacturer’s packaging and include all original
documentation and software, when applicable.

e. Able to fit a 1.5 ft x 1.5 ft footprint excluding any manufacturer provided draft shields
f. Have a “hanging” hook for weighing objects suspended from the bottom.
g. Compatible with the Fluid Metrology Group’s existing software for data acquisition

(I) This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial products or commercial services prepared in accordance with the format in Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO) Part 12 - Acquisition of Commercial Products and Commercial Services as supplemented with additional information included in this notice. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation; quotes are being requested and a written solicitation will not be issued.

(II) The solicitation number is 1333ND26QNB30500941 and this solicitation is a brand name only Request for Quotation (RFQ). This acquisition is being solicited as a total small business set-aside. 

Brand Name Only Justification: 

The NIST Fluid Metrology Group (FMG) maintains standards for realizing gas flow and is building a low flow standard for semiconductor process gases. FMG must determine the volumes of gas collection vessels with low uncertainty. FMG does this by weighing a vessel with a fluid that has a known, low-uncertainty density. FMG has historically used a 30+ year old Mettler Toledo mass comparator model that is no longer supported by Mettler Toledo. A replacement is now required. 

For the purposes of compatibility with existing research methods and reliable comparison of results with existing data, it is necessary to obtain a replacement mass comparator from the same manufacturer. FMG’s project protocols have been designed around the features of the proprietary Mettler Toledo mass comparator and only an instrument with the same properties is compatible with the existing protocols. Further, the FMG uses only Mettler Toledo weigh scales, in addition to the mass comparator, to ensure data compatibility across measurements. Mettler Toledo brand equipment is calibrated in a proprietary fashion and use of any other brand of product will jeopardize continuity of ongoing research data. 
(III) The solicitation document and incorporated provisions and clauses are those in effect through the RFO. 

(IV) The associated North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for this procurement is 334516, Analytical Laboratory Instrument Manufacturing, with a size standard of 1,000 employees.
