DRAFT STATEMENT OF WORK (SOW)
Advanced Instruments Osmo1 Single-Sample Micro-OsmometerClinical Chemistry LaboratoryCentral Arkansas Veterans Healthcare System (CAVHS)Little Rock, AR 72205

PURPOSE
The overall purpose is to establish a purchase contract to provide and install one Advanced Instruments Osmo1 Single-Sample Micro-Osmometer in the Clinical Chemistry Laboratory at Central Arkansas Veterans Healthcare System (CAVHS), 4300 W. 7th St, Little Rock, AR 72205.
This instrument will be installed in the Clinical Chemistry section of Pathology & Laboratory Medicine Service (P&LMS) and used for measurement of osmolality in serum, plasma, urine, and other body fluids to support patient care and meet CLIA and College of American Pathologists (CAP) requirements.
Osmolality testing is required for evaluation of electrolyte and water balance, toxic alcohol ingestion, and other critical clinical conditions. A dedicated microosmometer is necessary to support current and projected testing volumes, reduce turnaround time, and improve accuracy and reliability of results.

SCOPE
The Contractor shall provide, transport, install, and test all listed equipment. All products must meet all salient characteristics defined in this section.
All equipment and installation must meet manufacturer and VA specifications.
The Contractor shall furnish all materials, parts, tools, supplies, equipment, facilities, and services required for delivery and installation of the supplies and equipment.
The Contractor is responsible for any missing parts and components not included in order to carry out the installation.
The equipment will be a benchtop, singlesample microosmometer intended for clinical laboratory use to perform quantitative osmolality measurements using the freezing point depression method.
Specifications / Salient Characteristics
Advanced Instruments Osmo1 Single-Sample Micro-Osmometer (or equal)
Benchtop/tabletop instrument.
Uses freezing point depression principle for osmolality measurement.
Accepts serum, plasma, urine, and other body fluid samples as validated by the laboratory.
Sample volume requirement: 20 microliters or less per test.
Measuring range: at least 0–2000 mOsm/kg H₂O.
Resolution: 1 mOsm/kg H₂O.
Accuracy and precision must meet or exceed manufacturer’s stated performance claims across the analytical range.
Throughput sufficient to support routine clinical workload (minimum 20 patient samples per hour).
Integrated or attached touchscreen user interface.
Integrated barcode scanner for sample identification.
Integrated thermal printer for result printouts.
Capability to store results and operator information internally.
Connectivity ports (e.g., Ethernet and/or USB) for potential interface to a laboratory information system (LIS) or middleware, if requested by the facility.
Operation on standard electrical power (100–240 V, 50/60 Hz) with appropriate power cord.
Compact footprint suitable for placement on existing chemistry laboratory bench space.
Instrument must support 2 or 3point calibration and calibration verification to meet CLIA requirements.
Instrument must include onscreen or documented stepbystep guidance for calibration, quality control, and routine operation.
Consumables and Accessories
The Contractor shall provide initial consumables and accessories required for installation and validation, which shall include, at a minimum:
Microsample test kit(s) suitable for the Osmo1 instrument.
Calibration standards at multiple osmolality levels (e.g., low, mid, high) sufficient to perform initial calibration and calibration verification.
Quality control materials at low, normal, and high osmolality levels.
Any special sample holders, probes, or tools required for routine operation and maintenance.
Installation and validation of unit operation
The Contractor is responsible to set up and install the unit in final operating condition.
The Contractor must ensure the unit operates according to the manufacturer’s specifications upon completion of installation.
The Contractor shall assist, as needed, during the site’s verification/validation process (e.g., performance checks, calibration, and quality control setup) to confirm the instrument meets expected performance.
Onsite training of designated staff
The Contractor shall provide onsite training of designated Clinical Chemistry staff in routine operation, calibration, quality control, and basic maintenance of the unit within two weeks of installation.
When requested by the facility, the Contractor shall provide onsite training of designated Biomedical Engineering staff in basic maintenance and troubleshooting of the unit.
Documentation
The Contractor shall provide complete sets of operator’s manuals (hard copy and digital, if available).
The Contractor shall provide technical/service manuals, if available (hard copy and/or digital).
The Contractor shall provide manufacturer recommended maintenance schedules and procedures.

DELIVERY AND INSTALLATION
DELIVERY
The Contractor shall deliver all equipment to:
Central Arkansas Veterans Healthcare System (CAVHS)
2200 Fort Roots Drive (Building 182)
North Little Rock, Ar. 72114

Final location of instrument:
Central Arkansas Veterans Healthcare System (CAVHS)Pathology & Laboratory Medicine Service – Clinical Chemistry Laboratory4300 W. 7th St. Little Rock, AR 72205
Deliver materials in the manufacturer’s original sealed containers with brand name marked thereon.
Package to prevent damage or deterioration during shipment, handling, storage, and installation. Maintain protective covering in place and in good repair until removal is necessary.
Deliver specified items only when the site is ready for installation work to proceed.
Store products in dry conditions inside enclosed facilities, if storage at the VA is required prior to installation.
Any Governmentrequested delayed delivery up to 90 days after the initial delivery date shall be at no additional cost to the Government.
A predelivery meeting may be conducted prior to initial negotiated delivery date for verification of delivery and installation dates.
Delivery and installation will be coordinated through the Contracting Officer’s Representative (COR).
INSTALLATION
Install all equipment to manufacturer’s specifications while maintaining Federal, State, Local, and VA safety standards.
All work shall be completed between 8:00 a.m. and 4:30 p.m., Monday through Friday, excluding Federal holidays.
If there is an operational conflict with installation, night or weekend installation may be required. The Government will provide a minimum 72hour notice of change of installation hours.
The Contractor shall coordinate all deliveries, staging areas, installations, and parking arrangements with the COR.
The Contractor shall remove all related shipping debris and clean up any construction associated with delivery and installation of the specified items. The Contractor shall remove all packaging from the VA premises.
The Contractor shall be responsible for any damage to the building that occurs due to Contractor error or neglect.
SITE CONDITIONS
There shall be no smoking, eating, or drinking inside the hospital at any time.
The Contractor shall comply with all CAVHS infection control, safety, and access requirements while on site.

INSPECTION AND ACCEPTANCE
The Contractor shall conduct a joint inspection with the COR upon delivery and installation of equipment.
The Contractor shall provide dates of completion of punch list items and replacement parts and/or shortship items from the manufacturer.
The COR shall ensure all work is completed satisfactorily prior to acceptance. Disputes shall be resolved by the Contracting Officer.
Final acceptance will be contingent upon:
Successful installation and operation of the osmometer without critical errors.
Completion of onsite training for designated staff.
Successful completion of the laboratory’s verification/validation studies demonstrating that performance meets manufacturer and laboratory requirements.

DELIVERABLES
Equipment
One Advanced Instruments Osmo1 Single-Sample Micro-Osmometer (or VAapproved equivalent), fully assembled and operational.
All standard accessories required for operation as described under Salient Characteristics.
Consumables
Initial lot of reagents, standards, and controls sufficient to complete installation and method validation and to support approximately one month of routine testing (or as agreed to by the facility).
Documentation
Operation and Maintenance Manuals
Complete sets of operator’s manuals (hard copy and digital, if available).
Technical/service manuals, if available (hard copy and/or digital).
Maintenance Schedule
Compilation of all manufacturerrecommended maintenance and operation materials packaged in binder(s) or electronic format to the COR upon completion of installation.
Training
Documentation of onsite operator training (attendance sheets, topics covered).

OPERATOR TRAINING
The Contractor shall provide onsite training of the equipment to the users. Operator training shall be coordinated with the CAVHS COR after installation is complete.
Training shall include, at a minimum:
Instrument startup and shutdown procedures.
Sample handling and testing workflow.
Calibration and calibration verification procedures.
Quality control procedures, including interpretation of QC results and corrective actions.

Department of the Air Force: Justification for Other Than Full and Open Competition
to be installed on F-15EX aircraft. Incidental to the provision of EFHDs are field and depot-level support, engineering
necessary to implement future variants within the EX-airframe, provisioning and support equipment. Section IV of this
document explains these requirements in greater detail.
Contract Framework and Competition
This IDIQ will allow efficient award of depot activation capabilities associated with the EFHD. The CLIN structure may include
separately priced CLINs for intellectual property (IP) rights as negotiated with the Contractor. The Contractor will be asked to
include a data rights assertion list which will be provide as part of the RFP Package sent to the OEM.
Cost Ceiling Justification
The requested $ individual J&A ceiling is based on the program office's estimate for the entire EFHD DA IDIQ ordering
period, assuming each option is exercised. This ceiling was derived from current programmatic activities based on in-house
cost estimates for future projected DA requirements as explained above.
Cost Exclusions
In keeping with the programmatic need to leverage legacy EX hardware, the cost ceiling for this IDIQ excludes costs
associated with qualifying an entirely new EFHD solution, implementing that new solution onto existing EX airframes,
altering the production line to install that new solution on future EX airframes, and the stand up of new DA capabilities for
any EFHD solution other than the one being awarded under this contract. These duplicative costs have been excluded for
reasons explained in Section IV below.
IV. Statutory Authority Permitting Other Than Full and Open Competition (RFO 6.104-1(a)(4)):
10 U.S.C. 3204(a)(1), Only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements.
V. Rationale for Use of Authority (RFO 6.104-1(a)(5)):
Background
Currently, Astronautics Corporation of America produces the EFHDs installed on every F-15EX through sole-source
procurement and integration by The Boeing Company (Boeing). Astronautics Corporation of America is the only responsible
Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) capable of providing the EFHD and associated technical data rights necessary for
Depot Activation of the EFHDs. Historically, repairs have been contracted to Boeing, who subcontracted with Astronautics
Corporation of America for EFHD repairs and maintenance.
Astronautics Corporation of America EFHD is fully developed, integrated, and has been certified/qualified for use on all
F-15EX aircraft. The EFHD further meets all safety, suitability, and effectiveness requirements necessary for fielding EX
aircraft. As the OEM of the only compliant EFHD available to the USAF, Astronautics Corporation of America is the only
source in possession of the technical expertise, technical data, source code, proprietary engineering documentation, and
knowledge necessary to fulfill the delivery and DA requirements the USAF requires to continue fielding EX aircraft without
substantial impacts to cost and schedule.
The risk factors associated with procuring a new organic maintenance repair solution for an EFHD that is not the current
EFHD provided by Astronautics are as follows:
Integration Complexity
A new OEM must design and qualify a part, requiring the USAF to act as integrator while Boeing incorporates that part into
the aircraft. This process involves drawing updates, technical order updates, and training updates. The complexity increases
if, as is the case with EFHDs, the part contains software that interfaces with the mission computer, requiring additional
integration activities and a direct contract with Boeing for Operational Flight Program (OFP) updates to achieve flight
clearance.
Interim Support Degradation
MMaarrcchh 22002266 PPaaggee 33 ooff 77
Department of the Air Force: Justification for Other Than Full and Open Competition
The existing OEM has no incentive to continue maintaining OEM Specialized Test Equipment (STE) needed to repair existing
parts under Interim Contractor Support (ICS) or Contractor Logistics Support (CLS) while the USAF waits for new parts to
complete the design, qualification, and integration cycle. This results in degraded performance for maintaining existing
hardware during the transition period.
Depot Activation Continuity
New OEM selection must include the assumption that the new part will undergo depot activation. Otherwise, the USAF will
face the same OEM limitations with the new supplier as currently experienced with existing OEMs.
The challenges above present considerable cost, schedule, and budgetary risks that the USAF cannot expect to overcome via
the issuance of a competitive source selection for a new EFHD OEM.
Cost Prohibitions
Procuring and qualifying a new EFHD solution would result in substantial cost duplication that the Government cannot
expect to recover by conducting a competitive source selection.
Schedule Constraints
The schedule impacts associated with new EFHD qualifications and implementation are unacceptable. The timeline to award
and qualify a new EFHD solution includes: 1-2 years for a source selection, 3-5 years for qualification, and an additional 2-4
years to qualify a new EFHD source's facilities, personnel, processes, and procedures.
This entire 6-11 year process would be required if a new EFHD OEM is selected. With existing contractual support for
inorganic Depot Activation expiring at the end of FY 2026, any solution other than sole-source award to Astronautics
Corporation of America will result in EX aircraft being grounded during this extended timeline.
Astronautics' Unique Position
Astronautics Corporation of America EFHD is fully developed, integrated, and has been certified/qualified for use on all
F-15EX aircraft. The EFHD further meets all safety, suitability, and effectiveness requirements necessary for fielding EX
aircraft. As the OEM of the only compliant EFHD available to the USAF, Astronautics Corporation of America is the only
source in possession of the technical expertise, technical data, source code, proprietary engineering documentation, and
knowledge necessary to fulfill the delivery and DA requirements the USAF requires to continue fielding EX aircraft without
substantial impacts to cost and schedule.
Accordingly, Astronautics Corporation of America is the only viable OEM capable of providing the supplies and services
identified in Section III above without the cost, schedule and budgetary risks explained in this section.
VI. Integrated Market Analysis and Efforts to Solicit Competition (RFO 6.104-1(a)(6), (8), and (10)):
In accordance with FAR Subpart 5.2, a synopsis of the proposed contract action was published on SAM.gov.
Furthermore,market research was conducted to identify all potential sources for this requirement, consistent with the
procedures outlined below.
Regulatory Requirement
DFARS PGI 206.302-1(d) states that "When utilizing the authority at FAR 6.302-1, the Contracting Officer shall post a request
for information or a sources sought notice, and shall include the results of this inquiry in the justification required by FAR
6.303. This requirement to post may be waived by the Head of the Contracting Activity, or designee. The waiver authority
may not be delegated lower than a general or flag officer or a member of the Senior Executive Service."
Market Research Conducted
In fulfillment of this requirement, the Government conducted two separate market research inquiries via SAM.gov to identify
sources capable of meeting the full scope of the Government's needs.
MMaarrcchh 22002266 PPaaggee 44 ooff 77
Department of the Air Force: Justification for Other Than Full and Open Competition
Broad-Scope RFI: A Request for Information (RFI) was posted for 60 days (1 May - 28 June 2025) to identify sources capable
of providing depot-level maintenance and repair services for a variety of F-15EX components, including the EFHD.
Targeted RFI: A second, more targeted RFI was posted for 14 days (3 Dec - 16 Dec 2025) specifically seeking sources for their
integrated EFHD requirement, encompassing both immediate depot repair services and the elements required for a full
Depot Activation.
Results of Market Research
The comprehensive market research effort confirmed that no viable alternative sources exist.
No respondent to either RFI was able to demonstrate the existing capability to perform depot-level repair of the F-15EX
EFHD. Further, no respondent could demonstrate possession of, or a viable path to obtaining, the necessary proprietary
technical data, OEM-certified engineering expertise, and source code required to establish an organic DA capability.
The results of this inquiry affirm that Astronautics Corporation of America, as the OEM, is the only source with the unique
qualifications, proprietary data, and technical expertise required to perform both the immediate depot repair services and to
provide the essential support needed to establish a permanent, organic government depot solution.
VII. Determination of Fair and Reasonable Cost (RFO 6.104-1(a)(7)):
The Contracting Officer is responsible for evaluating, determining, and documenting the anticipated contract cost/price is
fair and reasonable in accordance with RFO Subpart 15.4, Contract Pricing.
VIII. Any Other Facts Supporting the Justification (RFO 6.104-1(a)(9)):
Contracting Officer Assessment
The F-15EX Contracting Officer has determined that the Government can obtain and negotiate a fair and reasonable price for
the EFHD requirement defined in Section III above if acquired from Astronautics Corporation of America on a sole-source
basis.
Analysis and Evaluation Support
Thorough technical, price, and cost analyses will be performed as necessary by the F-15 System Program Office (SPO) with
assistance from the Air Force Life Cycle Management Center (AFLCMC) Pricing Division, the Defense Contract Audit Agency
(DCAA), and the Defense Contract Management Agency (DCMA). The F-15EX program may utilize the DCMA Integrated Cost
Analysis Team (ICAT) for technical evaluation, pricing evaluation, and negotiation support, if warranted.
The undersigned Contracting Officer has determined that the anticipated cost to the Government for this acquisition of full
DA capability will be determined fair and reasonable.
This determination will be based on a comprehensive analysis of the contractor's proposal, as outlined below:
Comprehensive Government Cost Analysis
The SPO, with expert support from the Air Force Life Cycle Management Center (AFLCMC) Pricing Division, the Defense
Contract Audit Agency (DCAA), and the Defense Contract Management Agency (DCMA), will perform a thorough technical
and cost analysis of the contractor's proposal. This analysis will evaluate the reasonableness of all proposed costs for both
the recurring depot repair services and the non-recurring engineering and data deliverables associated with the Depot
Activation effort.
Final Negotiation and Verification
The Contracting Officer will use the results of the comprehensive government cost analysis as the primary basis for
negotiating a final, binding price.
Market Research Conducted
MMaarrcchh 22002266 PPaaggee 55 ooff 77
Department of the Air Force: Justification for Other Than Full and Open Competition
In accordance with DFARS PGI 206.302-1(d), the Program Office conducted comprehensive market research to identify all
potential sources for the required EFHD depot repair and sustainment services. This research included two separate Requests
for Information (RFI) posted on SAM.gov:
Broad RFI: A 60-day RFI (1 May - 28 June 2025) was published to survey the industrial base for sources capable of providing
depot-level maintenance for a wide range of F-15EX avionics, including the EFHD.
Targeted RFI: A subsequent 14-day RFI (3 Dec - 16 Dec 2025) was published, focusing specifically on sources for the
integrated EFHD requirement.

As a result of this extension, the overall ordering period on this contract is November 2017 to
October 2030, or 13 years. In accordance with Defense Federal Acquisition Regulation
Supplement (DFARS) 217.204 (e)(i)(C), the ordering period may not exceed 10 years unless the
head of the agency determines in writing that exceptional circumstances require a longer
ordering period; and (iii) requires Senior Procurement Executive (SPE) approval before issuing
an order that is expected to extend more than one year beyond the 10-year limit. Exceptional
circumstances exist here to justify extending the ordering period because of
a need to extend the existing contract to allow for the
potential transfer of AN/TPY-2 scope to the Army. Further details are contained in section 5 of
this J&A. The execution of this J&A by the SPE serves as the written approval to exceed the 10-
year ordering limit in accordance with DFARS 217.204(e)(iii).
3. Description of the Supplies and/or Services Required to Meet the Agency’s Needs
(including the estimated value) (FAR 6.303-2(b)(3)). The TBSX requires:
 Test Antenna Equipment Unit (AEU) with Spares Replenishment: This is a
procurement for a dedicated, non-tactical AEU for domestic and FMS element level
testing. This Test AEU will enable hardware and software upgrades to be developed and
verified without impacting warfighter missions, resulting in a more mature product and
reduced risk of operational downtime.
.
 Continuation of AN/TPY-2 Development: The RDC supports ongoing development
activities necessary to maintain and enhance the AN/TPY-2 radar’s critical mission of
acquiring, tracking, and discriminating threat missiles in the early, midcourse, and
terminal flight phases. A key part of maintaining the mission assets is obsolescence
mitigation and technology insertion: the AEU refurbishment program provides a
planned refurbishment of an operational asset yielding improved performance and
increased service life.
 Float AEU: An operational AEU spare is required to mitigate downtime when a unit
experiences AEU failure. The Float AEU temporarily takes the place of an AEU that
will be returned for depot-level refurbishment.

4. Statutory Authority Permitting Other than Full and Open Competition (FAR 6.303-
2(b)(4)). The statutory authority permitting other than full and open competition is 10 U.S.C.
3
J&A No: 24-0020
Amendment No: REQTB2500035
3204(a)(1) as implemented by Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 6.302-1(a)(2)(ii)(B),
“Supplies may be deemed to be available only from the original source in the case of a follow-on
contract for the continued development or production of a major system or highly specialized
equipment, including major components thereof, when it is likely that award to any other source
would result in unacceptable delays in fulfilling the agency’s requirements.”
5. Demonstration of Contractor’s Unique Qualifications or the Nature of the Acquisition
Requires use of the Authority Cited (FAR 6.303-2(b)(5)).
Raytheon possesses a deep understanding of the AEU’s intricate design, extensive expertise in
performance and interface requirements, and robust system test and integration facilities essential
for rapidly designing and successfully testing the non-tactical test antenna. A key factor in
mitigating schedule risk is the direct inclusion of OEM-produced components and software, such
as GaN TRIMMs, AC/DC Converters, and Common X-Band Software.
Raytheon is actively developing these new and
emerging requirements and will integrate the Test AEU into the Hardware-in-the-Loop
architecture established at their OEM facility and other test facilities. As the original product
developer for the X-Band Radar for MDA for over 25 years, Raytheon possesses the highly
specialized technical expertise and infrastructure required to meet the Agency’s requirements
within the required timeline.
An aging fleet, high operational tempo, and long lead procurement factors contribute to the
necessity to process AEU refurbishments in a timely manner. Without an AEU refurbishment
program, operational units would incur unacceptable downtime. Delays in starting an AEU
refurbishment program induces increased risk of unacceptable downtime due to lack of an AEU
replacement when the operational unit fails.
For the Test AEU, Float AEU and AEU refurbishment requirement sets, a new contractor would
face a significant learning curve, including performing design analyses, verifying technical data
packages, creating prototypes, and developing rigorous testing regimen to ensure compatibility
and performance.
Furthermore, due to
ongoing development and obsolescence efforts, a complete Technical Data Package
4
J&A No: 24-0020
Amendment No: REQTB2500035
incorporating the current system configuration, including a logistic support package, is currently
unavailable.
For the development requirements set, the software is built using a concurrent development
approach, with successive increments dependent on existing capabilities. Hardware is
continually assessed for obsolescence mitigation. The technical data for the current
configuration directly informs the development for the subsequent configuration. Software
builds are released approximately every two years and continual maintenance activities exist for
fielded software. A new contractor would face a significant learning curve and infrastructure
investment to establish the necessary processes and facilities to develop, integrate, and maintain
the software. Disruption and delays in the build cycle induces increased risk of not achieving
performance requirements within the expected cycle update schedule.
In the aggregate, the requirements set has benefitted from the single performer approach.
Raytheon, though currently on separate contracts for Development, Sustainment, and Production,
continually provides integration across these domains to yield efficient support for ongoing
actions. For the upcoming production oriented Test and Float AEU, the established Production
team will implement existing processes and infrastructure to yield products consistent with prior
system deliveries. For the refurbishment task, the logistics support, production, and development
teams will coordinate to identify repair/replace, spares, production, and development non-
recurring engineering necessary for the refurbishment. For the development task, especially
hardware obsolescence tasks, the development and production teams will collaborate to design,
build, and source replacement solutions. The teams’ crosstalk, expertise, established
infrastructure, and processes are vital to achieving the outcomes in the expected timeframe and
budget.
Raytheon and its supply chain have production lines and processes that meet MDA Quality,
Safety and Mission Assurance (QSMA) requirements. If a source other than the incumbent is
awarded a contract to build this hardware, that source would need approximately 18 months to
complete the MDA QSMA Directorate’s Production Readiness Validation Program before
commencing production. The Test and Float AEUs will be designed to host the most applicable
builds of software and will be based on the most recent hardware configuration. A new
contractor’s build using released data and vetted production processes would result in an older
configuration and later delivery than required. Factors such as verifying/certifying quality
inspection processes and ensuring capability to comply with regulations introduce schedule risk.
An additional schedule risk is introduced by the time needed to integrate a third-party radar into
the AN/TPY-2 test program executed by Raytheon. A series of acceptance and verification
events would require four to six months after providing the radar to Raytheon.
In conclusion, Raytheon’s existing expertise, established production and development
capabilities, and proven track record assures the Government that the delivered products will be
available within the schedules required. Award to any other source would result in unacceptable
delays in fulfilling the agency’s requirements.
6. Efforts to Obtain Competition (FAR 6.303-2(b)(6)). To ensure compliance with FAR
6.303-2(b)(6), the Agency continues to assess opportunities for future competition in support of
5
J&A No: 24-0020
Amendment No: REQTB2500035
AN/TPY-2, by conducting market research which is used to determine if sources capable of
satisfying the agency’s requirements exist. The CO will use market research conducted within
18 months before the award, if the information is still current, accurate, and relevant.
As required by FAR 5.201, the proposed contract action notice will be published, and any bids or
proposals received will be considered. Upon approval of this J&A, a redacted version will be
posted to Sam.gov for 15 days along with a notice of Intent to Sole Source.
a. Effective competition. There is no effective competition anticipated for this
acquisition.
b. Subcontracting competition. The RDC includes FAR Clause 52.244-5, Competition
in Subcontracting, which requires Raytheon to select subcontractors on a competitive basis to the
maximum practical extent with objectives and requirements of the contract. MDA will also take
steps to promote competition by increasing small business participation to grow and train small
businesses for future opportunities. This includes challenging the contractor to achieve goals
above historical performance with contract requirements for small business participation and
commitment plans for first and second tier subcontractors.
7. Determination of Fair and Reasonable Cost (FAR 6.303-2(b)(7)). In accordance with
FAR 15.403, the CO has determined that certified cost or pricing data will be required. This
determination is based on the fact that the anticipated contract value exceeds the Certified
Cost or Pricing Data threshold , and a preliminary assessment indicates that none
of the exceptions outlined in FAR 15.403-1(b) are applicable. Specifically, adequate price
competition is not anticipated, and the highly specialized nature of the required supplies and
services precludes classification as commercial items.
To proactively prepare for potential negotiations and ensure a fair and reasonable price, the
CO will engage the Defense Contract Audit Agency (DCAA) to conduct a comprehensive
review of Raytheon’s accounting practices and cost allowability. This DCAA review will
provide a detailed understanding of Raytheon’s cost structure and identify any potential areas
of concern that may warrant further scrutiny. Simultaneously, the CO will consult with the
Defense Contract Management Agency (DCMA) to assess Raytheon’s estimating system and
cost realism, gathering valuable insights into the contractor’s pricing methodologies and
ensuring that proposed costs are supported by sound estimating practices. These early
interactions with DCAA and DCMA are deemed essential for establishing a well-informed
and defensible government negotiation position.
Further bolstering the government’s ability to assess price reasonableness, the program office
has requested an Independent Government Cost Estimate (IGCE). The IGCE is developed by

Title: SPRRA226R0062 HELLFIRE SPARES � LOCKHEED MARTIN SOLE SOURCE
Solicitation number: SPRRA226R0062
PSC: 6920; NAICS: 336413
Description: THERE IS NO SOLICITATION AVAILABLE AT THIS TIME. REQUEST FOR A SOLICITATION WILL NOT RECEIVE A RESPONSE. This Sources Sought Synopsis (SSS) is in support of Market Research being conducted by the Defense Logistics Agency to identify potential manufacturing/supply sources, and if future efforts can be competitive or Set Aside for Small Business. The proposed North American Industry Classification Systems (NAICS) Code is 336413 and has a corresponding Size Standard of 1250 employees. This SSS is to notify companies that the Defense Logistics Agency, Redstone Arsenal, Alabama, is seeking qualified sources for the acquisition of: GUIDE SEC MISSILE, NSN: 6920-01-551-4067, Part Number 76100645 applicable to the Hellfire Missile weapon system. The technical data for this part has undergone full screening per the DFARS PGI 217.7506, Spare Parts Breakout Program. This item has been assigned AMC/AMSC Code 3P and must be acquired, for the second or subsequent time, directly from the actual manufacturer. The rights to use the data needed to purchase this part from additional source(s) are not owned by the Government and cannot be purchased, developed, or otherwise obtained. It is uneconomical to reverse engineer this part. This code is used in situations where the Government has the data but does not own the rights to the data. As a result, this acquisition is currently being procured under Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 6.302-1(a)(2) having only a limited number of responsible sources. The Government is interested in all businesses to include 8(a), small business and small disadvantaged business, Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned, Hubzone, and Women-Owned small business concerns. All offerors must meet prequalification requirements in order to be eligible for award. The U.S. Army Combat Capabilities Development Command Aviation & Missile Center�s (AvMc DEVCOM) System Readiness Directorate (SRD), Sustainment Division (SD) is the engineering source authority (esa). Firms that recognize and can produce the required item described above are encouraged to identify themselves. Firms are encouraged to seek source approval in order to compete for future solicitations by contacting the contract team. The closing date annotated is an estimated date and may be adjusted dependent upon the date of release for solicitation; however, the solicitation will not close prior to the date stated above. Foreign Firms are reminded that all requests for solicitation must be processed through their respective embassies. The contractor shall be capable of successfully performing and complying with any and all special requirements in accordance with the terms and conditions set forth in the solicitation annotated above, at the unit prices established at time of a contract award. The contractor will be responsible for recurring and nonrecurring engineering services associated with becoming a qualified source. The contractor will also be responsible for all aspects of the manufacturing/production process, including but not limited to: supply chain management, logistics, forecasting of parts, long-lead parts procurement, material forecasting, obsolescence issues and final delivery of assets as well as any and all additional costs incurred resulting from contract performance. DISCLAIMER: THIS SSS IS ISSUED SOLELY FOR INFORMATIONAL AND PLANNING PURPOSES. IT DOES NOT CONSTITUTE A SOLICITATION (REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL OR REQUEST FOR QUOTATION) OR A PROMISE TO ISSUE A SOLICITATION IN THE FUTURE AND SHALL NOT BE CONSTRUED AS A COMMITMENT BY THE GOVERNMENT. RESPONSES IN ANY FORM ARE NOT OFFERS AND THE GOVERNMENT IS UNDER NO OBLIGATION TO AWARD A CONTRACT AS A RESULT OF THIS ANNOUNCEMENT. NO FUNDS ARE AVAILABLE TO PAY FOR PREPARATION OF RESPONSES TO THIS ANNOUNCEMENT. ANY INFORMATION SUBMITTED BY RESPONDENTS TO THIS TECHNICAL DESCRIPTION IS STRICTLY VOLUNTARY. THIS ACQUISITION MAY CONTAIN TECHNICAL DATA WHOSE EXPORT IS RESTRICTED BY THE ARMS EXPORT CONTROL ACT (TITLE 22, USC., SEC 2751 ET SEQ) OR THE EXPORT ADMINISTRATION ACT (TITLE 50, USC., APP 2401-2402) EXECUTIVE ORDER 12470. ARMS EXPORT INFORMATION CANNOT BE RELEASED OUTSIDE THE UNTIED STATES WITHOUT PRIOR APPROVAL OF THE GOVERNMENT.

Title: 4610--EON ROVER ALX Dialysis Water Transport System (Portable Reverse Osmosis) - Brand Name or Equal
Solicitation number: 36C24226Q0485
PSC: 4610; NAICS: 333310
Award:
Description: DESCRIPTION THIS IS A SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE ONLY. The purpose of this sources sought is to conduct market research to support the procurement and installation of three (3) Evoqua EON® Portable Reverse Osmosis (RO) Water Purification System with ROVER® ALX Dialysis Water Transport System Brand Name or equal for the East Orange VA Medical Center. This notice serves to survey the market in an attempt to ascertain whether or not sources are capable of providing the requested equipment and services. This notice allows potential contractors/vendors to submit a non-binding statement of interest and documentation demonstrating their capability. The sources sought effort is intended to assess industry capabilities and develop/support the intended direction of acquisition planning. The Network Contracting Office 02 (NCO 02) is requesting responses from qualified business concerns; the qualifying NAICS code for this effort is 333310 Commercial and Service Industry Machinery Manufacturing. This sources sought is to gain knowledge of potential qualified sources and their size classifications (Service Disabled/Veteran Owned Small Business (SDVOSB/VOSB), Hub zone, 8(a), small, small disadvantaged, woman owned small business, or large business) relative to NAICS 333310. Responses to this notice, will be used by the Government to make appropriate acquisition decisions. After review of the responses to this notice, a solicitation announcement may be published. Responses to this notice are not considered adequate responses to any corresponding solicitation announcement. All interested offerors will have to respond to the solicitation announcement in addition to responding to this notice. The Department of Veterans Affairs is seeking vendors who can provide the required water treatment system per the attached schedule. The vendors must demonstrate the ability to meet all requirements for this notice. See attached schedule. INSTRUCTIONS: Submit a brief description, no more than three (3) pages (including cover letter) that demonstrates how your company can provide the requested services that are required in the attached draft schedule. Include past experience in providing this requirement to the VA, other Government (Federal or State) agency, or for a private facility. If your firm believes it possesses an equal item, please state so in your response. Pricing is NOT required. Please specify your availability and your address. The attached schedule and salients is a draft, and is NOT finalized. If any portions seem unclear, prohibited, and/or you are unsure about the draft description of the requirement please list your comments and/or concerns in your response so they can be addressed. PLEASE INDICATE WHETHER YOU HOLD A GSA FEDERAL-SUPPLY SCHEDULE CONTRACT THAT COVERS THESE SERVICES AND, IF SO, THE CONTRACT NUMBER. Provide BUSINESS SIZE AND SOCIO-ECONOMIC STATUS; (a) Indicate whether your business is large or small (b) If small, indicate if your firm qualifies as a small, emerging business, or small disadvantages business (c) If disadvantages, specify under which disadvantaged group and if your firm is certified under Section 8(a) of the Small Business Act (d) Indicate if your firm is a certified Service-Disabled Veteran Owned Small Business (SDVOSB) or Veteran Owned Small Business (VOSB) (g) Include the SAM UEI of your firm. (h) State whether your firm is registered with the System for Award Management (SAM) at http://www.sam.gov and/or the VetCert Registry at https://search.certifications.sba.gov/. If not, please NOTE that any future solicitation could only be awarded to a contractor who is registered in SAM and to receive award based on VOSB or SDVOSB status you must be registered in the VetCert Registry (i) provide current commercial pricing for all items listed in the attached schedule and any applicable discounts. (j) link to the respondent s General Services Administration (GSA) schedule, or attached file of same, if applicable (k) citation of any current or past customers (i.e., within the past two (2) years) to include contract number, point of contact telephone number or e-mail address; and (l) other material relevant to establishing core competencies of the firm. Vendors shall include authorization letters from the OEM if they do not manufacture the needed items. Response is due by 16:00 EST April 03, 2026. Please submit e-mail responses to Myra Florisa N. Green, at email address: Myra.Green2@va.gov . Your response should include a STATEMENT OF CAPABLILITY, GSA SCHEDULE INFORMATION (if available), SAM UEI, BUSINESS SIZE, AND SOCIO-ECONOMIC STATUS information as explained above. Please use SS 36C24226Q0485 RESPONSE - [YOUR FIRM S NAME] Dialysis Water Transport System in the subject line of your email. This notice is to assist the VA in determining sources only. NOTES: Issuance of this notice does not constitute any obligation whatsoever on the part of the Government to procure these supplies or services, or to issue a solicitation, nor to notify respondents of the results of this notice. No solicitation documents exists at this time; however, in the event the acquisition strategy demonstrates that GSA is a viable option for procuring a solution, the RFQ shall be posted to GSA eBuy where only those firms who currently hold a GSA Schedule with the applicable SIN will be able to respond. The Department of Veterans Affairs is seeking neither quotes nor accepting unsolicited quotes, and responses to this notice cannot be accepted as offers. Any information the vendor considers proprietary should be clearly marked as such. The U.S. Government will not pay for any information or administrative costs incurred in response to this RFI. Statement of Work (SOW) Background The Department of Veterans Affairs Medical Center (VAMC) East Orange, NJ requires portable dialysis water purification systems to support patient care in compliance with VA and FDA standards. Scope Supply and install three (3) EON®-ROVER® ALX kits Part # W3T591409 Brand Name or Equal. Each kit includes Evoqua EON® Portable Reverse Osmosis (RO) Water Purification System with ROVER® ALX Dialysis Water Transport System or equal. Each kit includes the RO system, transport system, two spare carbon block filter cartridges, installation, startup, and training. Salient Characteristics Maximum Product Flow Rate at 77°F: Up to 0.4 gpm (1.5 lpm) Nominal Recovery Rate: 50% Dry Weight: 65 lbs (29.5 kg) Operating Voltage: 115/230 V, 60/50 Hz, 15/7.5 amps Dimensions: Width 8.5 (21.6 cm), Depth 22.5 (57 cm), Height 24 (61 cm) pH Range: Operating 2.0 11.0; Cleaning 1.0 12.0 Inlet Pressure (Dynamic): Min 5 psi (0.34 bar), Max 120 psi (8.3 bar) Inlet Water Flow: Min 1.5 gpm (5.7 lpm) Total Hardness: <10 grains (pH dependent) Silt Density Index (SDI): <5 Total Chlorine: <0.1 ppm Training ½-day onsite clinical training for up to 8 staff. 1-day onsite technical training for up to 8 staff 1-hour System orientation immediately after setup. Place of Performance East Orange VA Medical Center 385 Tremont Avenue East Orange, NJ 07018 Delivery shall be FOB Origin. Vendor is responsible for installation and startup at VAMC East Orange, NJ. Warranty Vendor shall provide a minimum 12-month warranty covering parts and labor. Warranty excludes misuse or improper installation. Equal Product Requirements Any proposed equal product must meet or exceed all salient characteristics, include equivalent installation, training, and support services, and comply with VA dialysis water standards.

Description: Under the authority FAR 6.103-1, the United States Air Force has issued a Sole Source Justification for the Smart Shooter (SMASH) Fire Control System (FCS). This requirement includes five SMASH X4 units for the M4 rifle, a 12-month set of spare parts and special test equipment for maintenance, 1 SMASH 2000LE for M4, 1 SMASH CAST, and associated shipping and delivery to Spangdahlem Air Base, Germany. matters.title: ES-MCAT Mirror Shipping Crate
matters.text:
Federal notice (Justification), NATIONAL AERONAUTICS AND SPACE ADMINISTRATION.NATIONAL AERONAUTICS AND SPACE ADMINISTRATION.NASA JOHNSON SPACE CENTER
Title: ES-MCAT Mirror Shipping Crate
Solicitation number: 80JSC025PA006
PSC: 6650; NAICS: 811210
Description: The Orbital Debris Program Office (ODPO) at NASA Johnson Space Center operates and maintains the 1.3-m ES-MCAT telescope at Ascension Island Auxiliary Airfield (AAF). The primary objective of the ES-MCAT mission is to extend observations of orbital debris in geosynchronous orbit (GEO) to smaller/fainter objects than can be tracked by the Department of Defense (DoD). The current mirror coating has suffered rapid degradation due to a combination of environmental effects. Therefore, the mirror needs to be recoated as soon as possible and earlier than expected due to the poor quality of the coating that was previously applied. After the mirror has been recoated by Viavi Solutions, it needs to be shipped back to Ascension Island. The original shipping container degraded severely upon arrival at Viavi�s location and it is no longer useable. The vendor will now be required to rebuild a new container that will fit the mirror and be able to withstand up to 30g�s of force. The rationale supporting the use of 10 U.S.C. 3204(a)1 is because Viavi is the only known source available that has the requisite knowledge, experience, staff, tooling, and capacity to meet the requirement of both recoating it to the prescribed specifications and building the necessary shipping container. Viavi already has the mirror in its possession and it is the only vendor available to handle the mirror and maneuver it into a new container without disrupting the clean room environment the mirror must be stored in after it is recoated. Introducing a new company at this juncture introduces unknown contaminants into the cleanroom environment, which could introduce unknown contaminants onto the mirror surface after it has been recoated. In order for Viavi to guarantee a perfect coating, it must be the vendor that maintains control of the mirror, which also means controlling the manufacturing of the shipping container and the transfer of the mirror into the new container.

attachments.text:
NATIONAL AERONAUTICS AND SPACE ADMINISTRATION
JOHNSON SPACE CENTER (JSC)
JUSTIFICATION FOR OTHER THAN FULL AND OPEN COMPETITION
(JOFOC)
For
80JSC025PA006
1. Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 6.303-2(b)(1) – Identification of the agency and
the contracting activity, and specific identification of the document as a “Justification
for other than full and open competition.”
This document is a justification for other than full and open competition prepared by
National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA) JSC Office of Procurement.
The procuring agency is the National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA) and the
contracting activity is the JSC Projects Procurement Office (BH).
2. FAR 6.303-2(b)(2) – The nature and/or description of the action being approved:
This justification provides the rationale for contracting by other than full and open
competition to increase the value of a sole-source contract to Viavi, Inc. for the purpose of
recoating and creating a shipping container the primary mirror of the Eugene Stansberry
Meter Class Autonomous Telescope (ES-MCAT) deployed on Ascension Island.
3. FAR 6.303-2(b)(3) – A description of the supplies or services required, to meet the
Agency’s needs (including the estimated value):
The Orbital Debris Program Office (ODPO) at NASA Johnson Space Center operates and
maintains the 1.3-m ES-MCAT telescope at Ascension Island Auxiliary Airfield (AAF). The
primary objective of the ES-MCAT mission is to extend observations of orbital debris in
geosynchronous orbit (GEO) to smaller/fainter objects than can be tracked by the Department
of Defense (DoD). The telescope’s components are regularly exposed to high humidity and
sea spray conditions due to its location on Ascension Island, resulting in a need to recoat the
primary mirror every few years. The current mirror coating has suffered rapid degradation
due to a combination of environmental effects and an inferior-quality coating applied by the
previous coating vendor in 2022. Observations are no longer useful to achieve ES-MCAT’s
primary objective, leading to a lack of data available for building and validating orbital
debris models. Therefore, the mirror needs to be recoated as soon as possible and earlier than
expected due to the poor quality of the coating that was previously applied. After the mirror
has been recoated by Viavi Solutions, it needs to be shipped back to Ascension Island. The
original shipping container degraded severely upon arrival at Viavi’s location and it is no
longer useable. The vendor will now be required to rebuild a new container that will fit the
mirror and be able to withstand up to 30g’s of force. The total amount of the services are
estimated to cost $390,356.00 (including the additional amount of $8,000 for the container),
1

as indicated by an informal quote by Viavi based on the revised Statement of Work. The
final mirror product will be delivered 4 weeks after receipt of tooling and approval of the
qualification, which is approximately nine months After Receipt of the Order (ARO).
4. FAR 6.303-2(b)(4) – An identification of the statutory authority permitting other than
full and open competition:
The statutory authority permitting other than full and open competition is 10 U.S.C.
3204(a)1, as implemented by FAR 6.302-1 Only one responsible source and no other
supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements.
5. FAR 6.303-2(b)(5) – A demonstration that the proposed contractor’s unique
qualifications or the nature of the acquisition requires use of the authority cited:
The rationale supporting the use of 10 U.S.C. 3204(a)1 is because Viavi is the only known
source available that has the requisite knowledge, experience, staff, tooling, and capacity to
meet the requirement of both recoating it to the prescribed specifications and building the
necessary shipping container. Viavi already has the mirror in its possession and it is the only
vendor available to handle the mirror and maneuver it into a new container without
disrupting the clean room environment the mirror must be stored in after it is recoated.
Introducing a new company at this juncture introduces unknown contaminants into the
cleanroom environment, which could introduce unknown contaminants onto the mirror
surface after it has been recoated. In order for Viavi to guarantee a perfect coating, it must be
the vendor that maintains control of the mirror, which also means controlling the
manufacturing of the shipping container and the transfer of the mirror into the new container.
6. FAR 6.303-2(b)(6) – A description of the efforts made to ensure that offers are solicited
from as many potential sources as practicable, including whether a notice was or will be
publicized as required by Subpart 5.2 and, if not, which exception under 5.202 applies:
A notice to the Government Point of Entry (GPE) website (Sam.gov) on January 7, 2026
whereby the Contracting Officer notified industry of this requirement under NAICS code
321920. The notice closed on January 14, 2026 at 12:00pm CST. The notice received no
viable options, only general questions/inquiries. This solidifies that no other source is
available or responsible to meet this requirement, satisfying the requirements found in FAR
6.302-1.
7. FAR 6.303-2(b)(7) – A determination by the contracting officer that the anticipated cost
to the Government will be fair and reasonable:
The Contracting Officer’s signature on this document indicates that the Contracting Officer
has determined that the anticipated cost to the government will be fair and reasonable. The
Contractor shall be required to submit a proposal to be evaluated and negotiated by the
Government. Prior to execution of the contractual instrument, a proposal analysis will be
performed. The proposal analysis will ensure that the final agreed-to price for the contract

action is fair and reasonable. The proposed price will be compared to historical prices paid to
determine that the price proposed is in-line with industry averages and factoring in any
potential inflation costs against the Consumer Price Index (CPI) data, in accordance with
FAR 15.404-1(b)(2)(ii).
8. FAR 6.303-2(b)(8) – Description of the market research conducted, and the results, or a
statement of the reasons market research was not conducted (e.g., urgent, and
compelling requirement):
A notice to the Government Point of Entry (GPE) website (Sam.gov) on January 7, 2026
whereby the Contracting Officer notified industry of this requirement under NAICS code
321920. The notice closed on January 14, 2026 at 12:00pm CST. The notice received no
viable options, only general questions/inquiries. This solidifies that no other source is
available or responsible to meet this requirement, satisfying the requirements found in FAR
6.302-1 and FAR Part 10.
9. FAR 6.303-2(b)(9) – Any other facts supporting the use of other than full and open
competition:

A notice of NASA’s intent to award this sole-source action was synopsized on the GPE

supplies or services required:
The new container being procured as an addition to this JOFOC is expected to last 10-20
years. If a new container is ever needed, additional market research will be conducted to

Section C - Description/Specifications/Statement of Work
STATEMENT OF WORK
for
AN/SPN-43C Rotary Coupler Overhaul
1.0 Introduction
The AN/SPN-43C is the Navy's marshalling air traffic control (ATC) radar system used on all aircraft carriers and
amphibious assault ships for vectoring aircraft into final approach. The rotary coupler, which is a part of the AN/SPN-43C
system, requires overhaul. The Naval Air Warfare Center Aircraft Division (NAWCAD) Webster Outlying Field (WOLF)
has been tasked to overhaul two rotary couplers for AN/SPN-43C.
2.0 Background
In accordance with the OE-138A/SPN-43A Antenna Group Overhaul and Repair Manual, the rotary couplers must be
replaced or sent back to the depot for overhaul. The original rotary coupler was manufactured by ITT Gilfillan and
overhauled / repaired by Mesa Microwave. Mesa Microwave was the sole Depot Overhaul Point (DOP) in 2001.
Afterwards, Kevlin was appointed as the sole DOP and overhauled Mesa rotary couplers. Kevlin has since started
manufacturing new rotary couplers and is often labeling the units as "Beyond Economical Repair" (BER). The Navy
Supply system is in short supply of these rotary couplers and cannot afford to discard any assets that may be salvageable.
3.0 Scope
To repair a total of two rotary couplers for AN/SPN-43C within 28 weeks after receiving Government Furnished Property
(GFP).
4.0 Tasks

Title: SOLE SOURCE - Procurement of Test Program Sets (TPS) and Automated Test Equipment (ATE) for AN/ZPY-3 Multi-Function Active Sonar (MFAS) Shop Replaceable Assemblies (SRAs)
Solicitation number: N0016425GJW77_JobOrder0002
PSC: 5826; NAICS: 334511
Description: Naval Surface Warfare Center (NSWC) Crane has a requirement to procure Test Program Sets (TPS) and Automated Test Equipment (ATE) to support depot repair testing of AN/ZPY-3 Multi-Function Active Sonar (MFAS) Shop Replaceable Assemblies (SRAs). New TPS and ATE solutions will streamline multiple configurations and mitigate Diminishing Manufacturing Sources and Material Shortages (DMSMS) for legacy TPS solutions. The new TPS solutions will support organic depot level repair for applicable AN/ZPY-3 MFAS SRAs at the government-designated location defined herein as Fleet Readiness Center Southeast (FRCSE). This effort provides for all non-recurring engineering to manufacture and develop applicable TPS software and hardware and hosting ATE. The following table shows the list of SRAs that will require the contractor to deliver a complete list of TPS and the associated ATE for. Table 1: Planned FRCSE Depot SRA Capability UUT Description/Name: Auxiliary Synchronizer, Programmed Part Number(s): 218K154G05 ; 218K154G04 UUT Description/Name: Power Supply Aux Part Number(s): 820R045G03 ; 820R045G02 UUT Description/Name: Power Converter Assembly Part Number(s): 820R055G04 UUT Description/Name: Array Driver Part Number(s): 824R658G06; 824R658G05 UUT Description/Name: ECA, Beam Steering Control, Programmed Part Number(s): 331K120G01 UUT Description/Name: Wideband WFG, Programmed Part Number(s): 130K374G02 UUT Description/Name: 270 Volt Power Converter Part Number(s):139K983G03 UUT Description/Name: ECA, Programmed, SYNC/CBI Part Number(s): 130K389G02 UUT Description/Name: Reference Generator Part Number(s):130K380G05 UUT Description/Name: NB Waveform Gen Part Number(s): 130K369G02 UUT Description/Name: Dual RF Receiver Part Number(s): 218K022G01 UUT Description/Name: Digital Power Supply Part Number(s): 139K985G03 UUT Description/Name: Synthesizer Part Number(s): 130K364G02 UUT Description/Name: WBIF Receiver Part Number(s): 218K020G06 ; 218K020G09 UUT Description/Name: Analog Power Supply Part Number(s): 139K987G02 This effort includes the acquisition of ATE, ancillary equipment, and the development and delivery of one set of TPS hardware for each of the 15 required SRAs identified in the table above. The proposed contract action is for the procurement of supplies which the Government intends to solicit and negotiate with one source, Northrop Grumman Systems Corporation 1580 W Nursery Road, Linthicum Heights, MD 21090 under the authority of FAR 6.302-1(a)(2) (statutory authority 10 U.S.C 3204(a)(1)), only one responsible source. The requirement is being solicited on a sole source basis because Northrop Grumman Systems Corp is the Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) and they are unwilling to sell the complete data package to the Government to allow for full and open competition. In addition, parts from any other vendor would result in extensive duplication of costs to include re-engineering, re-certification, environmental qualifications to the government that is not expected to be recovered through competition, and unacceptable delays in fulfilling agency requirements through any other source. All responsible sources may submit a capability statement, proposal, or quotation, which shall be considered by the agency. Federal notice (Solicitation), DEPT OF DEFENSE.DEPT OF THE NAVY.NSWC CRANE
Title: SOLE SOURCE � cPCI BACKPLANES
Solicitation number: N0016426Q0093
PSC: 5998; NAICS: 334111
Description: N0016426Q0093 � SOLE SOURCE � cPCI BACKPLANES � FSG 5998 � NAICS 334111 ISSUE DATE 17-MAR-2026 � CLOSING DATE 25-MAR-2026 � 11:00 PM Eastern Time ITEM DESCRIPTION- Naval Surface Warfare Center (NSWC) Crane has a requirement for for a quantity of ten (10) Compact Peripheral Component Interconnect (cPCI) Backplanes from the Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM), Atrenne Computing Solutions, LLC (Part Number 9292809-01 REV C), with a required delivery time of 38 weeks from the date of award. The proposed contract action is for the supplies or services for which the Government intends to solicit and negotiate with one source, limited sources or brand name only Atrenne Computing Solutions, LLC of Brockton, Massachusetts, cage code 51398, under the authority of FAR 12.201-1 for simplified acquisition of commercial supplies. This is being solicited on a sole source only basis because the cPCI Backplanes are major components of the AN/SPS-73A(V)12 Radar System providing power distribution. The radar system is used for short-range, two-dimensional, surface search and navigation to provide contact range and bearing information. The OEM part number being purchased has been specifically tested to ensure compatibility and operational equivalence for the AN/SPS-73A(V)12 radar system. If the Government was to purchase cPCI backplanes from a source other than Atrenne Computing Solutions, the parts would require testing and evaluation to determine compatibility within the AN/SPS-73A(V)12 systems. The testing and evaluation would take approximately one to two years and cost the government in excess of $750,000. These costs would not be recovered in a competitive procurement. All responsible sources may submit a capability statement, which shall be considered by the agency. However, a determination by the Government not to compete with this proposed contract based upon responses to this solicitation is solely within the discretion of the Government. Information received will normally be considered solely for the purpose of determining whether to conduct a competitive procurement. Contractors must be properly registered in the System for Award Management (SAM). Offerors may obtain information on SAM registration and annual confirmation requirements by calling 866-606-8220 or via the internet at https://sam.gov. This solicitation is being issued pursuant to the procedures FAR 12.201-1 as a written Firm Fixed Priced Request for Quotes . Synopsis exception FAR 5.202(a)(13) applies and Solicitation Number N0016426Q0093 is hereby issued as an attachment hereto. All changes to the requirement that occur prior to the closing date will be posted to Contract Opportunities on https://sam.gov/. It is the responsibility of interested vendors to monitor https://sam.gov/ for any amendments, which may be issued to this solicitation. For changes made after the closing date, only those offerors that provide a quote will be provided any changes/amendments and considered for future discussions and/or award. Offers shall be e-mailed to rose.m.brown44.civ@us.navy.mil. All required information must be received on or before 25-MAR-2026 � 11:00 PM Eastern Time.

matters.title: Notice of Intent to Award a Sole-Source Contract to TCS Inc. for Servo Motors
matters.text:
Federal notice (Special Notice), DEPT OF DEFENSE.DEPT OF THE AIR FORCE.FA8222  AFSC OL H PZIE
Title: Notice of Intent to Award a Sole-Source Contract to TCS Inc. for Servo Motors
Solicitation number: 15394
PSC: 3410; NAICS: 335999
Description: Notice of Intent to Award a Sole-Source Contract to TCS Inc. for Servo Motors 1. Action This is a notice of intent to award a sole-source contract; it is not a request for competitive proposals. The 520th Software Engineering Squadron (SWES), supporting its Telemetry Antenna Control (TAC) program, intends to solicit and negotiate a firm-fixed-price contract exclusively with TCS Inc. 2. Requirement The Government requires the following item, for which it does not possess the necessary manufacturing data or specifications: Description: Servo Motor, 400/480 VAC Part Number: 303661-31 3. Authority and Justification The statutory authority permitting this action is FAR 13.106-1(B) (1) "Soliciting from a single source. (1) For purchases not exceeding the simplified acquisition threshold. (i) Contracting officers may solicit from one source if the contracting officer determines that the circumstances of the contract action deem only one source reasonably available (e.g., urgency, exclusive licensing agreements, brand-name or industrial mobilization)". Kollmorgen is the Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) of the required servo motors and TCS Inc. is the only authorized vendor for the motors. The Government does not possess the technical data package or intellectual property rights required to have this item manufactured by any other source. A new source would require significant time and investment to reverse-engineer, test, and receive source approval, which would result in unacceptable delays to the program. 4. Submission of Information All responsible sources may identify their interest and submit a capability statement in response to this notice. All responses received within five (5) business days of this notice's publication will be considered by the Government. Your response must demonstrate the capability to provide the exact part number listed above. 5. Disclaimer A determination by the Government not to compete with this proposed contract based on responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. The award will not be delayed for the purpose of evaluating new sources or pending source approval.

Section A: General Contract Information
Is this a Bridge Action as defined in the AF Bridge Action Reduction Plan? Yes No

Estimated Contract Cost (including Options):
Section B: Description of the Supplies/Services Required
The 520th Software Engineering Squadron (SWES), as part of its telemetry antenna control (TAC) program, requires the purchase
of new antenna servo motors. This acquisition is a critical component of a larger project to upgrade the 50-foot telemetry
tracking antennas used for rocket launches in Florida. The current antenna control systems, specifically the Microcomputer
Buffer System (MBS), Telemetry Radar Input Output (TRIO), and Telemetry Radar Acquisition Computer (TRAC), are obsolete and
have been identified as sustainment worst actors. To ensure the Long Range Telemetry System (LTRS) can continue providing
telemetry support to users such as Navy T&E, this project will address the control and drive systems of the four TAA-50 assets at
Jonathan Dickinson Missile Tracking Annex (JDMTA). These upgrades, including the new servo motors, will sustain their
functionality and ensure the antenna systems can continue interfacing with existing systems for serial pointing data and the
transport of Range User and/or Range Safety data.
Motor, 400/480 VAC
PN: 303661-31
Qty: 4 Ea
Price:
Total Estimated Cost:
Delivery is not to exceed 90 days ARO
Section C: Justification for Soliciting from a Single Source or Brand Name
FAR 13.106-1(B) (1) "Soliciting from a single source. (1)For purchases not exceeding the simplified acquisition threshold.
(i)Contracting officers may solicit from one source if the contracting officer determines that the circumstances of the contract
action deem only one source reasonably available (e.g., urgency, exclusive licensing agreements, brand-name or industrial
mobilization)".
The 520th Software Engineering Squadron (SWES) requires the immediate, single-source procurement of new antenna servo
motors for its telemetry antenna control (TAC) program.
To use any other brand is not possible; it would force a complete system redesign,
nullifying the government's existing investment in 16 identical motors and costing an estimated $1 million in redesign and re-
procurement costs. Therefore, this specific motor is the only viable path forward to prevent project failure and ensure mission
sustainment.

Federal notice (Solicitation), DEPT OF DEFENSE.DEPT OF THE NAVY.NSWC CRANE
Title: SOLE SOURCE � LATCH ASSEMBLIES

PSC: 1560; NAICS: 332721
Description: N0016426Q0066 � SOLE SOURCE � LATCH ASSEMBLIES � PSC 1560� NAICS 332721 Issue Date: 11-MAR-2026 � Closing Date: 23-MAR-2026 � 11:00 p.m. Time Eastern ITEM DESCRIPTION- Naval Surface Warfare Center (NSWC) Crane has a requirement for an initial purchase of a quantity of 200 Latch Assemblies, Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) Part Number ARN06002-90206, National Stock Number 1560-01-667-1213, with shipping costs and an option for the purchase of a quantity of 300, plus shipping with the option to be available for the period of one year from the date of the award The proposed contract action is for the supplies or services for which the Government intends to solicit and negotiate with one source, Arnprior Aerospace Portland, Inc., cage code, under the authority of FAR 12.102(a) for acquisition valued at or below the simplified acquisition threshold where only one source is available. The requirement is being solicited on a sole source basis because Arnprior Aerospace Portland, Inc. latch assembly (part number ARN06002-90206) has successfully undergone Boeing's qualification and approval process and is the only such assembly authorized for use in the P8 Aircraft for the TAS Program. The latch assembly is listed on a Boeing document which illustrates the OEM part number and lists Arnprior's cage code. The Government has no drawings or technical information needed for competition. Deviating from this material would result in an unapproved configuration of the Sonobuoy Storage Racks. Material must be purchased from this vendor or an authorized distributor to comply with the Boeing Illustration. Shifting to a different vendor/s part presents a financial risk, as the re-qualification costs are projected to surpass any achievable cost savings. All responsible sources may submit a capability statement or proposal which shall be considered by the agency. However, a determination by the Government not to compete this proposed contract based upon responses to this solicitation is solely within the discretion of the Government. Contractors must be properly registered in the System for Award Management (SAM). Offerors may obtain information on SAM registration and annual confirmation requirements by calling 1-866-606-8220 or via the internet at https://www.sam.gov. Questions or inquiries should be directed to ROSE M. BROWN, Code 0253, telephone 812-381-7285, e-mail rose.m.brown44.civ@us.navy.mil. Please reference the above solicitation number when responding to this notice.

matters.text:
Federal notice (Solicitation), DEPT OF DEFENSE.DEPT OF THE NAVY.NSWC CRANE
Title: SOLE SOURCE � PCO MEZZANINE CARDS
Solicitation number: N0016426Q0087
PSC: 5998; NAICS: 334112
Description: N0016426Q0087 � SOLE SOURCE � PCO MEZZANINE CARDS � PSC 5998 - NAICS 334112 ISSUE DATE 11-MAR-2026 � CLOSING DATE 27-MAR-2026 � 11:00 PM Eastern Time ITEM DESCRIPTION- Naval Surface Warfare Center (NSWC) Crane has a requirement for a quantity of 200 PCI Mezzanine Cards (PMC) Part Number RRT-SPL2498-1 with an option to be executed within two (2) years of the award for an additional quantity of 200 of the PCI Mezzanine Cards Part Number RRT-SPL2498-1. The proposed contract action is for the supplies or services for which the Government intends to solicit and negotiate with one source only Red Rock Technologies, Inc. out of Tempe, Arizona, cage code 00CP6, under the authority of FAR 12.201-1 for commercial products. This is being solicited on a sole source only basis because these PMC cards are a critical component within the AN/SPS-73 radar system and are being used to sustain legacy systems and fulfill CASREP requirements. The new PMC cards are part of a legacy circuit card assembly that is being replaced by a new design. The new design is using the same PMC card as the legacy design in order to expedite qualification. Red Rock Technologies Inc is the Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) of these PMC cards. The OEM cards have gone through an intense qualification and testing program to ensure compatibility with the AN/SPS-73 system. Supplementing the supply with another vendor�s product would cost the Government approximately two years and roughly $1,000,000 to select or design a compatible replacement. These costs would not be recovered in competitive action. The procurement specialist is requesting a Dissolution of the Total Small Business Set-Aside in order to issue a Sole Source, Commercial Request for Quotes utilizing PSC 5998 for electrical and electronic assemblies, boards, cards, and associated hardware and NAICS 334112 for computer storage device manufacturing. All responsible sources may submit a capability statement, which shall be considered by the agency. However, a determination by the Government not to compete with this proposed contract based upon responses to this solicitation is solely within the discretion of the Government. Information received will normally be considered solely for the purpose of determining whether to conduct a competitive procurement. Contractors must be properly registered in the System for Award Management (SAM). Offerors may obtain information on SAM registration and annual confirmation requirements by calling 866-606-8220 or via the internet at https://sam.gov. This solicitation is being issued pursuant to the procedures at FAR 12.201-1 as a written Firm Fixed Priced Request for Quotes. Synopsis exception FAR 5.202(a)(13) applies and Solicitation Number N0016426Q0087 is hereby issued as an attachment hereto. All changes to the requirement that occur prior to the closing date will be posted to Contract Opportunities on https://sam.gov/. It is the responsibility of interested vendors to monitor https://sam.gov/ for any amendments, which may be issued to this solicitation. For changes made after the closing date, only those offerors that provide a quote will be provided any changes/amendments and considered for future discussions and/or award. Offers shall be e-mailed to rose.m.brown44.civ@us.navy.mil. All required information must be received on or before 27-MAR-2026 � 11:00 PM Eastern Time.

This document serves as both the justification and approval for acquisitions conducted under the authorities
for proposed procurements using other than full and open competition pursuant to the authority under 41
U.S. Code § 3304 – Use of Non-Competitive Procedures and Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 6 –
Competition Requirements.
1. Identification of the agency and contracting activity.
Requiring Agency:
The Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives (ATF)
Forensic Crime Gun Intelligence Laboratory (FCGIL)
Explosives 4504 E 18th ST N
Wichita, KS 67208

Washington, DC 20226

1This is also known as a Justification & Approval. It is the document required by the FAR that justifies and obtains
approval for a sole-source contract.
2This is entered at or after small business review, including the header.
