2. The nature and/or description of the action being approved.
ATF intends to award a sole source Blanket Purchase Agreement (BPA) for ten (10) dual
wavelength 77+ Investigation laser and two (2) FSIS II Color imaging system. Arrowhead
Scientific, Inc. (also known as Arrowhead Forensics as part of Thomas Scientific, LLC), is the
only responsible source that can provide BOTH of the equipment with the necessary technical
specifications required for use in an ATF laboratory. This procurement will bring FCGIL up to
the same standard as the other laboratories in Laboratory Services (LS).
3. A description of the supplies and/or services required, including the delivery schedule
and/or the period of performance (inclusive of all option periods), and the estimated dollar
value of the acquisition.
Ten (10) Dual Wavelength Forensic Laser and two (2) Full spectrum color imaging systems are
required. This procurement will be used in the triage and latent print section of the new FCGIL
facility. This will bring the FCGIL up to the capabilities of the Forensic Science Laboratory
Washington ( FSL-W) and FSL Atlanta (FSL-A).
The laboratory requires systems that can provide specific technical requirements listed below:
Forensic laser capabilities:
The forensic laser must be able to produce at least 8W of blue at 445nm (nano meters) and
8W of green at 520nm from the handpiece.
Single pistol grip allows both wavelengths to be delivered from one hand piece.
Diodes located in handpiece to assure maximum output wattage at 10W- with no loss of
power by passing through the delivery device/handpiece cords.
System must be controlled by a smart touch screens software system.
The unit must contain integral batteries which can be charged by plugging the unit into a
standard outlet.
Power must be adjustable via a touchscreen in increments of 1% to 100% with LED lighted
screen feedback display.
The handpiece must have a .25”-20 threaded mount on bottom of laser pistol grip for
mounting.
The system must include orange (520 nm) and yellow (445 nm) curved bandpass filters.
The system must include an integrated optical system with flexible rubber fiber delivery
cable and handpiece.
The handpiece must have a “dead man’s finger” safety system for user safety.
There must be an “always on” option selectable on the touch screen for static use or for use
while photographing evidence.
System must operate with AC power (120V +/- 10%, 50Hz/60Hz) or better.
Warm up time must be less than 10 seconds.
System must include a durable pelican case for field deployment.
Must include two (2) pair of goggles for 445 nm.
Must include two (2) pair of goggles for 520 nm.
System must have at least a one (1) year component failure warranty (parts & labor).
Version MAR 2025
JOFOC No.:
Page 3 of 7
Full spectrum color imaging system capabilities:
All-In-One Computer (running Windows 11 or upgradable) Intel Six-Core 3.2GHz, 8GB
RAM, 1TB Hard Drive, with a 27-inch 5120 x 2880-pixel (5K resolution) display, a mouse
and keyboard.
Fully integrated software.
Full visible spectrum color imaging system camera.
Capture an image at least 5 x 3-inch area with 1000 PPI (pixels per inch) resolution.
Captures up to 3500 PPI resolution.
Able to capture FULL COLOR 24-bit images (60MB file size).
Camera is pre-threaded for optional tripod mounting.
HDR Enhancement is availablein live video and image capture.
Full resolution frame rate up to 18 f/s (feet/second).
Fast scan frame rate up to 60 f/s.
Zoom focus frame rate up to 142 f/s.
Integrated Foot Pedal switch (for hands-free image capture).
Hydraulic camera arm mount.
Flexible arm for light source.
Full spectrum color from 254 nm to 1100 nm.
50mm UV (ultraviolet) Lens with Universal Filter Holder.
Band-pass filters (254nm, 365nm UV, 450nm Blue, 550nm Orange, 695nm IR and 830nm
IRs).
3 Position Filter Slider includes: 254nm UV, 550nm Orange, 830nm IR Filter.
Shortwave (254nm) UV Light.
3 watt, 365nm (UV); a 3 watt, 455nm (Blue); 3 watt, 525nm (Green); 3 watt, 625nm (Red);
and 3 watt, 850nm (Infrared) lights.
Chargers for all lights (12V, 100-240VAC).
UV Face shield and orange goggles.
Two (2) Year Manufacturer Warranty.
Must hold patent for the 254nm bulb and enable the user to” paint with the light”
Ten (10) Dual wavelength forensic Lasers and two (2) Full spectrum color imaging system will be
delivered to any of the current ATF laboratories:
A. Forensic Crime Gun Intelligence Laboratory (FCGIL)
Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives
4504 E 18th ST N
Wichita, KS 67208
B. ATF FSL-A:
2600 Century Parkway NE, Suite 400
Atlanta, GA 30345
Version MAR 2025
JOFOC No.:
Page 4 of 7
C. ATF FSL-W
6000 Ammendale Road
Beltsville, Maryland 20705
The estimated dates of this BPA are as follows:
Base year: 3/30/2026-3/29/2027
Option year 1: 3/30/2027-3/29/2028
Option year 2: 3/30/2028-3/29/2029
Option year 3: 3/30/2029-3/29/2030
Option year 4: 3/30/2030-3/29/2031
The estimated cost for the lifecycle of the BPA is $547,881.54 with a required delivery date no later
than sixty (60) days after purchase order awarded.
4. Identify statutory authority permitting limiting sources.
This acquisition is conducted under the authority of 41 U.S. Code § 3304 – Use of Non-Competitive
Procedures and the exceptions listed under FAR 6.103 – Circumstances permitting other than full
and open competition..
FAR 6.103-1 Only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy
agency requirements.
FAR 6.103-2 Unusual and compelling urgency.
FAR 6.103-3 Industrial mobilization; engineering, developmental, or research capability; or
expert services.
FAR 6.103-4 International agreement.
FAR 6.103-5 Authorized or required by statute.
FAR 6.103-6 – National Security
FAR 6.103-7 Public Interest
5. A statement demonstrating the unique qualifications of the proposed contractor or the
nature of the action requiring use of the authority.
Arrowhead Forensics through Thomas Scientific LLC is the only vendor that can provide BOTH an
independent DUAL WAVELENGTH Forensic Laser and FSIS II color imaging system. Arrowhead
Forensics has the systems that meets all the technical requirements as required by the laboratory to
ensure all ATF laboratories have the same capabilities. According to their sole source document, only
Version MAR 2025
JOFOC No.:
Page 5 of 7
Arrowhead Forensicscan provide both these systems. Arrowhead now falls under Thomas Scientific
LLC, which is a small business.
During market research it was identified that Arrowhead Forensics/Thomas Scientific LLC was
awarded a sole source contract on 2/12/2024 by ATF (15A00024PAQA00081) and 6/14/2022 by
ATF (15A00022PAQA00250).Additionally, on 11/22/2021, Department of Justice – Federal Bureau
of Investigation (DOJ-FBI) sole sourced two (2) dual wavelength lasers (Dual 77+ pistol grip
investigation laser) under contract number 15F06722P0004263. On 3/11/2023, DOJ-FBI also sole
sourced the FSIS II system (Notice ID: PR-0002233) with Arrowhead Scientific, Inc./Arrowhead
Forensics.
No other vendor manufactures a dual laser and full color imaging system that meets the minimum
technical requirements. Market research identifies that other manufacturers make a dual wavelength
laser, but the only systems that meet the minimum technical requirements of ATFidentified in Section
3 are from Arrowhead Forensics/Thomas Scientific LLC
Denial of this purchase would impede upon and negatively impact ATF’s law enforcement
investigations and training of future law enforcement and examiners.
6. A description of efforts made to ensure offers/quotes were solicited from as many potential
sources as is practicable, including whether a notice was or will be publicized as required by
FAR 5.2 and, if not, which exception under FAR 5.202 applies.
On 01/22/2024, a Request for Information (RFI) (# DJA-24-ALAB-PR-0197) was posted on
SAM.gov seeking Brand Name or equal sources for the specifications listed in Section 5. No
responses were received.
On 01/27/2026, another RFI/Sources Sought was posted ( (# DJA-26-ALAB-PR-XXXX) on
SAM.gov and only two (2) responses were received, one (1) from Thomas Scientific Holdings,
DBA Arrowhead Forensics who can meetthis requirement. The other response from Government
Science Source in which they state they cannot meet ATF’s requirements as the items can only
be procured directly from Arrowhead Forensics.
The Contracting Officer intends to issue a special notice in accordance with FAR 5.201 advising
that ATF intends to solicit on a sole source basis as allowed under FAR 12.102-(a) to Thomas
Scientific Holdings, DBA Arrowhead Forensics.
7. The anticipated dollar value of the proposed acquisition, including options if applicable,
and a determination by the contracting officer that the anticipated cost to the government will
be fair and reasonable.
The estimated cost for this purchase is $547,881.54. At least two (2) dual wavelength 77+
Investigation lasers will be purchased in the base year to be delivered to FCGIL. It is anticipated as
the laboratory increases compacity, it will purchase a total of ten (10) lasers and two (2) color imaging
systems.
Version MAR 2025

Description: N00164-26-Q-0077 � SOLE SOURCE � TRANSFORMER MODULES � FSG 5950 - NAICS 335311 ISSUE DATE 09-MAR-2026 � CLOSING DATE 20-MAR-2026 � 11:00 PM Eastern Time ITEM DESCRIPTION- Naval Surface Warfare Center (NSWC) Crane has a requirement for of an initial purchase of a quantity of 25 each Transformer Converters, a quantity of 50 each Transformer Power, and a quantity of 25 each Transformer Power Step Downs with options to purchase an additional quantity of 2 each Transformer Converters, an additional quantity of 7 each Transformer Power, and an additional quantity of 3 each Transformer Power Step Downs. The lead time expected on this effort is 120 weeks from date of award. Delivery will be Freight on board destination, with inspection and acceptance completed at a government location by government personnel. The total contract period should span approximately 730 days between award and exercise of all options. This will be a firm fixed price, non-commercial purchase order to a sole source provider as described below. The proposed contract action is for the supplies or services for which the Government intends to solicit and negotiate with one source, only Vanguard Electronics LLC, Cage Code 03550, under the authority of FAR 13.101-(b). This is being solicited on a sole source because Vanguard Electronics LLC, Cage Code 03550, is the Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) of these parts. The Naval Ordnance System Command has only approved the OEM as the sole source of supply to manufacturer the items in accordance with specific government requirement drawings. Using another vendor product would require recertification, re tooling and transition of technology to qualify the parts and vendor as an authorized supplier. The requalification would set the schedule back in excess of several months in addition to costing the government over $750,000. The detriment to the government would not be recouped in competitive action. All responsible sources may submit a capability statement, which shall be considered by the agency. However, a determination by the Government not to compete with this proposed contract based upon responses to this solicitation is solely within the discretion of the Government. Information received will normally be considered solely for the purpose of determining whether to conduct a competitive procurement. Contractors must be properly registered in the System for Award Management (SAM). Offerors may obtain information on SAM registration and annual confirmation requirements by calling 866-606-8220 or via the internet at https://sam.gov. Contractors must be properly registered in the System for Award Management (SAM) and the Joint Certification Program (JCP) in order to receive the controlled attachments. Offerors may obtain information on SAM registration and annual confirmation requirements by calling 866-606-8220 or via https://sam.gov. Information about the JCP is located at https://www.dla.mil/logistics-operations/services/joint-certification-program/. The controlled attachments will be posted at the same time the solicitation is posted. This solicitation is being issued pursuant to the procedures at FAR Part 13 as a written Firm Fixed Priced Purchase Order. Synopsis exception FAR 5.202(a)(13) applies and Solicitation Number N00164-26-Q-0077 is hereby issued as an attachment hereto. All changes to the requirement that occur prior to the closing date will be posted to Contract Opportunities on https://sam.gov/. It is the responsibility of interested vendors to monitor https://sam.gov/ for any amendments, which may be issued to this solicitation. For changes made after the closing date, only those offerors that provide a quote will be provided any changes/amendments and considered for future discussions and/or award. Offers shall be e-mailed to rose.m.brown44.civ@us.navy.mil. All required information must be received on or before 20-MAR-2026 � 11:00 PM Eastern Time.

Agency and Contracting Activity.
The Air Force Materiel Command (AFMC) Air Force Life Cycle Management Center (AFLCMC), Electronic Systems Directorate 
(ES), Aerospace Management Systems Division (ESA), Contracting Office (ESAK), 75 Vandenberg Drive, Hanscom Air Force Base, MA 01731-2103 is the contracting organization responsible for this proposed contracting action and is seeking approval for this Justification and Approval (J&A) for Other Than Full and Open Competition. The Contracting Officer for this action is Ms. Janice E. Sullivan, phone (380) 456-3013, E-mail: janice.sullivan@us.af.mil. 
Nature and/or description of the action being approved.
AFLCMC/ESAK intends to award a twelve-month extension to the ordering period of the current DASR Sustainment 
Indefinite Delivery/Indefinite Quantity (ID/IQ) Contract, FA8730-20-D-0039, from March 28, 2026 to March 27, 2027, and increase the maximum amount from $ to $

 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 to $
 
 

 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 . AFLCMC/ESAK also intends to extend the date beyond which the contractor cannot be required to perform in FAR 52.216-22(d) from September 28, 2027 to September 28, 2029, for a total of 9 years of performance. 
 
The purpose of the extension is to enable the continued sustainment and modernization of the existing 157 Digital Airport 
Surveillance Radars (DASRs), on a sole source basis to the Raytheon Company located at 1001 Boston Post E., Marlborough, MA 01752-3789 while simultaneously establishing a new sole source contract that will cover DASR sustainment and modernization efforts through 2038. The expected award date for the new DASR ID/IQ Sustainment Contract is August 27, 2026. The follow-on contract is late due to the amount of time it took to prepare and coordinate the Justification and Approval and the Acquisition Strategy Panel briefing, due to the number of questions and comments received from during the coordination cycle. The Program Management Office (PMO) is also requesting a $
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 increase to the current IDIQ Sustainment Contract maximum amount raising it from $ to $

 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 to $
 
 

 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 . This increase is required to fund the procurement of the Mk3 Monopulse Secondary Surveillance Radar (MSSR) interrogators as a replacement for the obsolete Mk2 MSSR interrogators, which are no longer in production by Raytheon. 
 
Contract types for this effort include Cost Plus Fixed Fee, Cost Reimbursement, Firm Fixed Price, and Time and Materials. 
 
This ordering period extension will utilize Procurement (3080) and Operation and Maintenance Centralized Assets Management (CAM) (3400) funding and has an estimated maximum amount increase of $
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 . The Independent Government Cost Estimate incorporates the approved Department of Defense funding. 
Description of supplies/services required to meet agency needs.
DASR systems are terminal area radar systems that provide primary surveillance coverage, secondary surveillance coverage, and calibrated weather precipitation intensity reports to automation systems and air traffic controllers. DASR systems play a critical role in ensuring safety of flight by providing air traffic controllers with radar coverage and situational awareness of covered air space, ensuring safe separation and sequencing aircraft within the National Airspace System and at overseas locations. The Department of Defense (DoD) (including Army, Navy, and Air Force) and the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) jointly procured 157 DASR systems through two (2) production contracts. The Air Force is the lead service for the DASR Sustainment Program while the FAA is the lead service for the DASR configuration. The Air Force, as part of its lead service role, has an Interagency Agreement (693KA7-22-N-00006) with the FAA and a Memorandum of Agreement (MOA 21-01) with the Army and Navy. 
 
A twelve (12) month ordering period extension to the current ID/IQ Sustainment Contract is required to ensure continuous support, maintenance, and modernization of the existing 157 DASRs. This extension enables the continued sustainment and modernization of the existing 157 Digital Airport Surveillance Radars (DASR) pending the anticipated award of a new DASR Sustainment ID/IQ Contract, with a current estimated award date of August 27, 2026. This anticipated award date may slip to the right due to the required approval level at SAF/AQ and the additional twelve (12) month ordering period should prevent any gaps in sustainment. 
 
The Program Management Office (PMO) is also requesting a $
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 increase to the current IDIQ Sustainment Contract maximum amount raising it from $ to $

 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 to $
 
 

 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 . This increase is required to fund the procurement of Mk3 Monopulse 
Secondary Surveillance Radar (MSSR) interrogators as a replacement for the obsolete Mk2 MSSR interrogators, which are no longer in production by Raytheon. 
 
It is in the Government's best interest to extend the ordering period and increase the maximum amount of the existing ID/IQ Sustainment Contract to the Raytheon Company to ensure Government needs will continue to be met. DASR systems play a critical role in ensuring safety of flight in air traffic controllers by providing radar coverage and situational awareness of covered airspace, preventing aircraft collisions. DASR systems also play a critical role in detecting any foreign object in the airspace that might be a threat to national security.
Demonstration that the contractor's unique qualifications or the nature of the acquisition requires use of the authority cited above.
The statutory authority that permits other than full and open competition for this acquisition is 10 U.S.C. 3204(b)(B), as implemented by FAR 6.302-1(a)(2)(ii), Only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements. 
 
Consistent with the intent of FAR 6.302-1(a)(2)(ii), this action is a follow-on contract modification for the continued replacement of obsolete parts and provision of an item of highly specialized equipment, and as such may be deemed to be available only from Raytheon, the original equipment manufacturer (OEM), when it is likely that award to any other source would result in unacceptable delays and substantial duplication of costs in fulfilling the Air Force's requirements. Therefore, this acquisition will be a follow-on contract modification for the continued sustainment support of highly specialized equipment. 
 
The DASR Systems were derived from Raytheon Company's ASR-10SS and Mk2. The systems were initially delivered under the DoD National Airspace Systems Modernization Program, an ACAT IC Program for the replacement and modernization of existing domestic and overseas Air Traffic Control facilities. Although these systems were developed under DoD contracts they were based upon Independent Research and Development (IRAD) that Raytheon completed. Raytheon Company manufactured the DASR systems under two (2) production contracts: F19628-96-D-0038 (1996-2011) and FA8730-08-D-0001 (2008-2020). The initial production contract was competitively awarded to the Raytheon Company. The follow-on contract was awarded on a sole-source basis to Raytheon. 
 
The DASR PMO has determined that awarding this contract to a vendor other than Raytheon Company, would result in significant duplication of cost to the Government, without an expectation of recovery through competition, and would cause unacceptable delays in meeting the Government's requirements. Therefore, Raytheon Company is uniquely positioned to provide DASR sustainment, avoiding substantial and unrecoverable cost duplication and unacceptable delays. 
 
Several factors contribute to this determination: 
OEM Expertise: With over twenty-four (24) years of DASR production and sustainment experience, the Raytheon Company has developed significant expertise and knowledge of DASR System design and operation, and the repair of Line 
Replaceable Units (LRUs) to support the FAA Depot. As the OEM and owner of the DASR Technical Data Package (TDP), the Raytheon Company is uniquely qualified to support the sustainment of DASR. This acquisition will be an extension of the existing IDIQ sustainment contract for the continued sustainment, maintenance, and modernization of major DASR systems. 
 
1443861439926. 

 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 . 
 
 

 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Technical Data Package (TDP) Ownership and Data Rights limitations necessitate a system-level replacement, encompassing both primary and secondary radars, for any competitive acquisition. The estimated cost for qualifying, procuring, and fielding 157 new primary and secondary radar systems is $
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 (Attachment 2: Radar Replacement Cost Estimate), with an additional $ required to sustain existing radars until the new systems are deployed resulting in a total estimated cost of $
 
Existing Infrastructure: It took eight (8) years to qualify the initial DASR system and a further ten (10) years to field. The DASR PMO estimates it could take up to six (6) years to qualify a new radar system and an additional three (3) to four (4) years to field replacement systems (Attachment 3: DASR Integrated Master Schedule). A schedule delay of this magnitude will lead to DASR system failure, cause radar outages, and prevent the warfighters from performing Air Traffic Control missions. 
 
The Government does not intend to make any more attempts to purchase any Intellectual Property (IP) it does not have current rights to. The Government has limited rights in technical data and restricted rights in computer software. In 
November 2018 the Government requested a Rough Order of Magnitude (ROM) from the Raytheon Company seeking to 
acquire unlimited data rights for DASR, but the Raytheon Company refused to engage in any discussions regarding the purchase of additional data rights, stating that the Raytheon Company's IP related to DASR is not for sale. In November 2019, the Government issued a Request for Proposal (RFP) to the Raytheon Company requesting a priced option to purchase Government Purpose Rights for DASR, but Raytheon declined again, asserting the Government only has limited and restricted rights. 
 
In March 2025, the Government sent another request to the Raytheon Company for a ROM estimate for unlimited data rights to DASR; however, Raytheon Company again declined, stating that IP related to DASR is not available for sale. While not a substitute for full data rights, the Program Management Office (PMO) intends to request Interface Control Documents (ICDs) to support a Modular Open Systems Architecture (MOSA) as part of all future efforts. ICDs define system component inputs and outputs, facilitating subsystem design without requiring extensive system-level modifications. This will enable future competitive sourcing of individual subsystems, as they can be decoupled from the larger system. 
 
The DASR PMO has determined that award to any other source would result in substantial duplication of cost to the Government that is not expected to be recovered through competition and unacceptable delays in fulfilling the Government's requirements.

This is a COMBINED SYNOPSIS/SOLICITATION for commercial product prepared in
accordance with FAR part 12, as supplemented with additional information included in this
notice. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation; quotes are being requested and a
separate written solicitation will not be issued.
The solicitation number is N0040626QS139 is issued as a Request for Quotation (RFQ) for
Composite Shaft Replacement Parts. This acquisition is a sole source. This combined
synopsis/solicitation incorporates provisions and clauses by reference. The full text of provisions
and clauses may be accessed electronically at www.acquisition.gov.
The NAICS CODE is 333618 and the Small Business Size Standard is 750 employees.
The Government intends to solicit and award a firm fixed price (FFP) purchase order with only
one source, Palmer Johnson Power Systems, under the authority of FAR 12.102(a) on a sole
source basis. Interested parties may identify their interest and capability to respond to the
requirement and submit quotes. Determination by the Government not to compete with this
proposed contract based upon responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the
Government.
This Solicitation is a SOLE SOURCE REQUIREMENT for Palmer Johnson Power Systems
1. NOTICE TO ALL OFFERORS: The Government anticipates awarding a firm, fixed price
contract in accordance with FAR Part 12 in response to quotes/proposals received in response to
this solicitation. A firm fixed price contract places the maximum risk and full responsibility for
all costs and resulting profit or loss on the contractor, offerors are advised to consider these risks
when pricing their quotes/proposals.
2. This acquisition is being conducted pursuant to FAR 6.302-2, Unusual and Compelling
Urgency, as only one responsible source can meet the Government’s urgent requirement within
the required timeframe.
3. QUESTIONS: Offerors may submit their questions regarding clarification of solicitation
requirements by email to chloe.b.vernet.civ@us.navy.mil and ashley.a.rollin.civ@us.navy.mil no
later than 1 day before solicitation closing date and time. Any questions received after this
deadline may not be answered.

the right to reject any item that does not conform to the requirements of this Statement of Work.

52.204-26 Covered Telecommunications Equipment Or Services-Representation (OCT 2020) {if available in SAM reps and certs, duplication may not be required}

 (a) Definitions. As used in this provision, "covered telecommunications equipment or services" and "reasonable inquiry" have the meaning provided in the clause 52.204-25, Prohibition on Contracting for Certain Telecommunications and Video Surveillance Services or Equipment.

 (2) After conducting a reasonable inquiry for purposes of this representation, the offeror represents that it [__] does, [__] does not use covered telecommunications equipment or services, or any equipment, system, or service that uses covered telecommunications equipment or services.

(End of provision)


52.204-24 REPRESENTATION REGARDING CERTAIN TELECOMMUNICATIONS AND VIDEO SURVEILLANCE SERVICES OR EQUIPMENT (NOV 2021) {MUST BE FILLED IN, if “does” in 52.204-26} 

The Offeror shall not complete the representation at paragraph (d)(1) of this provision if the Offeror has represented that it "does not provide covered telecommunications equipment or services as a part of its offered products or services to the Government in the performance of any contract, subcontract, or other contractual instrument" in paragraph (c)(1) in the provision at 52.204-26, Covered Telecommunications Equipment or Services--Representation, or in paragraph (v)(2)(i) of the provision at 52.212-3, Offeror Representations and Certifications-Commercial Products and Commercial Services. The Offeror shall not complete the representation in paragraph (d)(2) of this provision if the Offeror has represented that it "does not use covered telecommunications equipment or services, or any equipment, system, or service that uses covered telecommunications equipment or services" in paragraph (c)(2) of the provision at 52.204-26, or in paragraph (v)(2)(ii) of the provision at 52.212-3.

(a) Definitions. As used in this provision-

Backhaul, covered telecommunications equipment or services, critical technology, interconnection arrangements, reasonable inquiry, roaming, and substantial or essential component have the meanings provided in the clause 52.204-25, Prohibition on Contracting for Certain Telecommunications and Video Surveillance Services or Equipment.

(b) Prohibition. 

(1) Section 889(a)(1)(A) of the John S. McCain National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2019 (Pub. L. 115-232) prohibits the head of an executive agency on or after August 13, 2019, from procuring or obtaining, or extending or renewing a contract to procure or obtain, any equipment, system, or service that uses covered telecommunications equipment or services as a substantial or essential component of any system, or as critical technology as part of any system. Nothing in the prohibition shall be construed to--

(i) Prohibit the head of an executive agency from procuring with an entity to provide a service that connects to the facilities of a third-party, such as backhaul, roaming, or interconnection arrangements; or

(ii) Cover telecommunications equipment that cannot route or redirect user data traffic or cannot permit visibility into any user data or packets that such equipment transmits or otherwise handles.

(2) Section 889(a)(1)(B) of the John S. McCain National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2019 (Pub. L. 115-232) prohibits the head of an executive agency on or after August 13, 2020, from entering into a contract or extending or renewing a contract with an entity that uses any equipment, system, or service that uses covered telecommunications equipment or services as a substantial or essential component of any system, or as critical technology as part of any system. This prohibition applies to the use of covered telecommunications equipment or services, regardless of whether that use is in performance of work under a Federal contract. Nothing in the prohibition shall be construed to--

(i) Prohibit the head of an executive agency from procuring with an entity to provide a service that connects to the facilities of a third-party, such as backhaul, roaming, or interconnection arrangements; or

(ii) Cover telecommunications equipment that cannot route or redirect user data traffic or cannot permit visibility into any user data or packets that such equipment transmits or otherwise handles.

(c) Procedures. The Offeror shall review the list of excluded parties in the System for Award Management (SAM) (https://www.sam.gov) for entities excluded from receiving federal awards for "covered telecommunications equipment or services."

(d) Representations. The Offeror represents that--

(1) It [ ___ ] will, [ ___ ] will not provide covered telecommunications equipment or services to the Government in the performance of any contract, subcontract or other contractual instrument resulting from this solicitation. The Offeror shall provide the additional disclosure information required at paragraph (e)(1) of this section if the Offeror responds "will" in paragraph (d)(1) of this section; and

(2) After conducting a reasonable inquiry, for purposes of this representation, the Offeror represents that--

It [ ___ ] does, [ ___ ] does not use covered telecommunications equipment or services, or use any equipment, system, or service that uses covered telecommunications equipment or services. The Offeror shall provide the additional disclosure information required at paragraph (e)(2) of this section if the Offeror responds "does" in paragraph (d)(2) of this section.

(e) Disclosures. 

(1) Disclosure for the representation in paragraph (d)(1) of this provision. If the Offeror has responded "will" in the representation in paragraph (d)(1) of this provision, the Offeror shall provide the following information as part of the offer:

(i) For covered equipment--

(A) The entity that produced the covered telecommunications equipment (include entity name, unique entity identifier, CAGE code, and whether the entity was the original equipment manufacturer (OEM) or a distributor, if known);

(B) A description of all covered telecommunications equipment offered (include brand; model number, such as OEM number, manufacturer part number, or wholesaler number; and item description, as applicable); and

(C) Explanation of the proposed use of covered telecommunications equipment and any factors relevant to determining if such use would be permissible under the prohibition in paragraph (b)(1) of this provision.

(ii) For covered services--

(A) If the service is related to item maintenance: A description of all covered telecommunications services offered (include on the item being maintained: Brand; model number, such as OEM number, manufacturer part number, or wholesaler number; and item description, as applicable); or

(B) If not associated with maintenance, the Product Service Code (PSC) of the service being provided; and explanation of the proposed use of covered telecommunications services and any factors relevant to determining if such use would be permissible under the prohibition in paragraph (b)(1) of this provision.

(2) Disclosure for the representation in paragraph (d)(2) of this provision. If the Offeror has responded "does" in the representation in paragraph (d)(2) of this provision, the Offeror shall provide the following information as part of the offer:

(i) For covered equipment--

(A) The entity that produced the covered telecommunications equipment (include entity name, unique entity identifier, CAGE code, and whether the entity was the OEM or a distributor, if known);

(B) A description of all covered telecommunications equipment offered (include brand; model number, such as OEM number, manufacturer part number, or wholesaler number; and item description, as applicable); and

(C) Explanation of the proposed use of covered telecommunications equipment and any factors relevant to determining if such use would be permissible under the prohibition in paragraph (b)(2) of this provision.

(ii) For covered services--

(A) If the service is related to item maintenance: A description of all covered telecommunications services offered (include on the item being maintained: Brand; model number, such as OEM number, manufacturer part number, or wholesaler number; and item description, as applicable); or

(B) If not associated with maintenance, the PSC of the service being provided; and explanation of the proposed use of covered telecommunications services and any factors relevant to determining if such use would be permissible under the prohibition in paragraph (b)(2) of this provision.

(End of provision)

Description: This is a notice of intent to award a sole-source, firm-fixed-price contract to Fluke Electronics Corporation (UEI: YA5LYT9J7TX5). The 60th Contracting Squadron, Travis AFB, CA, intends to procure one (1) new Fluke 5560A High-Performance Multi-Product Calibrator and one (1) 55XXA/Coil 50 turn current coil. This equipment is a direct replacement for an obsolete model and is required by the 60th MXS Precision Measurement Equipment Laboratory (PMEL) to support mission-critical calibration for a wide range of Test, Measurement, and Diagnostic Equipment (TMDE). This notice of intent is not a request for competitive proposals. However, all responsible sources may submit a capability statement, proposal, or quotation, which shall be considered by the agency. A determination by the Government not to compete this proposed contract based upon responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. Information received will normally be considered solely for the purpose of determining whether to conduct a competitive procurement. b. Justification for soliciting from a single source: Air Force Metrology and Calibration

(Tos) 33K8-4-14-1, 33K8-15-1 and other TOs – standardizing the use of the Fluke 5560A across
the Air Force. No other asset is available that meets the very specific, mandatory measurement
parameters and interoperability standards required for the Air Force calibration mission.
c. Efforts to obtain Competition: Market research was conducted and concluded that while
other manufacturers of calibration equipment exist, none produces an instrument that is certified
by AFMETCAL as the direct replacement for the 5520A. The Fluke 5560A with 55XXA Coil 50
is the only product that meets the government's minimum needs due to this mandatory
standardization requirement, which is essential for compatibility, interoperability, and
maintaining a consistent calibration process across the Air Force
d. Determination by the ordering activity contracting officer the purchase is priced fair and
reasonable: IAW FAR 15.403-1(f)(2) the Contracting Officer has determined this purchase to be
fair and reasonably priced through historical purchases or contracts. Contract # FA226324F0009
prices the 5560A W/55XXA COIL 50 at , which at the time was determined to be fair

annual increase of . While this is higher than some general inflation forecasts, several
factors specific to t e gh-precision test and measurement market can justify it.
(1) High Research & Development (R&D) Costs: The extreme precision of the 5560A is
built on significant and ongoing R&D. It features a patented, ultra-linear analog-to-digital design
to achieve its perfonnance specifications. These R&D costs are substantial for a low-volume
product and are factored in its price.
(2) Niche Market and Manufacturing Complexity: The market for high-perfonnance
calibrators is driven by regulated industries like aerospace, defense, electronics manufacturing,
and healthcare. These are not mass-market items. The test and measurement equipment market is
projected to grow at a CAGR of around 4.9% to 5.7%, indicating steady, value-driven demand.
(3) Sti·ingent Compliance and Certification: This equipment is used to ensure other
devices meet sti·ict quality standards (e.g., ISO/IEC 17025, FDA, FAA). The calibrator itself
must be manufactured and calibrated to the highest meti·ological standards, often including an
accredited ISO 17025 calibration ce1iificate, which adds to the cost and value.
(4) Long Product Lifecycle and Suppo1i: Unlike consumer goods, industi·ial calibrators
are expected to operate reliably for many years. The purchase price often includes the cost of
long-te1m manufacturer suppo1i, software updates, and the availability of service and repairs.
e. Steps to preclude future single source or brand name awards: The requiring activity will
monitor AFMETCAL directives and conduct market research for any new technologies or
alternative sources that may be approved in the future.
f. Conti·acting officer's decision: IAW 10 U.S. Code§ 3204(e)(l) I have dete1mined that the
circumstances of this conti·act action deem only a single source will satisfy the needs of the

4. Statuary Authority Permitting OtherThan Full and Open Competition.
10 U.S.C 3204(a)(1), Only one responsible source and no other supplies or service will satisfy agency
requirements.
5. Rationale Justifying Use of Cited Statutory Authority.
Pursuant to Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 6.302-1(a)(2)(ii)(B) and (iii)(B), award to any other source
would result in unacceptable delays in fulfilling the requirements. LMMFC is the original designer,
developer and manufacturer of the LGTR system and owns the proprietary data that is required to perform the
efforts set forth in Paragraph 2 above, including the applicable detailed specifications, software source code
and drawings. The LGTR is currently in production under contract N00019-17-C-0022. This requirement is a
follow-on production, maintenance and sustainment effort for the LGTR system. LMMFC has informed
NAVAIR that LGTR Proprietary Data is not for sale at this time or in the foreseeable future.
The Government's lack of technical data needed to support a competition will result in unacceptable delays in
fulfilling the agency's requirements. Based on the historical average time to develop a new missile, it would take
approximately 3.5 to 4 years for another source to complete an Engineering and Manufacturing Development
phase, create a production level technical data package, and to complete required testing. Further, it is estimated
that it would take an additional 1.5 to 2 years post-qualification for that vendor to deliver an LGTR system, based
on historical lead times. The additional 5 to 6 years to start receiving first deliveries results in unacceptable
delays in fulfilling the US Navy's requirements to replenish the LGTR in its inventory. As a result, LMMFC is the
only responsible source capable of providing supplies and/or services to satisfy the US Navy's requirements.

Federal notice (Presolicitation), COMMERCE, DEPARTMENT OF.NATIONAL OCEANIC AND ATMOSPHERIC ADMINISTRATION.DEPT OF COMMERCE NOAA
Title: Sole Source VectorNav Units
Solicitation number: 142082-26-0153
PSC: 6660; NAICS: 334511
Description: The National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration�s (NOAA) Acquisition and Grants Office, Eastern Acquisition Division-Kansas City intends to negotiate and award a purchase order, on a sole source basis, under authority of RFO FAR 6.103-1, with VectorNav Technologies for VN-100T-CR Wave Sensors to be delivered/performed at Stennis Space Center, MS. The sole source determination is based on NOAA�s compatibility to existing systems or equipment. Sole Source Justification: NDBC conducted market research to find a suitable replacement that would fit the current configurations on their observation stations. Ultimately it was narrowed to three products. Tests at NDBC showed the VectorNav VN100T-CR outperformed the other two products in those tests. NDBC intends to replace all of the old 3DM-GX1 systems with the VectorNav sensor. The VectorNav VN100T-CR is a miniature, high-performance Inertial Measurement Unit (IMU) and Attitude Heading Reference System (AHRS). It combines 3-axis accelerometers, gyros, and magnetometers into one device. The sensor interfaces to NDBC equipment to process the sensor measurements into wave products. In prior years, the NDBC learned that Lord Microstrain was planning to cease production of the 3DM-GX1 sensor which is the NDBC�s present operational sensor. Since that time, the NDBC has modified its wave system interface firmware to read the VN100T-CR input data stream and performed initial lab and field tests to confirm proper operation. Now the NDBC has mounted the sensor in place of the older obsolete part inside the operational tube. These sensors being purchased will be used to modify operational tubes to use the new VN100T-CR sensor. If the VN100T-CR product is not procured, the NDBC will reach a point where it cannot meet its requirement for wave observations due to lack of functioning sensors. Should another brand be procured, the NDBC would have to modify mounting and interface firmware, thus incurring more costs. Tests already completed for the VN100T-CR would have to be re-conducted. This includes field testing. These tests are required to confirm proper operation and quality of the measurements. Thus, the cost to the government would greatly increase and wave observations at some stations may not be possible until the required testing could be completed. This pre-solicitation notice is not a request for competitive proposals and no solicitation package is available. However, firms that believe they can fully meet the government's requirements may submit substantiating documentation or a request for additional information in writing to the (Contract Specialist) within 15 days after publication of this pre-solicitation notice. Such requests and documentation will be evaluated solely for the purpose of determining whether or not to conduct this procurement on a competitive basis. A determination by the government not to conduct a competitive procurement, based upon responses to this notice, is solely within the discretion of the government. Oral communications are not acceptable in response to this pre-solicitation notice.

Description: VHAPG Part 813.5 Simplified Acquisition Procedures for Certain Commercial Items Attachment 1: Request for Sole Source Justification Template >SAT-$7.5M under FAR13.5 Effective Date: 11/15/24 Page 1 of 9 REVISION: 01 Acquisition ID#: 36C250-26-AP-0288 DEPARTMENT OF VETERANS AFFAIRS SOLE SOURCE JUSTIFICATION UNDER SIMPLIFIED PROCEDURES FOR CERTAIN COMMERCIAL ITEMS IN ACCORDANCE WITH FAR 13.5 Acquisition Plan Action ID: 36C250-26-AP-0288 Contracting Activity: Department of Veterans Affairs, NCO 10, 24 Frank Lloyd Wright Dr., Ann Arbor, MI 48105, in support of the Lieutenant Colonel Charles S. Kettles VA Medical Center, 2215 Fuller Road, Ann Arbor, MI 48105. 2237: 506-26-2-1030-0011. Nature and/or Description of the Action Being Processed: This is a new requirement in accordance with FAR 13.5 Simplified Procedures for Certain Commercial Items and specifically FAR 13.510 Special Documentation Requirements, where acquisitions conducted under Simplified Acquisition Procedures are exempt from the requirements of FAR Part 6, but still require a justification using the format of FAR 6.303-2. The action will be awarded as a Firm-Fixed Price IDIQ with a five-year ordering period. This is a Cost Per Test (CPT) contract to provide gyn and non-gyn specimen testing for the Pathology and Laboratory Medicine Services at the Ann Arbor VA. Description of Supplies/Services Required to Meet the Agency s Needs: The procurement is for a CPT contract to provide one (1) standalone automated Cytology Processing and Papanicolaou nontoxic staining system, UPS (uninterrupted power supply), Printer, Toner, Parts, Service manual (technical and service manuals), Reagents, Consumable and Supplies, Shipping and Handling costs associated with receipt of reagents, Preventative and Emergency Repair Maintenance agreement including non-refurbished materials, labor, transportation necessary to perform maintenance/preventative maintenance, operator and Pathologists training, hardware and software and software updates to VA Ann Arbor Healthcare System. Period of Performance: 2/16/2026 2/15/2031 VA Ann Arbor Health care System � Non-GYN GYN GYN & NON-GYN Estimated Total Period of Performance Testing Previous Yearly Average 10% Increase Estimated Yearly Average Previous Yearly Average 10% Increase Estimated Yearly Average Year 1 Total Count 3500 350 3850 2000 200 2200 6050 Year 2 Total Count 3850 385 4235 2200 220 2420 6655 Year 3 Total Count 4235 424 4659 2420 242 2662 7321 Year 4 Total Count 4659 466 5124 2662 266 2928 8053 Year 5 Total Count 5124 512 5637 2928 293 3221 8858 Total for 5-Year � 23505 � 13431 36936 Statutory Authority Permitting Restricted Competition:� FAR 13.5 Simplified Procedures for Certain Commercial Items. The statutory authority for applying the Simplified Procedures for Commercial Items of FAR 13.5 is 41 U.S.C. § 1901 and is implemented by FAR 13.106-1(b)(2) for restricting competition on this procurement. � Competition is restricted on this procurement for the reason below: � � � � � � � (� X )� Only One Responsible Source and No Other Supplies or Services Will Satisfy Agency Requirements � � � � � � � (� )� Unusual and Compelling Urgency � � � � � � � (� ) � Industrial Mobilization, Engineering, Developmental or Research Capability or Expert Services � � � � � � � (� )� International Agreement � � � � � � � (� )� Authorized or Required by Statute � � � � � � � (� )� National Security � � � � � � � (� )� Public Interest Demonstration that the Contractor s Unique Qualifications or Nature of the Acquisition Requires the Use of the Authority Cited Above (applicability of authority): For screening of cervical cancer, there are two liquid-based cytoprocessing methods that are widely used, SurePath and ThinPrep. Both have similar diagnostic capabilities but differ in specimen collection, preservation and processing methods. SurePath and ThinPrep, both use a cervical brush or a broom-like device to collect the exfoliated cells from the affected area, where most of the precancerous and cancerous lesions originate. But the transfer of cells into the liquid medium differs and thereby affects specimen composition. With SurePath technology, after the collection, the device is detached and placed directly into the vial containing the preservative solution. There is minimal cell loss, but it also introduces contamination from which can potentially obscure cellular details and complicates interpretation. Whereas with ThinPrep technology, after the collection, the device is rinsed in the vial by swirling before discarding the brush. This cell transfer exhibits uniform monolayer cell distribution allowing clearer visualization of individual cellular morphology for better microscopic evaluation and reduces unwanted material. Demonstration that the Contractor’s Unique Qualifications or Nature of the Acquisition Requires the Use of the Authority Cited Above (applicability of authority): 

For screening of cervical cancer, there are two liquid-based cytoprocessing methods that are widely used, SurePath and ThinPrep. Both have similar diagnostic capabilities but differ in specimen collection, preservation and processing methods. SurePath and ThinPrep, both use a cervical brush or a broom-like device to collect the exfoliated cells from the affected area, where most of the precancerous and cancerous lesions originate. But the transfer of cells into the liquid medium differs and thereby affects specimen composition. 
With SurePath technology, after the collection, the device is detached and placed directly into the vial containing the preservative solution. There is minimal cell loss, but it also introduces contamination from which can potentially obscure cellular details and complicates interpretation. Whereas with ThinPrep technology, after the collection, the device is rinsed in the vial by swirling before discarding the brush. This cell transfer exhibits uniform monolayer cell distribution allowing clearer visualization of individual cellular morphology for better microscopic evaluation and reduces unwanted material. 
Currently the Ann Arbor VA is using the SurePath Cytoprocessor in Cytology for gyn and non-gyn specimens. Moving forward the Ann Arbor VA is shifting to ThinPrep sample collection over SurePath sample collection given the industry standards and FDA requirements for HPV testing on expanded specimen types. Liquid-based cytology testing and HPV testing is standard of care for a variety of patients and in order to deliver optimal care to a wider array of situations. 
HPV testing is FDA regulated and can only be performed on approved instrumentation, with approved protocols and reagents.  HPV testing with current instrumentation can only be performed on cervical specimens when in SurePath fixative. ThinPrep fixative would allow for HPV testing for vaginal and anal specimens. Therefore, to continue and expand HPV testing in-house, the VA must transition to ThinPrep. 
Making this shift will require proprietary equipment while also being mindful of technologist time, existing available resources as well as average workload. ThinPrep specimens are proprietary to the Hologic system and require a Hologic Cytoprocessor for slide preparation. 
With that in mind, the salient characteristics for the liquid-based cytology processing instrument are as follows:

Ability to process all types of ThinPrep collection vials.
Available with: ThinPrep 5000, ThinPrep 5000 Autoloader, ThinPrep Genesis
Not Available with: None
Ability to read Cerebro labels and option to interface with LIS.
Available with: ThinPrep 5000, ThinPrep 5000 Autoloader
Note Available with: ThinPrep Genesis
Automated batch processing to standardize processing of slides and allow more efficient use of technician time.
Available with: ThinPrep 5000, ThinPrep 5000 Autoloader
Not Available with: ThinPrep Genesis
Dimensions allow instrument to fit in available laboratory space.
Available with: ThinPrep 5000, ThinPrep Genesis
Not Available with: ThinPrep 5000 Autoloader

All the instruments researched provide at least one of these characteristics, but the only instrument to provide all of them is the Hologic ThinPrep 5000 processor. For this reason, the recommendation is to select the ThinPrep 5000 Cytoprocessor for use.

Description: A component of the 1st Special Operations Wing (1 SOW), has an urgent and compelling need. To meet this accelerated schedule, the unit has identified the Chimera Group-1 sUAS as the most viable platform. This decision was based on the fact that the squadron has already established an initial cadre of operators, who are trained and certified on the Chimera system through the AFSOC-approved Oak Grove Technologies Initial Training Course. Procuring any other system would render this existing expertise obsolete and require the unit to restart the entire training and certification process, introducing unacceptable delays. Market research confirmed that Oak Grove Technologies is the sole manufacturer and only authorized provider of the Chimera sUAS and its proprietary, AFSOC-approved training course. The Government is aware that Oak Grove Technologies holds an established IDIQ contract (ACC-APG-RS3, W15P7T-19-D-0087); however, this vehicle is scoped for services only and cannot be used for the procurement of supplies. Due to the urgent operational timeline, the existence of a trained initial cadre, and the lack of any other viable source or contract vehicle for the required system and training, this acquisition is being pursued on a sole-source basis.

matters.text:
Federal notice (Combined Synopsis/Solicitation), HOMELAND SECURITY, DEPARTMENT OF.US COAST GUARD.AVIATION LOGISTICS CENTER (ALC)(00038)
Title: Notice of Intent to Award to Sole Source BOA
Solicitation number: 70Z03826QB0000048
PSC: 1630; NAICS: 336413
Description: This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial items prepared in accordance with the format in FAR Part 12, as supplemented with additional information included in this notice. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation; quotations are being requested and a written solicitation will not be issued. Solicitation number 70Z03825QB0000048 is issued as a request for quotation (RFQ). This solicitation document and incorporated provisions and clauses are those in effect as of November 28, 2025, IAW the Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO). The applicable North American Industry Classification Standard Code is 336413. The small business size standard is 1,250 employees. This is a restricted requirement with intent to award to Basic Ordering Agreement (BOA) SPE4A1-25-G-0020. All responsible sources may submit a quotation which shall be considered by the agency. It is anticipated that a firm-fixed price delivery order shall be awarded on a Sole Source basis to Meggitt Aircraft Braking Systems Corporation (Cage Code: 0B9R9) as a result of this synopsis/solicitation. All parts must have clear traceability to the Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM), Meggitt Aircraft Braking Systems Corporation (Cage Code: 0B9R9). Traceability means a clear, complete, documented, and auditable paper trail which traces each step from the OEM or an OEM approved source. See attached documents titled: �Requirements � 70Z03826QB0000048,� �Terms and Conditions � 70Z03826QB0000048� and �Redacted J and A � 70Z03826QB0000048�. It is the Government's belief that Meggitt Aircraft Braking Systems is the only known source to provide traceability and genuine OEM parts with the packaging requirements stated in the Component Maintenance Manual (CMM). Concerns having the expertise and required capabilities to provide these items are invited to submit offers in accordance with the requirements stipulated in this solicitation. Parts must be approved in accordance with Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) guidelines to ensure safety of our aircrew. Best value to the Government is always the goal, but without jeopardizing quality or safety of flight. Only the use of airworthy commercial specifications or standard military specifications/military standard parts will be utilized and approved from this solicitation. Newly manufactured commercial items will only be procured from sources able to provide a certificate of conformance (COC). The Federal Aviation Regulation, Part 21, and Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) clause 52.246-15 outline these certification procedures. NO SUBSTITUTE OR ALTERNATE PARTS WILL BE CONSIDERED. ONLY NEW PARTS WILL BE ACCEPTED. NOTE: NO DRAWINGS, SPECIFICATIONS OR SCHEMATICS ARE AVAILABLE FROM THIS AGENCY. Closing date and time for receipt of offers is 13 February 2026 at 9:00 am EST. Quotes and questions shall be submitted by email to selmary.melendezgonzalez3 @uscg.mil. Please indicate solicitation 70Z03826QB0000048 in the subject line. Phone call quotes WILL NOT be accepted.

JUSTIFICATION FOR OTHER THAN FULL AND OPEN COMPETITION
1. Defense Logistics Agency (DLA) Troop Support, Construction and Equipment Supply Chain, is the
contracting activity.
2. The action being approved is the ability to solicit for DLA requirements on an other than full and
open competition basis.
3. The following are the supplies required to meet DLA’s needs:
Item Description: Fire Extinguisher
National Stock Number (NSN): 4210-01-481-3875
Manufacturer/Approved Source: Amerex Corporation (Corp.) (Cage Code )
Part Number: 15274
Estimated Quantity: 6,057 each per year
Estimated Unit Price:
Estimated Dollar Value for One (1) Year Base Term:
Number of One (1) Year Options: Four (4)
Estimated Dollar Value, Inclusive of Options:
Maximum Dollar Value: $4,000,000.00
4. The acquisition will be conducted using simplified procedures for certain commercial products in
accordance with FAR 13.5. Since simplified procedures will be used, the applicable statutory
authority permitting other than full and open competition is 41 U.S.C. § 1901, as implemented by
FAR 13.501(a), Sole Source Acquisitions. The analogous statutory authority for FAR Part 6 is 10
U.S.C. § 3204(a)(1), as implemented by FAR 6.302-1, Only one responsible source and no other
supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements.
5. The use of this authority is necessary because Amerex Corp. is the only Fire Extinguisher authorized
by the Army Engineering Support Activity (ESA). The NSN was set up by the Army ESA for the
Amerex Corp. part number.
This Fire Extinguisher has the unique feature of a mounting bracket for all the vehicles that carry the
Fire Extinguisher. Amerex Corp. is the original manufacturer of the Fire Extinguisher. The vehicle
mounting bracket distinguishes this item from other Amerex Corp. commercial part numbers as the
company sells a similar Fire Extinguisher commercially with a wall bracket. The Amerex Corp. part
number is the only product that can meet the customers’ requirements.
This is
the only Fire Extinguisher that will fit in the compartment space of the military units/platforms
assigned to this NSN.
The Fire Extinguisher is required on a continuous
basis to fulfill customers’ requirements. There is no other Fire Extinguisher that meets the
specifications of the Amerex Corp. part number.
If the Government receives an
alternate offer for this procurement, the information will be sent to the ESA for review and possible
approval.
6. The requirement will be synopsized on the Contract Opportunities in the System for Award
Management (SAM.gov) website as required by FAR 5.2 and published on the DLA Internet Bid
Board System (DIBBS). In addition, this J&A will be posted with the solicitation in accordance
with FAR 6.305(c).
7. As the contracting officer, I hereby determine that the anticipated cost to the Government will be
fair and reasonable
.
8. A Sources Sought Notice (SSN) was posted for the item August 15, 2024 through September 16,
2024 along with a Market Research Survey.
Additional market research was conducted via surveys sent directly to companies and online search
from August 15, 2024 through September 16, 2024.
Further market research was conducted by searching online for additional sources and commercial
pricing for this item. The item was found on General Services Administration (GSA) Advantage.
GSA contractors offering the Amrerex Corp. item are: Divine Imaging Inc., Pelican Sales Inc., and
Caprice Electronics Inc. The market research revealed subject item is available to the general public
and confirmed the item is commercial. The Government’s market research confirmed that the item is
only available from one manufacturer, Amerex Corp., so full and open competition is not possible.
However, the item is available from multiple distributors.
9. There are no additional facts supporting use of this authority.
10.
11. DLA Troop Support will continue to perform market research prior to any future acquisitions for this
requirement. It is likely that the required items will continue to be procured on a sole source basis
because of the nature and application of the item, however, the solicitation will be available to
various dealers and distributors in an effort to promote competition. Any alternate offers submitted in
response to the proposed procurement will be reviewed by this office and referred to the Engineering
Support Activity (ESA) for evaluation.
12. As the Contracting Officer, I hereby certify that this justification is accurate and complete to the
best of my knowledge and belief.
ASHLEY NIXON
Contracting Officer

supplies meet the Government’s needs in accordance with applicable specifications and that this justification
is accurate and complete to the best of my knowledge and belief.
Product Specialist

only the OEM, GE Precision Healthcare, can provide. FDA requires compliance with 100% OEM
specifications.
(5) A determination by the Contracting Officer that the anticipated cost to the Government will be fair
and reasonable.
The contracting officer for the resultant order has determined the prices offered to be fair and
reasonable for this justification for an exception to fair opportunity. All items are priced at or below the
contract price, which was previously determined fair and reasonable at time of contract award, and
there have been no significant changes to the industry or market conditions that would result in
changes to the reasonableness of the underlying contract prices.
(6) Any other facts supporting the justification.
The GE Discovery MI PET/CT scan is primarily utilized for detecting, diagnosing, and monitoring
various medical conditions, including cancers, cardiovascular diseases, and neurological disorders.
By combining the metabolic insights from PET with the detailed anatomical images from CT,
Healthcare providers can achieve more precise diagnoses and tailor treatment plans effectively.
Transitioning from a 3-ring to a 5-ring PET/CT system enhances the scan quality and efficiency,
offering several benefits. The 5-ring system expands the axial field of view, leading to faster imaging
times and reduced patient exposure to radiation. Additionally, it provides higher resolution images,
which improves the accuracy of detecting and characterizing lesions. This advanced technology
supports better patient outcomes by enabling earlier diagnosis and more effective monitoring of
treatment responses.
(7) A statement of the actions, if any, the agency may take to remove or overcome any barriers that led
to the exception to fair opportunity before any subsequent acquisition of the supplies or services is
made.
All prospective delivery orders are completed by all contract holders. Once an order is placed for
proprietary equipment, it is generally not possible to compete follow-on acquisitions for upgrades
because the system to be upgraded is proprietary in nature. Future requirements will be handled on a
case-by-case basis, and all attempts will be made to provide fair opportunity to all contract holders
when appropriate.
(8) The contracting officer’s certification that the justification is accurate and complete to the best of
the contracting officer’s knowledge and belief.
By signing this justification, the Contracting Officer hereby certifies that the justification is accurate
and complete to the best of their knowledge.
(9) Evidence that any supporting data is the responsibility of the technical or requirements personnel
(e.g., verifying the Government’s minimum needs or requirements or other rationale for an
exception to fair opportunity) and which form a basis for the justification have been certified as

By signing this justification, the Facility Biomedical Engineer hereby certifies that the justification is
accurate and complete to the best of their knowledge.

attachments.name: JA (2025_123) - W91247-26-P-A004 - Redacted.pdf
attachments.text:
Control No: MICC 2025-0123
FAR Part 6 Justification and Approval
for Other than Full and Open Competition
1. Requiring Activity: Headquarters, United States Army Reserve Command
(USARC), Fort Bragg, NC.
2. Contracting Activity: U.S. Army Mission and Installation Contracting Command
(MICC)-Fort Bragg, Fort Bragg North Carolina, 28310
3. Description of Action: Request approval to award a firm-fixed-price contract with
Laser Shot, Inc., 4214 Bluebonnet Drive, Stafford, Texas, 77477-2911. The
Government projects award for September 2025 and fiscal year 2025 Operations &
Maintenance Funds will be used.
4. Description of Supplies/Services: Refresh ten live-fire simulators (eight Mobile
Marksmanship Training Simulators (MMTS) and two Warrior Skills Trainers (WST)
Simulators). This requirement will include installation of new projectors and computers,
repair of existing hardware, and the associated labor. The 5-year extended warranty for
the systems will cover the repair and replacement by the vendor of any product that is
defective in material or workmanship. The weapons simulators that constitute the
USARC Preliminary Live-Fire Simulations (PLFS) portfolio include the MMTS and the
WST; these simulators are non-Program of Record and were purchased utilizing
NGREA funding. PLFS are a requirement to execute Table II of the Integrated Weapons
Training Strategy (Training Circular 3-20.0). Since the initial purchase of these
simulators in 2018, there has not been an established funding plan to maintain and
replace these system at the end of their life cycle (10 years per industry standard).
NGREA funding is limited to initial procurement and does not extend to services or
maintenance support.
Estimated delivery date: No later than 1 December 2025
Total Value: $
5. Authority Cited: 10 U.S.C. 3204(a)(1), as implemented by FAR 6.302-1, Only one
responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements.
6. Reason for Authority Cited: As described at FAR 6.302-1(a)(2), when the supplies
or services required by the agency are available only from one responsible source, or
for DoD, NASA and the Coast Guard, from only one or a limited number of responsible
sources, and no other types of supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements, full
and open competition need not be provided for.
a. Background. Laser Shot manufactures the Mobile Marksmanship Training
Simulator and Warrior Skills Trainer Simulator and is the only company approved to
repair, upgrade, and warranty these products, including computers and recoil kits. Laser
Shots cameras, software, and firmware have been developed and configured by Laser
3
Control No: MICC 2025-0123
Shot to work specifically with these simulators. Only Laser Shots technology and
software is guaranteed to work with the simulators as their technology is proprietary and
has been designed to integrate with other Laser Shot components. Laser Shot is the
publisher, holder of all copyrights, and the sole source for the only software and
firmware that works with these simulators.
b. Alternatives. The Government did not identify any viable alternatives to Laser
Shot, Inc. for this requirement.
The requiring activitys market research identified one alternate vendor, , who
responded that they could not repair, update, or warranty the existing Laser Shot MMTS
and WTS systems. Instead, proposed a solution to replace the current systems
with eight new training systems. This alternative was not pursued because it
would require full replacement of Government owned equipment, incur significant
additional cost, and delay training due to procurement, installation , and instructor re-
training.
A Sources Sought was posted to SAM.gov to determine whether other vendors were
capable of performing maintenance and warranty support on the existing MMTS and
WST systems. One business, , responded
with an expression of keen interest but did not submit any follow-up capability statement
or supporting documentation.
Additionally, the existing MMTS and WST systems warranties require that all
refresh, maintenance, and upgrades be performed by Laser Shot technicians. Using
any non-laser Shot source would void the warranty and risk system operability.
c. Impact if this justification is not approved. If the requirement is not approved, the
USARC risks losing critical training capability. Half of the simulators are already non-
operational, and without a systems refresh and warranty renewal, all 10 may become
unusable. This would significantly hinder units ability to execute Table II of the
Integrated Weapons Training Strategy (TC 3-20.0), degrade soldier marksmanship
readiness, and impact overall force preparedness.
7. Efforts to Obtain Competition: The Contracting Officer shall publish the notices
required by FAR 5.201 and any bids or proposals received shall be considered.
a. Effective Competition: Because this is a sole source action, effective competition
is not applicable.
b. Subcontracting Competition: Laser Shot is registered as a Small Business. IAW
with FAR 19.702(a)(2)(b) a subcontracting plan is not required.
8. Actions to Increase Competition: Laser Shot is the most cost-effective vendor
because the necessary equipment has already been purchased and integrated.
4
Control No: MICC 2025-0123
Selecting a different vendor would incur significant additional costs related to
procurement, installation, and training as well as increased risk to system operabilility
and mission readiness.
To increase competition in the future, the Government will conduct early market
research prior to the expiration of the current system warranty to identify additional
qualified vendors capable of providing compatible maintenance and training support.
This includes re-posting a sources sought on SAM.gov, engaging industry through
mandatory sources and other open-market research tools, and reviewing any new
vendors who have obtained the necessary technical data rights or certifications to
perform this work. These actions will help ensure that future requirements are competed
to the maximum extent practicable and aligned with operational timelines.
9. Market Research: Market research was conducted using CHESS, SAM.gov, and
open-source tools such as Google to identify vendors capable of maintaining and
warrantying the Laser Shot MMTS and WST systems.
Only Laser Shots proprietary technology and software are guaranteed to integrate
and function correctly with the existing simulators, as Laser Shot is the publisher and
sole owner of the software, firmware, and copyrights used in these systems. Therefore,
Laser Shot is the only source capable of ensuring full functionality and interoperability of
all simulator components.
The only vendor that responded to this market research was , a simulation
company that works under Google. On 06 June 2025, stated they cannot fix, or
update Laser Shot simulation equipment; instead, they submitted a proposal for eight
systems as an alternative to repairing existing systems.
10. Interested Sources: A Sources Sought Notice was posted on SAM.gov to identify
potential vendors capable of fulfilling this requirement. One business,
, responded with an expression of interest but did not submit
any follow-up capability statement or supporting documentation. As a result, there were
no qualified sources identified outside of the OEM, Laser Shot, Inc.
, who responded to the requiring activitys market research, stated that
they could not repair, update, or warranty the existing Laser Shot MMTS and WTS
systems. Instead, proposed a solution to replace the current systems with eight
new training systems. This alternative was not pursued because it would require
full replacement of Government owned equipment, incur significant additional cost, and
delay training due to procurement, installation , and instructor re-training.
11. Other Facts:
a. Procurement History. The Government previously procured and owns the
existing MMTS and WST systems, which were acquired under a different contract
5
Control No: MICC 2025-0123
vehicle by the requiring activity using NGREA funds. However, this current action is for
a refresh and extended warranty of the already-fielded systems and is being treated as
a new procurement action.
b. Laser Shot remains the only vendor that produces the MMTS and WST in their
current configuration and Laser Shot requires a refresh to their systems, performed by
their own technicians, prior to extending any warranty on their systems.
6

Control No: MICC 2025-0123
Approval
Based on the foregoing justification, I hereby approve the procurement of a Systems
Refresh and Warranty renewal for eight Mobile Marksmanship Training Simulators
(MMTS) and two Warrior Skills Trainers (WST) weapons simulators on an other than full
and open competition basis pursuant to the authority of Title 10 United States Code
Section 3204(a)(1), Only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will
satisfy agency requirements. The estimated value of the contract is $ with an
estimated delivery of no later than 1 December 2025. The approval is subject to
availability of funds, and provided that the services or supplies herein described have
otherwise been authorized for acquisition.
SCOTT D. KUKES
Alternate Advocate for Competition
U.S. Army Mission and Installation Contracting Command, JBSA Fort Sam Houston, TX
8

Defense Microelectronics Activity
4234 54th Street, McClellan, CA 95652
PWS # 25-5E6
Single Source Justification
1. Agency and Contracting Activity:
Office of Secretary of Defense, Defense Microelectronics Activity (DMEA).
2. Nature/Description of Action:
This acquisition is for a new Firm Fixed Price contract to procure production assembly and
testing for the DMEA-5521 Linear Variable Differential Transformer (LVDT) integrated circuit
(IC) (Re-Spin).
3. Description of Supplies/Services:
The contractor shall perform wafer dicing, packaging, and screening for the DMEA-5521 LVDT
IC (Re-Spin) in accordance with DMEA PWS 25-5E6. The anticipated dollar value of this
procurement is $203,000.00.
4. Authority Cited:
FAR 13.106-1(b)(1)(i), Soliciting from a single source.
5. Reason for Authority Cited:
DMEA has been supporting new construction efforts for the Virginia class submarines since
2005 by re-engineering the LVDT IC which is no longer available. This component is used in the
Submersible Electronic Limit Switch (SELS) assembly on various classes of submarines. This
task supports the package, assembly and test of the DMEA-5521 IC for the In-Service
Sustainment Fast Attack Submarines.
Wafer dicing, packaging, and screening for the DMEA-5521 LVDT IC was previously procured
from Golden Altos under contract HQ072722P0016. Moreover, Golden Altos has previously
provided services/supplies which include wafer dicing, supplying needed 18 pin sided-brazed
packages and lids, packaging and assembly, shipping tubes for packaged parts and Class Q/B
assembly process qualification testing and reports. Golden Altos can perform all desired services
in-house and do not require each task to be contracted separately. Additionally, Golden Altos is
International Traffic in Arms Regulation (ITAR) registered, which the US government mandates
that any company that manufactures, exports, as well as brokers of defense articles, defense
services, or a company that is involved with related technical data, must be ITAR compliant.
Furthermore, pursuing other contractors who do not have the combined experience and focus on
wafer dicing, packaging and screening as well as ITAR registration may result in damage to
DMEA’s supply of wafers, which is too great a risk for this project. Golden Altos' proven track
record, deep understanding of this project's complexities, and demonstrated execution
capabilities make a single-source award the most advantageous approach for the government.
This approach will significantly minimize the risk of unnecessary delays, control costs by
avoiding the complexities of managing unknown vendors with no technical background or
familiarity, and maximize the probability of another successful completion, ultimately ensuring
the availability of reliable LVDT IC components for critical defense applications.
DMEA # 26-03
6. Efforts to Obtain Competition:
No action was taken to obtain competition. The solicitation, accompanied by this approved
justification will be posted on SAM.gov. All responsible offers will be considered.
7. Fair and Reasonable Cost Determination:
I hereby determine that the anticipated cost to the Government for this contract action will be fair
and reasonable. This determination is based upon the Independent Government Estimate (IGE)
and previous purchases.
Typed Name: MIKE HALLOCK Date: ______________________
Title: Contracting Officer Signature: __________________
8. Market Research:
Internet searches for test labs who perform production, assembly and testing with focus in wafer
dicing, packaging and screening were researched. The result of the market research showed that
many contractors only perform printed circuit board fabrication and assembly and do not
perform IC packaging services in-house. However, based on previous purchases, Golden Altos
was identified as a company that can perform all desired services in-house and has previous
experience in LVDT IC packaging, assembly, and testing of limited production units with focus
in wafer dicing, packaging, assembly, screening, and qualification testing. Additionally, Golden
Altos is ITAR registered and a small business under NAICS 541330.
9. Other Facts:
Golden Altos has performed previous services under contracts H9400310P1022,
HQ072715P1524, HQ072720P0012 and HQ072722P0016.
10. Listing of Sources:
Golden Altos
www.goldenaltos.com
402 South Hillview Drive
Milpitas, CA 95035
POC: Ben Mendoza; (408) 956-1010 x110
bmendoza@goldenaltos.com
11. Actions to Increase Competition:
For subsequent acquisitions, market research will be conducted to identify potential vendors.
12. Contracting Officer Certification:
I certify that this justification is accurate and complete to the best of the contracting officer’s
knowledge and belief.
