Federal notice (Sources Sought), HEALTH AND HUMAN SERVICES, DEPARTMENT OF.FOOD AND DRUG ADMINISTRATION.FDA OFFICE OF ACQ  GRANT SVCS
Title: �Brand Name or Equal� Millipore-Sigma Steritest Symbio Laminar Flow Hood (LFH) pump
Solicitation number: FDA-SSN-132642
PSC: 6640; NAICS: 334516
Description: MARKET RESEARCH PURPOSES ONLY NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL OR SOLICITATION The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA), Office of Acquisitions and Grants Services (OAGS) is issuing this source sought announcement on behalf of the Irvine Medical Products Laboratory (IRVLMP), in order to determine if there are existing small business sources capable of providing a closed-filtration sterility pump. Other than small business concerns, especially vendors who may be able to offer domestic products, are also encouraged to submit a capability statement that provides company information, as well as information demonstrating that it can meet all of the minimum requirements included below, to include the country of manufacture of products offered. If your firm is considered a small business source under North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) Code 334516 - Analytical Laboratory Instrument Manufacturing; with a Small Business Size Standard of 1,000 employees and you believe that your firm would be able to provide the FDA with the supplies/services described below, please submit an email to Warren.Dutter@fda.hhs.gov. Background: The Food and Drug Administration (FDA), Irvine Medical Products Laboratory (IRVLMP) is a regulatory testing laboratory that is ISO 17025 accredited. The laboratory is responsible for microbiological testing of multiple pharmaceutical dosage forms which require sterility testing to determine if they comply with regulations. The laboratory performs sterility testing using Steritest ISL pumps manufactured by Millipore-Sigma. In order to remove existing bottlenecks in suitability testing which precedes sterility testing, the laboratory requires an additional closed-filtration sterility pump that is a �Brand Name or Equal� Millipore-Sigma Steritest Symbio Laminar Flow Hood (LFH) pump, to be used in a laminar air flow hood. The acquisition of a �Brand Name or Equal� Millipore-Sigma Steritest LFH pump will ensure compatibility with existing Millipore-Sigma Steritest ISL test kits, allowing their continued use with the new closed-filtration pump and enabling the laboratory to meet the suitability requirements specified in USP , the official compendial method for sterility testing. This is a Brand Name or Equal requirement. Products other than the specified Millipore-Sigma Steritest Symbio LFH pump are acceptable but shall meet all the salient characteristics contained in the Minimum Technical Requirements below. Minimum Technical Requirements (Salient Characteristics): The instrument shall consist of a peristaltic pump compatible with Steritest membrane filtration canister devices. The pump shall have a compact design to be used in a 6-foot biosafety cabinet or a laminar flow hood. The pump shall be equipped with a pump head capable of automatic opening and closing during operation. The pump housing is to be constructed of 316L stainless steel. The pump housing and components to be resistant to vaporized hydrogen peroxide gas. The peristaltic pump shall have adjustable speed control with a maximum speed of at least 200 rpm. The pump shall be equipped with an integrated pressure monitoring system to detect abnormal filtration conditions. The pump shall include a pressure regulation or limiting function to protect membrane integrity. The pump shall be equipped with a user interface capable of configuring instrument settings and displaying operating status. The interface shall include a display screen capable of presenting operating parameters and alerts. The pump shall be equipped with a timer function. The pump shall have the ability to store at least 50 filtration protocols. The pump shall be compatible with Millipore-Sigma, Steritest Symbio ISL Pump, Serial # ISL274, and Millipore-Sigma, Steritest Symbio ISL Pump, Serial # ISL268 Additional System Requirements: The components and equipment shall be newly manufactured, not used or refurbished, or previously used for demonstration. Offered systems shall be a turn-key solution i.e., the contractor shall be responsible for providing all hardware, components, instruments, computers, software, and that otherwise required to meet these specifications and the FDA�s stated need. The system and associated accessories shall include operations and maintenance manuals covering proper operation, routine maintenance, and troubleshooting for the system and controlling software. All manuals and documentation shall be provided in hard copy and/or electronic format. Systems shall be warranted for not less than one (1) year from FDA acceptance of the system(s). Warranty service shall include troubleshooting capabilities based on complete knowledge of the entire system, immediate access to replacement parts. Phone and email technical support shall be included for a minimum of one (1) year. Place of Performance: FOB Point Destination. All items shall include shipping, handling, and inside delivery to the destination identified herein. FDA/IRVLMP 19701 Fairchild Irvine, CA 92612 Period of Performance: Delivery shall occur within 90 calendar days from date of award. Responses to this Sources Sought shall unequivocally demonstrate that the respondent is regularly engaged in the sale of same or substantially similar product/service. Though the target audience is small business vendors or small businesses capable of supplying a U.S. service of a small business vendor or producer all interested parties may respond. At a minimum, responses shall include the following: Business name and bio, unique entity identification (UEI) number, business address, business website, business size status (i.e., SB, VOSB, SDVOSB, HUBZone SB, SDB, WOSB, LB), point of contact name, mailing address (if different from business address), phone number and email address. Provide this same information again if responding to provide a service offered by another firm. Past Performance information for the manufacturer and/or sale of same or substantially similar product and service or similar brand instruments to include date of sale, description, dollar value, client name, client address, client contact name, client point of contact mailing address (if different from that provided for client), client point of contact phone number, client point of contact email address, and name of the manufacturer (to include UEI number and size status) if not the respondent. Descriptive literature, brochures, marketing material, etc. detailing the nature of the product and service the responding firm is regularly engaged in manufacturing and/or selling. The offeror shall furnish sufficient technical information necessary for the Government to conclusively determine that the offered items/services meet the technical requirements identified above. If applicable, identification of Best in Class (BIC) contract information or other Government-wide or HHS-wide contracts that the equipment/service is available on. If applicable, identification of the firm's GSA Schedule contract(s) by Schedule number and SINs that are applicable to this potential requirement are also requested. If a large business, provide whether subcontracting opportunities exist for small business concerns. Standard commercial warranty and payment terms. Provide place of product manufacture or service performance and any other applicable information to enable review and analysis pertaining to the Buy American statute and requirements relating to Made in America in the event a nonavailability waiver request through the MIAO Digital Waiver Portal is needed. Informational pricing is desired. The Government is not responsible for locating or securing any information, not identified in the response. Interested Contractors must respond with capability statements which are due by email to the point of contact listed below on or before February 2, 2026, by 1:00 PM Central Time at the Food and Drug Administration, Field Operations Branch, FDA|OO|OFBA|OAGS|DAP, Attn: Warren Dutter, email warren.dutt

matters.text:
Federal notice (Combined Synopsis/Solicitation), DEPT OF DEFENSE.DEPT OF THE NAVY.NAVAL SURFACE WARFARE CENTER
Title: Sole Source to Ensign-Bickford Aerospace & Defense Company to Acquire 35 EA. Ejector Release Mechanisms-- See All Attachments.
Solicitation number: N61331-26-Q-JC08
PSC: 5999; NAICS: 332510
Description: Sole Source to Ensign-Bickford Aerospace & Defense Company to Acquire 35 EA. of Ejector Release Mechanisms for the Multi Mission Buoy (MMB). MK68 EJECTOR RELEASE MECHANISMS E4000-3361-1-PBOF ERM Linear Actuator, Part Number N83361-1 Quantity: 35 EACH The NSWC PCD has a requirement to acquire MK68 Ejector Release Mechanisms for the Multi Mission Buoy (MMB). This purchase is not suitable for full and open competition for the following reasons. a) Ensign-Bickford Aerospace & Defense (EBAD) is the sole developer and original equipment manufacturer (OEM) this item. As such they are the only source with sufficient knowledge of the linear actuator design and functionality to supply the component. b) After extensive testing in other relevant undersea weapon systems, non-successful testing of other actuator systems, and trade studies conducted by the development team, these actuators were designed into the MMB�s Anchor Separation Mechanism which created the system design. Replacing the actuators with another product or manufacturer will not only duplicate the effort and delay the delivery of the MMB due to required system redesign, Engineering Change Proposals (ECPs) and extensive testing, resulting in significant schedule delay and increase requirements of funding. The replacement will introduce undefined interface risks. c) The Government did not purchase or acquire the rights in data and design or a technical data package (TDP) for these items because they are commercial items developed to support the aerospace and defense industry at large. EBAD is the only source capable of meeting the requirement. As such, the Government does not expect significant savings through competition, and it is more advantageous for the Government to award on a sole source basis to EBAD.

entry; document reproduction, scanning, imaging, or destruction; operation, management, or maintenance of paper-
based or electronic mail rooms, file rooms, or libraries; and supervision in connection with functions listed herein.

management services are acquired will contain a requirement that:
(1) The support contractor not disclose any information;
(2) Individual employees are to be instructed by the support contractor regarding the sensitivity of the official
contract files;

competing to do so, to NAVSEA for the period of performance of its contract and for an additional three years
thereafter

information, irrespective of restrictive markings or the nature of the information submitted, by its file room

DEPARTMENT OF VETERANS AFFAIRS
Office of Acquisition and Logistics National Acquisition Center
P.O. Box 76 Hines, IL 60141
Justification for an Exception to Fair Opportunity - LOGICAL FOLLOW ON
(Implements the provisions and authorities of VA Class Deviation, modeled
FAR 16.507-6, “Exceptions to fair opportunity”)
(1) Identification of the agency and the contracting activity.
This Justification for an Exception to Fair Opportunity is on behalf of VISN 6, VAMC Durham, NC and
will be executed by the Veterans Affairs National Acquisition Center (NAC) located in Hines, Illinois.
(2) Nature and/or description of the action being approved.
This activity proposes to issue a sole-source delivery order as a logical follow - on against VA High Tech
Medical Equipment (HTME) Indefinite Delivery/Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) Contract No. SPE2D1-17-
D-023 as awarded to Siemens Medical Solutions USA, Inc. The proposed delivery order is to upgrade
the existing Siemens 3T MAGNETOM MRI System to the MAGNETOM Sola Fit with new
BioMatrix technology.
(3) A description of the supplies or services required to meet the agency’s needs, including the estimated
value.
The upgrade will include hardware and software upgrades, required to bring the entire system to
conformance. Upgrading to the MAGNETOM Sola Fit MRI system will upgrade the current system
from Windows 7 to Windows 10 Operating System (OS). Additionally, the MRI’s chiller is currently at
end of support. The chiller is a major component of the MRI system and replacement is required for
basic MRI functionality and conformity.
The total estimated value is $ 978,872.00
(4) An identification of the exception to fair opportunity (per FAR Subpart 16.507-6 (b)(3) and the
supporting rationale, including a demonstration that the proposed contractor’s unique
qualification or the nature of the acquisition requires use of the exception cited. If the
contracting officer uses the logical follow-on exception, the rationale shall describe why the
relationship between the initial order and the follow-on is logical (e.g., in terms of scope, period
of performance, or value).
The resulting delivery order will be issued on a sole-source basis as a logical follow - on to Contract
SPE2D1-17-D-023. The equipment was originally procured in FY2013, utilizing full competition via the
September Consolidation. The items were subsequently procured under delivery order VA797H-12-5-
0375 against PO 483-B20002, and installation was completed. The life cycle of this equipment is an
estimated 9 years; therefore, an upgrade currently is of much more benefit to the Government than a
full system replacement. This upgrade will provide current technology while maintaining components
of the original system, without requiring additional specialized site preparation.
The original equipment manufacturer (OEM), Siemens Medical Solutions USA, Inc, is the only contractor
1 | P a g e
who can provide the upgrade and as such is a logical follow-on to the original contract, due to the need
to operate with existing OEM’S components and the proprietary nature of the hardware and software.
The OEM is the only organization capable of owning trade information about the system and as such is
the only one qualified to provide and perform the upgrade, with the expectation that the systems will
continue operating as expected in a safe manner.
(5) A determination by the Contracting Officer is that the anticipated cost to the Government
will be fair and reasonable.
All items are currently on Siemens Medical Solutions USA, Inc. IDIQ contract SPE2D1-17-D- 023. The
prices under Siemens Medical Solutions USA, Inc. IDIQ contract remained the same from when they were
awarded. The quoted price for each item is at or below the IDIQ not-to-exceed contract price, and the
IDIQ contract pricing has been determined fair and reasonable by a contracting officer in accordance with
FAR Subpart 15.4.
(6) Any other facts supporting the justification.
This upgrade will take the current system to Windows 11 and upgrade the chiller, which is necessary to
bring the Greenville VA clinic to the current performance level. Upgrading the current MRI system to
improve image quality/resolution, acquisition time, and dose reduction.
(7) A statement of the actions, if any, the agency may take steps to remove or overcome any
barriers that led to the exception of fair opportunity before any subsequent acquisition of the
supplies or services is made.
All prospective delivery orders are completed by all contract holders. Once an order is placed for
proprietary equipment, it is generally not possible to compete follow-on acquisitions for upgrades
because the system to be upgraded is proprietary in nature. Future requirements will be handled on
a case-by-case basis, and all attempts will be made to provide fair opportunity to all schedule
holders.
(8) The contracting officer’s certification that the justification is accurate and complete to the
best of the contracting officer’s knowledge and belief.
By signing this justification, the required activity hereby certifies that the justification is accurate and
complete to the best of their knowledge.
(9) Evidence that any supporting data is the responsibility of the technical or requirements
personnel (e.g., verifying the Government’s minimum needs or requirements or other rationale
for an exception to fair opportunity) and which form a basis for the justification has been
certified as complete and accurate by the technical or requirements personnel.
The technical information contained in the proposal was reviewed and certified
by the facility’s Biomedical Engineer and clinical end user and determined to meet the Government’s
minimum requirements. By signing this justification, the required activity hereby certifies that the
justification is accurate and complete to the best of their knowledge.
(10) A written determination by the approving official that one of the circumstances listed within the above
cited FAR Part applies to the order.
Based on the information contained herein, a determination has been made that this requirement meets the
logical follow on FAR exception since the planned acquisition is a follow-on to the original delivery order
and the contract holders were given a fair opportunity to be considered for the original delivery order, via
competition.

matters.title: High Definition (HD) Camera and Cables Purchase (MVSS-R)
matters.text:
Federal notice (Justification), TRANSPORTATION, DEPARTMENT OF.FEDERAL AVIATION ADMINISTRATION.6973GH FRANCHISE ACQUISITION SVCS
Title: High Definition (HD) Camera and Cables Purchase (MVSS-R)
Solicitation number: 6973GH-25-J-MVSS
PSC: 5998; NAICS: 334511
Description: Title of Procurement High Definition (HD) Camera and Cables Purchase (MVSS-R) Nature of Procurement Action The Federal Aviation Administration Logistics Center (FAALC) requires the purchase of Mobile Video Surveillance System with Radar (MVSS-R) HD Camera and cables. These cameras and cables will be used as spares and deployed to the United States Southern Border in support of the United States Customs and Border Protection Program (CBP). PVP is the only source that can provide the parts necessary to satisfy this requirement. PVP president confirmed that all their components and configurations are proprietary through an email dated November 3, 2025. Description of Supplies/Services This effort is to procure HD Cameras and cables through PVP for the MVSS-R. Part Numbers Description Quantity 115910 HD Camera Assembly 2 113109 Cable, SAP to Radar 3 112352 Cable, SAP to Camera 3 Authority Authority for single source procurement is provided by FAA Acquisition Management System (AMS) policy section 3.2.2.4. Rationale Supporting Use of a Single Source It is in the best interest of the FAALC to use a single source to purchase the HD Cameras and cables of the MVSS-R, because the subject requirement is based on the safety of the CBP agents and security of U.S. southern border. Utilization of this sole source justification avoids excessive delays to permit open competition, collection of quotes, the evaluation of market conditions and other necessary steps that may cause an increase to the cost of the procurement. Impact. If this single source service cannot be provided it will impact the national security of the United States and the security of the CBP agents. CBP�s mission readiness of protecting the U.S. borders will also be impacted. These impacts cannot be tolerated. Specialized Expertise. As PVP designed and produced this HD Camera model and cables, PVP is the only source that has the capability of successfully providing this material. If the FAALC were to pursue another source, there is a potential that the cameras would not be configured correctly. This would require PVP to provide a re-work of what another vendor had tried to accomplish Standardization. As the HD Camera configuration and software are proprietary to PVP, it is necessary to use the parts and services that are the same form, fit, and function for replacement. The HD Camera is critical to the operational availability of the Mobile Video Surveillance System � Radar (MVSS-R) version. Any degradation of performance, or incompatibility of configuration/software, could have detrimental impacts on U.S. border security. CBP, nor the FAALC, maintains the technical ability to integrate parts into this system that is not currently in the system configuration baseline. As such, there are no existing Government processes to qualify additional sources for the manufacture of compatible spare parts for existing PVP components. Patents, Proprietary Data, and Unique Items. PVP is the only known source that can provide the required HD Camera and cables as the software and configuration are proprietary to PVP and only PVP has the specifications information. PVP president confirmed that all their components and configurations are proprietary through an email dated November 3, 2025. When these systems were procured, the Government did not purchase all necessary technical, logistics, and maintenance data needed to manufacture the camera and cables. The data and knowledge necessary to manufacture the camera and cables within the MVSS-R systems is the exclusive proprietary property of PVP. PVP has not licensed this data or knowledge to any other vendors. PVP will not sell or otherwise provide data, knowledge, or other intellectual property necessary to compete the required support. Market Analysis An Internet search was conducted by the Requiring Organization (AJW-L500) to see if any other sources could be located, to which no other sources could be located. A market survey was posted to sam.gov with a closing date of May 13, 2025. This market survey was for HD camera purchase and repair. Two potential offerors responded to the market survey by none of the respondents provided the requested information in the market survey. Furthermore, these two vendors do not have access to original equipment manufacturer (OEM) proprietary data. Other Facts Supporting Use of Single Source The single source nature of the required services from PVP is not anticipated to change during the life of the system. CBP estimates the life of the MVSS-R system will be in use for at least five more years. The proprietary camera and cables will be used in these systems until they are deactivated. If there is a future requirement for the same material the FAALC will reengage industry through market research to determine if the market has changed.

Description: The 82d Contracting Squadron, Sheppard AFB, TX intends to award a sole source, firm-fixed price purchase order for replacement parts to repair a Kardex Remstar Vertical Lift Module (VLM) to Southwest Solutions Group, 2535-B E, State Hwy 121, Suite 110, Louisville, Texas 75056. The statutory authority which permits other than full and open competition for this acquisition is 10 United States Code (USC) 2304 (c)(1), as implemented by FAR 13.106-1(b). This authority is supported by an approved Single Source Justification. It is the Government's intent to proceed with this sole-source action. The applicable NAICS code is 335312. The size standard as defined by the U.S. Small Business Administration is 1,250 employees. THIS NOTICE OF INTENT IS NOT A SOLICITATION, REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL OR A REQUEST FOR QUOTATION. A solicitation package will NOT be issued. Requests for copies of a solicitation in response to this notice will not be honored or acknowledged. Information received in response to this notice will be considered solely for the purpose of determining whether conducting a competitive procurement in the future is in the best interest of the Government. All information submitted should support the offeror's capability to provide the services required, and shall be furnished at no cost or obligation to the Government. Responses must be in writing and must provide clear and concise documentation indicating an offeror's capability to provide these services. Verbal responses are not acceptable and will not be considered. Responses and questions shall be received via email by e-mail, ashley.green.18@us.af.mil and kiana.perry@us.af.mil NLT 19 January 2026.

DEPARTMENT OF THE AIR FORCE
AIR EDUCATION AND TRAINING COMMAND
08 January 2026
MEMORANDUM FOR 82 CONS/PKAB
FROM: 82 TRSS/CC
SUBJECT: Brand Name Requirements Justification (Ref: Kardex Remstar Vertical Lift
Modules, Southwest Solutions Group)
1. Description of the Supplies/Services: In accordance with agency objectives, the 82
TRSS/TXTSD Trainer Development Flight has a need to purchase parts to repair a Kardex
Remstar Vertical Lift Modules (VLM). The parts must be new Kardex Remstar replacement
parts and services must be performed by an authorized factory-trained technician authorized by
the manufacturer to inspect, report, and maintain all vertical lift/shuttles.
2. Efforts to Obtain Competition: Kardex Remstar LLC is the manufacturer and a
government contractor #47QSMA21D08QV. Southwest Solutions Group and is the exclusive
authorized factory sales and service dealer for all Office & Government Kardex Remstar in the
state of Texas. No other companies are authorized in this area.
3. Market Research: To preclude necessity for future sole-source of the same supplies and
services, market research was done to ensure availability of supplies and services are not limited
to one company. Currently, no other known contractors provide this specific brand of VLM. No
other authorized factory-trained technicians for Kardex in the Texas area could be located.
4. Other Factors: All Trainer Development fabrication employees are trained to use Kardex
Remstar VLM systems thus greatly reducing the training time for a different manufacturer’s
system. We currently have four VLM systems in our facility that have greatly enhanced our
storage capacities. Southwest Solutions Group also performs all periodic maintenance and
repairs on our current VLM’s and has an outstanding record with us for both customer service
and quick reaction and repair times.
5. A Statement Of The Actions, If Any, The Agency May Take To Remove Or Overcome
Any Barriers To Competition Before Making Subsequent Acquisitions For The Supplies
Or Services Required: In order to help promote competition, the Government will continue to
reach out to Kardex Remstar to inquire if other authorized technicians have become available to
service the machines in this area.

Marine Corps Systems Command

2. Description of the Action Being Approved
This Justification and Approval (J&A) authorizes and approves, on
a noncompetitive basis, award of a sole source contract to
Kongsberg Defence and Aerospace (KDA) for the procurement of 175
RT-20 Turrets for the Amphibious Combat Vehicle Medium Caliber
Cannon (ACV 30) variant.
3. Description of Supplies and Services
This requirement is for the procurement of 175 RT-20 Turrets,
spare repair parts, support and test equipment, and field support
representative support for the Amphibious Combat Vehicle Medium
Caliber Cannon (ACV 30) variant for integration and fielding
beginning in and ending no later than
. The ACV-30 variant is one of four variants of the
ACV family of vehicles for the Marine Corps. The other three
are the personnel, command and control, and recovery variants.
The ACV-30 platform fulfills a capability that enables the
Marine Corps to perform a core agency mission - conduct
amphibious operations. The Independent Government Cost Estimate
(IGCE) for the procurement of 175 RT-20 Turrets, spare parts, support
and test equipment and field support representative support is
Estimated Dollar Value
The IGCE for the procurement of 175 RT-20 Turrets, spare parts,
support and test equipment and field support representative support
is . The funding table below shows the funding profile in
millions of dollars by Fiscal Year (FY) and appropriation type.
1

each type of turret. It is also estimated that a sole source
procurement with KDA will save an additional
through the elimination of BAE’s overhead costs and lower labor
costs associated with the procurement and installation of the
RT-20 Turret.
The schedule delay would negatively impact the production
schedule and introduce additional costs to keep the vehicle
assembly line open until the new turrets are produced and
installed. Further, the Marine Corps would be without this
critical weapon systems for at least . This in
turn would negatively impact the Marine Corps current plan to
start fielding the ACV-30 variant by . Finally, the
substantial duplication of costs would not be recovered through
any type of competition.
Accordingly, based on the above analysis, KDA is the only known
capable source that can meet the Marine Corps’ requirements.
6. Description of Efforts Made to Solicit Offers from as Many
Offerors as Practicable
A sources sought notice, M67854-24-I-0114, was issued on 31 May
2024. The notice assessed industry’s capability to manufacture and
provide ACV-30 Turrets, associated special tooling, associated
training, field service representatives for the turret
integration, work instructions for turret integration compatible
with the ACV-30 MRV, as well as subsequent fielding support. Two
responses were received on 14 June 2024, one of which was from
KDA. Both vendors stated they are able to meet the specifications
as defined in the sources sought notice and are capable of
delivering the required 175 turrets according to the required
schedule. However, only KDA has a turret that has been fully
integrated on an ACV-30 chassis, has completed prototype testing,
and is undergoing developmental testing. The other Contractor’s
turret does not currently possess the qualifications (i.e.,
completion of required ACV-30 compliance tests, Developmental, and
Operational testing) needed to circumvent the cost and time
invested in the already conducted prototype and developmental
testing for KDA’s RT-20 Turret.
Based on the Government’s assessment of the responses received,
the Government determined KDA is the only known source able to
fulfill the requirement for the procurement of ACV-30 Turrets,
associated special tooling, associated training, field service
representatives for the turret integration, work instructions for
turret integration compatible with the ACV-30, as well as
3
subsequent fielding support. Additionally, in accordance with FAR
5.201, notice of the proposed contract action will be made
available through SAM.gov prior to solicitation.
7. Determination of Fair and Reasonable Cost
The Contracting Officer has determined that the anticipated cost
to the Government of the supplies/services covered by the J&A
will be fair and reasonable.
8. Actions to Remove Barriers to Future Competition
If the Marine Corps decides to increase the acquisition
objective of the ACV-30 beyond the initial 175 vehicles, PEO LS
will assess whether competition for future requirements is
feasible. Any future actions will be reviewed by PEO LS to offer
competition to the greatest extent possible.

matters.text:
Federal notice (Special Notice), DEPT OF DEFENSE.DEPT OF THE ARMY.W7NK USPFO ACTIVITY MTANG 120
Title: Intent to Award a Sole Source Contract - Monaco D-21 Fire Alarm Control System Upgrades
Solicitation number: 
PSC: 6350; NAICS: 334220
Description: This is a notice of intent to award a sole-source, firm-fixed-price contract to Monaco Enterprises, Inc., located in Spokane, WA. The120th Airlift Wing has a requirement for the procurement and installation of equipment to upgrade the existing Monaco D-21 Fire Alarm Control systems installed base-wide at the 120th Airlift Wing, Great Falls, MT. The required supplies and services include, but are not limited to, proprietary Monaco D-21 system components, hardware, software, and the necessary factory-certified technical labor for installation, programming, testing, and commissioning to ensure a fully functional and compliant system. The proposed contract action is for supplies and services for which the Government intends to solicit and negotiate with only one source under the authority of Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 6.302-1, "Only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements." Market research has confirmed that Monaco Enterprises, Inc. is the original equipment manufacturer (OEM) and the sole provider of the proprietary D-21 fire alarm system. The existing infrastructure at the 120th Airlift Wing is comprised entirely of Monaco D-21 systems. The hardware components, system software, and programming tools required for maintenance and upgrades are proprietary to Monaco Enterprises, Inc. Furthermore, only Monaco-employed technicians are factory-trained and certified to install, program, and service these systems. Use of any other equipment would require the complete and cost-prohibitive replacement of the entire fire alarm infrastructure to maintain system integrity and UL certification. Therefore, Monaco Enterprises, Inc. is the only source capable of meeting this requirement without causing unacceptable delays and substantial duplication of cost that would not be recovered through competition. This notice of intent is not a request for competitive proposals or quotations. However, all responsible sources may submit a capability statement demonstrating their ability to provide the required supplies and services. A determination by the Government not to compete this proposed contract based upon responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. Information received will be considered solely for the purpose of determining whether to conduct a competitive procurement. Interested parties must submit a capability statement in writing to the contracting office by 8:00 AM Mountain Standard Time on 26 January 2026. The statement must provide clear and convincing evidence that the respondent has the necessary technical expertise, proprietary data, and certifications to meet the Government's requirement as described herein. The capability statement must include, at a minimum: Company name, address, CAGE code, and UEI number. Point of contact with name, telephone number, and email address. Evidence of ability to provide UL 864 Listed components that are 100% compatible and interoperable with the existing Monaco D-21 system. Evidence of access to proprietary Monaco software and programming tools. Proof that technical staff possess current factory certifications from Monaco Enterprises, Inc. to perform installation and programming on D-21 systems. Relevant past performance information on similar government or commercial contracts. All capability statements must be submitted via email to: Primary Contact: Anthony F. Barille, Contracting Officert, at anthony.barille@us.af.mil Telephone inquiries will not be accepted. All correspondence must be in writing.

Justification for an Exception to Fair Opportunity – Logical Follow-On
(Implements the provisions and authorities of VA Class Deviation, modeled
FAR 16.507-6, “Exceptions to fair opportunity”)
(1) Identification of the agency and the contracting activity.
This Justification for an Exception to Fair Opportunity is on behalf of VISN 16, VAMC Pineville, LA and
will be executed by the Veterans Affairs National Acquisition Center (NAC) located in Hines, Illinois.
(2) Nature and/or description of the action being approved.
This activity proposes to issue a sole-source delivery order as a logical follow-on against Indefinite
Delivery/Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) Contract No. SPE2D1-17-D-0022 as awarded to Canon Medical
Systems USA, Inc.
(3) A description of the supplies or services required to meet the agency’s needs, including the estimated
value.
This request is for an upgrade of the existing Canon Toshiba Aquilion One that has reached the end-of-life
cycle. The upgrade will include hardware and software upgrades, required to bring the entire system to
conformance.
The total estimated value is $ 794,149.00.
(4) An identification of the exception to fair opportunity (per FAR Subpart 16.507-6 (b)(3)) and the
supporting rationale, including a demonstration that the proposed contractor’s unique
qualification or the nature of the acquisition requires use of the exception cited. If the
contracting officer uses the logical follow-on exception, the rationale shall describe why the
relationship between the initial order and the follow-on is logical (e.g., in terms of scope, period
of performance, or value).
The resulting delivery order will be issued on a sole-source basis as a logical follow - on to
Contract V797P-6033B. The equipment was originally procured in FY2014, utilizing full
competition via the September Consolidation. The items were subsequently procured under
delivery order VA797H-13-J- 0220 against PO 502-B25016. This upgrade will provide current
technology while maintaining components of the original system, without requiring additional
specialized site preparation.
The original equipment manufacturer (OEM), Canon Medical Systems USA, Inc., is the only contractor
who can provide the upgrade and as such is a logical follow-on to the original contract, due to the need
to operate with existing OEM’S components and the proprietary nature of the hardware and software.
The OEM is the only organization capable of owning trade information about the system and as such is
the only one qualified to provide and perform the upgrade, with the expectation that the systems will

continue operating as expected in a safe manner.
(5) A determination by the Contracting Officer is that the anticipated cost to the Government
will be fair and reasonable.
All items are currently on Canon Medical Systems USA, Inc. IDIQ contract SPE2D1-17-D-0022. Even
though there have been increases to industry and market changes because of the COVID-19 pandemic,
the prices under the IDIQ contract remain the same from when they were awarded. The quoted price for
each item is at or below the IDIQ not-to- exceed contract price, and the IDIQ contract pricing has been
determined fair and reasonable by a contracting officer in accordance with FAR 13.106-3, 14.408-2 and
Subpart 15.4.
(6) Any other facts supporting the justification.
This is a medical device which received FDA 510K medical device certification in the specific
configuration which the OEM manufactured it. This information is known only to the OEM.

barriers that led to the exception of fair opportunity before any subsequent acquisition of the

provide fair opportunity to all schedule holders.

best of the contracting officer’s knowledge and belief.

DEFENSE LOGISTICS AGENCY
HEADQUARTERS
8725 JOHN J. KINGMAN ROAD
FORT BELVOIR, VIRGINIA 22060-6221
CLASS JUSTIFICATION FOR OTHER THAN
FULL AND OPEN COMPETITION
I. CONTRACTING ACTIVITY
This Class Justification and Approval (J&A) is submitted to request authority for Other Than
Full and Open Competition to support requirements generated by multiple customers, including
but not limited to the United States Air Force (USAF), the Defense Logistics Agency (DLA),
and Foreign Military Sales (FMS) and any/all DoD customers worldwide via a Captains of
Industry (COI) DLA formal solicitation. The contracting authority for this requirement is DLA
Aviation, Strategic Acquisition and Programs Directorate in Richmond, VA.
II. NATURE AND/OR DESCRIPTION OF THE ACTION BEING PROCESSED
Due to the circumstances described herein, this activity requests authority for the negotiation and
award of multiple contracts on a sole-source basis with Lockheed Martin Corporation (LM) for
performance-based supply chain management and logistics support of aircraft and systems
manufactured by LM including, but not limited to, the F16, C-5, C-130, F35, MH-60, P-3, F-22,
Patriot Guidance Enhanced Missile, CHAPARRAL Guided Missile Equipment Carrier, Sniper
Advanced Targeting Pod, Electro-Optics Targeting System, Distributed Aperture System
Window Panel, Q-70 Radar, MK41 Vertical Launch System, Aegis Cruiser, Sonar Buoys,
MEADS Radar, Sea Bass Torpedo and Stinger Missile. In addition to parts, the support may
include holistic support and logistics management services, including but not limited to
wholesale supply and logistics support, inventory management, maintenance planning,
configuration management, repair development, repair of repairables for Service customers, and
sustainment engineering associated with a LM aircraft, system, and/or end item. It may also
include additive manufacturing solutions, depot maintenance, depot-level support, material
management, engineering support and sustainment elements, packaging, storage, transportation,
reliability improvements, and field engineering support. The all-encompassing goal will be to
improve material and services availability for supported platforms. The acquisition will be
conducted using Other Than Full and Open Competition as prescribed by FAR 6.302-1, Only
One Responsible Source and No Other Supplies or Services Will Satisfy Agency Requirements.
The intent of the acquisition team is to award overarching terms and conditions that will remain
valid for 20 years. This duration of terms and conditions will enable the Strategic Contract
Division of DLA Aviation to award a variety of long-term subsumable contracts under those
terms and conditions. Such contracts will consist of one five (5) year base period and one five
Source Selection Information – See FAR 2.101 & 3.104
(5) year option period. In accordance with FAR Part 10, additional market research will be
conducted prior to the exercise of the five-year options. However, in no case will any of those
subsumable contracts exceed the ten-year period authorized by 10 U.S.C. 2304a(f), unless
appropriate approval is obtained.
This sole source requirement will be negotiated with the following company:
Lockheed Martin Corporation
100 Global Innovation Circle
Orlando, FL 32825-5002
The Government anticipates purchasing material and services under these contracts from, but not
limited to, the following LM CAGE codes:
02769 52088 1FUD6 64059 4A3W7 23892
16331 77609 06JJ5 11530 23917 8X044
38597 0WWN8 26629 94271 563J1
067V1 04939 56232 04WF2 74703
98897 25500 90536 08PL1 6U917
03640 55316 036W7 1NM30 02GJ5
0A489 24900 81755 1WL60 0L1E5
03538 54274 029K9 2AAC2 1G2P4
16848 80070 13030 3CUQ0 4A3W7
The length of the overarching terms and conditions contract period, as well as each base period
and term of the subsumable contracts, are considered optimal for the following reasons:
• It affords the Government flexibility and latitude to enter a variety of contracts for
present and projected needs while reducing the need for clause negotiation for
repetitive similar type efforts.
• It facilitates agility for the Government and supplier to adapt to unforeseen
requirements that may arise within the contract period.
• It affords the contractor sufficient time to recoup initial investments associated with
facilities, parts, obsolescence issues, and reliability management.
• It affords the contractor opportunities to enter long term commitments with
subcontractors (including organic depots) in order to provide sustained
efficiencies/economies of scale to the military service user.
• It enables the contractor to implement logistical and technical changes required to
realize reliability improvements.
• It allows for the elimination of duplicative contract and program administration costs
for like and similar items.
• It affords the supplier opportunity to leverage investment in support processes across
similar items, thereby saving additional costs.
Source Selection Information – See FAR 2.101 & 3.104


• Performance Based support will consist of logistics management, which includes
wholesale supply planning and support, depot-level consumable support, depot-level
repairable support, material management, engineering support and sustainment elements,
packaging, storage, transportation, reliability improvements, and field engineering
support for a to-be-determined population of items with frequent or recurring demand.
LM will be required to meet supply chain performance-based metrics for material
availability and backorder age for this population likely in a similar format to the current
Supplier Initiated Orders (SIO) construct. The performance metrics are expected to be
based on the level of demand for the individual NSN and will be measured against
DLA’s current performance baseline. Examples of potential contract metrics include but
are not limited to the following: improvement in production lead time (PLT), production
capacity, forecasting and material availability (MA), reduction of administrative lead
time (ALT), unfilled orders (UFOs), on time delivery (OTD), and backorder age.
• Stock support may include items that are unit priced and ordered at lead time like current
long-term contracts.
• Transactional support may include items that are priced on an ad-hoc basis using an
expedited pricing methodology to be negotiated. Such NSNs have been previously
identified and will be recertified as LM sole source items prior to being procured.
IV. STATUTORY AUTHORITY PERMITTING OTHER THAN FULL AND OPEN
COMPETITION
Use of Other than Full and Open Competition is authorized by 10 U.S.C. 2304(c)(1) and FAR
6.302-1, as there is only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy
agency requirements.
V. DEMONSTRATION THAT THE CONTRACTOR’S UNIQUE QUALIFICATIONS
OR NATURE OF THE ACQUISITION REQUIRES THE USE OF THE AUTHORITY
CITED ABOVE
The acquisition is restricted to the only source of supply known to have the capability of
furnishing the required support – Lockheed Martin Corporation. In addition to spares support,
this Class J&A covers performance-based support, forecasting, supply chain management, and
related efforts for LM aviation systems. Only LM can provide the necessary expertise, capacity,
capability, and proficiency to perform this overall effort. LM is the only company which
possesses the requisite engineering expertise, configuration management, tooling, and
management knowledge to ensure that items conform to the proper form, fit and function, thus
keeping complex platforms reliable and safe. LM is the only source that possesses the full range
of technical data (some of which is proprietary) required to manufacture the full range of items
that are covered by this Class J&A. LM is the only contractor that can leverage the production
capability and has an in-depth knowledge of the diverse and diminishing vendor base capable of
supporting these platforms at the required level of support. For the sole source material provided
for direct platform support, it has been determined the Government does not have complete,
unrestricted data packages available. Additionally, LM has established internal production
processes and qualified various industrial support contractors as suppliers. Regarding the
Source Selection Information – See FAR 2.101 & 3.104
material support for the repair of components at DoD repair depots, LM’s overall systems
engineering knowledge and technical expertise in the various platforms make it singularly
capable of performing the full scope of the depot support requirement. No contractor other than
LM, the sole manufacturer and integrator of the various platforms to be supported, has the
capability to perform all the requirements of the comprehensive performance-based supply chain
management program. LM is the only entity with the full data rights to provide all the sole
source material as well as the OEM-based data and systems engineering expertise to fully
support the complete range of depot maintenance requirements across the full spectrum of the
LM provided weapon systems.
The key overarching objective of these contracts is to maximize the availability/use of the
various weapon systems by providing timely material support through initiatives such as
incentivizing reliability improvements, streamlining supply chain management, and improving
maintenance processes and procedures. In order to meet this overarching objective, the provider
must have the ability to drive changes into the platform configurations and, more importantly,
understand, analyze, and assess the implications—both in terms of weapon system performance
and operational usage—of any potential configuration change. To do so, this effort may require
engineering and logistics support personnel with an unfettered ability to reach back to the OEM,
LM, to support engineering investigations, fault detection and isolation, repair development,
modification development, supportability analysis, and the associated technical documentation
development and support. LM is the only source that can provide this comprehensive capability.
Only LM has personnel with the requisite breadth and depth of experience and understanding of
the totality of technical data necessary to fulfill this requirement and ensure the currency,
accuracy, and completeness of the technical data and associated databases. Finally, once
modifications or process changes are made by the Government, only LM has the existing
infrastructure to ensure timely execution of such changes, including the ability to efficiently
execute changes simultaneously into production and fielded systems.
Furthermore, by having only one contractor responsible for the bulk of supply chain
management, the Government has a single focal point with management accountability and
contractual responsibility. No other source has the long-standing business relationships with the

Full and Open Competition to support requirements generated by multiple customers, including
but not limited to the United States Air Force (USAF), the Defense Logistics Agency (DLA),
and Foreign Military Sales (FMS) and any/all DoD customers worldwide via a Captains of

award of multiple contracts on a sole-source basis with Lockheed Martin Corporation (LM) for
performance-based supply chain management and logistics support of aircraft and systems
manufactured by LM including, but not limited to, the F16, C-5, C-130, F35, MH-60, P-3, F-22,
Patriot Guidance Enhanced Missile, CHAPARRAL Guided Missile Equipment Carrier, Sniper
Advanced Targeting Pod, Electro-Optics Targeting System, Distributed Aperture System
Window Panel, Q-70 Radar, MK41 Vertical Launch System, Aegis Cruiser, Sonar Buoys,
MEADS Radar, Sea Bass Torpedo and Stinger Missile. In addition to parts, the support may
include holistic support and logistics management services, including but not limited to
wholesale supply and logistics support, inventory management, maintenance planning,
configuration management, repair development, repair of repairables for Service customers, and
sustainment engineering associated with a LM aircraft, system, and/or end item. It may also
include additive manufacturing solutions, depot maintenance, depot-level support, material
management, engineering support and sustainment elements, packaging, storage, transportation,
reliability improvements, and field engineering support. The all-encompassing goal will be to
improve material and services availability for supported platforms. The acquisition will be
conducted using Other Than Full and Open Competition as prescribed by FAR 6.302-1, Only
One Responsible Source and No Other Supplies or Services Will Satisfy Agency Requirements.

valid for 20 years. This duration of terms and conditions will enable the Strategic Contract
Division of DLA Aviation to award a variety of long-term subsumable contracts under those
terms and conditions. Such contracts will consist of one five (5) year base period and one five
Source Selection Information – See FAR 2.101 & 3.104
(5) year option period. In accordance with FAR Part 10, additional market research will be
conducted prior to the exercise of the five-year options. However, in no case will any of those
subsumable contracts exceed the ten-year period authorized by 10 U.S.C. 2304a(f), unless
appropriate approval is obtained.
This sole source requirement will be negotiated with the following company:
Lockheed Martin Corporation

Orlando, FL 32825-5002

The length of the overarching terms and conditions contract period, as well as each base period
and term of the subsumable contracts, are considered optimal for the following reasons:
• It affords the Government flexibility and latitude to enter a variety of contracts for
present and projected needs while reducing the need for clause negotiation for
repetitive similar type efforts.
• It facilitates agility for the Government and supplier to adapt to unforeseen
requirements that may arise within the contract period.
• It affords the contractor sufficient time to recoup initial investments associated with
facilities, parts, obsolescence issues, and reliability management.
• It affords the contractor opportunities to enter long term commitments with
subcontractors (including organic depots) in order to provide sustained
efficiencies/economies of scale to the military service user.
• It enables the contractor to implement logistical and technical changes required to
realize reliability improvements.
• It allows for the elimination of duplicative contract and program administration costs
for like and similar items.
• It affords the supplier opportunity to leverage investment in support processes across
similar items, thereby saving additional costs.
Source Selection Information – See FAR 2.101 & 3.104


• Performance Based support will consist of logistics management, which includes
wholesale supply planning and support, depot-level consumable support, depot-level
repairable support, material management, engineering support and sustainment elements,
packaging, storage, transportation, reliability improvements, and field engineering
support for a to-be-determined population of items with frequent or recurring demand.
LM will be required to meet supply chain performance-based metrics for material
availability and backorder age for this population likely in a similar format to the current
Supplier Initiated Orders (SIO) construct. The performance metrics are expected to be
based on the level of demand for the individual NSN and will be measured against
DLA’s current performance baseline. Examples of potential contract metrics include but
are not limited to the following: improvement in production lead time (PLT), production
capacity, forecasting and material availability (MA), reduction of administrative lead
time (ALT), unfilled orders (UFOs), on time delivery (OTD), and backorder age.
• Stock support may include items that are unit priced and ordered at lead time like current
long-term contracts.
• Transactional support may include items that are priced on an ad-hoc basis using an
expedited pricing methodology to be negotiated. Such NSNs have been previously
identified and will be recertified as LM sole source items prior to being procured.

COMPETITION
Use of Other than Full and Open Competition is authorized by 10 U.S.C. 2304(c)(1) and FAR
6.302-1, as there is only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy
agency requirements.

OR NATURE OF THE ACQUISITION REQUIRES THE USE OF THE AUTHORITY
CITED ABOVE

furnishing the required support – Lockheed Martin Corporation. In addition to spares support,
this Class J&A covers performance-based support, forecasting, supply chain management, and
related efforts for LM aviation systems. Only LM can provide the necessary expertise, capacity,
capability, and proficiency to perform this overall effort. LM is the only company which
possesses the requisite engineering expertise, configuration management, tooling, and
management knowledge to ensure that items conform to the proper form, fit and function, thus
keeping complex platforms reliable and safe. LM is the only source that possesses the full range
of technical data (some of which is proprietary) required to manufacture the full range of items
that are covered by this Class J&A. LM is the only contractor that can leverage the production
capability and has an in-depth knowledge of the diverse and diminishing vendor base capable of
supporting these platforms at the required level of support. For the sole source material provided
for direct platform support, it has been determined the Government does not have complete,
unrestricted data packages available. Additionally, LM has established internal production
processes and qualified various industrial support contractors as suppliers. Regarding the

material support for the repair of components at DoD repair depots, LM’s overall systems
engineering knowledge and technical expertise in the various platforms make it singularly
capable of performing the full scope of the depot support requirement. No contractor other than
LM, the sole manufacturer and integrator of the various platforms to be supported, has the
capability to perform all the requirements of the comprehensive performance-based supply chain
management program. LM is the only entity with the full data rights to provide all the sole
source material as well as the OEM-based data and systems engineering expertise to fully
support the complete range of depot maintenance requirements across the full spectrum of the
LM provided weapon systems.
The key overarching objective of these contracts is to maximize the availability/use of the
various weapon systems by providing timely material support through initiatives such as
incentivizing reliability improvements, streamlining supply chain management, and improving
maintenance processes and procedures. In order to meet this overarching objective, the provider
must have the ability to drive changes into the platform configurations and, more importantly,
understand, analyze, and assess the implications—both in terms of weapon system performance
and operational usage—of any potential configuration change. To do so, this effort may require
engineering and logistics support personnel with an unfettered ability to reach back to the OEM,

modification development, supportability analysis, and the associated technical documentation
development and support. LM is the only source that can provide this comprehensive capability.

the totality of technical data necessary to fulfill this requirement and ensure the currency,
accuracy, and completeness of the technical data and associated databases. Finally, once
modifications or process changes are made by the Government, only LM has the existing
infrastructure to ensure timely execution of such changes, including the ability to efficiently
execute changes simultaneously into production and fielded systems.

DEFENSE LOGISTICS AGENCY

8725 JOHN J. KINGMAN ROAD
FORT BELVOIR, VIRGINIA 22060-6221
CLASS JUSTIFICATION FOR OTHER THAN
FULL AND OPEN COMPETITION
I. CONTRACTING ACTIVITY
This Class Justification and Approval (J&A) is submitted to request authority for Other Than
Full and Open Competition to support requirements generated by multiple customers, including
but not limited to the United States Air Force (USAF), the Defense Logistics Agency (DLA),
and Foreign Military Sales (FMS) and any/all DoD customers worldwide via a Captains of
Industry (COI) DLA formal solicitation. The contracting authority for this requirement is DLA
Aviation, Strategic Acquisition and Programs Directorate in Richmond, VA.
II. NATURE AND/OR DESCRIPTION OF THE ACTION BEING PROCESSED
Due to the circumstances described herein, this activity requests authority for the negotiation and
award of multiple contracts on a sole-source basis with Lockheed Martin Corporation (LM) for
performance-based supply chain management and logistics support of aircraft and systems
manufactured by LM including, but not limited to, the F16, C-5, C-130, F35, MH-60, P-3, F-22,
Patriot Guidance Enhanced Missile, CHAPARRAL Guided Missile Equipment Carrier, Sniper
Advanced Targeting Pod, Electro-Optics Targeting System, Distributed Aperture System
Window Panel, Q-70 Radar, MK41 Vertical Launch System, Aegis Cruiser, Sonar Buoys,
MEADS Radar, Sea Bass Torpedo and Stinger Missile. In addition to parts, the support may
include holistic support and logistics management services, including but not limited to
wholesale supply and logistics support, inventory management, maintenance planning,
configuration management, repair development, repair of repairables for Service customers, and
sustainment engineering associated with a LM aircraft, system, and/or end item. It may also
include additive manufacturing solutions, depot maintenance, depot-level support, material
management, engineering support and sustainment elements, packaging, storage, transportation,
reliability improvements, and field engineering support. The all-encompassing goal will be to
improve material and services availability for supported platforms. The acquisition will be
conducted using Other Than Full and Open Competition as prescribed by FAR 6.302-1, Only
One Responsible Source and No Other Supplies or Services Will Satisfy Agency Requirements.
The intent of the acquisition team is to award overarching terms and conditions that will remain
valid for 20 years. This duration of terms and conditions will enable the Strategic Contract
Division of DLA Aviation to award a variety of long-term subsumable contracts under those
terms and conditions. Such contracts will consist of one five (5) year base period and one five
Source Selection Information – See FAR 2.101 & 3.104
(5) year option period. In accordance with FAR Part 10, additional market research will be
conducted prior to the exercise of the five-year options. However, in no case will any of those
subsumable contracts exceed the ten-year period authorized by 10 U.S.C. 2304a(f), unless
appropriate approval is obtained.
This sole source requirement will be negotiated with the following company:
Lockheed Martin Corporation
100 Global Innovation Circle
Orlando, FL 32825-5002
The Government anticipates purchasing material and services under these contracts from, but not
limited to, the following LM CAGE codes:
02769 52088 1FUD6 64059 4A3W7 23892
16331 77609 06JJ5 11530 23917 8X044
38597 0WWN8 26629 94271 563J1
067V1 04939 56232 04WF2 74703
98897 25500 90536 08PL1 6U917
03640 55316 036W7 1NM30 02GJ5
0A489 24900 81755 1WL60 0L1E5
03538 54274 029K9 2AAC2 1G2P4
16848 80070 13030 3CUQ0 4A3W7
The length of the overarching terms and conditions contract period, as well as each base period
and term of the subsumable contracts, are considered optimal for the following reasons:
• It affords the Government flexibility and latitude to enter a variety of contracts for
present and projected needs while reducing the need for clause negotiation for
repetitive similar type efforts.
• It facilitates agility for the Government and supplier to adapt to unforeseen
requirements that may arise within the contract period.
• It affords the contractor sufficient time to recoup initial investments associated with
facilities, parts, obsolescence issues, and reliability management.
• It affords the contractor opportunities to enter long term commitments with
subcontractors (including organic depots) in order to provide sustained
efficiencies/economies of scale to the military service user.
• It enables the contractor to implement logistical and technical changes required to
realize reliability improvements.
• It allows for the elimination of duplicative contract and program administration costs
for like and similar items.
• It affords the supplier opportunity to leverage investment in support processes across
similar items, thereby saving additional costs.
Source Selection Information – See FAR 2.101 & 3.104


• Performance Based support will consist of logistics management, which includes
wholesale supply planning and support, depot-level consumable support, depot-level
repairable support, material management, engineering support and sustainment elements,
packaging, storage, transportation, reliability improvements, and field engineering
support for a to-be-determined population of items with frequent or recurring demand.
LM will be required to meet supply chain performance-based metrics for material
availability and backorder age for this population likely in a similar format to the current
Supplier Initiated Orders (SIO) construct. The performance metrics are expected to be
based on the level of demand for the individual NSN and will be measured against
DLA’s current performance baseline. Examples of potential contract metrics include but
are not limited to the following: improvement in production lead time (PLT), production
capacity, forecasting and material availability (MA), reduction of administrative lead
time (ALT), unfilled orders (UFOs), on time delivery (OTD), and backorder age.
• Stock support may include items that are unit priced and ordered at lead time like current
long-term contracts.
• Transactional support may include items that are priced on an ad-hoc basis using an
expedited pricing methodology to be negotiated. Such NSNs have been previously
identified and will be recertified as LM sole source items prior to being procured.
IV. STATUTORY AUTHORITY PERMITTING OTHER THAN FULL AND OPEN
COMPETITION
Use of Other than Full and Open Competition is authorized by 10 U.S.C. 2304(c)(1) and FAR
6.302-1, as there is only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy
agency requirements.
V. DEMONSTRATION THAT THE CONTRACTOR’S UNIQUE QUALIFICATIONS
OR NATURE OF THE ACQUISITION REQUIRES THE USE OF THE AUTHORITY
CITED ABOVE
The acquisition is restricted to the only source of supply known to have the capability of
furnishing the required support – Lockheed Martin Corporation. In addition to spares support,
this Class J&A covers performance-based support, forecasting, supply chain management, and
related efforts for LM aviation systems. Only LM can provide the necessary expertise, capacity,
capability, and proficiency to perform this overall effort. LM is the only company which
possesses the requisite engineering expertise, configuration management, tooling, and
management knowledge to ensure that items conform to the proper form, fit and function, thus
keeping complex platforms reliable and safe. LM is the only source that possesses the full range
of technical data (some of which is proprietary) required to manufacture the full range of items
that are covered by this Class J&A. LM is the only contractor that can leverage the production
capability and has an in-depth knowledge of the diverse and diminishing vendor base capable of
supporting these platforms at the required level of support. For the sole source material provided
for direct platform support, it has been determined the Government does not have complete,
unrestricted data packages available. Additionally, LM has established internal production
processes and qualified various industrial support contractors as suppliers. Regarding the
Source Selection Information – See FAR 2.101 & 3.104
material support for the repair of components at DoD repair depots, LM’s overall systems
engineering knowledge and technical expertise in the various platforms make it singularly
capable of performing the full scope of the depot support requirement. No contractor other than
LM, the sole manufacturer and integrator of the various platforms to be supported, has the
capability to perform all the requirements of the comprehensive performance-based supply chain
management program. LM is the only entity with the full data rights to provide all the sole
source material as well as the OEM-based data and systems engineering expertise to fully
support the complete range of depot maintenance requirements across the full spectrum of the
LM provided weapon systems.
The key overarching objective of these contracts is to maximize the availability/use of the
various weapon systems by providing timely material support through initiatives such as
incentivizing reliability improvements, streamlining supply chain management, and improving
maintenance processes and procedures. In order to meet this overarching objective, the provider
must have the ability to drive changes into the platform configurations and, more importantly,
understand, analyze, and assess the implications—both in terms of weapon system performance
and operational usage—of any potential configuration change. To do so, this effort may require
engineering and logistics support personnel with an unfettered ability to reach back to the OEM,
LM, to support engineering investigations, fault detection and isolation, repair development,
modification development, supportability analysis, and the associated technical documentation
development and support. LM is the only source that can provide this comprehensive capability.
Only LM has personnel with the requisite breadth and depth of experience and understanding of
the totality of technical data necessary to fulfill this requirement and ensure the currency,
accuracy, and completeness of the technical data and associated databases. Finally, once
modifications or process changes are made by the Government, only LM has the existing
infrastructure to ensure timely execution of such changes, including the ability to efficiently
execute changes simultaneously into production and fielded systems.
Furthermore, by having only one contractor responsible for the bulk of supply chain
management, the Government has a single focal point with management accountability and
contractual responsibility. No other source has the long-standing business relationships with the
supplier base that LM has developed relative to this requirement. No other source can leverage
this supplier base as well as LM can to assure the continued effective, reliable, and safe
sustainment of the supply chain. Any other contractor would introduce an unacceptable degree
of risk into the supply chain effort and, ultimately, into the LM weapon systems.
While the market includes many supply chain service providers that would be capable of
performing a portion of the logistics management required (such as forecasting and
warehousing), LM, as the OEM of the specified systems, is the single source with integration
ability at multiple levels with the military services and the engineering, obsolescence
management, modeling, and simulation capabilities to provide the system availability and end-
to-end support the customers require.
Source Selection Information – See FAR 2.101 & 3.104

Justification for an Exception to Fair Opportunity – Logical Follow-On
(Implements the provisions and authorities of VA Class Deviation, modeled

(1) Identification of the agency and the contracting activity.
This Justification for an Exception to Fair Opportunity is on behalf of VISN 23, Minneapolis, MN VAHCS
and will be executed by the Veterans Affairs National Acquisition Center (NAC) located in Hines,
Illinois.
(2) Nature and/or description of the action being approved.
This activity proposes to issue a sole-source delivery order as a logical follow-on against Indefinite
Delivery/Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) Contract No. VA797H-17-D-0022 as awarded to Philips.
(3) A description of the supplies or services required to meet the agency’s needs, including the estimated
value.
This request is for upgrade of the existing Philips Epiq 7 ultrasound systems for 12 units that have
reached their end-of-life cycle. The Philips EPIQ Elite advanced for general imaging is a premium
diagnostic ultrasound system featuring an uncompromised level of clinical performance and the latest
diagnostic applications and clinical packages. It offers Multi-Modality Query Retrieve that allows for the
viewing of DICOM CT, Mammography, NM, MRI and ultrasound images and can be reviewed while
live imaging. It also offers NetLink/DICOM 3.0 provides network print and store, commit, modality
worklist, DICOM Query and Retrieve, and structured reporting for adult and pediatric echo, vascular,
and OB/GYN. The upgrade will include hardware and software, required to bring the entire system to
conformance.
The total estimated value is $ 983,248.62.
(4) An identification of the exception to fair opportunity (per FAR Subpart 16.507-6 (b)(3)) and the
supporting rationale, including a demonstration that the proposed contractor’s unique
qualification or the nature of the acquisition requires use of the exception cited. If the contracting
officer uses the logical follow-on exception, the rationale shall describe why the relationship
between the initial order and the follow-on is logical (e.g., in terms of scope, period of performance,
or value).
The resulting delivery order will be issued on a sole-source basis as a logical follow - on to Contract
VA797H-17-D-0022. The equipment was originally procured in FY2015-2017, utilizing full competition via
the February Consolidation. The items were subsequently procured under Delivery Order Number
VA797H-15-J-0183, VA797A-17-J-0689, VA797A-17-J-0697, VA797A-17-J-0694, VA797A-17-J-0691, VA797A-
17-J-0696, VA797A-17-J-0698, VA797A-17-J-0699, VA797A-17-J-0700, VA797A-17-J-0693,
VA797A-17-J-0701, VA797A-17-J-0690. This upgrade will provide current technology without requiring
additional specialized site preparation.
The original equipment manufacturer (OEM), Philips, is the only contractor who can provide the upgrade
and as such is a logical follow-on to the original contract, due to the need to operate with existing OEM’S
components and the proprietary nature of the hardware and software. The OEM is the only organization
capable of owning trade information about the system and as such is the only one qualified to provide and
perform the upgrade, with the expectation that the systems will continue operating as expected in a safe
manner.

Description: The U.S. Army Contracting Command � New Jersey (ACC-NJ),on behalf of the Product Director Test Measurement and Diagnostic Equipment (PD-TMDE) awarded a contract modification under current contract W15QKN-23-D-0007 to The Boeing Company, 6200 James S. McDonnell Blvd, Saint Louis, MO, 63134-1939. This modification, P00004, to contract W15QKN-23-D-0007 increased the contract ceiling value and incorporated two additional one-year ordering periods to the current Next Generation Automated Test System (NGATS) production contract. The modification increased the ceiling value by $25,450,321.75 from $118,654,047.00 to a total value of $144,104,368.75, pursuant to the authority of 10 U.S.C. 3204(a)(1) as implemented by Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 6.302-1(a)(2) - Only One Responsible Source and No Other Supplies or Services Will Satisfy Agency Requirements. 1. Requiring Activity: Next Generation Automated Test System (NG.ATS) for the
Product Director Test, Measurement, and Diagnostic Equipment (PD TMDE)
2. Contracting Activity: United States (U.S.) Army Contracting Command - New Jersey
located at Picatinny Arsenal, NJ.

final-NGAT S consoles, Self Test Interface Adapters (STIAs), and shelter integrations
for fielding for Fiscal Year (FY) 2027 and 2028.

Contract ordering period by adding two (2) additional one-year ordering periods to the
current NG.ATS production Contract W15QKN-23-D-0007 with The Boeing Company
(Boeing) located at 6200 JS McDonnell Boulevard, Saint Louis, Missouri. The period of
performance for the contract will be extended until 19 December 2027. Further., the
modification will increase the ceiling from $118,654,047.00 to a total ceiling amount of
$144,104,368.00. It is anticipated that FY 2027 and 2028 Other Procurement Army funds
will be used to satisfy this requirement.

increased the Approved Acquisition Objective (MO)
NGA TS. The current contract ceiling supported the original AAO of the
-NG.ATS.

the revised MO, PD TMDE requires an increase of $25,450,321.35 to the contract ceiling
and the addition of two one-year ordering periods. This will enable PD TMDE to procure

6. Reason for Authority Cited: FAR 6.302-1(a)(2) is the appropriate cited authority for
this requirement as Boeing is the Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM), and the only
vendor capable of meeting the government's requirement. Boeing is the current and only
producer of NGATS production system that has completed First Article Testing (FAT),
Qualification, and received Approval for fielding. Further, Boeing is the only company that
can manufacture and deliver the NGAT S consoles, adapters and shelter integration in the
time frame necessary to meet the fielding requirements due to completing FAT.
a. Background: Contract W15QKN-23-D-0007 is a sole source Indefinite
Quantity Indefinite Delivery contract that was awarded on a Firm-Fixed Price
basis to the Boeing Company on 21 December 2022 for the Full Rate
Production of NGATS consoles, STIAs, and shelter integrations in order to
meet the Army's fielding schedule.

6
-
the Army's approved family of Automated Test Equipment (ATE). It is a highly
mobile, rapidly deployable, general-purpose, reconfigurable automatic test
system which directly supports testing and screening of Army weapon
systems to maintain their readiness to shoot, move, and communicate.
NGAT S is a modern, state of the art system designed and built utilizing open
architecture and commercial instrumentation.
The NGATS was designed and developed to replace the Direct Support
Electrical System Test Set, Integrated Family of ATE Version 3 and Version
5, and to support future weapon systems requirements. The NGAT S is the
only system which has the capability to perform field level diagnostics at the
Brigade level for multiple Army platforms, including Abrams, Bradley, Stryker,
Husky Mounted Detection System, and Common Remotely Operated
Weapons Systems.
b. Alternatives: There are no other known alternatives. Boeing is the only qualified
manufacturer with Qualification and Approval for fielding the NGATS.
Significant financial resources were consumed during performance of the
current contract, which brought the current OEM to the point of full-rate
production approval. If alternate vendors were to be considered, the total
additional cost to the Government would be around l!!l!ll!!l.1!11!!!!1■· This would
include the cost to qualify a Full Rate Production (FRP) NGATS, Assembly of
a First Article NGATS Console, Assembly of a First Article STIA, Physical
Configuration Audit (PCA), Integration, Contractor Acceptance Testing,
'Contractor First Article Testing (FAT), Government Operational Testing, and
costs associated with Cybersecurity Compliance (per NIST SP 800-171). An
alternative vendor would also duplicate logistical efforts and events such as
verification, validation, and logistics demonstrations. Further, this would cause
a delay to the program- since it would take a new vendor time to
complete qualification and be at FRP. The -substantial duplication costs, and
additional time cannot be recovered through competition.
Furthermore, due to the U.S. Army Transformation Initiative to modernize and
restructure the Army and operational factors and threat concepts coupled with
evolving warfare tactics, military strategies and reallocated budgets, the
NGATS budget has no known requirements for production past FY 2028.
Therefore, due to the duplication costs, program delays, and the fact there are
no known NGATS requirements beyond FY 2028, considering an alternative
vendor would not be advantageous to the Government.
c. Impact if not approved: If this modification is not approved, it would result in
an additional cost to the Government, and lead to unacceptable delays. Based
