Justification and Approval (J&A) Modified
for Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 13.501
1. Identification of the Agency and Contracting Activity:
This justification is executed by the Defense Health Agency Contracting Activity (DHACA),
Healthcare Contracting Division – West (HCD – W), San Diego, CA, on behalf of the Navy to
meet the requirements of the United States Naval Hospital Okinawa (USNHO) Pacific Command
Armed Services Blood Bank Center (PACOM ASBBC), Japan.
2. Nature and/or Description of Action being Approved:
USNHO PACOM ASBBC is one of two Department of Defense (DoD) blood donor testing
laboratories. PACOM ASBBC is mandated to screen donated blood to produce Food and Drug
Administration (FDA)-licensed blood products for the Indo-Pacific region. The Procleix Panther
analyzer is an FDA cleared and approved platform for testing human immunodeficiency virus
ribonucleic acid, hepatitis C virus ribonucleic acid, hepatitis B virus deoxyribonucleic acid, and
West Nile Virus ribonucleic acid, and Babesia, utilizing Nucleic Acid Testing. The analyzer
requires annual onsite maintenance not available from Biomed resources within USNHO. This
J&A is for a new contract award to continue annual preventative maintenance services.The
contract type will be Firm-Fixed-Price. This is a follow-on to contract N6264520P2059, and this
is an individual J&A Modified for FAR 13.501.
3. Description of Supplies/Services:
USNHO, the customer, requests procurement of non-personal services to perform preventative
maintenance and telephone support for the Grifols Procleix Panther analyzer, an FDA cleared
and approved Government-owned equipment. These services will ensure that the equipment is
performing in compliance with Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) standards and that
preventive maintenance will be conducted to minimize risk of equipment failure. Requirement:
The contractor shall provide telephone technical support, onsite emergency maintenance and
onsite preventive maintenance (PM) services for the PROCLEIX PANTHER Nucleic Acid Test
system. The contractor shall provide qualified technicians; OEM replacement parts; perform
system calibrations; and provide all supervision, equipment, supplies and transportation for

A Notice of Intent (NOI) to Sole Source under solicitation number HT941025N0071 was issued

7. Actions to Increase Competition/Remove or Overcome any Barriers to Competition:
USNHO and the DHA Western Markets Contracting Division will continue to survey and
engage the market of maintenance service providers for the Procleix Panther equipment currently
in place at USNHO and consider competing future requirements if there are other vendors
capable of meeting the Government’s requirements. In addition, review and due diligence will be
conducted by the Government for any vendor submitting capability statements for preventive
maintenance on the Procleix Panther equipment.
8. Market Research:
Market research was conducted by technical experts in March 2025, utilizing various methods
including reviews of similar previous procurements, online search engines, and mandatory
sources. The research efforts, which included posting a NOI to Sole Source on SAM.gov under
notice number HT941025N0071 from 01 April 2025 to 16 April 2025, revealed that only Grifols
Diagnostic Solutions can meet the Government's requirements. Previous procurements were
reviewed utilizingFederal Procurement Data System (FPDS)searches under North American
Industry Classification System (NAICS) code 811210 and keywords related to Panther
preventive maintenance. These reviews did not identify any other vendors with demonstrated

maintenance’), FPDS, AbilityOne, Unicor, Dynamic Small Business Search (DSBS) utilizing

search yielded no other vendors capable of meeting the Government's minimal requirements. The
limited number of qualified vendors is attributed to the Procleix Panther system’s proprietary
technology and Grifols’ exclusive control over maintenance and parts distribution. The
possibility of utilizing a third-party maintenance provider with OEM parts was explored, but

Authority: Title 10 United States Code (U.S.C.) Section 3204(a)(1) as implemented by

Justification and Approval
for Other than Full and Open Competition – FAR Part 6
1. Contracting Activity: Army Contracting Command-Redstone Arsenal (ACC-RSA),
CCAM- ALA, Redstone Arsenal, AL 35898-5000.
2. Description of Action: U.S. Army Aviation and Missile Command (AMCOM)
Logistics Center (ALC) requests approval to award a new, limited competitive
requirement for the procurement of the Wheel Landing Gear, for the Apache AH-64.
The result contract will be a single award, Firm-Fixed Price (FFP), spares buy contract
for 740. The projected award date is September 2023. Army Working Capital Funds
(AWCF) will be utilized.
3. Description of Supplies/Services: ALC has a requirement for contractor to provide
the Wheel Landing Gear on the AH-64. The following information is provided for the
Wheel Landing Gear:
Procurement Request Order Number (PRON): AX2F6104AX
Noun: Wheel, Landing Gear
NSN: 1630012905740
Order Qty: 740
Total Estimated Dollars:
4. Authority Cited: Authority: Title 10 U.S.C. Section 3204(a)(1), the supplies needed
by the Army are only available from a limited number of responsible sources and no
other type of supplies will satisfy the needs of the Army.
5. Reason for Authority Cited: The proposed acquisition requires the use of the cited statutory
authority because this spare part is procured to an approved part number and is a military
unique requirement. The data needed to produce the Wheel Landing Gear is proprietary and the
Government does not have unrestricted rights to this data sufficient to compete this requirement.
The Government can neither obtain this proprietary technical data, nor can it reverse engineer
the part without causing unacceptable delays.
The following contractors have access to this necessary proprietary data to produce the
spares buy:
6. Efforts to Obtain Competition:
a. A Sources Sought announcement was publicized on sam.gov on 22 November
2022, additional details can be found below in paragraph nine.
b. Subcontracting Competition: In accordance with FAR 19.702 and FAR 19.704, a
Subcontracting Plan is required for large businesses on acquisitions that exceed $750K.
3
According to FAR 19.704, the contractor must include FAR 52.219-8, entitled “Utilization
of Small Business Concerns,” in all subcontracts that offer further subcontracting
opportunities and shall require all subcontractors, except small businesses, that receive
subcontracts in excess of to adopt a plan that complies with the requirements of
the clause at FAR 52.219-9, “Small Business Subcontracting Plan”. In accordance with
DFARS 219.708(b)(1)(A), the solicitation and resulting contract will include DFARS
clause 252.219-7003, entitled “Small Business Subcontracting Plan (DoD Contracts)” to
ensure that all subcontracts are awarded on a competitive basis to the maximum extent
possible. The following approved sources for this requirement are large businesses and
will be required to comply with these requirements if awarded this proposed contract:
7. Actions to Increase Competition:
As previously stated, Technical data is currently not available to the Government to
support full and open competition. Only the sources as indicated in paragraph five
above, are authorized to compete for this requirement. There is a reasonable basis to
conclude that the Government’s minimum needs can only be satisfied by these four
vendors. As a result, there are currently no actions that the Government can take to
increase competition, and the Government does not anticipate being able to compete
this action on a full and open basis in the future.
8. Market Research: In accordance with FAR 10.002(b), meaningful market research
for the Gearbox Assembly, AI was conducted by the Logistics Management Specialist,
in February 2023. Research methods included the following:
(a) Discussion of the Lead Inventory Management Specialist’s knowledge of the
wheel landing gear. This is a one-time buy for 740 of the Wheel, Landing Gear,
National Item Identification Number (NIIN) 01-290-5740, in support of the Apache
(AH-64) Helicopter. This is a consumable item, and this buy is to provide pipeline
support in order to transfer management of this item to Defense Logistics Agency
(DLA);
(b) Discussion with following knowledgeable Government employees regarding the
commercial nature of this procurement: Supply Planning Team Lead
, Supply Planner , and Demand Planning Branch Chief
. The personnel listed above confirmed that this requirement
cannot be met with commercial items. They also discussed the Inventory Management
Processing Code 5A/1A relationship between the 5A Prime NIIN 01-290-5740 and the
1A related NIINs 01-164-3801 and 01-250-9860. The Prime NIIN 01-290-5740 is a 5A
prime shell NIIN only, and the two related 1A NIINs. When we start a new contract, the
buy must be dropped under the prime NIIN. The two 1A NIINs have different
manufacturers, so whoever bids and wins the contract, that is the NIIN that we will use.
Currently, our spares due ins are against NIIN 01-164-3801. These are also casting and
forging items, so the Production Lead Time is long;
(c) The review of Government and commercial databases for relevant information
(Logistics Modernization Program (LMP), Internet Parts Locator (IPL), Electronic
4
Document Access (EDA), and Army Aviation Sustainment Gateway (ARISE) and
the Small Business Administration (SBA) and found sources that are capable of
providing information for the Wheel, Landing Gear. Research from these
databases revealed this item as Non-Critical Safety Item. Also, this requirement
cannot be met with commercial items;
(d) The review of source lists for identical or similar items obtained from
Government, professional, and industry sources In Feb 2023, the Government
reviewed the Logistics Modernization Program (LMP) and the Electronic Data
Access (EDA) module within the Procurement Integrated Enterprise Environment
(PIEE). The vendor CAGE codes that were listed in the Material Master data in
LMP were reviewed for all three NIINs in this family. In EDA, the most recent
Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity contract (SPRRA1-17-D-0250) and delivery
orders (0001 and SPRRA119F0182) for NIIN 01-164-3801 were reviewed, these
contracts were awarded to
(e) Discussion of interchange meetings and conferences with potential offerors. This
market research review included attendance by Government Technical personnel
at Technical Conferences including Annual AAAA, AMCOM Industry Days,
Advanced Planned Briefings for Industry (APBI) Oct 2022. Leaders from Apache
Project Management Office attend these conferences annually. These
conferences allow companies in the Aviation enterprise the opportunity to
showcase the products with the technical capability, resources for knowledge
needed to support the Apache Weapon System;
(f) Publication of a formal request for information in the form of a sources sought
notice was issued on 20 Nov 2022 as detailed below in paragraph nine.
The results of the research confirmed that there are only four source capable of
providing the Wheel, Landing Gear as previously detailed in paragraph five. As
previously noted, the Sources Sought announcements were published on 20 November
2022 , and produced no new sources. Based upon this market research, it has been
determined that the Government’s needs cannot be satisfied with commercial items,
commercial items with customary or reasonable modifications, or non-developmental
items.
a. 9. Interested Sources: Effective competition. In accordance with DFARS
205.205- 71, DFARS 206.302-1(d), and DFARS Procedures, Guidance and Information
(PGI) 206.302-1(d), a Sources Sought announcement was publicized on sam.gov on 22
November 2022. No additional sources expressed interest in competing for this
requirement.
5
10 Other Facts: This procurement represents the fourth time that the AMCOM ALC
has procured the Wheel Landing Gear; it has also been previously procured through a
delivery orders from DLA. The following table has the details of the previous

matters.title: NOTICE OF INTENT TO NEGOTIATE A SOLE-SOURCE CONTRACT
matters.text:
Federal notice (Special Notice), COMMERCE, DEPARTMENT OF.NATIONAL OCEANIC AND ATMOSPHERIC ADMINISTRATION.NATIONAL OCEANIC AND ATMOSPHERIC ADMINISTRATION
Title: NOTICE OF INTENT TO NEGOTIATE A SOLE-SOURCE CONTRACT
Solicitation number: 140802-26-0051
PSC: 3950; NAICS: 333923
Description: The US Department of Commerce (DOC), National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA), Office of Marine and Aviation Operations (OMAO),NOAA Ship Nancy Foster is requesting three (3) RPC-90x-SA-MEA-REN units safe area measurement assemblies with rear enclosures and one (1) modified RA-90x-DE-SA-D01 enclosure customized to support four winch sensors with top-entry cabling; Eight (8) hours of vendor labor to configure modifications and prepare assemblies for installation. These units and configurations will be provided by Rugged Controls located at 4211 24th Avenue West Seattle, WA 98199. NOAA vessels rely on multiple winch systems for the deployment and retrieval of scientific instrumentation. The RPC-90x units provide updated measurement capability in a safe-area housing, while the modified RA-90x enclosure supports integration of four winch sensors through a consolidated top-entry arrangement. This the system brings into alignment with NOAA operational expectations for reliability, maintainability, and sensor interface compatibility. The intended use is to provide stable, accurate winch wire tension to critical and sensitive bridge navigation equipment and scientific equipment installed on these ships. Other manufacturer�s products will require a completely new installation, mounting and training for both the User/Operators and Maintainers who are the Chief Electronic Technician on each individual vessel. The training and support change will be more costly and more difficult to complete. Installation for RPC-90x could be completed while underway, and it is nearly a one for one swap and no training is required. In addition, other manufactured winch control display will require the vessel to be dockside for at least 1 to 2 weeks. This again a costly investment. The Original Equipment Manufacturer; hold proprietary rights to the design and configuration of these winch control displays, no other vendors have the necessary materials to perform the requested actions. The Government is not aware of any other vendors that are authorized to sell and configure the Rugged Controls RCP-90Xs therefore; the Government intends to acquire these parts/ service under the guidelines of FAR Part 13, Simplified Acquisitions Procedures and FAR Part 12, Commercial Items. The Government intends to solicit and negotiate directly with Rugged Control under the authority of FAR 13.106-1(b)(1)). This is not a solicitation for competitive quotes. However, if any interested party that can provide these parts and service and are authorized dealer, seller, and/or distributor by the OEM, without delaying or adding additional mark ups or compromising any warranties, may submit a statement of capabilities, in which if in timely received, will be considered by NOAA, OMAO. A statement of capabilities shall include the detailed of RPC-90x, OEM authorization letter, and a price list including installation, configuration services, this shall be received by 5:00pm EST on Tuesday, December 16, 2025 at 5pm ET. A determination by the Government not to compete this proposed requirement is based upon responses to this notice and it is solely within the discretion of the Government. Information received will normally be considered solely for the purpose of determining whether to conduct a competitive procurement in the future. Evidence must be provided of the Rugged Control Winch Display RPC-90X. The capability statement, a price list and any other information furnished must be in writing and must contain material in sufficient detail to allow the Government to determine if the party can meet the requirement. Capability statements and related materials must be e-mailed by 5:00pm EST on December 16, 2025 to alexander.cancela@noaa.gov.

CLASS JUSTIFICATION AND APPROVAL
FOR USE OF OTHER THAN FULL AND OPEN COMPETITION
1.Contracting Activity
The Naval Sea Systems Command (NAVSEA), Shipbuilding Contracts
Division (SEA 022).
2. Description of the Actions Being Approved
Award of contract actions on a sole source basis for Aircraft
Carrier Engineering Support (ACES) to Huntington Ingalls
Incorporated – Newport News Shipbuilding (HII-NNS) for
engineering, technical, design agent, and configuration
management support for CVN 68 class and CVN 78 class aircraft
carriers (CVNs) with an ordering provision for materials
required in support of the effort described herein. Ordering
provision requirements may include long lead time material as
well as material and supplies for engineering, technical,
design, configuration management, Integrated Logistics Support,
database management, and modernization support. Authority to
act under this class justification expires on 29 September 2029.
3. Description of Supplies/Services
The efforts covered by this Class Justification and Approval
(CJ&A) include consolidated engineering, technical, design agent,
configuration management support, Ford Class Design Support
(FCDS) and associated material needed to sustain existing
capabilities and offset obsolescence of CVNs.
Required efforts during the period of performance (beginning
approximately ) include:
Drawings and Related Technical Data; Design Studies, Design
Change Documentation; Pre-Advanced Planning for Refueling
Complex Overhaul (RCOH) and CVN Inactivation, Logistics
Technical Data (LTD); Configuration Management; Hull, Mechanical

J&A No: 22,008
Predecessor contract N00024-19-C-2100 was not competed. Work to
be performed under this contract requires detailed knowledge and
familiarity with specialized and critical technical details,
configurations, and performance characteristics of CVN 68 class
and CVN 78 class nuclear-powered aircraft carriers. HII-NNS,
located in Newport News, VA, is the only builder of U.S. Navy
nuclear-powered aircraft carriers and is the only contractor
with the detailed knowledge of and familiarity with these
vessels needed to perform the efforts anticipated. Specifically,
HII-NNS is the only contractor capable of performing the
engineering, technical, and design and configuration management
support requirements under the ACES effort for both CVN 68 class
and CVN 78 class aircraft carriers. This includes designation as
the CVN 68 class Propulsion Plant Engineering Activity (PPEA),
CVN 78 class Engineering Configuration Manager (ECM), and the In-
Service Engineering Agent (ISEA) for select CVN 78 class systems.
Additionally, HII-NNS maintains a data repository for all
aircraft carriers and a staff of highly trained personnel with
extensive specialized experience in the engineering,
modernization, technical, design and operational support of
CVNs, which are required to perform this effort. HII-NNS’s data
environment that is utilized in executing ECM functions includes
integrated data generated by the shipbuilder. Awarding this
requirement to any other contractor would result in unacceptable
delays in fulfilling the Navy’s requirements. Specifically, it
would take as much as for another engineering
firm to attain the necessary capability to perform the support
required of this contract, including ECM, to develop a 3D
product model that matches the efficacy of the product model
currently being executed under predecessor Contract N00024-19-C-
2100. Delaying this procurement to identify, develop, and
qualify another source would negatively impact the ACES program
and the operational capabilities of the United States Navy.
The Navy demands the highest level of operational availability
from the aircraft carrier fleet, which makes modernization
planning and execution and responding to emergent requirements an
extremely time-sensitive endeavor. The work must be accomplished
within narrow timeframes (often hours), and if schedules are not
met, deferred modernization or maintenance results in diminished
fleet capabilities.
Therefore, based on the above analysis, only HII-NNS has the
experience, capabilities, and toolsets to meet the requirements,
and can enable the program to accomplish its broad mission within
the requisite level of technical and managerial proficiency, and
3
J&A No: 22,008
at the Operations Tempo (OPTEMPO) required to meet the Navy’s
national defense mission without delay.
6.Description of Efforts Made to Solicit Offers from as Many
Offerors as Practicable
The proposed effort addressed by this CJ&A was synopsized on the
System for Award Management (SAM.gov) on 06 February 2023. No
responses have been received to date and no responses are
anticipated. In addition, in accordance with DFARS PGI 206.302-
1(d), a Sources Sought Notice was posted to SAM on 25 October
2022. The announcement received a response from one interested
firm, on 24 November 2022. A
Government technical assessment determined that does not
possess the ability to meet the demanding shipyard schedules and
required delivery dates. Additionally, does not have the
technical expertise or experience with CVN 68 or CVN 78 Class
propulsion plant design or engineering (or both). Therefore,
they are not a viable source to successfully fulfill all of the
Government’s requirement as stated in the synopsis as the prime
contractor. While no other sources have been identified to
provide prime contractor support, HII-NNS will be required to
promote competition where opportunities exist in selecting
subcontractors and suppliers.
7.Determination of Fair and Reasonable Costs
The Contracting Officer has determined the anticipated cost to
the Government of the supplies/services covered by this CJ&A will
be fair and reasonable.
8.Actions to Remove Barriers to Competition
For the reasons set forth in Paragraph 5, the Naval Sea Systems
Command has no plans at this time to compete future contracts
for the types of supplies/services covered by this document. If
another potential source emerges, the Naval Sea Systems Command
will assess whether competition for future requirements is
feasible.
As this is a follow-on for supplies and support efforts
previously awarded on a non-competitive basis, in accordance
with DFARS PGI 206.304(a)(S-70)(i), the prior J&A was provided
to the approval authority for review. Approval of this J&A
signifies the approval authority has made the determination
required by DFARS PGI 206.304(a)(S-70)(ii).

1. Contracting Activity: Department of Veterans Affairs, NCO15, Meds by Mail (MbM)-700
(Cheyenne, WY and Murfreesboro, TN).
Brief Description of Supplies/ Services required and the intended use/Estimated
Amount:
The existing VA Meds by Mail (MbM) OPEX mail scanner equipment at Murfreesboro, TN,
and Cheyenne, WY requires hardware upgrades to ensure IT compliance and compatibility
with Windows 11 and future operating systems. Specifically, the authorized ‘Falcon’
hardware component from OPEX is required to maintain secure and uninterrupted operation
as VA IT infrastructure evolves. The Falcon+ will integrate with the existing OPEX Model
72 extraction/opener equipment retained by MbM.
2. Unique characteristics that limit availability to only one source, with the reason no
other supplies or services can be used:
OPEX is the sole manufacturer and authorized provider of the specific scanner hardware and
software used in the MbM operations. The current OPEX Model AS7200i scanner system
and Model 72 extraction/opener are proprietary equipment exclusive to OPEX. No other
vendor offers compatible hardware or software that can integrate with or maintain the
existing system. VA maintains a current maintenance contract with OPEX, ensuring ongoing
support and compatibility. The equipment does not have an established end-of-life lifecycle,
and OPEX is committed to supporting the system as long as it is owned by the VA.
Therefore, no alternative sources exist for this upgrade.
3. Description of market research conducted and results or statement why it was not
conducted: Market research is limited due to the proprietary nature of the OPEX system in
use. The current MbM equipment consists solely of OPEX-manufactured scanners and
extraction/openers. The upgrade to the OPEX Falcon+ is necessary to maintain system
continuity and integration. Due to the exclusive ownership of the technology and ongoing
maintenance agreements, competitive market alternatives are not available or compatible
with existing infrastructure.

Utilizing the GSA Schedules Program to procure products and services complies with
Acquisition Alert AA-2014-07 and directly supports the Office of Management and Budget

enables agencies to save time and resources while ensuring compliance with the Federal
Acquisition Regulation (FAR). This approach promotes strategic sourcing and enhances
efficiency, aligning with OMB's broader efforts to optimize government-wide acquisition
strategies.

Title: 31- BEARING, PLAIN, SELF-ALIGNING
Solicitation number: SPE4A625RX146
PSC: 3120; NAICS: 332991
Description: Solicitation Number SPE4A625RX146 Solicitation will result in a Commercial Indefinite Delivery Contract IAW FAR 13.5, having a base period of five years. The final contract award decision may be based upon a combination of price, past performance, and other evaluation factors as described in the solicitation. The solicitation date is anticipated to be November 21, 2024. A copy of the solicitation will be available via the DIBBS Website https://www.dibbs.bsm.dla.mil/ on the issue date cited in the RFP. From the DIBBS Homepage, select "Requests for Proposal (RFP) / Invitation for Bid (IFB)" from the menu under the tab "Solicitations." Then search for and choose the RFP you wish to download. RFPs are in portable document format (PDF). To download and view these documents you will need the latest version of Adobe Acrobat Reader. This software is available free at: http://www.adobe.com. A paper copy of this solicitation will not be available to requestors. Surplus dealers, small business dealers and distributors (having existing stock of surplus or newly manufactured material) are invited to respond to this synopsis. The response should include a completed surplus certificate, DLAD 52.211-9000, Government surplus Material or adequate traceability documentation to show that the product is acceptable. In addition, respondents should identify quantity available and price. The government may alter the acquisition strategy if purchase of existing surplus or newly-manufactured inventory is in the best interest of the Government. NSN: 3120-00-011-9167. Bearing, Plain, Self-Aligning. Approved Source: RBC Transport Dynamics Corp (09455), New Hampshire Ball Bearings Inc (15860), and The Boeing Company (77272). Terms are FOB Destination, Inspection and Acceptance at Origin. Stocked Item. QCC of REJ. Estimated Annual Demand is 1413, the Minimum is 354, and the Maximum is 1413. This is a Critical Safety Item (CSI) and a Critical Application Item (CAI). COQC applies. First Article Test (FAT) applies. Production Lot Test (PLT) applies. Serialization applies. Covered Defense Information applies. Requested delivery of 562 days ARO. This NSN is commercial of a type and will utilize solicitation and award procedures IAW FAR 13.5.

matters.text:
Federal notice (Presolicitation), DEPT OF DEFENSE.DEFENSE LOGISTICS AGENCY.DLA AVIATION
Title: Sole Source Parker Hannifin LTC Adds
Solicitation number: SPE4A526R0091
PSC: 1650; NAICS: 336412
Description: Defense Logistics Agency (DLA) Aviation, Richmond proposes to issue a Letter Request for Proposal (RFP) to support a DLA Strategic Initiative. This strategic effort includes multiple NSNs to support various sole source weapon systems / operational platforms. A total of 120 NSNs for various platforms / weapon systems are targeted for this RFP and contract action. OEM Parker Hannifin Corporation (59211) has been identified as the approved source of supply for the listed items; therefore, the proposed action is intended to be awarded on a sole source basis to the OEM. It is anticipated that 120 items will be awarded and priced with lead-times as add-ons to the OEM's existing Long-Term Contracts (LTCs): Captains of Industry (COI) Supplier Capabilities Contract (SCC) SPE4AX-21-D-9402 for commercial items and SPE4AX-21-D-9403 for military unique items (Parker Hannifin Commercial Subsumable Contract). It is the Government's intent to use a letter solicitation format to the sole source Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM); therefore, if a non-OEM source is interested in any of the NSNs, please notify the Contracting Officer prior to the synopsis closing date. These items have been identified as sole source; however, some items may have history showing awards to other than the OEM. Surplus dealers are also invited to respond to this synopsis. The response should include a completed surplus certificate, DLA Procurement Note 04, Government Surplus Property Material or adequate traceability documentation to show that the product is acceptable. (Note: DLA Procurement Note M05 Evaluation Factor for Unused Former Government Surplus Property, will apply and other Aviation sites will provide their equivalent surplus documentation, as applicable). Responses to this announcement from other than the OEM should identify items of interest and include evidence of ability to supply the items in accordance with the aforementioned acquisition strategy. In addition, respondents should identify the available quantities, prices, and lead-times. DLA will consider all such responses and may alter the acquisition strategy if purchase of existing surplus or newly manufactured inventory is in the best interest of the government. Responses to this announcement from other than the OEM are required by Tuesday, November 26, 2025. A copy of the letter of interest should be forwarded to the contracting officer identified. If your company desires to be reviewed and qualified as an "Approved Source" for any of the items listed, submit an application package through the Source Approval Request (SAR) Program as outlined in the attached SAR document. A SAR package contains all of the technical data needed to demonstrate that the prospective contractor can competently manufacture the product to the same level of quality, or better, than the Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM). The onus is on the contractor to document and demonstrate their product is equal to, or better, than the currently approved item which DLA Aviation is procuring. (Note: To submit your SAR please send an email to: dlaavnsmallbus@dla.mil, subject� request a SAR drop off�. After we receive your email request a �request for drop off� will be returned, where you can download your file. Include CAGE code, the NSN, and the email address where you want to receive the link. For guidance on completing a SAR package, please review the Source Approval Handbook. Current procurements will not be held pending review; therefore, any actions will be for future procurements or strategic efforts.) Export Control: Items cited require data which is restricted to contractors certified by DoD to access unclassified data per DoD 5220.22M. Certification is obtained by submitting DD Form 2345, Military Critical Technical Data Agreement, to the Defense Logistics Information Services. Additionally, letters expressing interest in subcontracting provided to the Contracting Officer will be forwarded to the identified Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM). FAR Parts 12 / 15 procedures may apply. The attached 120 NSNs have been identified for the current procurement. If other NSNs are subsequently added, as defined by this strategic initiative and contract terms, they will be synopsized separately. The anticipated closing date March 3, 2026 . If you are interested in this opportunity, you may contact Kenya Allamby at kenya.allamby@dla.mil. Contracting Office Address: 6090 Strathmore Rd Richmond, Virginia 23237 United States

Obtaining part samples is a required portion of the qualification process. The
Government must obtain prototypes that can be used for testing and integration to
ensure that the component being proposed meets the requirements outlined throughout
the source-controlled drawing. This process would cost an estimated $350,000.
Once these part samples are obtained, the Government requires reverse engineering
efforts to be completed. This consists of several integration and fabrication processes
that must be done for quality validation and testing, including detailed analysis of
manufacturing the circuit cards. This also includes the implementation of several
electrical, mechanical, and structural forms of integration within the assembly of the
component and the recovery vehicle itself. The form, fit, and function must be validated
throughout this process. The total cost of this is estimated to be $4,500,000 to the U.S
Government in house reverse engineering facility.
After these processes are complete, there are several forms of qualification testing that
are required. The RT Box Qualification Testing would include but is not limited to
vibration, thermal, operational, shutdown limit, and washdown testing. In addition, there
are various internal and external signal requirements that must be met as outlined in
source control drawing 12365133. The total cost of this testing is estimated to be
around $750,000.
Lastly, the Government must develop new documentation once qualification testing is
completed. This process consists of engineering creating an Engineering Change
Proposal (ECP) for the source-controlled drawing. An ECP will allow the Government to
alter the drawing to represent that a new source(s) has been qualified for the
component. This is done using Computer-Aided Design (CAD). Engineering must also
work to develop the necessary changes and work with Configuration Management to
release them. This total cost is estimated to be $10,000.
The Government would not be able to recover, through subsequent competition, the
duplication of costs involved in the qualification of an additional source within a
reasonable time frame. At the current usage rate of 12 units per year, at the current unit
cost of $55,774.00 each, and assuming 10% savings achieved through competition, the
$66,928.80 annual savings would take 84 years to offset the estimated $5,610,000 cost
of qualifying another source.
6. Efforts to Obtain Competition:
a. Effective competition: Due to the reasons cited in section 5 above we are not
pursuing competition for this item. This action will be synopsized in accordance
with FAR 5.201.
b. Subcontracting competition: The solicitation and resulting contract will include
FAR clauses 52.219-8, "Utilization of Small Business Concerns"; 52.244-5,
"Competition in Subcontracting"; 52.219-16, "Liquidated Damages--

7. Actions to Increase Competition: There are no plans to increase competition for
future procurements due to the reasons cited above.
This item is source controlled to Benchmark Electronics Huntsville Inc., CAGE: 380Q6,
and Ducommun Labarge Technologies, Inc., CAGE: 65648. These manufacturers are
the only approved sources of supply for this item. Due to the duplication of costs
involved in qualifying a new source, the Government is not actively pursuing qualifying a
new source for future procurements.
8. Market Research: A Sources Sought Notice was posted to www.SAM.gov on 10
April, 2023 and was open for 11 days. No response received.
Additional Market Research Efforts:
Online market research was performed by Ground Vehicle System Center (GVSC)
Engineering during December of 2022, by searching online vendor catalogs and product
literature published, to find other manufacturers and/or commercial items or non-
developmental items that could meet Government needs or could be modified to meet
Government needs.
Upon review it was determined that while there are many vendors that have the
capability to manufacture a Remote Terminal Unit, they do not meet the requirements in
source control drawing 12365133 for approval. Some of the companies that were
researched include Schweitzer Engineering Laboratories, Remsdaq, and Emerson. Any
potential new vendors would require extensive analysis, prototyping, and vehicle testing
as described in section 5 above to ensure that the M88 vehicle will properly meet
performance specifications with a new supplier’s hardware.

Description: Solicitation Number SPE4A625RXF84 Solicitation will result in a Commercial Indefinite Delivery Contract IAW FAR 13.5, having a base period of five years. The final contract award decision may be based upon a combination of price, past performance, and other evaluation factors as described in the solicitation. The solicitation date is anticipated to be September 24, 2025. A copy of the solicitation will be available via the DIBBS Website https://www.dibbs.bsm.dla.mil/ on the issue date cited in the RFP. From the DIBBS Homepage, select "Requests for Proposal (RFP) / Invitation for Bid (IFB)" from the menu under the tab "Solicitations." Then search for and choose the RFP you wish to download. RFPs are in portable document format (PDF). To download and view these documents you will need the latest version of Adobe Acrobat Reader. This software is available free at: http://www.adobe.com. A paper copy of this solicitation will not be available to requestors. Surplus dealers, small business dealers and distributors (having existing stock of surplus or newly manufactured material) are invited to respond to this synopsis. The response should include a completed surplus certificate, DLAD 52.211-9000, Government surplus Material or adequate traceability documentation to show that the product is acceptable. The government may alter the acquisition strategy if purchase of existing surplus or newly-manufactured inventory is in the best interest of the Government. NSN: 3110-01-398-0705. CONTROLLED UNCLASSIFIED INFORMATION
Single Source Justification (Simplified Acquisition)
Based on the market research efforts discussed in Section D below, Phillips Corporation is currently the
only interested/capable vendor in the market to meet the Government's requirement. Therefore, use of the
authority at FAR 13.106-1(b)(1)(i), which states “Contracting Officers may solicit from one source if the
contracting officer determines that the circumstances of the contract action deem only one source
reasonably available,” is appropriate to meet this requirement.
Section D: Efforts to Obtain Competition
On 20 August 25, a search was conducted on GSA Advantage to determine if the requested products and/ or
product numbers were available to meet the subject requirements. A determination that the products were
potentially procurable via GSA was made based on the product description provided by the Project Manager.
A Request for Information (RFI77239) was issued on 20 August 2025 with a closing date of 26 August 2025
using the eBuy tool. The RFI was issued under the category MAS: 811310MR and complementary special
item number (SIN) OLM. Two responses were received, both of which stated that the vendor does not sell the
products required via GSA Advantage. In accordance with FAR 8.004, PZIA considered satisfying the
requirement from or through the non-mandatory sources list in FAR 8.004(a)(1) before considering
commercial sources in the open market.
A Sources Sought Notice (FA910125Laser_ RotaryTable) was issued on the SAM.gov website on 20 August
25 with a closing date of 26 August 25. The notice was issued to determine if there is a small or large business
with the capability to meet the subject requirement for a Trunnion Rotary Table for an existing Haas
Computer Numerical Control (CNC) Machine. Interested vendors were required to provide a budgetary
estimate along with projected delivery time frame. PZIA did not receive any responses to this notice.
Isel USA and Phillips Corporation were contacted on 26 August 25 to confirm the interest and capability in
meeting the subject requirement, as the PM identified the vendors are known sources potentially capable of
meeting the requirement. On 28 August 2025, Isel USA denied interest and/or capability. On 3 September
2025, Phillips confirmed their interest and capability in meeting the requirement by supplying a budgetary
estimate that included specifications.
A search of the System for Award Management (SAM) website was conducted on 3 September 2025
confirming Phillips Corporation has an active profile and there are no active exclusions in the Responsibility/
Qualification section of SAM.
A synopsis of proposed contract action in the form of a Notice of Intent (Notice ID: FA910125RotaryTable)
was issued on the SAM.gov website (IAW FAR Subpart 5.2) on 8 September 2025 to provide notification that
PZIA intends to solicit and negotiate with a single source, Phillips Corporation. Responses to the notice were
due to PZIA on 12 September 2025 in which PZIA received no responses.
IAW FAR 10.001(a)(2)(iii), market research was conduct appropriate to the circumstances before soliciting
offers for acquisitions with an estimated value less than the simplified acquisition threshold when adequate
information is not available and the circumstances justify its cost and to the maximum extent practicable.

matters.title: Photocatalytic Reactor for Annealing Air Pollution Control System
matters.text:
Federal notice (Justification), DEPT OF DEFENSE.DEPT OF THE NAVY.NSWC INDIAN HEAD DIVISION
Title: Photocatalytic Reactor for Annealing Air Pollution Control System
Solicitation number: FY25-AUG13-37
PSC: 4610; NAICS: 221310
Description: CIP 452: Procurement Synopsis The Naval Surface Warfare Center, Indian Head (NSWC IHD) has a requirement to procure 2 advanced oxidation photocatalytic reactors to destroy nitrate esters and other organics dissolved in recirculating process-water sourced from an existing air scrubbing process and 2 reverse osmosis units to remove dissolved salts from a potable water utility make-up water source. All process-water wet surfaces of the reactor system will be constructed of stainless-steel material that is resistant to water pH as low as 0 from nitrate ions. All seals will be commercially sourced and made from hexafluoropropylene and vinylidene difluoride copolymer materials. The entirety of each reactor system must fit in a contiguous facility floor space area of 0.91m x 1.85m. The reactor systems must be able to be placed back-to-back and be fully serviceable from the freely accessible short end of each reactor with both placed within a total contiguous facility floor space area of 1.52m x 1.85m. The reactor system must be capable of completely mineralizing nitrate esters and other organics present to CO2, H2O, N2, NO3- & resultant minerals. Catalyst materials must not leave the reactor system. Each reactor must be able to control the nitrate ester and organics process-water concentrations to below maximum safe and effective levels during long term continuous operating periods of the existing process. Each reactor system must be able to lower the process-water nitrate ester concentration to a non-detectable level according to State of Maryland standards when running on a closed loop after no more nitrate esters are added within an acceptable period as determined by the NSWC IHD. Each reactor system must be rated at 40-kW or less input power and be compatible with a 240-VAC 3-Phase electrical power feed system. The reactors must include a complete and fully functional stand-alone programmable logic controller (PLC)/human machine interface (HMI) system and historian compatible with the existing facility air scrubber PLC/HMI control system and process-water control elements including necessary alarm and response communications. Each reverse osmosis system will be a Veolia LT4-2 model capable of producing 2.00-GPM of RO water from 2.67-GPM of potable water or an off-the-shelf equivalent capability system as determined by the NSWC IHD of the same or smaller facility floor footprint and electrical power requirements. The Contractor must have provided a reactor system of similar design and functionality to another client and that reactor system must have been operational for more than 5 years with an acceptable uptime and repair record as determined by the NSWC IHD. The same period will be used for the second reactor system upon exercising the contract option. 5.Rationale Justifying Use of Cited Statutory Authority.
The pollution control system (PCS) currently installed is a design unique to the facility. Due
to environmental considerations, the system was built to capture and destroy nitroglycerine
that evaporate in the ovens. Due to the unique nature of this system, any AOP reactor the
Government uses must go through sufficient testing to determine if the reactor is able to meet
requirements. This would be required of any company that is not able to provide sufficient
evidence of being able to meet our need. As a result, the companies would be required to
prove their efficacy through a pilot scale experiment or showing results of an existing system
that is similar in nature and function. Purifics has a deep knowledge and expertise of our
system and its requirement as they were the company that designed and built the legacy
pollution control system. Purifics has shown that they are able to meet our requirement over
the life of our annealing facility.
The proprietary Purifics Photo-Cat® AOP+ reactor system includes a patented Ceramic Ultra-
Filtration (CUF®) unit. This filtration is important for keeping the proper catalyst
concentration within the reactor system flow passages. Without the recirculation of catalyst,
the catalyst concentration will decrease below effective range producing undesirable
intermediates and allows the catalyst to build up in the PCS creating deposits of the catalyst
material. This reactor system does not require the addition of chemicals, such as hydrogen
peroxide or any other adjuncts, which are known to cause undesirable intermediates that clog
the system.
Purifics, Inc. cites the following patents: #5,462,674; #5,554,300; #5,589,078; #6,136,203;
#6,215,126B1; #6,398,971B1; #7,008,473B2; #7,326,278B2; #7,425,272B2; #7,588,688B2;
#7,800,310B2; #7,837,952B2; #9,259,502B2; #9,133,047B2; #8,491,789; #10,071,927;
#10,005,686; #10,315,935.
If the government were to test any other technology discovered or offered, it would take
approximately 545 days and $1M. These costs are not expected to be recouped by
competition and would create unacceptable delays in meeting fleet requirements.

responses were received.

supplies/services covered by this J&A will be fair and reasonable.

future contracts for the types of supplies/services covered by this document. If another
potential source emerges, NSWC IHD will assess whether competition for future
requirements is feasible.

NEGOTIATION SENSITIVE
Justification and Approval (J&A) for Other Than Full and Open Competition
I. Agency and Contracting Activity.
United States Air Force
AFSC/PZAAB
Tinker AFB, OK 73145
Purchase Request (PR)#: FD2030-24-00335
II. Nature and/or description of the action being approved.
This individual Justification and Approval (J&A) authorizes the use of other than full and open competition procedures to
obtain a new, firm fixed price, sole source contract. The contemplated contract will be with MOOG, Incorporated,
Commercial and Government Entity (CAGE) 94697, for the procurement of the Linear Valves. MOOG, Incorporated is
currently the only source approved for manufacture of these valves. This is not a bridge action and is a non-commercial
acquisition. The estimated total dollar value is $643,200.00 with an estimated period of performance of May 2025 - May
2027.
III. Description of supplies/services required to meet agency needs.
Re-manufacture of:
Noun: Primary Valve / Secondary Valve
National Stock Number (NSN): 4810-01-326-0862PR / 4810-01-326-0863
P/N (Part Number): 1886-280 / 1886-290
AMC/AMSC: R3/D
Type of Fund Appropriation: 97X4930
Maximum Total Quantity:
Estimated Unit Price:
Estimated Total Value: $643,200.00
Contract Summary
YEAR Max Quantity Unit Price Estimated Total Dollars Estimated Period of Performance
CLIN 0001 $289,440.00 May 2025 - May 2027
CLIN 0002 $353,760.00 May 2025 - May 2027
IV. Demonstration that the contractor's unique qualifications or the nature of the acquisition requires use of the
authority cited above.
MOOG, Incorporated is the Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) and possesses the specifications,
plans, and drawings relating to the manufacture of these linear valves. This re-manufacture contract is
required to support the USAF for the manufacture of F110 engines. These are critical safety items that
require engineering source approval to prevent any risk during installation on the engine and during
flight. The 421st SCMS has determined that award to any other source would result in unacceptable
delays by increasing lead time to fulfill Air Force Requirements. This acquisition will be for a new
manufacture contract for the continued production of this highly specialized re-manufacture with
NEGOTIATION SENSITIVE
August 2023 Page 2 of 5
NEGOTIATION SENSITIVE
Justification and Approval (J&A) for Other Than Full and Open Competition
MOOG, Incorporated. Data is available and any interested vendors are required to submit a Source
Approval Request (SAR)package. These items are critical safety items and considered highly specialized
components of a major military engine. These items require effective process control and the need to
maintain strict adherence to process parameter values and the shop practices that optimize material
structure and mechanical properties. The interrelationships between process parameters, material
structure, and mechanical properties are very complex. MOOG, Incorporated possesses unique
capabilities derived from knowledge and expertise gained during previous re-manufacture of these
items. Probability of failure would be unacceptable from the standpoint of safety of personnel and/or
equipment. Therefore, this acquisition will be a new manufacture contract to produce this highly
specialized re-manufacture with MOOG, Incorporated.
The 421st SCMS has determined that award to any other source would result in unacceptable delays in
fulfilling the USAF requirement. Delays in manufacture will have the potential of disrupting the
availability of F110 engines, thereby leaving USAF unable to meet critical mission requirements
resulting in a Mission Incapable Awaiting Parts (MICAP) situation. A delay in this acquisition would
generate backorders/MICAPs at a rate of 3ea per month. These parts require engineering source
approval by the design control activity in order to maintain the quality of the parts. Existing unique
design capability, engineering skills, and manufacturing knowledge by the qualified source requires
acquisition of the part from an approved source. An alternate source must qualify in accordance with
the design control activity's procedures, as approved by the cognizant Government engineering
activity. New sources are required to submit a Source Approval Request (SAR) package to the
engineering source for approval. Interested sources must be approved for both Phase I and Phase II of
the SAR process based on the qualification requirements, MQR-PSD-1, dated 29 Oct 2019.
Accordingly, MOOG, Incorporated is the only firm capable of providing the new manufacture services
described in Section III above without the USAF experiencing unacceptable delays in fulfilling
requirements.
V. Description of efforts made to ensure that offers are solicited from as many potential sources as practicable,
including whether a notice was or will be publicized as required by subpart 5.2 and, if not, which exception under
FAR 5.202 applies.
A Sources Sought Synopsis was posted under FD20302400335 on 21 April 2025 with a closing date of 29 April
2025. This requirement will be synopsized in https://sam.gov as a notice of proposed contract action IAW FAR
5.201. Government defined pre-award qualifications of new sources cannot be identified due to the
unavailability of the necessary technical data as described in section IV. The OEM is currently the only entity
capable of approving additional sources.
VI. Determination by the Contracting Officer that the anticipated cost to the Government will be fair and reasonable.
The Contracting Officer will ensure that the items described herein are negotiated at a fair and reasonable
price to the Government. IAW FAR as supplemented, the contractor will be required to submit Other Than
Certified Cost or Pricing Data. A detailed price analysis will be performed. The Contracting Officer will request a
technical evaluation from the Defense Contract Management Agency (DCMA) to aid in the evaluation of the
contractor's proposal if necessary. The Contracting Officer will seek audit assistance from the Defense Contract
Audit Agency (DCAA) if necessary.
NEGOTIATION SENSITIVE
August 2023 Page 3 of 5
NEGOTIATION SENSITIVE
Justification and Approval (J&A) for Other Than Full and Open Competition
VII. Description of the market research conducted and the results, or a statement of the reasons market research was
not conducted.
Market research, in accordance with FAR 10, was conducted by a multi-functional team consisting of the Item
Manager, Equipment Specialist, Logistics Officer, and Engineer. This research was conducted on 21 April 2025
and concluded on 29 April 2025, which included inquiries into internet sites including Google, the Thomas
Register, Haystack, and similar item manufacturer's websites. Other sources manufacture similar items, but
none have been identified as having data rights described in section IV. Further, this requirement cannot be
satisfied with a commercial or modified commercial item.
VIII. Any other facts supporting the use of Other Than Full and Open Competition.
The development of additional sources to produce this item is not feasible within allowable timeframes. USAF has not
received any SAR packages for this item. Once a SAR is submitted by a vendor, a period of 2 years can be required to
process and validate an alternate suppliers approach. As there is no vendor-submitted SAR present to initiate this process,
the proposed sole source approach is USAF's remaining alternative to execute the requirement between now and the
need date for the item. Delays in new procurement have the potential of causing a work stop of F100 engines, thereby
grounding related aircraft and leaving USAF unable to meet critical mission requirements. For these reasons, the prime
vendor is the only source capable of providing the supplies described in paragraph III without USAF experiencing
unacceptable delays in fulfilling requirements.
IX. List of any sources that expressed, in writing, an interest in the acquisition.
None.
X. A statement of the actions, if any, the agency may take to remove or overcome any barriers to competition before
any subsequent acquisitions for the supplies or services required.
Actions to increase competition on this acquisition will be performed by the Cognizant Engineering authority.
USAF will continue to monitor the marketplace for source development and will continue discussions with the
OEM regarding additional approved sources. USAF will continue to synopsize the requirement, rescreen the item,
and attempt to acquire the data necessary to qualify additional sources.

As evidenced by their signature, the contracting officer certifies that this justification is accurate and complete to the
best of their knowledge and belief.

As evidenced by their signatures, the technical and/or requirements personnel have certified that any
supporting data contained herein, which is their responsibility, is both accurate and complete.

attachments.text:
JUSTIFICATION FOR SOLE SOURCE PROCUREMENT
10 U.S.C. § 3205
In compliance with Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 13.501(a)(1)(ii), this justification
uses the format at FAR 6.104-1 and is modified to state that the procedures in FAR subpart
13.5 are used.
1. Agency and Contracting Activity.
The Department of Homeland Security, United States Coast Guard (USCG), Surface
Forces Logistics Center (SFLC), Contracting and Procurement Division (CPD)2 2402
Hawkins Point Road, Baltimore, MD 21226-5000 proposes to enter into a contract for a
sole source, in accordance with Subpart 13.5 Simplified Procedures for Certain
Commercial Products and Commercial Services and FAR 13.501(a)(i) Special
documentation requirements for sole source (including brand name) acquisitions.
2. Nature and/or Description of the Action being Approved.
(a) Nature of the action: The U. S. Coast Guard SFLC proposes to enter a
contract on a sole source basis with Neuver Maritime to purchase two (2)
each steering actuator rotors.
(b) Name and address of the contractor:
Neuver Maritime
Aarsundvegen 24
6270 Brattvåg
POC: Stine Ødegaard Urke
+47 920 16 904
stine.urke@neuver.com
(c) Type of action: Firm Fixed Price contract.
(d) Estimated total value (including options): Total Price $313,280.86
(e) Type of funding: Surface Operations funds
(f) Year of funding: Fiscal Year 2026
(g) PR number: Pending FY26 funding
(h) Background information about the requirement:
USCG Healy has two (2) rotors onboard. The current rotors are the original
equipment manufacturer (OEM) built rotors from 1997. This requirement is for the
Last Updated 01/06/25 1
new OEM replacement Rotors for the CGC Healy Steering Actuator.
3. Description of Supplies/Services.
The requirement is to provide two (2) Steering Actuator Rotors in long-term reusable
shipping and storage containers as ready for issue rotors for CGC Healy. The rotors are
required to be in the same configuration as those provided for the CGC Healy production
line.
The Steering Actuator Rotors are installed onboard the 420’ WAGB, servicing the
steering system on the cutter.
The items provided must be OEM, due to proprietary rights and no vendors licensed to
build these. Due to the long lead time of these rotors, the parts must be purchased in
advance of the cutter’s scheduled dockside availability. Rotors are in accordance with
OEM part number specifications. Compatibility with the original equipment is required.
Items required to complete the assembly must be manufactured by or for the OEM,
NEUVER Maritime Inc. The end item identification is: STEERING ACTUATOR
ROTOR TO BE USED ON THE USCGC Healy 420 FT WAGB. The rotors’ dimensions
are L1400xW1400xH1600 mm, each weighing 4700 kg. and the following description
applies.
Name Part Number NSN QTY
Steering Actuator P80069 Styremotor HS 2030-01-
02
(ROTOR) 700-04 2 x 40 Rotor F24-7004
4. Identification of Statutory Authority Permitting Sole Source Procurement.
Section 3205 of Title 10, U.S. Code permits sole source procurement. The FAR
implements this authority in section 13.501(a) (sole source (including brand name
acquisitions) as the FAR defines such term in section 2.101).
5. Identification of Exception to the Buy American Act. in accordance with
The Buy American Act does not apply. Per FAR 25.103(b)(1)(i), spare and replacement
parts are an exception, under 25.104(a)(30).
6. Demonstration that the Proposed Contractor’s Unique Qualifications or the Nature
of the Acquisition Require Use of the Authority Cited.
Neuver Maritime is the only sole source to possess the drawings and proprietary
information needed for this requirement. As the rotors approach their maximum operating
hours, they are replaced/repaired as part of the routine overhaul and maintenance during
scheduled drydock availabilities. The lead time for the repair/overhaul of the rotor from
arrival at the repair facility is approximately 280 days. If the rotor is not delivered in time
for an upcoming drydock availability, during which time the cutter will be docked for
Last Updated 01/06/25 2
access to pull the shafts & rudders to make repairs, it could cause catastrophic failure and
further delays to the cutters’ missions. The anticipated lead time to procure new rotors is
approximately 180 days.
Critical tolerances and clearances ensure proper operating parameters are met. Use of this
rotor will ensure physical and functional inter-changeability, as well as configuration and
performance requirements. Using other than OEM rotors would be high risk because
Neuver Maritime rotors must be configured in accordance with USCG system architecture
requirements.
Procuring an alternative product other than Neuver Maritime rotors will require complete
infrastructure replacement with a significant increase in cost. These costs include: The
composition of the material, heat treatment (if required), determining whether the
assemblies are forged or cast, as well as all dimensions (with tolerances), and operating
parameters would be the minimum information needed before an evaluation of a rotor
assembly could be attempted. Even if this information was available, the Coast Guard
does not have the organic capabilities to evaluate and determine if all of the assemblies
meet the OEM standards. Without the data and manufacturing specifications from the
OEM, proving that the non-OEM assemblies are equal to the Neuver Maritime rotors
would be impossible to determine.
During market research, a sources sought notice was posted and yielded no capable vendors.
Per information obtained from the OEM vendor, they maintain proprietary rights, have no
licensed vendors and do not intend to sell the rights to any vendors or the USCG.
7. Description of Efforts Made to Ensure that Offers are Solicited from as Many
Potential Sources as is Practicable.
In accordance with FAR subpart 5.2, an effort to solicit as many potential sources as
practicable, a sources sought notice was posted in SAM.GOV, to confirm or deny whether
Neuver Maritime is the only responsible source. Refer to para. 9. for the information.
The notice yielded one (1) company stating their interest in this requirement.
The CGC Healy – Steering Actuator (Rotor) purchase was submitted in the Acquisition
Planning Forecast System (hereafter APFS) on February 20, 2025. APFS F2025069435
was published on 07 August 2025, and no responses have been received.
On Aug 6, 2025, Neuver Maritime responded to a USCG e-mail sent by Mr. Alan
Randolph regarding Steering Actuator Rotors list of authorized supply distributors and
repair facilities. Based on the specificity of the requirement at the time, which was to
provide supply parts and repairs, Neuver Maritime informed USCG that they do not have
authorized distributors and do not plan to license any for our equipment.
8. Determination by the Contracting Officer that the Anticipated Cost to the
Government will be Fair and Reasonable.
Last Updated 01/06/25 3
The Contracting Officer (KO) anticipates that the overall cost of the Coast Guard will be
fair and reasonable based on historical pricing and the independent Government cost
estimate (IGCE).
9. Description of Market Research.
Extensive market research was conducted by the Contracting Officer’s Representative
(COR), from February 2025 – August 2025 in an effort to identify companies that can
provide new OEM parts. Market research was conducted by identifying various companies
on the internet, through searching General Service Administration (GSA) Advantage and
Department of Homeland Security’s Strategic Sourcing Vehicles. Information was also
obtained from NESSS/NE-TIMS, Neuver Maritime Inc, FEDLOG, FLS, and HAYSTACK,
and through the Acquisition Planning Forecast System. Market Research revealed that the
OEM has a network of Neuver Maritime Inc. distributors within the U.S.
Neuver Maritime Inc. technical data is currently unavailable to the U.S. Coast Guard.
Manufacturing resources of parts that could satisfy the OEM requirements has been
determined to be a sole source, since a significant portion of this data remains proprietary to
Neuver Maritime Inc, and they do not have, nor are they allowing any vendors to obtain
proprietary rights to perform any of the work required.
The contracting officer issued a sources sought notice number 70Z08525S_HEALY
STEERING ACTUATOR, on August 26, 2025, to determine if a domestic end product
exists that meets this requirement. The sources sought notice closed on Sept 5, 2025, and
one (1) response was received. The company responded with interest, however, did not
provide any evidence of their capability to build these rotors or that they have any licenses
with Neuver Maritime to meet the specifications identified in the sources sought notice.
Based on the results of all the market research, it has been determined that the requisite
supplies are not available from any other source.
10. Any Other Facts Supporting the Use of Sole Source Procurement.
Neuver Maritime Inc. is the only known company possessing the specifications, engineering
control procedures and proprietary methods to ensure the design configuration, manufacturing
and quality control required to produce the rotors to the engineering specifications and
requirements. Therefore, the Government does not have any data to compare other
manufacturers’ parts to ensure the same fit, form, and function, nor does the Government
possess the independent expertise to evaluate other manufacturer’s parts. These steering
actuator rotors are designed, engineered and built to close tolerances and have undergone
numerous shop tests and rigorous operational testing before being certified and approved by
the OEM for use by the end user. After market (non-OEM) parts manufacturers/distributors do
not have access to this proprietary information and therefore could not produce parts that are
equal.
11. A Listing of the Sources, if Any, that Expressed, in Writing, an Interest in the
Last Updated 01/06/25 4
Acquisition.
Neuver Maritime
Aarsundvegen 24
6270 Brattvåg
POC: Stine Ødegaard Urke
+47 920 16 904
stine.urke@neuver.com
The sources sought notice received one response from the following company:
BHPE, LLC. BHPE; UEI# UPDJHPJUYQ71; Cage Code: 9SWS7
Point of Contact and Company Address:
Jonathan Howard
405-473-0422
Jonathan@bh.pe
Address:
10601 S Western AVE
SUITE- 113
Oklahoma City, Oklahoma 73170
The company stated interest in the requirement, however, did not submit any further
information that supported their ability to perform the required work.
12. A Statement of the Actions, if Any, the Agency May Take to Remove or Overcome
Any Barriers to Competition Before Any Subsequent Acquisition for Supplies or
Services Required.
Neuver Maritime owns the technical data and drawings, and they have stated the company
does not intend to sell the rights to such data to the Coast Guard, or any other vendors. The
Coast Guard has made several attempts to acquire them with no success. The proprietary
data is required to allow competition for the requirement. To date, Neuver Maritime has
not expressed any interest in selling or otherwise providing the appropriate data rights to
USCG. Based on the findings of the market research conducted it is determined that this
requirement is only available from one source. The Coast Guard will continue to engage
Neuver Maritime for the release of proprietary data prior to any subsequent
acquisitions. All future requirements will be synopsized. Unsuccessful efforts to obtain
OEM data make it unlikely that barriers to competition will be overcome. At this time, no
other known equipment manufacturers produce aftermarket assemblies that are suitable or
interchangeable with the Neuver rotors.
13. Contracting Officer’s Certification.
I certify that the data supporting the recommended use of a sole source procurement is accurate
and complete to the best of my knowledge and belief.
Last Updated 01/06/25 5
KLOEPPEL.ROBI Digitally signed by
KLOEPPEL.ROBIN.B.1229493945
N

STEERING ACTUATOR, on August 26, 2025, to determine if a domestic end product
exists that meets this requirement. The sources sought notice closed on Sept 5, 2025, and
one (1) response was received. The company responded with interest, however, did not
provide any evidence of their capability to build these rotors or that they have any licenses
with Neuver Maritime to meet the specifications identified in the sources sought notice.
Based on the results of all the market research, it has been determined that the requisite
supplies are not available from any other source.
10. Any Other Facts Supporting the Use of Sole Source Procurement.
Neuver Maritime Inc. is the only known company possessing the specifications, engineering
control procedures and proprietary methods to ensure the design configuration, manufacturing
and quality control required to produce the rotors to the engineering specifications and
requirements. Therefore, the Government does not have any data to compare other
manufacturers’ parts to ensure the same fit, form, and function, nor does the Government
possess the independent expertise to evaluate other manufacturer’s parts. These steering
actuator rotors are designed, engineered and built to close tolerances and have undergone
numerous shop tests and rigorous operational testing before being certified and approved by
the OEM for use by the end user. After market (non-OEM) parts manufacturers/distributors do
not have access to this proprietary information and therefore could not produce parts that are

This anticipated contract will be for the repair of the KC-135 Inflight Refueling Shroud. This item is repaired directly by the

personnel and technical data to satisfy the USAF's needs. Due to the complexity and criticality of this
component, market research revealed there is only one qualified source, Mission. This KC-135 item is a critical
application items as defined in the Aviation and Critical Safety Item Management handbook. Repair of this NSN is a highly
specialized service due to the need for process control of the quality of equipment and tooling, shop practices, knowledge of
process material interrelationships, and quality assurance surveillance necessary to satisfy the USAF’s minimum need for the
KC-135 weapons system. This repair is imperative to allow the Government to be mission ready at all times. Therefore, this

KC-135 Inflight Refueling Shroud. The repair data and acceptance test criteria needed to foster additional competition for the

quote. Mission has been the only approved source since 2012. The Government has established Qualifications Requirements

The 424th SCMS believes that award to any other source would result in substantial duplication of cost to the Government

4. Statutory Authority Permitting Other Than Full and Open Competition
10 U.S.C. 2304(c)(1), Only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency
requirements.
5. Rationale Justifying Use of Cited Statutory Authority
Northrup Grumman is the original equipment manufacturer and only known source for manufacture of
P/Ns 247819, 247815, or 6867277-1for the AN/SPQ-9B.
Blank Ordering Agreement (BOA) # N0002415G5354 was sole sourced to Northrop Grummen for the
AN/SPQ-9B systems and procurement of the technical data package. Northrop Grumman has confirmed
that they retain the intellectual property (IP)/data rights of P/Ns 247819, 247815, or 6867277-1. The
Government then utilized the technical data package to compete Contract # N0002418C5395. It was
awarded to DRS Laurel and BOA # N0002419G5502 was then sole sourced to DRS Laurel. Currently
Naval Sea Systems Command (NAVSEA) 02551 has competitive synopsis Solicitation # N00024R5528
posted to SAM.gov for AN/SPQ-9B systems. The NAVSEA 02551 Contracting Officer for Solicitation #
N0002424R5528 confirmed with the program office that Northrop Grummen retains the IP/data rights for
P/Ns 247819, 247815, or 6867277-1. Currently the program office has enough of these parts to provide
them as Government Furnished Material (GFM) for synopsized Solicitation # N0002424R5528.
NSWC Crane does not does hold the source code for P/N 247815. NSWC Crane engineers do not have
the expertise to design and develop the firmware. Writing the firmware requires an in depth understanding
of the SPQ-9B system and the system software. Northrop Grummen is unable to offer the IP rights for
P/N 6867277-1 due to the technology being used across multiple large defense programs. Furthermore,
the construction of this unit takes place in a specialized and licensed chamber. Awardee of Contract #
N0002418C5395, DRS Laurel, confirmed that they cannot manufacture P/Ns 247819, 247815, or
6867277-1 and these parts are currently provided as GFM through Northrup Grumman.
It would not be cost effective to establish another source to manufacture P/Ns 247819, 247815, or
6867277-1. It is estimated it would 23 months and $98k for P/N 247819, 23 months and $171k for P/N
247815, and 30 months and $130k for P/N 6867277-1 ($399k total) to certify another source to
manufacture these items. A new source would have to reengineer and validate, through testing, any new
design.
The program does not have the required funding to establish another manufacturing source. In addition,
the program cannot encounter a two year delay. It would seriously jeopardize installation schedules and
fleet readiness. The array logic boards, phase shifter driver boards, and TR limiter, are integral
components of the AN/SPQ-9B Radar Antenna. Without the Radar Antenna the multiple ship platforms
would be vulnerable to missile attack because there is no operational anti-missile search radar. These
parts are "single point of failure". Therefore, if one of these parts fail, the radar fails to detect any enemy
incoming missiles. There are no equivalent backup systems aboard U.S. Navy ships that are equipped
with AN/SPQ-9B radars that provide protection/detection.
6. Description of Efforts Made to Solicit Offers from as Many Offerors as Practicable
A sources sought synopsis was posted to the Government-wide Point of Entry (GPE) on 28 September
2022, in accordance with Defense Acquisition Regulations Supplement PGI 206.302-1(d). One response
was received from DataCon providing information that they had proposed to be a subcontractor to
2
J&A Number:CR-22240
Northrop Grummen for some of the items on the AN/SPQ-9B in 2009. Datacon believes they could
manufacture the required items with updated IP and data, however the Navy does not retain or have the
authority release the required IP and data in order to allow for competition on this requirement.
A synopsis was posted to the GPE on 28 November 2022. To-date, no responses have been received, and
any will be considered.
Market Research was conducted by the requiring technical activity and contracting officer which verified
that Northrop Grumman has all IP/data rights and Northrop Grummen provides these parts to the current
contract holder. The contracting officer reviewed the circumstances surrounding the need to obtain the
required supplies/services without providing full and open competition and confirmed the basis of this
J&A. The government is unable to procure IP/data rights as Northrupp Grumman will not release them.
This solicitation will be advertised at SAM.gov. Responses will be reviewed to determine if additional
sources exist.
7. Determination of Fair and Reasonable Cost.
The Contracting Officer has determined the anticipated costs to the Government for the supplies/services
covered by the J&A will be fair and reasonable prior to award. It is anticipated that DCMA pricing
assistance and/or DCAA audit services o fthe contractor’s proposal will be requested, along with the
offeror’s certificate of current cost and pricing data to support the fair and reasonable price determination.
Both price analysis and cost analysis of the proposal, along with a technical evaluation, will be conducted.
8. Actions to Remove Barriers to Future Competition.
For the reasons set forth in Paragraph 5, NSWC Crane Division has no plans at this time to compete
future contracts for the types of supplies covered by this document. If other potential sources emerge,
NSWC Crane Division will assess whether competition for future requirements is feasible.
As this is a follow-on for supplies and services previously awarded on a non-competitive basis, in
accordance with DFARS PGI 206.304(a)(S-70)(i), the prior J&A was provided to the approval authority
for review. Approval of this J&A signifies the approval authority has made the determination required by
DFARS PGI 206.304(a)(S-70)(ii).

Through market research conducted by the Requiring Technical
Activity (RTA) and the Contract Specialist, ALKAN was
identified as the only source that can meet the Government
requirement. A Request for Information (RFI), N0016421SNB15,
was issued on the Beta SAM website on 11 December 2020. NSWC
Crane stated their intent to award a sole-source contract to
ALKAN for sub-components for depot repair of the BRU-65
Ejector Rack Assembly for MH-60 Helicopter platforms. One
response was received from
. After discussion with
ALKAN, ALKAN confirmed that only ALKAN will be supporting this
effort as does not have the experience and
expertise required to support the effort. In accordance with
FAR 5.201(b), the proposed contract was synopsized on the Beta
SAM website on 5 February 2021. To date, there have been no
responses to the synopsis. Any responses from interested
sources received prior to contract award will be reviewed.

The Contracting Officer has determined that the anticipated cost
to the Government for the supplies/services covered by this J&A
will be fair and reasonable. The Contracting Officer will use
cost and price analysis to determine a fair and reasonable
price. Historical pricing information will also be used to aid
in determining fair and reasonable prices. Certified cost and
pricing data is not required for this requirement, however,
Defense Contract Management Agency (DCMA) and/or Defense

Contract Audit Agency (DCAA) assistance and/or audit may be
requested to support the fair and reasonable cost determination.
8. Actions to Remove Barriers to Competition
For the reasons set forth in Paragraph 5, NSWC-CR has no plans
at this time to compete future procurements for the required
supplies and services. NSWC-CR will continue to survey the
market for future requirements and if another potential source
emerges, NSWC-CR will assess if competition for future
requirements is feasible.
