matters.title: Honeywell Engineering Sustainment Support, Sole Source to Honeywell
matters.text:
Federal notice (Presolicitation), DEPT OF DEFENSE.DEFENSE LOGISTICS AGENCY.DLA AVIATION
Title: Honeywell Engineering Sustainment Support, Sole Source to Honeywell
Solicitation number: SPE4A625R0421
PSC: 1680; NAICS: 336413
Description: The Defense Logistics Agency (DLA) Aviation intends to solicit on a sole source basis, to Honeywell International Inc., via a Letter Request for Proposal (RFP) for sustainment engineering and program management services of out of production parts. Honeywell International Inc. is the sole source OEM for the target NSNs and market research has not resulted in the identification of any other source(s) that can provide this requirement. This contract will establish a priced sustainment engineering Contract Line Item Number (CLIN). Specific tasks will include engineering reviews of each part number to assess the status of engineering drawings, data packages, and specifications. In addition, contractor support actions will be included to ensure that communication is maintained with the Government. It is contemplated that this requirement will be added to the Honeywell Supplier Capabilities Contract (SCC), contract number SPE4AX-22-D-0003. This contract action is anticipated to be Firm Fixed Price (FFP), with a 12 month Period of Performance (PoP) from the SCC modification effective date and yearly renewal options as needed. This solicitation is unrestricted using Other Than Full and Open Competition as prescribed by FAR 6.302-1, Only One Responsible Source and no Other Supplies or Services will Satisfy Agency Requirements. Therefore, a sole source letter RFP will be utilized, and solicitation will not be posted to DIBBS. Any responsible source may submit a capability statement detailing specifically how the contract requirements in the letter RFP will be met. If it is found that sources other than the OEM can meet the Government�s requirements, a RFP will be posted to DIBBS at https://www.dibbs.bsm.dla.mil/RFP/. The solicitation issue date is expected to be on or around October 8, 2025. Any questions in regards to this requirement should be directed to the Acquisition Specialist, Ms. Chadney Thompson at Chadney.Thompson@dla.mil

matters.title: Logistics Modernization Integration Support (LMIS) for Defense Logistics Agency (DLA) Distribution, Pool 1, Enterprise Facility Modernization, EDC Equipment Modernization
matters.text:
Federal notice (Justification), DEPT OF DEFENSE.DEFENSE LOGISTICS AGENCY.DLA DISTRIBUTION
Title: Logistics Modernization Integration Support (LMIS) for Defense Logistics Agency (DLA) Distribution, Pool 1, Enterprise Facility Modernization, EDC Equipment Modernization
Solicitation number: SP3300-20-F-1300-P00035_P00036
PSC: 3910; NAICS: 333922
Description: In accordance with FAR 6.302-1, the Defense Logistics Agency (DLA) anticipates issuing modifications to existing EDC Modernization Delivery Order SP3300-20-F-1300 on a sole source basis to Advantaged Solutions, Inc. for updating cybersecurity requirements, integrating the Okta solution, incorporate WES software changes, integrating the parcel robotic system, AGV pathways updates, and for the contract PoP extension required to complete installations and software integration. Advantage Solutions Inc. has a general contractor on site to make modifications to the facility, to include the requirements listed above. Awarding to another vendor would add unwarranted complexity to the integration of systems. Additional vendors would require them to mobilize multiple times at an increased cost. ASI is already contracted to perform the installation and integration requirements listed above, which need to be appropriately coordinated for the work to be performed. In accordance with FAR 6.302-1, Advantage Solutions, Inc. is the only responsible source capable of providing these requirements at this time. The J&A for the modifications are being posted as part of this notice. This is not a solicitation for proposals or an invitation for bids. The Government does not anticipate receiving responses to this notice of a non-competitive action.

This sole source justification is provided in accordance with FAR 13.5 Simplified Procedures for
Certain Commercial Products and Commercial Services and specifically under FAR 13.501
Special Documentation Requirements, where acquisitions conducted under Simplified
Acquisition Procedures are exempt from the requirements of FAR Part 6 but still require a
justification using the format of FAR 6.104-1 (FAR Class Deviation 25-11). As provided under
FAR 13.501, this justification is modified to reflect that the procedures under FAR subpart 13.5
were used in accordance with 41 U.S.C. 1901 – Simplified Acquisition Procedures.
1. Agency and Contracting Activity. Identification of the agency and the contracting
activity, and specific identification of the document as a “sole source justification.”
The Department of Homeland Security (DHS), Federal Emergency Management Agency
(FEMA), Office of National Continuity Programs (ONCP), intends to execute a new
award to L3Harris Technologies, Inc. on a sole source basis.
2. Nature and/or description of the action being approved.
This is a Commercial Off-The-Shelf (COTS) sole source action to procure at a Firm
Fixed Priced to L3Harris Technologies, Inc., 1680 University Avenue, Rochester, NY
14610 using simplified acquisition procedures without seeking competition for Manpack
Radio consisting of AN/PRC-160(V)1 and AN/PRC-117G(V)1(C) including accessories;
and any applicable warranties for proprietary products. This action is being taken
pursuant to FAR 13.501. L3Harris Technologies, Inc is the only company that provides
the required items to support the agency needs.
3. Description of Supplies/Services. Describe the supplies or services to be acquired.
Provide the estimated total value (including options, if any).
The requirement includes Manpack Radios consisting of four (4) AN/PRC-117G(V)l (C)s
and eight (8) AN/PRC-160(V)ls, accessories, and any applicable warranties. These
radios must be built to tactical specifications meeting MIL-STD-810G standards, meet all
National Security Agency (NSA) crypto-modernization security standards, capable of
operating on the 4G Automatic Link Establishment (ALE) waveforms, as well as capable
of providing High Frequency (HF), and Very High Frequency (VHF) support. In
addition, the radio must meet space constraint requirements in our current environment.
The radio must not weigh more than 10.5 pounds, nor exceed the following dimensions:
Depth – 9.5 Inches, Height – 9 Inches, Width 3.5 Inches.

attachments.name: Redacted Justification.pdf
attachments.text:
CUI
JUSTIFICATION FOR OTHER THAN
FULL AND OPEN COMPETITION
I. Agency and Contracting Activity.
This Justification and Approval is to request authority for Other Than Full and Open
Competition to support requirements generated for the Air Force Sustainment Center (AFSC),
638 Supply Chain Management Group (SCMG), 408 Supply Chain Management Squadron
(SCMS) / GULB. The contracting activity for this requirement is Defense Logistics Agency
(DLA) Aviation, Warner Robins, DLA/AWB. The purchase request number supporting this
contracting action is FD2060-24-00058.
II. Nature and/or description of the action being approved.
Due to the circumstances described herein, the activity requests authority to procure the
production of the redesigned legacy AN/ALQ-172 Countermeasures Transmitter Line-
Replaceable Units (LRU) using Other Than Full and Open Competition as prescribed by FAR
6.302-1, “Only One Responsible Source and No Other Supplies or Services Will Satisfy Agency
Requirements.” This action will result in a new Firm Fixed Price (FFP) one-time buy definitive
C type contract The period of performance to include all deliveries is anticipated to be FY24 -
.
FY27. This sole source requirement will be procured from the following company:
L3Harris Technologies, Inc.
77 River Rd
Clifton, NJ 07014-2000
CAGE: 28527
Large Business
III. Description of supplies/services required to meet agency needs.
The purpose of this effort is for the production of the redesigned LRU-4 to replace legacy LRU-4
National Stock Number (NSN) 5865-01-533-9874 which is no longer sustainable due to
obsolescence, Diminishing Manufacturing Sources and Material Shortages (DMSMS), and
reliability issues due to legacy technology of the LRU. Temporary NCC number 5865NCC664879
is referenced for this effort until the replacement LRU is cataloged and a new NSN is assigned.
The LRU-4 is a component of the AN/ALQ-172(V)2 Countermeasure Set (CMS) applicable to the
US Air Force (USAF) Global Strike Command B-52H strategic bombers.
CUI

CUI
L3Harris Technologies Inc. is the only vendor with unique capabilities, experience, expertise,
and relationships to satisfy the Government's requirements of the test program sets (TPS) for
these highly specialized items.
L3Harris Technologies Inc. is the original designer and developer of the AN/ALQ-172
Countermeasures System. They are currently on contract for the AN/ALQ-172 redesigns of
LRUs -1, 2, 4, 7, 8, 9, 10, 12, 21 and Radio Frequency Interface Unit (RFIU). The Government
Furnished Equipment (GFE) accountable under contract FA8522-18-C-0001 required for the
redesign effort and development of the TPS is located at L3Harris Technologies Inc.
The Government does not possess a full technical data package for the AN/ALQ-172(V) System.
A contractor must have access to the technical data and have extensive knowledge and expertise
of the AN/ALQ-172 system in order to complete this effort. Due to the lack of completed
functional/interface specifications between the LRUs, system knowledge and experience will be
required in order to properly stimulate Radio Frequency (RF) and digital and analog signals
between the UUTs. A vendor must have expertise on the ALQ-172 theory of operation, greatly
above the knowledge of a generic radar or Circuit Card Assembly level expertise. L3Harris
Technologies Inc. is the only vendor that possesses the knowledge and expertise of the
redesigned AN/ALQ-172 Countermeasures System.
Harris Corporation is currently developing a Form Fit Function and Interface (FFFI) replacement
for the LRU hardware. The development contract(s) will result in qualified prototypes and
delivery of full Level-3 technical data package for each redesigned LRU. The Government will
have full data rights to compete future acquisition of LRU production units.
The LRUs (LRU-1, 2, 4, 7, 8, 9, 10, 12, 21 and RFIU) are highly specialized to the AN/ALQ-172
system because the AN/ALQ-172 system provides Situational Awareness (SA) and Self-
Protection (SP) capabilities to large aircraft such as B-52. This is a unique capability for the B-52
and C-130 aircraft defense against threats. The AN/ALQ-172 Electronic Countermeasures
(ECM) System has been upgraded over the last 40+ years since its inception in the early 1970s.
The system architecture is comprised of three (3) subsystems, pulse (LRU-1 and 2), PD/CW
(LRU-4 and 10) and antenna (LRU-7, 8, and 9), in order to meet its requirements with a
significantly reduced number of LRUs. The small footprint of the system requirement resulted in
a distributed processing architecture between the subsystems, each performing specialized
functions while collaborating with other subsystems. Therefore, internal system interfaces, and
other timing requirements between subsystems, LRUs and SRUs are critical factors for the
proper integration and full operations of the system. Harris Corporation is the only vendor who
has knowledge of the critical factors required to make the system fully operational.
Accordingly, L3Harris Technologies Inc. is the only firm capable of providing the production
units described in Section III above without the U.S. Air Force experiencing substantial
duplication in cost and unacceptable delays that is not expected to be recovered through reverse
engineering the legacy unit.
VI. Description of efforts made to ensure that offers are solicited from as many
CUI
CUI
potential sources as practicable, including whether a notice was or will be publicized
as required by subpart 5.2 and, if not, which exception under FAR 5.202 applies.
A Sources Sought (SS) / Request for Information (RFI) synopsis was posted to SAM.gov on 1
November 2023 with a response date of 16 November 2023 under Solicitation Number
SPRWA1-24-R-MARSLRU-4. The SS/RFI requested responses from interested vendors that
possess the expertise, capabilities, and experience to meet qualification requirements for this
effort. No responses to the posted SSS were received from any potential sources/vendors.
The requirement will be synopsized in SAM.gov in accordance with FAR 5.201. It is anticipated
that sources having an interest in subcontracting may be identified through synopsis. Any source
who responds to the Government as a result of this synopsis will be identified to the prime
contractor as a potential subcontracting possibility.
VII. Determination by the Contracting Officer that the anticipated cost to the
Government will be fair and reasonable.
The contracting officer will complete a price analysis, as well as a detailed cost analysis based on
the submission of certified cost or pricing data to determine the price fair and reasonable.
Support from the Defense Contract Management Agency or the Defense Contract Audit Agency
may be requested as appropriate to aid in evaluating the proposal.
VIII. Description of the market research conducted and the results, or a statement of the
reasons market research was not conducted.
The LRUs within the ALQ-172 are extremely specific and complex in their design and
integration requirements. One major requirement of being successful in production of the MARS
(Maintenance and Reliability System) LRU-4 is having the equipment and expertise to
accomplish both build and acceptance testing of the assets. The cost and time involved in having
another source acquire the equipment and develop the expertise would not be cost effective or
feasible to meet the current mission need. The Government does not possess the data, facilities,
or equipment to furnish a new source in order to accomplish this requirement.
Four (4) search methods were employed herein. The first method employed was review of the
previous ALQ-172 MARS LRU production contracts to identify those vendors with potential
technical expertise for accomplishing the production effort. This research technique is identified
below as Contract Search by Resident Experts (CSRE).
(1) Contract Search by Resident Experts (CSRE):
A review of contracted efforts within the Air Force Supply Chain (AFSC) regarding previous
ALQ-172 MARS LRU production efforts was conducted. The review identified only one
potential source with direct MARS LRU-4 experience as well as expertise with both the legacy
and MARS redesigned ALQ-172 ECM LRU Suites, L3Harris. This vendor is analyzed and
discussed in the Vendor Survey section of this report.
CUI
CUI
(2) General Search by Resident Experts (GSRE):
The Integrated Product Team (IPT) has conducted on-going and continual research into the
industry capabilities to support the ALQ-172. Market research efforts consisted of searching
current contract databases, on-line databases and other Internet sources, and discussions with
industry representatives and engineers with industry knowledge of the ALQ-172.
A general web search was accomplished to identify potential sources for the work effort, using
variations of key terms "ALQ-172", "ALQ-172 LRU-4", "Radar Electronic Warfare
Transmitter", "LRU-4 Countermeasures Transmitter", and "ALQ-172 LRU Production". Market
Research web searches of http://www.gsaadvantage.gov, http://www.testmart.com, and
http://www.thomasnet.com resulted in no additional identified potential sources of procurement.
The query key terms, in order, was "ALQ-172", "ALQ-172 LRU-4", "Radar Electronic Warfare
Transmitter", "LRU-4 Countermeasures Transmitter", and "ALQ-172 LRU Production".
Searches utilizing the two (2) web search tools (SAM.gov and Google.com) yielded no
additional potential sources of procurement.
The web page https://SAM.gov identified 5 solicitations/pre-solicitations in response to the
search terms stated. The results reviewed did not identify any additional sources then the source
already identified in the CSRE.
The google search identified approximately 14,588,500 total hits in response to the listed search
terms. A majority of the hits provided lose or unrelated responses regarding experience with the
ALQ-172 system or production of ALQ-172 LRUs. Many of the search results returned also
pointed to existing contracts with L3Harris relating to efforts in support of development and/or
sustainment and repair of the ALQ-172 system and associated components. The results reviewed
did not identify any additional sources then the source already identified in the CSRE.
(3) Internet Dynamic Small Business Search (DSBS):
An Internet Dynamic Small Business Search (DSBS) was accomplished in order to meet the
FAR prerequisites regarding identification of qualified small businesses that could potentially
perform the work effort. [https://web.sba.gov/pro-net/search/dsp_dsbs.cfm] The DSBS database
search started out with the general key term "ALQ-172" followed by "ALQ-172 LRU-4", "Radar
Electronic Warfare Transmitter", "LRU-4 Countermeasures Transmitter", and "ALQ-172 LRU
Production". There were no filters applied to the NAICS code so that the maximum number of
hits would be identified.
A search using the web search tool DSBS was conducted in an effort to locate qualified small
business sources that may not have been revealed in the two other search methods (CSRE and
GSRE). Search outcomes yielded no additional potential sources of procurement.
(4) SS/RFI Responses:
CUI
CUI
SS/RFI SPRWA1-24-R-MARSLRU-4 was submitted to SAM.gov on 1 November 2023 and
closed on 16 November 2023. No Responses were received from potential sources.
The LRU-4 does not fit the definition of a commercial item as defined in FAR Part 2.101. This
item is defined as military unique and is not customarily used by the general public or by non-
Governmental entities. The Government requires parts that meet an exact form, fit, and function
as determined by the specific mission. There are no aircraft in the commercial market with the
same or similar components.
The market research concluded L3Harris Technologies is the only vendor capable of fulfilling
the Government’s requirement.

None.

CONTROLLED UNCLASSIFIED INFORMATION
Justification and Approval (J&A) for Other Than Full and Open Competition
I. Agency and Contracting Activity.
The Procurement Office responsible for the proposed contracting action is the Air Force Life Cycle Management Center,
Cryptologic and Cyber Systems Division (CCSD), (AFLCMC/HNCKJ).
II. Nature and/or description of the action being approved.
The Advanced Atmospheric Research Equipment (AARE) system performs a critical role in the national nuclear treaty
monitoring mission. The suite includes an airborne gas and particulate sampling subassembly. The particulate sampling
platform, or foil contains 13 filter paper cartridges that are automatically manipulated to place one filter in the aircraft
exterior air stream at a time. Established "jukebox" Wurlitzer-technology is used to lift and place each filter in the air stream
much like the old jukeboxes would select a specific record and place it on the turntable. The Filter Insertion System (FIS) was
redesigned approximately 10 years ago. The newer design maximizes the strength of the machined aluminum parts with
efficient weight reduction designs to keep the subassembly strong and as lightweight a possible. The alignment tool ensures
components are aligned and not obstructed during this process. Mis-alignment could result in mission failure and/or
damage to the aircraft. Very tight tolerances must be maintained with the Filter Insertion System (FIS) components to
provide form/fit and function in a very tight envelope on the airframe. This requirement, will be a new Firm Fixed Price
contract to procure Filter Insertion Systems in support of the Advanced Atmospheric Research Equipment (AARE) system
described in this section.
III. Description of supplies/services required to meet agency needs.
The United States Air Force has a requirement to manufacture the approved quantities of Filter Insertion System (FIS)
assemblies and Alignment tools and provide updated and complete drawings from red-line to production. Updated
drawings will enable any qualified vendor to produce these systems, thus ensuring the delivery of the Filter Insertion System
(FIS) assemblies to sustain mission readiness. However, vendor qualification is not limited to those that can simply produce
this equipment. Qualification includes extensive testing to ensure the equipment being installed on the airframe is suitable
for in-flight operation, meets airworthiness standards through testing, and passes ground and flight tests.

POP: 1 Sep 2025 - 31 Aug 2026

contracts (e.g. FA830715M0087, FA830719P0077, FA830720C0009) involving the FIS and FIS alignment tool. Additionally, a
notice of intent was posted on GPE, and no other vendors demonstrated that they had the capability to fulfill the

VIII. Any other facts supporting the use of Other Than Full and Open Competition.
The FIS assembly and FIS parts are critical components of the airborne platform. Sierra Peaks is the only company with the
program history, experience and capabilities that can provide the combined engineering and manufacturing services that
are required to meet the US Air Force's objectives for maintenance, support and sustainment of the WC-135 nuclear debris
collection system. Sierra Peaks is the current manufacturer of FIS components; these components are called out in the
Technical Orders, Technical Instructions and drawings identifying Sierra Peaks as the manufacturer of choice. The AARE
system has been base-lined and is under configuration control by the AARE Configuration Control Board (CCB). The base-
lined documentation calls out these specific items to be used on the AARE platform as referenced in Technical Instructions
1A-AARE-1 and 1A-AARE-4. Due to the complexity of the AARE suite and FIS subassembly, there are occasions when the
repair capability exceeds the expertise of our technicians creating the need for replenishment per this Purchase Request.
IX. List of any sources that expressed, in writing, an interest in the acquisition.
There were no sources that expressed, in writing, an interest in the acquisition.
X. A statement of the actions, if any, the agency may take to remove or overcome any barriers to competition before
any subsequent acquisitions for the supplies or services required.
The designer of the AARE was Sandia Labs in Albuquerque, NM. They contracted to Sierra Peak (formerly MSI) for much of
their fabrication of the FIS assembly due to their precision machining/ manufacturing expertise. The assembly must meet
Airworthiness certification and inspection requirements. There is no single document that comprehensively details each
component of the Filter Insertion System (FIS) or the core elements of the AARE system. The AARE system was certified as a
complete, integrated system rather than as individual components. Before flight testing, all relevant data is submitted for
review by the System Program Office (SPO), before it is ever installed for ground testing. If it passes, it then moves to flight
testing, then the system undergoes final evaluation. Upon this step, approval is granted for operational deployment of the
weapon system-AARE in this case. Any change to the configuration must go through approval at the SPO and Configuration
Control Board (CCB). Currently CCB guidance directs FIS purchases to MSI. Continuous research, testing and qualifications are
ongoing to identify machinists that can produce products the CCB would recommend. Following the previous contract's
completion, the Government was confident that it possessed all the necessary data. To date, no products have been
identified as suitable substitutes, because it was determined that the Government does not possess the data that is
necessary to recreate these items. The need for additional data was identified after contacting multiple contractors in an
effort to seek out new/additional suppliers. To address the Government's oversight, the contractual requirements have been
updated, to be clear and encompassing. Additionally, the Government has strengthened their engineering and
manufacturing expertise to prevent similar situations of data gaps in the future. After the Government acquires the revised/
updated drawings, all future acquisitions/solicitations will include a sufficient period for new vendors to go through the CCB
process in an effort to increase the vendor pool for these parts.

DEPARTMENT OF THE NAVY
NAVAL SEA SYSTEMS COMMAND
1333 ISAAC HULL AVENUE, S.E.,
WASHINGTON NAVY YARD, DC 20376-2020
IN REPLY REFER TO
CJ&A Number: 22,057
Code: 02244

CLASS JUSTIFICATION AND APPROVAL
FOR USE OF OTHER THAN FULL AND OPEN COMPETITION
JUSTIFICATION
1. Contracting Activity
The Naval Sea Systems Command, Shipbuilding Contracts Division (SEA
022).
2. Description of the Action Being Approved
Award of a class of contractual actions on a sole source basis to
Huntington Ingalls Incorporated, acting through its Ingalls
Shipbuilding division (“Ingalls”), 1000 Access Road, Pascagoula, MS
39567 for LHA(R) Class post-delivery planning yard support.
Authority to act under this class justification expires on 31
December 2030.
3. Description of Supplies/Services
The proposed contract actions will provide post-delivery planning,
engineering, production, management, material procurement and
support for planned and unplanned industrial availabilities and
emergent work; as well as, the execution of the Industrial Post
Delivery Availability (IPDA) and Post-Delivery Availability (PDA).
Industrial availabilities include, but are not limited to, IPDA,
PDA, Fitting-Out Availability (FOA), Post Shakedown Availability
(PSA, Continuous Maintenance Availabilities (CMAV), Restricted
Availabilities (RAVs), Dry- docking Availabilities, and Technical
Availabilities which may be required from the time of ship delivery
through the Ship Construction (Navy) (SCN) Obligation Work Limiting
Date (OWLD).
The anticipated period of performance (PoP) for these efforts will
be from CY2025 through CY2030. The anticipated contract will
consist of a base period and, if all options are exercised, work
will continue through 2030.
The total estimated dollar value for this procurement is as
illustrated below. This requirement will be funded with SCN and
Post Delivery (PD)-SCN appropriations.

CJ&A Number: 22,057
the ship has not yet sailed away. There is another availability,
called a PDA, which must be accomplished for crew training,
familiarization and certifications. Emergent work is often found
during this period, necessitating industrial efforts to occur.
These efforts must be done by the construction yard as the ship
has not yet sailed away.
Any unplanned availability during the post-delivery period for the
ships must also be scheduled and accomplished within a relatively
short time frame as to not delay the deployment of the ships.
Given the limited interval of the ship's post-delivery period,
Ingalls is uniquely qualified to competently perform the planning
and accomplish any emergent industrial availability for LHA(R)
Class due to their knowledge of the detail design and the
construction methodology. Additionally, Ingalls has experience
with and access to resources that are necessary to quickly respond
to the emergent requirements.
Ingalls was awarded a sole source contract for the Detail Design
and Construction of LHA 8 in June 2017 and for LHA 9 in October
2022. In constructing LHA 8, Ingalls has acquired a level of
knowledge of the ship that cannot be duplicated. Ingalls possesses
all of the construction drawings and design specifications for the
Hull, Mechanical and Electrical and Combat Systems.
Ingalls also has pre-existing contractual relationships with
equipment vendors that will enable them to provide reach-back, as
required. Therefore, Ingalls is uniquely qualified to perform the
role as Post-Delivery Planning Yard.
In addition, PEO Ships Memorandum for the Record, Ser SHIPS/142 of
22 Sep 15, assigns the LHA(R) construction yard as the planning
yard through the ship’s OWLD.
6. Description of Efforts Made to Solicit Offers from as Many
Offerors as Practicable
The proposed efforts addressed by this Class Justification and
Approval (CJ&A) were synopsized on the sam.gov website on 23
January 2025. No responses have been received to date and none are
anticipated. No market research was conducted for this effort
because it is not practicable, for the reasons discussed in
paragraph 5 above, for any company other than Ingalls to perform
the contemplated efforts. A waiver of the sources sought notice
requirement at DFARS PGI 206.302-1 was approved via NAVSEA Letter
Ser 0224/012 dated 25 March 2025.
7. Determination of Fair and Reasonable Costs
The Contracting Officer has determined the anticipated cost to the
Government of the supplies/services covered by this J&A will be
fair and reasonable. The Contracting Officer will use cost and
pricing analysis to determine that the final cost and price is
3
CJ&A Number: 22,057
fair and reasonable. The Contractor will submit cost and pricing
data in accordance with FAR 15.403-4. Information from technical
analysts, the Supervisor of Shipbuilding, Gulf Coast and DCAA rate
analysts may also be utilized to analyze, evaluate and assist in
negotiations based upon detailed cost and pricing data which will
be certified by the Contractor at the conclusion of negotiations.
8. Actions to Remove Barriers to Competition
For the reasons set forth in paragraph 5, the Naval Sea Systems
Command, Shipbuilding Contracts Division (SEA 022) has no plans at

4. Statutory Authority Permitting Other Than Full and Open Competition.
10 U.S.C. 3204(a)(1), Only One Responsible Source and No Other Supplies or Services Will
Satisfy Agency Requirements.
5. Rationale Justifying Use of Cited Statutory Authority.
The procurement of these hardware components is deemed available only from the original OEM,
Elliott Manufacturing through their distributor, Kampi Component Company (KCC). Elliott
Manufacturing is the OEM for all of the components listed in Table 1. Elliott Manufacturing owns
and utilizes proprietary information and technical data to manufacture the required hardware which
has been shock and vibration qualified. Elliott Manufacturing was selected as the OEM for the FDB
during the shipbuilding phase of the LHD-1 Class of vessel. The Government does not have
sufficient data rights to allow for competition of these items. Additionally, Elliott Manufacturing
owns all propriety drawings to manufacture all of the material listed and the Government has no
access to these drawings and manufacturing information.
The Government has no ability to redesign these FDB’s for the LHD-1 Class. It would require years
of engineering analysis and design to find adequate replacements for the current units. These costs
are difficult to quantify but estimated as extremely cost prohibitive. It would require excessive work
during Chief of Naval Operations (CNO) availability to remove the existing units, perform large
hull cuts and interference removals, and install new FDB’s. Additionally, significant upfront costs
exist to reengineer the LHD1 Class FDB. The material and tooling that will be potentially procured
under this IDIQ are required to serve as 2SCOG stock rotating spares, as well as unique components
in support of FDB proactive maintenance strategy. Lacking the prerequisite technical data described
above, another company with interest in developing equivalent spare parts kits and rotor
procurement would be required to reverse engineer the LHD-1 Class FDB’s. Having a competitive
2
J&A No. 0232-24-265-00
award for the development of a new FDB, integration into the fleet and potentially supplying the
above parts would take an estimated 156 months at a projected cost of $216,125,000. The time line
and costs for this project are so high as this would amount to a full redesign of the combustion air
system of the LHD-1 Class Main Propulsion plant. This would require updates and changes to the
ducting, steam piping, blower foundations, support equipment, ILS information, and various other
adjacent systems. It would require large scale hull cuts to remove the existing units and replace with
the new units. All of this upfront and complex engineering work leads to the long lead time and the
very expensive costs to perform these changes.

Based on the above, only the Steam Propulsion Plant Elliott Model 44BH-2 FDB rotors from the
original equipment manufacturer, Elliott Manufacturing through their distributor, Kampi
Component Company (KCC) will meet the Navy’s stringent requirements.
6. Description of Efforts Made to Solicit Offers from as Many Offerors as Practicable.
In accordance with DFARS PGI 206.302-1, a Request for Information (RFI) was posted to
SAM.gov on 21 August 2024, and closed on 23 September 2024. Additionally, a synopsis was
posted 04 September 2024 with a closing date of 19 September 2024. No responses were received
to either notice (other than from Elliott Manufacturing) as of the closing date of the notices, or the
drafting of this J&A.
7. Determination of Fair and Reasonable Cost.
The Contracting Officer has determined that the anticipated cost to the Government for the supplies
covered by the J&A will be fair and reasonable. The Contractor will submit a formal price proposal
with sufficient information to support the accuracy and reliability of the estimate. Experienced
Technical Analysts and Contract Specialists with the aid of necessary field pricing support will
review the Contractor’s proposal. The Contracting Officer will use cost and pricing analysis as the
basis for negotiating a fair and reasonable price.
8. Actions to Remove Barriers to Future Competition.
For the reasons set forth in paragraph 5, the Government has no plans at this time to compete future
contracts for the items covered by this document. If another potential source emerges, the
Government will assess whether competition for future requirements is feasible. The Procuring

J&A No. 0232-24-265-00
Contracting Officer (PCO) will review the circumstances surrounding the need to obtain the
required supplies without providing full and open competition annually.

CUI
JUSTIFICATION FOR OTHER THAN
FULL AND OPEN COMPETITION
I. Agency and Contracting Activity.
This Justification and Approval is to request authority for Other Than Full and Open
Competition to support requirements generated for the Air Force Sustainment Center (AFSC),
638 Supply Chain Management Group (SCMG), 408 Supply Chain Management Squadron
(SCMS) / GULB. The contracting activity for this requirement is Defense Logistics Agency
(DLA) Aviation, Warner Robins, DLA/AWB. The purchase request number supporting this
contracting action is FD2060-25-00066 and FD20602500123.
II. Nature and/or description of the action being approved.
Due to the circumstances described herein, the activity requests authority to procure the
production of the Electrical Limiter (5895-01-497-2529), Frequency Converter (5895-01-498-
1190) and Power Supply (6130-01-551-5132) using Other Than Full and Open Competition as
prescribed by FAR 6.302-1, “Only One Responsible Source and No Other Supplies or Services
Will Satisfy Agency Requirements.” This action will result in a follow-on Firm Fixed Price
(FFP) IDC Requirements type contract The period of performance to include all deliveries is
.
anticipated to be FY25 - FY29.
This sole source requirement will be procured from the following company:
Raytheon Company
6380 Hollister Avenue
Goleta, CA 93117
CAGE: 06129
Large Business
III. Description of supplies/services required to meet agency needs.
The purpose of this effort is to procure spares of the B-52H AN/ALQ-172 Electronic
Countermeasures (ECM) Line Replaceable Unit (LRU)-8 Phased Array Antenna Electrical
Limiter and Frequency Converter and LRU-7 Countermeasures Converter Power Supply. The
Electrical Limiter NSN is 5895-01-497-2529, the Frequency Converter NSN is 5895-01-498-
1190 and the Power Supply NSN is 6130-01-551-5132.
Delivery requirements are 133 Electrical Limiters, 69 Frequency Converters and 40 Power
Supplies. The Ordering Period 1 urgent quantities are 13 Frequency Converters and 25 Electrical
Limiters. Early delivery is acceptable.
This effort will be Firm Fixed Price. The total estimated value for this procurement is
The estimated value for the Urgent Ordering Period 1 is . Unit
prices were estimated using SPM and these assets will be procured with CSAG dollars.
CUI

CUI
components of the ALQ-172(V)2 ECM System for the B-52 Aircraft.
The LRU-7 contains the electronic groups required to provide the high band Phased Array
Antenna System (PAAS) control processing and interface functions. The countermeasures
converter contains Amplitude Direction Finding (ADF), polarization encoding, beam steering
and polarization control, quadrant switch assembly control, and digital interface circuits. In
addition, the countermeasures converter contains a regulating EMI/EMP protected power
supply which converts aircraft ac power into DC voltages for use by both LRU-8 and LRU-9.
The LRU-8 Phased Array Antenna is a key component of the ALQ-172(V)2 ECM System.
The LRU-8 provides the high band PAAS with electronically steerable antenna beam in the
azimuth plane and a fixed antenna beam in the elevation plane. The LRU-8 antenna consists of
16 circuit cards, a polarimeter, receive circulator assemblies, a dual circulator driver, electrical
limiter, frequency converter, power supply, and IF phase shifter. Due to increased failure rates,
beyond economical repair (BER) rates, and increasing age of the items specific to this market
research report, procurement of these items is required to support the needs of the fleet.
This effort is posed to procure the LRU-7 power supply, LRU-8 electrical limiters and down
converters in order to continue repair and sustainment of the LRU-7 and LRU-8, critical
components of the ALQ-172 ECM System working in tandem with the other LRUs in the ALQ-
172 ECM Suite to provide effective electronic warfare capabilities for the B-52 fleet.
There are multiple AMC/AMSC codes for this contract, they are as follows:
(cid:120) 3/R The “3” indicates Acquisition directly from the actual manufacturer, whether or not
the prime contractor is the actual manufacturer. The “R” indicates that the Government
does not have adequate data, lacks rights to data, or both, and the part needs to be
purchased from the Original Equipment Manufacturer. (NSN 5895-01-498-1190EW)
(cid:120) 3/P The “3” indicates Acquisition directly from the actual manufacturer, whether or not
the prime contractor is the actual manufacturer. The “P” indicates that the rights to use
the data needed to purchase this part from additional source(s) are not owned by the
Government and cannot be purchased, developed, or otherwise obtained. It is
uneconomical to reverse engineer this part. This code is used in situations where the
Government has the data but does not own the rights to the data. (NSN 5895-01-497-
2529EW)
(cid:120) 3/R The “3” indicates Acquisition directly from the actual manufacturer, whether or not
the prime contractor is the actual manufacturer. The “B” indicates that this part must be
acquired from a manufacturing source(s) specified on a source control or selected item
drawing as defined by the current version of DoD-STD-100. Suitable technical data,
Government data rights, or manufacturing knowledge are not available to permit
acquisition from other sources, nor qualification testing of another part, nor use of a
second source part in the intended application. Although, by DoD-STD-100 definition,
altered and selected items shall have an adequate technical data package, data review
discloses that required data or data rights are not in Government possession and cannot
be economically obtained. (NSN 6130-01-551-5132EW)
CUI
CUI
IV. Demonstration that the contractor's unique qualifications or the nature of the
acquisition requires use of the authority cited above.
This agency's minimum needs can only be satisfied by the unique supplies available from
Raytheon as identified on the design requirements and Source Control Drawings (SCD).
Raytheon possesses unique capabilities demonstrated as follows:
Raytheon, CAGE 24587 is the original designer and developer of the Phased Array Antenna
Subsystem (PAAS) that includes the AN/ALQ-172(V2) LRU 7, 8, and 9. The Government did
not purchase a full data package for the LRU-7 or its SRUs. Raytheon was asked through email
by the Government in February 2024 if they would sell the data for these SRUs and the request
was denied due to them wanting to repair these assets for the life of the LRU. The Government’s
data is limited to a Source Control Document (SCD) that lists Raytheon as the only approved
source of supply. Raytheon, having developed the PAAS, is the only known source with the data,
skills, and experience to provide the required support. Qualifying a new source would include
new supplier startup, performing qualification, first article testing, acceptance testing and flight
test. Since production drawings cannot be furnished, the new supplier would have to reverse
engineer the existing ALQ-172 LRU-7 and develop procedures and equipment to test a new
ALQ-172 LRU-7. The research provided no additional sources. Market Research has identified
Raytheon as the only source with the required capabilities and knowledge to meet the
Government’s requirements and delivery schedule. Marker Research also indicates that the
current manufacturer within Raytheon is CAGE 06129.
Raytheon’s original part number SCD referenced Cage Code 24587 which was originally Sedco
Systems, Inc. but was purchased by Raytheon. The suitable sub part number which is what we
are buying has a SCD for the suitable sub part for both the BIT Limiter and Power Supply but
not the Down Converter. These suitable sub part SCDs show a Raytheon Cage Code of 49956
which is another Raytheon Cage when the drawing was originally drafted. These drawings were
created in the late 90s and early 00s and Raytheon has chosen to propose their production
location for these parts under cage 06129.
The LRUs within the ALQ-172 are extremely specific and complex in their design and
integration requirements. One major requirement of being successful in the production of the
LRU-8 SRUs specific to this market research is having the equipment and expertise to
accomplish the build of these assets. The time involved in having another source acquire the
equipment, required technical data, and develop the expertise would not be cost effective or
feasible to meet the current mission need. The Government does not possess the data, facilities,
or equipment to furnish a new source in order to accomplish this requirement.
Accordingly, Raytheon is the only vendor capable of providing the requirements described in
Section III above without the United States Air Force (USAF) experiencing substantial delays
and work stoppages that will cause these assets to MICAP.

The overall cost of this acquisition will be fair and reasonable to the Government. In accordance

Interested parties should clearly address the challenge of integrating with existing Bio-Rad electrophoresis workflows and Bio-Rad Stain-Free workflows. A determination not to compete this requirement, based upon responses to this notice, is solely within the discretion of the Government. matters.title: Pre-solicitation Notice of Intent to Sole Source Avidity Science BFS-675 Bottle Filling Station
matters.text:
Federal notice (Special Notice), VETERANS AFFAIRS, DEPARTMENT OF.VETERANS AFFAIRS, DEPARTMENT OF.RPO EAST (36C24E)
Title: Pre-solicitation Notice of Intent to Sole Source Avidity Science BFS-675 Bottle Filling Station
Solicitation number: 36C24E26Q0103
PSC: 6640; NAICS: 334516
Description: Pre-Solicitation Notice for the notice of intent to award a sole source contract.
 This is not a solicitation. The Veterans Health Administration (VHA), Office of Research and Development (R&D), Regional Procurement Office (RPO) – East in Pittsburgh, PA intends to negotiate on a sole source basis for Avidity Science Bottle Filling Station to replace the current Avidity Edstrom Model BFS-675 Bottle Filling Station for Research Services at the Michael E. DeBakey VA Medical Center that is twenty years old and reached the end of its life expectancy. The facility requires the replacement to be the same size and same make/model to utilize the existing space, power hookups, drain, and water inlet valve without new construction or abatement.
 The Avidity Science Bottle Filling Station consists of:
 Edstrom Model BFS-675 Bottle Filling Station
 Made in the USA
 Frame and cabinet components constructed of 316 stainless steel
 Corrosion resistant wetted parts compatible with untreated, purified, acidified & chlorinated water
 Able to chlorinate, acidify or medicate bottled water for animals
 Adjustable, no drip fill nozzles to ensure uniform filling
 Interchangeable custom designed fill manifold for multiple size bottles
 Two user programmable fill times for two different bottle sizes
 Removable sidewall allows loading cases from conveyor feed systems
 Solution and injection tank located on sides for easy access
 Solution tank has screw-on lid to prevent spills
 Mixing chamber assures complete dispersal of chemical additives
 Optional pH monitor available for acidification application
 Separate stainless-steel platform for reservoir tank mounts on either side
 Discharge capacity: 1000 to1200 ML/min per dispensing nozzle
 Removal of old unit
 Installation of the same model
 This notice of intent is not a request for competitive quotes. However, any responsible source who can provide an equivalent service with the features described above, and who is the Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM), authorized dealer, authorized distributor, or authorized reseller of all the items listed above, may submit a capability statement to the contracting office no later than September 14, 2026, 2:00 PM, MT. Interest/capability statements which specifically detail how your equipment meets the requirement may be sent to Robert.Dobson1@va.gov. No telephone responses will be accepted. A determination not to compete the proposed requirement based upon the responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government

Part 1 -INTRODUCTION
F-101 General.
(a) This appendix contains procedures and instructions for the use, preparation, and distribution of
the Wide Area Work Flow (WAWF) Receiving Report (RR), WAWF Reparable Receiving Report
(WAWF RRR), the WAWF Energy RR, and commercial shipping/packing lists used to document
Government contract quality assurance. The WAWF RR is the electronic equivalent of the DD Form
250, Material Inspection and Receiving Report (MIRR). The WAWF Energy RR is the electronic
equivalent of the DD Form 250 for overland shipments and DD Form 250-1, Tanker/Barge Material
Inspection and Receiving Report, for waterborne shipments. The WAWF RRR is the electronic
equivalent of the DD Form 250 for repair, maintenance, or overhaul of Government-furnished
property.
(b) The use of the DD Form 250 series documents is on an exception basis (see DFARS (a)) because
use of the WAWF RR is now required by most DoD contracts. WAWF provides for electronic
preparation and documentation of acceptance of supplies and services, and electronic invoicing. In
addition WAWF allows the printing of a RR that can be used as a packing list or when a signed copy
is required.
F-102 Applicability.
(a) DFARS 252.232-7003, Electronic Submission of Payment Requests and Receiving Reports,
requires payment requests and receiving reports using WAWF in nearly all cases.
(b) When DoD provides quality assurance or acceptance services for non-DoD activities, prepare a
MIRR using the instructions in this appendix, unless otherwise specified in the contract.
F-103 Use.
(a) The WAWF RR, WAWF RRR, and the DD Form 250 are multipurpose reports used—
(1) To provide evidence of Government contract quality assurance at origin or destination;
(2) To provide evidence of acceptance at origin, destination, or other;
(3) For packing lists;
(4) For receiving;
(5) For shipping;
(6) As a contractor invoice (the WAWF RR, WAWF RRR, or DD Form 250 alone cannot be used as an
invoice, however the option exists to create an invoice from the Receiving Report or a Combo
(Invoice and Receiving Report) both of which minimize data entry); and
(7) As commercial invoice support.
(b) Do not use the WAWF RR, WAWF RRR, or the DD Form 250 for shipments—
(1) By subcontractors, unless the subcontractor is shipping directly to the Government; or
(2) Of contract inventory. The WAWF Property Transfer document should be used for this type of
shipment. Training for the preparation of this document type is available at
https://wawftraining.eb.mil, under the Property Transfer and Receipt section.
(c) The contractor prepares the WAWF RR, WAWF RRR, or the DD Form 250, except for entries that
an authorized Government representative is required to complete. When using a paper DD Form
250, the contractor shall furnish sufficient copies of the completed form, as directed by the
Government representative.
(d) Use the WAWF Energy RR or the DD Form 250-1:
(1) For bulk movements of petroleum products by tanker or barge to cover—
(i) Origin or destination acceptance of cargo; or
(ii) Shipment or receipt of Government owned products.
(2) To send quality data to the point of acceptance in the case of origin inspection on FOB
destination deliveries or preinspection at product source. Annotate the forms with the words
“INSPECTED FOR QUALITY ONLY.”
(e) In addition to the above uses, the WAWF RR and WAWF RRR provide additional functionality, not
provided by the paper DD Form 250 that complies with the following requirements:
(1) Item Unique Identification (IUID), when the clause at DFARS , Item Unique Identification and
Valuation is used in the contract, reporting of IUID data is required. WAWF captures the IUID data
and forwards the data to the IUID registry after acceptance. WAWF shall be used to report Unique
Item Identifiers (UIIs) at the line item level, unless an exception to WAWF applies, and can also be
used to report UIIs embedded at the line item level.
(2) Radio Frequency Identification (RFID), when the clause at DFARS , Radio Frequency
Identification, is used in the contract, WAWF will capture the RFID information and forward the data
to the receiving location. Using WAWF is the only way a contractor can comply with the clause to
furnish RFID data via an Advance Shipping Notice (ASN). The RFID information may be added at
time of submission, or via the WAWF Pack Later functionality after acceptance.
(3) Reporting of Government-furnished property, when the clause at DFARS , Reporting of
Government-Furnished Property, is used in the contract, use of the WAWF RRR will capture the
shipment of Government-furnished property items after acceptance of repair services and forward
the data to the IUID registry. WAWF is the only way a contractor can report the transfer of
Government-furnished property items in the IUID registry.
F-104 Application.
(a) WAWF RR and DD Form 250.
(1) Use the WAWF RR or DD Form 250 for delivery of contract line, subline, exhibit line, or exhibit
subline items. Do not use the WAWF RR or DD Form 250 for those exhibit line or exhibit subline
items on a DD Form 1423, Contract Data Requirements List, that indicate no DD Form 250 is
required.
(2) If the shipped to, marked for, shipped from, mode of shipment, contract quality assurance and
acceptance data are the same for more than one shipment made on the same day under the same
contract, contractors may prepare one WAWF RR or DD Form 250 to cover all such shipments.
(3) If the volume of the shipment precludes the use of a single car, truck, or other vehicle, prepare a
separate WAWF RR or DD Form 250 for the contents of each vehicle.
(4) When a shipment is consigned to an Air Force activity and the shipment includes items of more
than one Federal supply class (FSC) or material management code (MMC), prepare a separate
WAWF RR or DD Form 250 for items of each of the FSCs or MMCs in the shipment. However, the
cognizant Government representative may authorize a single WAWF RR or DD Form 250, listing
each of the FSCs or MMCs included in the shipment on a separate continuation sheet. The MMC
appears as a suffix to the national stock number applicable to the item.
(5) Consolidation of Petroleum Shipments on a Single WAWF RR or DD Form 250.
(i) Contiguous United States. Contractors may consolidate multiple car or truck load shipments of
petroleum made on the same day, to the same destination, against the same contract line item, on
one WAWF RR or DD Form 250. To permit verification of motor deliveries, assign each load a load
number which can be identified to the shipment number in Block 2 of the DD Form 250. Include a
shipping document (commercial or Government) with each individual load showing as a minimum—
(A) The shipper;
(B) Shipping point;
(C) Consignee;
(D) Contract and line item number;
(E) Product identification;
(F) Gross gallons (bulk only);
(G) Loading temperature (bulk only);
(H) American Petroleum Institute gravity (bulk only);
(I) Identification of carrier's equipment;
(J) Serial number of all seals applied; and
(K) Signature of supplier's representative.
When acceptance is at destination, the receiving activity retains the shipping document(s) to verify
the entries on the consignee copy of the DD Form 250 forwarded by the contractor (reference F-401,
Table 1) before signing Block 21b.
(ii) Overseas. The same criteria as for contiguous United States applies, except the consolidation
period may be extended, if acceptable to the receiving activity, shipping activity, Government
finance office, and the authorized Government representative having cognizance at the contractor's
facility. In addition, the contractor may include more than one contract line item in each WAWF RR
or DD Form 250 if the shipped to, marked for, shipped from, mode of shipment, contract quality
assurance, and acceptance data are the same for all line items.
(6) Consolidation of Coal Shipments on a Single WAWF RR or DD 250. Contractors may consolidate
multiple railcar or truck shipments of coal made on the same day, to the same destination, against
the same contract line items, on one WAWF RR or DD 250. To permit verification of truck deliveries,
assign each load a load number which can be identified to the shipment number in Block 2 of the DD
Form 250 and the analytical test report. Include a commercial shipping document with each
individual truck load showing as a minimum—
(i) The shipper;
(ii) The name or names;
(iii) Location and shipping point of the mine or mines from which the coal originates;
(iv) The contract number;
(v) The exact size of the coal shipped; and
(vi) A certified weighmaster's certification of weight for the truckload.
Include a waybill with each rail shipment showing the identical information. To permit verification of
rail deliveries, identify each railcar number comprising the shipment to the shipment number in
Block 2 of the DD Form 250 and the analytical test report. When acceptance is at destination, the
receiving activity must retain the shipping document(s) to verify the entries on the consignee copy of
the DD Form 250.
(b) WAWF RRR or DD Form 250. Use as in paragraph (a) of this section for delivery of services for
repair, overhaul, or maintenance.
(c) WAWF Energy RR or the DD Form 250-1.
(1) Use a separate form for each tanker or barge cargo loaded.
(2) The contractor may report more than one barge in the same tow on a single form if on the same
contract and consigned to the same destination.
(3) When liftings involve more than one contract, prepare separate forms to cover the portion of
cargo loaded on each contract.
(4) Prepare a separate form for each product or grade of product loaded.
(5) Use a separate document for each tanker or barge cargo and each grade of product discharged.
(6) For discharge, the contractor may report more than one barge in the same tow on a single form if
from the same loading source.
Part 2 -CONTRACT QUALITY ASSURANCE ON SHIPMENTS
BETWEEN CONTRACTORS
F-201 Procedures.
Follow the procedures at PGI F-201 for evidence of required Government contract quality assurance
at a subcontractor’s facility.

attachments.text:
PCA-NHGRI-10510 Meridian BreathID replacement

Statement of Need: A replacement Breath ID instrument is required to replace the existing unit, which is no longer operational. The replacement must be the same model as the current instrument to ensure consistency and continuity in the ongoing patient history studies and for an upcoming clinical trial this fall. Using the same model is necessary to maintain consistency in sample analysis, instrument performance, data collection, and study procedures. Introducing a different model could create variability in measurements or require changes to established study methods, potentially affecting comparability of data collected before and after replacement. The replacement is also critical to the continuation of important ongoing patient-history studies that rely on this instrument for data collection and analysis. Without a functioning Breath ID instrument, we will be unable to continue these studies as planned, which could result in interruptions to data collection and delays in research activities.

Purpose and Need

This machine is used on patients with rare disorders enrolled in our natural history and gene therapy protocols for a breath test (propionate oxidation breath test) that measures whole body enzyme activity of their respective disease gene. 

Support of NIH/HHS Mission
This replacement directly supports NHGRI’s mission to advance genomic research and the development of innovative genomic therapeutics. The government requires a replacement BreathID machine to enable measurement of propionate metabolism in patients with genetically inherited disorders of that mitochondrial pathway both to track health in the patient population over time and to determine the effectiveness of future clinal trial therapies.


Limitations of Current In-House Capabilities
Our current equipment is no longer operational or reliable and there is no other effective in-house method to replace this system.

United States Department of Agriculture
Item Peculiar to One Manufacturer
Under the Simplified Acquisition Threshold
Identification Number: 12444026Q0220
In accordance with the Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Federal Acquisition
Regulation (FAR) 16.507-6 (d)(1), the following documents exception to fair opportunity.
(1) Mission Area and Contracting Activity.
Requisition Number: 1174489
Requesting Activity Agency: USDA, Agricultural Research Service (ARS)
Contracting Activity:
(2) Brief Description of Supplies or Services
The USDA Agricultural Research Service requires acquisition of a high-volume, high-accuracy,
image-based seed counter capable of processing large batches of corn seed (up to 1500 g) at speeds of
approximately 75 seeds per second, while capturing individual seed image metrics (area, length, width)
and exporting data in .csv or Excel formats.
The equipment will be used for large-scale grain sample processing, seed inventory management, and
high-resolution phenotyping necessary for ARS research programs. It must seamlessly integrate with
barcode scanners and laboratory balances to collect mass and identification data concurrently.
This acquisition enhances operational efficiency, ensures highly accurate data capture (≥99.9%
accuracy), and provides capabilities not currently available in the laboratory.
(3) Suggested Source
(4) Identify the exception to fair opportunity.
The statutory authority supporting the placement of an order or establishment of a Blanket Purchase
Agreement (BPA) that exceeds the micro-purchase threshold on a sole source basis is: FAR 16.507-7 -
Items Peculiar to One Manufacturer
(5) Demonstrate that the proposed contractor's unique qualifications or the nature of the
acquisition requires using the authority cited.
Page 1 of 3
Rev. 3/10/26
United States Department of Agriculture
Item Peculiar to One Manufacturer
Under the Simplified Acquisition Threshold
Identification Number: 12444026Q0220
Only the Ball-Coleman Seed Counter meets the ARS technical requirements. Market research showed
that alternative seed counters either:
• do not support large batch sizes (~1500 g),
• cannot achieve required speeds (75 seeds/sec for corn),
• lack high-resolution image-based per-seed measurement capability, or
• cannot export full-sample measurement datasets.
Ball-Coleman is uniquely capable of providing the full required feature set. The Ball-Coleman counter
delivers image-based detection, 99.9% accuracy, simultaneous mass-capture, barcode integration, and
large-batch hopper capacity—all explicitly required and not matched by any discovered competitor.
Only one comparable machine exists (Data Technologies S-25), but it is foreign-manufactured and not
acceptable. ARS excluded this device because detailed specifications were limited, it did not meet
batch-size requirements and was manufactured in Israel—making it non-compliant with domestic
sourcing objectives.
The Ball-Coleman system is sold primarily by the manufacturer and only one verified U.S. reseller.
No other U.S. distributors were found during extensive market research. The system must be
compatible with ARS workflows and existing research pipelines. Its export formats, data structures,
imaging specifications, and barcode integration are already aligned with ARS templates and
downstream data software, reducing operational burden and ensuring accuracy.
Given these constraints, restricting competition is necessary to meet ARS’ minimum technical
requirements and ensure compatibility with existing lab processes.
(6) Describe market research conducted and the results or the reason why no market research
was conducted.
ARS conducted extensive market research including:
• Hands-on evaluation of a Ball-Coleman counter at the Iowa State University Seed Science Center.
The device demonstrated required performance and data capabilities.
• Internet searches, product literature review, and use of AI-assisted tools to identify comparable
machines. No other U.S.-made machines matched the required specifications.
• Review of GSA Advantage, AbilityOne, USDA-wide contracts, Federal Prison Industries, SEWP,
NITAAC, STARS, VETS, Alliant, and SBA Dynamic Small Business Search—none listed any
comparable seed counting technology.
• Evaluation of Data Technologies S-25 (Israel). It was excluded due to foreign manufacture, limited
specification transparency, and insufficient performance capabilities.
• Outreach to knowledgeable individuals in the seed-technology field who confirmed Ball-Coleman as
the only known solution with required capabilities.
Market research conclusively supports restricting competition to Ball Technologies and Sciotex as the
only viable domestic sources.

attachments.name: B.1.4 NOI PCA-NHGRI-10510 Statement of Need .docx
attachments.text:
PCA-NHGRI-10510 Meridian BreathID replacement

Statement of Need: A replacement Breath ID instrument is required to replace the existing unit, which is no longer operational. The replacement must be the same model as the current instrument to ensure consistency and continuity in the ongoing patient history studies and for an upcoming clinical trial this fall. Using the same model is necessary to maintain consistency in sample analysis, instrument performance, data collection, and study procedures. Introducing a different model could create variability in measurements or require changes to established study methods, potentially affecting comparability of data collected before and after replacement. The replacement is also critical to the continuation of important ongoing patient-history studies that rely on this instrument for data collection and analysis. Without a functioning Breath ID instrument, we will be unable to continue these studies as planned, which could result in interruptions to data collection and delays in research activities.

Purpose and Need

This machine is used on patients with rare disorders enrolled in our natural history and gene therapy protocols for a breath test (propionate oxidation breath test) that measures whole body enzyme activity of their respective disease gene. 

Support of NIH/HHS Mission
This replacement directly supports NHGRI’s mission to advance genomic research and the development of innovative genomic therapeutics. The government requires a replacement BreathID machine to enable measurement of propionate metabolism in patients with genetically inherited disorders of that mitochondrial pathway both to track health in the patient population over time and to determine the effectiveness of future clinal trial therapies.


Limitations of Current In-House Capabilities
Our current equipment is no longer operational or reliable and there is no other effective in-house method to replace this system.

Statement of Work (SOW)
Combination 360 Seam Gauge System
1. Background
The FDA utilizes a SEAMSCAN XTS-111 system for inspection of metal can double seams.
Additional measurement capability is required to obtain seam thickness and countersink
depth parameters necessary for Low-Acid Canned Food (LACF) inspections and laboratory
analysis.
Current commercially available solutions for this capability are provided as standalone
systems that support data analysis within existing laboratory workflows. The required
system must be compatible with existing analysis processes used in conjunction with
SEAMSCAN XTS-111 data.
2. Scope
The Government requires the acquisition of a combination 360 seam gauge system
capable of measuring seam characteristics of food containers. The system will be used to
support inspection, compliance, and laboratory analysis activities, including LACF
inspections.
3. Requirements
The system shall:
• Provide automated seam thickness and countersink depth measurements
• Be capable of nondestructive measurement of seam characteristics
• Perform 360-degree or multi-point seam measurements around the full
circumference of the container (minimum of 50 data points or continuous
profile measurements)
• Provide accurate and repeatable measurements suitable for laboratory and
inspection use (Thickness accuracy must be within ±0.01 mm; countersink
accuracy must be within ±0.02 mm).
• Be capable of scanning multiple measurement points around the container to
support full seam analysis
• Provide seam thickness and countersink depth measurements required for FDA
LACF can inspections
• Be compatible with existing laboratory workflows and capable of supporting data
integration with existing analysis systems used in conjunction with the SEAMSCAN
XTS-11I
• Provide output formats suitable for statistical analysis and reporting
• The Government will consider equipment that meets these requirements and
provides comparable functionality
• Must provide digital data export capability (USB/RS232) to interface with quality
assurance data collection networks
4. Deliverables
The Contractor shall provide:
• One (1) combination 360 seam gauge system
• All components necessary for full system operation
• Required hardware, accessories, and documentation
Table 1. Deliverables / Schedule
Deliverable Quantity Delivery Date
360 Deg Combination seam gauge system 1 September 16
5. Installation and Training
The Contractor shall:
• Deliver and install the system at the designated FDA laboratory
• Perform system setup and operational verification
• Provide on-site training for Government personnel on system operation,
maintenance, and basic troubleshooting
• Contractor personnel shall be escorted at all times while on-site and will not require
access to FDA information systems
6. Warranty
The Contractor shall provide:
• A minimum one (1) year manufacturer warranty covering parts, labor, and travel
• Technical support during standard business hours
7. Delivery Location
FDA Laboratory
6502 S. Archer Road
Bedford Park, IL 60501
8. Period of Performance
The Contractor shall deliver, install, and complete training within the timeframe specified in
the contract.

potential conflicts with existing construction responsibilities, delay project execution, and
increase the risk of improper utility connections or inadequate site preparation. Because the
consultation directly informs the installation requirements, the same contractor must perform

ensures that installation work is completed by the contractor authorized and qualified to support

Project
Cobalt-60 Reload of Foss Therapy Model 484F-C Cobalt-60 Irradiator.
General Information
1.0 Scope of Work
Reload irradiator between November 2026 and February 2027.
Include travel, transportation, handling, and disposal of depleted sources in accordance with regulatory requirements.
Provide documentation of reload and certification of continued operational safety.

2.0 Background
The Phoenix Rearing Facility (PRF) is part of a federally appropriated program that aligns with the Congressional Findings in Specialty Crops Competitiveness Act (7 U.S.C. 1621 et seg.) The (PRF) is testing the Sterile Insect Technique (SIT) to determine how it can be used as a tool in an area-wide IPM program for the California Nut Industry.

USDA PRF has been at its current location since 1992. The building covers 69,000 square feet. The PRF is currently producing over 750,000 sterile navel orangeworm (NOW) moths 6 days a week with the goal of doubling that within the next year and continuing to increase production over the next few years. At the current rate and age of our cobalt Co-60 sources, it takes over 8 minutes for each irradiation cycle to reach the required dose of 30 kilorad. Over 8 cycles are required to sterilize enough insects for the day’s shipment. Due to this the total irradiation time is over 90 minutes and will continue to increase as the radioactive material decays. The goal of increasing the number of sterile insects requires a shorter irradiation time. 

The purpose of this Statement of Work is to allow the PRF to maintain its capability to irradiate NOW moths at 30 Kilorad in less than 5 minutes. The optimum irradiation time after proper calibration time will be no greater than 2 minutes per irradiation cycle. 


Contractor Requirements
3.0 Technical Requirements / Tasks
The Contractor shall as of the Contract Award Date and for the duration of this contract be appropriately licensed by the Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) and/or Agreement State, to perform Manufacturing and Distribution (M&D) activities on a Foss Therapy Model 484F-C Cobalt-60 Irradiator.

The Contractor is responsible for shipping and transportation of the sources and is responsible for the proper packaging and security of the radioactive materials in compliance with the NRC and Department of Transportation (DOT) regulations. The Contractor, shall as of the Contract Award Date or within a reasonable, defined schedule, possess a current NRC-approved DOT Type B Transportation Quality Assurance (QA) Program to package and transport Type B quantities of Co-60 or contract with a vendor that is properly licensed and possess a Type B QA program.

Contractor must possess and present in advance of Cobalt 60 reload, all necessary licenses and authorizations, including Trustworthy and Reliable determination documentation, required by the US Nuclear Regulatory Commission, as well as the USDA Radiation Safety Division, which demonstrate regulatory approval or authorization to work on this machine at this location.

3.1
Cobalt-60 Reload

3.1.1
The Contractor shall complete a turn-key Cobalt-60 source reload operation of the Foss Therapy Model 484F-C Cobalt-60 Irradiator. The Contractor shall install approximately 20,000 Curies of Cobalt-60 into the Foss Therapy Model 484F-C Cobalt-60 Irradiator. 

3.1.2
The new source capsules shall be approved for use in the Foss Therapy Model 484F-C Cobalt-60 Irradiator by the NRC. Contractor must provide sealed source certifications as well as proof of size, activity, and serial number for each source prior to delivery to the designated location. Leak test certificates shall also be provided to USDA. 

3.1.3
Contractor is responsible for the delivery of the sources to and from the designated locations using methods in accordance with the NRC, DOT, and/or any applicable Agreement State regulations. 

3.1.4
Contractor shall maintain security of the radiation sources in accordance with NRC and/or Agreement State requirements and the contractor’s license conditions at all times during the reloading of an irradiator. USDA will provide additional security during installation and ensure that the installed irradiator meets NRC requirements and USDA license conditions. 

3.1.5
Contractor is responsible for arrangements of any material handling equipment such as forklifts during the reload operation. The contractor must provide all appropriate radiation exposure monitoring instruments and tools to the site.
3.1.6
Contractor is responsible for the proper removal, transportation and disposal of USDA’s depleted sources in accordance with NRC or Agreement State regulations. The contractor shall provide source transfer documentation to USDA upon taking possession of the current Co-60 sources.

3.1.7
The contractor shall clean source tubes and change or clean source rods in the irradiator. All existing sources must be removed from the irradiator before cleaning of the source tubes is carried out.

3.1.8
Contractor shall be responsible for properly spacing all sources in Foss Therapy Model 484F-C Cobalt-60 Irradiator to optimize radiation dose to NOW canisters per PRF requirements.
3.1.9
After the reload, Contractor shall conduct an external radiation level survey and demonstrate that the limits are not exceeded for Foss Therapy Model 484F-C Cobalt-60 Irradiator specified in the National Sealed Source and Device Registry (NSSDR). Contractor shall be responsible for providing/installing any additional shielding necessary to meet these specified external radiation levels at no extra cost to the government. Contractor shall provide the designated Radiation Safety Officer (RSO) with a report demonstrating the external survey results within two (2) days of work completion.
3.1.10
Contractor shall perform a National Institutes of Standards and Technology (NIST) traceable map of dose rates in the irradiator chamber after loading the new sources. New isodose curves for each position of the irradiator turntable and each source configuration shall be provided to PRF. Contractor shall provide a radioactive decay chart for cobalt-60 sources installed in the irradiator. Contractor shall provide sealed source certification and leak test for cobalt-60 sources installed in the irradiator. 
3.1.11
The Contractor shall provide a detailed written work plan to PRF and the designated RSO describing the process to safely reload the irradiator including how the contractor will safely clean the source tubes and change or clean the source rods, and how the source transfer will take place. The plan must include emergency procedures specific to the reload location that would be followed in the event of an unplanned incident. The contractor shall provide a copy of the written plan no later than three weeks after award of contract. Prior to the commencement of work, the contractor must first obtain the designated RSO concurrence on the work plan. 

3.1.12
Contractor shall not contaminate any area of the facility with radioactive material. If contamination occurs, the contractor shall solely be responsible for decontaminating the area to the satisfaction of the Rearing Facility Director, Radiation Safety Officer and contracting officer. Contractor is responsible for the repair of any damage to the irradiator or the facility during the reload operation.

3.2
Preventive Maintenance
Preventive maintenance of operational and safety system, interlock testing, and verification to be performed on Foss Therapy Model 484F-C Cobalt-60 Irradiator. Work to be performed includes:

3.2.1New negator return springs installed and adjusted for all sources.

3.2.2Check and adjust all mechanical systems including, but not limited to, source operation and movement, door operation, and turntable operation. Identify and correct problems or recommend necessary repairs.

3.2.3Test all electrical systems for proper operation and conformance with the SSDR. Check for additional degradation or nonfunctional parts. Any problems will be identified and corrected, as required, or recommendations will be made for necessary repair. 

3.2.4Test all safety systems for proper operation and conformance with the SSDR. Check for additional degradation or nonfunctional parts. Any additional problems will be identified and corrected, as required, or recommendations will be made for necessary repair. 

3.2.5Perform incidental repairs related to or detected during maintenance and servicing procedures. If incidental repairs are needed, the contractor shall provide the replacement parts and perform the repairs at no additional cost to the Government. Incidental repairs include but are not limited to replacements up to a total of $50 per occurrence in direct material, with exception of the anti-tamper connectors and cables.

3.2.6Identify and correct deficiencies as required or recommend necessary repairs. All repair work, with exception of incidental repairs, must be approved by the Contracting Officer prior to beginning work. The contractor shall provide an estimate for other repair work. The Government reserves the right to obtain services for repair and parts from another vendor.

3.2.7Check general appearance.

3.2.8Perform any additional preventive maintenance service on the device as appropriate or indicated in device manual.

3.2.9Verify external radiation levels.

3.2.10Complete and submit written summary report of the work performed, and safety and other system performance to Facility Director or Equipment Specialist, PRF.

3.3
Training
Contractor will provide training to USDA personnel in the safe operation, routine maintenance procedures, maintenance findings/repairs, and scope of allowed maintenance to USDA personnel for the Foss Therapy Model 484F-C Cobalt-60 Irradiator at time of source installation.
