United States Department of Agriculture
Justification to Restrict Competition
FAR 12.102(b)
Identification No. _1172541
1. Identification of the agency and the contracting activity.
Agency: USDA APHIS PPQ Phoenix Rearing Facility
Contracting Activity: AAMD Acquisition Branch, Minneapolis
2. Nature and/or description of the action being approved.
This is to secure a contract for a reload of 20,000 curies Cobalt 60 for the Model 484F-C irradiator at the
Phoenix Rearing Facility (PRF).
3. A description of the supplies or services required to meet the agency’s needs, including the
estimated value.
The Foss Therapy 484F-C Cobalt Irradiator is used to sterilize navel orangeworm moths. At the current
rate and age of our cobalt Co-60 sources, it takes over 8 minutes for each irradiation cycle to reach the
required dose of 30 kilorad. Over 8 cycles are required to sterilize enough insects for the current
production rate shipments. Due to this, the total irradiation time is over 90 minutes and will continue to
increase as the radioactive material decays. The goal of increasing the number of sterile insects requires
a shorter irradiation time. A turn-key Cobalt-60 source reload operation is needed for the Foss Therapy
484F-C Cobalt-60 Irradiator. The required amount needed to be installed is approximately 20,000 Curies
of Cobalt-60. This will allow the Phoenix Rearing Facility to meet the coming year’s production rate.
4. Identify the statutory authority permitting other than full and open competition.
The statutory authority permitting other than full and open competition is 41 U.S.C. 1901 and 1903 as
implemented by FAR 12.102.
5. Demonstrate that the proposed contractor’s unique qualifications or the nature of the
acquisition requires using the authority cited.
Foss Therapy Services Inc. manufactured and installed the irradiator and they are the only company
qualified to perform the reload. Foss Therapy is the only company that performs this service on this
model of machine.
6. Provide a description of efforts made to ensure that offers are solicited from as many
Potential sources as possible, including whether a notice was or will be publicized as
required by Part 5 and, if not, which exception under Part 5 applies.
Foss Therapy Services (FTS) holds the proprietary designs, exact engineering tolerances, and
mechanical blueprints for the Model 484F-C. Third-party providers do not possess the proprietary
Page 1
mechanical specifications necessary to align and properly configure the replacement sealed source
capsules into the machine's specific multi-source holders
7. A determination by the Contracting Officer that the anticipated cost to the Government will be
fair and reasonable.
To determine fair and reasonable pricing, the USDA reviewed historical pricing data on the USA
Spending website, and internal USDA documents, as available, to compare pricing offered to that
previously paid. Factors such as inflation, size, and capacity were taken into consideration. From this
review, USDA determines that pricing offered for this procurement is expected to be similar to previous
pricing paid by USDA, and other Departments, for purchases similar in nature.
8. A description of the market research conducted, and the results or a statement of the reason
Market Research was not conducted.
Because the Foss Therapy 484F‑C Cobalt irradiator is a highly specialized, shielded device
manufactured exclusively by Foss Therapy Services, they are the only company authorized to perform
critical maintenance tasks, including cobalt‑60 source reloading. Foss Therapy is the original
manufacturer and the only entity authorized by both the Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) and the
California Radiologic Health Branch (CRHB) to work on the shielding and source‑related components
of this irradiator model. No other vendor is verified to possess the regulatory authorization, technical
specifications, or manufacturer approval necessary to safely and legally reload cobalt‑60 sources for the
484F‑C unit. Therefore, Foss Therapy Services is the only responsible source available to perform this
work.
9. Any other facts supporting use of other than full and open competition.
This acquisition will be a small business set aside as all businesses are registered as a small business in
the SAM database.
10. A listing of the sources, if any, that expressed an interest in the acquisition in writing.
None
11. A statement of the actions, if any, the agency may take to remove or overcome any barriers to
competition before any subsequent acquisition of the supplies or services required.
USDA will conduct regular market research and engage with industry to identify new irradiation sources
and emerging technologies for potential use in future requirements of a similar nature.
12. Certifications & Approvals
Supporting data that is the responsibility of technical or requirements personnel and which form the
basis for this justification are accurate and complete to the best of my knowledge.

Federal notice (Special Notice), INTERIOR, DEPARTMENT OF THE.US GEOLOGICAL SURVEY.OFC OF ACQUSITION  GRANTS-NATIONAL

Description: This is a notice of intent to solicit from a single source. The US Geological Survey (USGS) intends to award a purchase order to Innovasea Marine Systems Canada Inc. in Bedford, Nova Scotia, for 43 Innovasea NexTrak R1 acoustic telemetry receivers and 150 compatible V16-4x 64 kHz kHz acoustic transmitters to support long-term telemetry monitoring of migratory fishes throughout Atlantic coast river systems and estuaries. The delivered acoustic receivers and tags must: - Operate at a frequency of 69 kHz to ensure compatibility with existing collaborative telemetry arrays and coastwide telemetry infrastructure. - Be compatible with all Innovasea coded 69 kHz transmitters and sensor tags currently used by partner institutions and monitoring programs. - Support long-term riverine and estuarine deployments with receiver battery life of approximately 13 months. - Provide sufficient onboard storage capacity to support extended deployments with approximately 5 million detections. - Support deployments in a wide range of aquatic environments with a minimum depth rating of 750 meters. - Include logging capabilities for environmental and operational metrics including noise, tilt, temperature, and signal strength. - Include programmable self-transmitter functionality to support equipment diagnostics and deployment verification. - Integrate with Fathom Connect software for efficient telemetry data offload, management, and analysis. - Be compatible with the VR100-300 Deckbox and VHTx 69 kHz transponding hydrophone system for communication with deployed receivers. - Include acoustic transmitters capable of long-term monitoring of migratory fish species in riverine, estuarine, and coastal environments. - Include acoustic transmitters with variable programming options appropriate for a range of species and study objectives, including Atlantic sturgeon, shortnose sturgeon, American eel, striped bass, and river herring. - Include coded acoustic transmitters capable of providing unique identification codes to allow simultaneous monitoring of large numbers of tagged fish within collaborative telemetry arrays. - Include acoustic tags with battery life sufficient to support seasonal, multi-year, or long-term movement studies depending on project requirements. - Include acoustic tags capable of transmitting environmental or biological sensor information, including depth and temperature, where required for project objectives. - Include acoustic tags designed for high detection efficiency and compatibility with existing Innovasea receiver infrastructure currently deployed throughout Atlantic coast telemetry networks. - Include acoustic transmitters and sensor tags fully compatible with coastwide telemetry databases and collaborative data-sharing frameworks utilized by state, federal, academic, and non-governmental telemetry partners. Award will be made in accordance with Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) procedures at FAR Part 12 entitled, Acquisition of Commercial Items. Innovasea Marine Systems Canada Inc. is, to the knowledge of the USGS, the only source who can provide this proprietary equipment that is compatible with existing systems. Responses or inquiries shall only be accepted through e- mail addressed to the contract specialist, Miranda_blankenship@ios.doi.gov, and must be uploaded and received in their entirety no later than 09/11/2026 at 1300 EDT. attachments.name: DnF for OTFOC-Novacene-3_Redacted.pdf
attachments.text:
Novacene Photonics acquired the intellectual property and partial assets of M-squared,
including the Equinox 532nm pump laser. The Equinox was developed by M-squared as
an improved alternative to the Lighthouse Photonics Sprout 532 pump laser. This will
allow us to continue using the existing Solstice Titanium (Ti):Sapphire laser system, add
a pick-off for 532 light and realign the modules for the optical (EMM-1950) and near
ultraviolet (ECD-X) wavelengths instead of purchasing new systems.
Although there are multiple companies in the commercial marketplace that provide a
532nm pump-laser, only one company can provide a direct replacement to the existing
Sprout pump while maintaining full capabilities of the existing government-owned M-
squared Ti:Sapphire laser system. This option also adds a 532 nm variable pump pick-
off capability. The Novacene Equinox is a direct replacement for an existing Sprout-G-
12W that pumps an M-squared Solstice Ti:Sapphire laser. It has a required dimension to
fit with the M-squared laser and steers the pump beam from the pump to the Solstice
laser head via a sealed beam path and matches the pump beam height, pump beam
optics, and a manually adjustable pump beam x, y steering mirror to optimize pump
beam alignment. Alignment must be conducted by someone who is knowledgeable
about the Solstice laser system to prevent safety hazards and damage to the system.
Novacene is the sole authorized service provider for legacy M Squared laser systems.
Therefore, the only other laser available that is compatible is the Novacene Equinox and
no substitutes exist.
Market research determined that Novacene Photonics Limited is the only company
capable of meeting the Government’s minimum requirements of one (1) replacement
532-nanometer (nm) pump laser for an existing government owned m-squared laser with
pick-off, and alignment to the existing system.

attachments.text:
SALIENT CHARACTERISTICS
Model 990 Antenna Control System

Antenna Control System must be technically compatible with and capable of controlling a AN/FSC-78 system: a full motion, large aperture 18m antenna terminal capable of tracking up to 10 degrees/sec in azimuth and elevation up to 85 degrees.

Antenna Control System must be capable of controlling a total of four brushless DC motors: 2, 40 HP in azimuth and 2, 10.6 HP in elevation.

All four brushless DC motors must be permanent magnet type with torque source to control the antenna to zero RPM.

All four DC motors must provide DC tachometer, virtual tachometer, and incremental encoder motor rate feedback.

Antenna Control System must use Kollmorgen motor controllers, variable speed.

Position encoder must be two, Heidenhain Position Encoders with 25 Bit Resolution and +/-20 Arc-Second accuracy per revolution.

DSP servo loop closures must be located in the Power Drive Unit and managed by QNX Real Time Operating System.

CPU logic must be located in the Power Drive Unit.

A drive isolation transformer must be part of the Antenna Control System.

Power Drive Unit cabinet must be stainless steel, NEMA-4X rated enclosure.

Power Drive Unit must have redundant, fail-safe interlock logic to immediately disable drives upon an axis or system fault, safety rated relays that interface directly to emergency stop switches, and soft stop logic for non-emergency stops (issues zero rate command and allows motors to gradually decelerate prior to disabling the axis).

Antenna Control Unit display must be 15” touch screen LCD color display with Az/El actual and commanded positions, currently selected modes/states, summary fault indicator and individual status and fault message display. 

Antenna Control Unit operations modes must include Tracking (Optrack, Steptrack, Monopulse), Pointing (StarTrack, Preset, Designate, NORAD, Table Track), and Other (Maintenance, Manual, Stop, Computer, Simulator). 

Antenna Control Unit must be time synchronized via NTP, IRIG-B, or 1PPS.

Antenna Control System must include a Portable Maintenance Unit that provides manually commanded, bi-directional control of all axes, hand held, backup means of moving antenna and ACU independent, four line 20 character display for axis positions, mode, and scrolling status messages, modes to include position jog and hi/lo variable speed, and a function to enable/disable the antenna per axis.

Antenna Control System must include Power Drive Unit Logic redundancy to provide antenna control in case of primary antenna control board failure. Redundant component must include an additional Antenna Control Board, Expansion Board, PLC Arbitrator, T-Bar Relay, and associated Power Supplies.

Federal notice (Special Notice), NATIONAL TRANSPORTATION SAFETY BOARD.NATIONAL TRANSPORTATION SAFETY BOARD.NTSB ACQ  LEASE MGMT DIVISION
Title: Notice of Intent to Sole-Source Award for the 25 Hour Enhanced Airborne Flight Recorder (EAFR) Golden Chassis

Description: THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSALS, AN INVITATION FOR BIDS, OR A REQUEST FOR QUOTATIONS. FURTHER, IT DOES NOT REPRESENT A COMMITMENT BY THE GOVERNMENT TO PAY FOR COSTS INCURRED IN PREPARATION AND SUBMISSION OF DATA OR ANY OTHER COSTS INCURRED IN RESPONSE TO THIS ANNOUNCEMENT. This is a Sources Sought Notice with the intent to award a sole source award to General Electric Aerospace (GE) under the authority of FAR 13.106-1 based on GE�s unique technical qualifications as the only manufacturer and provider of the 25 Hour Enhanced Airborne Flight Recorder (EAFR) Golden Chassis as described below. Notice is provided as information to the marketplace, market research, and is an invitation for any other qualified companies to express their interest in and demonstrate their capability to provide the equipment/software that performs the required functions. Background The National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) is an independent federal agency charged by Congress with investigating every civil aviation accident in the United States and significant events in the other modes of transportation�railroad, transit, highway, marine, pipeline, and commercial space. We determine the probable causes of the accidents and events we investigate and issue safety recommendations aimed at preventing future occurrences. In addition, we conduct transportation safety research studies and offer information and other assistance to family members and survivors for each accident or event we investigate. We also serve as the appellate authority for enforcement actions involving aviation and mariner certificates issued by the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) and US Coast Guard, and we adjudicate appeals of civil penalty actions taken by the FAA. The NTSB�s Office of Research and Engineering, Vehicle Recorder Division (RE-40) requires the capability to download data from a variety of vehicle recording devices, especially flight data recorders (FDR) and cockpit voice recorders (CVR) from aircraft involved in aviation accidents. These systems require proprietary hardware and software from the manufacturer to download data. The 25 Hour EAFR and associated download equipment is designed and manufactured by GE and is required to download data from undamaged and damaged EAFR�s recovered from aircraft involved in accidents investigated by the NTSB. The GE product is proprietary and is not sold through any third-party resellers nor is it available for purchase through any government-wide acquisition vehicles. No other commercially available products are available currently that provide the same functionality. The EAFR download equipment are considered the definitive method of downloading data from the GE EAFR among industry professionals. Required Capabilities The NTSB requires the 25 Hour Enhanced Airborne Flight Recorder (EAFR) Golden Chassis. Sources capable of fully satisfying the above requirements are invited to submit capability statements/expressions of interest providing the Government the necessary information to determine actual capability. At a minimum, this information, which must be prepared specifically in response to this notice should, must include: (1) identification of company or organization; (2) an assertion of existing, full capability to meet proposed requirements; (3) business/contracts/marketing office point(s) of contact; (4) notification of business size and/or special status; and (5) any additional information that may be useful to the successful procurement of the requirements, if solicited. These expressions of interest shall adhere to a ten (10)-page submission limit plus web links and any specialized product descriptions. The statement of qualifications should include only information that clearly demonstrates the respondent's capabilities, expertise, and experience to perform the requirements described in this notice. General marketing material should not be included. The NTSB prefers that companies do not submit proprietary material. However, the Government recognizes that proprietary data may be a part of your submittal. If so, clearly mark such restricted or proprietary data and present it as an addendum to the non-restricted/non-proprietary information. Information received will be considered solely for the purpose of determining whether to conduct a competitive procurement. A determination by the Government not to compete the proposed order based upon responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. All responsible sources may submit a capability statement, which shall be considered by NTSB. Parties must submit information within five (5) days of publication of this notice. NTSB will not return capability statements and the supporting documentation submitted in response to this notice. Telephone responses and inquiries will not be accepted. Federal notice (Special Notice), COMMERCE, DEPARTMENT OF.NATIONAL OCEANIC AND ATMOSPHERIC ADMINISTRATION.NATIONAL OCEANIC AND ATMOSPHERIC ADMINISTRATION
Title: NOTICE OF INTENT TO NEGOTIATE A SOLE-SOURCE CONTRACT
Solicitation number: 140802-26-0601
PSC: 5995; NAICS: 334511
Description: The US Department of Commerce (DOC), National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA), Office of Marine and Aviation Operations (OMAO), requires one (1) Klein armored side scan sonar cable, 0.40-inch BHD, 350 meters, P/N 14104200-350M, and one (1) compatible cable termination kit, BHD armored coax 0.40-inch, P/N 14102947, for NOAA Ship THOMAS JEFFERSON. The cable and termination kit are required for use with the Government-owned Klein 5900 v1 and v2 side scan sonar system. Required delivery is on or before October 13, 2026, to the Marine Operations Center - Atlantic, 439 W York Street, Norfolk, VA 23510. These supplies will be provided by Klein Marine Systems, Inc., located at 65 Parker Street, Suite 5, Newburyport, Massachusetts 01950. Klein Marine Systems, Inc. is the manufacturer of the Klein 5900 v1 and v2 side scan sonar system. The required replacement cable must interface with the existing Klein TPU and towfish, termination and tow-point attachment hardware, and the installed CLARS side scan winch and sheaves. The cable termination must also be compatible with either Focal or Alpha 8-pin sliprings. The existing CLARS winch and sheaves are sized for a 0.40-inch cable, and the Klein 5900 v1 and v2 system requires a 50-ohm impedance match. The Government is operating near the transmission-loss limits of the cable, making the electrical and mechanical tolerances critical. Use of a cable that has not been specifically manufactured and configured for this equipment would introduce substantial uncertainty regarding signal integrity, telemetry performance, mechanical termination, and compatibility with the existing winch and slipring arrangement. A non-compatible cable could result in data loss, system failure, damage to Government equipment, or loss of the towed sonar asset. The Government is not aware of any other source reasonably available that can provide the required cable and termination kit at the level of compatibility and performance required for the existing Klein 5900 v1 and v2 side scan sonar system. The Government intends to acquire these supplies under the guidelines of FAR Part 13, Simplified Acquisition Procedures and FAR Part 12, Acquisition of Commercial Products and Commercial Services. The Government intends to solicit and negotiate directly with Klein Marine Systems, Inc., under the authority of FAR 13.106-1(b)(1). The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for this acquisition is 334511. This is not a solicitation for competitive quotes. However, any responsible source that believes it can provide an item that fully meets the Government's minimum technical requirements may submit a statement of capabilities, which, if received in a timely manner, will be considered by NOAA. A statement of capabilities must be received by September 03, 2026 at 12PM ET. A determination by the Government not to compete this proposed requirement based upon responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. Information received will normally be considered solely for the purpose of determining whether to conduct a competitive procurement in the future. Evidence must be provided of the ability to provide the required cable and termination kit. The capability statement and any other information furnished must be in writing and contain sufficient technical detail to allow the Government to determine whether the source can meet all requirements, including compatibility with the existing Klein 5900 v1 and v2 side scan sonar system, 50-ohm impedance requirement, 0.40-inch cable size, existing termination and tow-point hardware, Focal or Alpha 8-pin sliprings, installed CLARS winch and sheaves, and the required delivery date. Capability statements and related materials must be e-mailed to Alexander Cancela at alexander.cancela@noaa.gov by September 03, 2026 at 12PM ET.

Federal notice (Special Notice), AGRICULTURE, DEPARTMENT OF.FOREST SERVICE.USDA-FS, CSA EAST 6
Title: Intent to Sole Source: Opsytec Dr. Gr�bel GmbH UV Equipment and Calibration Services
Solicitation number: 1174144

Description: SPECIAL NOTICE: NOTICE OF INTENT TO SOLE SOURCE General Information Document Type: Special Notice Notice Sub-Type: Intent to Sole Source / Only One Responsible Source Requisition Number: 1174144 Product Service Code (PSC): 6636 (Environmental Chambers and Related Equipment) NAICS Code: 334516 (Analytical Laboratory Instrument Manufacturing) Place of Performance: USDA ARS Eastern Regional Research Center, 600 E Mermaid Ln, Wyndmoor, PA 19038 Statutory Authority The U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA), Agricultural Research Service (ARS), Northeast Area (NEA), intends to negotiate a sole-source, firm-fixed-price contract with Opsytec Dr. Gr�bel GmbH (UEI: HQ2KD3G82EP2), located at Am Hardtwald 6-8, D-76275 Ettlingen, Germany. This acquisition is conducted under the authority of FAR 13.106-1(b)(1) and AGAR 413.106, which permits soliciting from a single source for purchases not exceeding the Simplified Acquisition Threshold (SAT) when the Contracting Officer determines that only one source is reasonably available to satisfy agency requirements. Description of Requirement & Salient Characteristics The USDA-ARS Characterization and Interventions for Foodborne Pathogens Research Unit requires the procurement of a laboratory-grade UV-LED Irradiation Chamber (Model: BSL-01i ECO+), complete with an integrated UV-MAT touch irradiation controller, an RMD sensor calibrated to 405 nm, specialized PC operating software, and an internal sample heating/cooling plate. This system will be utilized to conduct non-thermal biological research evaluating the precise inactivation effects of blue light (specifically at a 405 nm wavelength) on foodborne pathogens across various agricultural commodities. The government has verified that the following baseline technical specifications are mandatory to support active research configurations: Wavelength Operations: Must operate at a true 405 nm blue light spectrum. Irradiance Range: Dynamically variable and adjustable from 0 to 800 mW/cm� with intensity scaling increments from 1% to 100%. Thermal Tracking: Integrated heating/cooling mechanism operating within non-thermal limits from 10�C to 40�C to preserve sample biological integrity during testing. Data Log Metrics: Built-in sensor loop measuring irradiance constantly with digital data recording rates scalable from 1 second to 1 hour. Physical Footprint: Benchtop laboratory configuration conforming strictly to the available facility spatial limitations of 40 x 30 x 50 cm. Operator Safety: Interlocked enclosure operational layout to ensure strict radiation shielding for laboratory personnel. Market Research & Justification Summary In accordance with FAR Part 10 and USDA Desk Book guidance, market research was conducted from January through March 2026. A comprehensive review of peer-reviewed scientific literature and direct inquiries across established commercial channels (including Fisher Scientific, GSA Advantage!, and alternative equipment developers) confirmed that zero domestic or international alternatives can fulfill these combined parameters. Alternative systems operate exclusively on traditional UV wavebands, lack high-output dynamic variance tuning, or fail to meet the mandatory structural benchtop dimensions necessary for safe deployment within the active testing facility. Opsytec Dr. Gr�bel GmbH is the sole market source capable of supplying this specialized instrumentation package without causing extensive project delay or a critical loss of scientific capability. Submission Instructions & Response Deadline This announcement does not constitute a Request for Quotes (RFQ) or a Request for Proposals (RFP), and no formal solicitation package is available. However, in compliance with FAR and AGAR public notice transparency standards, the government will evaluate capability statements received from interested market sources to determine if a competitive acquisition strategy should be pursued in the future. Entities believing they can fully satisfy the government�s stated requirements must submit a comprehensive technical capability statement. Submissions must include detailed technical documentation, manufacturer specifications, and explicit verification that their system meets every mandatory salient characteristic listed above. All capability statements must be submitted electronically via email to the Contract Specialist , Michael J. Wheelock, at Michael.Wheelock@usda.gov. Responses must be received in full no later than 01:00 A.M. EST on September 2, 2026. A determination by the Government not to compete this proposed action based upon responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government.

attachments.text:
UV-LED chamber
Specifications
The research unit “Characterization and Interventions for Foodborne Pathogens” at the Eastern Regional Research Center in Wyndmoor, PA investigates innovative technologies to control and inactivate pathogens in different food commodities. Some of these interventions include nonthermal processes such as cold plasma and light technologies. This purchase is for a UV-LED chamber to conduct research evaluating the effect of blue light (405 nm) on microbial inactivation for different food commodities such as eggs, fruits and vegetables.

Specifications:
The UV-LED chamber must have the following specifications:
Works at least 405 nm (wavelength). It is desirable to have additional wavelengths.
Have a variable irradiance (from 0 to 800 mW/cm2)
Being a lab unit
Irradiance can be adjusted from 1 to 100%
Have a sensor that measures irradiance constantly
Have a heating/cooling plate for temperature control
The chamber dimensions fit the footprint of the lab (40 x 30 x 50 cm, 15.74 in x 11.81 in x 19.68 in)
The working temperature goes from 10 to 40⁰C
The cooling of the chamber is done with air cooling
The system has a dose controller
It has a data recording rate from 1 s to 1 h
The system has a timer that counts seconds 
It has an enclosure during operation to protect the operator

STATEMENT OF WORK (SOW)
FOR
WASTEWATER AERATION BLOWER
1.0 GENERAL
1.1 BACKGROUND
The U.S. Coast Guard (USCG) Training Center (TRACEN) Petaluma, located at 599 Tomales
Road, Petaluma, CA 94952, is responsible for the operation and maintenance of a wastewater
treatment facility utilizing a 0.085 MG Average Dry Weather Flow Activated Sludge Tertiary
Treatment system. The most critical element in this process is the introduction of oxygen to
keep the microorganisms alive that safely break down the raw sewage. Industrial wastewater
aeration blowers are utilized to introduce oxygen into the system. This Statement of Work
(SOW) formally outlines the requirements for their procurement.
1.2 SCOPE
The contractor must provide one Kaeser wastewater aeration blower that meets the physical,
functional, and performance characteristics specified in this SOW. The contractor is responsible
for adhering to all requirements and ensuring timely delivery.
1.3 OBJECTIVE
The objective of this SOW is to procure a Kaeser wastewater aeration blower. This blower must
provide continuous oxygen to the wastewater system at precise levels and be fully compatible
with the existing system for seamless integration and maintenance. The SOW ensures
alignment between TRACEN Petaluma and the contractor regarding specifications, safety
features, delivery, acceptance criteria, and terms, supporting successful project completion.
2.0 SPECIFIC REQUIREMENTS/TASKS
Contractor must provide one aeration blower that meets all specs in TASK ONE w/out
exceptions.
2.1 TASK ONE. WASTEWATER AERATION BLOWER DESCRIPTION
One (1) Kaeser Rotary Blower, Model EB 421 C, designed for wastewater aeration. The blower
must be a 40hp unit capable of providing a continuous oxygen supply at 6.1 PSI with a relative
humidity of 40%.
2.1.1 PRODUCT CHARACTERISTICS
• Brand/Model: Kaeser EB 421 C
• Drive motor rated power: 40.0 hp
• Motor efficiency in mains operation: 93.0%
• Drive motor rated speed: 3600 rpm
• Electrical supply: 460V/3/60Hz
• Sound Enclosure: Must be included.
2.2 ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
The wastewater aeration blower must meet all the specified physical, functional, and
performance characteristics as outlined in this SOW. Upon delivery, TRACEN Petaluma will
conduct an acceptance inspection to ensure compliance with the provided specifications. The
wastewater aeration blower will be considered accepted if it meets all requirements outlined in
this SOW and passes the acceptance inspection.

attachments.text:
SALIENT CHARACTERISTICS & TECHNICAL SPECIFICATIONS
Floor-Model Preparative Laboratory Ultracentrifuge System
1. Scope of Requirement
The United States Department of Agriculture (USDA), Forest Service (USFS), CSA East 6,
requires the procurement of a high-performance, floor-model preparative laboratory
ultracentrifuge system. This scientific instrumentation is utilized for the high-speed
sedimentation, separation, and purification of macromolecular biological samples, including viral
particles, proteins, exosomes, cellular organelles, and nanoparticles. The system must support
active research in plant virology and molecular biology by delivering exact particle
sedimentation thresholds under continuous high-vacuum and strict thermal parameters.
2. Core Performance Specifications
Technical Parameter Minimum Mandatory Requirement
Maximum Rotational Speed Minimum of 90,000 Rotations Per Minute
(RPM) capable of precision acceleration.
Maximum Centrifugal Force Minimum of 694,000 x g (Relative
Centrifugal Force / RCF) at full operational
capacity.
Speed Control Precision Must maintain a rotation precision threshold
within +/- 2 RPM at speeds above 1,000
RPM.
Operational Temperature Range Selectable from 0°C to 40°C in exact 1°C
increments to safeguard sample integrity.
Temperature Control Accuracy Must maintain steady-state temperature
within +/- 0.5°C across the entire operating
range.
Drive Implementation Type Vacuum-encased induction drive system
functioning inside a single shared vacuum
environment.
3. Mandatory Salient Characteristics
To be considered technically acceptable, any alternative instrumentation must natively possess
all of the following salient physical, safety, and interface features without requiring post-
manufacturing adaptations:
• Total Legacy Asset Component Interoperability (Rotor Compatibility): The centrifuge
drive spindle, hub geometry, and vacuum chamber dimensions must maintain 100% native,
un-adapted mechanical compatibility with the government's existing inventory of heavy
titanium preparative rotors, specifically including legacy Beckman SW 28 swing-bucket and
Type 90 Ti fixed-angle rotor platforms. Alternative units requiring proprietary vendor
conversion adapters are technically unacceptable.
• Comprehensive Multi-Stage Overspeed Prevention: The hardware configuration must
incorporate three independent, simultaneous layers of safety check structures: (1) Dynamic
Rotor Inertia Verification calculating kinetic energy profiles during initial spool-up, (2) an
optical physical sensor array reading an overspeed ring disk at the base of the drive spindle,
and (3) an independent magnetic sensor cross-checking real-time spindle rotations.
• Environmental & Infrastructure Restraints: Cooling and refrigeration systems must
operate entirely refrigerant gas-free, utilizing a solid-state thermoelectric cooling and heating
block that contains 100% zero Chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs) or synthetic chemical gaseous
mediums to comply with native facility environmental parameters.
• Power Quality Handling: The system must feature a built-in automated input voltage
handling matrix supporting 180 to 264 VAC line switching, alongside an un-braked
momentum-coast system allowing continued operation or safe recovery during transient low-
voltage anomalies (< 85 VAC) or complete electrical drop-outs.
• Data Management & Security Protocols: Features an embedded graphical workspace
including local user log tracking supporting up to 50 unique operator IDs, multi-level data
access hierarchy restrictions (Administrator, Super User, and Operator), electronic signature
chain-of-custody recording, and real-time operational temperature/speed plotting exportable
natively to local USB flash storage or a networked drive via Ethernet in generic XML and
CSV spreadsheets.
• Physical Dimensions & Structural Safety: Footprint dimensions must not exceed a
localized footprint configuration of 940 mm (Width) by 681 mm (Depth) to fit existing
laboratory floor plan layouts. The structural casing must possess a minimum net weight of
485 kg (1,069 lbs) paired with a high-tensile seamless steel containment sleeve layout to
satisfy localized maximum credible accident (MCA) safety containment regulations.
4. Lifecycle and Field Service Requirements
To ensure continuous mission performance and strict engineering verification, the following
lifecycle support items must accompany any technical submission:
• On-Site Delivery and Basic Installation Service: Logistics must include secure freight
delivery, inside uncrating, layout leveling, utility connections, and operational verification.
• Basic Operator Verification Training: Provision of introductory on-site training sessions
covering general hardware interaction, menu sequencing, rotor attachment, and safety log
extraction methodologies.
• Field Calibration & Verification Lifecycle Support: The responding vendor must have
local, manufacturer-trained field service technicians available to complete on-site validation
(Installation Qualification/Operational Qualification - IQ/OQ) and routine technical
monitoring programs.
• Minimum Technical Warranty Coverage: Standard baseline warranty coverage must
guarantee a minimum of 1 year on the primary system frame, 5 years on any accompanying
rotor bodies, and 10 years on the main vacuum-encased drive unit core.

SPECIFICATIONS

Specifications Description: Gel/membrane digital imager and analysis system
Quantity: 1
Unit Type: Each 
Minimum Requirements:
The digital imager must be self-contained without the requirement of a separate computer.
A Charge-Couple Device (CCD) camera sensor is preferred over Complementary Metal-Oxide-Semiconductor (CMOS) sensor.
Peltier cooling of the CCD sensor is preferred.
The instrument’s camera must be capable of capturing images of greater than or equal to 8.0 MP
Light source requirements:
The unit must be capable of producing ultraviolet transillumination at wavelengths of 302 and 365 nm. 
The unit must be capable of both epi-white and trans-white illumination. 
Must contain RGB LEDs for true color imaging of opaque and translucid samples
The unit must be able to detect chemiluminescence. 
A blue light source (400-500 nm) is desired but not required.
The imaging system must have a safety door sensor that automatically deactivates light sources when the door is open to prevent accidental exposure to UV or other excitation sources. 
The trans-illuminator should have safety override enabling band excision from gel.
The ability to excite and detect common fluorophores is desired but not required. The ability to upgrade for this purpose is preferred. 
Desired fluorophores include, but are not limited to Alexa Fluor 488, SYBR Green, Alexa Fluor 647, Cy5, Phycoerythrin.
 A motorized filter wheel capable of holding at least six (6) filters is greatly preferred.
The footprint of the unit cannot exceed the dimensions of 50 x 60 x 40 cm (W x H x D)
Automatic image focusing is greatly preferred.
The imaging system must detect samples with a spatial resolution of at least 50 µm.
Analysis software must be included in the final price.
Software must be able to perform molecular weight analysis, densitometry, array normalization, automated band and lane detection, and background subtraction. Colony counting and multiplex analysis is preferred but not required. 
Software compatibility with both PC and Mac operating systems is greatly preferred. 
The unit must be able to run without internet access.
 Non-proprietary file formatting is greatly preferred.
 Data must be exportable to USB. 
The unit must run off a 120V power supply.
The unit must be Made in America.

United States Department of Agriculture
Decision to Restrict Competition under the Simplified Acquisition Threshold
Identification Number: 1232SA26Q1012
In accordance with the Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul (RFO) FAR
12.102(a), the following documents the decision to restrict competition for this acquisition.
(1) Mission Area and Contracting Activity
Requisition Number: 1174258
Requesting Activity Agency: USDA-ARS Agricultural Water Efficiency and Salinity Research
Unit (129156)
Contracting Activity: USDA-ARS Acquisition and Property Division (1232SA)
(3) Brief Description of Supplies or Services
The acquisition involves procuring a laboratory-grade microwave digestion system, the Milestone
Ethos UP with its MAXI-44 rotor. This system is needed to perform closed-vessel acid digestion of
plant and soil samples prior to elemental analysis on the ICP-OES. Microwave digestion is a
critical preparatory step in producing fully digested plant and soil materials in solution suitable for
macronutrient and micronutrient quantification. It provides controlled microwave heating through
precise pressure and temperature management. This results in reproducible digestion conditions
across large sample batches to ensure the efficient and uniform breakdown of these environmental
samples. The analytes must be fully in solution prior to analysis for nutrient cycling studies, water
efficiency assessments, and soil chemistry research conducted by the laboratory.
(1) Suggested Source
The suggested contractor is:
Milestone Inc.
25 Controls Drive
Shelton, CT 06484
UEI: VJ19GM8NHHT7
(4) Justification for Restricting Competition and the Basis for that Decision.
A. Explain the unique qualifications/characteristics of the proposed contractor or product and why no
other contractor or product/service can meet the Government's need.
The acquisition of the microwave digestion system must be restricted to the Milestone Ethos UP
due to several unique qualifications and characteristics exclusive to their product. The USDA-ARS
Salinity Laboratory currently operates the Milestone Ethos EZ microwave digestion system, which
has supported years of validated digestion protocols and established methods for plant and soil
materials. However, the Ethos EZ is an aging system with essential parts becoming obsolete and
serviceability diminishing. Upgrading to the Ethos UP will allow the laboratory to preserve
existing digestion workflows, maintain compatibility with our existing analyzer, improve
operational reliability, and ensure continued production of high quality digested needed for
ongoing research and analytical projects. All plant and soil digestion methods, including reagent
volumes, temperature ramps, pressure profiles, and power input/output, are built around
Rev. 3/4/26
United States Department of Agriculture
Decision to Restrict Competition under the Simplified Acquisition Threshold
Identification Number: 1232SA26Q1012
Milestone’s hardware design. These methods were optimized specifically for Milestone vessel
geometry, rotor configuration, and microwave distribution. Switching to another contractor or
product will invalidate all current digestion protocols. This will require the development, testing,
and validation of new digestion programs. Different systems will also alter the digestion kinetics
and have varying microwave energy delivery, vessel materials, pressure mechanisms, and
temperature feedback system. This will introduce the risk of error during the method development
process and will disrupt the workflow of essential salinity and nutrient analysis research. The final
data produced on the ICP-OES from the digested products will also be impacted due to a change in
the microwave contractor. Calibration standards, detection limits, quality control/quality assurance,
and method accuracy have all been evaluated and calibration in tandem with Milestone’s system.
The Ethos UP provides a spacious stainless-steel cavity for corrosion resistance and acid gas
containment. The rotating microwave diffuser ensures uniform energy distribution. This in
combination with the contactless temperature control allows the temperature of all vessels to be
monitored simultaneously. The PTFE-TFM vessels with vent and reseal safety technology allows
for the controlled release of excess vessel pressure and resealing after pressure relief. Alternative
systems rely on other safety features that pose more risk compared to the Ethos UP. Milestone’s
design preserves vessel integrity and minimizes the loss of volatiles which is essential for trace
element analysis. Only the Milestone MAXI-44 rotor canhandle 44-100 mL vessels positioned in a
single rotor. This design allows for the ability to digest a high number of samples in one batch
without downsizing the vessels, splitting batches, or performing multiple runs. Being able to
simultaneously digest 44 samples under identical chemical and thermal conditions is incredibly
efficient and accelerates sample turnaround. There will also be less variability between samples.
Overall, Milestone provides a direct upgrade path to ensure continuity and maintain workflow with
unique and specific engineering features that are not available in other models on the market. The
Ethos UP is the only microwave digestion system that meets every one of the USDA-ARS Salinity
Laboratory’s technical, operational, and safety requirements in a single integrated platform while
preserving full compatibility with existing Milestone digestion methods. No other system on the
market provides this complete suite of capabilities simultaneously without compromising other
features such as vessel volume, batch size, and temperature monitoring precision.
B. Describe market research conducted and the results or the reason why no market research was
conducted.
Market research was conducted to determine whether comparable microwave digestion systems
available from other vendors would meet the laboratory’s minimum technical and operational
requirements. This included reviewing commercially available rotor-based digestion platforms,
analyzing vendor specifications, and closely examining competing systems’ vessel materials,
pressure and temperature management designs, vessel temperature monitoring capabilities, and
batch throughput configurations. The findings confirmed that no other microwave digestion
systems could provide all required specifications simultaneously without compromising vessel
volume, the temperature control system, and existing validated digestion methods.

forms a basis for this justification, is complete and accurate.

Description: NOTICE OF INTENT TO AWARD A SOLE SOURCE This Notice of Intent is not a request for competitive proposals. This is not a solicitation or request for offers. No solicitation package is available and telephone requests will not be honored. Only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements. The FWS KY ESFO intends to award a sole source purchase order to NTERTEST, INC. to furnish: Thermal cameras for bat roost monitoring USFWS approached Intertest about needing to monitor mammalian bat activity inside and at the entrances of caves and mines as well as at other roosts like bridges, culverts and trees. Currently available camera solutions do not provide the clarity and accuracy required for our monitoring purposes. The camera needed to be IP67-rated to endure wet environments and have thermal vision optics. White lighting could not be used as it would disrupt the bats' natural behavior. USFWS also needed the system to be simple and portable without an auxiliary battery supply. Finally, the system needed to have interchangeable focusing lenses to capture different views of the bats' activity depending upon the type of feature being surveyed. InterTest developed the camera around the Sierra Olympia Viento 10 with a 60 Hz frame rate and long-wave infrared (LWIR) imaging. InterTest ensured that Viento focusing lenses worked with the custom IP-67-rated housing. Additionally, a ruggedized tablet device was chosen for viewing the live camera footage while simultaneously powering the camera. A durable cord grip secured the cable and ensured the camera housing remained IP67-rated. The interchangeable lenses featured a germanium window that sealed and attached seamlessly to the camera housing, ensuring the system remained IP67-rated. The cable enabled the camera to draw enough power from the tablet, so no auxiliary power source was needed. Additionally, the tablet provided a method of data storage, allowing still images and video capture. The result was a fully portable, IP67 rated, infrared camera system with adjustable lenses that accurately monitored bats in their natural habitat. The North American Industry Classification System Code (NAICS) for this requirement is 333316 with the size standard of 1250 employees. The Federal Supply Code (FSC) / Product Service Code (PSC) procurement is 5836. Federal notice (Special Notice), DEPT OF DEFENSE.DEPT OF THE ARMY.W2SD ENDIST BALTIMORE
Title: Notice of Intent - Sole Source Award to Time Manufacturing Co.
Solicitation number: W912DR26X1CCG0
PSC: 3920; NAICS: 333998
Description: The purpose of this special notice is to issue notice of intent to restrict competition for certain commercial products under the simplified acquisition threshold. The Washington Aqueduct has a requirement for the acquisition and delivery of one Versalift SST-40-EIH insulated end-mounted 40 ft. 12.2m telescopic aerial platform lift 45 ft. working height, 27 ft. 9 in. horizontal reach with a 50 kV rated liner and cover, fully integrated and installed on a 2026 Ford F-550 Reg Cab 4x4 chassis with a 132 inches long x 40 inches high x 94 inches wide service body, associated accessories, and delivery to Washington, DC. Authority to Restrict Competition: 41 U.S.C. 1901: Simplified acquisition procedures, as implemented by RFO 12.102. Reason for Authority Cited: RFO 12.102a allows the Contracting Officer KO to restrict competition when procuring commercial products under the SAT when they determine that only one source is reasonably available to fulfill the requirement. The Government requires an insulated aerial lift vehicle tested and certified for electrical work at 46 KV and below in accordance with ANSI A92.2 requirements to support immediate utility, maintenance, and facility operations. Standard manufacturing lead times for a custom-built chassis and integrated aerial lift of this magnitude typically span several months to over a year. According to market research, contractor Time Manufacturing Co, a large business, has an exact, fully compliant unit in stock and available for immediate delivery. Procuring this specific in-stock unit avoids the extensive operational delays and administrative costs associated with a lengthy manufacturing process, directly satisfying the Governments critical schedule. Because no other known contractor has a fully compliant, certified vehicle in stock and available for immediate delivery, it is determined that only one source is reasonably available to provide this commercial product valued below the SAT.

Title: Intent to Sole Source Thomas Electronics Cathode Ray Tubes
Solicitation number: FA480926Q0086
PSC: 6625; NAICS: 334519
Description: Notice of Intent to Sole-Source: The 4th Contracting Squadron at Seymour Johnson AFB, NC intends to award a non-competitive firm fixed priced purchase order to Thomas Electronics, Inc. The requirement is for Cathode Ray Tubes that adhere to the existing F3I parent assembly constraints. The specified part is identified as Part Number 08M352P43. The statutory authority permitting other than full and open competition for this acquisition is 10 U.S.C. 2304(c)(1) and RFO Part 12.102(a). The original equipment manufacturer, Thomas Electronics, retains full intellectual property (IP) rights for the design and manufacturing of Part Number 08M352P43. As a result of these proprietary rights, Thomas Electronics is the sole source supplier to Air Force and other government-contracted entities. Comprehensive market research was conducted to identify alternative sourcing avenues. This investigation confirmed that no other manufacturers produce a compatible unit. Furthermore, an exhaustive search for suitable substitute part numbers yielded no viable alternatives. Thomas Electronics was identified as the only supplier capable of fulfilling this requirement. Procurement must be directed to Thomas Electronics on a sole-source basis. This is because Thomas Electronics is the only responsible source, and no other type of supplies will satisfy the agency's requirements due to the proprietary nature of the required part. The manufacturer's intellectual property rights prevent the development and sourcing of alternative parts from other suppliers. To address the long-term constraints of this sole-source situation, we will continue to invest in monthly sustainment efforts. These efforts will include working closely with the Systems Program Office and WRALC/WAQ to explore and refine potential alternative avenues for future procurement. THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR COMPETITIVE OFFERS, and a solicitation will not be issued. All responsible sources may submit a capability statement, proposal, or quotation, which shall be considered by the agency. Any response to this notice must show clear and convincing evidence that competition of this requirement would be advantageous to the Government. All responsible sources may submit a capability statement, proposal, or quotation, which shall be considered by the agency. If no affirmative written response is received, the award will be made without further notice. Oral communications are not acceptable in response to this notice. 5. Rationale Justifying Use of Authority Cited: The Nidek Global refraction equipment (branded as Marco
Lombart EPIC 6100 Refraction Workstation and TRS-6100) is being requested as a sole source purchase
due to its required compatibility and integration with the ophthalmology diagnostic equipment currently
in use within our department, combined with the manufacturer's exclusive distribution network.
The department has recently acquired new Marco Lombart autorefractors, which are designed to
integrate directly with the EPIC 6100 workstation and the RT 6100 M Photosphere, Head and Digital
Refraction System. The EPIC 6100 provides a centralized, integrated platform for performing refractions
and transferring patient measurements and data between the autorefractors and the digital refraction
system. Purchasing this exact workstation will allow us to fully utilize the functionality of the new
autorefractors and maintain an integrated ophthalmic examination workflow. The workstation is
specifically designed to communicate with and support the existing equipment, reducing the need for
duplicate data entry, minimizing potential transcription errors, and improving efficiency and consistency
in the patient examination process.
An alternative workstation from another manufacturer will not provide the direct integration or
interoperability required with the existing government-owned systems. Selecting an incompatible or
non-integrated workstation would require additional software, interfaces, manual data entry, or
workflow modifications, resulting in increased costs and reduced operational efficiency. Standardizing
the refraction equipment on this platform also provides continuity with the equipment already
purchased, allows staff to utilize a consistent workflow, and maximizes the value and functionality of our
existing ophthalmology equipment investment.
Because Nidek Global manufactures these items and Marco Lombart is the sole authorized distributor
able to sell them in North America, no other vendors are authorized to fulfill this requirement.
Therefore, this action must be executed as a Sole Source procurement.
6. Efforts to Obtain Competition: In accordance with RFO guidelines, the solicitation will be completed as
a Sole Source acquisition since Marco Lombart is the exclusive North American distributor for the
required Nidek Global equipment. To increase transparency and market visibility, a Notice of Intent to
Sole Source will be published to SAM.gov. Furthermore, to promote future transparency, a redacted
copy of this finalized J&A will be posted to SAM.gov following the contract award.

barriers to competition for future requirements, the Government will continuously conduct market
research to determine if alternative commercial ophthalmic refraction platforms achieve FDA clearance
and warranty-backed compatibility with current autorefractors. The Contracting Activity will also

CUI
Department of the Air Force: Justification for Other Than Full and Open Competition
I. Agency and Contracting Activity (RFO 6.104-1(a)(1)):
Agency: Air Combat Command (ACC)
Contracting Activity: 99th Contracting Squadron, Nellis Air Force Base, NV 89191.
II. Nature and/or description of the action being approved (RFO 6.104-1(a)(2)):
This document approves the award of a purchase order on a sole source basis to SSK Military Industries, Inc. for Cybernetic
Parachute Release System/Automatic Activation Device (CYPRES/AAD) in support of the 414th Combat Training Squadron,
Nellis AFB, NV 89191. This justification is made on an individual basis.
III. Description of supplies/services required to meet agency needs (RFO 6.104-1(a)(3)):
The CYPRES/AAD is a backup safety device that automatically deploys a reserve parachute when a jumper is in free-fall too
low to the ground, it uses electronic altitude and speed sensing to fire a cutter in emergencies and deploy the parachute.
The military version is built to operate in pressurized aircraft and accept programmable altitude offsets for remote drop
zones. CYPRE/AAD is the only device that meets mission needs as defined per AFI 10-3503.
Estimated value (no options):
Appropriation and funding: Operations & Maintenance (O&M), 3400
Anticipated contract type: Purchase Order
Major items and associated quantities: [Qty. 10] Military EC Cypress-2 1-Pin Changeable- w/LTM.
[Qty. 1] Military EC Cypress Data Collector
[Qty. 1] Military EC Cypress IR Remote
IV. Statutory Authority Permitting Other Than Full and Open Competition (RFO 6.104-1(a)(4)):
10 U.S.C. 3204(a)(1), Only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements.
V. Rationale for Use of Authority (RFO 6.104-1(a)(5)):
Airtec GmbH is the sole manufacturer of the required parachute release system, and its products are distributed exclusively
through SSK Military Industries, Inc.
VI. Integrated Market Analysis and Efforts to Solicit Competition (RFO 6.104-1(a)(6), (8), and (10)):
A search on USASPENDING.gov revealed that the Department of War awarded similar contracts solely to SSK Military
Industries Inc. The sole sourced contracts are the following: W56HZV21F0097 / FA441722P0053 / FA486123P0056 /
FA940123P0077 / FA486123P0114 / FA486124P0025 / FA441824P0045 / FA487724P0056 and FA940125P0058. Additionally,

6. Reason for Authority Cited:
a. Background: Anatomage Inc. is the sole developer, owner, and exclusive licensor
of the Anatomage Table software, associated digital anatomy libraries, and
system-specific updates. The required equipment and support listed above, including
the interactive 3D anatomical datasets, proprietary imaging models, and integrated
instructional modules—are not available from any other source. This equipment will be
used in identifying, assessing, and engaging qualified medical professionals for Army
service. This capability is needed to enhance the Brigade’s outreach, education, and
demonstration efforts by providing medically accurate, interactive anatomical content
that aligns with modern medical training environments. The Anatomage platform
enables the Government to demonstrate Army medical career pathways, illustrate
clinical concepts to prospective recruits, and support recruiting events with advanced,
immersive medical visualization tools.
Anatomage Inc is the sole provider of the equipment and support listed above. Their
company’s proprietary system provides medically accurate, interactive 3D anatomy
models aligned with current medical school curricula and clinical training standards.
These capabilities are essential for effectively engaging prospective medical
professionals and demonstrating the Army’s advanced medical training environment.
b. Alternatives. Anatomage Inc. is the sole developer, manufacturer, and exclusive
licensor of the Anatomage Table software, digital anatomy libraries, and associated
system updates. The system operates on a closed, proprietary architecture, and no
third-party vendors are authorized to provide software renewals, content updates, or
technical support. As a result, only Anatomage Inc. can meet the Government’s
requirements. Anatomage is the sole distributer of their products in the United States,
there are no authorized resellers per their website.
3
Control No.: KNOX-SAT-2026-0144
c. Impact if justification not approved: Failure to approve this action would result in
a reduction in the capabilities of the Medical Recruiting Brigade. A reduction in
capability would result in a reduction in outreach for potential Army soldiers. The
Anatomage digital anatomy platform, which is essential for conducting effective medical
recruiting, outreach, and educational engagements. Without the Anatomage system, the
Brigade would be unable to demonstrate modern, medically accurate anatomical
content that aligns with current medical school curricula—significantly reducing its ability
to engage and attract qualified medical professionals.
7. Efforts to Obtain Competition: The Contracting Officer shall publish the notices
required by FAR 5.101.
a. Effective competition: The research confirmed that no other vendor can provide
Anatomage hardware or software environment. The Anatomage platform operates on
proprietary architecture, and Anatomage Inc. is the sole developer, manufacturer, and
exclusive licensor of the required software updates, content libraries, and technical
support. No third-party vendors are authorized to provide these services.
b. Subcontracting competition: Because this requirement is based on proprietary
technology for which Anatomage Inc. is the sole developer, manufacturer, and exclusive
licensor, opportunities for subcontracting competition are inherently limited. The
required software updates, digital anatomy content, and technical support can only be
performed by Anatomage personnel due to the proprietary nature of the system and the
company’s exclusive control over its intellectual property, source code, and digital
anatomy datasets.
8. Actions to Increase Competition: Although the current requirement is proprietary
to Anatomage, the Government remains committed to promoting competition to the
maximum extent practicable. The following actions will be taken to increase competition
for future requirements.
a. Conduct recurring market research at least annually to identify emerging
technologies, new vendors, or evolving capabilities in the digital anatomy and
virtual dissection market. This includes reviewing industry publications, attending
medical technology conferences, and monitoring academic medical simulation
trends.
b. Engage with industry through Requests for Information (RFIs), Sources Sought
notices, and vendor capability inquiries to determine whether any new entrants
can provide comparable or interoperable systems.
9. Market Research:. Market research was conducted within the past 12 months in
accordance with FAR Part 10 and DFARS 210.001 to identify all qualified sources
capable of meeting the Medical Recruiting Brigade’s requirement for the Anatomage
hardware and support. The research included a review of industry capabilities via Digital
Marketplace and vendor outreach via emails with manufacturer. Market research

capable of supplying the required equipment and support. A SONA approval

directly to Anatomage, the manufacturer, and they confirmed it has no authorized third-
party resellers, establishing Anatomage as the only source able to provide the required
equipment and support.

Portland District, U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (COE), Bonneville Lock and Dam project requires
the purchase of Miller ProHeat 35 Induction Heating System, including essential accessories and
on-site training, to support critical welding operations for powerhouse infrastructure maintenance
and repair, specifically Headgate and Tail Log repairs.

weld standards.

Description: NOTICE OF INTENT TO SOLE SOURCE: This notice is being published in accordance with Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO) Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Subpart 5.101 requiring dissemination of information for proposed contract actions. This is a Notice of Intent to award a sole source contract and is not a request for competitive quotes/proposals. The Defense Health Agency Contracting Activity Healthcare Contracting Division, Southeast (DHACA-HCD-SE) is issuing this Notice of Intent (NOI) to inform industry contractors of the Government�s intent to execute a Sole Source contract under RFO FAR 6.103-1, Only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements. This notice satisfies posting requirements at FAR Part 5.101. The intended contractor is Ivoclar Vivadent, Incorporated, who is identified as a sole proprietor. The place of delivery/service is U.S. Army Dental Laboratory, Eisenhower Army Medical Center, 300 E Hospital Rd Bldg, 322, Fort Gordon, Georgia. This requirement is for a non-personal services contract with a performance period consisting of a one-year base period and four (4) one-year option periods. The contractor shall provide installation, delivery, and preventative and corrective maintenance support for the PrograMill PM7 Dental Milling System. The contractor shall accomplish the installation of the base system and its scope of delivery (including the PrograMill Suction Unit, CAM software, PC/Monitor, and all associated accessories). Following installation, the contractor shall provide ongoing maintenance to ensure the machine can accurately dry mill zirconia, polymethylmethacrylates (resins), and wax to fabricate inlays, onlays, crowns, bridges, and complete dentures. The contractor shall provide all personnel, equipment, supplies, facilities, transportation, tools, materials, supervision, and other items and non-personal services necessary to deliver, install, and maintain PrograMill 7 Dental Mill System. All supplies, maintenance and technical support services must be in accordance with all federal, state, and local laws, including all regulations, manufacturers recommended standards, and commercial requirements. The Contractor must have a current/approved Authority to Operate (ATO) certificate from Defense Health Agency (DHA) for the specific model of system being submitted. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) for this requirement is 339114, Dental Equipment and Supplies Manufacturing. The Product/Service Code (PSC) is 6520. No solicitation document is available, and telephone requests will not be honored. No award will be made based on unsolicited quotations or offers received in response to this notice. The intent of this synopsis is for informational purposes only. Information received will normally be considered solely for the purpose of determining whether to conduct a competitive procurement. A determination by the Government to not compete this action based on this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. All inquiries and concerns must be addressed in writing via email to Brittany Belsches at brittany.n.belsches.civ@health.mil and Lenore Paseda at lenore.y.paseda.civ@health.mil with the following information referenced in the subject line, PrograMill 7 Dental Mill System, Eisenhower Army Medical Center. All interested parties who are responsible, certified, and capable may identify their interest and may submit a Capabilities Statement on company letterhead no later than 10:00AM Eastern Standard Time (EST) August 24, 2026, to the above listed contacts. The interested parties bear full responsibility to ensure complete, timely transmission and confirmation of receipt.

Vendor Questions/Government Answers RFQ 36C24926Q0324
1. CLIN 0003 requires installation of 13 DCI Series 5 track lights and one A-dec 577L
track light, but CLIN 0001 only requires the contractor to furnish 13 DCI lights. Will the
A-dec 577L be Government-furnished, or must it be included in the contractor's price?
Answer: The A-dec 577L track light will be furnished as Government-Furnished Property
(GFP). The Government currently owns this item and will provide it to the Contractor for
installation under CLIN 0003. The Contractor is not required to furnish or include the
cost of the A-dec 577L in its proposed price. CLIN 0001 remains limited to the 13 DCI
Series 5 track lights, as written.
2. The instructions require a Salient Characteristics Compliance Matrix “below,” but no
matrix appears in the solicitation. May offerors create and submit their own matrix
addressing each characteristic?
Answer: Yes. If the referenced matrix is not included in the solicitation, offerors may
create and submit their own Salient Characteristics Compliance Matrix, provided it
addresses each listed characteristic and clearly identifies whether the offered product
"Meets" or "Does Not Meet" each requirement. Alternatively, offerors may use the matrix
template attached at the bottom of this document/amendment.
3. Page 30 directs offerors to complete VAAR 852.219-75 for services and construction,
while the solicitation contains VAAR 852.219-76 for supplies and products. Please
confirm that offerors should complete and return 852.219-76.
Answer: Offerors shall complete and return VAAR 852.219-76 (the version applicable to
supplies/products), as included in the solicitation. The reference to VAAR 852.219-75
on page 30 is in error and will be corrected by amendment. Offerors should disregard
the page 30 reference to 852.219-75 and complete only VAAR 852.219-76.

confirm that files should instead be named using the correct RFQ number,

service for the entire light assembly and related components, and whether the standard
DCI manufacturer warranty satisfies this requirement.
6. For VAAR 852.219-76 compliance, has the Government determined that DCI is a
domestic small-business manufacturer, or is an SBA nonmanufacturer-rule waiver
applicable to this acquisition?
Answer: NAICS 339114 (Dental Equipment and Supplies Manufacturing) is covered
under an SBA-approved class waiver of the nonmanufacturer rule. Accordingly, an
SDVOSB nonmanufacturer offeror may supply the product of any manufacturer
(including a large business) and still qualify as compliant with the nonmanufacturer rule
under this set-aside, provided the offeror otherwise meets all other applicable SDVOSB
and small business nonmanufacturer requirements (e.g., primarily engaged in
retail/wholesale trade, normally sells the type of item supplied, takes
ownership/possession of the item with its personnel, etc.). A separate Government
determination regarding DCI's specific size status as a manufacturer is therefore not
required for offerors relying on the class waiver.

STATEMENT OF REQUIREMENT (SOR)
Procurement of Automotive Air Conditioning System Trainers (Model N98-ND9130)
Naval Construction Training Center (NCTC) Port Hueneme, California
1. Purpose
The purpose of this procurement is to purchase six (6) Automotive Air Conditioning System
Trainers, Model N98-ND9130, manufactured by NADA Scientific, to support training operations
within the Construction Mechanic (CM) "C" School Automotive Air Conditioning course (CIN
A-610-0052) at Naval Construction Training Center (NCTC), Port Hueneme, California.
2. Scope of Work
The contractor shall provide six (6) new Automotive Air Conditioning System Trainers (Model
N98-ND9130), including all manufacturer-standard components, accessories, documentation, and
operational materials required for full training capability. Equipment shall be factory new, fully
assembled, and ready for instructional use upon delivery.
3. Equipment Description
The Automotive Air Conditioning System Trainer is a complete automotive HVA C training
platform mounted on a chassis frame designed for instruction in the operation, maintenance,
diagnostics, troubleshooting, and repair of modern automotive air conditioning systems.
4. Technical Requirements
• Integrated R134a automotive air conditioning system
• Piston compressor
• Condenser assembly
• Evaporator unit
• Expansion valve
• Pressure switch
• Thermostat
• Dehydrating filter
• Fault simulation capability for instructional troubleshooting exercises
• Troubleshooting device capable of simulating multiple system faults
• Mounted training platform on stand with wheels for mobility
• Clear instructional layout allowing component identification and diagnostics
• Maximum power consumption approximately 2 kW
5. Electrical Requirements
The trainer shall operate electrically and be compatible with a 220V electrical supply. Electrical
configuration shall be suitable for training laboratory installation.

matters.agency: National Institute of Standards and Technology
matters.text:
Federal notice (Sources Sought), COMMERCE, DEPARTMENT OF.NATIONAL INSTITUTE OF STANDARDS AND TECHNOLOGY.DEPT OF COMMERCE NIST
Title: Combined Sources Sought Notice and Notice of Intent to Award a Sole Source Contract for ScanWave Pro electronic controller for a Vero AFM
Solicitation number: NB643090-26-01166
PSC: 6625; NAICS: 334515
Description: BACKGROUND The Office of Acquisition and Agreements Management (OAAM), Acquisition Management Division (AMD), of the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST), on behalf of the NIST Material Measurement Laboratory (MML), intends to negotiate on a sole source basis with PrimeNano Inc., 4701 Patrick Henry Drive, Building 8, Santa Clara, CA 95054 (UEI: K2RLBZKD2CX7), for the acquisition of one ScanWave Pro electronic controller for NIST's existing scanning Microwave Impedance Microscopy (sMIM) module installed on an Oxford Instruments/Asylum Research Vero Atomic Force Microscope (AFM). NIST requires a ScanWave Pro electronic controller that is fully compatible with the Government-owned Vero AFM and existing ScanWave 2.0� Probe Interface. The controller will replace the existing modular electronics assembly currently used with the sMIM module. The existing assembly consists of a microwave electronics box, power supply, temperature controller, and reflectometer calibrator and is more than ten years old. Additionally, the existing power supply and reflectometer calibrator are currently on loan to NIST from Oxford Instruments/Asylum Research. The required ScanWave Pro electronic controller shall provide the hardware, software, and accessories necessary to operate with NIST's existing ScanWave 2.0� Probe Interface and Vero AFM. The requirement includes the ScanWave Pro electronic controller, reflectometer, calibration sample, Windows 11-compatible ScanWave software, associated documentation, installation and integration with the existing Vero AFM and ScanWave 2.0� Probe Interface, and training for up to two (2) NIST personnel. The Contractor shall deliver the required equipment, software, and documentation within sixty (60) calendar days after award. Installation and integration of the ScanWave Pro electronic controller with the Government-owned Vero AFM and existing ScanWave 2.0� Probe Interface shall be completed within ten (10) calendar days after delivery. Training for up to two (2) NIST personnel shall also be completed within ten (10) calendar days after delivery. Sole source determination is based on the following: The ScanWave Pro electronic controller is manufactured by PrimeNano Inc. and is specifically designed for operation with PrimeNano's ScanWave 2.0� Probe Interface and sMIM technology. NIST currently owns a ScanWave 2.0� Probe Interface that is integrated with its Oxford Instruments/Asylum Research Vero AFM. The required electronic controller must be fully compatible with this existing Government-owned equipment and preserve the sMIM measurement functionality of the existing system. The existing sMIM electronics are more than ten years old and do not provide the measurement sensitivity required for NIST's current nanoscale impedance characterization work. The ScanWave Pro provides the required improved measurement sensitivity while maintaining compatibility with NIST's existing ScanWave 2.0� Probe Interface and Vero AFM. Market research identified other manufacturers of scanning probe microscopy and related impedance measurement equipment; however, no other source was identified that offers an electronic controller capable of directly integrating with NIST's existing PrimeNano ScanWave 2.0� Probe Interface and Vero AFM while satisfying NIST's required sMIM functionality and performance requirements. PrimeNano Inc. has confirmed that it is the sole manufacturer and supplier of the ScanWave Pro electronic controller and that there are no authorized resellers for this product. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for this acquisition is 334515 � Instrument Manufacturing for Measuring and Testing Electricity and Electrical Signals, with a small business size standard of 750 employees. No solicitation package will be issued. This Notice of Intent is not a request for competitive quotations; however, responsible sources that believe they can satisfy the Government's requirements may submit a written capability statement demonstrating their ability to furnish the complete requirement. Capability statements shall specifically address the respondent's ability to: Furnish an electronic controller that is fully compatible with NIST's existing PrimeNano ScanWave 2.0� Probe Interface and Oxford Instruments/Asylum Research Vero AFM without replacement or modification of the existing Government-owned probe interface; Provide the required sMIM measurement functionality and performance, including the hardware, software, reflectometer, calibration sample, and other components necessary to provide a complete and operational solution; Provide software compatible with the Government's Windows 11 operating environment; Install and integrate the proposed electronic controller with NIST's existing Vero AFM and ScanWave 2.0� Probe Interface within ten (10) calendar days after delivery; and Provide training for up to two (2) NIST personnel within ten (10) calendar days after delivery. Respondents shall identify any additional hardware, software, interfaces, modifications, licenses, Government-furnished information, or other resources that would be required to integrate the respondent's proposed solution with NIST's existing Vero AFM and ScanWave 2.0� Probe Interface. Responses must be received by August 14, 2026. A determination by the Government not to compete the proposed acquisition based upon responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. Information received will normally be considered solely for the purpose of determining whether to conduct a competitive procurement.
