Description: BACKGROUND The National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) is conducting market research to identify alternative sources that (a) are capable of meeting NIST�s minimum requirements for the following commercial products and commercial services and (b) would be interested in competing for that requirement: NIST requires one (1) scanning Microwave Impedance Microscopy (sMIM) electronic controller to support nanoscale impedance property measurements for research conducted by Division 643. The required controller will integrate with the Government-owned Vero Atomic Force Microscope (AFM) through the existing ScanWave 2.0� Probe Interface module and will replace the current modular assembly consisting of a microwave electronics unit, power supply, temperature controller, and reflectometer calibrator. The required system shall provide enhanced nanoscale impedance characterization capabilities while maintaining compatibility with the Government's existing Vero AFM configuration. The controller must support direct impedance measurements of material samples and enable integration of electrical characterization with the Vero AFM's existing multimodal measurement capabilities, including current, surface potential, capacitance, piezoelectric, thermal, and mechanical (elastic and plastic) characterization techniques. At a minimum, the required electronic controller shall: Be fully compatible with the Government-owned Vero AFM and the existing ScanWave 2.0� Probe Interface module without requiring replacement or modification of the existing interface. Provide scanning Microwave Impedance Microscopy (sMIM) capability for direct nanoscale impedance measurements. Replace the existing modular microwave electronics assembly with a single integrated electronic controller. Provide substantially improved measurement sensitivity over the existing measurement configuration (approximately a tenfold increase in sensitivity). Integrate with the existing customized Vero AFM holder and associated instrumentation to preserve current system functionality and research workflows. Be capable of supporting multimodal characterization in conjunction with the Vero AFM's existing electrical, mechanical, thermal, and piezoelectric measurement capabilities. Include the manufacturer's standard commercial warranty. The Government intends to acquire only the equipment identified above. Installation, training, and any associated support services shall be provided as customarily offered under the manufacturer's standard commercial terms, as applicable. matters.text:
Federal notice (Combined Synopsis/Solicitation), DEPT OF DEFENSE.DEPT OF THE AIR FORCE.FA9302  AFTC PZZ
Title: Notice of Intent to Sole Source: F-16 FINS Aviation Power Converters (Champion Aerospace)
Solicitation number: F1S0AY6191A001
PSC: 6125; NAICS: 336413
Description: NOTICE OF INTENT TO SOLE SOURCE 1. Action Code: Combined Synopsis/Solicitation 2. Date: 13th Aug 2026 3. Year: 2026 4. Contracting Office Zip Code: 93524 5. Product or Service Code: 6125 (Converters, Electrical, Nonrotating) 6. Contracting Office Address: AFTC/PZZF, Edwards AFB, CA 7. Subject: F-16 FINS Aviation Power Converters 8. Proposed Solicitation Number:F1S0AY6191A001 9. Closing Response Date: 17th Aug, 2026 at 12:00 PM Pacific Time 10. Contact Point:Josiah Broadway, Josiah.broadway@us.af.mil 11. Description: The Air Force Test Center (AFTC), Edwards AFB, CA, intends to award a Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) Sole Source Purchase Order to S3 Aerodefense (CAGE: 4GPC1) for four (4) Champion Aerospace 28VS50Y-30 Aviation Power Converters. This action is conducted under the authority of 41 U.S.C. 1901, as implemented by RFO FAR 12.102(a), which authorizes restricted competition for acquisitions valued at or below the Simplified Acquisition Threshold (SAT) when only one source is reasonably available. This notice serves as a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial products in accordance with RFO Part 12. A separate written solicitation will not be issued. Requirement Baseline: The F-16 FINS project requires a Commercial Off-the-Shelf (COTS) direct drop-in replacement for the inactive military power supply. To prevent cost-prohibitive structural and wiring modifications to the F-16 avionics bay, the procurement is restricted to the Champion Aerospace 28VS50Y-30. Market research dictates this is the only known commercial unit providing the exact Form, Fit, and Function (F3) equivalent, specifically: Form: Strict compliance with the 9.5" x 4.6" x 4.2" F-16 avionics bay envelope. Fit: Native integration with the existing legacy MS27472E16B8P receptacle. Function: Fully compliant with MIL-C-7115F power conversion, ripple, and surge tolerances. Instructions to Industry: This Notice of Intent is NOT a request for competitive quotes. The Government intends to solicit and negotiate with only one source. However, any responsible firm that believes it manufactures a COTS product meeting these exact F3 specifications may submit a capability statement or quotation prior to the closing date. Generic marketing material will be discarded. To be considered, submissions must include detailed mechanical drawings, pinout configurations, and MIL-C-7115F testing certifications proving the unit is an exact drop-in equivalent. A determination by the Government not to compete this proposed contract based upon responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Contracting Officer. Attachments: Redacted Single Source Justification (D&F)

Single Source Justification (Simplified Acquisition)
Section A: General Contract Information
Is this a Bridge Action as defined in the AF Bridge Action Reduction Plan? Yes No
Contracting Activity: 700th Contracting Squadron
Project/Program Name: Parts for Stripe Hog Truck
Purchase Request / Local ID Number: F3N0426147A001
Estimated Contract Cost (including Options): $60,000.00
Section B: Description of the Supplies/Services Required
The 435th Construction and Training Squadron performs runway marking and rubber removal at eight to
ten Air Force bases in Europe. The high pressure pump, blower and sprocket of one of our rubber removal
trucks broke down and need to be replaced to resume our rubber removal missions at full capacity.
The affected vehicle is the rubber removal truck, Make: MAN SH8000 Stripe Hog
Required Parts:
1 EACH - High Pressure Pump, Power, End, 4200, Gen 2, RH, Y. Item No. 32384
1 EACH - Blower, 6", Tuthill. Item No. 30720
1 EACH - Sprocket, 14MX-36S-37, 2517. Item No. 60711
Section C: Justification for Soliciting from a Single Source or Brand Name
The product is proprietary to Jetstream / Federal Signal and protected by US patent
6,126,524 and Hog technologies / Federal Signal US patent 7,798,158 B2.
The vehicles from Hog Technologies are specialized vehicles and are only manufactured by the company
STRIPE Hog. They contain vehicle-specific parts that can only be supplied with the required quality by this
manufacturer. Other competitors cannot provide or manufacture these parts because they are not
compatible or of sufficient quality to work effectively with the existing technology of our vehicles.
The vehicles operate at a water pressure of 2700 bar. It is essential to ensure that the parts meet these
requirements to prevent injuries or damage to both personnel and machinery, which could lead to
downtime and high maintenance costs.
If the Rubber Removal Trucks fail to function, rubber buildup on the runways at "Theater Wide" Air Bases
could compromise tire grip for aircraft in the touchdown zone, posing a safety hazard for the aircraft and
its crew. Purchasing these original spare parts ensures that the vehicles remain operational during their
deployment across Europe, avoiding delays that could impact flight operations and the missions of various
bases.
The vehicle requires the use of proprietary parts approved by the manufacturer, as using non-approved or
third-party components would void the warranty and may result in incompatibility or damage; the vehicle
costs approximately $997,094.69 (GSA price), and the delivery time is currently unknown and may take

several years.
Section D: Efforts to Obtain Competition
We conducted market research and contacted several vendors. The vendors we contacted then reached
out to company Stripe Hog who in return contacted us and sent us a sole source justification, explaining
why we should only purchase the required parts through them. There is no cost benefit to be achieved by
going outside of Jetstream / Hog Technologies.
Section E: Steps to Preclude Future Single Source or Brand Name Awards
700 CONS will keep researching for when other brands become authorized to provide the products and
services to fulfill the future requirements. We are consistently exploring new sources and will continue
searching for additional companies on GSA. In addition, 700 CONS will continue its ongoing market
research to monitor the market situation for potential sources for future procurements.
Section F: Contracting Officer's Determination
I have determined, in accordance with FAR 13.106-1(b)(1), that the circumstances of this contract action deem only a
single source is reasonably available.

Federal notice (Presolicitation), DEPT OF DEFENSE.DEPT OF THE AIR FORCE.FA8224  AFSC OL H PZIM
Title: NOTICE OF INTENT TO AWARD A HUBZONE SOLE SOURCE: E-6 Portable Automated Test Set (PATS)70-A Fuel Quantity Indicating System (FQIS) Build-to-Print Kits
Solicitation number: FA822226225KH
PSC: 5935; NAICS: 334417
Description: NOTICE OF INTENT TO AWARD A HUBZONE SOLE SOURCE 1. GENERAL INFORMATION: The Department of the Air Force, Air Force Materiel Command (AFMC), AFSC OL:H/PZIEB at Hill AFB, intends to award a sole-source, firm-fixed-price contract for the manufacturing and delivery of custom E-6 Portable Automated Test Set (PATS)70-A Fuel Quantity Indicating System (FQIS) Build-to-Print Kits. 2. STATUTORY AUTHORITY: This sole-source acquisition is issued under the statutory authority of 15 U.S.C. 657a, as implemented by FAR 6.302-5 (Authorized or Required by Statute), FAR 19.203 (Relationship among small business programs), and FAR 19.1306 (HUBZone sole source awards). 3. INTENDED SOURCE: The Government intends to award this contract to Cherokee Nation Aerospace Defense, an active SBA-certified HUBZone small business concern (UEI: MDECKDN1HW18, CAGE Code: 82ML8). 4. DESCRIPTION OF REQUIREMENT: The contractor shall manufacture, test, and deliver 7 custom E-6 Portable Automated Test Set (PATS)70-A Fuel Quantity Indicating System (FQIS) Build-to-Print Kits in accordance with the Government's Technical Data Package (TDP). These cables are critical to diagnosing 16 aircraft components on Navy aircraft, E-6, the Boeing Airborne Command and Control aircraft, and require highly specialized manufacturing capabilities to ensure compatibility with existing legacy enclaves. The total estimated value of this contract action is $400,000.00, with a performance period of 25 weeks after receipt of order. 5. MARKET RESEARCH & JUSTIFICATION: A public Request for Information (RFI) / Sources Sought Notice was previously published on SAM.gov under Notice ID FA8228260159KH. Based on the technical evaluation of the responses received, only the intended source possesses the required technical capability, tooling, and certified quality controls to meet the immediate delivery schedule of the Air Force. The Contracting Officer has determined there is not a reasonable expectation of receiving competitive offers from two or more HUBZone concerns. 6. RESPONSE INSTRUCTIONS (DISCLAIMER): This notice of intent is NOT a request for competitive proposals or quotes, and no competitive solicitation package will be publicly issued. However, any responsible HUBZone source that believes it can meet the Government's requirement may submit a written technical capability statement demonstrating its ability to manufacture and deliver identical, fully compliant cables. Responses must be submitted via email to the Primary Point of Contact listed below no later than 8/28/2026 at 4:00 PM MST. A determination by the Government not to compete this proposed contract based upon responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. Information received will normally be considered solely for the purpose of determining whether to conduct a competitive procurement in the future. Federal notice (Special Notice), DEPT OF DEFENSE.DEPT OF THE NAVY.NAVSUP FLT LOG CTR  SAN DIEGO
Title: Notice of Intent for Sole Source for NADA SCIENTIFIC N98-ND9130
Solicitation number: N0024426Q0072
PSC: 4910; NAICS: 333618
Description: NOTICE OF INTENT THIS IS A NOTICE OF INTENT TO AWARD A SOLE SOURCE CONTRACT AND IS NOT A REQUEST FOR COMPETITIVE QUOTES Naval Supply Systems Command (NAVSUP) Fleet Logistics Center San Diego (FLCSD) intends to award a firm fixed price contract under the authority of FAR 13.106-1(b)(1)(i); Only One Source Responsibly Available and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements to: NADA SCIENTIFIC LIMITED, 39 BUTTERNUT ST, CHAMPLAIN, NY 12919-5123, for six (6) Automotive Air Conditioning System Trainers, Model N98-ND9130, manufactured by NADA Scientific, to support training operations within the Construction Mechanic (CM) "C" School Automotive Air Conditioning course (CIN A-610-0052) at Naval Construction Training Center (NCTC), Port Hueneme, California. The items are listed in the Resource Requirement List (RRL) and no other vendor can supply the NADA Scientific Automotive Air Conditioning System Trainer for CM "C" School for Automotive Air Conditioning. Acquiring equipment outside the RRL would require curriculum modification, instructor retraining, and revision of course materials, resulting in unacceptable delays to personnel training and potentially disrupt the Navy�s training pipeline. The anticipated award date of this action is on or before 17 August 2026. The applicable NAICS code is 336390. This notice of intent is not a request for competitive proposals and no solicitation document exists for the requirement. Sources interested in responding to this notice are required to submit a capability statement that includes management and technical data and cost information, in sufficient detail and with convincing evidence that clearly demonstrates the capability to provide the licenses and proof as being an authorized distributor of the product. Capability statements shall not exceed 6 (8.5 x 11 inch) pages using a font size no smaller than 10-point. All capability statements received by the due date of this notice will be considered by the Government. A request for documentation or additional information or submissions that only ask questions will not be considered as an affirmative response. A determination by the Government not to compete based on responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. Information received will be considered solely for the purpose of determining whether to conduct a competitive procurement or to proceed with a sole source purchase order. Capability statements are due by 8:00 AM Pacific Standard Time (PST), 17 August 2026. Capability statements shall be submitted by e-mail ONLY as a Microsoft Word or Adobe PDF attachment to Charles E. Bruce, Contract Negotiator at the following email address at: charles.e.bruce2.civ@us.navy.mil NO TELEPHONE REQUESTS/OFFERS WILL BE HONORED

attachments.text:
STATEMENT OF REQUIREMENT (SOR)
Procurement of Automotive Air Conditioning System Trainers (Model N98-ND9130)
Naval Construction Training Center (NCTC) Port Hueneme, California
1. Purpose
The purpose of this procurement is to purchase six (6) Automotive Air Conditioning System
Trainers, Model N98-ND9130, manufactured by NADA Scientific, to support training operations
within the Construction Mechanic (CM) "C" School Automotive Air Conditioning course (CIN
A-610-0052) at Naval Construction Training Center (NCTC), Port Hueneme, California.
2. Scope of Work
The contractor shall provide six (6) new Automotive Air Conditioning System Trainers (Model
N98-ND9130), including all manufacturer-standard components, accessories, documentation, and
operational materials required for full training capability. Equipment shall be factory new, fully
assembled, and ready for instructional use upon delivery.
3. Equipment Description
The Automotive Air Conditioning System Trainer is a complete automotive HVA C training
platform mounted on a chassis frame designed for instruction in the operation, maintenance,
diagnostics, troubleshooting, and repair of modern automotive air conditioning systems.
4. Technical Requirements
• Integrated R134a automotive air conditioning system
• Piston compressor
• Condenser assembly
• Evaporator unit
• Expansion valve
• Pressure switch
• Thermostat
• Dehydrating filter
• Fault simulation capability for instructional troubleshooting exercises
• Troubleshooting device capable of simulating multiple system faults
• Mounted training platform on stand with wheels for mobility
• Clear instructional layout allowing component identification and diagnostics
• Maximum power consumption approximately 2 kW
5. Electrical Requirements
The trainer shall operate electrically and be compatible with a 220V electrical supply. Electrical
configuration shall be suitable for training laboratory installation.

Title: Notice of Intent to Award a Sole Source Modification
Solicitation number: N0003922D0070_SYNOPSIS
PSC: 5825; NAICS: 334220
Description: The Naval Information Warfare Systems Command (NAVWAR), in support of the Portfolio Acquisition Executive Mission Systems (PAE MS) ? Capability Portfolio Executive (CPE): Comms, Sensor, Electronic Warfare (EW), and Positioning, Navigation, and Timing (PNT) (previously Program Executive Office Command, Control, Communications, Computers and Intelligence (PEO C4I), Communications and Global Positioning System (GPS) Navigation Program Office (PMW/A 170)), intends to award an estimated five (5)-year Period of Performance (PoP) extension to the current five (5) year, sole-source, Indefinite Delivery, Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) contract N00039-22-D-0070 with L3Harris Technologies Incorporated (L3Harris), 1680 University Ave, Rochester, NY 14610, under the authority of 10 U.S.C. 3204(a)(1) and Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 6.103-1, as only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements. PRP is the overarching solution to provide tactical, portable radios for the Navy (USN), Marine Corps (USMC), Air Force (USAF), Army, Coast Guard, and other Stakeholders. PRP provides portable radios with secure waveform capabilities and critical Satellite Communications (SATCOM) to meet the United States Military Services and Agencies requirements. The proposed contract action will provide for the procurement of various tactical portable radios and related ancillary parts that are used as the principal command and control tools for all Naval Forces including Navy Expeditionary Combat Command (NECC) and Naval Special Warfare (NSW); interoperable with already fielded Joint and Coalition/Allied Forces? radios; and provide portable, shipboard emergency communications. The proposed contract extension will utilize the remaining unused ceiling, which equates to an estimated total value of $2.47 Billion (B). L3Harris is the original designer, developer, and manufacturer of tactical portable radios. As such, L3Harris is the only source capable of continued production of the aforementioned tactical portable radios and related ancillary parts. As the sole provider of tactical portable radios meeting the Form, Fit, and Function (FFF) requirements, L3Harris is the only entity capable of fulfilling tactical portable radio requirements without substantial duplication of cost to the Government that is not expected to be recovered through competition and without creating unacceptable program delays in fulfilling the Government?s requirements. This notice of intent is not a request for competitive proposals. A competitive solicitation will not be posted. However, interested parties may submit information identifying their interest and capability to respond. The Government reserves the sole discretion to determine whether to compete this procurement based on the responses received. Responses should be submitted by email no later than fifteen calendar days from the date of this synopsis to the Contract Specialist at blake.a.erickson3.civ@us.navy.mil with courtesy copy to the Contracting Officer at kenneth.b.nickel2.civ@us.navy.mil. Verbal questions will NOT be accepted. Questions will be answered by posting answers to the SAM.gov website; accordingly, questions shall NOT contain proprietary or classified information.

Description: Notice of Intent to Sole Source Soldier Monitoring System (SMS) Life Cycle Management and Sustainment Office: U.S. Army Capabilities Program Executive for Simulation, Training, Testing and Threats (CPE ST3), Orlando, FL 32826-3276 Tentative Product Service Code (PSC): 5825 Radio Navigation Equipment � Except Airborne Tentative NAICS Code: 518210 Data Processing, Hosting, and Related Services Place of Performance: Multiple locations including Fort Benning, GA; West Point, NY; Fort Rucker, AL; Fort Sill, OK; Yuma Proving Ground, AZ; Fort Campbell, KY; Fort Bragg/Camp Mackall, NC. Description The U.S. Army Capabilities Program Executive for Simulation, Training, Testing and Threats (CPE ST3), Product Manager Combat Training Instrumentation Systems (PdM CTIS), intends to award a sole source, firm-fixed-price contract to Black Ohm, 100 S McClintock Dr. Ste 200 Chandler, AZ 85226, under the authority of RFO FAR 6.103-1, Only One Responsible Source and No Other Supplies or Services Will Satisfy Agency Requirements. Background & Objective The Soldier Monitoring System (SMS) is the Army�s materiel solution for Soldier monitoring, safety, and training performance analysis. Military training contains significant inherent risk, which is amplified during individual and isolated training such as land navigation. The SMS reduces these risks by providing persistent/real-time geo-tracking and automated alerts. The objective of this effort is to ensure continuity and delivery of efficient, effective, and quality services of upgraded or new solutions to the nation�s warfighters. Scope of Work The Contractor shall provide life cycle management to ensure SMS technology and equipment are maintained at or above 95% Availability (Ao) and provide necessary support desk capabilities. This effort enables PdM CTIS to perform life cycle management in support of SMS including Continuous Technology Refresh (CTR), technology insertion, concurrency, upgrades, and disposal. Support services required for this effort include maintaining or providing the following components: Monitoring Station (MS): Graphical tracking, device status/alerts, and After-Action Review (AAR) playback. The MS normally consists of a laptop and a network connection. Mobile Monitoring Device (MMD): Portable dismounted devices to monitor and locate Soldiers in the field. MMD normally consists of a tablet and a network connection. Soldier Worn Device (SWD): Small, rugged, waterproof GPS-enabled radios utilizing an LTE network with Soldier-initiated SOS capability. The SWD's built-in GPS transmits precise location and status data over LTE for real-time monitoring. Communication Network and SaaS: The SMS network connects devices via commercial cellular and LoRa to an AWS-hosted SaaS platform, accessible through an intuitive UI. Additional Services: Help desk support, field service, repair/replacement of damaged components, inventory management, training materials, and propagation studies. Period of Performance The anticipated Period of Performance (PoP) consists of one (1) 12-month Base Year and one (1) 12-month Option Year. Cybersecurity & Compliance Requirements The Contractor must ensure solutions incorporate secure engineering principles in accordance with NIST SP 800-160 and meet DoD Risk Management Framework (RMF) requirements to maintain a FedRAMP Moderate Authority to Operate (ATO). Strict compliance with OPSEC, AT Level 1, and CUI handling procedures is required. Submission Instructions / Public Note THIS NOTICE OF INTENT IS NOT A REQUEST FOR COMPETITIVE PROPOSALS. However, interested parties may identify their interest and capability to respond to the requirement or submit proposals. All responses received prior to the stated submission deadline will be considered by the Government. The Government is not responsible for any costs incurred as a result of responding to this notice. A determination by the Government not to compete this proposed contract based upon responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. Information received will normally be considered solely for the purpose of determining whether to conduct a competitive procurement. Capability statements, quotes, or proposals must be submitted electronically via email to the Point of Contact listed below no later than 15 August 2026 at 3:00pm. Contact Information 1. Primary Point of Contact Robert Verica, Contracting Officer Email: robert.j.verica2.civ@army.mil 2. Secondary Point of Contact Denis M. attachments.text:
TITLE: Single Source Acquisition for Slocumb Gate Actuator

The 4th Contracting Squadron, Seymour Johnson AFB, NC intends to award a sole source contract to Delta Scientific Corporation (CAGE: 0AUE0) for the replacement part to a barrier system that is proprietary to this company.
This procurement is for the replacement of an actuator (Model No. MPAI-A4300RM34A) for a proprietary barrier system (HD300EM) at Seymour Johnson AFB. The actuator must be uniquely and specifically configured to be operable within the barrier system. Market research conducted reveals the unique and specific configuration of the actuator that is required is proprietary only to Delta Scientific Corporation. There are no other sources that can calibrate the actuator to correctly deploy and retract as the Slocumb Gate barrier system was awarded to Delta Scientific Corporation.
APPLICABILITY OF AUTHORITY: 
This contract action is for supplies and services for which the Government intends to solicit and 
negotiate with only one source under the authority of R-DFARS 206.103-170, Only one 
responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements. Market 
Research confirms the HD300EM Barrier is a proprietary system, and only the Original Equipment Manufacturer, Delta Scientific Corporation, can supply the fully configured MPAI-A4300RM34A actuator for the barrier system, which otherwise, if incorrectly calibrated may cause significant safety risk to the base populace. 

This notice of intent is not a request for competitive proposals. A determination by the 
Government not to compete this proposed contract lies solely within the discretion of the 
Government. Information received will be considered solely for the purpose of determining 
whether to conduct a competitive requirement.
 
The closing date for responses to this synopsis is 19 July 2026 at 4:30 PM EST. The anticipated 
award date is unknown. For information regarding this purchase, please contact SSgt Ashley Goodwin at ashley.goodwin.2@us.af.mil. All responses must be submitted via email to the point of contact. Telephone inquiries will not be accepted.

attachments.text:
Notice of Intent to Sole Source
HT941026N0104
THIS IS A NOTICE OF INTENT TO AWARD A SOLE SOURCE PURCHASE ORDER
CONTRACT AND IS NOT A REQUEST FOR COMPETITIVE QUOTES. The Defense
Health Agency Contracting Activity (DHACA), Healthcare Contracting Division - West (HCD-
W), Echo Branch intends to negotiate and award a firm-fixed price delivery order contract to
supply SIRTEX MEDICAL, INC., for SIR-Spheres (Yttium-90 Micro Resin Spheres) and
accessories for Madigan Army Medical Center, CA, in accordance with Federal Acquisition
Regulation (FAR) 12.102(b), restricting competition, only one source being available to meet the
Government’s needs to:
SIRTEX MEDICAL, INC.
300 Unicorn Park DR FL 2, Woburn, Massachusetts, 01801-3363
UEI: CWH2GM13A2V6
CAGE: 45EE6
The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for this requirement is
325412 - Pharmaceutical Preparation Manufacturing; the business size standard is 1,3000 (# of
employees). The Product Service Code (PSC) is 3650, chemical and pharmaceutical products
manufacturing machinery.
The requirement is for SIR-Spheres (Yttium-90 Micro Resin Spheres) and accessories for an
emergency surgery, and failure to acquire materials in the time requested will require additional
surgeries, further delaying treatments resulting in negative patient outcomes. SIRTEX
MEDICAL, INC., is the only vendor that is capable of providing the SIR-Spheres and
accessories meet the emergent delivery schedule.
Delivery Location: Madigan Army Medical Center, Bldg. 9040A Jackson Ave., Joint Base Lewis
McChord, WA 98431
Estimated Delivery Date: August 13, 2026
Based on market research and previous acquisition history, it has been determined that SIRTEX
MEDICAL, INC., is the only source that can meet the Government’s specialized requirement.
This notice of intent is not a request for competitive proposals, and no solicitation document
exists for this requirement. Sources interested in responding to this notice are required to submit
a capability statement that includes management and technical data and cost information, in
sufficient detail and with convincing evidence that clearly demonstrates the capability to provide
the required cornea tissue locally. Capability statements shall not exceed six (8.5 x 11 inch)
pages using a font size no smaller than 10-point. All capability statements received by the due
date of this notice will be considered by the Government. A request for documentation or
additional information or submissions that only ask questions will not be considered as an
affirmative response. A determination by the Government not to compete based on responses to
this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. Information received will be
considered solely for the purpose of determining whether to conduct a competitive procurement
or to proceed with a sole source purchase order.
If a vendor challenges the basis of this requirement, please email capability statements as a
Microsoft Word or Adobe PDF attachment to Mariangela Monsalve at
mariangela.j.monsalve.civ@health.mil. The closing date for challenges is no later than 10:00
a.m. Pacific Time, August 25, 2026.
NO TELEPHONE REQUESTS/OFFERS WILL BE HONORED.

29 July 2026
Background & Scope: The USAF School of Aerospace Medicine, Occupational and
Environmental Health (USAFSAM/OEC), requires the procurement of one (1) RSX-1 Sodium
Iodide Radiation Detector, measuring 4" x 4" x 16". This acquisition is critical for enabling
directional radiation source identification and for conducting comprehensive Health Risk
Assessments (HRAs) to protect Air Force personnel from high levels of ionizing radiation.
USAFSAM/OEC currently possesses a single RSX-1 unit. While this detector provides essential
radiation identification and detection capabilities, it lacks the intrinsic ability to determine the
directionality of a radiation source. This limitation necessitates the use of secondary equipment
and time-consuming procedures to locate the origin of radioactive contamination, reducing
operational efficiency and potentially increasing exposure risk.
The acquisition of an additional RSX-1 unit is required to create a networked sensor system. By
operating two identical detectors in tandem, personnel can triangulate and pinpoint the exact
location of radiation sources with speed and precision. This directional capability is mission-
essential for effective contamination control and accurate risk assessment.
The specified 4" x 4" x 16" dimensions and the RSX-1 model are the only specifications that will
ensure seamless integration with existing equipment. Compatibility is paramount for creating the
multi-detector array necessary for achieving the required directional functionality. The use of
any other model would fail to meet this critical interoperability requirement.
Requirements/Salient Characteristics: The proposed system must meet or exceed the
following salient characteristics:
1. Detector Physics and Geometry
• Detector Material: Thallium-activated Sodium Iodide (NaI(Tl)) scintillation crystal.
• Crystal Geometry: Rectangular prism measuring 4 inches x 4 inches x 16 inches (101.6
mm x 101.6 mm x 406.4 mm).
• Active Volume: Minimum of 4.0 Liters (approx. 256 cubic inches) of detection volume
per unit to ensure high geometric sensitivity.
2. Spectroscopic Performance
• Energy Resolution: Must be <8.5% for accurate nuclide identification.
• Energy Range: Must cover a minimum detection range from 20 keV to 3.0 MeV.
• Spectral Output: Must output a fully linearized, high-resolution 1024-channel energy
spectrum.
• Gain Stabilization: Must feature automatic multi-peak gain stabilization utilizing
naturally occurring background isotopes (no external radioactive check sources required
for routine stabilization).
1
3. Signal Processing and Electronics
• Digital Integration: The detector pack must contain an internally integrated Advanced
Digital Spectrometer (ADS) or equivalent digital signal processing (DSP) hardware.
• Throughput & Dead Time: Must be capable of processing high count rates up to
250,000 counts per second (cps) per crystal. System must maintain effectively zero dead-
time under typical environmental background conditions and <20% dead-time at
maximum saturation.
• Linearization: Must support fully linearized spectral summation to allow multiple
detector packs to be combined without degrading the spectrum resolution or distorting the
Poisson distribution.
4. Physical and Environmental Characteristics
• Enclosure: Must be housed in a ruggedized, weather-sealed enclosure (e.g., carbon fiber,
heavy-duty aluminum) designed to withstand severe vibrations and shocks associated
with off-road vehicle or aviation environments.
• Dimensions: Must not exceed approximately 750 mm (L) x 170 mm (W) x 180 mm (H).
• Weight: Total assembly weight must not exceed 25 kg (approx. 55 lbs).
• Operating Temperature: Must operate continuously in extreme field conditions from -
30°C to +45°C.
• Power Consumption: Must be compatible with standard vehicle/aircraft power,
operating on 9–40 VDC and drawing no more than 6 Watts under normal operation.
Deliverables:
• One (1) 4L NaI(Tl) Gamma-Ray Scintillation Detector assembly meeting the
specifications above.
• Manufacturer calibration certificates and initial quality assurance/resolution test results.
• Integration documentation, mechanical interface drawings, and standard digital interface
cables (e.g., Ethernet/USB/Serial as applicable).
2

252.211-7003 ITEM UNIQUE IDENTIFICATION AND VALUATION (JAN 2023)

Definitions. As used in this clause—

“Automatic identification device” means a device, such as a reader or interrogator, used to retrieve data encoded on machine-readable media.

“Concatenated unique item identifier” means—

For items that are serialized within the enterprise identifier, the linking together of the unique identifier data elements in order of the issuing agency code, enterprise identifier, and unique serial number within the enterprise identifier; or

For items that are serialized within the original part, lot, or batch number, the linking together of the unique identifier data elements in order of the issuing agency code; enterprise identifier; original part, lot, or batch number; and serial number within the original part, lot, or batch number.

“Data matrix” means a two-dimensional matrix symbology, which is made up of square or, in some cases, round modules arranged within a perimeter finder pattern and uses the Error Checking and Correction 200 (ECC200) specification found

within International Standards Organization (ISO)/International Electrotechnical Commission (IEC) 16022.

“Data qualifier” means a specified character (or string of characters) that immediately precedes a data field that defines the general category or intended use of the data that follows.

“DoD recognized unique identification equivalent” means a unique identification method that is in commercial use and has been recognized by DoD. All DoD recognized unique identification equivalents are listed
at https://www.acq.osd.mil/asda/dpc/ce/ds/unique-id.html .

“DoD item unique identification” means a system of marking items delivered to DoD with unique item identifiers that have machine-readable data elements to distinguish an item from all other like and unlike items. For items that are serialized within the enterprise identifier, the unique item identifier shall include the data elements of the enterprise identifier and a unique serial number. For items that are serialized within the part, lot, or batch number within the enterprise identifier, the unique item identifier shall include the data elements of the enterprise identifier; the original part, lot, or batch number; and the serial number.

“Enterprise” means the entity (e.g., a manufacturer or vendor) responsible for assigning unique item identifiers to items.

“Enterprise identifier” means a code that is uniquely assigned to an enterprise by an issuing agency.

“Government’s unit acquisition cost” means—

For fixed-price type line, subline, or exhibit line items, the unit price identified in the contract at the time of delivery;

For cost-type or undefinitized line, subline, or exhibit line items, the Contractor’s estimated fully burdened unit cost to the Government at the time of delivery; and

For items produced under a time-and-materials contract, the Contractor’s estimated fully burdened unit cost to the Government at the time of delivery.

“Issuing agency” means an organization responsible for assigning a globally unique identifier to an enterprise, as indicated in the Register of Issuing Agency Codes for ISO/IEC 15459, located at http://www.aimglobal.org/?Reg_Authority15459.

“Issuing agency code” means a code that designates the registration (or controlling) authority for the enterprise identifier.

“Item” means a single hardware article or a single unit formed by a grouping of subassemblies, components, or constituent parts.

“Lot or batch number” means an identifying number assigned by the enterprise to a designated group of items, usually referred to as either a lot or a batch, all of which were manufactured under identical conditions.

“Machine-readable” means an automatic identification technology media, such as bar codes, contact memory buttons, radio frequency identification, or optical memory cards.

“Original part number” means a combination of numbers or letters assigned by the enterprise at item creation to a class of items with the same form, fit, function, and interface.

“Parent item” means the item assembly, intermediate component, or subassembly that has an embedded item with a unique item identifier or DoD recognized unique identification equivalent.
“Serial number within the enterprise identifier” means a combination of numbers, letters, or symbols assigned by the enterprise to an item that provides for the differentiation of that item from any other like and unlike item and is never used again within the enterprise.

“Serial number within the part, lot, or batch number” means a combination of numbers or letters assigned by the enterprise to an item that provides for the differentiation of that item from any other like item within a part, lot, or batch number assignment.

“Serialization within the enterprise identifier” means each item produced is assigned a serial number that is unique among all the tangible items produced by the enterprise and is never used again. The enterprise is responsible for ensuring unique serialization within the enterprise identifier.

“Serialization within the part, lot, or batch number” means each item of a particular part, lot, or batch number is assigned a unique serial number within that part, lot, or batch number assignment. The enterprise is responsible for ensuring unique serialization within the part, lot, or batch number within the enterprise identifier.

“Type designation” means a combination of letters and numerals assigned by the Government to a major end item, assembly or subassembly, as appropriate, to provide a convenient means of differentiating between items having the same basic name and to indicate modifications and changes thereto.

“Unique item identifier” means a set of data elements marked on items that is globally unique and unambiguous. The term includes a concatenated unique item identifier or a DoD recognized unique identification equivalent.

“Unique item identifier type” means a designator to indicate which method of uniquely identifying a part has been used. The current list of accepted unique item identifier types is maintained at https

Commercial Availability Certification:
I have evaluated the commercial marketplace and determined that all of the salient characteristics documented below are available in products/services offered in the commercial marketplace. 


Signature (typed name): Christopher Meredith
Technical Point of Contact (TPOC) 

The Government requires two (2) Tektronix 4 Series Mixed Signal Oscilloscopes (MSO) (Model Number: MSO46B - MSO46B 4-BW-500) that meets the following minimum requirements:
Equipped with six (6) analog input channels each with: 
Direct current (DC) and alternating current (AC) input coupling
One (1) Megaohm (MΩ) and 50 ohm (Ω) input impedances
One (1) MΩ sensitivity range: 500 microVolt per division (µV/div) to ten (10) Volt per division (V/div)
50 Ω sensitivity range: one (1) mV/div to one (1) V/div
Maximum input voltage: one (1) MΩ to 300 root mean square voltage (VRMS)
Maximum input voltage: 50 Ω to five (5) VRMS, with peaks less than ±20 Volts (V)
500 Megahertz (MHz) bandwidth on all six (6) analog channels, with the ability to upgrade to a higher GHz bandwidth
Capable of real-time analog sampling at 6.25 GigaSamples/second (GSa/s) when using six (6) channels simultaneously
The record length on each channel shall be 31.25 million points 
Up to 16-bit vertical resolution
Equipped with edge, pulse width, rise/fall time, sequence, logic, window, timeout trigger types 
Capable of automatic saving of waveforms based on trigger
Equipped with a 500,000 waveforms per second capture rate
Equipped with both an auxiliary-in connection for triggering and auxiliary-out connection to send a pulse out when oscilloscope triggers
Remote control of oscilloscope over a network connection using standard web browser
Capable of simultaneously observing both time- and frequency-domain views of the six (6) input signals with independent settings for each domain
Equipped with solid state drives (SSD) with a closed embedded operating system 
Equipped with a 13.3 inch (”) built-in, touchscreen display with 1920x1080 pixel resolution
Able to fit in a standard 19” instrumentation rack
Equipped with a handle for carrying 
Equipped with one (1) Gb/s Ethernet port, High-Definition Multimedia Interface (HDMI) connection, and four (4) or more USB 2.0 ports
One (1) year Manufacturer’s warranty
Shipping to APG, MD 21005

Description: This is a request for a Firm Fixed Price quotation for commercial products. This solicitation is issued in accordance with the Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO) Part 12 - Acquisition of Commercial Products and Commercial Services as supplemented with additional information included in this notice. This solicitation is a Request for Quotation (RFQ). The solicitation document and incorporated provisions and clauses are those in effect through the RFO. The associated North American Industrial Classification System (NAICS) code for this procurement is 344419 - Other Electronic Component Manufacturing. The small business size standard of 750 employees. This is an unrestricted competition. Both other than small businesses and small businesses under the applicable NAICS code are eligible to respond. DESCRIPTION OF REQUIREMENTS Non-Competitive (Single-sole Source (Including Brand-Name)) Determination: The purpose of this acquisition is to obtain a field-programmable gate array (FPGA) (AMD Zynq UltraScale+ RFSoC ZCU111 Evaluation Kit, EK-U1-ZCU111-G) board that can be used in the NIST ITL's quantum network testbed to measure and forward information based on detection events with extremely low latency. Quantum information routing and detection in deployed optical fibers require state-of-the-art FPGAs to be able to process single-photon detection information and make decisions that are comparable with the speed of light in optical fibers. This is a brand name request, as ITL requires this specific evaluation board to be compatible with software that has already been written and developed by our PML colleagues. All FPGAs are different and require device-specific programming and configuration. NIST ITL has an existing software library that was previously developed by a NIST PML postdoctoral researcher. The software library was specifically written for the AMD Zynq platform and took two years to develop. Since these libraries are specifically written and optimized for the AMD Zynq system, any other platform would require a rewrite of the existing libraries, which would take about one full year in FTE. Utilizing this library will reduce development time and risk while supporting compatibility with the required FPGA platform. Failure to acquire this specific FPGA will result in non-compatible systems, and excessive costs related to developing new software and operating conditions. Objectives The purpose of this acquisition is to obtain a brand name only FPGA evaluation board to measure and forward information based on detection events with extremely low latency. BACKGROUND This is a Sources Sought Notice (SSN) for industry to help the Government determine the availability and capability of small business and other than small businesses which can provide any or all of the products and services required by the U.S. Department of Commerce, National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST). NIST is conducting market research to identify potential sources that can provide a Mecademic Robotics MECA500-R4-OB Robot Arm (OR EQUAL) that meets all technical specifications identified in this notice. This notice is strictly to request information for market research purposes to help NIST determine the appropriate acquisition strategy for this requirement. This notice shall not be construed as a solicitation, an obligation, or commitment by NIST. OVERVIEW The Intelligent Systems Division (ISD) of the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) needs a Mecademic Robotics MECA500-R4-OB (or equivalent) ROBOT ARM suitable for robotic assembly applications and portable for demonstrations. NIST requires one (1) Mecademic Robotics MECA500-R4-OB (or equivalent) ROBOT ARM, including hardware, software, accessories, calibration certificate, and warranty. The ROBOT ARM must have a position repeatability of less than or equal to � 0.005 mm. The ROBOT ARM must have Six (6) degrees of freedom. LINE ITEM 2: Quantity One (1) each, PS200-R4 POWER SUPPLY (OR EQUAL) The POWER SUPPLY must be compatible with the ROBOT ARM in LINE ITEM 1 and have appropriate connectors that fit the ROBOT ARM. LINE ITEM 5: Quantity One (1) each, MEGP-25E electric GRIPPER (OR EQUAL) The GRIPPER must have the following minimum salient characteristics: The GRIPPER must be compatible with the ROBOT ARM in LINE ITEM 1. The power/energy for the GRIPPER may be provided through the ROBOT ARM in LINE ITEM 1. LINE ITEM 6: Quantity One (1) each, MEGP-25LS electric GRIPPER (OR EQUAL) The GRIPPER must have the following minimum salient characteristics: The GRIPPER must be compatible with the ROBOT ARM in LINE ITEM 1 The GRIPPER must have a stroke of 48 mm (or more). matters.text:
Federal notice (Presolicitation), DEPT OF DEFENSE.DEPT OF THE AIR FORCE.FA5004  354 CONS PK
Title: Notice of Intent to Sole Source: F-35 Engine Run Simulator
Solicitation number: FA500426Q1143
PSC: 6930; NAICS: 333310
Description: Pre-Solicitation Notice: F-35 Engine Run Simulator This is a pre-solicitation synopsis of a proposed contract action in accordance with RFO Subpart 5.2. Description: The U.S. Air Force has a requirement to procure a high-fidelity F-35 engine run simulator. The system's core objective is to serve as a critical training tool, enabling personnel to master engine start sequences, effectively respond to a range of emergency scenarios, and diagnose system fault codes in a controlled environment. A paramount requirement is that the simulator must replicate the physical characteristics and tactile feedback of a genuine F-35 cockpit. This is essential for building operator familiarity, muscle memory, and the confidence needed for real-world engine run operations. The final product must be delivered in a compact form factor that operates on standard power and cooling infrastructure. The Government has the intent to procure this requirement to a sole source in accordance with 6.301-1 Only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements. Intent to Sole Source: The Government intends to award this contract to IPerformX (CAGE: 8BHF8) under the authority of FAR 12.102(a) because they are the only source that can provide a life-like inject capabilities or the required level of customer support. iPerformX is the proprietary owner and sole manufacturer capable of providing the fully unclassified system with the mandatory 24-month software/56-month hardware warranties because of this the requirement must be procured as a Sole Source directly to iPerformX. This is not a formal solicitation. However, if your business can fulfill this requirement, email a capability statement to the Contracting Officer at ronald.greig@us.af.mil by August 20, 2026 by 1:00PM AKST. We will evaluate all submissions received before the deadline to decide if we should compete this purchase.

attachments.name: F35 Engine Run Simulator- Salient Characteristics.pdf
attachments.text:
Salient Characteristics of the Requirement
1. General Scope
The Government requires a turnkey, fully integrated F-35 engine run simulator that replicates
the engine start sequence, emergency scenarios, and fault codes. The system must replicate
the physical characteristics, dimensions, and articulation of a true F-35 cockpit to build
familiarity, muscle memory, and confidence during engine run operations. The delivered
product must be a self-contained system requiring no additional Government-furnished IT
hardware to operate.
2. Physical & Environmental Characteristics
• Form Factor: Must be a compact design capable of deployment/storage (e.g., fits within
standard ISU-90 footprint). Maximum dimensions shall not exceed 70" L x 45" W x 60"
H.
• Power: Must operate on standard US power (110 VAC, 60 Hz).
• Durability: Components must be constructed of commercial/industrial-grade materials
designed to withstand continuous, high-repetition training environments.
3. Functional Hardware Requirements
• Power Control Panel: Must feature all three ICC switches, battery switch, cabin dump,
IPP start, and IPP emergency stop switches.
• Throttle Box: Must articulate forwards and backwards and include a master light switch,
communications transmission switch, and friction adjustment knob.
• Foot Pedals (Qty 2): Must be fully functional and simulate realistic braking pressure.
• Panoramic Control Display (PCD): Must be a touchscreen display capable of rendering
data true to the real F-35 cockpit experience (including thrustmeter with all gauges,
prognostic health management, cautions, and warnings). Must respond accurately to
simulated emergency conditions and corrective actions.
• Ejection Seat: Must be visually and physically representative of the real aircraft seat
(functional ejection capability is not required).
• Flight Control Stick: Must feature true-to-life dimensions, articulation, and
responsiveness.
• Parking Brake Switch: Must be functionally able to be set "on" and "off" and register the
status on the PCD.
• Engine Run Switch: Must be functional to simulate engine run and motoring with full
forward, middle, and aft positions.
• Vehicle Systems Built-In Test (V-BIT) Switch: Must be functional and indicate running
tests on the display, with the ability to generate fault codes.
4. Software, IT, and Compliance
• System Processing: Must include all necessary internal computing hardware/processors
to run the simulation seamlessly without lag or degradation.
• Network Independence: The system must be capable of stand-alone, air-gapped operation
and shall not require connection to a Department of Defense (DoD) network to function.
• Licensing & Updates: Must include a perpetual software license for the simulation
operating system. Routine software patches and bug fixes must be provided at no
additional cost during the warranty period.
• Compliance: The system and its manufacturing, wholesale, and distribution must strictly
comply with all International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR) standards.
5. Delivery, Installation, and Support
• Delivery: F.O.B. Destination to Eielson AFB, AK.
• Installation & Training: Must include on-site installation, configuration, and a
comprehensive "train-the-trainer" operator training session by qualified personnel for

software, with dedicated technical troubleshooting support.

Description of the Supplies/Services Required:
The requirement is for the procurement of a turnkey, fully integrated, and self-contained F-
35 Engine Run Simulator to meet training requirements at Eielson AFB, AK. The system
must replicate the engine start sequence, emergency scenarios, and fault codes of a true F-
35 aircraft, requiring no additional Government-furnished IT hardware to operate.
Explanation for soliciting from Single Source or Brand Name:
Market research was conducted in accordance with RFO 10. Research confirmed that iPerformX
holds the exclusive distribution rights for the iPerformX F-35 Simulator within the United States. No
other authorized resellers or equivalent systems that meet the exact mixed-reality training
specifications for this requirement were identified. There are no active patents on the hardware or
software, but the vendor holds strict proprietary control over the technical data and licensing.
Attempting to reverse-engineer or develop a custom simulator from scratch would result in
substantial duplication of costs to the Government that are not expected to be recovered through
competition, as well as unacceptable delays in fulfilling the training requirements at Eielson AFB.
Efforts to Obtain Competition
To date, only iPerformX was conforming to the sources sought requirements and
expressed a written interest in this acquisition. 2 other companies expressed interest but
had software and hardware from foreign countries and could not provide the same
warranty options.
Steps to Preclude Future Single Source or Brand Name Awards
The Government will continue to monitor the market for new technologies, alternative F-
35 simulator platforms, and changes to authorized reseller networks. Market research will
be conducted prior to any future acquisitions or extended maintenance contracts to
determine if other sources have become available.

The crane also shall possess the following additional specifications:
• Engine heater for diesel engine,

Broderson Manufacturing Corp is the only manufacturer that produces a crane meeting the
Government’s specific operational and safety requirements. The Broderson ten (10) U.S. ton,
diesel-powered, industrial carry deck crane (Model IC-100-B) fulfills each of the four (4) core
characteristics as follows:
1. Physical Envelope Constraints: The Broderson IC-100-B crane possesses a compact
chassis necessary for the constrained environment. Its specifications confirm an overall
transport length of 12 feet 10 inches (154 inches) and an overall transport width of six (6)
feet six (6) inches (78 inches). These dimensions are within the maximum permissible
footprint of enabling the equipment to
access and maneuver within the required workspaces.
2. Lifting Capacity: The Broderson IC-100-B meets the required lifting capacity. The
manufacturer's specifications rate the crane for a maximum capacity of ten (10) U.S. tons
(20,000 lbs.) "over front on outriggers" at a five-foot load radius, which is sufficient to
handle the large, heavy items as required.
3. Design Configuration: The unit is purpose-built as an Industrial Carry Deck Crane,
featuring the requisite flat, heavy-duty cargo deck integrated into its chassis. Furthermore,
the crane is equipped with a three-section, telescoping 15 feet to 35 feet boom and
provides continuous 360-degree boom rotation, satisfying the Government's design
configuration requirements for hoisting and maneuvering loads.
4. Power Source: The Broderson IC-100-B is equipped with a Kubota V3307 diesel-powered
internal combustion engine that meets EPA Tier 4F emission standards. This meets the
specific operational demand for a diesel power source, as alternative fuel or power
configurations are not acceptable for this requirement.
Alternative manufacturers of carry deck cranes were considered, including Grove U.S. LLC
(owned by The Manitowoc Company, Inc.) and JMG America. While these alternatives were
considered, neither manufacturer produces a crane that meets all of the Government’s
essential requirements. Grove U.S. LLC does not offer a ten (10) U.S. ton carry deck crane.
The closest available models are the GCD09, with a maximum capacity of nine (9) U.S. tons,
which is insufficient for the Government's minimum ten (10) U.S. ton lifting requirement, and
the GCD15, with a capacity of 15 U.S. tons. However, the larger GCD15 crane has an overall
transport length of 13 feet 9.6 inches (165.6 inches), which is too large for the application and
exceeds the strict spatial limitations of the operating environment. JMG America offers an
11.02 U.S. ton capacity crane (Model MC 100RE) and a 55.12 U.S. ton capacity crane (Model
MC 50000RE). However, these cranes, like all JMG models, are exclusively available with an
all-electric, battery-powered configuration. This does not meet the Government's explicit
requirement for a diesel-powered engine.
Due to the critical constraints of physical size, lifting capacity, and required power source, the
Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM), Broderson Manufacturing Corp, is the only source
reasonably capable of providing a crane that meets the Government's requirements. A
Sources Sought notice was posted concurrently to GSA (Reference: RFI1824456) and
SAM.gov from 21 July 2026 through 28 July 2026. Upon the closing of the response window,
the Sources Sought identified two (2) resellers of the subject requirement: American Material
Handling, Inc. (AMH, Inc) (CAGE Code: 0SUS7; Small Business) and Ecology Mir Group LLC
(CAGE Code: 7DCV4; Small Business). As such, competition among the OEM and its
resellers will be facilitated.
*************************************************************************************************
6. FAIR AND REASONABLE PRICE DETERMINATION:
It has been determined that the anticipated cost to the Government will be fair and reasonable and
that approval of this recommendation is in the best interest of the government. This justification is
accurate and complete to the best of my knowledge and belief.

attachments.text:
Evaluation Criteria – Comparative Evaluation
In accordance with IAW RFO FAR 12.203(c)(2), comparative evaluation procedures will be utilized. Comparative evaluation is the comparison of all offers received in response to this solicitation against each other. An item-by-item comparison of each offer to one another will be performed to determine which offer provides the most benefit to the government. Award will be made to the offer that is most advantageous to the Government. The Government may award to the lowest priced offeror that meets the Government’s minimum requirements; however, the Government reserves the right to award to a higher priced offeror exceeding the minimum requirements if it is most advantageous to the Government. In order to be considered for award, an offer must meet the Government’s minimum technical requirement contained in this solicitation. All evaluation factors will be weighted equally. The below evaluation factors will be utilized during evaluation (in no order of relative importance): 
Price:
Price will be evaluated based on the total proposed price, including options, (if any). The Government reserves the right and discretion to perform price realism analysis on any offer that appears to be so low as to pose a risk to the Government in understanding the requirements of the solicitation.

Technical Acceptability:
The technical acceptability element of the evaluation will be a determination as to whether the proposed product/service meets the performance characteristics and specifications in the solicitation. The Technical element of the evaluation shall be based solely on information furnished by the vendor. The Government is not responsible for locating or securing any information, which is not identified in the proposal. To ensure sufficient information is available, vendors must furnish as part of their proposal all descriptive material (such as cuts, illustrations, drawings, or other information) necessary for the Government to determine whether the product and/or capabilities meet(s) the performance characteristics and specifications of the requirement. If the offeror proposes to modify a product so as to conform to the requirement of this solicitation, the offeror shall include a clear description of such proposed modifications and clearly mark any descriptive materials to show modifications.
 
Past Performance:
Past performance will be evaluated on an acceptable/unacceptable rating basis. An “Acceptable” rating is defined as the Government having reasonable confidence that the offeror can complete all requirements under the contract and meet stated delivery dates. An “Unacceptable” rating is defined as the Government having minimal confidence that the offeror can complete all requirements under the contract and meet stated delivery dates/performance period. The ratings will be based upon past performance information submitted by the offeror and/or past performance information the Government obtains. Only offerors rated “Acceptable” will be eligible for award.

Notice of Intent to Sole Source (Brand Name) The U.S. Army Test and Evaluation Command (ATEC), Applied Sciences Division at Dugway Proving Ground (DPG) intends to solicit and negotiate on a sole-source basis with Affinisep USA, LLC. This acquisition is restricted to the brand-name Affinisep sampling media under the authority of FAR 12.201-1 for restricting competition for commercial acquisitions valued at or below the simplified acquisition threshold. As support for this brand-name restriction, this specific Affinisep media has undergone an extensive, multi-year Verification and Validation (V&V) process for chemical agent testing Programs of Record. No other brand or source can meet the Government's technical and regulatory requirements without rendering all test results scientifically invalid and non-compliant with established ISO 17025 procedures. Line Items & Quantities CLIN 0001: AttractSPE� Disks Bio - SDB SPE Disks for molecular biology purpose with PS-DVB sorbent, 47mm diameter, 20/pk (Part No: SPE-Disks-Bio-DVB-47.20-NF) Quantity: 13 Packs CLIN 0002: AttractSPE� Custom Made 102-Bio PS-DVB for biomolecular application Pads 10x20cm - 40/pk (Part No: SPE-Pads-DVB-Bio-T1.100x200.40) Quantity: 2 Packs CLIN 0003: Administrative and Shipping fees (Part No: SF100) Quantity: 1 Each CLIN 0004: Container - Pelican Quantity: 3 Each Description of Requirements These items are critical support consumables required for chemical agent testing. To ensure data integrity and compliance with ISO 17025 standards: Single Lot Sourcing: All 13 packs of disks and 2 packs of pads must originate from a single, documented production lot to eliminate batch-to-batch variability. Controlled Shipping Chain: To prevent chemical degradation, the items must be shipped in protective containers directly from the manufacturer (Affinisep USA, LLC) to the end-user. Procurement through third-party distributors is not authorized. Date and Place of Delivery and Acceptance Delivery Date: No later than 30 September 2026 F.O.B. Point: Destination Place of Delivery: U.S. Army Dugway Proving Ground, Dugway, UT 84022 Basis for Award The Government intends to award a contract to the responsible offeror submitting the lowest-priced, technically acceptable quotation. Technical Acceptability: Met by explicitly quoting the exact brand-name Affinisep items and providing a mandatory written guarantee that all media will be sourced from a single production lot and shipped in protective containers directly from the manufacturer. Price: Evaluated for fairness and reasonableness using price analysis. Submission of Offers Offerors may submit quotations in their preferred company format. Quotations must explicitly reference Request for Quotation # W911S626QA029. To be considered for award, the offeror�s quote must include: Completed pricing for CLINs 0001 through 0004. The written Technical Quality & Traceability Guarantees (Single lot sourcing & Direct-from-manufacturer shipping). Offeror's CAGE Code, Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) number, tax identification number, and discount/payment terms. A completed copy of the provision at DFARS 252.225-7000, Buy American�Balance of Payments Program Certificate (specifically identifying the country of origin for CLINs 0001 and 0002). Quotes must be submitted via email directly to the Contract Specialist, Amy Eilerts, at amy.m.eilerts.civ@army.mil. Mail and facsimile quotes will NOT be accepted. Submissions are required to be received no later than 10:00 AM MDT on Monday, August 17, 2026. All responsible sources may submit a capability statement, proposal, or quotation, which shall be considered by the agency. Project
Flexible film materials testing system
General Information
1.0 Scope of Work
The vendor shall provide a fully integrated 5 kN universal materials testing system, including a dual-column load frame,
load-weighing system, control software, and data acquisition electronics. The system must meet all specified
performance, safety, and compatibility requirements, including precise crosshead control, calibrated load cells, collision
mitigation features, and multi-mode mechanical testing capability. The supplier shall install the equipment, verify
performance to applicable ASTM specifications, and deliver on-site training along with full documentation. The vendor
shall also provide warranty coverage and access to factory-trained service personnel for support and maintenance.
2.0 Background
The USDA is working with collaborators to develop and identify food packaging materials that are resistant to insect
feeding and penetration under long term storage conditions and requires an instrument that is capable of testing
physical properties of various materials used in food packaging, including woven bags and thin films, for elongation,
penetration resistance, tensile strength, seal strength and puncture resistance following published American Society for
Testing and Materials standard methods. The instrument must have a load measurement accuracy of +/- 0.5% down to
1/250th of a load cell capacity and +/- 1.0% down to 1/500th of load cell capacity. It must meet or exceed ASTM eF,
BS1610, DIN, 51221, ISO 7500-1, EN 100002-2, JIS B7721, JIS B7733, and AFNOR A03-501 standards. It also must have a
displacement accuracy of +/- 0.02 mm or 0.15% of displacement (whichever is greater) and perform accurate
measurements under a range of environmental conditions, including at storage temperatures ranging from -25-55 C and
at 10-90% humidity.
Contractor Requirements
3.0 Technical Requirements / Tasks
II. MATERIAL TESTING SYSTEM SPECIFICATIONS
This unit shall integrate the following major sub-systems into a complete operating system. The major sub-systems and
their specifications are:
A. LOAD FRAME
1. The load frame should be a dual column loading frame that includes a digital closed loop command and feedback
motion control system with a high-performance AC servo motor.
2. The moving crosshead will be driven by precision screws each with a preloaded nut providing zero backlash during
reverse stress loading. Systems without ball screws or preload nuts that are not preloaded are not acceptable.
3. For lateral stiffness and robustness purposes, in addition to the ball screws described above, the load frame should
include at least two (2) 25 mm diameter smooth ground guidance rods that the moving crosshead also rides on.
4. The moving crosshead must be a solid single machined piece that encloses the ball screws and guidance rods for
maximum overall stiffness
5. The ball screws shall be fully enclosed to eliminate pinch points and protect the precision surfaces from damage
from grips and contamination.
6. The load frame shall include a bright red ISO approved emergency stop switch.
7. The vertical distance between the load frame table and crosshead shall be 1172 mm (46.1 in) and for load cells, grips
and fixtures. Maximum distance of 1651 mm (65.0 in) is an option.
8. The maximum load capacity shall be 5 kN (500 kgf, 1125 lbf)
9. The speed range should be 0.05 to 1016 mm/min (0.002 in/min to 40 in/min).
10. The maximum crosshead return speed is 1500 mm/min (59 in/min) for rapid testing turn-around.
11. The steady state speed accuracy shall be within +/-0.2%, of set speed measured over full speed range.
12. The frame shall have variable speed jog with software-defined speed. When jog is initiated, the crosshead shall
gradually accelerate to reach a maximum jog speed of 1500 mm (59 in) per minute.
13. The frame column shall be powder coated to resist dents and scratches for protection.
14. The frame column shall have t-slots to allow easy attachment and movement of accessories without need to drill or
use fasteners.
3
15. The frame column shall have a fixed measurement tape rule for easy spotting and setting of the moving crosshead
and test load strings.
16. The load frame will have two secondary position limits using a microswitch to prevent crosshead run-away as a
system fail-safe. The user settable limits must be attached to a solid metal rod for durability and stiffness.
17. For safety purposes, the frame shall incorporate an auto-frame standby mode that automatically stops the frame
when the transducer, interface, or computer is disconnected or shutdown.
18. The system shall have an operator panel with buttons to start and stop tests, return crosshead to the origin, and jog
the crosshead. The operator panel shall contain four colored status LEDs to indicate the status of the system:
disabled (white), setup (blue), caution (yellow), and testing (red).
19. The machine's movement is restricted to prevent unintended motion of the crosshead with an Operator Protect
function - a two-button press sequence to move between testing modes.
20. The system shall have an Operator Protection mechanism that allows limiting crosshead jog speed and reduce grip
closing pressure while setting up a test.
21. The system shall include a “PIP” input jack to allow use of an external pipping device to manual mark points of
interest during data acquisition
22. The system shall have a 25 pin connection for an auxiliary encoder.
23. The system shall have active LED indicators for the user to quickly determine system status.
Users are provided clear communication on when it is safe to enter, and when to stay clear of test space. The LEDs
on the Operator Panel shall match the software’s border to indicate that status of the system at all times.
24. The system shall have exhaust vents with filter to help minimize particle ingress and regulate the frame internal
operating temperature.
25. The system shall include four shock absorbing feet on each corner of the frame that can be (height) adjusted for
leveling the test frame. The feet must be designed for absorbing shocks to minimize vibrations to the test frame and
transducers.
26. The system shall include a Collison Mitigation function to reduce damage to equipment and delicate specimens by
stopping the crosshead if force is detected upon return or during a jog. The crosshead will also automatically
reverse marginally to prevent damage and allow safe removal of any contacted object.
27. The system shall allow continuous operation for up to ten days (14400 hours).
B. LOAD WEIGHING SYSTEM, TRANSDUCERS, & ELECTRONICS
1. The load weighing system accuracy shall be within +/-0.5% of reading down to 1/250th and within +/- 1% of reading
down to 1/500th of the load cell capacity respectively.
2. Any load cell provided shall have over range protection that will stop the frame automatically.
3. Any changing of transducers on the test system must be Plug in, Calibrate, and Run - including changing load cells.
4. Transducers, including Load Cells and Extensometers must be single piece assemblies to avoid mismatch of parts.
5. Load cells must be complete assemblies with a rigid clevis connection for easy and quick attachment to fixtures.
6. The system shall be equipped with Collision Mitigation which monitors the load readings during jog and return and
will stop the crosshead if unexpected load is observed. The crosshead will also automatically reverse marginally to
prevent damage and allow safe removal of any contacted object.
7. The data acquisition (DA) electronics shall be designed to be located in the test frame close to the load cell and
properly shielded from the known electronic noise generated in the test frame.
8. The transducers will be automatically identified by the electronics and software with automatic calibration. This
eliminates the need for any calibration curves storage or correction.
9. The system shall be compatible with Instron 2519, 2530, 2580 Series load cells used with Instron dual column table-
top 336X, 446X, 556X, and 596X test systems.
B. PNEUMATIC AIR CONTROL KIT (OPTIONAL)
1. The system shall have a pneumatic air control kit integrated into the base of the frame with a push-fit connection
for the inlet, accepting up to 120 psi (8.3 bar).
2. The air kit shall provide connections for two pneumatic grips via push-fit connections.
4
3. The air kit shall be activated with a dual-pedal footswitch. The right pedal shall close one grip upon the first press
and the second grip when pressed again. The left pedal shall open both grips simultaneously.
4. The air control kit shall include a dual-stage pressure manifold which initially closes the grips at a lower
administrator defined pressure in the testing software.
5. Upon starting the test, the air control kit shall move to a higher, method-defined pressure.
C. TEST FRAME CONTROL
a) The control software will have a graphical user interface meeting all Microsoft Windows standards.
b) The software must have multi levels of user access based on his or her login name and password, including support
for Windows Active Directory.
