Quillen VAMC 1 Veterans Way Mountain Home TN POSTAL CODE 37684 COUNTRY USA CONTACT INFORMATION CONTRACTING OFFICE ADDRESS Department of Veterans Affairs Network Contracting Office 9 (90C) 1639 Medical Center Parkway, Suite 204 Murfreesboro TN 37129 POINT OF CONTACT* Contracting Specialist Ryan Mick Ryan.Mick@va.gov 423-979-1408 DESCRIPTION This notice is in accordance with (IAW) Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul 5.3. The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), Network Contracting Office (NCO) 09, hereby provides notice of its intent to award a sole source, firm-fixed price contract for the product/service listed below to a large business, Patterson Dental, headquarters out of Saint Paul, Minnesota. The contract is expected to be awarded under the authority of FAR Overhaul 12.102(a). A Sole Source Justification has been prepared. The anticipated award date is no later than 08-24-2026. The contractor will provide the product/service listed below to the place of performance listed on the cover page of this notice. James H. Quillen VAMC Dental Services is requesting a replacement of the Dental Vacuum Compressor due to the failure of the pumps. Repair parts are not available due to the life of the equipment. This is an emergency requirement. This system is mandatory for the service and is designed to filter mercury-containing filling particles from wastewater. The Amalgam Separator is a system with multiple vacuums. The dental service is currently working off only one vacuum. If too many suction tubes are open in the dental clinic there is no way to increase suction. As demand increases another vacuum will come on to increase suction. Also, if anything happens to the working pump or the controller the whole dental clinic will be completely shut down which will disrupt patient care. There are no longer repair parts available for this system. Most systems have a 10-year lifespan. This system is around 450 pounds and is bolted to the building, hard wired and part of the plumbing system. This system is critical for dental service and patient care. Market Research shows that the Dental Vacuum Compressor system is manufactured by Air Techniques (No Sam). Research shows that similar items could be procured, however, due to this emergency requirement, a solicitation would not be in the best interest of the government. Market research consisted of the following: reviewed the results of recent market research undertaken to meet similar or identical requirements; queried commercial and the Government-wide database of contracts and other procurement instruments intended for use by multiple agencies; participated in interactive, online communication among industry, acquisition personnel, and customers. Items Required: This procurement consists of the Amalgam Separator and multiple vacuums. Period of Performance: 90 days ARO NAICS code: 339114 Dental Equipment and Supplies Manufacturing. (SBA Small Business Size Standard: 750 Employees) PSC: 6520 Dental Instruments, Equipment, and Supplies. THIS NOTICE OF INTENT IS NOT A SOLICITATION OR REQUEST FOR COMPETITIVE QUOTES. However, interested parties may identify their interest and capability to respond to this requirement and may submit a bid, proposal, or quotation (as appropriate) that the agency shall consider within the given closing/due date of this notice. A determination not to compete this requirement, based upon responses to this notice, is solely within the discretion of the Government. Information received will normally be considered solely for determining whether to conduct a competitive procurement. The Department of Veterans Affairs will NOT be responsible for any costs incurred by interested parties in responding to this notice of intent. Only written responses will be considered. All responses from responsible sources will be fully considered. As a result of analyzing responses to this notice of intent, the Government shall determine if a solicitation will be issued. Any prospective contractor must be registered in the System for Award Management (SAM) to be eligible for award and must submit a current authorized distributor letter from the manufacturer. Interested parties are encouraged to furnish information by email only with RESPONSE TO SOLE SOURCE NOTICE 36C24926Q0346 in the subject line. All documents submitted will not be returned. All interested parties shall submit clear and convincing documentation demonstrating their capabilities to satisfy the requirements listed above to Ryan Mick, contracting specialist, by email at Ryan.Mick@va.gov NO LATER THAN the given closing date and time on this notice. The capability documentation should include general information and technical background describing in detail the prospective contractor's capabilities like an authorized distributor/reseller letter from their source of supply if not a manufacturer that will demonstrate the ability to support this requirement.

matters.text:
Federal notice (Sources Sought), COMMERCE, DEPARTMENT OF.NATIONAL INSTITUTE OF STANDARDS AND TECHNOLOGY.DEPT OF COMMERCE NIST
Title: Combined Sources Sought Notice and Notice of Intent to Award a Sole Source Contract for ScanWave Pro electronic controller for a Vero AFM
Solicitation number: NB643090-26-01166
PSC: 6625; NAICS: 334515
Description: BACKGROUND The National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) is conducting market research to identify alternative sources that (a) are capable of meeting NIST�s minimum requirements for the following commercial products and commercial services and (b) would be interested in competing for that requirement: NIST requires one (1) scanning Microwave Impedance Microscopy (sMIM) electronic controller to support nanoscale impedance property measurements for research conducted by Division 643. The required controller will integrate with the Government-owned Vero Atomic Force Microscope (AFM) through the existing ScanWave 2.0� Probe Interface module and will replace the current modular assembly consisting of a microwave electronics unit, power supply, temperature controller, and reflectometer calibrator. The required system shall provide enhanced nanoscale impedance characterization capabilities while maintaining compatibility with the Government's existing Vero AFM configuration. The controller must support direct impedance measurements of material samples and enable integration of electrical characterization with the Vero AFM's existing multimodal measurement capabilities, including current, surface potential, capacitance, piezoelectric, thermal, and mechanical (elastic and plastic) characterization techniques. At a minimum, the required electronic controller shall: Be fully compatible with the Government-owned Vero AFM and the existing ScanWave 2.0� Probe Interface module without requiring replacement or modification of the existing interface. Provide scanning Microwave Impedance Microscopy (sMIM) capability for direct nanoscale impedance measurements. Replace the existing modular microwave electronics assembly with a single integrated electronic controller. Provide substantially improved measurement sensitivity over the existing measurement configuration (approximately a tenfold increase in sensitivity). Integrate with the existing customized Vero AFM holder and associated instrumentation to preserve current system functionality and research workflows. Be capable of supporting multimodal characterization in conjunction with the Vero AFM's existing electrical, mechanical, thermal, and piezoelectric measurement capabilities. Include the manufacturer's standard commercial warranty. The Government intends to acquire only the equipment identified above. Installation, training, and any associated support services shall be provided as customarily offered under the manufacturer's standard commercial terms, as applicable. NIST has not yet determined its acquisition strategy for this requirement and encourages interested sources to respond to this Notice. If NIST�s market research indicates there are alternative sources that are capable and interested in competing to fill this requirement, separate and apart from Primenano, Inc. (UEI: K2RLBZKD2CX7) then NIST will consider conducting a competitive acquisition in accordance with law and regulation. To be clear, NIST�s identification of Primenano, Inc. in this Notice does not constitute a binding commitment or obligation for it to conduct a sole source procurement with Primenano, Inc. for this requirement. Instructions for Responding to Respond to This Notice Parties that respond to this Notice are requested to voluntarily submit the requested information via email in Microsoft Word, Adobe PDF, and/or Microsoft Excel format to the designated point(s) of contact whose name and email address appears at the bottom of this notice. Please provide only the information requested by this Notice, and do not include proprietary, classified, confidential, or sensitive information in a response to this Notice. Information Requested in Response to This Notice: To help NIST with its market research, NIST is requesting that industry sources carefully review this notice and any attachments to it and voluntarily provide the following information: 1. Company Summary Notice Identification: Notice ID and Title of this posting. Corporate Details: Company name, physical address, website address, and Unique Entity Identifier (UEI). Point of Contact (POC): Name, phone number, and email address. Company Size Standard: Your company�s size status relative to the NAICS code provided in this Notice. (Refer to the SBA Table of Small Business Size Standards). System for Award Management (SAM) Registration: Indicate whether your company has an active registration for procurement purposes in SAM.gov. 2. Feedback for Draft Requirements Review the potential requirements/minimum specifications included with this Notice. Then, please provide suggestions to (a) improve clarity of it; (b) to make it more competitive; (c) to indicate whether there anything in it that may inadvertently exclude domestic involvement; and (d) to indicate how the requirements could potentially be revised to improve the ability for domestic (�Made in America�) end products to be considered. 3. Information Regarding Your Company�s Products and Services Provide specifications, company name of the original equipment manufacturer, and the country of manufacture for products and services that your company is legally authorized to sell and that may meet NIST�s minimum requirements. Indicate whether, in your opinion, the product(s) meet the definition of (a) commercial product or (b) commercially available off-the-shelf (COTS) item or COTS item as described at https://www.acquisition.gov/far-overhaul/far-part-deviation-guide/far-overhaul-part-2 and, if so, which definition applies ((a) or (b)). Indicate whether, in your opinion, the service(s) meet the definition of commercial service as described at https://www.acquisition.gov/far-overhaul/far-part-deviation-guide/far-overhaul-part-2. Standard Commercial Pricing: Provide your company�s standard commercial pricing information for the identified products and services and explain what is included in those standard prices. Estimated Price Range: You may provide an estimated price or price range for the requirements, including a brief explanation of how the price estimate was developed. Standard Commercial Terms and Conditions: Provide a copy of the standard commercial terms and conditions for the commercial products and commercial services identified in the response to this notice, including nature and duration of standard commercial warranty. 4. Regulatory and Supply Chain Compliance Indicate whether your company could comply with FAR Clause 52.219-14, Limitations on Subcontracting (OCT 2022) if this acquisition were to be set aside for small businesses. Provide a brief supporting explanation. 5. Existing Governmentwide Contract Vehicles Indicate whether your company has its own GSA Multiple Award Schedule (MAS) contract or other federal contract vehicles under which NIST could award an order and, if so, provide the contract details (contract number, Contracting Officer name/contact, SOW, terms and conditions, and price lists). We truly appreciate your company�s willingness to provide the above-mentioned information which NIST will be valuable in helping NIST complete its market research. Important Notes This Notice does not obligate the Government to award a contract or otherwise pay respondents to this notice for information provided in response to this Notice. Following a review of the responses and market research, NIST may publish a solicitation on an authorized site, depending on the chosen acquisition strategy. Responses received after the closing date for this Notice may not be considered. There is no solicitation available at this time. The Government reserves the right to use information that it receives in response to this Notice as it deems appropriate to establish final requirements or for other legally appropriate purposes. Any organization responding to this notice should ensure that its response is complete and sufficiently detailed to allow the Government to determine the organization�s capability. Respondents

252.211-7003 ITEM IDENTIFICATION AND VALUATION (MAR 2016)
As prescribed in 211.274-6(a)(1), use the following clause: 
ITEM UNIQUE IDENTIFICATION AND VALUATION (MAR 2016) 
(a) Definitions. As used in this clause—
“Automatic identification device” means a device, such as a reader or interrogator, used to retrieve data encoded on machine-readable media.
“Concatenated unique item identifier” means—
(1) For items that are serialized within the enterprise identifier, the linking together of the unique identifier data elements in order of the issuing agency code, enterprise identifier, and unique serial number within the enterprise identifier; or
(2) For items that are serialized within the original part, lot, or batch number, the linking together of the unique identifier data elements in order of the issuing agency code; enterprise identifier; original part, lot, or batch number; and serial number within the original part, lot, or batch number.
“Data matrix” means a two-dimensional matrix symbology, which is made up of square or, in some cases, round modules arranged within a perimeter finder pattern and uses the Error Checking and Correction 200 (ECC200) specification found within International Standards Organization (ISO)/International Electrotechnical Commission (IEC) 16022.
“Data qualifier” means a specified character (or string of characters) that immediately precedes a data field that defines the general category or intended use of the data that follows.
“DoD recognized unique identification equivalent” means a unique identification method that is in commercial use and has been recognized by DoD. All DoD recognized unique identification equivalents are listed at https://www.acq.osd.mil/asda/dpc/ce/ds/unique-id.html .
“DoD item unique identification” means a system of marking items delivered to DoD with unique item identifiers that have machine-readable data elements to distinguish an item from all other like and unlike items. For items that are serialized within the enterprise identifier, the unique item identifier shall include the data elements of the enterprise identifier and a unique serial number. For items that are serialized within the part, lot, or batch number within the enterprise identifier, the unique item identifier shall include the data elements of the enterprise identifier; the original part, lot, or batch number; and the serial number.
“Enterprise” means the entity (e.g., a manufacturer or vendor) responsible for assigning unique item identifiers to items.
“Enterprise identifier” means a code that is uniquely assigned to an enterprise by an issuing agency.
“Government’s unit acquisition cost” means—
(1) For fixed-price type line, subline, or exhibit line items, the unit price identified in the contract at the time of delivery;
(2) For cost-type or undefinitized line, subline, or exhibit line items, the Contractor’s estimated fully burdened unit cost to the Government at the time of delivery; and
(3) For items produced under a time-and-materials contract, the Contractor’s estimated fully burdened unit cost to the Government at the time of delivery.
“Issuing agency” means an organization responsible for assigning a globally unique identifier to an enterprise, as indicated in the Register of Issuing Agency Codes for ISO/IEC 15459, located at http://www.aimglobal.org/?Reg_Authority15459.
“Issuing agency code” means a code that designates the registration (or controlling) authority for the enterprise identifier.
“Item” means a single hardware article or a single unit formed by a grouping of subassemblies, components, or constituent parts.
“Lot or batch number” means an identifying number assigned by the enterprise to a designated group of items, usually referred to as either a lot or a batch, all of which were manufactured under identical conditions.
“Machine-readable” means an automatic identification technology media, such as bar codes, contact memory buttons, radio frequency identification, or optical memory cards.
“Original part number” means a combination of numbers or letters assigned by the enterprise at item creation to a class of items with the same form, fit, function, and interface.
“Parent item” means the item assembly, intermediate component, or subassembly that has an embedded item with a unique item identifier or DoD recognized unique identification equivalent.
“Serial number within the enterprise identifier” means a combination of numbers, letters, or symbols assigned by the enterprise to an item that provides for the differentiation of that item from any other like and unlike item and is never used again within the enterprise.
“Serial number within the part, lot, or batch number” means a combination of numbers or letters assigned by the enterprise to an item that provides for the differentiation of that item from any other like item within a part, lot, or batch number assignment.
“Serialization within the enterprise identifier” means each item produced is assigned a serial number that is unique among all the tangible items produced by the enterprise and is never used again. The enterprise is responsible for ensuring unique serialization within the enterprise identifier.
“Serialization within the part, lot, or batch number” means each item of a particular part, lot, or batch number is assigned a unique serial number within that part, lot, or batch number assignment. The enterprise is responsible for ensuring unique serialization within the part, lot, or batch number within the enterprise identifier.
“Type designation” means a combination of letters and numerals assigned by the Government to a major end item, assembly or subassembly, as appropriate, to provide a convenient means of differentiating between items having the same basic name and to indicate modifications and changes thereto.
“Unique item identifier” means a set of data elements marked on items that is globally unique and unambiguous. The term includes a concatenated unique item identifier or a DoD recognized unique identification equivalent.
“Unique item identifier type” means a designator to indicate which method of uniquely identifying a part has been used. The current list of accepted unique item identifier types is maintained at https://www.acq.osd.mil/asda/dpc/ce/ds/unique-id.html .
(b) The Contractor shall deliver all items under a contract line, subline, or exhibit line item.
(c) Unique item identifier.

NOTICE OF INTENT TO SOLE SOURCE
The Department of Veterans Affairs, Network Contracting Office (NCO) 07, located at 1670 Clairmont

Government’s intent to execute a Sole Source Contract under FAR Part 13.5. This notice satisfies the

The intended Contractor is Kub Technologies Inc., located at 111 Research Drive, Stratford, CT 06615.
The Joseph Maxwell Cleland Atlanta VA Medical Center has a (1) Mozart 3-D Specimen
Tomosynthesis System from KUB Technologies, for X-rays of breast specimens after localization
lumpectomies or excisions. Mozart iQ system utilizes 3D specimen tomosynthesis (the standard of
care in breast cancer surgery) to take X-ray images of breast specimens. Viewing the image in 3
dimensions allows for accurate and precise identification of the tumor and clip, which can be obscured
by dense tissue on traditional 2D imaging. Currently, Atlanta VA does not have such a device.
The Mozart System from KUBTEC is a major advancement in the surgical treatment of breast cancer.
The system uses 3D specimen tomosynthesis, the gold standard for diagnostic mammography, to
enable surgeons and radiologists to accurately identify positive or close margins intraoperatively. In
addition, the crisp, high quality images with 3D magnification allow you to see finer details such as
microcalcifications, spiculations and lymph nodes and shaved cavities more clearly. It enables
surgeons to differentiate between healthy and involved tissue for greater breast conservation and
ultimately a superior cosmetic outcome for patients. The Mozart System has been shown to decrease
re-excisions by 50%, while preserving healthy tissue for breast cosmesis. The Image Blender allows the
user to overlay the x-ray image to the specimen jpeg image to further enhance the viewing and
interpretation of the specimen.

solicit from one source if the Contracting Officer determines that the circumstances of the contract

Description: NOTICE OF INTENT This is a notice of intent to award a sole-source contract using simplified acquisition procedures and is not a request for competitive quotes. The U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) Office of Water (OW) intends to award a sole source contract under the simplified acquisition threshold for a Cryo Mill cryogenic grinder instrument from Verder Scientific Inc. that is capable of grinding polymers into mico/ nanoplastics to a size less than 1000 nanometers (nm). In accordance with FAR 6.303-1(a)(1), there is the only responsible source available that can satisfy agency requirements. The Cryo Mill is the only cryogenic grinder that the government has determined can meet the government�s specifications. These specifications include: 1. Closed-vial system to reduce polymer contamination during use. 2. Stainless steel grinding chamber/ vial and accessories to reduce sample contamination. 3. Liquid nitrogen autofill accessories to provide continuous cooling of system during grinding and liquid nitrogen sensors for safety precautions. 4. Capacity to grind at least 50 mL of material. 5. Ability to use various sizes of grinding slugs or balls to optimize grinding procedures to make reproducible protocols. 6. Benchtop model to fit in current lab space configuration (under 2 ft2 size) 7. Availability of multiple grinding chambers to avoid cross contamination between different polymers, reduce downtime, and increase sample processing 8. Demonstrated ability to create nanoplastic particles (<1000 nm) 9. Programmable ability to store multiple protocols for accurate replication of procedures The capability to configure Cryo Mill instrumentation to reliably create micro/nanoplastics has been demonstrated by members of the scientific community at the National Institute of Standards and Technology. Only this suggested source can furnish equipment that meets these requirements to the exclusion of other sources. The government could not find evidence that comparable cryogenic grinders could reliably meet this requirement. This requirement includes expiring funds, and it is anticipated that the EPA will award this action no later than September 30, 2026. The applicable NAICS Code is 334516 (Analytical Laboratory Instrument Manufacturing) PSC is 6630 (Chemical Analysis Instruments). The anticipated delivery date is October 30, 2026 and will be sent to the Environmental Protection Agency, 27 Tarzwell Drive, Narragansett, RI. 02882. This notice of intent is not a request for competitive quotations. Any party who believes they can perform this requirement should submit a capability statement for government�s consideration. Federal notice (Special Notice), INTERIOR, DEPARTMENT OF THE.US FISH AND WILDLIFE SERVICE.FWS, IT SERVICES
Title: 19--Special Notice of Intent to Award a Sole Source Contract
Solicitation number: DOIFFBO260155
PSC: 1920; NAICS: 336612
Description: NOTICE OF INTENT TO AWARD A SOLE SOURCE CONTRACT THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR COMPETITIVE QUOTES. Agency: U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service (USFWS) Office: Lower Suwannee Nation Wildlife Refuge (LWR Suwannee NWR) Posting Type: Notice of Intent to Sole Source Authority: FAR 12102(a) - for acquisitions valued at or below the simplified acquisition threshold (SAT) of $350K. 1. Description of Requirement The U.S Fish and Wildlife Service intends to award a firm-fixed price sole source contract for a 2027 SaltRiver 23 shallow-draft operations boat required to support daily LWR Suwannee NWR operational needs. The required supplies/services must meet specific technical, performance, and compatibility standards essential to mission continuity. 2. Intended Sole Source Vendor Gulfshore Manufacturing, Inc - DBA: Young Boats, Inc. 131 Highway 19 N Inglis, Florida 34449 The vendor is the only known source able to provide hull design optimized for shallow-water maneuverability, draft depth suited to mudflats, oyster bars, tidal creeks, and river shoals, performance characteristics required for refuge patrol, survey work, and heavy-load operation, and are within 75-mile service area for warranty service, repairs, and haul-out, which are essential for USFWS mission requirements. 3. Sole Source Justification Market research conducted by USFWS indicates that Gulfshore Manufacturing, Inc - DBA: Young Boats, Inc. is the only responsible source capable of providing the required supplies/services. Research included reviewing comparable products or services, evaluating technical compatibility, and contacting regional vendors. Findings demonstrated that no other source could meet all required specifications, performance criteria, installation/integration requirements, or compliance standards necessary for USFWS operations. 4. No Solicitation Will Be Posted This Notice is not a solicitation, and no solicitation package will be issued. However, interested parties may submit a capability statement demonstrating their ability to meet all requirements listed in this notice. Responses that do not clearly demonstrate the ability to meet every requirement will not be considered. 5. Response Instructions Responses must include: - Business name and Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) - Demonstrated technical capability to meet all requirements - Evidence of product/service equivalency - Confirmation of SAM.gov registration - Ability to meet delivery/performance timelines Responses will be evaluated solely to determine whether additional sources exist that can satisfy USFWS requirements. Email for responses: lawrence_aragon@ios.doi.gov Response Deadline: August 14, 2026, 5:00 PM EST 6. Determination A determination by the Government not to compete this requirement based on responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of USFWS. The Government will not reimburse any costs incurred by interested parties in responding to this notice. NO TELEPHONE REQUESTS/OFFERS WILL BE HONORED

The requirement is for a new 53-month effort to be incorporated into contract number W58RGZ-26-C-0002 to provide up to (12) Apache AH-64E aircraft. This action includes all resources, material, and services necessary to produce, support, and provide up to 12 Apache AH-64E aircraft. The technical scope includes the remanufacture of up to 12 Apache aircraft, and management and mitigation of obsolescence for critical electronic components, including redesign and qualification efforts. The AH-64E is the Army�s premier Attack Helicopter, and its production requires a highly specialized skill set and proprietary data. The Boeing Company is the sole designer, developer, manufacturer, and system integrator of the AH-64 Apache aircraft. The Government does not own a complete production-level Technical Data Package (TDP) or the rights to the proprietary data necessary to complete this procurement. 2. Submission of Capability Statements Notwithstanding the Government's intent to award a sole-source contract, all responsible sources are encouraged to submit a capability statement demonstrating their ability to meet the requirements outlined above. Interested parties must submit a capability statement that is no more than ten (10) pages in length. The capability statement should provide clear and convincing evidence that the respondent has the necessary technical expertise, proprietary data or data rights, facilities, and experience to manufacture, assemble, integrate, and support the AH-64E aircraft. Submission of a capability statement is voluntary, and the Government will not pay for any information or administrative costs incurred in response to this notice. The information provided will be used solely for market research purposes. A determination by the Government not to complete this proposed contract action based upon responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government.

3. System and Spare Parts Interchangeability: Various laboratories within ARL use
similar Tektronix oscilloscopes for their research. Procuring the same brand
ensures that high-value peripheral components, probes, interfaces, and critical
spare parts can be immediately shared, swapped, and interchanged between
different laboratories as testing requirements dictate. It is critical to ensure
interchangeability of systems and spare parts with other laboratories within ARL,
which simplifies maintenance and support.
Tektronix, Inc., the Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM), is the only source available
that meets each of the Government’s three (3) primary requirements:
1. Only Tektronix-branded systems can ensure full compatibility with the existing
oscilloscopes. Because the new oscilloscopes must operate in tandem with the
’s established suite of hardware, any new equipment must seamlessly
interface with the native communication protocols and hardware architectures of
the existing fleet. Since these protocols and architectures are proprietary, no other
brand of oscilloscopes are capable of achieving the necessary integration with the
pre-existing Tektronix hardware configuration.
2. Only Tektronix-branded systems have access to the existing fleet’s proprietary
Tektronix software suite. Since multiple Tektronix systems are used
simultaneously for the , any new equipment must be able to
communicate with and utilize the same software to meet the Government’s critical
requirements for time synchronization and live, multi-unit data analysis.
• Time synchronization relies on a proprietary protocol within the Tektronix
software and hardware ecosystem, ensuring that the internal clocks of all
connected units are aligned to the microsecond or nanosecond level. A
non-Tektronix oscilloscope lacks the specific hardware and software
receptors to receive, interpret, and align its internal clock with these
proprietary Tektronix timing signals. Therefore, it is impossible to guarantee
that its measurements are taken at the exact same instant as those from
the Tektronix units, which would make the combined data unreliable and
scientifically useless for reconstructing a rapid sequence of events.
• Live, multi-unit data analysis relies on a proprietary language of specific
command sets and data formats that only Tektronix devices are designed
to understand and respond to. An oscilloscope from another brand would
not recognize these commands and therefore could not be integrated into
the live-viewing session, rendering it invisible to the analysis software and
preventing its data from being plotted alongside the others.
3. Third, only Tektronix-branded systems provide system and spare parts
interchangeability within the existing fleet of oscilloscopes. Multiple research
divisions and laboratories across ARL have standardized their experimental
setups on similar Tektronix oscilloscope architectures. Due to Tektronix’s
proprietary hardware and software configurations, only Tektronix-branded
systems can ensure full interchangeability and compatibility with the existing
oscilloscopes.
Failure to procure the Tektronix MSO46B - MSO46B 4-BW-500 oscilloscopes would
severely degrade the Government’s testing capabilities, resulting in compromised data
integrity, the waste of high-value materials, and unacceptable schedule delays. If the
Government were to procure a different brand of oscilloscope, the would face the

competition will be utilized to determine a vendor that can fulfill the Government's
technical requirements.

(a) Definitions. As used in this provision—

Backhaul, covered telecommunications equipment or services, critical technology, interconnection arrangements, reasonable inquiry, roaming, and substantial or essential component have the meanings provided in the clause 52.204-25, Prohibition on Contracting for Certain Telecommunications and Video Surveillance Services or Equipment.
(b) Prohibition.
 
(1) Section 889(a)(1)(A) of the John S. McCain National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2019 (Pub. L. 115-232) prohibits the head of an executive agency on or after August 13, 2019, from procuring or obtaining, or extending or renewing a contract to procure or obtain, any equipment, system, or service that uses covered telecommunications equipment or services as a substantial or essential component of any system, or as critical technology as part of any system. Nothing in the prohibition shall be construed to—

(i) Prohibit the head of an executive agency from procuring with an entity to provide a service that connects to the facilities of a third-party, such as backhaul, roaming, or interconnection arrangements; or

(ii) Cover telecommunications equipment that cannot route or redirect user data traffic or cannot permit visibility into any user data or packets that such equipment transmits or otherwise handles.

(2) Section 889(a)(1)(B) of the John S. McCain National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2019 (Pub. L. 115-232) prohibits the head of an executive agency on or after August 13, 2020, from entering into a contract or extending or renewing a contract with an entity that uses any equipment, system, or service that uses covered telecommunications equipment or services as a substantial or essential component of any system, or as critical technology as part of any system. This prohibition applies to the use of covered telecommunications equipment or services, regardless of whether that use is in performance of work under a Federal contract. Nothing in the prohibition shall be construed to—
(i) Prohibit the head of an executive agency from procuring with an entity to provide a service that connects to the facilities of a third-party, such as backhaul, roaming, or interconnection arrangements; or

(ii) Cover telecommunications equipment that cannot route or redirect user data traffic or cannot permit visibility into any user data or packets that such equipment transmits or otherwise handles.

(c) Procedures. The Offeror shall review the list of excluded parties in the System for Award Management (SAM) ( https://www.sam.gov) for entities excluded from receiving federal awards for "covered telecommunications equipment or services".

Description: This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial products or commercial services prepared in accordance with RFO FAR PART 12. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation. Offers are being requested and a separate written solicitation will not be issued. Solicitation number W911S626QA029 is issued as a Request for Quotation (RFQ) for Affinisep brand Solid Phase Extraction (SPE) sampling media. Please see the attached SF 1449 RFQ document for full requirement details and clauses. This acquisition is not set-aside for small business concerns. This solicitation incorporates provisions and clauses by reference. The full text of provisions and clauses may be accessed electronically at www.acquisition.gov. Notice of Intent to Sole Source (Brand Name) The U.S. Army Test and Evaluation Command (ATEC), Applied Sciences Division at Dugway Proving Ground (DPG) intends to solicit and negotiate on a sole-source basis with Affinisep USA, LLC. This acquisition is restricted to the brand-name Affinisep sampling media under the authority of FAR 12.201-1 for restricting competition for commercial acquisitions valued at or below the simplified acquisition threshold. As support for this brand-name restriction, this specific Affinisep media has undergone an extensive, multi-year Verification and Validation (V&V) process for chemical agent testing Programs of Record. No other brand or source can meet the Government's technical and regulatory requirements without rendering all test results scientifically invalid and non-compliant with established ISO 17025 procedures. Line Items & Quantities CLIN 0001: AttractSPE� Disks Bio - SDB SPE Disks for molecular biology purpose with PS-DVB sorbent, 47mm diameter, 20/pk (Part No: SPE-Disks-Bio-DVB-47.20-NF) Quantity: 13 Packs CLIN 0002: AttractSPE� Custom Made 102-Bio PS-DVB for biomolecular application Pads 10x20cm - 40/pk (Part No: SPE-Pads-DVB-Bio-T1.100x200.40) Quantity: 2 Packs CLIN 0003: Administrative and Shipping fees (Part No: SF100) Quantity: 1 Each CLIN 0004: Container - Pelican Quantity: 3 Each Description of Requirements These items are critical support consumables required for chemical agent testing. To ensure data integrity and compliance with ISO 17025 standards: Single Lot Sourcing: All 13 packs of disks and 2 packs of pads must originate from a single, documented production lot to eliminate batch-to-batch variability. Controlled Shipping Chain: To prevent chemical degradation, the items must be shipped in protective containers directly from the manufacturer (Affinisep USA, LLC) to the end-user. Procurement through third-party distributors is not authorized. Date and Place of Delivery and Acceptance Delivery Date: No later than 30 September 2026 F.O.B. Point: Destination Place of Delivery: U.S. Army Dugway Proving Ground, Dugway, UT 84022 Basis for Award The Government intends to award a contract to the responsible offeror submitting the lowest-priced, technically acceptable quotation. Technical Acceptability: Met by explicitly quoting the exact brand-name Affinisep items and providing a mandatory written guarantee that all media will be sourced from a single production lot and shipped in protective containers directly from the manufacturer. Price: Evaluated for fairness and reasonableness using price analysis. Submission of Offers Offerors may submit quotations in their preferred company format. Quotations must explicitly reference Request for Quotation # W911S626QA029. To be considered for award, the offeror�s quote must include: Completed pricing for CLINs 0001 through 0004. The written Technical Quality & Traceability Guarantees (Single lot sourcing & Direct-from-manufacturer shipping). Offeror's CAGE Code, Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) number, tax identification number, and discount/payment terms. A completed copy of the provision at DFARS 252.225-7000, Buy American�Balance of Payments Program Certificate (specifically identifying the country of origin for CLINs 0001 and 0002). Quotes must be submitted via email directly to the Contract Specialist, Amy Eilerts, at amy.m.eilerts.civ@army.mil. Mail and facsimile quotes will NOT be accepted. Submissions are required to be received no later than 10:00 AM MDT on Monday, August 17, 2026. All responsible sources may submit a capability statement, proposal, or quotation, which shall be considered by the agency. However, a determination by the Government not to compete this proposed contract based upon responses to this solicitation is solely within the discretion of the Government.

matters.text:
Federal notice (Sources Sought), COMMERCE, DEPARTMENT OF.NATIONAL INSTITUTE OF STANDARDS AND TECHNOLOGY.DEPT OF COMMERCE NIST
Title: Combined Sources Sought Notice and Notice of Intent to Award a Sole Source Contract for X-ray Computed Tomography Microscope
Solicitation number: NIST-AMD-NOISSN-26-30500006
PSC: 6650; NAICS: 334516
Description: Combined Sources Sought Notice and Notice of Intent to Award a Sole Source Contract for X-ray Computed Tomography Microscope Notice ID: NIST-AMD-NOISSN-26-30500006 Contract Opportunity Type: Sources Sought Response Date: August 18, 2026 at 11:00 AM ET Product Service Code (PSC): 6650 � Optical Instruments, Test Equipment, Components and Accessories NAICS Code: 334516 � Analytical Laboratory Instrument Manufacturing, with the small business size standard of 1,000 Employees BACKGROUND The National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) is conducting market research to identify alternative sources that (a) are capable of meeting NIST�s minimum requirements for the following commercial products and commercial services and (b) would be interested in competing for that requirement: The Precision Imaging Facility at the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) is involved in the characterization of metals, semiconductors, and insulators in support of multiple projects. Materials characterization allows NIST scientists to make direct correlations between material processing, (nano)structure, and resulting properties. This work involves the correlation of processing, structure, and properties of semiconductor material devices using three-dimensional X-ray computed tomography (XCT). Consistent with NIST�s mission to develop measurement science, a particular research focus is to evaluate the sources of systematic and statistical error that limit the efficacy of XCT techniques, to devise strategies to mitigate these uncertainties, and to develop metrics that quantify the results. The NIST PIF owns and performs research using a Zeiss Versa XRM 500 microscope system. The system is now over ten years old and is no longer eligible for technical service support from the manufacturer or any third parties. NIST now requires a new XCT microscope for micro-scale three-dimensional imaging of semiconductor materials and devices. The new microscope must meet the requirements detailed below and the ability to produce data which is compatible with data previously produced by NIST�s current Zeiss Versa XRM 500 microscope system. Line Item 0001: Description: X-ray Computed Tomography Microscope (One) The XCT instrument shall (1) accept prepared (e.g. a glass tube of powder) or bulk samples (e.g. a computer chip) for analysis, (2) generate a high-energy X-ray beam which is transmitted through the thin specimen, (3) detect the transmitted X-rays to produce an projected image of the specimen, (4) rotate and move the specimen using a built-in high-precision specimen while collecting additional images, and (5) use a software algorithm to reconstruct the collected images into a three-dimensional representation of the specimen. The system shall also include the following: System Resolution The system shall have an ultimate spatial resolution of 450 nm or smaller. The minimum achievable voxel size shall be 40 nm or smaller. The system shall be mechanically and electronically stable enough to perform continuous data collection actions that last up to 36 hours. X-ray Source: The X-ray source shall be a sealed tube X-ray source The source voltage shall be variable from 30 kV to 160 kV The maximum power output shall be 25 W or higher. All X-ray source parameters shall be fully controllable from the instrument control software. The instrument shall include all X-ray filters that are required to achieve optimal imaging performance for all X-ray powers, detectors, imaging modes, and software packages included in these specifications. The tool shall include a �filter wheel� or similar fixture to house multiple X-ray filters. The X-ray filters within the �filter wheel� shall be adjustable via the instrument control software without physical interaction with the tool. The X-ray source shall move as necessary to accommodate all lenses, detectors, and imaging modes. Specimen Stage: The specimen stage shall allow for 360� rotation of a specimen. The specimen stage shall have a minimum travel of: 50 mm in the X-direction (horizontal, perpendicular to the X-ray source) 100 mm in the Y-direction (parallel to the X-ray source) 50 mm in the Z-direction (vertical, perpendicular to the x-ray source) The stage shall accommodate specimens with a mass up to 25 kg Optics If required by the system design, the instrument shall include all lenses and other optics to attain the system resolution(s) in Section A of this document. The system shall include a two-stage optics-based magnification/detection system to leverage both geometric and optical magnification. The optical system shall include lenses with magnifications of 0.4X, 4X, 20X, and 40X. The optical system shall include a detector that is at least 60 megapixels Detectors, Cameras, and Imaging Modes The instrument shall include a visible light camera inside the radiation enclosure to visualize stage movements with the enclosure door closed. The system shall include a flat-panel type X-ray detector. The total detector size of shall be 6 megapixels or more. The flat panel detector shall allow for a spatial resolution of 12 �m or smaller. The system shall include all required optics, lenses, detectors, or imaging modes to allow for the maximum resolution specified in Section A of this document. The system shall include all lenses, detectors, software, and imaging modes required to enable a wide-field imaging mode using one of the standard detectors listed in item b above. The system shall include all lenses, detectors, software, and imaging modes require to enable a wide-field imaging mode with a maximum 2D field of view of 140 mm x 93 mm. The system shall be field upgradable to include a diffraction contrast tomography imaging mode, including all detectors, hardware, and software to enable diffraction contrast tomography. Software The instrument shall include software that provides full control over the instrument, including, but not limited to: Adjusting X-ray energy and/or power Moving all instrument stages in all dimensions Starting, stopping, or modifying data acquisition Saving all data and metadata in an accessible, open format and/or providing full, easy to use export to open formats such as hdf5 or similar for both raw (projection, stage motions, etc.) and processed (3D reconstructions, volumetric resolutions, etc.) data and metadata. The Contractor shall include software and associated licenses to provide support for 3D reconstruction of tomographic datasets. This software shall include: Standard 3D reconstruction of tomographic data sets. Vertical stitching of tomographic data sets to allow for higher effective vertical field of view Segmenting, virtual sectioning, and manipulation of reconstructed 3D tomographic data sets. The Contractor shall provide acquisition and reconstruction software that is integrated with modern artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) algorithms. These algorithms shall allow a user to enhance reconstruction, speed up reconstruction, enhance data collection, or speed up data collection. This integrated acquisition and reconstruction software shall be licensed (with software updates) for a minimum of two years. The instrument shall include a software API such that the instrument can be fully controlled using a common scripting language. The API shall include robust documentation for all API functions. Vacuum System: All vacuum pumps and/or vacuum pumping systems that are required by or included with the system shall be oil free. All routine operations of any vacuum system shall be integrated into the instrument control software with software/hardware interlocks that prevent users from accidentally venting any or all of the vacuum system. attachments.text:
SPECIFICATIONS AND DESCRIPTIONS
The following specifications must be met in order to fulfill this bona fide need, justified by this
procurement request.
The drone platform must be able to support multiple spectral sensors, including the dual camera
Micasense RX, and WIRIS thermal camera. The platform must be able to support the sensor payload as
well as allow exchanging payloads based on the mission requirements. Even with the addition of the
sensor payloads the platform must have a flight time 15 minutes or greater to allow for harmful algal
bloom mapping. The platform must pass the NOAA UAS requirements to meet the airworthiness
certification for the Wide Area Field Operations. The platform must be covered under NOAA UAS
training program in order to meet the NOAA training requirement. The platform must be compliant
under all UAS regulations from both the (National Defense Authorization Act) NDAA and FCC.
The technical specifications for the Astro drone platform are listed below in detail.
Specifications in Detail:
General:
Capable of supporting multispectral payloads
Customizable mount for a variety of sensor integration
Provide flight time ≥15min under payload
Approved NOAA UAS platform
Astro Platform:
Unfolded Diameter: 55.4” (1407 mm)
Empty Weight: 6.8 lbs. (3095 g)
Maximum Payload: 3.3 lbs. (1500 g)
Maximum Gross Weight for Takeoff: 14.7 lbs. (6665 g)
Flight Time (No Payload): 39 min
Flight Time (Full Payload): 25 min
Payload Mounts: Vibration Isolated, Smart Dovetail
Operating Temperature: -4° –122 °F (-20° – 50°C)
Available I/O Connections: VBAT Power Out, USB C, PWM, UART, TELEM, CAN
Flight Controller:
Onboard Modules: Cortex-A53 Computer, LTE
Connectivity: BLE, Wifi, USB C, LTE (North America)
Supported Radios: Freefly Pilot Pro
Supported GNSS: L1/L2 GPS, GLONASS, Beidou and Galileo bands
Batteries:
Battery Chemistry: Lithium-Ion
Battery Voltage: 21.6V
Capacity: 157 Wh
Communications: OLED User Screen CAN
Continuous Current 80 A
Max Peak Current 120 A
Operating Temperature: -4° –122 °F (-20° – 50°C)
RTK:
Multi-band system with centimeter level precision
GNSS provides stable height and position holding capabilities

***NOTE TO VENDORS: All responses to vendor questions are noted in RED.***
1. The SOW requires cages to have the option of arriving pre-filled with Alpha-Dri bedding,
but the Price/Cost Schedule lists standard mouse and rat cage-bottom part numbers and
no separate pre-bedded CLINs. Please confirm whether the quantities are intended to
be:
a. empty cage bottoms;
b. pre-bedded Alpha-Dri bottoms; or
c. available in either configuration at the same CLIN price.
They are intended to be empty cage bottoms. The Statement of Work has been
updated to remove the statement that “These cages need to have the option of
coming pre-filled with rodent bedding of a specific type (Alpha Dri).” Please see
the attached pdf titled S02 - 36C26326R0068 - Updated 07-31-2026.
2. Does the 7–10-day delivery requirement mean calendar or business days?
Please use calendar days. The Statement of Work has been updated to specify
calendar days. Please see the attached pdf titled S02 - 36C26326R0068 - Updated
07-31-2026.
3. Does the 7–10-day requirement apply to the initial rack and equipment order as well as
recurring consumables?
No. This has been updated in the Statement of Work as well as being stated here.
To clarify, orders are expected to be done on an estimated monthly basis. For
orders $10,000.00 or under, the order must be delivered within 14 calendar days of
the order being processed. For orders exceeding $10,000.00, the order must be
delivered within 30 calendar days of the order being processed. So, for the initial
rack and equipment order that is expected to exceed $10,000.00, the order is
expected to be delivered within 30 calendar days of the order being processed.
Please see the attached pdf titled S02 - 36C26326R0068 - Updated 07-31-2026.
4. Please confirm whether the initial quantities in Ordering Period 1 are expected to be
ordered immediately following award and delivered by September 30, 2026.
Yes, the intent is to immediately place an order for Ordering Period 1 for the initial
consumables (cages) with the initial order of the racks. They are expected to be
ordered immediately following award; delivery would occur as stipulated (by
September 30, 2026).
5. Each ordering period includes one “Shipping Costs” CLIN, although multiple delivery
orders may be placed during that period. Should the shipping CLIN represent:
a. Freight for each individual delivery order
b. An annual aggregate freight charge
c. Freight for the estimated annual quantities?
Page 2 of 4
The Shipping CLIN for each ordering period has been updated to reflect a Quantity
of 12 and Unit of Month. For each ordering period, a Delivery Order
encompassing the entire year will be issued with applicable funding information.
Each month, depending on study needs, supplies are expected to be ordered off
the Ordering Period’s Delivery Order. Offerors should price this CLIN with the
expectation of one estimated order each month. Offerors should recognize that
as the monthly order is an estimate, there may be times when more than one order
is placed during a month within the Ordering Period.
6. If multiple delivery orders are placed during an ordering period, how should incremental
freight be invoiced?
See the answer to Question 5.
7. The SOW requires installation/setup and training, including representative travel “as
needed” at no additional cost. Please define:
a. Expected number of visits;
b. Anticipated duration;
c. Number of shifts or training sessions;
d. Whether the requirement is limited to initial installation
e. Whether additional visits requested after initial installation will be reimbursable
The Contractor shall provide a Contractor representative for installation/set up
purposes and training. The Contractor must include one visit to assemble the
racks and give a one-time training on how to use the racks. The duration of this
training is estimated at, but not limited to, 1-3 hours. The installation and training
shall take place during the tours of the Veterinary Medical Unit team (6:00am –
2:30pm Central Time, Monday – Friday, excluding federal holidays). The
requirement would be limited to initial installation; additional visits requested after
initial installation would be reimbursable and would be paid for via Government
Purchase Card and new quotes. The Statement of Work has been updated to
reflect this information as well. Please see the attached pdf titled S02 -
36C26326R0068 - Updated 07-31-2026.
8. Are replacement rack filters or other recurring equipment-maintenance components
expected under the IDIQ? If so, please identify the applicable CLINs and estimated
quantities.
Yes, additional CLINs have been added to the solicitation document. Please see
the attached pdf titled S02 - 36C26326R0068 - Updated 07-31-2026.
9. Please confirm the period-six quantities, particularly the 5,000 mouse lids, bottoms and
feeders compared with only 1,000 mouse water bottles.
The correct amount should be 5,000 mouse water bottles. The CLIN for Ordering
Period 6 has been updated to correct this. Please see the attached pdf titled S02 -
36C26326R0068 - Updated 07-31-2026.
Page 3 of 4
10. Will the Government accept a separate Excel pricing schedule in addition to the
completed solicitation, or must all pricing be entered directly into the SF 1449
continuation pages?
Yes, the Offeror may provide this information in a separate Excel spreadsheet
provided that all information for every line item in the Price/Cost Schedule is

The North American Industrial Classification System (NAICS) code for this effort is 334516. The Department of Energy has accepted the deviations of RFO Part 12. This solicitation is issued as a full and open competition. All responsible business sources may submit a quotation for consideration by the Agency. BRAND NAME JUSTIFICATION: This brand name justification is written in accordance with RFO FAR 16.507-7(a) under the authority of 41 U.S.C. 3304 (a)(5) as implemented by RFO FAR 11.204. Haskel AGT-32/62 Two-Stage Gas Booster Roller Bar System is needed because the Haskel unit is required for compatibility with an existing rollbar booster system and to maintain standardization without changes to configurations and laboratory designs. The new Haskel roller bard system is required to plug in and play to the current infrastructure within the space allotted for the equipment. The following clauses apply to this acquisition: FAR Clause 52.212-1, Instructions of Offerors-Commercial Products and Commercial Services (DEVIATION NOV 2025) FAR Clause 52.212-4, Contract Terms and Conditions-Commercial Products and Services (DEVIATION NOV 2025) A full list of applicable provisions and clauses is available in FedConnect. Quoters shall include a completed copy of their Representations and Certifications with their quote or ensure that their SAM.gov profile is up to date. Representations and Certifications must conform to the RFO provisions. Interested vendors are to submit their quotation on the attached RFQ Standard Form (SF) 1449, and provide all supporting documents, as necessary, via the FedConnect portal at www.fedconnect.net by the due date and time indicated in Block 8 of the RFQ SF-1449. EVALUATION: Selection will be based on the quotation that is considered technically acceptable with the lowest firm-fixed price quote. The vendor shall be an approved and authorized reseller of the brand/manufacturer as of the submission date of their quote. The Government reserves the right to request vendors provide documentation that validates they are an approved and authorized reseller and that the products/services quoted meet the requirement. To be considered for evaluation, vendors must quote on all items/services listed in the solicitation. The Government anticipates issuing a single award from this RFQ. Vendors shall submit descriptive literature detailing features, technical capabilities and warranty data, as necessary. Technical acceptability shall be determined solely on the content and merit of the information submitted in response to this solicitation. Submission Requirements and Inquiries All quote and questions must be submitted electronically through FedConnect. Only those quotes and questions posted to FedConnect will be accepted. Quoter must register with FedConnect to respond as an interested party to submit quote, questions, and to view responses to questions. Questions will not be answered over the phone. The Contracting Officer must receive questions regarding the quote via FedConnect within 5 business days after the issuance of the quote. The Government reserves the right to not respond to any questions received after this timeframe. All responses to the solicitation questions will also be released on FedConnect referencing the RFQ number, with copies of both questions and answers, without reference to the originating sources. This is an electronic RFQ therefore no hard (paper) copies of the RFQ and related documents will be made available. attachments.text:
Attachment A – Specification Requirements
HASKEL AGT-32/62 TWO-STAGE GAS BOOSTER ROLL BAR SYSTEM
NETL requires one (1) Haskel gas boost roll bar system for delivering Carbon Dioxide (CO2) gas containing small amounts of impurities to experimental testbeds for interrogating the impact of impurities on materials performance exposed to high pressure CO2 environments. 
 The delivered roll bar system shall meet the following minimum specifications:
Haskel AGT-32/62 two stage roll pump with 32:1 and 62:1 pressure ratios.
Seals modified for CO2 service with minor impurities.
Maximum rated inlet pressure: 250 PSIG.
Maximum rated outlet pressure: 9000 PSIG.
Maximum drive air pressure 150 PSIG.

The system shall be a “plug and play” system that includes all the needed safety and control features and includes air controls (filter, regulator, pressure gauge, and speed control valve), inlet and outlet gas filters, inlet and outlet pilot switches with panel adjustable outlet pressure for automatic shutoff at user specified pressure, panel mounted gauges, relief valve, and all fittings and appropriate tubing plumbed and mounted in a rollbar frame.
The system shall be designed and constructed to American Society of Mechanical Engineers Boiler and Pressure Vessel Code standards. The vendor shall provide documentation on design of the system and operational manuals (including subcomponents).
Electrical components shall be OSHA National Recognized Testing Laboratory certified.
Shipping to NETL, 1450 Queen Ave., SW, Albany, Oregon, 97321 shall be included in the quotation.
FOB Destination.

HOW TO SUBMIT AN INVOICE FOR PAYMENT.
In accordance with FAR 52.232-33 invoices are paid by electronic funds transfer (EFT) routed to your company’s financial institution by the Oak Ridge Financial Service Center. Invoices shall be submitted electronically through the U.S. Department of Energy’s Vendor Inquiry Payment Electronic Reporting System (VIPERS) at https://vipers.doe.gov.  The customer service number for any registration/technical or invoice/payment related questions is 1.888.251.3557.   Please include the order number on the invoice. 
NOTICE OF INVOICE PROCESSING BY SUPPORT CONTRACTOR. 
A support service Contractor performs the function of processing of all invoices submitted to the National Energy Technology Laboratory, against its awards.  Therefore, this Contractor has access to price/rate information (where applicable).  A special provision in this Contractor’s award requires the confidential treatment by all Contractor employees of any and all business confidential information of other Contractors and financial assistance recipients to which they have access. 
ONSITE ACCESS SECURITY REQUIREMENTS.  
Services shall take place at the NETL Federal site in Pittsburgh, PA. The Contractor shall provide all U.S. citizens with valid (Real I.D.) photo identification to work under this requirement. The Contractor’s employees shall be restricted to those areas necessary to perform work under this requirement as well as direct routes to and from work site.  As applicable, delivery drivers must have a valid (Real I.D.) state driver license for the state in which they are operating.  Delivery drivers may be required to provide proof of valid (Real I.D.) state driver license upon entering the Government site. A.    All personnel working at the National Energy Technology Laboratory will be required to wear identification badges at all times.  The performance of this contract requires that employees of the Contractor have physical access to DOE-owned or leased facilities; however, this clause does not control requirements for an employee’s obtaining a security clearance.  The Contractor understands and agrees that DOE has a prescribed process with which the Contractor and its employees must comply in order to receive a security badge that allows such physical access.  The Contractor further understands that it must propose employees whose background offers the best prospect of obtaining a security badge approval for access. The following criteria, which are not all inclusive and may vary depending on access requirements, shall be considered reasons to deny access to NETL: 1.      Is, or is suspected of being, a terrorist;2.      Is the subject of an outstanding warrant;3.      Has deliberately omitted, concealed, or falsified relevant and material facts from any Questionnaire for National Security Positions (SF-86), Questionnaire for Non-Sensitive Positions (SF-85), or similar form;4.      Has presented false or forged identity source documents;5.      Has been barred from Federal employment;6.      Is currently awaiting a hearing or trial or has been convicted of a crime punishable by imprisonment of six (6) months or longer; or7.      Is awaiting or serving a form of pre-prosecution probation, suspended or deferred sentencing, probation or parole in conjunction with an arrest or criminal charges against the individual for a crime that is punishable by imprisonment of six (6) months or longer. B.     The Contractor understands and agrees that DOE may unilaterally deny a security badge to an employee and that the denial remains effective for that employee unless DOE subsequently determines that access may be granted.  The denial of a security badge to individual employees by DOE shall not be cause for extension of the period of performance of this purchase order or any Contractor claim against DOE. C.     The Contractor shall return to the Contracting Officer or designee the badge(s) or other credential(s) provided by DOE pursuant to this clause, granting physical access to DOE -owned or leased facilities by the Contractor’s employee(s), upon (1) the termination of this purchase order; (2) the expiration of this purchase order; (3) the termination of employment on this purchase order by an individual employee; or (4) demand by DOE for return of the badge. D.    The Contractor shall include this clause, including this paragraph (D), in any subcontract, awarded in the performance of this purchase order, in which an employee(s) of the subcontractor will require physical access to DOE –owned or leased facilities. All questions and compliance issues should be directed to the NETL Security Officer.*Specific details regarding the Real I.D. requirements will be provided by the technical point of contact to the contractor upon award.

Federal notice (Presolicitation), DEPT OF DEFENSE.DEPT OF THE AIR FORCE.FA4427  60 CONS LGC
Title: Sole Source Notice for L3Harris AN/PRC-163 Multi-Channel Handheld Radios
Solicitation number: FA442726QZ068
PSC: 5820; NAICS: 334220
Description: 1. This pre-solicitaion notice is in accordance with RFO 5.101(c). This is not a Request for Quotation (RFQ), a Request for Proposal (RFP), or an Invitation for Bid (IFB). The Government is not soliciting quotes or proposals at this time. 2. Description: Travis Air Force Base 60th Operations Support Squadron requires 8 (Brand Name) AN/PRC-163 Falcon IV Handheld Radios, in support of secure military communications. 3. Procedures for Award: The Government intends to issue a Request for Quotation (RFQ) and award a firm-fixed-price purchase order. The award basis is anticipated to include Technical and Price. The Government anticipate to award on or about 28 Aug 2026. 4. Trade Agreements Language: Not Applicable. 5. Technical Data: Not Applicable 6. Construction Contract Information: Not Applicable 7. Statement Regarding Responsible Sources: All responsible sources may submit a quotation, bid, or proposal, as appropriate, which will be considered by the agency. 8. Competitive Status IAW RFO 5.101(c)(4)(vii): This procurement is executed as a sole-source acquisition with L3Harris Technologies Inc. because the AN/PRC-163 Falcon IV is the only handheld radio possessing the built-in capability to meet the strict cryptographic and waveform mandates of AFTTP 3-3. To secure near-peer communications, the AN/PRC-163 interfaces directly with the USAF�s AN/PYQ-10 Simple Key Loader (SKL) to load mission-critical telemetry. Additionally, it is the only transceiver capable of maintaining simultaneous, multi-band connectivity with the KC-46 tanker fleet across its primary radio networks�including VHF/UHF LOS, SINCGARS, Havequick I/II, UHF SATCOM, and future SATURN waveforms. Because no other commercial radio possesses the hardware integration to bridge these vital systems without introducing severe cyber and operational vulnerabilities, L3Harris is the sole source capable of fulfilling this requirement. 9. Qualification Requirement: Must be authorized to supply the required items.

SPECIFICATIONS – Buchi S-300 (Brand Name or Equal) Mini Spray Dryer System
Background:
The acquisi(cid:415)on involves procuring a Mini Spray Dryer that will support our project “Emerging processing
and preserva(cid:415)on technologies to produce healthy foods and develop concept products”. A spray dryer is
a unit opera(cid:415)on used to dry food or liquid emulsions. The emulsion is sprayed out of a nozzle into micro
sizes and dried within seconds in a heated chamber, and the par(cid:415)culates are collected within the
chamber. The dried emulsion can be hydrated quickly and used as an ingredient in other food products.
The rapid drying helps to preserve nutrients. A spray dryer can also be used for microencapsula(cid:415)on to
encapsulate ac(cid:415)ve materials (flavors, drugs, probio(cid:415)cs) within a protec(cid:415)ve shell/matrix, forming a dry
powder, using heat to instantly evaporate solvent. This process provides long-term stability, controlled
release, and ingredient protec(cid:415)on.
The Buchi S-300 Mini Spray Dryer System is a small benchtop unit (62x64x105 cm). It is capable to safely
handle aqueous formula(cid:415)ons with up to 20% organic solvents. It is capable of producing par(cid:415)cles at a
fast rate in the range of 2-60 microns. The residence (cid:415)me is extremely low (<2s) ensuring the stability of
labile ac(cid:415)ve compounds. It also measures the product temperature in the collec(cid:415)on vessel using PT-1000
temperature probes for faster response and greater accuracy. The unit can also run in auto-mode. The
Buchi S-300 will be essen(cid:415)al in suppor(cid:415)ng our project.

Minimum Requirements:
- Must be a benchtop unit
- Must be compa(cid:415)ble with organic solvents
- Small par(cid:415)cle size (no bigger than 100 microns)
- Fast flow rate
- Short residence (cid:415)me (<2s)
- Product temperature measurement in collec(cid:415)on vessel
- Auto-mode capability to run samples una(cid:425)ended
- One year extended warranty
- Installa(cid:415)on

Description: Naval Surface Warfare Center (NSWC) Crane has a requirement for Thermistor Connectors. The proposed contract action is for the supplies or services for which the Government intends to solicit and negotiate with one source, Teledyne Instruments, INC, 162 Corporate Dr Portsmouth, New Hampshire, 03801-6815, United States under the authority of FAR 13.106-1. This is being sole sourced because only Teledyne has met this requirement and are currently qualified to build the connectors. These elements are all necessary and critical to enable both timely and accurate testing. All responsible sources may submit a capability statement, which shall be considered by the agency. However, a determination by the Government not to compete with this proposed contract based upon responses to this solicitation is solely within the discretion of the Government. The information received will normally be considered solely for the purpose of determining whether to conduct a competitive procurement. Contractors must be properly registered in the System for Award Management (SAM). Offerors may obtain information on SAM registration and annual confirmation requirements by calling 866-606-8220 or via the internet at https://sam.gov. This solicitation is being issued pursuant to the procedures at FAR Part 13. Synopsis exception FAR 5.202(a)(13) applies and Solicitation Number N00164-26-Q-0266 is hereby issued as an attachment hereto. All changes to the requirement that occur prior to the closing date will be posted to Contract Opportunities on https://sam.gov/. Federal notice (Special Notice), DEPT OF DEFENSE.DEPT OF THE ARMY.W6QK ACC-APG-ORLANDO
Title: Intent to Sole Source - Soldier Monitoring System (SMS)
Solicitation number: PANORL-26-P-0000-O27400
PSC: 5825; NAICS: 518210
Description: Notice of Intent to Sole Source Soldier Monitoring System (SMS) Life Cycle Management and Sustainment Office: U.S. Army Capabilities Program Executive for Simulation, Training, Testing and Threats (CPE ST3), Orlando, FL 32826-3276 Tentative Product Service Code (PSC): 5825 Radio Navigation Equipment � Except Airborne Tentative NAICS Code: 518210 Data Processing, Hosting, and Related Services Place of Performance: Multiple locations including Fort Benning, GA; West Point, NY; Fort Rucker, AL; Fort Sill, OK; Yuma Proving Ground, AZ; Fort Campbell, KY; Fort Bragg/Camp Mackall, NC. Description The U.S. Army Capabilities Program Executive for Simulation, Training, Testing and Threats (CPE ST3), Product Manager Combat Training Instrumentation Systems (PdM CTIS), intends to award a sole source, firm-fixed-price contract to Black Ohm, 100 S McClintock Dr. Ste 200 Chandler, AZ 85226, under the authority of RFO FAR 6.103-1, Only One Responsible Source and No Other Supplies or Services Will Satisfy Agency Requirements. Background & Objective The Soldier Monitoring System (SMS) is the Army�s materiel solution for Soldier monitoring, safety, and training performance analysis. Military training contains significant inherent risk, which is amplified during individual and isolated training such as land navigation. The SMS reduces these risks by providing persistent/real-time geo-tracking and automated alerts. The objective of this effort is to ensure continuity and delivery of efficient, effective, and quality services of upgraded or new solutions to the nation�s warfighters. Scope of Work The Contractor shall provide life cycle management to ensure SMS technology and equipment are maintained at or above 95% Availability (Ao) and provide necessary support desk capabilities. This effort enables PdM CTIS to perform life cycle management in support of SMS including Continuous Technology Refresh (CTR), technology insertion, concurrency, upgrades, and disposal. Support services required for this effort include maintaining or providing the following components: Monitoring Station (MS): Graphical tracking, device status/alerts, and After-Action Review (AAR) playback. The MS normally consists of a laptop and a network connection. Mobile Monitoring Device (MMD): Portable dismounted devices to monitor and locate Soldiers in the field. MMD normally consists of a tablet and a network connection. Soldier Worn Device (SWD): Small, rugged, waterproof GPS-enabled radios utilizing an LTE network with Soldier-initiated SOS capability. The SWD's built-in GPS transmits precise location and status data over LTE for real-time monitoring. Communication Network and SaaS: The SMS network connects devices via commercial cellular and LoRa to an AWS-hosted SaaS platform, accessible through an intuitive UI. Additional Services: Help desk support, field service, repair/replacement of damaged components, inventory management, training materials, and propagation studies. Period of Performance The anticipated Period of Performance (PoP) consists of one (1) 12-month Base Year and one (1) 12-month Option Year. Cybersecurity & Compliance Requirements The Contractor must ensure solutions incorporate secure engineering principles in accordance with NIST SP 800-160 and meet DoD Risk Management Framework (RMF) requirements to maintain a FedRAMP Moderate Authority to Operate (ATO). Strict compliance with OPSEC, AT Level 1, and CUI handling procedures is required. Submission Instructions / Public Note THIS NOTICE OF INTENT IS NOT A REQUEST FOR COMPETITIVE PROPOSALS. However, interested parties may identify their interest and capability to respond to the requirement or submit proposals. All responses received prior to the stated submission deadline will be considered by the Government. The Government is not responsible for any costs incurred as a result of responding to this notice. A determination by the Government not to compete this proposed contract based upon responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. Information received will normally be considered solely for the purpose of determining whether to conduct a competitive procurement. Capability statements, quotes, or proposals must be submitted electronically via email to the Point of Contact listed below no later than 07 August 2026 at 3:00pm. Contact Information 1. Primary Point of Contact Robert Verica, Contracting Officer Email: robert.j.verica2.civ@army.mil 2. Secondary Point of Contact Denis M. Serrano Maldonado, Contract Specialist Email: denis.m.serranomaldonado.civ@army.mil

Description: The U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) Forest Service (USFS) intends to issue a sole-source, firm-fixed-price contract to Vence Corp (16855 W Bernardo Dr, Ste 100, San Diego, CA 92127). The regulatory authority for this non-competitive commercial acquisition is FAR Subpart 12.2 (Streamlined Procedures for Commercial Products) and FAR 12.102 (Brand Name/Single Source Restrictions for Commercial Products). This procurement is for proprietary Vence Solar 24V US Base Stations to support the agency's Grazing Action Plan across western states. The USFS requires Virtual Fence (VF) base station towers to establish invisible containment barriers for domestic livestock grazing. This equipment minimizes physical boundaries, directly improving native wildlife habitat and migration corridors. Brand Name: Vence Model: Base Station, Solar, 24V, US (Self-Install and Assisted-Install Models Market research confirms that Vence is the only commercial provider capable of meeting the agency's strict technical and regional operational mandates: Proprietary Software Lock-in: Vence is the sole proprietor of the closed-source software required to communicate with and control the active livestock collar fleet deployed across the region. Alternative hardware cannot run this software. Regional Infrastructure Continuity: The USFS maintains a substantial capital investment in active Vence base station towers across multiple western districts. Introducing a non-Vence brand would fragment the grid, as competing architectures cannot interoperate with existing infrastructure. Avoidance of Duplication of Costs: Procuring an alternative system would require a total, cost-prohibitive infrastructure teardown and replacement of all active field assets and collars to maintain a single management interface. Zero Cellular Reliance: Vence hardware functions entirely via long-range radio frequencies, eliminating dependency on commercial cellular coverage in remote Forest Service lands. Data-Cost Shifting: The Vence commercial framework allows a hardware-only purchase, successfully shifting long-term recurring data subscription costs to external grazing permittees or partner non-profit This is not a request for competitive proposals, and no solicitation package is available. in accordance with FAR Part 12 streamlined commercial procedures, interested parties who believe they can fully meet the exact requirements listed above may submit a capability statement. Submissions must provide verifiable proof of seamless, out-of-the-box software and hardware compatibility with the agency's existing regional Vence infrastructure network. A determination by the Government not to compete this proposed contract based upon responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government.
