matters.text:
Federal notice (Special Notice), COMMERCE, DEPARTMENT OF.NATIONAL OCEANIC AND ATMOSPHERIC ADMINISTRATION.DEPT OF COMMERCE NOAA
Title: Notice of Intent to Negotiate a Sole-Source Contract - Sexton Corporation Underwater Cameras AFSC
Solicitation number: REQUIREMENTS-26-3133
PSC: 6760; NAICS: 334511
Description: NOTICE OF INTENT TO SOLE SOURCE NOAA's National Marine Fisheries Service - Alaska Fisheries Science Center - intends to negotiate, on a sole source basis, under authority of FAR 13.106-1(b)(1); with the Sexton Corporation, for the procurement of three (3) underwater camera systems which provide imaging during bottom and midwater trawls conducted in Alaskan waters. Researchers with the Alaska Fisheries Science Center utilize bottom and midwater trawls to assess populations of fish species and movements of those populations. This analytical work is conducted directly in support of Executive Order 14276 � �Restoring American Seafood Competitiveness�. Sole Source Justification The sole source determination is based on the need of NMFS researchers to accurately obtain information related to growth and movement of commercially valuable fish species. Researchers can then use this data to make recommendations for the expansion of some and reduction of other active fishing areas to support healthy fish populations. Sexton underwater cameras utilize an open-source image acquisition protocol which is compatible with existing data analysis software in use by AFSC research teams. AFSC researchers have developed extensive image analysis and visualization pipelines to better ascertain numbers and species of fish in groups sighted during trawl surveys. Special Notice This notice of intent is not a request for competitive quotes and no solicitation package is available. However, firms that believe they can provide equipment or service that fully meets the Government's requirements may submit substantiating documentation to the identified point of contact within 15 days after publication of this synopsis. Such documentation will be evaluated solely for the purpose of determining whether or not to conduct this procurement on a competitive basis. Responses can be sent via e-mail to jason.jenks@noaa.gov. A determination by the Government not to conduct a competitive procurement, based upon responses to this notice, is solely within the discretion of the Government. Oral communications are not acceptable in response to this notice. All responsible sources may submit a Capability Statement in accordance with this notice, which shall be considered by the agency if received on or before 1600 PM EST on Aug 13, 2026. The Capability Statement must contain material in sufficient detail to allow NOAA to determine if the party can meet all of the requirements. Incomplete statements do not warrant consideration. Phone calls in regard to this notice will not be accepted. All electronic correspondence shall have the subject line read: Announcement Number: REQUIREMENTS-26-3133 Project Title: NOAA NMFS MACE Underwater Camera upgrade FY26 NMFS�s AFSC Operations, Management, and Information Division requires that all contractors doing business with this office be registered with the System for Award Management (SAM). No award can be made to a company unless registered in SAM. For additional information and to register in SAM, please access the following web site: www.sam.gov. Background:

Installation Procedure:
Mobilization of equipment and materials
Develop Shutdown procedure for space in Building 409 on the VAMC Campus in Tomah, WI
Shutdown existing units and perform appropriate LOTO procedure
Evacuate/Recover existing freon system in preparation of existing Condensing Unit removal.
Remove and Replace Condensing Unit

Perform evacuation of sealed system and also perform a pressure test.
Recharge new system with freon
Perform any pre-programming required for new unit operation
Commission system for operation





B.8 Salient Characteristics
Daikin Variable Refrigerant Volume Outdoor Unit
Brand‑Name Only Requirement
Model: REYQ‑120AATJB

1. Brand‑Name Requirement
The Department of Veterans Affairs located at Tomah VA Medical Center: 500 East Veterans Street
Tomah, WI 54660 requires a brand‑name‑only Daikin Variable Refrigerant Volume (VRV) Outdoor Unit: Model REYQ‑120AATJB.
Alternate products or “equivalents” are not acceptable, as they will not integrate with existing indoor VRV units, controls, refrigerant systems, or facility programming.

2. Required Functional Characteristics
2.1 Outdoor Heat Recovery Condensing Unit
The unit must function as a Daikin Heat Recovery VRV condensing system, designed to support simultaneous heating and cooling operations.

3. Mandatory Technical Specifications
3.1 Electrical Requirements

Must operate on 208‑230V / 60 Hz / 3‑Phase power.

3.2 Compressor Technology

Must contain Daikin Inverter Scroll Compressors.
Compressors must be designed for and compatible with R‑410A refrigerant, to ensure interoperability with existing facility VRV systems that use the same refrigerant type

3.3 Condenser Coil

Aluminum‑fin / copper‑tube coil construction is required.

3.4 Controls Compatibility (Facility‑Specific Requirement)

Must accept field‑installed Daikin PCB control boards to interface with existing Generation III control architecture used in Tomah VAMC buildings.

3.5 Compatibility With Existing VRV System Architecture

Must integrate directly with installed indoor units (facility‑provided model REYQ120PBTJ and related VRV components).
No deviations in connectivity, control logic, or refrigerant piping design are permissible, as these may cause system faults or lengthy outages.


4. Installation Requirements

Units must be new, free from damage, and ready for installation.
Installation will be performed on‑site by local VA staff, with no additional training required.


5. Warranty Requirements

Manufacturer‑provided warranty must be included.
A 10‑year limited parts warranty is required as provided by Daikin’s authorized representative.



6. Delivery Requirements
Supplier must provide estimated delivery timeframes and coordination with the facility.
Units must be shipped FOB Destination to:
Tomah VA Medical Center
Warehouse Dept.
500 E. Veterans Street
Tomah, WI 54660

Manufacturing location =please confirm.

List of authorized distributors = please confirm.
Confirmation whether an equivalent domestic end product exists = please confirm.

8. Summary
The Daikin REYQ‑120AATJB unit must meet all specifications above to ensure safe, functional, and compatible operation within the existing VRV infrastructure at the Tomah VAMC. Requirements are based on the facility’s operational environment, existing VRV configuration, refrigerant compatibility needs, and prior system commissioning performed by Daikin OEM‑authorized personnel

Description: NOTICE OF INTENT TO SOLE SOURCE TO: SSK MILITARY INDUSTRIES INC. (UEI: K5NED6NJNYL6 / CAGE: 3DLD5) The 336 Training Support Squadron (TRSS) has a requirement for twenty-seven (27) Cypres Automatic Activation Devices (AADs), part number AAD2C1M1535L, for use at 336 TRSS located at Fairchild AFB, WA. The requested activation devices are a training specific item that meets Air Force requirements as stated in AFI 10-3503, Personnel Parachute Program, from April 2026, AFMAN11-301V1, and the USAF Personnel Parachute Program (PPP) Approve for Use List (AUL). The required activation devices are only manufactured/distributed by SSK Military Industries Inc (SSK). The Air Force Personnel Parachute Program Authorized Use List (AUL) mandates that the only authorized Automatic Activation Devices (AADs) are manufactured by SSK Military Industries Inc (SSK). This requirement is for military free fall parachute operations manufactured by SSK and specifically designed for free fall parachute systems as an emergency cutting device therefore a sole source purchase is justified. While competition for Cypres AADs is limited due to Air Force policy, an Internet search was conducted to look for authorized resellers of SSK equipment. A sources sought was posted on SAM.gov and SSK responded in confirmation that there are no authorized resellers of this product. Until other AAD products are authorized by the Air Force, SKK will continue to be the only source for the required activation device. The government will continue to monitor the updated Air Force Instructions for all future purchases of this nature to verify if competition is available. 5. JUSTIFICATION FOR THE AUTHORITY CITED ABOVE:
The item(s) listed in section one above is available from only one source and competition is precluded
for reasons indicated below. There are no substitutes available.
_X_ Compatibility: The item(s) must be compatible in all aspects (form, fit, and function) with
existing systems presently installed. Describe the equipment you have now and how the
new item/service must coordinate, connect, or interface with the existing system:
The Power and Energy Sciences Division at the United States Army Combat Capabilities
Development Command (DEVCOM) Army Research Laboratory (ARL) requires an
upgrade to an existing battery testing system. The MACCOR 4000H-48 system is
currently being used and operated in the Zahl Building at ARL (Z2A-16).The existing
system was purchased with 48 channels, as well as pre-wiring for an additional 48
additional channels. This procurement requirement will specifically focus on outfitting
these additional channels and thermocouple inputs to the existing cabinet. These
Template last updated 4/23/2018
channels must have a current range of -25 to 25A with a current accuracy of 0.025% of
the full-scale (FS). The voltage measurement range must be 0 to 5V with an accuracy of
0.02% of the full-scale. Due to compatibility with the existing system and hardware
interfaces the required procurement is only available from the original equipment
manufacturer (OEM), MACCOR, Inc.
The Maccor 4000H-48 is the only system with the required specifications and
compatibility with existing ARL test procedure files (developed on other DEVCOM ARL
Maccor systems). This will save DEVCOM ARL researchers significant time and
resources by avoiding creation of redundant procedure files and learning new user
interfaces/controls. In addition, the unique compatibility of the Maccor cycler with the
Associated Environmental Systems chambers used at ARL is not matched by any other
vendor. This includes patch cabling and direct interfacing with Associated Environmental
Systems “ATTPRIME” cell test fixtures. Beyond these compatibility aspects, no other
vendor offers a system with the specific/required current ranges and specifications
(accuracy, resolution, and measurement time).
Market research was conducted by , a materials engineer within
the battery science branch at ARL. searched on the General Supply
Schedule (GSA) website and contacted subject matter experts within the Government to
include (Chemist, FCDD-RLA-GD) and (Research
Materials Engineer, FCDD-RLA-GD). Market research concluded that MACCOR, Inc. is
the only company capable of meeting the Government’s minimum requirements.

data are described as follows:

experimental continuity:

warranty. Provide a brief explanation for the use of this reason and the impact that would
occur if the item was purchased from another manufacturer/provider:
___ Direct Replacement: These are “direct replacement” parts/components for existing
equipment and no substitutes exist.
_ Other reasoning to support a sole-source buy:
*************************************************************************************************
6. FAIR AND REASONABLE PRICE DETERMINATION:
It has been determined that the anticipated cost to the Government will be fair and reasonable and
that approval of this recommendation is in the best interest of the government. This justification is
accurate and complete to the best of my knowledge and belief.

In accordance with RFO 6.103-1(c)(2), the Government will allow for capacity statements for follow-on contracts. MDA is seeking alternate sources that can provide AFSS Integration to support the Missile Defense System test program. If no alternate sources are identified for the AFSS, the Government intends to issue a sole source modification on the MRBM T1/T2 Contract, HQ0147-14-C-0001 to Aerojet Rocketdyne Coleman Aerospace, Inc. (ARCA), CAGE 7VXX4, 7675 Municipal Dr., Orlando, FL 32819-8930 under Statutory Authority 10 U.S.C. 3204(a)(1) as implemented under Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 6.103-1(b) - Only One Responsible Source and No Other Supplies or Services Will Satisfy Agency Requirements. Based on currently available information, MDA believes that only ARCA is capable of providing the required AFSS integration services and interfaces without substantial duplication of cost that is not expected to be recovered through competition and unacceptable delays, since ARCA owns the MRBM T1/T2 Technical Data Package. The period of performance for this effort will be the existing contract period of performance ending in December 2029. Under the modification discussed above, the existing MRBM T1/T2 contract period of performance will not be extended. This notice is intended to meet the requirements of both FAR Part 5 and Defense Federal Acquisition Regulations Supplement (DFARS) Procedures, Guidance, and Information (PGI) 206.103-170. MDA is also seeking alternate sources that can provide Hypersonic Target Vehicle � 2 Integration Kits to support the Missile Defense System test program. If no alternate sources are identified, the Government intends to issue a sole source modification for Hypersonic Target Vehicle � 2 Kits on the MRBM T1/T2 Contract, HQ0147-14-C-0001 to ARCA, CAGE 7VXX4, 7675 Municipal Dr., Orlando, FL 32819-8930 under Statutory Authority 10 U.S.C. 3204(a)(1) as implemented under FAR 6.103-1(b) - Only One Responsible Source and No Other Supplies or Services Will Satisfy Agency Requirements. Based on currently available information, MDA believes that only ARCA is capable of providing the required services without substantial duplication of cost that is not expected to be recovered through competition and unacceptable delays, since ARCA owns the MRBM T1/T2 Technical Data Package and Interface Control Document. ARCA will integrate the Hypersonic Target Vehicle � 2 on its MRBM T1/T2 booster, modify test procedures for hard and soft mate, perform analysis and make minor modifications to the current Carriage Extraction System. The period of performance for this effort will be the existing contract period of performance ending in December 2029. Under the modification discussed above, the existing MRBM T1/T2 contract period of performance will not be extended. This notice is intended to meet the requirements of both FAR Part 5 and DFARS PGI 103-170. Description of the Requirement: MDA requires an Autonomous AFSS with an independent Flight Termination System (FTS) that replaces or supplements the command destruct system that renders a vehicle non-propulsive. The autonomous FTS determines if a vehicle termination is required based on vehicle trajectory, on-board tracking data, computing, and pre-designated decision termination criteria. The AFSS uses on-board tracking and system health data to determine if flight termination is required based on pre-determined criteria that is programmed into the system. When the pre-determined criteria are violated, the AFSS will initiate flight termination. The requirement for MDA to transition from command destruct flight termination to AFSS was introduced in the letter �Requirement to Establish Automated Flight Safety Systems into Ballistic Missile Defense System Targets and Interceptors� dated July 18, 2019. In response, Directorate for Test (DT) and Ground-Based Midcourse Defense have agreed to accommodate this transition. DT shall no longer provide traditional flight termination systems on its ship-based or land-based range assets beginning in 2030. The Hypersonic Target Vehicle � 2 missions require a more complex front end than the current Modified Ballistic Re-Entry Vehicle -7 (MBRV-7) or Hypersonic Target Vehicle � 1. MDA/Medium Range Targets will develop the Hypersonic Target Vehicle � 2 front end by performing additional system level analyses and concept of operation changes from the current MBRV-7 and Hypersonic Target Vehicle � 2 and ensuring the Hypersonic Target Vehicle � 2 will fit the current Coleman Front Section Common Interface Control Document. Then ARCA will integrate the Hypersonic Target Vehicle � 2 on the MRBM T1/T2 booster, modify test procedures for hard and soft mate, perform analysis and make minor modifications to the current Carriage Extraction System. Responses should also address the associated detailed schedule that supports AFSS integration and Hypersonic Target Vehicle � 2 Kit integration for air-launched MRBM T1/T2 targets. Responses should also address the cost estimate associated for the effort. JUSTIFICATION & APPROVAL
FOR OTHER THAN FULL AND OPEN COMPETITION
UNDER FAR PART 6 AS AUTHORIZED BY 41 U.S.C. § 3304
Pursuant to the Competition in Contracting Act (CICA), as implemented by FAR Subpart 6.1, this
Justification and Approval (J&A) support the use of the statutory authority to limit competition under FAR
6.103. This J&A is based on the facts and rationale contained herein, as required by FAR 6.104-1. In
accordance with FAR 6.104-1(a), each J&A shall, at a minimum, include the following information:
1. Identification of the Agency, Contracting Activity, and Specific Identification of the Document.
(a) Agency: Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA)
(b) Contracting Activity: Office of Acquisition (FA)
(c) Requiring Activity: Aviation Division (OA)
(d) Document Identification: J&A for Other Than Full and Open Competition

award for the purchase one (1) new Textron Beechcraft B360CER aircraft.

(c) Recurring Requirement: Yes No

3. Description of Supplies or Services: The Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) has a requirement for
the purchase of one (1) new Beechcraft King Air 360CER-67A/B300CER twin turbo-prop aircraft. This
aircraft will be utilized and operated by the DEA as a multi-role operational aircraft.
4. Identification of Statutory Authority Permitting Other Than Full and Open Competition:

5. A Demonstration that the Proposed Contractor’s Unique Qualifications or the Nature of the
Acquisition Requires using the Authority Cited:
Textron Aviation Inc. is the original and exclusive manufacturer of the King Air model B300 (marketed as the
model 360) aircraft.
Additionally, Textron Aviation is the holder of all licenses, copyrights, patents, intellectual property rights,
and the Type Certificate Data Sheet of the King Air model B300 aircraft. New King Air model B300 aircraft
are only offered by way of factory-direct sales with Textron Aviation.
The DEA’s Aviation Division (OA) established critical mission requirements for the acquisition of new
aircraft based on flight operations, maintenance and support management to define the mission requirements
for the aircraft needed. The following are the minimum requirements to meet DEA’s needs:
• minimum seating capacity of two (2) crew members and eight (8) passengers to meet personnel
transport mission requirements;
• cargo door opening of at least 50 x 50 inches and 350 cubic feet;
• pressurized cabin to accommodate bulk cargo transport mission requirements;
• interior baggage/storage space of no less than 50 cubic feet;
• weight capacity of no less than 500 lbs. for flight crew and mission essential personnel baggage and
equipment.
This specific aircraft will allow the DEA to continue mission-critical flight capabilities that include conditions
of high ambient temperature and humidity resulting in high density altitudes. It is essential that the aircraft
have a high temperature/high altitude and long endurance performance capability. The aircraft must be twin-
engine turbine powered; thereby giving a greater margin of safety while performing extended overwater
flights. The above specifications are mission-critical due to extended over-water operational flights,
extradition flights, and heavy-load cargo transportation flights. No other similar aircraft on the market meets
these critical performance requirements. Without these specifications, any other aircraft type or frame other
than the Beechcraft King Air B300 series could lead to degraded mission capabilities.
Furthermore, DEA's current fleet of aircraft are made up of 96.4 percent of Textron products, including 51
Cessna, 10 Beechcraft and 20 Bell aircraft. Introducing a new airframe to DEA’s Aviation fleet would
negatively impact all aspects of operational readiness and result in increased incidental costs to the
Government beyond the purchase of the airframe. First, use of a different airframe would increase operational
downtime due to new training and rating requirements for both DEA pilots and maintenance staff. Currently,
pilot cadre operates in a highly streamlined operational environment and use of a consistent aircraft
manufacturer allows for effective transitioning between all DEA Textron models, as many models share
common avionics and type ratings, reducing pilot training time and overall management costs. Additional
airframes would require the introduction of new training requirements and type ratings ultimately increasing
cost and delaying the operational deployment of the new aircraft. Second, continuing operation of Textron
Aviation product allows for conformity within the existing Textron Aviation maintenance networks, parts
programs, and pilot training platforms without introducing unfamiliar manufacturer systems. Finally, DEA
has invested more than $20 million in spare parts, engines and components which support Textron platforms,
therefore reducing long term lifecycle costs and ensuring continued operational capabilities. DEA’s
significant investment associated with its Aviation operations and capabilities means that transitioning even
one plane from current Textron products and aircraft would result in increased costs, increased operational
downtime due to new training and rating requirements for DEA pilots and maintenance challenges. The
significant risks associated with the adaptation of new airframes supports DEA’s determination that it is in the
best interest of the Government to acquire the Beechcraft B360CER-67A aircraft.

Possible, Including Whether a Notice was or will be Publicized as Required by Part 5 and, if not, Which
Exception under Part 5 Applies:
A Source Sought Notice 15DDHQ26N00000016 was posted on SAM.gov on 04/10/2026 to identify potential
sources. The notice closed on 05/07/2026. Following receipt of seven (7) responses from interested vendors, it
was confirmed that only Textron Aviation can provide a new King Air 360CER (B300CER) aircraft.
A Notice of Intent to Sole Source will be posted to SAM.gov pursuant to Federal Acquisition Regulation
(FAR) part 5.1.
7. Contracting Officer’s Determination that the that the Anticipated Cost to the Government will be
Fair and Reasonable:
Considering this is a non-competitive contract action, the Contracting Officer, at a minimum, will utilize the
following techniques to determine the vendor’s proposed price is fair and reasonable: (a) Comparison of
proposed price with price’s paid for the same or similar items by the Government; and (b) Comparison of the
proposed price with the Government’s Independent Cost Estimate (IGCE).
8. Market Research Conducted (See Part 10) and the Results or a Statement of the Reason Market
Research was not Conducted: See section 6 above.
9. Any Other Facts Supporting Using Other than Full and Open Competition. No vendors outside of
Textron Aviation were determined capable of providing either an aircraft fully compatible with DEA’s
existing pilot ratings and training platforms and maintenance programs or a new Beechcraft B360CER
aircraft.
10. A Listing of Sources, if any, that Expressed an Interest in the Acquisition in Writing.
BR Consulting LL, Jadaya LLC, Jones Aviation Group, MAG Aerospace, Starlight LLC, Textron Aviation,
and Vertical Acquisition Group.
11. A Statement of the Actions, if any, the Agency May Take to Remove or Overcome any Barriers to
Competition Before any Subsequent Acquisition for the Supplies or Services Required. There have been
numerous attempts to foster competition for this requirement. OA has an extensive history with this aircraft
and has performed years of market research and has determined that the Textron/Beechcraft King Air
360CER (B300CER) is the only aircraft that meets the mission/operational needs underlying the current
requirement. OA will continue to monitor the global aviation industry and attend expositions and conferences
where aircraft manufactures display new aircraft developments to identify other aircraft that will meet the
operational requirements of DEA Aviation.

matters.text:
Federal notice (Solicitation), DEPT OF DEFENSE.DEPT OF THE AIR FORCE.FA4855  27 SOCONS LGC
Title: 20 SOAMXS Compact Mini Crawler Cranes � SpyderCrane URW375/URW376 Brand Name or Equal
Solicitation number: FA485526Q0055
PSC: 3950; NAICS: 333923
Description: Notice to Offeror(s): Funds are not presently available for this effort. No award will be made under this solicitation until funds become available. The Government reserves the right to cancel this solicitation, either before or after the closing date. In the event the Government cancels this solicitation, the Government has no obligation to reimburse any offeror for any costs. DESCRIPTION The 20th Special Operations Aircraft Maintenance Squadron requires two new, unused, current-production compact mini crawler cranes/spider cranes to support CV-22 aircraft maintenance lifting operations. The cranes will be used in restricted-access and limited-maneuverability areas where hangar lifting equipment, fixed lifting equipment, or conventional mobile crane support is unavailable or impractical. The cranes must be suitable for aircraft maintenance operations on paved and unimproved surfaces and must be sufficiently compact and transportable to support temporary-duty, deployed, and austere operating environments. Each crane shall be furnished as a complete and operational system. The acquisition also includes the accessories and support items identified in the solicitation pricing schedule, including: Single-person, boom-tip-mounted work platform; Heavy-duty protective crane covers in tan; Non-marking tracks suitable for aircraft maintenance and hangar environments; Hydraulic tilt-deck trailer; Track mats; Two-year spare-parts and maintenance-support package; Manufacturer warranty coverage; Manufacturer operating, maintenance, safety, and technical documentation; Parts availability; and Technical and maintenance support. Operator training is not required under this acquisition. 2. Brand Name or Equal The brand-name reference is SpyderCrane URW375/URW376 or equal. The brand name is used to describe the configuration, quality, compact transportability, lift performance, controls, safety systems, accessory compatibility, field-operating capability, and supportability required to satisfy the Government's aircraft maintenance mission. Use of the brand-name reference does not preclude competition. An equal product will be considered when the quoter demonstrates that the offered product meets or exceeds every minimum salient physical, functional, and performance characteristic stated in this solicitation. FAR 52.211-6, Brand Name or Equal, applies to this acquisition. 3. Minimum Salient Characteristics A. Configuration The offered product shall be a compact, crawler-mounted mini crane/spider crane suitable for aircraft maintenance lifting operations in restricted-access and limited-maneuverability areas. The crane shall include a hydraulically telescoping boom, crawler-mounted mobility, and a multi-position stabilizing outrigger system capable of supporting safe lifting operations. B. Load and Working-Radius Capability Official manufacturer load charts shall demonstrate that the offered crane is capable of safely lifting not less than 5,000 pounds at a 10-foot working radius. The documentation shall identify the applicable: Boom length and configuration; Working radius; Outrigger or stabilizer configuration; Parts-of-line and hook-block configuration; and Operating conditions or limitations applicable to the rated capacity. Maximum advertised crane capacity alone is insufficient. The required capacity at the specified working radius must be shown in an official manufacturer load chart. C. Hook Height The crane shall provide a hook or boom-tip height of not less than 41 feet, without relying on a modification. The quoter shall provide official manufacturer documentation identifying the offered crane's maximum standard-boom hook or tip height and any applicable operating limitations. D. Load-Chart Verification Official manufacturer load charts must show rated lifting capacities at the applicable working radii, boom configurations, outrigger configurations, and hook heights. Generic capacity statements, maximum-capacity ratings, marketing literature without a supporting load chart, or unsupported statements from a dealer or reseller will not satisfy this requirement. E. JP-8 Fuel Compatibility The crane shall be furnished in a manufacturer-approved configuration capable of operating on JP-8 fuel. The quotation must include written documentation from the original equipment manufacturer confirming JP-8 compatibility. The documentation shall address: Engine compatibility; Fuel-system compatibility; Emissions-system compatibility; Manufacturer warranty coverage during JP-8 operation; JP-8-specific maintenance requirements; and Any restrictions, limitations, or required modifications associated with JP-8 operation. A general diesel-fuel rating or an unsupported dealer, distributor, or reseller statement is insufficient. The proposed crane will be determined technically unacceptable if the manufacturer does not confirm JP-8 compatibility. F. Mobility and Transportability The crane shall be crawler-mounted and suitable for operation on unimproved surfaces, ramps, and limited-access aircraft maintenance areas. Travel or fully stowed dimensions shall not exceed: Width: 51 inches; Height: 71 inches; Length: 171 inches; and Crane weight: 8,760 pounds. Dimensions shall be measured with the crane in its normal transport configuration, with the boom, outriggers, hook, and permanently installed equipment fully stowed. The crane shall be sufficiently compact and transportable to support the Government's aircraft deployment and transportation requirements. G. Stabilization The crane shall include an outrigger or stabilizer system capable of supporting safe lifting operations on paved and unimproved surfaces. The system shall include outrigger and boom interlocks, stability monitoring, or an equivalent manufacturer-installed system that prevents crane operation outside the authorized load and stability configuration. H. Operator Controls The crane shall include: Full-function wireless or radio remote-control capability; Onboard operator controls; Variable or proportional controls suitable for precise load positioning; and Emergency-stop capability. The control system must permit safe and precise load positioning in restricted aircraft maintenance areas. I. Safety Systems The offered crane shall include, at a minimum: Load Moment Indicator or equivalent rated-capacity monitoring system; Anti-two-block system; Over-winding prevention device or equivalent protection; Automatic winch brake or equivalent braking system; Emergency-stop capability; Outrigger and boom interlock monitoring; Hydraulic pressure-relief protection; Minimum wire-rope automatic stop or equivalent protection; and Automatic hook-stow system or equivalent secure transport configuration. Safety systems shall be installed or approved by the original equipment manufacturer. J. Boom and Crane Operation The crane shall include: Hydraulically telescoping boom; Continuous or unrestricted 360-degree swing operation; Positive boom and hydraulic holding valves; Onboard diagnostic capability; and Rated-capacity monitoring appropriate for the crane's boom, radius, and outrigger configuration. K. Accessories All accessories shall be compatible with and approved by the crane's original equipment manufacturer. Accessories shall not invalidate or reduce the manufacturer's crane certification, safety rating, rated lifting capability, or warranty coverage. The boom-tip-mounted work platform must be approved for use with the offered crane and include all required attachment components, controls, safety devices, and documentation. The non-marking tracks shall be suitable for use on aircraft maintenance and hangar flooring. The hydraulic tilt-deck trailer shall be sized and rated for safe transportation of the offered crane and the associated accessories. The trailer shall include all necessary tie-down points, ramps or hydraulic loading components, and track mats identified in the pricing schedule. L. Warranty and Support The offered equ

Telecommunications Equipment or Services, of this solicitation.

matters.text:
Federal notice (Solicitation), DEPT OF DEFENSE.DEPT OF THE AIR FORCE.FA4855  27 SOCONS LGC
Title: 20 SOAMXS Compact Mini Crawler Cranes � SpyderCrane URW375/URW376 Brand Name or Equal
Solicitation number: FA485526Q0055
PSC: 3950; NAICS: 333923
Description: Notice to Offeror(s): Funds are not presently available for this effort. No award will be made under this solicitation until funds become available. The Government reserves the right to cancel this solicitation, either before or after the closing date. In the event the Government cancels this solicitation, the Government has no obligation to reimburse any offeror for any costs. DESCRIPTION The 20th Special Operations Aircraft Maintenance Squadron requires two new, unused, current-production compact mini crawler cranes/spider cranes to support CV-22 aircraft maintenance lifting operations. The cranes will be used in restricted-access and limited-maneuverability areas where hangar lifting equipment, fixed lifting equipment, or conventional mobile crane support is unavailable or impractical. The cranes must be suitable for aircraft maintenance operations on paved and unimproved surfaces and must be sufficiently compact and transportable to support temporary-duty, deployed, and austere operating environments. Each crane shall be furnished as a complete and operational system. The acquisition also includes the accessories and support items identified in the solicitation pricing schedule, including: Single-person, boom-tip-mounted work platform; Heavy-duty protective crane covers in tan; Non-marking tracks suitable for aircraft maintenance and hangar environments; Hydraulic tilt-deck trailer; Track mats; Two-year spare-parts and maintenance-support package; Manufacturer warranty coverage; Manufacturer operating, maintenance, safety, and technical documentation; Parts availability; and Technical and maintenance support. Operator training is not required under this acquisition. 2. Brand Name or Equal The brand-name reference is SpyderCrane URW375/URW376 or equal. The brand name is used to describe the configuration, quality, compact transportability, lift performance, controls, safety systems, accessory compatibility, field-operating capability, and supportability required to satisfy the Government's aircraft maintenance mission. Use of the brand-name reference does not preclude competition. An equal product will be considered when the quoter demonstrates that the offered product meets or exceeds every minimum salient physical, functional, and performance characteristic stated in this solicitation. FAR 52.211-6, Brand Name or Equal, applies to this acquisition. 3. Minimum Salient Characteristics A. Configuration The offered product shall be a compact, crawler-mounted mini crane/spider crane suitable for aircraft maintenance lifting operations in restricted-access and limited-maneuverability areas. The crane shall include a hydraulically telescoping boom, crawler-mounted mobility, and a multi-position stabilizing outrigger system capable of supporting safe lifting operations. B. Load and Working-Radius Capability Official manufacturer load charts shall demonstrate that the offered crane is capable of safely lifting not less than 5,000 pounds at a 10-foot working radius. The documentation shall identify the applicable: Boom length and configuration; Working radius; Outrigger or stabilizer configuration; Parts-of-line and hook-block configuration; and Operating conditions or limitations applicable to the rated capacity. Maximum advertised crane capacity alone is insufficient. The required capacity at the specified working radius must be shown in an official manufacturer load chart. C. Hook Height The crane shall provide a hook or boom-tip height of not less than 41 feet, without relying on a modification. The quoter shall provide official manufacturer documentation identifying the offered crane's maximum standard-boom hook or tip height and any applicable operating limitations. D. Load-Chart Verification Official manufacturer load charts must show rated lifting capacities at the applicable working radii, boom configurations, outrigger configurations, and hook heights. Generic capacity statements, maximum-capacity ratings, marketing literature without a supporting load chart, or unsupported statements from a dealer or reseller will not satisfy this requirement. E. JP-8 Fuel Compatibility The crane shall be furnished in a manufacturer-approved configuration capable of operating on JP-8 fuel. The quotation must include written documentation from the original equipment manufacturer confirming JP-8 compatibility. The documentation shall address: Engine compatibility; Fuel-system compatibility; Emissions-system compatibility; Manufacturer warranty coverage during JP-8 operation; JP-8-specific maintenance requirements; and Any restrictions, limitations, or required modifications associated with JP-8 operation. A general diesel-fuel rating or an unsupported dealer, distributor, or reseller statement is insufficient. The proposed crane will be determined technically unacceptable if the manufacturer does not confirm JP-8 compatibility. F. Mobility and Transportability The crane shall be crawler-mounted and suitable for operation on unimproved surfaces, ramps, and limited-access aircraft maintenance areas. Travel or fully stowed dimensions shall not exceed: Width: 51 inches; Height: 71 inches; Length: 171 inches; and Crane weight: 8,760 pounds. Dimensions shall be measured with the crane in its normal transport configuration, with the boom, outriggers, hook, and permanently installed equipment fully stowed. The crane shall be sufficiently compact and transportable to support the Government's aircraft deployment and transportation requirements. G. Stabilization The crane shall include an outrigger or stabilizer system capable of supporting safe lifting operations on paved and unimproved surfaces. The system shall include outrigger and boom interlocks, stability monitoring, or an equivalent manufacturer-installed system that prevents crane operation outside the authorized load and stability configuration. H. Operator Controls The crane shall include: Full-function wireless or radio remote-control capability; Onboard operator controls; Variable or proportional controls suitable for precise load positioning; and Emergency-stop capability. The control system must permit safe and precise load positioning in restricted aircraft maintenance areas. I. Safety Systems The offered crane shall include, at a minimum: Load Moment Indicator or equivalent rated-capacity monitoring system; Anti-two-block system; Over-winding prevention device or equivalent protection; Automatic winch brake or equivalent braking system; Emergency-stop capability; Outrigger and boom interlock monitoring; Hydraulic pressure-relief protection; Minimum wire-rope automatic stop or equivalent protection; and Automatic hook-stow system or equivalent secure transport configuration. Safety systems shall be installed or approved by the original equipment manufacturer. J. Boom and Crane Operation The crane shall include: Hydraulically telescoping boom; Continuous or unrestricted 360-degree swing operation; Positive boom and hydraulic holding valves; Onboard diagnostic capability; and Rated-capacity monitoring appropriate for the crane's boom, radius, and outrigger configuration. K. Accessories All accessories shall be compatible with and approved by the crane's original equipment manufacturer. Accessories shall not invalidate or reduce the manufacturer's crane certification, safety rating, rated lifting capability, or warranty coverage. The boom-tip-mounted work platform must be approved for use with the offered crane and include all required attachment components, controls, safety devices, and documentation. The non-marking tracks shall be suitable for use on aircraft maintenance and hangar flooring. The hydraulic tilt-deck trailer shall be sized and rated for safe transportation of the offered crane and the associated accessories. The trailer shall include all necessary tie-down points, ramps or hydraulic loading components, and track mats identified in the pricing schedule. L. Warranty and Support The offered equ

matters.title: 20 SOAMXS Compact Mini Crawler Cranes � SpyderCrane URW375/URW376 Brand Name or Equal
matters.text:
Federal notice (Solicitation), DEPT OF DEFENSE.DEPT OF THE AIR FORCE.FA4855  27 SOCONS LGC
Title: 20 SOAMXS Compact Mini Crawler Cranes � SpyderCrane URW375/URW376 Brand Name or Equal
Solicitation number: FA485526Q0055
PSC: 3950; NAICS: 333923
Description: Notice to Offeror(s): Funds are not presently available for this effort. No award will be made under this solicitation until funds become available. The Government reserves the right to cancel this solicitation, either before or after the closing date. In the event the Government cancels this solicitation, the Government has no obligation to reimburse any offeror for any costs. DESCRIPTION The 20th Special Operations Aircraft Maintenance Squadron requires two new, unused, current-production compact mini crawler cranes/spider cranes to support CV-22 aircraft maintenance lifting operations. The cranes will be used in restricted-access and limited-maneuverability areas where hangar lifting equipment, fixed lifting equipment, or conventional mobile crane support is unavailable or impractical. The cranes must be suitable for aircraft maintenance operations on paved and unimproved surfaces and must be sufficiently compact and transportable to support temporary-duty, deployed, and austere operating environments. Each crane shall be furnished as a complete and operational system. The acquisition also includes the accessories and support items identified in the solicitation pricing schedule, including: Single-person, boom-tip-mounted work platform; Heavy-duty protective crane covers in tan; Non-marking tracks suitable for aircraft maintenance and hangar environments; Hydraulic tilt-deck trailer; Track mats; Two-year spare-parts and maintenance-support package; Manufacturer warranty coverage; Manufacturer operating, maintenance, safety, and technical documentation; Parts availability; and Technical and maintenance support. Operator training is not required under this acquisition. 2. Brand Name or Equal The brand-name reference is SpyderCrane URW375/URW376 or equal. The brand name is used to describe the configuration, quality, compact transportability, lift performance, controls, safety systems, accessory compatibility, field-operating capability, and supportability required to satisfy the Government's aircraft maintenance mission. Use of the brand-name reference does not preclude competition. An equal product will be considered when the quoter demonstrates that the offered product meets or exceeds every minimum salient physical, functional, and performance characteristic stated in this solicitation. FAR 52.211-6, Brand Name or Equal, applies to this acquisition. 3. Minimum Salient Characteristics A. Configuration The offered product shall be a compact, crawler-mounted mini crane/spider crane suitable for aircraft maintenance lifting operations in restricted-access and limited-maneuverability areas. The crane shall include a hydraulically telescoping boom, crawler-mounted mobility, and a multi-position stabilizing outrigger system capable of supporting safe lifting operations. B. Load and Working-Radius Capability Official manufacturer load charts shall demonstrate that the offered crane is capable of safely lifting not less than 5,000 pounds at a 10-foot working radius. The documentation shall identify the applicable: Boom length and configuration; Working radius; Outrigger or stabilizer configuration; Parts-of-line and hook-block configuration; and Operating conditions or limitations applicable to the rated capacity. Maximum advertised crane capacity alone is insufficient. The required capacity at the specified working radius must be shown in an official manufacturer load chart. C. Hook Height The crane shall provide a hook or boom-tip height of not less than 41 feet, without relying on a modification. The quoter shall provide official manufacturer documentation identifying the offered crane's maximum standard-boom hook or tip height and any applicable operating limitations. D. Load-Chart Verification Official manufacturer load charts must show rated lifting capacities at the applicable working radii, boom configurations, outrigger configurations, and hook heights. Generic capacity statements, maximum-capacity ratings, marketing literature without a supporting load chart, or unsupported statements from a dealer or reseller will not satisfy this requirement. E. JP-8 Fuel Compatibility The crane shall be furnished in a manufacturer-approved configuration capable of operating on JP-8 fuel. The quotation must include written documentation from the original equipment manufacturer confirming JP-8 compatibility. The documentation shall address: Engine compatibility; Fuel-system compatibility; Emissions-system compatibility; Manufacturer warranty coverage during JP-8 operation; JP-8-specific maintenance requirements; and Any restrictions, limitations, or required modifications associated with JP-8 operation. A general diesel-fuel rating or an unsupported dealer, distributor, or reseller statement is insufficient. The proposed crane will be determined technically unacceptable if the manufacturer does not confirm JP-8 compatibility. F. Mobility and Transportability The crane shall be crawler-mounted and suitable for operation on unimproved surfaces, ramps, and limited-access aircraft maintenance areas. Travel or fully stowed dimensions shall not exceed: Width: 51 inches; Height: 71 inches; Length: 171 inches; and Crane weight: 8,760 pounds. Dimensions shall be measured with the crane in its normal transport configuration, with the boom, outriggers, hook, and permanently installed equipment fully stowed. The crane shall be sufficiently compact and transportable to support the Government's aircraft deployment and transportation requirements. G. Stabilization The crane shall include an outrigger or stabilizer system capable of supporting safe lifting operations on paved and unimproved surfaces. The system shall include outrigger and boom interlocks, stability monitoring, or an equivalent manufacturer-installed system that prevents crane operation outside the authorized load and stability configuration. H. Operator Controls The crane shall include: Full-function wireless or radio remote-control capability; Onboard operator controls; Variable or proportional controls suitable for precise load positioning; and Emergency-stop capability. The control system must permit safe and precise load positioning in restricted aircraft maintenance areas. I. Safety Systems The offered crane shall include, at a minimum: Load Moment Indicator or equivalent rated-capacity monitoring system; Anti-two-block system; Over-winding prevention device or equivalent protection; Automatic winch brake or equivalent braking system; Emergency-stop capability; Outrigger and boom interlock monitoring; Hydraulic pressure-relief protection; Minimum wire-rope automatic stop or equivalent protection; and Automatic hook-stow system or equivalent secure transport configuration. Safety systems shall be installed or approved by the original equipment manufacturer. J. Boom and Crane Operation The crane shall include: Hydraulically telescoping boom; Continuous or unrestricted 360-degree swing operation; Positive boom and hydraulic holding valves; Onboard diagnostic capability; and Rated-capacity monitoring appropriate for the crane's boom, radius, and outrigger configuration. K. Accessories All accessories shall be compatible with and approved by the crane's original equipment manufacturer. Accessories shall not invalidate or reduce the manufacturer's crane certification, safety rating, rated lifting capability, or warranty coverage. The boom-tip-mounted work platform must be approved for use with the offered crane and include all required attachment components, controls, safety devices, and documentation. The non-marking tracks shall be suitable for use on aircraft maintenance and hangar flooring. The hydraulic tilt-deck trailer shall be sized and rated for safe transportation of the offered crane and the associated accessories. The trailer shall include all necessary tie-down points, ramps or hydraulic loading components, and track mats identified in the pricing schedule. L. Warranty and Support The offered equ

matters.title: REQUIREMENTS-26-4191 NOTICE OF INTENT TO SOLE-SOURCE TO INNOVASEA
matters.text:
Federal notice (Special Notice), COMMERCE, DEPARTMENT OF.NATIONAL OCEANIC AND ATMOSPHERIC ADMINISTRATION.DEPT OF COMMERCE NOAA
Title: REQUIREMENTS-26-4191 NOTICE OF INTENT TO SOLE-SOURCE TO INNOVASEA
Solicitation number: REQUIREMENTS-26-4191
PSC: 6640; NAICS: 334513
Description: NOTICE OF INTENT TO NEGOTIATE A SOLE-SOURCE PURCHASE ORDER THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR QUOTE. THIS IS A NOTICE OF THE GOVERNMENT�S INTENT TO ISSUE A SOLE SOURCE PURCHASE ORDER. National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) Fisheries, hereby gives public notice of the intent to negotiate a sole-source purchase order pursuant to the authority of 41 U.S.C. 1901, using simplified procedures up to $9M, in accordance with Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul (RFO) 12.201-1, as the supplies required by the agency are available from only one responsible source and no other services will satisfy agency requirements The government seeks products from INNOVASEA MARINE SYSTEMS CANADA, INC (INNOVASEA) for the acquisition of purchase acoustic telemetry equipment and supplies to quantify steelhead survival in Puget Sound. The delivery date is 90 days after award. The reason justifying this sole source procurement is that the Government believes only one responsible source can provide the equipment that will satisfy the agency's requirement. Northwest Fisheries Science Center (NWFSC), located at 7305 Beach Drive East Port Orchard, WA 98366, has an urgent need for scientific evidence describing the magnitude of pinniped impacts on Endangered Species Act (ESA) listed salmonids, and for analyses demonstrating the effects of proposed pinniped management actions. NWFSC is required to provide survival estimates for ESA listed steelhead in the Nisqually River to monitor effects of potential pinniped management actions. NWFSC needs to purchase 200 transmitters to implant into steelhead smolts and two (2) test tags to estimate detection efficiency. NWFSC needs 14 hydrophones to detect the tagged steelhead in order to monitor migration, estimate survival, and identify steelhead predators (13 additional receivers are being provided by a project partner for a total of 27 moorings). NWFSC also needs to purchase 27 acoustic-release rope canisters for yearly hydrophone retrieval and download, and a surface transponder to communicate with the receivers. NWFSC needs three (3) different rope canister line lengths to accommodate the various mooring depths in Puget Sound. The following VEMCO INNOVASEA products are required: ARC-150 Mooring recovery system (rope canister) ARC-300 Mooring recovery system (rope canister) NexTrak AR Transponding Acoustic release receiver VR100 Surface Transponder V7T-2x-A69-2951 Rounded case V7T-2x-A69-2951 Rounded case - delay programming V7T-2x-A69-2801 Rounded case - range test Responses to this notice must be provided within eight (8) calendar days from the date of this notice. This is a sole source notice published for informational purposes only and not a request for competitive quotes. Therefore, no solicitation document exists for this requirement. Vendors who believe they can meet this requirement are required to submit in writing an affirmative response demonstrating a comprehensive understanding of the requirement. All written responses must include a capabilities statement that determines the ability to provide an authorized reseller letter from INNOVASEA. The response must be sufficient to permit agency analysis to establish a bona fide capability to meet the requirement. Failure to submit such documentation will result in the Government proceeding as previously stated. A determination by the Government not to open the requirement to competition based upon responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. Affirmative written responses must be received no later than 2:00 P.M. Pacific Standard Time, July 31, 2026. The responses must be submitted via e-mail the Contracting Officer, Rachel Stone, at Rachel.Stone@noaa.gov.

matters.text:
Federal notice (Sources Sought), DEPT OF DEFENSE.DEPT OF THE NAVY.NAVFACSYSCOM MID-ATLANTIC
Title: Market research for brand-name specifications for Direct Digital Controllers utilizing software for Configuration/Programming and for Connection to the EMCS located at various government installations located in the Hampton Roads area, Virginia
Solicitation number: N4008526ML076
PSC: 4130; NAICS: 334512
Description: Market research for brand-name specifications for Direct Digital Controllers utilizing software for Configuration/Programming and for Connection to the EMCS located at various government installations located in the Hampton Roads area, Virginia Naval Facilities Engineering Systems Command, Mid-Atlantic (NAVFAC MIDLANT), is issuing this Sources Sought Notice for market research purposes only. This notice does NOT constitute a request for proposal, quote, and/or invitation for bid. The purpose of this notice is to determine the availability of Facility Related Control Systems (FRCS) building heating, ventilating, and air conditioning (HVAC) system Direct Digital Controllers with the following salient characteristics from responsible sources: Capability of controlling Heating, Ventilating, and Air-Conditioning (HVAC) systems. Capability of being operated using Automated Logic Corporation (ALC) software (WebCTRL� and EIKON� including SiteBuilder and ViewBuilder), Johnson Controls International PLC (JCI) software (Metasys� including System Configuration Tool and Controller Configuration Tool), Siemens Inc. software (Desigo� including ABT Site Engineering and Commissioning Tool) or Siemens, Inc. Apogee Building Automation System for their configuration and programming to create, modify, and download control programming, database, graphics, and controller configuration files and shall be installed by manufacturer authorized/trained/certified companies and individuals. Capability to connect to existing Energy Management Control Systems (EMCS) at government installations located in the Hampton Roads area, Virginia. Capability to obtain and maintain Authority to Operate (ATO) certification in accordance with Department of Defense Instruction (DODI) 8500.01 and DODI 8510.01. BACKGROUND: NAVFAC MIDLANT is working on multiple Class Justification and Approvals (J&As) for various projects across multiple installations in the Hampton Roads area, Virginia. These Class J&As would authorize the inclusion of brand-name specifications, under the authority of 10 U.S.C. 3204(a)(1), for Direct Digital Controllers utilizing software for Configuration/Programming and for Connection to the EMCS located at various government installations located in the Hampton Roads area, Virginia. It is anticipated that the proposed Class J&As will cover various construction projects from Fiscal Year (FY) 2026 to 2031. The ALC WebCTRL Building Automation System is a type of Direct Digital Controller (DDC) System that monitors and controls the HVAC system for a building. The WebCTRL Building Automation System consists of several hardware components including, but not limited to, building controllers, equipment controllers, central plant controller controllers, room controllers, routers and integrators. The WebCTRL Building Automation System also consists of the software necessary to operate the system in addition to allowing the integration of multiple WebCTRL Building Automation Systems. Further technical specifications pertaining to the WebCTRL Building Automation System can be found on ALC�s website at: https://automatedlogic.com The Johnson Controls International Metasys Building Automation System is a type of Direct Digital Controller (DDC) System that monitors and controls the HVAC system for a building. The Metasys Building Automation System consists of several hardware components including, but not limited to, building controllers, equipment controllers, central plant controller controllers, room controllers, routers and integrators. The Metasys Building Automation System also consists of the software necessary to operate the system in addition to allowing the integration of multiple Metasys Building Automation Systems. Further technical specifications pertaining to the Metasys Building Automation System can be found on JCI�s website at: https://www.johnsoncontrols.com/ The Siemens Desigo Building Automation System is a type of Direct Digital Controller (DDC) System that monitors and controls the HVAC system for a building. The Siemens Desigo Building Automation System consists of several hardware components including, but not limited to, Desigo PXC family of controllers, PXC4 and PXC5 Controllers, DXR controllers and TX-I/O modules. The Siemens Desigo Building Automation System also consists of the software necessary to operate the system in addition to allowing the integration of multiple Siemens Building Automation Systems. Further technical specifications pertaining to the Siemens Desigo Building Automation System can be found on Siemens website at: https://www.siemens.com/us/en.html The Siemens Apogee Building Automation System is a type of Direct Digital Controller (DDC) System that monitors and controls the HVAC system for a building. The Siemens Apogee Building Automation System consists of several hardware components including, but not limited to programmable building controllers, network controllers and routers, digital controllers, zone controllers, VAV controllers, unitary and equipment controllers, and expansion modules. The Siemens controllers will be configured and programmed using government-licensed Siemens software. The Siemens Apogee Building Automation System also consists of the software necessary to operate and maintain the system in addition to allowing the integration of multiple Siemens Building Automation Systems. Further technical specifications pertaining to the Siemens Apogee Building Automation System can be found on Siemens website at: https://www.siemens.com/us/en.html Based on internal Government research, the following was found to be sufficient preliminary rationale to permit other than full and open competition under the authority of 10 U.S.C. 3204(a)(1), Only One Responsible Source/Limited Number of Sources and No Other Type of Property or Services Will Satisfy the Needs of the Agency. Establish and maintain a defensible cybersecurity posture. Maximize utilization of existing government-licensed software to configure and program the controllers. Maintain installation networked facilities control and monitoring system so that all controllers can be programmed from a central station versus a hybrid system composed of many different controllers and associated configuration/programming software Avoid the significant operational burden and cost of having maintenance and engineering staff become proficient with the configuration, programming, commissioning, operation, and maintenance of controllers from multiple manufacturers. INSTRUCTIONS TO INTERESTED PARTIES: Please note that this is not a Request for Proposal (RFP), a promise to contract, or a commitment of any kind on the part of the Government. There will be no debrief, evaluation letters, and/or results to be issued to interested parties that choose to respond. Information obtained from this Sources Sought Notice is for market research purposes to determine whether another companies� similar products can meet, or be modified to meet, the Governments needs which will facilitate the decision-making process. matters.agency: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
matters.text:
Federal notice (Special Notice), HEALTH AND HUMAN SERVICES, DEPARTMENT OF.CENTERS FOR DISEASE CONTROL AND PREVENTION.CENTERS FOR DISEASE CONTROL AND PREVENTION
Title: Notice of Intent to Sole Source Serology DV-1-4 EDIII Reagents
Solicitation number: 99068
PSC: 6640; NAICS: 325413
Description: The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention intends to award a sole source firm fixed price purchase order/contract to UNIVERSITY OF NORTH CAROLINA -CH Microbiology & Immunology for custom-produced biotinylated EDIII antigens for Zika virus and dengue virus serotypes 1�4 are specifically designed for the CDC flavivirus serologic assay development and validation using streptavidin-based capture and multiplex immunoassay platforms. The requested HaloTag control antigen also provides a matched control for assessing nonspecific binding, assay background, and reagent-related signal. Published assay validation work using EDIII antigens demonstrated high sensitivity and specificity for distinguishing prior dengue and Zika virus exposure, supporting the technical need for these specialized reagents. Commercially available whole-virus antigens, full-length envelope proteins, NS1 antigens, non-biotinylated recombinant EDIII antigens, and generic flavivirus assay reagents were considered. However, these alternatives do not meet the Branch�s technical requirements. Whole-virus and full-length flavivirus antigens contain conserved epitopes that can produce substantial cross-reactive antibody binding between dengue and Zika viruses, reducing assay specificity. Non-biotinylated or differently tagged antigens are not suitable substitutes because the current assay workflow depends on biotin�streptavidin capture for stable antigen immobilization, consistent antigen orientation, and reproducible assay conditions. Generic or off-the-shelf antigens also may differ in sequence, tag configuration, purity, lot consistency, or manufacturing method, which could introduce unacceptable variability and compromise comparability with existing validation data and ongoing laboratory protocols. Use of alternative reagents would require additional optimization, bridging studies, and validation before they could be incorporated into existing workflows. This would delay laboratory testing and research activities, increase costs, and risk generating data that are not comparable with prior or ongoing assay development work. The selected supplier�s custom production of the required biotinylated EDIII and HaloTag control antigens is therefore necessary to maintain reagent consistency, assay performance, and continuity of the Dengue Branch�s serologic assay validation strategy. This contract action is for supplies/services for which the Government intends to solicit and negotiate with only one source under the authority of Revolutionary FAR Overhaul 6.103-1 (SAP) ; under the authority of 41 U.S.C. 1901, as implemented in FAR subpart 12.102. Interested persons may identify their interest and capability to respond to the requirement or submit proposals. This notice of intent is not a request for competitive quotations; however, all quotations/responses received within 15 days of the issuance of this notice shall be considered by the government. A determination by the government not to compete this proposed contract based upon responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the government. Information received will normally be considered solely for the purpose of determining whether to conduct a competitive procurement. Any quotation/response should be emailed to contract specialist at email qsx8@cdc.gov by August 6, 2026 before 5pm EST.

matters.title: 20 SOAMXS Compact Mini Crawler Cranes - SpyderCrane URW375/URW376 Brand Name or Equal
matters.text:
Federal notice (Solicitation), DEPT OF DEFENSE.DEPT OF THE AIR FORCE.FA4855  27 SOCONS LGC
Title: 20 SOAMXS Compact Mini Crawler Cranes - SpyderCrane URW375/URW376 Brand Name or Equal
Solicitation number: FA485526Q0053
PSC: 3950; NAICS: 333923
Description: The 27th Special Operations Contracting Squadron, Cannon Air Force Base, New Mexico, is issuing Solicitation FA485526Q0046 as a Request for Quotation (RFQ) for two compact mini crawler cranes, commonly referred to as spider cranes, SpyderCrane URW375/URW376 brand name or equal, and associated accessories and support items. The Government anticipates awarding a single Firm-Fixed-Price purchase order. This acquisition is a 100-percent small business set-aside. NAICS 333923 - Overhead Traveling Crane, Hoist, and Monorail System Manufacturing PSC 3950 - Winches, Hoists, Cranes, and Derricks 1. Requirement The 20th Special Operations Aircraft Maintenance Squadron requires two new, unused, current-production compact mini crawler cranes/spider cranes to support CV-22 aircraft maintenance lifting operations. The cranes will be used in restricted-access and limited-maneuverability areas where hangar lifting equipment, fixed lifting equipment, or conventional mobile crane support is unavailable or impractical. The cranes must be suitable for aircraft maintenance operations on paved and unimproved surfaces and must be sufficiently compact and transportable to support temporary-duty, deployed, and austere operating environments. Each crane shall be furnished as a complete and operational system. The acquisition also includes the accessories and support items identified in the solicitation pricing schedule, including: Single-person, boom-tip-mounted work platform; Heavy-duty protective crane covers in tan; Non-marking tracks suitable for aircraft maintenance and hangar environments; Hydraulic tilt-deck trailer; Track mats; Two-year spare-parts and maintenance-support package; Manufacturer warranty coverage; Manufacturer operating, maintenance, safety, and technical documentation; Parts availability; and Technical and maintenance support. Operator training is not required under this acquisition. 2. Brand Name or Equal The brand-name reference is SpyderCrane URW375/URW376 or equal. The brand name is used to describe the configuration, quality, compact transportability, lift performance, controls, safety systems, accessory compatibility, field-operating capability, and supportability required to satisfy the Government's aircraft maintenance mission. Use of the brand-name reference does not preclude competition. An equal product will be considered when the quoter demonstrates that the offered product meets or exceeds every minimum salient physical, functional, and performance characteristic stated in this solicitation. FAR 52.211-6, Brand Name or Equal, applies to this acquisition. 3. Minimum Salient Characteristics A. Configuration The offered product shall be a compact, crawler-mounted mini crane/spider crane suitable for aircraft maintenance lifting operations in restricted-access and limited-maneuverability areas. The crane shall include a hydraulically telescoping boom, crawler-mounted mobility, and a multi-position stabilizing outrigger system capable of supporting safe lifting operations. B. Load and Working-Radius Capability Official manufacturer load charts shall demonstrate that the offered crane is capable of safely lifting not less than 5,000 pounds at a 10-foot working radius. The documentation shall identify the applicable: Boom length and configuration; Working radius; Outrigger or stabilizer configuration; Parts-of-line and hook-block configuration; and Operating conditions or limitations applicable to the rated capacity. Maximum advertised crane capacity alone is insufficient. The required capacity at the specified working radius must be shown in an official manufacturer load chart. C. Hook Height The crane shall provide a hook or boom-tip height of not less than 41 feet, without relying on a modification. The quoter shall provide official manufacturer documentation identifying the offered crane's maximum standard-boom hook or tip height and any applicable operating limitations. D. Load-Chart Verification Official manufacturer load charts must show rated lifting capacities at the applicable working radii, boom configurations, outrigger configurations, and hook heights. Generic capacity statements, maximum-capacity ratings, marketing literature without a supporting load chart, or unsupported statements from a dealer or reseller will not satisfy this requirement. E. JP-8 Fuel Compatibility The crane shall be furnished in a manufacturer-approved configuration capable of operating on JP-8 fuel. The quotation must include written documentation from the original equipment manufacturer confirming JP-8 compatibility. The documentation shall address: Engine compatibility; Fuel-system compatibility; Emissions-system compatibility; Manufacturer warranty coverage during JP-8 operation; JP-8-specific maintenance requirements; and Any restrictions, limitations, or required modifications associated with JP-8 operation. A general diesel-fuel rating or an unsupported dealer, distributor, or reseller statement is insufficient. The proposed crane will be determined technically unacceptable if the manufacturer does not confirm JP-8 compatibility. F. Mobility and Transportability The crane shall be crawler-mounted and suitable for operation on unimproved surfaces, ramps, and limited-access aircraft maintenance areas. Travel or fully stowed dimensions shall not exceed: Width: 51 inches; Height: 71 inches; Length: 171 inches; and Crane weight: 8,760 pounds. Dimensions shall be measured with the crane in its normal transport configuration, with the boom, outriggers, hook, and permanently installed equipment fully stowed. The crane shall be sufficiently compact and transportable to support the Government's aircraft deployment and transportation requirements. G. Stabilization The crane shall include an outrigger or stabilizer system capable of supporting safe lifting operations on paved and unimproved surfaces. The system shall include outrigger and boom interlocks, stability monitoring, or an equivalent manufacturer-installed system that prevents crane operation outside the authorized load and stability configuration. H. Operator Controls The crane shall include: Full-function wireless or radio remote-control capability; Onboard operator controls; Variable or proportional controls suitable for precise load positioning; and Emergency-stop capability. The control system must permit safe and precise load positioning in restricted aircraft maintenance areas. I. Safety Systems The offered crane shall include, at a minimum: Load Moment Indicator or equivalent rated-capacity monitoring system; Anti-two-block system; Over-winding prevention device or equivalent protection; Automatic winch brake or equivalent braking system; Emergency-stop capability; Outrigger and boom interlock monitoring; Hydraulic pressure-relief protection; Minimum wire-rope automatic stop or equivalent protection; and Automatic hook-stow system or equivalent secure transport configuration. Safety systems shall be installed or approved by the original equipment manufacturer. J. Boom and Crane Operation The crane shall include: Hydraulically telescoping boom; Continuous or unrestricted 360-degree swing operation; Positive boom and hydraulic holding valves; Onboard diagnostic capability; and Rated-capacity monitoring appropriate for the crane's boom, radius, and outrigger configuration. K. Accessories All accessories shall be compatible with and approved by the crane's original equipment manufacturer. Accessories shall not invalidate or reduce the manufacturer's crane certification, safety rating, rated lifting capability, or warranty coverage. The boom-tip-mounted work platform must be approved for use with the offered crane and include all required attachment components, controls, safety devices, and documentation. The non-marking tracks shall be suitable for use on aircraft maintenance and hangar flooring. The hydraulic tilt-deck trailer shall be sized and rated for safe transportation of the offered crane an

Notice of Intent to Sole Source HT941026N0088
THIS IS A NOTICE OF INTENT TO AWARD A SOLE SOURCE SUPPLY CONTRACT
AND IS NOT A REQUEST FOR COMPETITIVE QUOTES.
The Defense Health Agency Contracting Activity (DHACA), Healthcare Contracting Division –
West (HCD-W), intends to award a firm-fixed-price purchase order for seven (7) Marco SC-
1600 LCD Acuity Systems (Manufacturer: Marco Ophthalmic). This procurement supports the
operational requirements of the NMRTC Camp Pendleton Optometry Department and is
conducted in accordance with Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 12.102(a) under the
Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO)for the acquisition of commercial products and services.
Lombart Brothers, Inc. DBA Marco Lombart
5358 Robin Hood Rd
Norfolk, VA 23513
UEI: E7HDM4M51NJ8
CAGE: 8CJP0
The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for this requirement
is 339112 (Surgical and Medical Instrument Manufacturing), which has an associated small
business size standard of 1,000 employees. The corresponding Product Service Code
(PSC) is 6540 (Ophthalmic Instruments, Equipment, and Supplies).
The objective of this procurement is to execute a sole-source contract award for seven (7) Marco
SC-1600 LCD Acuity Systems, manufactured by Marco Ophthalmic, to support the NMRTC
Camp Pendleton Optometry Department. This equipment is required to accurately measure
patients' refractive errors by providing standardized Snellen and specialty optotype charts,
contrast sensitivity testing, and binocular balance tests. Crucially, the Marco SC-1600 is the only
system capable of seamless integration with the department's existing TRS-6100 Automated
Refraction Systems, allowing providers to control all chart functions directly from the refractor’s
central control unit. This specific manufacturer’s equipment has been the interoperability
standard across Navy optometry clinics since 2008. Camp Pendleton's currently integrated
equipment, procured between 2013 and 2014, has exceeded its operational life expectancy; age
and wear have caused internal gears to grind and physical charts to fade, compromising patient
readings. Upgrading to the SC-1600 will resolve these hardware failures, modernize the
examination rooms, and align Camp Pendleton with over ten other Navy optometry clinics that
have already transitioned to this generation of refractive technology. Additionally, retaining the
Marco Ophthalmic standard eliminates the need to retrain clinical personnel and leverages the
facility's established maintenance support infrastructure, preventing operational downtime and
unacceptable delays in patient care. Because this requirement relies on strict compatibility with
existing proprietary hardware, and market research indicates no reasonable expectation of
receiving quotes from two or more small businesses for an equivalent integrated system, the
Government intends to execute this procurement on a sole-source basis under the authority of
Other Than Full and Open Competition.
Delivery Date: 30 Days ARO
Delivery Location: NMRTC Camp Pendleton Optometry Department: Sequoia Rd., Bldg. H-135,
Camp Pendleton, CA 92055
Lombart Brothers, Inc. DBA Marco Lombart is the sole source capable of meeting the
Government’s minimum requirements to provide the Marco SC-1600 LCD Acuity System at
NMRTC Camp Pendleton Optometry Department.
This notice of intent is not a request for competitive proposals, and no formal solicitation
document exists for this requirement. Sources interested in responding to this notice are required
to submit a capability statement. Submissions must include management, technical, and cost data
in sufficient detail accompanied by convincing evidence to clearly demonstrate the capability to
provide the required equipment and preventive maintenance. Capability statements shall not
exceed four (4) pages (8.5" x 11" format) using a font size no smaller than 10-point. All
capability statements received by the due date of this notice will be considered by the
Government. Requests for documentation, inquiries for additional information, or submissions
consisting solely of questions will not be considered affirmative responses. A determination by
the Government not to compete this requirement based on responses to this notice is solely
within the discretion of the Government. Information received will be considered exclusively for
the purpose of determining whether to conduct a competitive procurement or to proceed with a
sole-source purchase order.
Response Instructions:
If a vendor challenges the basis of this requirement, please email capability statements as a
Microsoft Word or Adobe PDF attachment to:
• Cha-on Gordon at cha-on.p.gordon2.civ@health.mil
The closing date for challenges is no later than 1000 Pacific Daylight Time, Monday, August 3,
2026.
NO TELEPHONE REQUESTS/OFFERS WILL BE HONORED.
