﻿Notice of Intent to Award a Sole Source Contract for a Wire Bonder

Notice ID: NIST-SS26-161

Contract Opportunity Type: Notice of Intent to Sole Source Name Brand Only model TPT HB05 Wire Bonder

Response Date: August 4,2026

Product Service Code (PSC): 6640

NAICS Code: 333242

BACKGROUND

The National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) is conducting market research to identify alternative sources that (a) are capable of meeting NIST’s minimum requirements for the following commercial products and (b) would be interested in competing for that requirement:

The National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) Physical Measurement Laboratory (PML) requires a Wire Bonder for wire bonding electrical connections in quantum devices. The wire bonder provides precise control over bonding force, ultrasonic power, bond time, temperature, and stage motion to make reliable interconnects with delicate nanoscale structures. The Wire Bonder is used to package low-dimensional van der Waals devices and other quantum devices for mission-critical experiments in physics and metrology, quantum information science, and electrical standards dissemination. For research devices with fine bond pads, fragile substrates, and limited contact areas, we require the wire bonder to support fine wire with stable, repeatable operation and accurate control of bonding parameters, such as force and ultrasonic power. The Wire Bonder shall be a model TPT HB05, compatible and interchangeable with the existing NIST TPT HB05 wire bonder in PML, providing the same exact bonding characteristics and capability, the same user experience and control, and the same work area required for our device-packaging requirements.

If NIST’s market research indicates there are alternative sources that are capable and interested in competing to fill this requirement, separate and apart from Cook and Weil Inc. UEI# GJMEHZQFN2D9 then NIST will consider conducting a competitive acquisition in accordance with law and regulation. To be clear, NIST’s identification of Cook and Weil Inc. in this Notice does not constitute a binding commitment or obligation for it to conduct a sole source procurement with Cook and Weil Inc. for this requirement.

STATEMENT OF WORK
RIFLES

General Information 
A Long gun is a weapon specifically designed for and used by Police Officers responding to dangerous tactical situations. After substantial research and testing, the Office of Security and Law Enforcement (OS&LE) has chosen a weapon with the following specifications: M-4 Platform, 11.5-inch short barrel configuration; .223/5.56 mm caliber; with collapsible stock, tactical equipment mounting; and sling. The Long gun is required to have a weapon mounted light and an optic to increase effectiveness of faster target acquisition and better situational awareness. Optional equipment may include but not be limited to sight risers, quick attachments/detachments, or fore/front grips. The magazines will come from a reputable source and have 30 round capacity. The Long gun should be fully ambidextrous controls—selector, magazine catch, and an ergonomic bolt interface—support right- or left-handed operation and seamless shoulder transitions for all VA Connecticut Police Officers.

Background
The United States Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) VA Connecticut Medical Center is protected by uniformed VA Police Officers. VA Police Officers are employees who have appointed authority under statue to enforce Federal law within VA’s jurisdiction. Such officers are armed with Department-approved weapons and are the primary initial response force to Active Threat incidents on VA-owned, leased or controlled property. VA Police Officers also complete substantial training in Active Threat Response (VA Handbook 0730/5, July 2014), and the VA has determined it necessary to add a long gun to the inventory of weapons available to VA Police Officers to protect against such threats. VA police officers will only deploy the long gun in response to life-threatening emergency situations in which the capabilities of a long gun are needed or perceived to be needed by an individual officer that chooses to deploy the long gun. VA police officers will be trained to recognize when the long gun is appropriate for deployment (VA Handbook 0720/1). Some examples of life-threatening emergencies include, but are not limited to: Active Threat, Hostage Situation, Felony Traffic Stops, and Armed Suspects.
General Requirements
The Vendor shall be capable of the entire quantity of long guns within the required time frames. 
Vendor shall ensure that all applicable laws have been complied with concerning construction, packaging, labeling, registration, and transporting.
The vendor shall not make any unannounced alterations to the design or components without prior notification and written approval by the COR.
The vender shall acquire and deliver the long guns within 90 days of the contract award. The Long guns will be shipped direct to each duty station within VISN 1. Addresses and shipping info will be provided at contract award.
Quantity Requested and Reason
The VA Police in Connecticut and Central Western Mass will require the vender to deliver a total of 26 long guns and associated accessories. The Rhode Island VA Police will require a TBD number of long guns without the associated optic. The breakdown of the total long guns is as follows:
Central Western Mass
4
VA Connecticut 
22
Providence RI
4

Equipment Specifications 
The Long gun must meet the following characteristics: 
 
Barrel: 11.5” Heavy Barrel, Free Float Barrel
Rifling: 1 in 7”, Right Hand Twist, 6 Grooves
Caliber: 5.56mm NATO
Operation: Air-cooled, gas-operated, firing from a closed bolt
Controls: Ambidextrous Selector, Bolt Release, Magazine Catch
M5 Upper: Colt Enhanced Rail & Upper Receiver Design with Anti-Torsion Lug
Rail System: 1-piece MLOK Free Floating Rail System / 9.35" length
Charging Handle: Radian Raptor (Part Number: 402828)
Front Sight: Magpul MBUS 3 Sight (Part Number: 403790)
Rear Sight: Magpul MBUS 3 Sight (Part Number: 403789)
Flash Hider: Huxwrx OSS (Part Number: 403099)
Pistol Grip: Magpul K2 (Part Number: 402333)
Sling: Magpul MS1 QDM (Part Number: MAG939

Accessories
Magazine: Magpul PMag 30 Round “Windowed”, Includes (3) Magazines (Part Number: 99812)
Optic: Eotech EXPS3 Sight, Black (Part Number: 401181)
Light: Streamlight HLX Pro-Tac M-LOK
Stock: Magpul STR (Part Number: 401346)
 Magpul Hand Stop Kit, Includes: (1) M-LOK Index Panel, (1) M-LOK Rail Cover Type 2 (Part Number: 402447)

Additional Services
Training – The vendor shall provide training for up to 20 students to become certified armorers with the selected manufactures long gun at no cost to the agency.
Warranty and Service- The vendor will provide a warranty and repair agreement for defective parts for a period of 5 years.
Parts- The vendor will guarantee replacement parts can be purchased directly from the manufacture for a period of 10 or more years.

Federal notice (Special Notice), AGRICULTURE, DEPARTMENT OF.FOREST SERVICE.USDA-FS, CSA EAST 6
Title: Notice of Intent to Sole Source - UV Laser Marking Device
Solicitation number: 1174226
PSC: 3611; NAICS: 333517
Description: The US Department of Agriculture, Forest Service, Forest Products Laboratory intends to negotiate a sole-source, firm-fixed-price contract award with Keyence Corporation of America for a 3-Axis UV Laser Marking System. The Forest Biopolymers Science and Engineering Research Work Unit (RWU4707) at FPL conducts research on the multiscale material characterization of wood and wood products. Wood and cellulose-based materials are highly heterogeneous complex materials that require full-field deformation measurements to properly characterize the mechanical behavior for use in various forest products markets. The most effective methods for full-field metrology utilize imaging of patterned surfaces. A UV laser marking device enables high contrast �cold marking� of specimen surfaces at high resolution while minimizing thermal damage. The Government intends to acquire this equipment under the authority of FAR 13.106-1(b), soliciting from a single source. Keyence Corporation of America is the only known manufacturer capable of providing a 355 nm UV marking laser with an integrated 3-axis controller capable of automatic non-planar contour detection and a dynamic focus depth of field of at least +/-20 mm, which is required to prevent thermal and mechanical degradation of heterogeneous wood specimens during characterization. This notice is not a request for competitive proposals. However, interested parties who believe they can fully satisfy the technical requirements may submit a capability statement. All capability statements received within 15 days of this posting will be considered by the Government. A determination by the Government not to compete this proposed contract based upon responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government.

STATEMENT OF WORK
RIFLES

General Information 
A Long gun is a weapon specifically designed for and used by Police Officers responding to dangerous tactical situations. After substantial research and testing, the Office of Security and Law Enforcement (OS&LE) has chosen a weapon with the following specifications: M-4 Platform, 11.5-inch short barrel configuration; .223/5.56 mm caliber; with collapsible stock, tactical equipment mounting; and sling. The Long gun is required to have a weapon mounted light and an optic to increase effectiveness of faster target acquisition and better situational awareness. Optional equipment may include but not be limited to sight risers, quick attachments/detachments, or fore/front grips. The magazines will come from a reputable source and have 30 round capacity. The Long gun should be fully ambidextrous controls—selector, magazine catch, and an ergonomic bolt interface—support right- or left-handed operation and seamless shoulder transitions for all VA Connecticut Police Officers.

Background
The United States Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) VA Connecticut Medical Center is protected by uniformed VA Police Officers. VA Police Officers are employees who have appointed authority under statue to enforce Federal law within VA’s jurisdiction. Such officers are armed with Department-approved weapons and are the primary initial response force to Active Threat incidents on VA-owned, leased or controlled property. VA Police Officers also complete substantial training in Active Threat Response (VA Handbook 0730/5, July 2014), and the VA has determined it necessary to add a long gun to the inventory of weapons available to VA Police Officers to protect against such threats. VA police officers will only deploy the long gun in response to life-threatening emergency situations in which the capabilities of a long gun are needed or perceived to be needed by an individual officer that chooses to deploy the long gun. VA police officers will be trained to recognize when the long gun is appropriate for deployment (VA Handbook 0720/1). Some examples of life-threatening emergencies include, but are not limited to: Active Threat, Hostage Situation, Felony Traffic Stops, and Armed Suspects.
General Requirements
The Vendor shall be capable of the entire quantity of long guns within the required time frames. 
Vendor shall ensure that all applicable laws have been complied with concerning construction, packaging, labeling, registration, and transporting.
The vendor shall not make any unannounced alterations to the design or components without prior notification and written approval by the COR.
The vender shall acquire and deliver the long guns within 90 days of the contract award. The Long guns will be shipped direct to each duty station within VISN 1. Addresses and shipping info will be provided at contract award.
Quantity Requested and Reason
The VA Police in Connecticut and Central Western Mass will require the vender to deliver a total of 26 long guns and associated accessories. The Rhode Island VA Police will require a TBD number of long guns without the associated optic. The breakdown of the total long guns is as follows:
Central Western Mass
4
VA Connecticut 
22
Providence RI
4

Equipment Specifications 
The Long gun must meet the following characteristics: 
 
Barrel: 11.5” Heavy Barrel, Free Float Barrel
Rifling: 1 in 7”, Right Hand Twist, 6 Grooves
Caliber: 5.56mm NATO
Operation: Air-cooled, gas-operated, firing from a closed bolt
Controls: Ambidextrous Selector, Bolt Release, Magazine Catch
M5 Upper: Colt Enhanced Rail & Upper Receiver Design with Anti-Torsion Lug
Rail System: 1-piece MLOK Free Floating Rail System / 9.35" length
Charging Handle: Radian Raptor (Part Number: 402828)
Front Sight: Magpul MBUS 3 Sight (Part Number: 403790)
Rear Sight: Magpul MBUS 3 Sight (Part Number: 403789)
Flash Hider: Huxwrx OSS (Part Number: 403099)
Pistol Grip: Magpul K2 (Part Number: 402333)
Sling: Magpul MS1 QDM (Part Number: MAG939

Accessories
Magazine: Magpul PMag 30 Round “Windowed”, Includes (3) Magazines (Part Number: 99812)
Optic: Eotech EXPS3 Sight, Black (Part Number: 401181)
Light: Streamlight HLX Pro-Tac M-LOK
Stock: Magpul STR (Part Number: 401346)
 Magpul Hand Stop Kit, Includes: (1) M-LOK Index Panel, (1) M-LOK Rail Cover Type 2 (Part Number: 402447)

Additional Services
Training – The vendor shall provide training for up to 20 students to become certified armorers with the selected manufactures long gun at no cost to the agency.
Warranty and Service- The vendor will provide a warranty and repair agreement for defective parts for a period of 5 years.
Parts- The vendor will guarantee replacement parts can be purchased directly from the manufacture for a period of 10 or more years.

Description: NOTICE: The U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) National Energy Technology Laboratory (NETL) is issuing the following Brand-Name/Exact Match only Request for Quote (RFQ) for the Perkin Elmer Avio 3000 Inductively Coupled Plasma Optical Emission Spectrometer (ICP-OES) per the attached requirements list and is prepared in accordance with the Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO) Part 12, as supplemented with additional information included in this notice. The North American Industrial Classification System (NAICS) code for this effort is 334516. This requirement is a total small business set-aside. Only quotes submitted by small business concerns will be accepted by the Government. Any quote that is submitted by a contractor that is not a small business concern will not be considered for award. The small business size standard is 1000. The Department of Energy has accepted the deviations of RFO Part 12. BRAND NAME JUSTIFICATION: This brand name justification is written under the authority of 41 U.S.C. 3304 (a)(5) as implemented by Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO) 11.204(a)(1). NETL currently utilizes the Perkin Elmer ICP-OES for conducting ongoing analysis research for the NETL Pittsburgh Analytical Lab. The Perkin Elmer Avio 3000 ICP-OES has a next-generation BSI-CMOS Detector and UV Boost Mode. The proprietary detector allows full spectral coverage with independent per-analyte integration times measured simultaneously. The integrated UV Boost Mode significantly amplifies sensitivity in the UV region for elements with weak emission lines. This capability is critical for NETL researchers who must measure challenging, low-concentration analytes in highly complex environmental and materials matrices. Given NETL�s prior use of this instrument and in an effort to ensure continuity and compatibility to ensure new data is comparable with historical data this brand name/exact match is required. The following clauses apply to this acquisition: FAR Clause 52.212-1, Instructions of Offerors-Commercial Products and Commercial Services (DEVIATION NOV 2025) FAR Clause 52.212-4, Contract Terms and Conditions-Commercial Products and Services (DEVIATION NOV 2025) A full list of applicable provisions and clauses is available in FedConnect. Representations and Certifications must conform to the RFO provisions. Interested vendors are to submit their quotation on the attached RFQ Standard Form (SF) 1449, and provide all supporting documents, as necessary, via the FedConnect portal at www.fedconnect.net by the due date and time indicated in Block 8 of the RFQ SF-1449. EVALUATION: Selection will be based on the small business quotation that is considered technically acceptable with the lowest firm-fixed price quote. The vendor shall be an approved and authorized reseller of the brand/manufacturer as of the submission date of their quote. The Government reserves the right to request vendors provide documentation that validates they are an approved and authorized reseller and that the products/services quoted meet the exact match/brand-name requirement. To be considered for evaluation, vendors must quote on all items/services listed in the solicitation. The Government anticipates issuing a single award from this RFQ. Vendors shall submit descriptive literature detailing features, technical capabilities and warranty data, as necessary. Technical acceptability shall be determined solely on the content and merit of the information submitted in response to this solicitation. The technical acceptability determination will be based on the quotation(s) with an exact match/brand-name only of the product/service as identified within this RFQ and per the attached specifications. NO SUBSTITUTION ITEMS proposed will be considered for award. Vendors can find the solicitation by clicking �Search Public Opportunities� and searching by the solicitation number 89243326QFE000545. 252.211-7003 ITEM IDENTIFICATION AND VALUATION (MAR 2016)
As prescribed in 211.274-6(a)(1), use the following clause: 
ITEM UNIQUE IDENTIFICATION AND VALUATION (MAR 2016) 
(a) Definitions. As used in this clause—
“Automatic identification device” means a device, such as a reader or interrogator, used to retrieve data encoded on machine-readable media.
“Concatenated unique item identifier” means—
(1) For items that are serialized within the enterprise identifier, the linking together of the unique identifier data elements in order of the issuing agency code, enterprise identifier, and unique serial number within the enterprise identifier; or
(2) For items that are serialized within the original part, lot, or batch number, the linking together of the unique identifier data elements in order of the issuing agency code; enterprise identifier; original part, lot, or batch number; and serial number within the original part, lot, or batch number.
“Data matrix” means a two-dimensional matrix symbology, which is made up of square or, in some cases, round modules arranged within a perimeter finder pattern and uses the Error Checking and Correction 200 (ECC200) specification found within International Standards Organization (ISO)/International Electrotechnical Commission (IEC) 16022.
“Data qualifier” means a specified character (or string of characters) that immediately precedes a data field that defines the general category or intended use of the data that follows.
“DoD recognized unique identification equivalent” means a unique identification method that is in commercial use and has been recognized by DoD. All DoD recognized unique identification equivalents are listed at https://www.acq.osd.mil/asda/dpc/ce/ds/unique-id.html .
“DoD item unique identification” means a system of marking items delivered to DoD with unique item identifiers that have machine-readable data elements to distinguish an item from all other like and unlike items. For items that are serialized within the enterprise identifier, the unique item identifier shall include the data elements of the enterprise identifier and a unique serial number. For items that are serialized within the part, lot, or batch number within the enterprise identifier, the unique item identifier shall include the data elements of the enterprise identifier; the original part, lot, or batch number; and the serial number.
“Enterprise” means the entity (e.g., a manufacturer or vendor) responsible for assigning unique item identifiers to items.
“Enterprise identifier” means a code that is uniquely assigned to an enterprise by an issuing agency.
“Government’s unit acquisition cost” means—
(1) For fixed-price type line, subline, or exhibit line items, the unit price identified in the contract at the time of delivery;
(2) For cost-type or undefinitized line, subline, or exhibit line items, the Contractor’s estimated fully burdened unit cost to the Government at the time of delivery; and
(3) For items produced under a time-and-materials contract, the Contractor’s estimated fully burdened unit cost to the Government at the time of delivery.
“Issuing agency” means an organization responsible for assigning a globally unique identifier to an enterprise, as indicated in the Register of Issuing Agency Codes for ISO/IEC 15459, located at http://www.aimglobal.org/?Reg_Authority15459.
“Issuing agency code” means a code that designates the registration (or controlling) authority for the enterprise identifier.
“Item” means a single hardware article or a single unit formed by a grouping of subassemblies, components, or constituent parts.
“Lot or batch number” means an identifying number assigned by the enterprise to a designated group of items, usually referred to as either a lot or a batch, all of which were manufactured under identical conditions.
“Machine-readable” means an automatic identification technology media, such as bar codes, contact memory buttons, radio frequency identification, or optical memory cards.
“Original part number” means a combination of numbers or letters assigned by the enterprise at item creation to a class of items with the same form, fit, function, and interface.
“Parent item” means the item assembly, intermediate component, or subassembly that has an embedded item with a unique item identifier or DoD recognized unique identification equivalent.
“Serial number within the enterprise identifier” means a combination of numbers, letters, or symbols assigned by the enterprise to an item that provides for the differentiation of that item from any other like and unlike item and is never used again within the enterprise.
“Serial number within the part, lot, or batch number” means a combination of numbers or letters assigned by the enterprise to an item that provides for the differentiation of that item from any other like item within a part, lot, or batch number assignment.
“Serialization within the enterprise identifier” means each item produced is assigned a serial number that is unique among all the tangible items produced by the enterprise and is never used again. The enterprise is responsible for ensuring unique serialization within the enterprise identifier.
“Serialization within the part, lot, or batch number” means each item of a particular part, lot, or batch number is assigned a unique serial number within that part, lot, or batch number assignment. The enterprise is responsible for ensuring unique serialization within the part, lot, or batch number within the enterprise identifier.
“Type designation” means a combination of letters and numerals assigned by the Government to a major end item, assembly or subassembly, as appropriate, to provide a convenient means of differentiating between items having the same basic name and to indicate modifications and changes thereto.
“Unique item identifier” means a set of data elements marked on items that is globally unique and unambiguous. The term includes a concatenated unique item identifier or a DoD recognized unique identification equivalent.
“Unique item identifier type” means a designator to indicate which method of uniquely identifying a part has been used. The current list of accepted unique item identifier types is maintained at https://www.acq.osd.mil/asda/dpc/ce/ds/unique-id.html .
(b) The Contractor shall deliver all items under a contract line, subline, or exhibit line item.
(c) Unique item identifier.

(i) Delivered items for which the Government’s unit acquisition cost is $5,000 or more, except for the following line items:

Federal notice (Award Notice), DEPT OF DEFENSE.DEPT OF THE ARMY.W6QK ACC-APG
Title: Notice of Sole Source Award: JBTDS
Solicitation number: W911SR-26-D-A005
PSC: 6665; NAICS: 334511
Award: CHEMRING SENSORS AND ELECTRONIC SYSTEMS, INC. Charlotte NC 28273 USA 48811629.00
Description: Army Contracting Command � Aberdeen Proving Ground (ACC-APG), Edgewood Division, along with Capability Program Executive for Chemical, Biological, Radiological, and Nuclear Sensors (CPE-CBRND) has awarded a sole-source, Indefinite-Delivery/Indefinite-Quantity (IDIQ) contract to Chemring Sensors and Electronic Systems, Inc. (CSES) for the Full Rate Production (FRP) of the Joint Biological Tactical Detection System (JBTDS). The contract has a 36-month ordering period. The JBTDS provides the Joint Forces with a mission-critical capability for sustained operations in a CBRN environment as well as force protection in peacetime and contingency operations. JBTDS is the only militarized, tactical, lightweight biological surveillance system designed specifically for rapid detection, collection, identification and warning of Biological Warfare agents. The system fills a validated Joint Requirement for tactical level biological detection interoperable across Services, highly mobile and sustainable under the constraints of modern force structure. The JBTDS system is a lightweight, man-portable, battery- operable system designed to provide detection, collection and identification of airborne biological warfare agents. The system�s modular architecture Detector/ Collector (D/C), Identifier and Data Station (DS) enable flexible, task-organized deployment across multiple mission sets. The FRP scope encompasses production, quality assurance, testing, configuration management, logistics support and delivery of the production-representative Technical Data Package (TDP). This action represents the logical follow-on to contract W911QY-15-C-0035, under which CSES executed the Engineering and Manufacturing Development (EMD) and Low-Rate Initial Production (LRIP) phases. The FRP contract is required to ensure transition from LRIP to sustained production and fielding. Sole Source Justification (Non-Competitive Award): In accordance with FAR 6.302-1(a)(2)(ii)(A) (Only One Responsible Source: follow-on production of a major system/highly specialized equipment), this action was not awarded competitively. CSES is the only source capable of executing all components of the contract. The redacted Justification and Approval (J&A) will be posted to SAM.gov in accordance with RFO requirements.

attachments.text:
FAR Part 6 Justification and Approval
for Other than Full and Open Competition
1. Requiring Activity: JPdD BDS, JPM CBRN Sensors - 2800 Scully Road
Aberdeen Proving Ground, MD 21010-5424
2. Contracting Activity: U.S. Army Contracting Command - Aberdeen Proving
Ground (ACC-APG), Edgewood Contracting Division (ECD), 8456 Brigade Street,
Aberdeen Proving Ground, MD 21010-5401
3. Description of Action: ACC-APG-ECD intends to award a single award Indefinite
Delivery/Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) contract to Chemring Sensors and Electronic
Systems (CSES), 4205 Westinghouse Commons Drive, Charlotte, NC 28273 (CAGE
6KWZ6), for FRP of the JBTDS. This action represents the logical follow-on to contract
W911QY-15-C-0035, under which CSES executed the Engineering and Manufacturing
Development (EMD) and is currently performing the JBTDS Low-Rate Initial Production
(LRIP) phase. The competitively awarded EMD/LRIP contract, issued in April 2015,
delivered the technical baseline, qualification testing, and LRIP hardware now
supporting Multi-Service Operational Test and Evaluation (MOT&E). The FRP contract
is required to ensure uninterrupted transition from LRIP to sustained production and
fielding, in alignment with the approved Single Acquisition Management Plan (SAMP)
and the Major Capability Acquisition (MCA) pathway of the Adaptive Acquisition
Framework (AAF).
The FRP contract will be established as an Indefinite Delivery/Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ)
contract with a single thirty-six (36) month ordering period. The contract is planned for
award in FY26 and will utilize FY26, FY27, and FY28 Defense-Wide Procurement
appropriations, subject to the availability of funds. All orders will be placed within the
established ordering period; no options are anticipated for the base IDIQ contract
vehicle. The IDIQ structure provides the flexibility to issue delivery orders as
requirements are identified, and funds become available throughout the ordering
period.
4. Description of Supplies/Services: The JBTDS provides the Joint Forces with a
mission-critical capability for sustained operations in a CBRN environment as well as
force protection in peacetime and contingency operations. JBTDS is the only militarized,
tactical, lightweight biological surveillance system designed specifically for rapid
detection, collection, identification and warning of Biological Warfare agents. The
system fills a validated Joint Requirement for tactical-level biological detection
interoperable across Services, highly mobile and sustainable under the constraints of
modern force structure. The JBTDS system is a lightweight, man-portable, battery-
operable system of record designed to provide detection, collection and identification of
airborne biological warfare agents. The system’s modular architecture Detector/
Collector (D/C), Identifier and Data Station (DS) enable flexible, task-organized
deployment across multiple mission sets. The approved performance specification
defines stringent thresholds for probability of detection, false
3
alarm rates and environmental survivability. The FRP scope encompasses production,
quality assurance, testing, configuration management, logistics support and delivery of
the production-representative Technical Data Package (TDP).
The JBTDS program is an Acquisition Category (ACAT) II effort with Director,
Operational Test and Evaluation (DOT&E) oversight. The Army Acquisition Executive
delegated Milestone Decision Authority to the Capability Program Executive for CBRN
(Chemical, Biological, Radiological and Nuclear) Defense. A FRP Decision is projected
in March 2026, with First Unit Equipped (FUE) projected for FY27, Initial Operational
Capability (IOC) in FY29, and Full Operational Capability (FOC) in FY35. The system’s
key components are:
a. Detector/ Collector (D/C). This component houses the detection subsystem and
aerosol collector. The detection subsystem continuously samples ambient air and uses
laser induced fluorescence to detect suspicious particulate matter. Upon detection of an
anomaly, it automatically initiates the collection of an aerosol sample. The device
incor‑porates meteorological sensors and Global Positioning System to geo reference
detections and communicates via an integrated radio to the Data Station. It is capable of
stand alone operation or networked array operation and must withstand tra‑nsportation
and long term storage
‑
b. Ide‑ntifier and Data Station (DS). The DS provides remote command, control and
communications for a D/C array. It consolidates and displays alarms; initiates resets or
sample commands and interfaces with Joint Warning and Reporting Network and the
CBRN Sensor Command and Control (CSC2) systems. The DS software can reside on
Government furnished command and control hardware or a dedicated ruggedized
laptop. When used with an internet protocol based radio, the DS enables long range
communicati‑on with multiple D/C ‑units‑ and is the operator’s primary interface with
higher echelon C2 systems. ‑ ‑
c. C‑onsumable Sets. Single use components—filters, reagents, identification strips
and sample vials are required for each collection and identification cycle. The
consumable set supports both th‑e detection and identification functions and is sized to
support one mission cycle per kit. Consumables must meet stringent shelf life,
packaging and storage requirements and are replenished through the supply system.
‑
Program Support. In addition to production hardware and consumables, the FRP
contract includes program management, systems engineering, software support,
integrated logistics support, obsolescence management and the delivery of technical
data. Specific deliverables include Manufacturing Plan (DI MGMT 81889), Quality
Assurance Program Plan, Configuration Management Plan, Failure Modes and
Criticality Analyses, operator and maintenance technical m‑anuals,‑ training materials,
packaging instructions, Bills of Materials and the production representative TDP and
Software Data Package with Government Purpose Rights.
‑
4
The system is modular and can be fielded as a stand-alone unit or in a networked array
enabling units to tailor configurations to mission needs.
Quantities and delivery timelines are aligned to a FRP Decision no later than 2nd
quarter FY26, FUE in FY27, IOC in FY29 and FOC in FY35. These milestones are
tracked in the program’s Acquisition Program Baseline and remain under DOT&E
oversight. Executing FRP within this window is critical to avoid delays to IOC/ FOC,
prevent breaches of cost/schedule/performance thresholds and ensure timely JBTDS
fielding to meet validated Joint Service operational requirements.
5. Authority Cited: This action is being pursued under the authority of 10 U.S.C. §
3204(a)(1), as implemented in FAR 6.302-1 “Only one responsible source and no other
supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements.” Authority, 6.302-1(a)(2)(ii)(A),
”Supplies may be deemed to be available only from the original source in the case of a
follow-on contract for the continued development or production of a major system or
highly specialized equipment, including major components thereof, when it is likely that
award to any other source would result in-(A) Substantial duplication of cost to the
Government that is not expected to be recovered through competition.”
6. Reason for Authority Cited: FAR 6.302-1(a)(2)(ii)(A) provides for award of follow-on
production contracts without full and open competition when the requirement is a logical
continuation of prior development or limited production efforts, and when award to
another source would result in a substantial duplication of cost that is not expected to be
recovered through competition.
5


a. Reverse engineering at scale. Decomposing hardware, materials and processes
to production fidelity; deriving equivalency data; validating performance in qualification
testing and re-establishing quality baselines. This is multi-year, high-risk and costly-
particularly for bio-detection assays and unique collection/identifier components where
tacit know-how is decisive.
b. Licensing and specially negotiated licenses (SNLs). Negotiate expanded licenses
from CSES and multiple lower-tier IP holders. Because several contributors assert
rights, the Government would face serial or parallel negotiations to assemble a legally
clean production stack, often at premium pricing and with ongoing use restrictions.
c. Parallel development. Funding a clean-room alternative design to avoid
encumbered IP. That means new integration, new qualifications, and new sustainment
pipelines. Additionally, there is a risk that performance equivalence cannot be proven
without access to restricted test methods or data.
Each path adds cost, defers fielding, and introduces legal exposure if any restricted
data or software is inadvertently used. None of these paths delivers near-term
production capacity more efficiently than continuing with the rights-holding OEM or
negotiating targeted rights expansions where they matter most.
DoD’s current policy framework DoDI 5000.85 MCA and DoDI 5010.44 IP Acquisition
and Licensing emphasize two complementary imperatives: Secure the data and rights
necessary to execute program and capability sustainment and avoid paying for rights
providing no clear value to mission or sustainment outcomes. For JBTDS, forcing an
FRP competition without the production-level TDP and associated rights would run
counter to these principles. It would obligate the Government to spend heavily on
reverse engineering, licensing mosaics or re-development simply to recreate what
already exists-without demonstrable mission benefit and with real risk to schedule and
readiness. In short, competing FRP under the current IP posture would spend more to
achieve less, and would undercut the policy goal of smart, use-case-driven rights
acquisition.
Recommended course of action (to protect cost, schedule and readiness). While the
Government cannot lawfully authorize a third-party manufacture today, there are
pragmatic options to increase flexibility over time without wasteful spending:
• Targeted rights expansion where it matters. Negotiate SNLs for specific use
cases (e.g., depot repair of defined Line Replaceable Units, cyber assurance of critical
software modules, or competition for designated spares).
• Modular Open Systems Approaches (MOSA) informed segmentation going
forward. For upgrades or follow-on increments, anchor the design in MOSA with well-
defined Modular System Interfaces and Form-Fit-Function artifacts. This limits vendor
lock to true black boxes and creates future competitive seams without demanding
unnecessary DMPD today.
8
• Assay (lab test or analytical procedure) and process-knowledge access. Where
sustainment risk is concentrated in assays and consumables, prioritize data packages
and rights documenting performance envelopes, verification methods and quality
attributes the minimum to qualify alternates rather than attempting to purchase full
trade-secret processes.
• Supply assurance via OEM backed subcontracts. To mitigate near-term fragility,
use OEM-managed second sources (under the OEM’s licenses) for chokepoint parts
while negotiations for Government use-case rights proceed.
This approach preserves readiness, avoids litigation risk and channels resources into
rights delivering measurable sustainment or competition value fully consistent with DoD
policy. Given the current rights posture that provides Limited Rights for critical
subsystems, Restricted Rights for software and only partial GPR on select assay
processes, the Government cannot lawfully authorize another vendor to manufacture
JBTDS. Attempting to compete FRP now would entail costly reverse engineering,
complex licensing across multiple IP holders or parallel development all high-risk and
low value compared to negotiating targeted rights expansions and shaping future
increments with MOSA.

(CSES) for the Full Rate Production (FRP) of the Joint Biological Tactical Detection System (JBTDS). The contract has a 36-month ordering period. The JBTDS provides the Joint Forces with a mission-critical capability for sustained operations in a CBRN environment as well as force protection in peacetime and contingency operations. JBTDS is the only militarized, tactical, lightweight biological surveillance system designed specifically for rapid detection, collection, identification and warning of Biological Warfare agents. The system fills a validated Joint Requirement for tactical level biological detection interoperable across Services, highly mobile and sustainable under the constraints of modern force structure. The JBTDS system is a lightweight, man-portable, battery- operable system designed to provide detection, collection and identification of airborne biological warfare agents. The system�s modular architecture Detector/ Collector (D/C), Identifier and Data Station (DS) enable flexible, task-organized deployment across multiple mission sets. The FRP scope encompasses production, quality assurance, testing, configuration management, logistics support and delivery of the production-representative Technical Data Package (TDP). This action represents the logical follow-on to contract W911QY-15-C-0035, under which CSES executed the Engineering and Manufacturing Development (EMD) and Low-Rate Initial Production (LRIP) phases. The FRP contract is required to ensure transition from LRIP to sustained production and fielding. FAR Part 6 Justification and Approval
for Other than Full and Open Competition
1. Requiring Activity: JPdD BDS, JPM CBRN Sensors - 2800 Scully Road
Aberdeen Proving Ground, MD 21010-5424
2. Contracting Activity: U.S. Army Contracting Command - Aberdeen Proving
Ground (ACC-APG), Edgewood Contracting Division (ECD), 8456 Brigade Street,
Aberdeen Proving Ground, MD 21010-5401
3. Description of Action: ACC-APG-ECD intends to award a single award Indefinite
Delivery/Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) contract to Chemring Sensors and Electronic
Systems (CSES), 4205 Westinghouse Commons Drive, Charlotte, NC 28273 (CAGE
6KWZ6), for FRP of the JBTDS. This action represents the logical follow-on to contract
W911QY-15-C-0035, under which CSES executed the Engineering and Manufacturing
Development (EMD) and is currently performing the JBTDS Low-Rate Initial Production
(LRIP) phase. The competitively awarded EMD/LRIP contract, issued in April 2015,
delivered the technical baseline, qualification testing, and LRIP hardware now
supporting Multi-Service Operational Test and Evaluation (MOT&E). The FRP contract
is required to ensure uninterrupted transition from LRIP to sustained production and
fielding, in alignment with the approved Single Acquisition Management Plan (SAMP)
and the Major Capability Acquisition (MCA) pathway of the Adaptive Acquisition
Framework (AAF).
The FRP contract will be established as an Indefinite Delivery/Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ)
contract with a single thirty-six (36) month ordering period. The contract is planned for
award in FY26 and will utilize FY26, FY27, and FY28 Defense-Wide Procurement
appropriations, subject to the availability of funds. All orders will be placed within the
established ordering period; no options are anticipated for the base IDIQ contract
vehicle. The IDIQ structure provides the flexibility to issue delivery orders as
requirements are identified, and funds become available throughout the ordering
period.
4. Description of Supplies/Services: The JBTDS provides the Joint Forces with a
mission-critical capability for sustained operations in a CBRN environment as well as
force protection in peacetime and contingency operations. JBTDS is the only militarized,
tactical, lightweight biological surveillance system designed specifically for rapid
detection, collection, identification and warning of Biological Warfare agents. The
system fills a validated Joint Requirement for tactical-level biological detection
interoperable across Services, highly mobile and sustainable under the constraints of
modern force structure. The JBTDS system is a lightweight, man-portable, battery-
operable system of record designed to provide detection, collection and identification of
airborne biological warfare agents. The system’s modular architecture Detector/
Collector (D/C), Identifier and Data Station (DS) enable flexible, task-organized
deployment across multiple mission sets. The approved performance specification
defines stringent thresholds for probability of detection, false
3
alarm rates and environmental survivability. The FRP scope encompasses production,
quality assurance, testing, configuration management, logistics support and delivery of
the production-representative Technical Data Package (TDP).
The JBTDS program is an Acquisition Category (ACAT) II effort with Director,
Operational Test and Evaluation (DOT&E) oversight. The Army Acquisition Executive
delegated Milestone Decision Authority to the Capability Program Executive for CBRN
(Chemical, Biological, Radiological and Nuclear) Defense. A FRP Decision is projected
in March 2026, with First Unit Equipped (FUE) projected for FY27, Initial Operational
Capability (IOC) in FY29, and Full Operational Capability (FOC) in FY35. The system’s
key components are:
a. Detector/ Collector (D/C). This component houses the detection subsystem and
aerosol collector. The detection subsystem continuously samples ambient air and uses
laser induced fluorescence to detect suspicious particulate matter. Upon detection of an
anomaly, it automatically initiates the collection of an aerosol sample. The device
incor‑porates meteorological sensors and Global Positioning System to geo reference
detections and communicates via an integrated radio to the Data Station. It is capable of
stand alone operation or networked array operation and must withstand tra‑nsportation
and long term storage
‑
b. Ide‑ntifier and Data Station (DS). The DS provides remote command, control and
communications for a D/C array. It consolidates and displays alarms; initiates resets or
sample commands and interfaces with Joint Warning and Reporting Network and the
CBRN Sensor Command and Control (CSC2) systems. The DS software can reside on
Government furnished command and control hardware or a dedicated ruggedized
laptop. When used with an internet protocol based radio, the DS enables long range
communicati‑on with multiple D/C ‑units‑ and is the operator’s primary interface with
higher echelon C2 systems. ‑ ‑
c. C‑onsumable Sets. Single use components—filters, reagents, identification strips
and sample vials are required for each collection and identification cycle. The
consumable set supports both th‑e detection and identification functions and is sized to
support one mission cycle per kit. Consumables must meet stringent shelf life,
packaging and storage requirements and are replenished through the supply system.
‑
Program Support. In addition to production hardware and consumables, the FRP
contract includes program management, systems engineering, software support,
integrated logistics support, obsolescence management and the delivery of technical
data. Specific deliverables include Manufacturing Plan (DI MGMT 81889), Quality
Assurance Program Plan, Configuration Management Plan, Failure Modes and
Criticality Analyses, operator and maintenance technical m‑anuals,‑ training materials,
packaging instructions, Bills of Materials and the production representative TDP and
Software Data Package with Government Purpose Rights.
‑
4
The system is modular and can be fielded as a stand-alone unit or in a networked array
enabling units to tailor configurations to mission needs.
Quantities and delivery timelines are aligned to a FRP Decision no later than 2nd
quarter FY26, FUE in FY27, IOC in FY29 and FOC in FY35. These milestones are
tracked in the program’s Acquisition Program Baseline and remain under DOT&E
oversight. Executing FRP within this window is critical to avoid delays to IOC/ FOC,
prevent breaches of cost/schedule/performance thresholds and ensure timely JBTDS
fielding to meet validated Joint Service operational requirements.
5. Authority Cited: This action is being pursued under the authority of 10 U.S.C. §
3204(a)(1), as implemented in FAR 6.302-1 “Only one responsible source and no other
supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements.” Authority, 6.302-1(a)(2)(ii)(A),
”Supplies may be deemed to be available only from the original source in the case of a
follow-on contract for the continued development or production of a major system or
highly specialized equipment, including major components thereof, when it is likely that
award to any other source would result in-(A) Substantial duplication of cost to the
Government that is not expected to be recovered through competition.”
6. Reason for Authority Cited: FAR 6.302-1(a)(2)(ii)(A) provides for award of follow-on
production contracts without full and open competition when the requirement is a logical
continuation of prior development or limited production efforts, and when award to
another source would result in a substantial duplication of cost that is not expected to be
recovered through competition.
5


a. Reverse engineering at scale. Decomposing hardware, materials and processes
to production fidelity; deriving equivalency data; validating performance in qualification
testing and re-establishing quality baselines. This is multi-year, high-risk and costly-
particularly for bio-detection assays and unique collection/identifier components where
tacit know-how is decisive.
b. Licensing and specially negotiated licenses (SNLs). Negotiate expanded licenses
from CSES and multiple lower-tier IP holders. Because several contributors assert
rights, the Government would face serial or parallel negotiations to assemble a legally
clean production stack, often at premium pricing and with ongoing use restrictions.
c. Parallel development. Funding a clean-room alternative design to avoid
encumbered IP. That means new integration, new qualifications, and new sustainment
pipelines. Additionally, there is a risk that performance equivalence cannot be proven
without access to restricted test methods or data.
Each path adds cost, defers fielding, and introduces legal exposure if any restricted
data or software is inadvertently used. None of these paths delivers near-term
production capacity more efficiently than continuing with the rights-holding OEM or
negotiating targeted rights expansions where they matter most.
DoD’s current policy framework DoDI 5000.85 MCA and DoDI 5010.44 IP Acquisition
and Licensing emphasize two complementary imperatives: Secure the data and rights
necessary to execute program and capability sustainment and avoid paying for rights
providing no clear value to mission or sustainment outcomes. For JBTDS, forcing an
FRP competition without the production-level TDP and associated rights would run
counter to these principles. It would obligate the Government to spend heavily on
reverse engineering, licensing mosaics or re-development simply to recreate what
already exists-without demonstrable mission benefit and with real risk to schedule and
readiness. In short, competing FRP under the current IP posture would spend more to
achieve less, and would undercut the policy goal of smart, use-case-driven rights
acquisition.
Recommended course of action (to protect cost, schedule and readiness). While the
Government cannot lawfully authorize a third-party manufacture today, there are
pragmatic options to increase flexibility over time without wasteful spending:
• Targeted rights expansion where it matters. Negotiate SNLs for specific use
cases (e.g., depot repair of defined Line Replaceable Units, cyber assurance of critical
software modules, or competition for designated spares).
• Modular Open Systems Approaches (MOSA) informed segmentation going
forward. For upgrades or follow-on increments, anchor the design in MOSA with well-
defined Modular System Interfaces and Form-Fit-Function artifacts. This limits vendor
lock to true black boxes and creates future competitive seams without demanding
unnecessary DMPD today.
8
• Assay (lab test or analytical procedure) and process-knowledge access. Where
sustainment risk is concentrated in assays and consumables, prioritize data packages
and rights documenting performance envelopes, verification methods and quality
attributes the minimum to qualify alternates rather than attempting to purchase full
trade-secret processes.
• Supply assurance via OEM backed subcontracts. To mitigate near-term fragility,
use OEM-managed second sources (under the OEM’s licenses) for chokepoint parts
while negotiations for Government use-case rights proceed.
This approach preserves readiness, avoids litigation risk and channels resources into
rights delivering measurable sustainment or competition value fully consistent with DoD
policy. Given the current rights posture that provides Limited Rights for critical
subsystems, Restricted Rights for software and only partial GPR on select assay
processes, the Government cannot lawfully authorize another vendor to manufacture
JBTDS. Attempting to compete FRP now would entail costly reverse engineering,
complex licensing across multiple IP holders or parallel development all high-risk and
low value compared to negotiating targeted rights expansions and shaping future
increments with MOSA.

Description: Brand Name or Equal Brush Chipper Morbark BVR16 The intended use would be to chip/mulch up wood debris when the Grounds Crew does routine utility line clearing, vegetation management, in and around a 280-acre campus. The Morbark BVR16 woodchipper has incorporated many consumer/customer inspired innovations that increase the unit s efficiency and safety while reducing the average operating maintenance cost. This unit has been installed with improved drive belts and clutch discs creating a zero-clutch system. This removes the anxiety of engaging the chipper drum. No other woodchipper in the market offers these enhanced safety features and durability.

matters.title: Sole Source Siemens Service Agreement for Rapidpoint Blood Gas Analyzer for Red Lake Hospital
matters.text:
Federal notice (Special Notice), HEALTH AND HUMAN SERVICES, DEPARTMENT OF.INDIAN HEALTH SERVICE.BEMIDJI SUB-AREA,
Title: Sole Source Siemens Service Agreement for Rapidpoint Blood Gas Analyzer for Red Lake Hospital
Solicitation number: 
PSC: 6640; NAICS: 621511
Description: NOTICE OF INTENT TO ISSUE SOLE SOURCE AWARD The U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (HHS), Indian Health Service (IHS), Bemidji Area intends to award a Firm Fixed Priced Contract on a sole source basis to Siemens Healthcare for the Red Lake Hospital in Red Lake MN. The sole source action will be issued under the authority of Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 13.501(a) - only one source reasonably available. Siemens Rapidpoint 500e Analyzer (Serial number 68459, Functional location code 1010069) is already in use at the Red Lake Hospital and a new service and maintenance agreement plus reagents is needed. This service is proprietary to the manufacturer and it�s specific equipment. All supplies are analyzer specific and cannot be interchanged with another vendor. All service on the analyzer must be completed by a Siemens representative. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code is 621511-Medical Laboratories: Focuses on medical/diagnostic tests Product or Service Code (PCS) is 6640-Laboratory Equipment and Supplies: General laboratory equipment Point of contact for this acquisition is Purchasing Agent, Winona Kitto at winona.kitto@ihs.gov. This notice of intent is not a request for competitive quotes. Interested persons may identify their interest and capability to respond to the requirement or submit a quote to Purchasing Agent, Winona Kitto at winona.kitto@ihs.gov. Information received in response to this notice will be considered solely for the purpose of determining whether to conduct a competitive procurement. Any response to this notice must show clear and convincing evidence that competition would be advantageous to the Government. In doing so, interested sources must submit technical capabilities, and other information that demonstrates their ability to meet the Government's needs.

matters.text:
Federal notice (Special Notice), DEPT OF DEFENSE.DEPT OF THE AIR FORCE.FA4620  92 CONS LGC
Title: Notice of Intent to Sole Source: Butler Parachute Harnesses
Solicitation number: FA462026QA278
PSC: 1670; NAICS: 314999
Description: NOTICE OF INTENT TO SOLE SOURCE TO: BUTLER PARACHUTE SYSTEMS, INC. (UEI: E1URFZC1QLL7 / CAGE: 0D4Z0) The 22nd Training Readiness Squadron (TRS) has a requirement for ten (10) Butler low profile parachute (LPP) training harnesses, part number 11094, for use at the SERE school located at Fairchild AFB, WA. The requested harnesses are a training specific item that meets Air Force requirements as stated in AFI 10-3503, Personnel Parachute Program, from April 2026, AFMAN11-301V1, and the USAF Personnel Parachute Program (PPP) Approve for Use List (AUL). The required harnesses are only manufactured/distributed by Butler Parachute Systems, Inc (BPS). The Air Force Personnel Parachute Program Authorized Use List (AUL) mandates that the only authorized low-profile parachutes (LLP) are manufactured by Butler Parachute Systems (BPS). This requirement is for the LPP training hanging harness manufactured by BPS and specifically designed for training to simulate the use of the mandated LPP from the AUL therefore a sole source purchase is justified. While competition for parachute equipment is limited due to Air Force policy, an Internet search was conducted to look for authorized resellers of BPS equipment. Butler Parachute Systems was contacted and confirmed there are no authorized resellers of this product. Until other LPP products are authorized by the Air Force, BPS will continue to be the only source for the required harnesses. The government will continue to monitor the updated Air Force Instructions for all future purchases of this nature to verify if competition is available. THIS NOTICE OF INTENT IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSALS. This notice is for informational purposes only and is not to be construed as a commitment by the government. Vendors that believe they can provide the items listed above are invited to submit substantiating documentation in writing to the identified point of contact. Information received will be considered solely for the purpose of determining whether to conduct a competitive procurement. Oral communications are not acceptable in response to this notice. A determination by the government to compete this proposed contract based on responses to this notice is solely at the discretion of the government.

matters.agency: National Institute of Standards and Technology
matters.text:
Federal notice (Sources Sought), COMMERCE, DEPARTMENT OF.NATIONAL INSTITUTE OF STANDARDS AND TECHNOLOGY.DEPT OF COMMERCE NIST
Title: Combined Sources Sought Notice and Notice of Intent to Award a Sole Source Contract for Automated Inverted Microscope
Solicitation number: NIST-SS26-152
PSC: 6640; NAICS: 334516
Description: BACKGROUND The National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) is conducting market research to identify alternative sources that (a) are capable of meeting NIST�s minimum requirements for the following commercial products and commercial services and (b) would be interested in competing for that requirement: The Biophysical and Biomedical Measurement Group within the Microsystems and Nanotechnology Division of the Physical Measurements Laboratory will acquire an inverted microscope to advance measurement science for its Organ-on-a-Chip (OoC)/ Microphysiological Systems (MPS) program. Therefore, we require an inverted microscope system that is relatively easy to use, capable of maintaining live cell culture incubation conditions, and compatible with other existing Zeiss microscopes in the lab. The microscope will be used to image biological cells on substrates ranging from microscope slides to multi-well plates to our custom-made OoC/MPS platforms. The project aims to monitor cell behavior under drug and other stimuli to detect changes in cell state. Therefore, continuous automated imaging of cells before, during, and after exposure to different stimuli for hours to days on different substrates, thus the requirement of cell culture incubation components is required. The substrates expected to be used (but not limited to) are: microscope slides, multi-well plates, and our custom-made OoC/MPS platforms, is required. The areas within these substrates to be imaged will vary depending on what is analyzed in and around the cells. The microscope must fulfill a wide range of requirements as outlined above. It most supports various imaging modalities such as brightfield imaging, widefield fluorescence, and phase contrast microscopy with high spatial resolution and fast scan rates (20 fps or more at the highest resolution). Additionally, the microscope should be part of a complete system that includes filter sets for multi-color imaging and light sources for bright field imaging and widefield fluorescence imaging from ?385 nm to 735 nm to enable its use with common fluorophores. The system should feature a high level of automation, allowing image capture in multiple modes, and be programmable for continuous monitoring over several days. The automation should also allow integration of other microscope features, such as focus tracking, to enhance long-term monitoring alongside image capture. Automation should also extend to microscope features such as motorized sample stages, nosepiece to allow changes in objectives and filters. See Attachment 1 for required minimum technical specifications. NIST has not yet determined its acquisition strategy for this requirement and encourages interested sources to respond to this Notice. If NIST�s market research indicates there are alternative sources that are capable and interested in competing to fill this requirement, separate and apart from Carl Zeiss Microscopy, LLC (UEI: H41JAKKNEXY1), then NIST will consider conducting a competitive acquisition in accordance with law and regulation. To be clear, NIST�s identification of Carl Zeiss Microscopy, LLC in this Notice does not constitute a binding commitment or obligation for it to conduct a sole source procurement with Carl Zeiss Microscopy, LLC for this requirement. INSTRUCTIONS FOR RESPONDING TO RESPOND TO THIS NOTICE Parties that respond to this Notice are requested to voluntarily submit the requested information via email in Microsoft Word, Adobe PDF, and/or Microsoft Excel format to the designated point(s) of contact whose name and email address appears at the bottom of this notice. Please provide only the information requested by this Notice, and do not include proprietary, classified, confidential, or sensitive information in a response to this Notice. Information Requested in Response to This Notice: To help NIST with its market research, NIST is requesting that industry sources carefully review this notice and any attachments to it and voluntarily provide the following information: 1. Company Summary Notice Identification: Notice ID and Title of this posting. Corporate Details: Company name, physical address, website address, and Unique Entity Identifier (UEI). Point of Contact (POC): Name, phone number, and email address. Company Size Standard: Your company�s size status relative to the NAICS code provided in this Notice. (Refer to the SBA Table of Small Business Size Standards). System for Award Management (SAM) Registration: Indicate whether your company has an active registration for procurement purposes in SAM.gov. 2. Feedback for Draft Requirements Review the potential requirements/minimum specifications included with this Notice. Then, please provide suggestions to (a) improve clarity of it; (b) to make it more competitive; (c) to indicate whether there anything in it that may inadvertently exclude domestic involvement; and (d) to indicate how the requirements could potentially be revised to improve the ability for domestic (�Made in America�) end products to be considered. 3. Information Regarding Your Company�s Products and Services Provide specifications, company name of the original equipment manufacturer, and the country of manufacture for products and services that your company is legally authorized to sell and that may meet NIST�s minimum requirements. Indicate whether, in your opinion, the product(s) meet the definition of (a) commercial product or (b) commercially available off-the-shelf (COTS) item or COTS item as described at https://www.acquisition.gov/far-overhaul/far-part-deviation-guide/far-overhaul-part-2 and, if so, which definition applies ((a) or (b)). Indicate whether, in your opinion, the service(s) meet the definition of commercial service as described at https://www.acquisition.gov/far-overhaul/far-part-deviation-guide/far-overhaul-part-2. Standard Commercial Pricing: Provide your company�s standard commercial pricing information for the identified products and services and explain what is included in those standard prices. Estimated Price Range: You may provide an estimated price or price range for the requirements, including a brief explanation of how the price estimate was developed. Standard Commercial Terms and Conditions: Provide a copy of the standard commercial terms and conditions for the commercial products and commercial services identified in the response to this notice, including nature and duration of standard commercial warranty. 4. Regulatory and Supply Chain Compliance Indicate whether your company could comply with FAR Clause 52.219-14, Limitations on Subcontracting (OCT 2022) if this acquisition were to be set aside for small businesses. Provide a brief supporting explanation. 5. Existing Governmentwide Contract Vehicles Indicate whether your company has its own GSA Multiple Award Schedule (MAS) contract or other federal contract vehicles under which NIST could award an order and, if so, provide the contract details (contract number, Contracting Officer name/contact, SOW, terms and conditions, and price lists). We truly appreciate your company�s willingness to provide the above-mentioned information which NIST will be valuable in helping NIST complete its market research. IMPORTANT NOTES This Notice does not obligate the Government to award a contract or otherwise pay respondents to this notice for information provided in response to this Notice. Following a review of the responses and market research, NIST may publish a solicitation on an authorized site, depending on the chosen acquisition strategy. Responses received after the closing date for this Notice may not be considered. There is no solicitation available at this time. The Government reserves the right to use information that it receives in response to this Notice as it deems appropriate to establish final requirements or for other legally appropriate purposes. Any organization responding to this notice should ensure that its response is complete and

MINIMUM REQUIREMENTS

The Contractor shall provide a system that meets all technical specifications identified below. All items must be new. Used or remanufactured equipment will not be considered for award. Experimental, prototype, or custom items will not be considered. The use of “gray market” components are not acceptable. All line items shall be shipped in the original manufacturer’s packaging and include all original documentation and software, when applicable. 

Line Item 001:
Description: Microscope Body
Quantity: 1
Technical Specifications
Inverted microscope body with the following features:
One or two side ports to attach cameras
Motorized focus drive with minimum step width of 20 nm or better
Motorized nose piece to automatically switch objectives
Motorized filter turret
All optics to allow bright field illumination in transmission AND reflection modes.
Binocular tube and eyepieces when required.
Motorized condenser capable of phase contrast and DIC microscopy.
Focus tracking: Ability to use an infrared light emitting diodes (LED) to independently and continually track microscope focus drift independent of imaging channels.
Sample Stage: Motorized X-Y scanning stage with the following features:
Travel range: ≥100 mm (X-axis) and ≥100 mm (Y-axis)
Resolution: better than 0.5 μm along each axis.
Mounting surface: adapt to allow standard microscope slides (25 mm x 75 mm) or multi-well plates.

Line Item 002: 
Description: Microscope Objectives
Quantity: Total 4, one each with the specifications below
Technical Specifications
All objectives shall be optimized for visible light illumination. 

Line Item 003:
Description: Camera
Quantity: 1
Technical Specifications
Detector: Complementary metal-oxide semiconductor (CMOS)
Resolution: > 15 Megapixels
Cooling method: forced air; stabilize to 25 °C.
Interface: USB 3 with a separate PCIe acquisition interface for fast frame rate readout.
Frame rate: fast frame readout > 20 fps.
Lens mount: C-mount
Exposure Time Range: 0.1 ms to 60 s
Hardware Trigger: Trigger-in for exposure time control, trigger-out for exposure time
Software: Fully integrated into microscope interface
Minimum pixel size: 3 μm x 3 μm or better
Spectral Range: 350 nm to 1000 nm
Adjustable Signal Amplification: from 1x to up to 16x

Line Item 0004:
Description: Illumination Sources and Filter Sets
Quantity: 1
Technical Specifications
Multi-channel light emitting diode (LED) source that replaces traditional mercury vapor sources.
Integrated control unit for continuous brightness adjustment, quickly switchable, and stable for long term experiments.

The combination of source and filters must provide flat illumination across channels.
Minimum of 4-channel fluorescent light source, but up to 7-channel fluorescent excitation lines are preferred.
The preferred 7 channels with excitation filters centered at the following wavelengths are:
UV (385 nm)
Violet (423 nm)
Blue (469 nm)

Filter sets, matching filter cubes and all related accessories to measure commonly used fluorophores including: for UV (385 nm) - DAPI, Alexa 405, Hoechst 33258 and similar dyes; for Violet (423 nm) - eCFP, Lucifer Yellow, Alexa 430 and similar dyes; for Blue (469 nm) - eGFP, Fluo4, FITC and similar dyes; for Green(555 nm) - Cy3, TRITC, DsRed and similar dyes; for Yellow (591 nm) for excitation of mCherry, Alexa 568, mPlum and other similar dyes; for Red (631 nm) - Cy5, Alexa 631, TOTO-3 and similar dyes; and for Far Red (735 nm) for excitation of Cy7 and other similar dyes.

Line Item 0005:
Description: Software
Quantity: 1
Technical Specifications
Software with graphical user interface to operate microscope, all imaging modalities, attached cameras, and accessories supplied by the vendor.
Image acquisition and processing to allow data capture, storage and post-processing of brightfield and fluorescence images.
Ability to export images to standard image formats (e.g., TIFF, JPEG, etc.)
Automation of all motorized components to allow time lapse imaging, sequencing and long-term measurements, z-stack, automated focus tracking, and image tiling.
High dynamic range imaging with the ability to merge images with different excitation intensities.
Ability to script or run microscope automation.
Compatibility of data processing software with Zeiss software microscopes.

Line Item 0006:
Description: Heating/Temperature Control and Carbon Dioxide (CO2) Control Units
Quantity: 1 each
Technical Specifications
Heating/Temperature Control Unit to support mammalian cell cultures at 37 °C for days and weeks.
CO2 Control Unit to maintain carbon dioxide conditions conventionally used in mammalian cell cultures.

Line Item 0007:
Description: Workstation
Quantity: 1
Technical Specifications
Workstation class personal computer with Intel Xeon processor
32 GB RAM or greater 
Dedicated graphics card (Nvidia or equivalent) with 16 GB memory or greater.
A single monitor with a screen measuring 30” or greater diagonally.
All control cards necessary to operate microscope hardware.
SSD of 2 TB or more

Line item 0008:
Description: Interchangeability of parts and software
We require that the system described above (automated inverted microscope system) be compatible with other existing Zeiss microscopes in the lab to enable exchanging components and analyzing data between microscopes (i.e., software must be compatible with Zeiss software for imaging acquisition and analysis).

Title: Notice of Intent to Sole Source: Butler Parachute Harnesses
Solicitation number: FA462026QA278

Description: NOTICE OF INTENT TO SOLE SOURCE TO: BUTLER PARACHUTE SYSTEMS, INC. (UEI: E1URFZC1QLL7 / CAGE: 0D4Z0) The 22nd Training Readiness Squadron (TRS) has a requirement for ten (10) Butler low profile parachute (LPP) training harnesses, part number 11094, for use at the SERE school located at Fairchild AFB, WA. The requested harnesses are a training specific item that meets Air Force requirements as stated in AFI 10-3503, Personnel Parachute Program, from April 2026, AFMAN11-301V1, and the USAF Personnel Parachute Program (PPP) Approve for Use List (AUL). The required harnesses are only manufactured/distributed by Butler Parachute Systems, Inc (BPS). The Air Force Personnel Parachute Program Authorized Use List (AUL) mandates that the only authorized low-profile parachutes (LLP) are manufactured by Butler Parachute Systems (BPS). This requirement is for the LPP training hanging harness manufactured by BPS and specifically designed for training to simulate the use of the mandated LPP from the AUL therefore a sole source purchase is justified. While competition for parachute equipment is limited due to Air Force policy, an Internet search was conducted to look for authorized resellers of BPS equipment. Butler Parachute Systems was contacted and confirmed there are no authorized resellers of this product. Until other LPP products are authorized by the Air Force, BPS will continue to be the only source for the required harnesses. The government will continue to monitor the updated Air Force Instructions for all future purchases of this nature to verify if competition is available. THIS NOTICE OF INTENT IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSALS. This notice is for informational purposes only and is not to be construed as a commitment by the government. Vendors that believe they can provide the items listed above are invited to submit substantiating documentation in writing to the identified point of contact. Information received will be considered solely for the purpose of determining whether to conduct a competitive procurement. Oral communications are not acceptable in response to this notice. A determination by the government to compete this proposed contract based on responses to this notice is solely at the discretion of the government.
