matters.text:
Federal notice (Sources Sought), COMMERCE, DEPARTMENT OF.NATIONAL INSTITUTE OF STANDARDS AND TECHNOLOGY.DEPT OF COMMERCE NIST
Title: Combined Sources Sought Notice and Notice of Intent to Sole Source for Piezoelectric Z-stage Upgrade for Optical Microscope
Solicitation number: NIST-SS26-CHIPS-149
PSC: 6640; NAICS: 334516
Description: ***THIS IS A COMBINED SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE AND NOTICE OF INTENT TO SOLE SOURCE*** The purpose of this sources sought notice is to conduct market research and identify potential sources of commercial products/services that satisfy the Government�s anticipated needs. If no alternate sources are identified, the Government intends to issue a Sole Source Award Carl Zeiss Microscopy LLC, 1 N Broadway STE 1501, White Plains, NY 10601-2335 US, under the authority of Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO) FAR 12.102(a). The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for this acquisition is 334516, Analytical Laboratory Instrument Manufacturing. BACKGROUND The National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) Microsystems and Nanotechnology Division (MND) develops integrated microsystems by advancing the state of the art in nanofabrication, enabling the transfer of NIST measurement technologies to the industrial, academic, and government communities. The MND owns two Zeiss Axio Observer microscopes that serve CHIPS Metrology project GC6.01 � Universal Microscopy Standards. To meet mission-critical requirements, the MND needs to procure a piezoelectric z-stage upgrade for one of these microscopes. This acquisition will provide the Division and CHIPS Metrology with essential capabilities for calibration and measurement method development, assessment of nanofabrication processes, and characterization of microscopy NIST is developing traceable standards for calibrating microscopy systems, including optical microscopes, scanning-electron microscopes, and atomic-force microscopes. A key component of this process is traceable optical microscopy to rapidly characterize standards and establish traceable critical dimensions, enabling the transfer of traceability from the NIST line-scale interferometer (LSI) to other microscopies. Current efforts have established that such characterization, scale calibration in particular, is sensitive to sample positioning in the z direction relative to the optical microscope at the nanometer scale, requiring the ability to adjust the sample position with high fidelity while all optical components of the microscope remain stationary. NIST is seeking information from sources that may be capable of providing a solution that will achieve the objectives described above, and meet the following essential requirements: Piezoelectric z-stage for microscopy (Quantity: 1) Technical Specifications Must integrate with the existing x-y stage of a Zeiss Axio Observer 7 optical microscope. Must be able to be controlled by Zeiss Zen microscope control software, including integration with experiment design functionality in Zen. Must have a travel range in z of 500 micrometers or more Must have a resolution of 1 nm or less Must have a reproducibility of +/- 5 nm or less Must include a stage insert for sample mounting NIST conducted market research from December 2025 to April 2026 by performing internet searches, reviewing product literature, and speaking with vendors to determine what sources could meet NIST�s minimum requirements. The results of that market research revealed that only Carl Zeiss Microscopy LLC (UEI: H41JAKKNEXY1) appears to be capable of meeting NIST�s requirements. HOW TO RESPOND TO THIS NOTICE In responding to this notice, please DO NOT PROVIDE PROPRIETARY INFORMATION. Please include only the following information, readable in either Microsoft Word 365, Microsoft Excel 365, or .pdf format, in the response: Submit the response by email to the Primary Point of Contact and, if specified, to the Secondary Point of Contact listed in this notice as soon as possible, and preferably before the closing date and time of this notice. Please note that to be considered for award under any official solicitation, the entity must be registered and �active� in SAM at the time of solicitation response. Provide the complete name of your company, address, name of contact for follow-up questions, their email, their phone number and, if your company has an active registration in https://sam.gov, your company�s Unique Entity ID (UEI). Identify the equipment that your company sells that can meet the objectives addressed in the BACKGROUND section of this notice. For each product recommended to meet the Government�s requirement, provide the following: Manufacturer name Model number Technical specifications If your company is not the manufacturer, provide information on your company�s status as an authorized reseller of the product(s) Describe performance capabilities of the product(s) your company recommends to meet the Government�s requirements. Additionally, if there are other features or functions that you believe would assist NIST in meeting its objectives described above, please discuss in your response. Discuss whether the equipment that your company sells and which you describe in your response to this notice may be customized to specifications and indicate any limits to customization. Identify any aspects of the NIST market research notice, including instructions, and draft minimum specifications in the BACKGROUND section you cannot meet and state why. Please offer suggestions for how the market research notice and draft minimum specifications could be made more competitive. State whether the proposed equipment is manufactured in the United States and, if not, state the name of the country where the equipment is manufactured. Identify any plans/possibilities for changes in manufacturing location of the aforementioned equipment and provide relevant details, including timeline. For the NAICS code listed in this notice: Indicate whether your company is (a) a small business or (b) other than small business. See the Table of Small Business Size Standards and the associated .pdf download file for small business size standards and additional information. If you believe the NAICS code listed in this notice is not the best NAICS code for the type of product addressed in this notice, identify an alternative NAICS code that you believe would be more appropriate for the planned procurement. Describe services that are available with the purchase of the aforementioned equipment from your company such as installation, training, and equipment maintenance. Describe standard terms and conditions of sale offered by your company for the recommended equipment such as: delivery time after your company accepts the order; FOB shipping terms; manufacturer warranty (including details regarding nature and duration); if available, description(s) of available extended warranty; equipment setup and test; operator and service instruction manual(s); cleanup after installation; and if applicable, other offered services. Provide a copy of manufacturer standard terms and conditions that typically relate to the sale of the specified equipment, if available. State whether your company offers facility renovation services related to installation of the recommended equipment at its delivery destination, if required per the NIST-identified minimum specifications, and provide description of said services. Indicate if your company performs the facility renovation services or typically subcontracts the work to another company. Indicate if your company would be interested in inspecting the intended installation site during the market research phase. State published price, discount, or rebate arrangements for recommended equipment and/or provide link to access company�s published prices for equipment and services. If the recommended equipment and related services are available for purchase on any existing Federal Supply Schedule contract(s) or other contracts against which NIST may be able to place orders, identify the contract number(s) and other relevant information. Identify any customers in the public or private sectors to which you provided the recommended or similar equipment. matters.text:
Federal notice (Special Notice), VETERANS AFFAIRS, DEPARTMENT OF.VETERANS AFFAIRS, DEPARTMENT OF.NETWORK CONTRACT OFFICE 23 (36C263)
Title: SOLE SOURCE - ONE LAMBDA HLA PRO PRIMARY
Solicitation number: 36C26326Q0919
PSC: 6640; NAICS: 334516
Description: INTENT TO SOLE SOURCE � 36C26326Q0919 � DESCRIPTION AND INSTRUCTIONS Department of Veterans Affairs intends to issue a sole source award to One Lambda, Inc. for HLA Pro Primary. This award will be a purchase order for the equipment and under FAR Part 12 of the Revolutionary FAR Overhaul. The NAICS code is 334516 and the size standard is 1000 employees. The PSC is 6640. This notice of intent is not a request for competitive quotations. The Government will consider responses received by the closing date of this notice. Information received will be considered solely for the purpose of determining whether or not to conduct a full and open competitive acquisition or a small business set-aside competitive acquisition. The Government will not pay for any information received in response to this announcement. If the Government decides to compete this requirement in the open market, a synopsis shall be issued utilizing the combined synopsis/solicitation procedure identified in FAR 12 of the Revolutionary FAR Overhaul. A determination to not compete this requirement based upon responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. Description of the Requirement: One Lambda Inc, HLAPROPR � allows for automation of the One Lambda single antigen Class I and Class II assay which are utilized daily in the VA HLA lab for patient care. The One Lambda HLA-Pro is an automation solution for what is currently a completely manual method for single antigen assay for the Iowa City VA HLA lab. The reagents that are currently utilized in the Iowa City VA HLA lab are purchased from One Lambda and this HLA-Pro automation is specifically designed to utilize their reagents for Class I and Class II antigens in an automation platform that; takes patient specimens, prepares them, adds reagents, washes the specimen/reagent and finally prepares the specimen for analysis in the Luminex 3-D instrument. One Lambda HLA-Pro automation is specifically designed to use the One Lambda reagents that the VA HLA labs currently utilize for the Class I and Class II antibody assay. This automation will increase consistency and efficiency of the lab Single antigen lab results. * Lambda(TM) HLA PRO Primary * Lambda(TM) HLA PRO Accessory Kit * Lambda(TM) HLA PRO Starter Kit POTENTIAL SOURCES SHALL INCLUDE THE FOLLOWING INFORMATION IN THEIR RESPONSE: 1. Company name, address, primary contact(s), e-mail address & phone number. 2. A letter from the manufacturer stating your firm is an authorized distributor of theirs. This letter shall be signed by the manufacturer and dated not more than one year ago. 3. SAM UEI number. 4. State if your firm, under the NAICS code, is a large business, small business, service-disabled-veteran-owned small business, veteran-owned small business, HUB zone 8(a), women-owned small business or a small-disadvantaged business. 5. INTENT TO SOLE SOURCE – 36C26326Q0919 – DESCRIPTION AND INSTRUCTIONS
Department of Veterans Affairs intends to issue a sole source award to One Lambda, Inc. for HLA Pro Primary. This award will be a purchase order for the equipment and under FAR Part 12 of the Revolutionary FAR Overhaul. The NAICS code is 334516 and the size standard is 1000 employees. The PSC is 6640. 
This notice of intent is not a request for competitive quotations. The Government will consider responses received by the closing date of this notice. Information received will be considered solely for the purpose of determining whether or not to conduct a full and open competitive acquisition or a small business set-aside competitive acquisition. The Government will not pay for any information received in response to this announcement.
If the Government decides to compete this requirement in the open market, a synopsis shall be issued utilizing the combined synopsis/solicitation procedure identified in FAR 12 of the Revolutionary FAR Overhaul.
A determination to not compete this requirement based upon responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government.
Description of the Requirement: 

One Lambda Inc, HLAPROPR – allows for automation of the One Lambda single antigen Class I and Class II assay which are utilized daily in the VA HLA lab for patient care. The One Lambda HLA-Pro is an automation solution for what is currently a completely manual method for single antigen assay for the Iowa City VA HLA lab. The reagents that are currently utilized in the Iowa City VA HLA lab are purchased from One Lambda and this HLA-Pro automation is specifically designed to utilize their reagents for Class I and Class II antigens in an automation platform that; takes patient specimens, prepares them, adds reagents, washes the specimen/reagent and finally prepares the specimen for analysis in the Luminex 3-D instrument. One Lambda HLA-Pro automation is specifically designed to use the One Lambda reagents that the VA HLA labs currently utilize for the Class I and Class II antibody assay. This automation will increase consistency and efficiency of the lab Single antigen lab results.

4. RECORDS MANAGEMENT OBLIGATIONS
A.  Applicability
This clause applies to all Contractors whose employees create, work with, or otherwise handle Federal records, as defined in Section B, regardless of the medium in which the record exists.  
B.  Definitions
“Federal record” as defined in 44 U.S.C. § 3301, includes all recorded information, regardless of form or characteristics, made or received by a Federal agency under Federal law or in connection with the transaction of public business and preserved or appropriate for preservation by that agency or its legitimate successor as evidence of the organization, functions, policies, decisions, procedures, operations, or other activities of the United States Government or because of the informational value of data in them.  
The term Federal record:
includes Iowa City VAHCS records. 
does not include personal materials.
applies to records created, received, or maintained by Contractors pursuant to their Iowa City VAHCS contract.
may include deliverables and documentation associated with deliverables.
C.  Requirements
Contractor shall comply with all applicable records management laws and regulations, as well as National Archives and Records Administration (NARA) records policies, including but not limited to the Federal Records Act (44 U.S.C. chs. 21, 29, 31, 33), NARA regulations at 36 CFR Chapter XII Subchapter B, and those policies associated with the safeguarding of records covered by the Privacy Act of 1974 (5 U.S.C. 552a). These policies include the preservation of all records, regardless of form or characteristics, mode of transmission, or state of completion. 
In accordance with 36 CFR 1222.32, all data created for Government use and delivered to, or falling under the legal control of, the Government are Federal records subject to the provisions of 44 U.S.C. chapters 21, 29, 31, and 33, the Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) (5 U.S.C. 552), as amended, and the Privacy Act of 1974 (5 U.S.C. 552a), as amended and must be managed and scheduled for disposition only as permitted by statute or regulation. 
In accordance with 36 CFR 1222.32, Contractor shall maintain all records created for Government use or created in the course of performing the contract and/or delivered to, or under the legal control of the Government and must be managed in accordance with Federal law. Electronic records and associated metadata must be accompanied by sufficient technical documentation to permit understanding and use of the records and data. 
Iowa City VA HCS and its contractors are responsible for preventing the alienation or unauthorized destruction of records, including all forms of mutilation. Records may not be removed from the legal custody of Iowa City VAHCS or destroyed except for in accordance with the provisions of the agency records schedules and with the written concurrence of the Head of the Contracting Activity. Willful and unlawful destruction, damage or alienation of Federal records is subject to the fines and penalties imposed by 18 U.S.C. 2701. In the event of any unlawful or accidental removal, defacing, alteration, or destruction of records, Contractor must report to Iowa City VAHCS. The agency must report promptly to NARA in accordance with 36 CFR 1230.
The Contractor shall immediately notify the appropriate Contracting Officer upon discovery of any inadvertent or unauthorized disclosures of information, data, documentary materials, records or equipment. Disclosure of non-public information is limited to authorized personnel with a need-to-know as described in the [contract vehicle]. The Contractor shall ensure that the appropriate personnel, administrative, technical, and physical safeguards are established to ensure the security and confidentiality of this information, data, documentary material, records and/or equipment is properly protected. The Contractor shall not remove material from Government facilities or systems, or facilities or systems operated or maintained on the Government’s behalf, without the express written permission of the Head of the Contracting Activity. When information, data, documentary material, records and/or equipment is no longer required, it shall be returned to Iowa City VA HCS control or the Contractor must hold it until otherwise directed. Items returned to the Government shall be hand carried, mailed, emailed, or securely electronically transmitted to the Contracting Officer or address prescribed in the [contract vehicle]. Destruction of records is EXPRESSLY PROHIBITED unless in accordance with Paragraph (4).
The Contractor is required to obtain the Contracting Officer's approval prior to engaging in any contractual relationship (sub-contractor) in support of this contract requiring the disclosure of information, documentary material and/or records generated under, or relating to, contracts. The Contractor (and any sub-contractor) is required to abide by Government and Iowa City VA HCS guidance for protecting sensitive, proprietary information, classified, and controlled unclassified information.
The Contractor shall only use Government IT equipment for purposes specifically tied to or authorized by the contract and in accordance with Iowa City VAHCS policy. 
The Contractor shall not create or maintain any records containing any non-public Iowa City VAHCS information that are not specifically tied to or authorized by the contract. 
The Contractor shall not retain, use, sell, or disseminate copies of any deliverable that contains information covered by the Privacy Act of 1974 or that which is generally protected from public disclosure by an exemption to the Freedom of Information Act. 
The Iowa City VA HCS owns the rights to all data and records produced as part of this contract. All deliverables under the contract are the property of the U.S. Government for which Iowa City VA HCS shall have unlimited rights to use, dispose of, or disclose such data contained therein as it determines to be in the public interest. Any Contractor rights in the data or deliverables must be identified as required by FAR 52.227-11 through FAR 52.227-20.
The Contractor is responsible for confirming training has been completed according to agency policies, including initial training and any annual or refresher training. 
D.  Flowdown of requirements to subcontractors
The Contractor shall incorporate the substance of this clause, its terms and requirements including this paragraph, in all subcontracts under this [contract vehicle], and require written subcontractor acknowledgment of same. 
Violation by a subcontractor of any provision set forth in this clause will be attributed to the Contractor.

attachments.name: Product Description_LP Analyzer_rev2.pdf
attachments.text:
Product Description
SciAps X-550 XRF Pb HUD/EPA Lead Paint Analyzer Quantity = 1
Measures:
* 0.3% mg in aluminum alloy within 2 seconds
* 0.1% Si in Steels within 6 seconds
* P and S in Steels or Stainless
* low atomic number elements in mining samples
Environmental Temperature Range: 10*F to 13*F (-12*C to 54*C) at 25% duty cycle
Apps: The XRF-550 has the following apps pre-loaded: Lead Paint
Excitation Source: At least a 5W X-Ray Tube. Typically a 50kV, 200uA Rh anode.
Power: On-board rechargeable Li-ion battery, (rechargeable inside device or with external charge)
Weight: 2.98 lbs. (1.35 kg) with battery
Dimensions: 8.5 x 9.5 x 2.4 inches
Display: 2.7-inch color capacitive touchscreen, 400 MHz Qualcomm Adreno 306 2D/3D graphics accelerator.
Rear-facing display for easy results viewing, readable in all conditions.
Security: Password protected usage (user level) and internal settings (admin).
Regulatory: CE, RoHS, USFDA registered, Canada RED Act.
X-Ray Filtering: 6 position filter wheel for beam optimization.
Processing Electronics and Host Processing: 1.2GHz quad ARM Cortex A53 64/32-bit, RAM: 2GB LP-DDR3,
Storage: 16 GB eMMC (storage).
Pulse Processor: 14 bit with digitization rate of 80 MSPS 8K channel MCA USB 2.0 for high-speed data transfer
to host processor. Digital filtering implemented in FPGA for high-throughput pulse processing 20 nS - 24 uS
peaking time.
Detector: 20 mm2 silicon drift detector (active area), 140 eV resolution FWHM at 5.95 Mn K-alpha line.
Calibration Check: External 316 stainless check standard for calibration verification and energy scale validation.
Analytical Range: 32 elements standard, specific elements vary by app. Additional elements may be added upon
user request.
Grade Library: Standard library contains 500+ grades, no practical size limit. Multiple libraries supported,
grades may be added on analyzer or via PC software package (Profile Builder).

MEMORANDUM
Subj: SOLE SOURCE JUSTIFICATION MEMORANDUM FOR AERO-64 SOFT BELT
ADAPTERS
1. Identification of the agency and the contracting activity, and specific identification
of the document as a “Sole Source Justification.”
This is a sole source justification. Contracting activity is NSWC-PCD, Code 024, 110 Vernon
Ave., Panama City, FL, 32407.
2. Nature and/or description of the action being approved.
This action will award a firm fixed price contract to DeVal lifecycle support for the items listed
in Paragraph 3 of this document..
3. A description of the supplies or services required to meet the agency’s needs
(including the estimated value).
Qty.: 28
Item: 1567575
Desc.: AERO-64 Soft Belt Adapter
This acquisition will be conducted using simplified acquisition procedures with a total estimated
value greater than $25,000. The Government's minimum needs have been verified by the
certifying technical and requirements personnel. This memo does not authorize acquisition for
other requirements.
4. Identification of the justification rationale and, if applicable, a demonstration of the
proposed contractor’s unique qualifications to provide the required supply or service.
Restricting Competition for Commercial Acquisitions Below the Simplified Acquisition
Threshold FAR 12.102(a).
The Naval Surface Warfare Center Panama City Division (NSWC PCD) currently has a
requirement for the item(s) listed in Paragraph 3 of this document. DeVal Lifecycle Support is
the OEM of the items listed in Paragraph 3 of this document. These items are the only adapters
certified and approved for use with the support equipment. If another belt were to be selected, it
would have to go through certification and approval, resulting in significant project delay and
unplanned costs. These items are only available direct from DeVal Lifecycle Support as they do
not sell through distribution.
As such, the government does not expect significant savings through competition and it is more
advantageous to the Government to award on a sole source basis to the DeVal Lifecycle Support
for the item(s) listed in Paragraph 3 of this document.

represents the best value consistent with FAR 12.102(a).
The Contracting Officer has determined that this order represents the best value to the Government.
This determination is based on the unique and time-sensitive mission requirements of Special
Operating Forces. Awarding this as a sole-source order is the most advantageous approach. The best
value is achieved by ensuring mission readiness and avoiding the costs and operational impacts of
extended equipment downtime.

results or a statement of the reason market research was not conducted.
For the reasons specified in paragraph 4 above, DeVal Lifecycle Support is the only source that
can meet the Government’s needs. This requirement will be synopsized in the government point
of entry sam.gov because it is estimated greater than $25,000.00.
7. Any other facts supporting the justification.
None.
8. A statement of the actions, if any, the agency may take to remove or overcome any
barriers that led to the restricted consideration before any subsequent acquisition for the
supplies or services is made.
As stated in paragraph 4 above, DeVal Lifecycle Support is the only source that can meet this
requirement

A complete quote is necessary to be adequately considered for award. Respond to each item listed below, if the response is None or Not applicable, explicitly state and explain. In accordance FAR Part 23, sustainable acquisition policies apply to both contracts for products and services that require the delivery, use, or furnishing of products/services to the Government. Indicate if any the following sustainable acquisition categories apply to any products or services proposed: Energy Efficient, Water Efficient, Recycled, Bio-Based, Environmentally Preferable, Non-ozone depleting substances, Less Toxic and/or Less GHGs.c. Authorized Source Confirmation: The following product certification statement below applies to ALL line items and each offeror must submit supporting documentation, as needed: To be considered for award, the offeror/contractor is required to submit documentation confirming that they are an authorized source. An Authorized Source is defined as the original manufacturer, a source with the express written authority of the original manufacturer or current design activity, or an authorized aftermarket manufacturer.3. Price Quote: Submit complete pricing for each individual item listed in the DESCRIPTION OF REQUIREMENTS Section above to include the unit of issue, the extended price for each line item and a total price in US Dollars ($). Note: Ensure FOB Destination shipping costs are included in the pricing.4. Commercial Warranty: If available, provide the terms and length of the Workmanship and/or Manufacturer Warranty on the product(s) and/or services proposed included in the proposed purchase price.EVALUATION FACTORS FOR AWARD:Basis for Award: The Government intends to award a contract to the lowest priced offeror that meets the brand name technical requirements, and who is registered in the System for Award Management (SAM); however, the Government reserves the right to award no contract at all, depending on the quality of quotes submitted and availability of funds. A quote will be considered non-responsive if technical requirements are not met. Technical requirements are defined in Factor I below.Factor I ? Technical: The Government will evaluate the quote and verify if the following specification requirements are met to include all information required for a complete quote as defined in paragraph 2 above:The Government will evaluate the quote and verify specification requirements are met and perform an item risk assessment to determine technical acceptability.This requirement contains supplies that are Brand Name pursuant to FAR 11.105, Items Peculiar to One Manufacturer. To be considered for award, the offeror is required to certify that the product being offered is an original, new, and Trade Agreements Act (TAA) compliant (reference 2(c) above) Quickset Defense Technologies, LLC product. The Government will only accept the required brand name product as specified in Attachment 01. Factor II ? Price: The Government will evaluate the total price to determine if it is fair and reasonable. The price quote shall include a unit price for each item and a total firm-fixed-price for all line items. The total firm-fixed-price shall include all applicable taxes, shipping, and handling costs to the shipping address listed above as outlined in paragraph 3 above.The Government will evaluate the total price and perform a price risk assessment to determine fair and reasonableness.Factor III ? Past Performance: The Government will evaluate past performance, beginning with the lowest priced quote, by reviewing sources that may include, but are not limited to, information from Government personnel and information from sources such as the offerors Responsibility/Qualification (R/Q) documentation in System for Award Management (SAM). The Government will consider supplier risk to assess the risk of unsuccessful performance and supply chain risk using the past performance data in the Supplier Performance Risk System (SPRS) to include quality, delivery, and other contractor performance information.DUE DATE AND SUBMISSION INFORMATIONEligible Offerors: All offerors must have a completed registration in the System for Award Management (SAM) website prior to award of contract. Federal notice (Sources Sought), COMMERCE, DEPARTMENT OF.NATIONAL INSTITUTE OF STANDARDS AND TECHNOLOGY.DEPT OF COMMERCE NIST
Title: Combined Sources Sought Notice and Notice of Intent to Sole Source for an Electrochemical Analysis System
Solicitation number: NIST-SS26-CHIPS-148
PSC: 5961; NAICS: 334516
Description: ***THIS IS A COMBINED SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE AND NOTICE OF INTENT TO SOLE SOURCE*** The purpose of this sources sought notice is to conduct market research and identify potential sources of commercial products/services that satisfy the Government�s anticipated needs. If no alternate sources are identified, the Government intends to issue a Sole Source Award to Gamry Instruments, Inc., 734 Louis Dr, Warminster, PA 18974, US, under the authority of Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO) FAR 12.102(a). The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for this acquisition is 334516, Analytical Laboratory Instrument Manufacturing. BACKGROUND The National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST), Materials Measurement Laboratory, Materials Science and Engineering Division (MSED), Polymers Processing Group is executing a project focused on the recovery of critical minerals�specifically gold, palladium, copper, and rare earth elements�from electronic waste (e-waste). This research requires characterizing the thermodynamics and kinetics of selective electrowinning from complex, multi-ion leachates. To accurately model these systems, the Government requires a high-performance, modular electrochemical workstation capable of high-frequency impedance spectroscopy and hydrodynamic control. The contract shall provide a research-grade, multi-channel potentiostat/galvanostat system which will enables precise measurement of reduction mechanisms and mass-transport kinetics essential for optimizing "urban mining" processes. This system is required to distinguish between metal deposition and competing side reactions during rapid separation cycles. These insights are essential to understanding the recovery processes of these rarely recycled elements from microelectronic waste, directly supporting CHIPS Act goals of strengthening the domestic semiconductor supply chain. NIST is seeking information from sources that may be capable of providing a solution that will achieve the objectives described above, and meet the following essential requirements: Line Item 0001: Research-Grade Potentiostat/Galvanostat/ZRA Channel (Quantity: 1) The Contractor shall provide a research-grade standalone potentiostat/galvanostat/ZRA channel meeting the following specifications: Compliance Voltage: � 12 V minimum Maximum Continuous Current: � 1 A full-scale Data Acquisition speed: Natively support high-speed data acquisition up to 1 MHz (1 �s per point) for transient pulse techniques Current Resolution: 1 pA or better, with potential control resolution down to 1 �V. Electrochemical Impedance Spectroscopy (EIS): Integrated frequency response analyzer (FRA) supporting a frequency Range from 10 �A to 2 MHz without external add-ons, with a benchmark accuracy of 1% up to 100 kHz Included Components: Must include a comprehensive suite of pre-licensed control software covering DC Corrosion, Physical Electrochemistry, Electrochemical Energy, Pulse Voltammetry, and Electrochemical Noise techniques, alongside a 0.6 m cell cable, 2 m USB cable, UDC6 2 kOhm calibration/AC dummy cell, and digital operator's manual. System Assurance: Includes a two-year standard system assurance plan. Line Item 0002: High-Current Application Electrochemical Channel (Quantity: 1) The Contractor shall provide a high-current standalone potentiostat/galvanostat/ZRA channel meeting the following specifications: Compliance Voltage: � 6 V minimum Maximum Continuous Current: � 5 A full-scale Data Acquisition speed: Natively support high-speed data acquisition up to 1 MHz (1 �s per point) for transient pulse techniques Current Resolution: 1 pA or better, with potential control resolution down to 1 �V. Must include pre-licensed control software matching the comprehensive DC, Physical, Energy, Noise, and Pulse Voltammetry suites listed under Line Item 0001, alongside an Interface 5000 cell cable kit (0.6 m) and an Interface 5000 dummy cell. System Assurance: Includes a two-year standard system assurance plan. Line Item 003: Interface Power Hub (120V) (Quantity: 1) The Contractor shall provide a centralized desktop multi-unit docking station and power management infrastructure hub meeting the following specifications: Capacity: Must include all internal slots, power lines, and generic Type B power cables necessary to support up to eight (8) interface cable kits or distinct instrument channels simultaneously. Temporal Clock Synchronization: The infrastructure must include dual interface family bipotentiostat synchronization links/cables to physically tie the internal master clocks of separate channels together. This must guarantee microsecond-level clock alignment and remove temporal latency during concurrent dual-channel (disk and ring) measurements. Electrical Isolation: Connected channels must maintain independent, fully floating ground states to eliminate risk of parasitic ground loops during multi-working electrode setups. Included Accessories: Must include the main 120V Interface Power Hub unit, a 6 ft USB 2.0 cable, and 8 Interface cable kits Warranty: Includes a two-year warranty on the Interface Power Hub. Line Item 0004: RxE 10k Rotating Electrode (Quantity: 1) The Contractor shall provide a complete laboratory rotator system providing hydrodynamic boundary layer management meeting the following specifications: Rotational Dynamics: Adjustable, continuous operational rotation speed spanning from 100 RPM to 10,000 RPM. Rotational Precision: Speed control must be regulated to maintain a constant accuracy of � 1 RPM across the entire velocity range to ensure linear, repeatable Koutecky-Levich data. Included Components: Package must feature the core rotator motor, a heavy-duty laboratory baseplate equipped with a height-adjustable vertical stand, a dedicated electronic motor control unit with matching control cable, a power supply unit, and a USB communications cable. Software: Full integration with the primary electrochemical software to automate Levich and Koutecky-Levich analysis without manual data extraction. Warranty: Includes a two-year limited warranty. Line Item 0005: Description: RDE/RCE Shaft (Quantity: 1) The Contractor shall provide a specialized, dual-purpose drive shaft assembly compatible with the Line Item 0004 rotator meeting the following specifications: Mechanical Integrity: Built with a structural mechanical runout of < 0.1 mm to prevent mechanical wobble and shield low-current signals from hydrodynamic background noise. Dual-Compatibility: The shaft thread pattern must accept interchangeable laminar RDE tips or threaded turbulent RCE cylinder sleeves to allow for both fundamental transport modeling and high-shear industrial scale-up testing. Line Item 0006: Rotating Disk Electrode (RDE) - Glassy Carbon (GC) (Quantity: 1) The Contractor shall provide a thread-mounted Rotating Disk Electrode (RDE) tip consisting of high-purity Glassy Carbon (GC) embedded symmetrically within a chemically inert shroud, engineered to generate perfect laminar fluid flow profiles under uniform rotation. Line Item 0007: Cell Kit for Rotating Electrode Experiments (Standard) (Quantity: 1) The Contractor shall provide a fundamental laminar flow volumetric cell kit containing the following components: Glassware: One (1) 200 mL standard glass cell tailored for sample volumes from 25 mL to 150 mL. Cell Cap: One (1) compatible chemical-resistant PTFE cell cap featuring at least five (5) ports for electrode insertion and gas purging. Electrodes and Bridges: One (1) reference electrode bridge tube, one (1) counter electrode bridge tube, one (1) solid Platinum counter electrode, and one (1) 6-inch secondary Graphite counter electrode. Purge system: One (1) integrated gas bubbler line. Line Item 0008: Silver/Silver Chloride Reference Electrode (Quantity: 1) The Contractor shall provide one (1) premium Silver/Silver Chloride Ag/AgCl laboratory reference electrode, sized and configured to fit securely within the reference electrode

Federal notice (Award Notice), DEPT OF DEFENSE.DEPT OF THE ARMY.W6QK ACC-APG
Title: Notice of Sole Source Award: JBTDS
Solicitation number: W911SR-26-D-A005
PSC: 6665; NAICS: 334511
Award: CHEMRING SENSORS AND ELECTRONIC SYSTEMS, INC. Charlotte NC 28273 USA 48811629.00
Description: Army Contracting Command � Aberdeen Proving Ground (ACC-APG), Edgewood Division, along with Capability Program Executive for Chemical, Biological, Radiological, and Nuclear Sensors (CPE-CBRND) has awarded a sole-source, Indefinite-Delivery/Indefinite-Quantity (IDIQ) contract to Chemring Sensors and Electronic Systems, Inc. (CSES) for the Full Rate Production (FRP) of the Joint Biological Tactical Detection System (JBTDS). The contract has a 36-month ordering period. The JBTDS provides the Joint Forces with a mission-critical capability for sustained operations in a CBRN environment as well as force protection in peacetime and contingency operations. JBTDS is the only militarized, tactical, lightweight biological surveillance system designed specifically for rapid detection, collection, identification and warning of Biological Warfare agents. The system fills a validated Joint Requirement for tactical level biological detection interoperable across Services, highly mobile and sustainable under the constraints of modern force structure. The JBTDS system is a lightweight, man-portable, battery- operable system designed to provide detection, collection and identification of airborne biological warfare agents. The system�s modular architecture Detector/ Collector (D/C), Identifier and Data Station (DS) enable flexible, task-organized deployment across multiple mission sets. The FRP scope encompasses production, quality assurance, testing, configuration management, logistics support and delivery of the production-representative Technical Data Package (TDP). This action represents the logical follow-on to contract W911QY-15-C-0035, under which CSES executed the Engineering and Manufacturing Development (EMD) and Low-Rate Initial Production (LRIP) phases. The FRP contract is required to ensure transition from LRIP to sustained production and fielding. Sole Source Justification (Non-Competitive Award): In accordance with FAR 6.302-1(a)(2)(ii)(A) (Only One Responsible Source: follow-on production of a major system/highly specialized equipment), this action was not awarded competitively. CSES is the only source capable of executing all components of the contract. The redacted Justification and Approval (J&A) will be posted to SAM.gov in accordance with RFO requirements.

The item description and salient characteristics are as follows: the Hot Flusher cleans the FOHE while it is installed on the aircraft, which prevents overheating and unnecessary downtime, saves the FOHE from premature failure, and expedites aircraft availability. The specific requirement is for one Fuel Oil Heat Exchanger Flush Kit, Part Number: HF11 AF F 15, utilized for F-15 fuel/oil heat exchanger flushing. The system must meet the following technical specifications: designed for a portable flight line or shop use environment; utilizes a solvent-free thermal oil system; operates at 185�F to 195�F oil heat; features a flow rate of 4 to 80 GPM with a maximum regulated oil pressure of 80 PSI; includes a 4 to 100-gallon reservoir; utilizes a 120 PSI air purge; features an automated reversing flow mechanism; contains a filtration system consisting of a 28-micron reusable screen, a 10-micron disposable filter, and a 50-micron reservoir filter; utilizes quick-connects and an air hose with a nozzle; is equipped with digital temperature and pressure gauges alongside a flow meter; includes safety features such as auto-timers, an automatic shutoff dirty-filter sensor, and an Emergency Stop (E-Stop). The sole-source determination is based on market research, which included a review of previous contracts and current market availability for Fuel Oil Heat Exchanger Flush Kit, Part Number: HF11 AF F 15. On 12 July 2024, the F-15 System Program Office (SPO) confirmed that units participating in the fuel-oil heat exchanger cleaning program must use the Fuel Oil Heat Exchanger Flush Kit, Part Number: HF11 AF F 15 and coordinate with the F-15 SPO to ensure the equipment is properly configured prior to use on the F-15 weapon system. The Government intends to award a sole source award to Hot Flush LLC based on the requirement for the Brand Name item specified above and supporting market research. The determination not to compete this proposed contract action is solely within the discretion of the Government. Information received will normally be considered for the purposes of determining whether to conduct a competitive procurement. Description: *****THIS IS A COMBINED SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE AND NOTICE OF INTENT TO SOLE SOURCE***. BACKGROUND The National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) Physical Measurement Laboratory (PML), Nanoscale Device Characterization Division, Advanced Electronics Group intends to purchase a microwave resonator accessory add-on for NIST existing Bruker Biospin ELEXSYS-II E500 continuous wave X-band electron spin resonance (ESR) spectrometer. This cavity must be 100% compatible with the existing instruments software and hardware components. The only known company able to provide this needed equipment without sacrificing the integrity of the system or requiring substantial efforts to implement is Bruker Biospin. A primary strategic focus of the division involves utilizing ESR to resolve the chemical and physical nature of atomic-scale defects in materials. This research is critical for identifying and controlling defect entities responsible for critical failure and drift mechanisms in solid state devices. Furthermore, the ability to be quantitative, i.e. being able to count how many defects are present, is critical to evaluate different processing and materials synthesis steps. Thus, this procurement seeks an add-on accessory resonator capable of providing in situ quantitative measurements through a rectangular double cavity design, known as a TE104 variety microwave resonator. Furthermore, the new resonator must be fully compatible with the division�s existing ESR infrastructure. This integration is vital to ensure operational continuity and to leverage established institutional expertise without requiring significant retraining or specialized knowledge deviation. NIST is seeking information from sources that may be capable of providing a microwave resonator. If no alternate sources are identified, the Government intends to issue a Sole Source Award to, Bruker Scientific under the authority of FAR 12.102(b) The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for this acquisition is 334516. The microwave resonator must meet the following minimum specifications: The microwave resonator shall be fully compatible and seamlessly integrate into the NIST existing electron spin resonance spectrometer, a Bruker Biospin ELEXSYS-II E500 and its control software (proprietary Bruker Biospin software Xepr). The microwave resonator shall be fully compatible and seamlessly integrate with the auto tuning capabilities of the existing spectrometer. The microwave resonator shall be a double rectangular cavity operating in the transverse electric 104 mode (TE104). The microwave resonator shall have an unloaded Q value of at least 7000. The microwave resonator shall have a nominal resonance frequency of 9.7 GHz and support modulation frequencies between 1 kHZ and 100 kHz. DEPARTMENT OF THE AIR FORCE
97TH AIR MOBILITY WING (AETC)
ALTUS AIR FORCE BASE OKLAHOMA
16 March 2026
MEMORANDUM FOR 97 MX/MXOBP
FROM: 97AMW/MXMCF
SUBJECT: Air Compressor Replacements for Hangars 518
1. The 97th Maintenance Squadron is wanting to procure 1ea replacement air compressors
used in performing aircraft maintenance. The air compressors will be used to replace the
current worn, damaged air compressors. The current air compressors do not provide
adequate air supply and quality. As a result, we experience excessive damage to tools and
insufficient air supply required for use with the fall restraint systems. This creates safety
hazards for personnel and potentially damaged tools.
Specifications
• Type: Two-Stage Reciprocating Air Compressor
• Intended Use: Heavy shop or industrial applications (e.g., automotive service,
manufacturing, farming)
• Power: 25 HP (18.6 kW)
• Motor: 230/460V Open Drip Proof (ODP) motor with a 460V E-Series Starter
• Tank Size: 120-Gallon ASME-coded receiver tank
• Rated Pressure: 175 psig (12 bar g)
• Capacity (FAD): 82.0 cfm (2.32 m³/min)
• Duty Cycle: 100% continuous duty
• Pump Life: Designed for over 15,000 hours of use
• Construction: Durable, 100% cast iron pump
• Weight (Air-cooled): 1951.62 lbs (887.1 kg)
• Dimensions: 76.0 in (L) x 51.0 in (W) x 62.0 in (H)
• Key Features:
• Air-cooled aftercooler
• Low oil level switch
• Electronic drain valve
• Dual control with a centrifugal unloader
• Maintenance: Uses All Season Select synthetic lubricant, allowing for 2,000 hours
between changes.
• Designed for easy service with individually cast cylinders.
• Included Accessories: High Dust Filter Silencer and a standard installation kit.

• Electrical installation to include all materials for connecting to existing facilities
without modifications.
• Mechanical installation to include all materials for connecting to existing facilities
without modifications.

Description: ***THIS IS A COMBINED SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE AND NOTICE OF INTENT TO SOLE SOURCE*** The purpose of this sources sought notice is to conduct market research and identify potential sources of commercial products/services that satisfy the Government�s anticipated needs. If no alternate sources are identified, the Government intends to issue a Sole Source Award to Quantum Design, Inc., 10307 Pacific Center Ct, San Diego, CA US, under the authority of Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO) FAR 12.102(a). The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for this acquisition is 334516, Analytical Laboratory Instrument Manufacturing. BACKGROUND The National Institute for Standards and Technology�s (NIST) Materials Science and Engineering Division (MSED) is involved in the development of standard reference materials (SRMs) for magnetic moment � a critical standard for measuring magnetic materials for next generation memory and computing, in transformers for the power grid, and for AC-DC conversion for chargers such as for your cell phone, among many applications. NIST magnetic SRMs are the only source of SRMs for calibrating magnetometers and thus providing traceable and quantitative magnetic measurements. The NIST Magnetic Property Measurement System 3 (MPMS3) Superconducting Quantum Interference Device Vibrating Sample Magnetometer (SQUID VSM) is one of the first built (serial #9, installed at NIST in 2007), and suffered a recent failure of the probe, which houses the superconducting magnet and the SQUIDs. Over the past 17 years, there have been significant changes to the probe, which have improved the sensitivity and noise levels of these instruments and the ability to repair the instrument on site. These instruments are the most sensitive magnetometers available, and as such, NIST�s SQUID VSM is vital to its magnetics standards work. Without the SQUID VSM, NIST support of current SRMs and development of new SRMs will be halted, which will have significant impacts across many applications and industries. This repair is urgently needed to maintain capabilities for developing and testing new magnetic SRMs and developing the associated documentary standards that use the new SRMs. The contractor shall provide one (1) new replacement probe for the Superconducting Quantum Interference Device Vibrating Sample Magnetometer (SQUID VSM). attachments.name: Coverpage_Solicitation_FA910126QB058.pdf
attachments.text:
DEPARTMENT OF THE AIR FORCE
HEADQUARTERS AIR FORCE TEST CENTER
EDWARDS AIR FORCE BASE CALIFORNIA
COMBINED SYNOPSIS/SOLICITATION_FA910126QB058
This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for a commercial product prepared in accordance with the format
in the Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation Overhaul (RFO) subpart 12.202, as supplemented
with additional information. The Government reserves the right to reject any or all offers received in
response to this solicitation. Furthermore, the Government maintains the right to not make an award under
this solicitation, and reserves the unilateral right to cancel this solicitation, in whole or in part, at any
point prior to award if it is determined to be in the Government's best interest.
All solicitation provisions and contract clauses applicable to this procurement are incorporated and set
forth in Attachment 2 – SF 1449. Submission of a quote constitutes acknowledgement and acceptance of
all terms contained within this attachment.
Solicitation Number: FA910126QB058
Solicitation Type: Request for Quote (RFQ)
North American Industry NAICS code 332912 - Fluid Power Valve and Hose Fitting
Classification System (NAICS) Manufacturing
Code:
Federal Supply Code (FSC): 4810 - Valves, Powered
Size Standard: 1,000 Employees
Set-Aside Status: 100% Small Business Set-Aside
Nonmanufacturer Rule (NMR) Not Applicable
Description of Requirement:
The Government requires a quantity of three (3) brand-name only Parker SE60 Servo Valves (P/N:
SE60SAAHANA25) to be delivered to Silver Spring, Maryland. This is purely a supply procurement
with no "or equal" products or incidental services. All items must be factory-new and provided by an
authorized reseller. See “Attachment 1 - Parker SE60 Specifications” for full details.
Justification for Brand Name Restriction:
The required valves operate in parallel within the facility's existing control infrastructure. Procuring the
identical brand-name model is technically essential to maintain immediate interchangeability and
operational usability. Utilizing any alternative brand would require a major, unfunded control system
redesign to accommodate different electrical drive signals and flow characteristics. Procuring the exact
Parker valves is required to prevent extended facility downtime, avoid costly system re-engineering, and
maintain critical wind tunnel testing throughput. Based on the rationale, competition shall be restricted to
only authorized resellers of the brand name requirement.
Determination for 100% Small Business Set-Aside:
Based on market research, at least two small businesses are interested in and capable of meeting the
subject brand name requirement; therefore, in accordance with RFO Part 19, this acquisition is solicited
as a 100% Small Business Set-Aside.
One AFMC…Powering the World’s Greatest Air Force
Non-Applicability of NMR:
The total estimated value to meet the subject requirement is below the Simplified Acquisition Threshold
(SAT); therefore, the Nonmanufacturer Rule does not apply.
DPAS Priority Rating:
DO-C9 in accordance with RFO 52.211-15. The "DO" rating ensures the manufacturer gives this order
preferential lead-time treatment over unrated commercial orders. The "C9" program identification symbol
was selected because AEDC Hypervelocity Wind Tunnel 9 conducts testing and evaluation that directly
supports miscellaneous national defense and Research & Development (R&D) programs, aligning with
the "Miscellaneous / Testing" designation under DPAS Schedule I (15 CFR Part 700).
CMMC Exemption:
The Government has determined that the product required under this solicitation is a Commercially
Available Off-the-Shelf (COTS) item. Because this procurement is exclusively for a COTS product, the
Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification (CMMC) requirements are not applicable. Offerors are not
required to hold or demonstrate a CMMC certification level to be eligible for award under this
solicitation.
Basis for Award:
The Government intends to award a single, firm-fixed-price purchase order to the responsible offeror
whose quote conforms to the solicitation and offers the lowest reasonable price to the Government.
The evaluation process will be conducted in the following sequential steps:
1. Price Sorting: Rank all quotes by the total quoted price, from lowest to highest.
2. Size Standard Validation: Beginning with the lowest-priced quote, confirm compliance with the
solicitation in relation to the small business size standard under NAICS code 332912, which is
1,000 employees.
NOTE: Offers from vendors that do not meet the small business size standard of 1,000 employees
will not be considered for an award and the evaluation process will end here.
3. Technical Validation: Validate that the offeror with the lowest priced quote meeting the business
size standard is an authorized reseller of the brand name requirement and that the quoted product
meets the required specifications per Attachment 1. If the lowest-priced quote is determined
technically "Acceptable," the evaluation stops, and that offeror will be selected for award
(pending an affirmative responsibility determination and price reasonableness). If the lowest-
priced quote is determined to be technically "Unacceptable," the Government will evaluate the
next lowest-priced quote, continuing this process until a technically acceptable quotation is
identified.
NOTE: If the lowest priced quote requires resolution of minor or clerical errors to any aspect of
the quote, the Government will consider the correction potential and may enter interchanges with
that offeror. If, after interchanges to resolve minor or clerical errors, the quote is determined
technically “Acceptable” and remains the lowest priced quote, the order will be awarded to that
offeror. If the Government deems the quote not easily correctable, or if at any time the quote
becomes other than the lowest priced, the next lowest priced quote will be evaluated for technical
acceptability. Interchanges will take place as necessary or deemed appropriate by the
Government.
4. Responsibility Determination:
The Government will evaluate the apparent successful offeror to determine responsibility in
accordance with RFO Subpart 9.1. This includes verifying that the offeror has an active
registration in the System for Award Management (SAM.gov), does not have any active
exclusions or suspensions, and possesses a satisfactory record of performance, integrity, and
business ethics. If the lowest-priced, technically acceptable offeror is determined to be non-
responsible, the Government will refer the matter to the Small Business Administration (SBA) for
a Certificate of Competency (COC) determination or proceed to evaluate the next lowest-priced
quote if appropriate.
5. Determination of Price Reasonableness:
The final quoted price will be evaluated for reasonableness in accordance with RFO 12.209, using
the price analysis techniques defined in RFO 15.404-1.
Instructions to Offerors:
Offerors must submit a complete quote that conforms to all solicitation requirements. Quotes must be
valid for a minimum of 60 days from the submission deadline.
Submission Method
Quotes must be submitted electronically via email to the Contracting Officer, Brooke Vandeman
(brooke.vandeman@us.af.mil), and Contract Specialist, Paytonne Szatkowski
(Paytonne.Szatkowski@us.af.mil), no later than 1:00 PM Central Time on 9 July 2026. Late quotes will
not be accepted.

INTENT TO SOLE SOURCE
The Department of Veterans Affairs, Network Contracting Office 4 (NCO4) intends to sole
source a contract for the instrumentation, reagents supplies and services to perform Clinical
Laboratory Chemistry, Immunochemistry, Chemiluminescent and Hematology Testing on an
automation line with auto-verification. All work is to be completed in accordance with the
Statement of Work. This sole source contract will be solicited and negotiated with Beckman
Coulter, LLC under the authority of FAR 13.106-1 – Single Source Justification.
See attached Draft Statement of Work (SOW).
The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for this procurement is
334516. The Small Business Administration (SBA) size standard is 1,000 employees.
Interested vendors that can meet this requirement, shall identify their interest and capability, and
respond to this notice by 07/08/206 NLT 10:00 AM EST. Interested vendors must send a
capability statement, no more than one page in length; to include Company Name, ueiSAM
Number, Socioeconomic Category, brief description of your business entities capability to
handle this project at the Wilkes-Barre VA Medical Center.
This Special Notice of Intent to Sole Source is for planning purposes only. No solicitation will be
made available. This is NOT a request for quotations. All information shall be provided at no
cost or obligation to the Government. Responses must be sent via email to the Contracting
Specialist at christa.stine@va.gov.
Responses received will be evaluated; however, a determination by the Government not to
compete the proposed procurement based upon the responses to this notice is solely at the
discretion of the Government. If no responses are received, Contracting will proceed with the
sole source negotiation with Beckman Coulter, Inc.
Special Notice
Page 2 of 38
STATEMENT OF WORK
Clinical Laboratory Chemistry, Immunochemistry, Chemiluminescent and Hematology
Instrumentation with Automation Line and Auto-verification
DESCRIPTION/SPECIFICATIONS/STATEMENT OF WORK
SCOPE OF PROCUREMENT:
1. The instrumentation shall have the capability of performing or reporting the clinical
parameters as defined in the statement of work. The instrument shall have random access
capability (if discrete testing is required) and be able to able to simultaneously perform the
complete profile as described below to meet the performance characteristics for accuracy
and precision as defined by the 1988 Clinical Laboratory Improvement Act (CLIA) and the
Clinical and Laboratory Standards Institute (CLSI). This request is for the instrumentation,
reagents supplies and services to perform Clinical Laboratory Chemistry, Immunochemistry,
Chemiluminescent and Hematology Testing on an automation line with auto-verification.
2. ORDERING METHOD: The participating facility may order products via Electronic Data
Interchange (EDI), telephone, Electronic mail or other written communication, identifying the
products by number, quantity, purchase price, address for delivery, and any special
instructions.
2.1.1. Equipment must maintain, or preferably reduce the number of workstations or
overall labor required to accomplish the required testing by each laboratory.
2.1.1. Equipment should be acquired for Wilkes-Barre VAMC. Equipment must meet
the volume and turnaround time requirements of Wilkes-Barre VAMC Lab. Typically
routine hematology samples should be completed in under 20 minutes, routine
chemistry in no more than 70 minutes and routine immunochemistry samples in 90
minutes. STATs are typically 60 minutes from receipt in lab to verification in lab
computer.
2.1.2. The Contractor is required to provide a continuously stocked inventory of
reagents, standards, controls, supplies, disposables and any other materials
required to properly perform tests on the equipment such that equipment
operations are not interrupted. These items shall be of the highest quality,
sensitivity, specificity and tested to assure precision and accuracy. Sigma
performance may be included to support test quality. Expiration date must be
clearly marked on reagent, standards and control containers. Unexpected changes
in methodology/technology shall be at the expense of the Contractor.
Page 1 of 38
Alert/Notification of any delays in shipment as well as any or all technical
advisory/recalls/alerts, prior to or simultaneously with field alerts should be
forwarded to the designated individuals determined at contract award. The
Contractor shall provide a copy of all relevant permits/licenses and certifications
inclusive of any sanctions current or pending throughout the United States of
America.
2.1.3. Special handling for emergency orders of supplies: In the event that the supplies
are found to be defective and unsuitable for use with the Contractor’s equipment, or
the Contractor has failed to comply with the requirements for routine supply
delivery, the Contractor is required to deliver the supplies within 24 hours of receipt
of a verbal order for emergency delivery. If either circumstance has occurred, the
Contractor shall deliver to the Government site in the most expeditious manner
possible without additional cost to the Government, the necessary consumables in
sufficient quantity as required to allow operation of the Contractor’s equipment for
one week (under normal Government test load volume). If additional requests for
emergency supply delivery are required by the Government, they shall be honored
by the Contractor until the arrival at the laboratory of the monthly standing
order/routine supplies delivery.
3. DEFINITIONS:
3.1.1. Cost per Patient Reportable Result (CPRR)- a Cost-Per-Test Clinical
Laboratory Analyzers - Contractors are required to provide a price for a reportable
patient result. The per patient reportable result price shall include costs covering:
(1) installation of new equipment and equipment use for the entire contract period,
(2) all reagents, standards or calibrators, quality controls, supplies,
consumable/disposable items to include but not limited to printer paper, Printer
maintenance kits, printer cartridges, parts, accessories (including replacement of
printers as they fail) and any other item required for the proper operation of the
Contractor’s equipment including water supply systems and maintenance of these
systems and anything necessary for the generation of a patient reportable result.
This per patient reportable result price shall also encompass all costs associated
with dilution; repeat and confirmatory testing required producing a single patient
reportable result. It shall also include the material to perform as well as all other
costs associated with quality control, calibration and correlation study testing that is
prescribed by the Clinical and Laboratory Standards Institute (CLSI). (3) all
necessary maintenance to keep the equipment in good operating condition (This
Page 2 of 38
element includes both preventive maintenance and emergency repairs) and (4)
training for Government personnel both off-site and on-site. Contractors shall
provide delivery, installation and removal of equipment at no additional charge.
3.1.2. Cost per Test (CPT) - , Part III, Cost-Per-Test Clinical Laboratory Analyzers –
Contractors are required to provide a price for each test that can be performed on
its equipment. The per test price shall include costs covering (1) equipment use
for the life of the contract, (2) all reagents, standards/ calibrators, quality controls,
supplies, consumable/disposable items, paper, parts, accessories (including
replacement of printers as they fail) and any other item required for the proper
operation of the Contractor’s equipment including water supply systems and
maintenance of these systems and anything necessary for the generation and
reporting of a test result, (3) all necessary maintenance to keep the equipment in
good operating condition (This element includes both preventive maintenance and
emergency repairs) and (4) training for Government personnel both off-site and on-
site. Contractors are required to provide delivery, installation and removal of
equipment at no additional charge.
3.2. TEST MENU: Refer to Attachment A Test List for desired test menu and estimated
annual volumes.
4. GENERAL REQUIREMENTS:
4.1. Automation Line/Middleware
4.1.1. Automation line must support all instruments provided by the vendor.
4.1.2. Must be able to connect instrumentation to an automated line. The automated
line must be able to accept all size tubes, all types of caps, with minimal bar-code
readers. It must contain an automated refrigerated stockyard that holds at least
10000 samples.
4.1.3. Automation line must have large input module for volume and have automated
specimen retrieval capabilities.
4.1.4. Must have middleware to control all instrumentation, track all specimens on the
system, and be programmable for automatic reflex testing and automatic rerun.
4.1.5. Automatic calculations performed by instrument or middleware
4.1.6. Specimen archival through mapping of specimens to racks; for easy retrieval
once moved off-line.
4.1.7. Must support the current auto verification software in use at the WBVAMC which
requires maintaining and adding rules for both the Remisol Advance software and
Data Innovations Instrument Manager wrapper rules for the current instruments and
Page 3 of 38
new instruments added to the automation line. There must be Data Innovations
support included to assist in writing new rules for newly added instrumentation and
for troubleshooting any issues that may occur that could break current rules.
4.2. Chemistry and Immunochemistry
4.2.1. Primary analyzer(s) – Base equipment offered that shall fully support the scope
of operations (minimal requirements). Multiple analyzers are required to meet the
productivity specifications defined herein. Therefore, additional analyzer(s) shall,
likewise, be considered primary instrumentation and shall meet all of the technical
specifications of this solicitation. (2 primary analyzers for Chemistry and 2 primary
analyzers for Immunochemistry).
4.2.2. Operational Features- The instrumentation offered shall have the following:
4.2.2.1. The capability of performing analysis on 100% of the tests listed in
Attachment A Test List.
4.2.2.2. Sufficient capacity and throughput to meet the volume/ service demands
as defined in Attachment A Test List.
4.2.2.3. Safety features to avoid unnecessary exposure to biohazardous and
chemical material. The exposure to and the volume of biohazardous and
chemical material generated by the equipment must be minimal and require a
minimum amount of handling. Contractor must provide a mechanism for the
Clinical Laboratory to meet local discharge requirements (i.e. mercury and
formaldehyde SDS sheets must be provided in advance for review).
4.2.2.4. A bi-directional, bar-coded computer interface compatible with the current
VA laboratory information system. The fully operational interface (both
hardware and software) shall be immediately available for implementation to
the VA computerized hospi

Justification for Other than Full and Open Competition Under Simplified Procedures for Certain
Commercial Items in Accordance with Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 13.5
On the basis of the following, I, as the Contracting Officer, hereby approve the use of a brand name
contractual action pursuant to the authority of: (cid:1800) 41 U.S.C. 1901 (cid:1407) 41 U.S.C. 1903
1. Contracting Activity
The Naval Research Laboratory’s (NRL) Contracting Division, Code 1320, proposes a brand name
requirement for Keysight Technologies, Inc. (Keysight) parts, accessories, and licenses under
simplified procedures for certain commercial items in accordance with FAR Subpart 12.2.
The instrument to be procured from Keysight Technologies is the Keysight Infiniium UXR
oscilloscope, a state-of-the-art instrument with bandwidth up to 110 GHz (W-band) with 4-channel
configurations.
2. Description of the Action Being Approved
This action requests approval for the use of other than full and open competition, on a brand name
basis, as implemented by FAR 12.102 for the procurement of a UXR0404BP Oscilloscope,
subcomponents, and licenses. This instrument will allow Code 5710 to characterize phenomena up to
W band in bench and chamber set-ups, increasing branch’s current capability to a higher frequency
range that is currently not achievable with existing infrastructure. This procurement also includes
Vector Signal Analysis supporting base software, which seamlessly integrates with the UXR-Series
oscilloscope, and a calibration module for W band.
3. Description of Supplies/Services
The required oscilloscope is a test and measurement tool that will be used to visualize and analyze the
spectral content (frequency characteristics) of radar signals. The NRL will utilize this oscilloscope to
identify system design issues, optimize performance, and understand signal behavior from adversarial
radar systems. The signal analyzer and its associated accessories and licenses will be integrated into
existing Electronic Warfare (EW) system suites.
The Infiniium UXR oscilloscope offers unparalleled performance, with ultra-low noise and the
highest signal fidelity available in the market, enabling engineers and scientists to observe and
understand even the fastest phenomena. The UXR-BP is a state-of-the-art instrument with bandwidth
up to 110 GHz (W-band) with 4-channel configurations. The instrument will enable characterization
capabilities up to W band in bench and chamber set ups, which will enhance Code 5710’s current
capability to a higher frequency range, currently not achievable with existing infrastructure.
Page 1 of 4
Keysight Infiniium UXR Oscilloscope Purchase Request No.: 57-1014-26 / 1301352027
J&A No.: J&A13.501-26-TS09
The Keysight Infiniium UXR-BP oscilloscope is configurable up to have 110 GHz of real-time
oscilloscope bandwidth. Due to cost considerations, the UXR-BP will allow Code 5710 to reach up to
110 GHz with 5MHz bandwidth windowing. Larger bandwidth windows (10, 20 GHz, etc.) are an
additional cost which are currently not being considered, but can be added at a later point if there is a
need. The UXR-BP has high-definition 10-bit analog-to-digital converter (ADC), with full bandwidth
and channel upgradability and the industry’s highest Effective Number of Bits (ENOB), which
measures the real-world performance of an Analog-to-Digital Converter (ADC) or digital signal
system, capturing errors from noise, distortion, and jitter, at all supported bandwidth. As previously
stated, this procurement also includes Vector Signal Analysis supporting base software, which
seamlessly integrates with the UXR-Series oscilloscope, and a calibration module for W band.
It is estimated that delivery of the UXR-BP will occur within 17 weeks after receipt of the purchase
order, and software delivery will occur within five weeks after receipt of purchase. The Government’s
minimum needs have been verified by the certifying technical and requirement personnel. This
oscilloscope, accessories, and licenses are estimated to be , which will be funded with
FY26 Capital Improvement Program (CIP) funds.
4. Statutory Authority Permitting Other Than Full and Open Competition
The authority for permitting other than full and open competition is 41 U.S.C. 1901(e)(2),
implemented by FAR 12.102(b).
(cid:1409) 41 U.S.C. 1901 (cid:1407) 41 U.S.C. 1903
5. Rationale Justifying Use of Cited Statutory Authority
Market research was conducted per FAR 10.001 to identify potential sources for an oscilloscope,
subcomponents, and licenses that meets the Government’s technical needs. Initial market research
determined that Keysight, the original equipment manufacturer (OEM) of the required items, and its
authorized resellers/distributors, are the only vendors that could meet the Government’s technical
requirements. Further market research revealed multiple authorized resellers/distributors of Keysight
equipment. Because there are multiple authorized resellers/distributors, the Government will pursue
this procurement on a brand name basis. A small business set-aside is not appropriate because the
Non-Manufacturer Rule (NMR) requires the small business to either manufacture the product itself,
supply a product manufactured by another small business if it is a nonmanufacturer, or supply the
product of any sized manufacturer if the Small Business Administration (SBA) has granted a waiver
to the NMR. Keysight the OEM, is a large business, and the SBA has not granted a waiver under
NAICS 334515.
Keysight equipment is the only equipment identified that can meet the Government’s requirements
for a multi-channel, W band, low signal noise oscilloscope with measurement capabilities. Keysight
is the only vendor in the market that currently manufactures an oscilloscope with multichannel and W
band capabilities due to their custom ASICs and FPGAs along with their custom software packages.
Keysight’s Infiniium UXR oscilloscope offers unparalleled performance, with ultra-low noise and the
highest signal fidelity available in the market. Additionally, Keysight’s custom software package
allows NRL engineers to work off of an existing successful software base layer. Any other non-OEM
software package would require re-development of code or code integration, effectively duplicating
the initial software development phase, resulting in substantial duplication of costs and significant
unplanned labor costs and schedule overruns, and impacting overall budget and delivery timelines.
The estimated duplication of effort is 2,000 labor hours resulting in a cost of approximately
$270,000.00 and approximately one year of delay.
Page 2 of 4
Keysight Infiniium UXR Oscilloscope Purchase Request No.: 57-1014-26 / 1301352027
J&A No.: J&A13.501-26-TS09
The Contract Specialist has determined through market research that the required products offered by
Keysight are commercial in nature, valued greater than the SAT, but less than $9.0 million, and as
such, this action permits the use of FAR 12.201-1.
6. Description of Efforts Made to Solicit Offers from as Many Offerors as Practicable
Market research was performed through contacting knowledgeable individuals in Government,
conducting internet searches, contacting the Keysight directly, and other instrumentation companies
such as Rohde & Schwarz. Code 5710, routinely monitors the commercial marketplace and maintains
up-to-date knowledge of current market solutions through conferences, trade shows, seminars, and
publications such as Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineer (IEEE) Communications and
Journal of Electromagnetic Defense (JED). Keysight is the only manufacturer that currently offers a
multi-channel, W band off the shelf oscilloscope that meets the requirements of augmenting
characterization capabilities for Code 5710.
It has been determined that Keysight equipment is the only brand technically acceptable that meets
NRL’s required specifications. Market research identified that while the OEM (Keysight) does not
hold a GSA Schedule, at least one authorized small business reseller (Tevet) does. However, due to
the Non-Manufacturer Rule (FAR 19.505) and the absence of an SBA waiver for NAICS 334515, a
small business set-aside is not permissible. To ensure the Government receives the best value and
allows for competition between the OEM and all of its authorized resellers (both on and off GSA), the
Government will pursue this effort through the open market on an unrestricted brand name basis.
7. Determination of Fair and Reasonable Cost
The Contracting Officer has determined that the anticipated cost to the Government for the equipment
covered by this J&A is fair and reasonable through adequate price competition (FAR 12.204(a)), or
through the use of other price analysis methods. The Government identified multiple authorized
resellers/distributors for Keysight equipment and has a reasonable expectation of competition based
on the market research conducted.
8. Actions to Remove Barriers to Future Competition
For the reasons set forth in Paragraph 5, NRL has no plans at this time to compete future contracts for
the type of equipment covered by this document. Code 5710 routinely monitors the commercial
marketplace using the internet and publications to stay informed on current state-of-the-art laboratory
equipment alternatives that could be used to further work at NRL. If another potential source emerges
or new technology is developed, which can advance future research, NRL will assess whether
competition for future requirement is technically feasible and reasonably priced.
In accordance with FAR 12.202(b)(1)(iii) this justification, redacted as necessary, will be made
publicly available with the solicitation.
Page 3 of 4
Keysight Infiniium UXR Oscilloscope Purchase Request No.: 57-1014-26 / 1301352027
J&A No.: J&A13.501-26-TS09
CERTIFICATION AND APPROVAL
TECHNICAL/REQUIREMENTS CERTIFICATION
I certify that the facts and representations under my cognizance which are included in this Justification
and its supporting acquisition planning documents, except as noted herein are complete and accurate to
the best of my knowledge and belief.
LEGAL REVIEW
I have determined this Justification is legally sufficient.
6
CONTRACTING OFFICER CERTIFICATION
I certify that this Justification is accurate and complete to the best of my knowledge and belief.
COMPETITION ADVOCATE APPROVAL
Upon the basis of the above justification, I hereby approve, as the Competition Advocate, the solicitation
of the proposed procurement described herein using other than full and open competition, pursuant to the
authority of 10 U.S.C. 2304(c)(1).
