CUI
Department of the Air Force: Justification for Other Than Full and Open Competition
I. Agency and Contracting Activity (RFO 6.104-1(a)(1)):
The contracting organization that is responsible for the proposed contract action is the Air Force Test
Center (AFTC), Directorate of Contracting, Installation Contracting Division, AFTC/PZZG, 5 South Wolfe
Avenue, Edwards AFB, CA 93524-1185. Justification for other than full and open competition.
II. Nature and/or description of the action being approved (RFO 6.104-1(a)(2)):
The current F-35 cockpit architecture (TR-2) has reached its maximum computational capacity. Transitioning to the TR-3
modernization suite is a mission-essential requirement to enable Block 4 capabilities and maintain air dominance against
near-peer threats.
III. Description of supplies/services required to meet agency needs (RFO 6.104-1(a)(3)):
The legacy mobile demonstrator was originally procured as a low-fidelity outreach tool for public engagement. However, the
system currently fails to meet the technical fidelity requirements for mission-relevant training. A hardware upgrade is
essential to achieve configuration parity with our existing simulation architecture and ensure tactical consistency across the
trainer enterprise.
IV. Statutory Authority Permitting Other Than Full and Open Competition (RFO 6.104-1(a)(4)):
10 U.S.C. 3204(a)(1), Only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements.
V. Rationale for Use of Authority (RFO 6.104-1(a)(5)):
Even if the legacy system works fine today, its parts are facing Diminishing Manufacturing Sources and Material Shortages
(DMSMS). Buying the upgrade now avoids massive, unpredictable maintenance and reverse-engineering costs in the next
5-10 years
VI. Integrated Market Analysis and Efforts to Solicit Competition (RFO 6.104-1(a)(6), (8), and (10)):
Market research for this procurement was limited solely to evaluating the capabilities and pricing of Driven Technologies.
Due to the highly specialized nature of the existing JSE F-35 cockpits architecture, introducing an alternative vendor would
result in a substantial duplication of cost that is not expected to be recovered through competition, as well as unacceptable
delays in fulfilling the Department of War's mission requirements. Therefore, market research focused strictly on validating
Driven Technologies' ability to continue providing this critical support
VII. Determination of Fair and Reasonable Cost (RFO 6.104-1(a)(7)):
The Contracting Officer is responsible for evaluating, determining, and documenting the anticipated contract cost/price is
fair and reasonable in accordance with RFO Subpart 15.4, Contract Pricing.
VIII. Any Other Facts Supporting the Justification (RFO 6.104-1(a)(9)):
The proposed F-35 cockpit is a specialized design tailored to meet IFAST (445TS/EWJN) mission requirements, distinguishing it from
legacy JSE cockpits. It will replace our current low-fidelity PMIC cockpit, which is fabricated from PVC pipe and no longer
adequately supports critical training and mission rehearsals.
March 2026 Page 2 of 3
CUI
Department of the Air Force: Justification for Other Than Full and Open Competition
While Driven manufactured the original Joint Simulation Environment (JSE) F-35 cockpits, the cockpit requested here is uniquely
configured to support the specific mission requirements of the Integrated Flight Avionics Systems Testbed (IFAST) under the 445th
Test Squadron (445TS/EWJN). Our current Precision Measurement Equipment Laboratory/Instructional cockpit (PMIC) is a low-
fidelity, highly portable PVC-pipe construction that fails to realistically represent an actual aircraft. Because this legacy setup no
longer adequately supports essential mission rehearsals or Flight Test Conductor courses, replacing it with a high-fidelity,
representative cockpit is critical to meeting our operational training standards.
Hardware degradation in the aging legacy cockpit poses a significant risk to operational readiness, threatening to delay essential
mission rehearsals and Flight Test Conductor (FTC) courses within the IFAST (445TS/EWJN). Furthermore, the current estimated
lead time to field a replacement is projected to exceed 12 months, compounding the risk of mission impact if action is delayed.
Competing this effort to a new vendor would force the government to fund the design from scratch. Lacking the existing design
baselines, a new vendor would introduce severe pricing uncertainty, with engineering estimates indicating that development
duplication would double the baseline cockpit cost.
IX. Actions to Overcome Barriers to Competition (RFO 6.104-1(a)(11):

STATEMENT OF WORK
National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA)
NOAA FISHERIES
Southeast Fisheries Science Center-Panama City Laboratory


. 

Background/Overview: Shark depredation, the removal or damage of fish by sharks, has become a growing issue with consequences ranging from economic losses from lost or damaged catch, bait, and gear; increased mortality of released fish and degraded fishing experiences. This has increased the calls for NOAA-Fisheries to address depredation. Multiple theories exist for why depredation is such a problem including shark population increases, increased recreational effort coupled with greater numbers of released fish and shark behavioral adaptation. Emerging evidence indicates that individual sharks may learn from repeated encounters with fishing activity and associate the sound of vessel engines or the hauling of gear with feeding opportunities. Several areas have been identified as “high depredation risk areas” in the Gulf of America (Drymon et al. 2022; Aycock et al., Figure 1). Areas will be chosen for experimental analysis; potentially one in Federal waters off Alabama and one off the west coast of Florida. Within those areas, one site will be designated as a control while the other as the experimental site. The literature shows some degree of site fidelity for some shark species but the degree of site fidelity to high depredation risk areas currently is unquantified. 

Scope of Work: The development of electronic animal tagging technologies (i.e., biologging, telemetry) over 60 yr ago was a watershed moment for the study of aquatic animal behavior, and continued advances and miniaturization of electronic tags have allowed researchers to quantify previously unobserved processes important to population dynamics, reproductive performance, and fitness in a wide range of taxa. In particular, the study of fish biology has benefited immensely over the past 25 yr with a near exponential increase in the number of published studies utilizing electronic tagging technology. A key development that has enabled this is the passive acoustic array and that acoustic tags often now can be equipped with sensors (e.g., pressure, temperature, acceleration) increasing the range of behaviors that can be studied. Commercial shark longline vessels will also be contracted to capture sharks in high depredation areas. Sharks will have acoustic pinger tags inserted to monitor, with a listening station array at each site, their movements and residency for one year. Simultaneously, depredation rates will be monitored in both the control and experimental sites with cooperating for-hire or recreational fisherman with Captain and Crew reporting depredation rates using electronic reporting applications (no cost associated)

Tasks: The contractor will provide (1) VR100 – Surface Transponder and Manual Tracking Acoustic Receiver (Model VR100-300); (1) VHTx 69kHz Transponding Hydrophone 25 meter waterproof cable for VR100; (190) V16-4x-A69-2801; Rounded Case; (27) NexTrak AR – Transponding Acoustic Release Receiver with battery; and (3) Magnetic Activation Probe for acoustic receivers.

Description: NIST-SS26-06 6640 / 334516 Primary POC: Liz Timberlake (Elizabeth.timberlake@nist.gov)? Secondary POC: Donald Collie (Donald.collie@nist.gov)? ? Title:? Dual Optical Frequency Comb System BACKGROUND ***THIS IS A COMBINED SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE AND NOTICE OF INTENT TO SOLE SOURCE*** The National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) is seeking information from sources that may be capable of providing a dual optical frequency comb system. If no alternate sources are identified, the Government intends to issue a Sole Source Award to X3 Optics LLC (1880 S Flatiron Ct, Suite F, Boulder, CO 80301) under the authority of FAR 12.102(a) only one reasonably found source. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for this acquisition is 334516. NIST has a need for a dual optical frequency comb system that meets or exceeds the following draft minimum specifications: The Contractor shall provide one (1) array spectroradiometer that meet the following minimum specifications: 1.Comb Architecture: The system should have two optical frequency combs with 50 MHz repetition rate (or less) each and a controllable difference in repetition rates (from 0 to 10?kHz tuning). 2.Spectral Coverage and Power: The system should have a center wavelength at 1550 nm and >30 nm of bandwidth. Average optical power should be 10 mW (or more). 3.Carrier offset frequency: The system should have an integrated carrier offset frequency detection with high signal to noise ratio of (> 30 dB). The system should have a locked carrier envelope offset frequency with 10 Hz). 5. Optical or RF lock: The system should have an option to lock a comb line to an optical reference CW laser at 1550 nm. In addition, the system should have an outputting repetition rate beat note for directly locking the repletion rates of each comb to a RF reference. 6. Interface: The system should have a digital control interface for phase locking the two degrees of freedom of each comb. 7. Output: The system should have optical outputs terminated with polarization maintaining fiber with FC/APC connector. 8. The system shall operate using a 100-230 VAC, 1 phase, 50-60 Hz 9. The laser system shall have Programmability with Python, MATLAB, LabVIEW, C. The vendor shall supply scripts to control the systems using Python, MATLAB, and LabView NIST conducted market research from February through April of 2026 by attending conferences, speaking with colleagues, performing internet searches, and speaking with vendors to determine what sources could meet NIST�s minimum requirements. The results of that market research revealed that only X3 Optics LLC appears to be capable of meeting NIST�s requirements. Title: Notice of Intent to Sole Source Near Field Range Antenna
Solicitation number: W51AA1-26-R-0013
PSC: 6625; NAICS: 334515
Description: Notice of Intent to Sole Source Notice Type: Special Notice / Notice of Intent to Sole Source Solicitation Number: W51AA1-26-R-0013 Agency/Office: Department of the Army, Army Contracting Command, Tobyhanna Army Depot (TYAD) Location: Tobyhanna, PA 18466 NAICS Code: 334515 - Instrument Manufacturing for Measuring and Testing Electricity and Electrical Signals PSC Code: 6625 - Electrical and Electronic Properties Measuring and Testing Instruments 1. Description of Intent The U.S. Army Contracting Command, on behalf of Tobyhanna Army Depot (TYAD), intends to negotiate and award a firm-fixed-price contract on a sole-source basis to NSI-MI TECHNOLOGIES INC., 1125 Satellite BLVD NW STE 100, Suwanee, Georgia, 30024-4629 This acquisition is conducted under the authority of FAR 13.106-1(b)(1), Only One Responsible Source. 2. Requirement Overview TYAD possesses and utilizes Near-Field Ranges (NFRs) to troubleshoot, test, and calibrate antenna systems in support of its Command, Control, Communications, Computers, Cyber, Intelligence, Surveillance, and Reconnaissance (C5ISR) mission. To modernize existing capabilities and support emerging requirements, TYAD requires a vertical Cylindrical Near-Field (CNF) system. The Contractor shall supply, deliver, install, and calibrate all necessary hardware and software items to enable these measurement operations. The required deliverables include: See Attachment 1 � SOW (DRAFT) for more information. Place of Performance: Tobyhanna Army Depot, Tobyhanna, PA 18466. 3. Submission of Capabilities This Notice of Intent is not a request for competitive proposals or quotes. A formal solicitation will not be issued. However, any firm that believes it can meet this requirement in its entirety may submit a capability statement. Capability statements must demonstrate the firm's ability to provide the exact equipment (MEC-AZ-20 and ELE-ARC), integrate it with TYAD's existing near-field range infrastructure, and provide the perpetual CNF software licenses and precision calibration services required. Submission Detail Information Response Deadline June 1, 2026 @ 1:00PM EST Format Electronic submission via email only Point of Contact Mark Buonomo Email Address mark.buonomo2.civ@army.mil Information received will normally be considered solely for the purpose of determining whether to conduct a competitive procurement in the future. A determination by the Government not to compete this proposed contract based upon responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. 4. Disclaimer Any responses received will not be considered a proposal or quote, and the Government will not pay for any information submitted in response to this notice.

STATEMENT OF WORK (SOW) / EQUIPMENT SPECIFICATION)
Near-Field Range UpgradeAntenna forForCylindrical Near-Field Measurement CapabilityTobyhanna Army Depot (TYAD)June 2, 2026

PART 1 — GENERAL INFORMATION
1. GeneralThis is a supply contract for the procurement, delivery, installation, and calibration of commercial equipment. The personnel performing the installation and integration are not subject, either by the contract's terms or by the manner of its administration, to the supervision and control usually prevailing in relationships between the Government and its employees.
1.1 Description of Equipment/IntroductionThis is a supply contract to provide, integrate, and test an Azimuth Antenna Positioner (AAP), Antenna Range Controller (ARC), all necessary cabling & ancillary equipment, and cylindrical near-field software for use in an existing Near-Field Range (NFR) to enable Cylindrical Near-Field (CNF) measurements. The Contractor shall supply, deliver, install, and calibrate all necessary hardware and software items to enable these measurement operations.
1.2 BackgroundTobyhanna Army Depot (TYAD) possesses and utilizes NFRs to troubleshoot, test, and calibrate antenna systems which are part of its Command, Control, Communications, Computers, Cyber, Intelligence, Surveillance, and Reconnaissance (C5ISR) support mission. To modernize existing capabilities in support of emerging requirements, TYAD requires a vertical CNF system. The equipment and software delivered on this contract will augment existing range capabilities to ensure maximum readiness and precision measurement of complex antenna systems.
1.3 ScopeThe Contractor shall provide all equipment, supplies, transportation, tools, materials, personnel, supervision, and other items necessary to supply, deliver, install, and calibrate the hardware and software as described in this SOW and associated contract documents, except for those items specified in Part 3 – Government Provided Utilities, Equipment, and Materials. The Contractor shall perform to the standards and acceptable quality levels identified in this SOW and associated contract documents. Specifically, the Contractor shall deliver, install, and calibrate one (1) AAP, one (1) ARC, all necessary cabling, and CNF software at TYAD.
1.4 Objectives
Deliver a fully functional set of equipment, including:
MEC-AZ-20 Azimuth Rotary Positioner
ELE-ARC Antenna Range Controller
All required cabling including, but not limited to, motor cable, power cable, and V35 to ARC cable
Radio Frequency (RF) Absorber for RF reflection / scattering mitigation
Deliver technical documentation for the CNF equipment, including:
Interface Control Diagram
User’s Guide
Maintenance Manual
Transport, install, and integrate all equipment at the designated NFR at TYAD.
Calibrate and perform operational testing to verify equipment performance and measurement capabilities.
Provide over-the-shoulder training for TYAD operators to include software operation, equipment usage, maintenance, and troubleshooting.
1.5 General Information
1.5.1 Quality Control Plan (QCP)This acquisition is for commercial items performed under FAR Part 12. In accordance with FAR 12.208, the Contractor's existing quality assurance system will be utilized. The Contractor shall submit their Quality Control / Installation Plan within 10 days of award.
1.5.2 Recognized HolidaysInstallation and calibration work shall not be performed on U.S. federally recognized holidays occurring during the normal workweek unless otherwise directed by the Contracting Officer.
1.5.3 Operating Hours
1.5.3.1 Government Facility Office Hours: The Government facility office hours are 0700-1530, Monday through Friday, except U.S. Holidays or when the Government facility is closed due to local or national emergencies, administrative closings, or similar Government-directed closings.
1.5.3.2 Contractor Installation Hours: The Contractor shall perform installation and integration tasks between the hours of 0700-1530, Monday through Friday. The Contractor shall maintain an adequate workforce to ensure the uninterrupted delivery and installation of all items defined within this SOW when the Government facility is open.
1.5.4 Place of PerformanceThe delivery and installation under this contract will be performed at Tobyhanna Army Depot, Tobyhanna, PA 18466.
1.5.5 Davis Bacon Act ComplianceWhile the primary scope of this effort is the procurement and installation of equipment, the Contractor shall comply with the Davis-Bacon Act (DBA) for any associated construction, alteration, or repair activities required for site preparation and installation. If the Contractor performs incidental construction tasks—such as pouring concrete foundations, executing structural modifications, or installing facility integrations (e.g., conduit, HVAC connections)—that constitute a substantial and segregable portion of the overall contract, the Contractor shall apply DBA prevailing wage requirements to that specific work. In such instances, the Contractor shall ensure that all laborers and mechanics performing the segregable construction tasks are paid no less than the local prevailing wage rates determined by the Secretary of Labor (as specified in the wage determination attached to this contract). Furthermore, the Contractor shall adhere to all associated DBA reporting requirements, including the submission of certified payroll records in accordance with applicable Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) clauses.
1.6 Security Requirements
1.6.1 Installation AccessAccess to U.S. installations, buildings, and controlled areas is limited to personnel who meet security criteria and are authorized. Failure to submit required information/data and obtain required documentation or clearances will be grounds for denying access to U.S. installations, buildings, and controlled areas.
1.6.2 Installation Pass LogThe Contractor shall provide the Contracting Officer, via the COR, an Initial Installation Pass Log within 3 calendar days after contract award. The log must contain, at a minimum: employee name, company, position, clearance level (if applicable), and installation pass number. An Updated Installation Pass Log shall be submitted to the COR within five (5) days of any changes.
1.6.32 Background ChecksThe Contractor shall submit all required personnel information to the TYAD Security Office, via the COR, to facilitate background checks for installation access. Unfavorable results will result in the personnel not being allowed access to the installation.
1.6.34 Operations Security (OPSEC) RequirementsContractor personnel shall adhere to facility security policies and restrictions. The Contractor shall immediately report suspicious activities to security personnel.
1.7 Safety
1.7.1 Safety Laws and Regulations: The Contractor shall comply with FAR 52.236-13, Accident Prevention, the references contained therein (e.g., U.S. Army Corps of Engineers Safety and Health Requirements Manual (EM 385-1-1)), and all applicable Federal, State, and Safety Laws and Regulations. An Accident Prevention Plan shall be submitted prior to the commencement of installation activities.
1.8 Data RightsThe Government has unlimited rights to all documents and materials produced under this contract.
1.9 Protection of Government and Contract InformationPer Public Use Notice of Limitations stated by the Defense Imagery Management Operations Center at www.dimoc.mil/resources/limitations/, the Contractor shall not cite any information obtained through this contract on any hard copy or digital marketing tools to include its company website.

PART 2 — DEFINITIONS & ACRONYMS
2.1 Definitions
Contracting Officer: means a person with the authority to enter into, administer, and/or terminate contracts and make related determinations and findings on behalf of the Government.
Contracting Officer's Representative (COR): As defined in DFARS 202.101, means an individual designated and authorized in writing by the Contracting Officer to perform specific technical or administrative functions.
Contractor: means a supplier or vendor awarded a contract to provide specific supplies or equipment to the Government.
Day: means, unless otherwise specified, a calendar day.
Deliverable: means anything that can be physically delivered, but may include non-manufactured items such as meeting minutes or reports.
PART 3 — GOVERNMENT PROVIDED UTILITIES, EQUIPMENT, AND MATERIALS
3.1 - Site Access and Utilities: The Government will provide the Contractor access to the designated installation site at Tobyhanna Army Depot during standard normal working hours as defined in this SOW. Access outside of normal working hours will be coordinated through the COR. During the installation phase, the Government will permit the Contractor to utilize existing, standard facility utilities (e.g., 120V electrical power, running water) strictly for the purpose of executing the installation and testing of the equipment.
3.2 - Staging and Delivery: The Government will designate a temporary staging and offloading area for the receipt of the equipment. The Government will provide unloading and transportation to the staging area. The Government will not provide material handling equipment or labor to assist with uncrating or final installation of the equipment.
3.3 - Contractor Responsibilities: Except for the specific site access and basic utilities explicitly stated above, the Government will not provide any tools, specialized testing equipment, incidental construction materials (e.g., fasteners, conduit, wiring), or labor. The Contractor shall furnish all necessary tools, materials, material handling equipment, and labor required to complete the delivery, installation, and integration of the equipment in accordance with this SOW.

PART 4 — CONTRACTOR FURNISHED ITEMS AND INSTALLATION SUPPORT
4.1 GeneralThe Contractor shall furnish all equipment, supplies, transportation, tools, materials, personnel, supervision, and other items necessary to deliver and install the items as described in this SOW and associated contract documents, except for those items specified in Part 3 Government Provided Utilities, Equipment, and Materials.
4.2 MaterialsThe Contractor shall provide the AAP, ARC, all necessary cabling & ancillary equipment, mounting hardware, CNF measurement software, and all necessary calibration instruments to perform the installation and operational testing.
4.3 Background ChecksThe Contractor shall provide personnel information for the performance of Background Checks in accordance with paragraph 1.6.3 of this SOW.

PART 5 — SPECIFIC TASKS
5.1 Installation ScopeThe Contractor shall provide near-field equipment delivery, installation, and calibration as described in the following Task Statements. All work shall be performed IAW the standards identified herein.
5.2 Tasks
5.2.1 Equipment Delivery: The Contractor shall deliver the near-field equipment within 90 days after receipt of order to Tobyhanna Army Depot. The delivery shall include all hardware, software, and physical & electronic copies of manuals.
5.2.2 Installation: The Contractor shall install the near-field equipment at the designated facility within TYAD. The Contractor shall assemble, mount, and integrate the positioner with facility power and local control systems. The Contractor shall remove and properly dispose of all packaging, crating, and installation debris from TYAD.
5.2.3 Testing and Calibration: The Contractor shall perform initial operational testing and precision calibration of the installed near-field equipment to ensure it meets COTS manufacturer specifications for precision measurement. The Contractor shall submit an Installation and Calibration Report.
5.2.4 Program and Contract Management: The Contractor shall manage all logistics, scheduling, and personnel requirements associated with this delivery and installation.
5.2.5 Training: The Contractor shall provide on-site, over-the-shoulder

matters.text:
Federal notice (Combined Synopsis/Solicitation), GENERAL SERVICES ADMINISTRATION.FEDERAL ACQUISITION SERVICE.GSA/FAS/GSS/QSCB, SUPPLY CHAIN MANAGEMENT CONTRACTING DIVISION
Title: Brand Name NI � Various PXI/PXIe Test and Measurement Modules
Solicitation number: 47QSSC-26-Q-0187
PSC: 6625; NAICS: 334515
Description: The General Services Administration, Office of Contracting Operations, Supply Chain Management Contracting Service Center is issuing a Request for Quote (RFQ) for a commercial item. This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial products prepared in accordance with FAR Part 12 (GSA Class Deviation RFO-2025-12). This announcement constitutes the only solicitation. Offers are being requested and a separate written solicitation will not be issued. ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- This is an All-or-None, Brand Name Only procurement. Solicitation number 447QSSC-26-Q-0187 is issued an as RFQ for the procurement of National Instruments (NI) PXI/PXIe test and measurement modules. The requirement includes: QTY (1) - 787358-01 PXIE-6509, 96-CH 5V/TTL/CMOS (24MA) DIGITAL I/O MODULE QTY (1) - 780587-48 NI PXIe-2748 3 GHz 16x1 Multiplexer QTY (1) - 785117-01 PXIe-5433 PXI Waveform Generator, 80 MHz, 16 bits, 800 MS/s, 1 Channels, 512 MB QTY (1) - 778572-69 PXI-2569 PXI Relay Module, SPST (open), 100-Channel, 100 V, 1 A QTY (1) - 780587-24 PXIe-2524 2 A, Multi-bank Multiplexer (16 banks of 8x1, 1-wire) End item application: National Instruments PXIe-1084 PXI Express test rack ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- This solicitation incorporates provisions and clauses by reference. The full text of provisions and clauses may be accessed electronically at www.acquisition.gov. All delivery locations will be within the Continental United States and shipments must be compliant with MIL-STD-129 marking and labeling. Full delivery addresses will be provided on awarded Purchase Orders. Delivery addresses will either be disclosed at time PO is issued, or the vendor may be required to contact the GSA Transportation Department at time of shipment to obtain shipping information. Submit requests to dodtransportationrequest@gsa.gov. Prices are requested on a FOB Destination basis with offerors' best delivery lead time. Offerors who submit quotes must be registered to receive Purchase Orders via EDI, through OMS Vendor Portal, or be willing to onboard within 5 business days of award. To be considered for award, offerors must: Submit a complete, accurate, and fully compliant quote with all required documentation and completed fields. Submit a quote via email with all required documentation by the closing date and time stated in the solicitation. Offers received after the time specified in the solicitation will be deemed �late�. Acceptance of incomplete or late submissions is solely at the discretion of the Contracting Officer. Offerors determined to have met all administrative and technical requirements of the RFQ by the solicitation closing date and time will proceed to the final evaluation factor, Price. If there is a tie on the lowest quoted price, DARO will be the tiebreaker. Award will be made on an all-or-none basis as a result of this RFQ. Find attached: RFQ document MIL-STD-129 form Please contact brandon.israel@gsa.gov with any questions.

MILITARY STANDARD 129R MARKING AND SHIPPING LABEL REQUIREMENTS

Unit and Intermediate Container marking- Barcoded NSN-no dashes, NSN with hyphens, cage code,
part number (PN specified in the contract may be the PN assigned by the Government procuring activity
or the PN of the actual manufacturer. Letters “PN” or “P/N” shall be used to identify this information),

number, Shelf-life marking, If TCN Number available indicate. If both the contract number and the
purchase order cannot be placed on the label, place the purchase order number on the label.
Exterior Containers marking - use the same basic label format as unit containers, but without
the item description. In addition the NSN, Purchase Order Number and CAGE Code must also be
barcoded. This can be done on one large label, or two smaller labels placed side-by-side.

STATEMENT OF WORK
Rate Integrating Gyroscope Manufacturing and Refurbishment
26-JUNE-2025
1 BACKGROUND AND SCOPE
This Statement of Work (SOW) establishes the requirements for the refurbishment, manufacturing, qualification, inspection, and delivery of the Rate
Integrating Gyroscope, MIL-G-81168/5B, PN#7517308 used in the MK-82 Gun and Guided Missile Director. Naval Surface Warfare Center (NSWC)
Crane Division is the designated overhaul point for the MK-82 Director, a subsystem of the MK-99 Fire Control System (FCS).
2 APPLICABLE DOCUMENTS
7517308 Long life Gyroscope
MIL-G-81168 Revision Gyroscope, Rate Integrating
MIL-G-81168/5 Revision B Gyroscope, Rate Integrating
MIL-STD-129 Military Marking for Shipment and Storage
3 REQUIREMENTS
3.1 General Requirements:
3.1.1 The contractor shall furnish all equipment, parts, and labor necessary for the refurbishment and/or
manufacture of Gyroscope PN# 7517308.
3.1.2 The contractor shall be responsible for shipment of all overhauled and new manufactured MK-82 Rate
Integrating Gyroscopes to NSWC Crane 300 Highway 361 Crane, IN 47522.
3.1.3 For Rate Integrating Gyroscopes to be delivered to the Government, the contractor shall perform marking
for shipment and storage processes IAW MIL-G-81168 Para 5.1 & 5.2 Level C Packaging
3.1.4 For Rate Integrating Gyroscopes to be delivered to the Government, the contractor shall apply
equipment markings and identification processes using MIL-STD-129 IAW MIL-G-81168 Para 5.3.
3.1.5 Requirements of MIL-G-81168/5 supersede those of MIL-G-81168 when conflicting.
3.2 Manufacturing Requirements
3.2.1 The contractor shall manufacture the MK-82 Rate Integrating Gyroscope IAW MIL-G-81168/5. Testing documentation IAW para 3.4 of this
SOW is applicable.
3.3 Refurbishment Requirements
3.3.1 Subcomponents which exhibit failures, or deterioration leading to imminent failure shall be designated for replacement.
3.4 Testing Requirements (CDRL A001)
3.4.1 Gyroscope Assemblies shall be tested IAW MIL-G-81168 Table I Schedule 2, paragraph 4.8, 4.9, and MIL-5-81168/5 Sheets 8 & 9.
3.4.2 Performance parameters are specified in MIL-G-81168/5 when not specified within MIL-G-81168.
3.4.3 Testing performed IAW SOW para 3.4 shall not include MIL-G-81168 Table I Schedule 1 tests.
3.5 Qualification
3.5.1 The Contractor is exempt from execution of qualification requirements in MIL-G-81168 Para 4.3.2, if the Contractor is currently production
or has been in-production within the last 24 months.
N0016426RLL11
Page 7 of 64
3.6 Component Certifications (CDRL A002, Certificate of Compliance)
3.6.1 As specified in the drawing specifications of each assemblies' components, certificates of compliance shall be delivered to the government
with each order.
3.6.2 Contractor shall inspect each manufactured item and/or purchased item against drawings/specifications, and shall provide a Certificate of
Compliance (COC) to document compliance of each hardware item with item drawings/specifications. The contractor shall provide a hard copy of the
COC with each hardware item produced IAW with this SOW. Contractor shall make hard copies of the COCs available to the Government upon

B. 2 - Statement of Work
___________________________________________________

A. BACKGROUND

The VA Iowa Health Care System has a need for the purchase Brand Name or Equal Thoren Maxi-Miser Caging System – Model No. 9-126-9-14-1-4-5TMGB.

B. SALIENT CHARACTERISTICS 

Specifications – Brand Name or Equal – Thoren Maxi-Miser Caging System – Model No. 9-126-9-14-1-4-5TMGB.

General Equipment Name: Animal Caging System
Description & Salient Characteristics
System must hold minimum 126 small mouse cages
System must be on casters to keep it mobile.
System maximum dimensions, 28”W X 67”L X 84”H
System must hold cages size, 7.7” X 12.17” X 5.25: or 7.7” X 12.17” X 5.875”
System must include Udel Polysulfone cages (126) or other approved.
System must a cage air flow system with dual 99.99% efficient HEPA filters for supply and exhaust with prefilters to extend life of HEPA filters
 8 amperes at full load, 120 volts single phase, 60hertz
5-10 DB range
Required Individual Line Items & Quantity of Items
(1) Vented Animal Caging System 
(2) Maintenance Manuals (CD, PDF or Word)
(2) User Manuals
(1) Cleaning Instructions for all equipment, supplies and accessories
Warranty Requirements
Manufacturer must offer a (1) one-year minimum warranty that product is free from defects in materials and workmanship. All defects will be replaced or repaired by the manufacturer at no cost to the buyer.


Installation
No installation required.
Training
No training required. 

C. PERIOD OF PERFORMANCE:

60 DAY ARO

D. TYPE OF CONTRACT 

This is a Firm-Fixed-Priced, one-time supply contract with no option year(s).

This contract is assigned a POC and will provide general instructions for administrating the contract. The POC is not authorized to grant permission(s) to change the scope of the project. Location
Iowa City VA Health Care System
POC:
Assigned at the time of Award by email.

The vendor shall deliver the equipment via standard delivery with F.O.B. destination as scheduled. See Section C for delivery schedule period-of-performance. 

The equipment shall be delivered to the following address:

Iowa City VA Health Care System
601 Highway 6 West, 
Iowa City, IA 52246

Before performing any action in a non-contractual nature or is considered out-of-scope, the Contractor shall contact the Point of Contact (POC) and the Contract Officer identifying the reason(s) for change. All changes shall have prior authorization from a VA Contract Officer in the form of a written modification. 
I. POST-AWARD PERFORMANCE CONFERENCE
The POC, Contract Specialist, or Contract Officer may schedule a post-award performance conference with Contractor, if deemed necessary, for contract orientation purposes.
J. SECURITY
No security language required.
K. PRIVACY
No Privacy language required.

End of Statement of Work

Federal notice (Special Notice), DEPT OF DEFENSE.DEPT OF THE AIR FORCE.DEPT OF THE AIR FORCE
Title: Intent to Sole Source - 304 SABRE Parachute and Equipment
Solicitation number: FA487726QA150
PSC: 1670; NAICS: 314999
Description: This is not a solicitation, and quotes are not being accepted at the moment. The 355th Contracting Squadron intends to issue a sole-source procurement action for the procurement of the following items: 0001 SABRE 3 170 - 2 ea 0002 SABRE 3 190 - 4 ea 0003 SABRE 3 210 - 6 ea 0004 SABRE 3 230 - 3 ea 0005 PD176 7 CELL RESERVE CANOPY - 2 ea 0006 PD193 7 CELL RESERVE CANOPY - 4 ea 0007 PD218 7 CELL RESERVE CANOPY - 6 ea 0008 PD235 7 CELL RESERVE CANOPY - 3 ea 0009 CHANGEABLE MODE CYPRES 2 1-PIN - 15 ea 0010 VECTOR 3 W/OPTIONS - 15 ea 0011 FULL RIGGING, ASSEMBLY AND PACK - 15 ea 0012 Shipping & H Fee - 1 ea 0013 TP-460 M3 9 CELL MAIN CANOPY - 3 ea 0014 EZ-425 (VS-425) CONTROL LINE - 1 ea 0015 SET TP-460 COMPLETE LINE SET - 1 ea 0016 CLOSING LOOP-VECTOR 3 MAIN - 50 ea This requirement is accomplished in accordance with FAR Part 13.501(a) �Soliciting from a single source�. In accordance with AFI 10-3503, Personnel Parachute Operations, rescue operators are required to wear parachute risers, drogues and airbags as part of free-fall jumps, and per AFI 10-3503 Chapter 9, 9.1.1.3, USAF parachutists will only use the equipment for which they have received system-specific training. An Approved For Use List exists that is signed by the AF Personnel Parachute Program Manager. The Air Force Personnel Parachute Program (PPP) Approved For Use List (AUL) specifically identifies the SPECIAL OPERATIONS VECTOR-3 TANDEM SIGMA (SOV-TS), MAIN , SPECIAL OPERATIONS VECTOR-3 TANDEM SIGMA (SOV3-TS), RESERVE , and TANDEM PHOENIX (TP) SERIES as authorized parachute systems to be worn by rescue operators. These parachute systems are manufactured and sold by Complete Parachute Solutions, INC (CPS). Since the AUL exists that mandates specific items that are certified for use by the Air Force and only one company manufactures the approved items, the requirement is intended to be Sole Sourced to COMPLETE PARACHUTE SOLUTIONS, INC. C-204-H001 USE OF NAVY SUPPORT CONTRACTORS FOR OFFICIAL CONTRACT FILES (Oct 2018)
(a) NAVSEA may use a file room management support contractor, hereinafter referred to as "the support contractor", to manage its
file room, in which all official contract files, including the official file supporting this procurement, are retained. These official files
may contain information that is considered a trade secret, proprietary, business sensitive or otherwise protected pursuant to law or
regulation, hereinafter referred to as "protected information". File room management services consist of any of the following:
secretarial or clerical support; data entry; document reproduction, scanning, imaging, or destruction; operation, management, or
maintenance of paper-based or electronic mail rooms, file rooms, or libraries; and supervision in connection with functions listed
herein.
(b) The cognizant Contracting Officer will ensure that any NAVSEA contract under which these file room management services are
acquired will contain a requirement that:
(1) The support contractor not disclose any information;
(2) Individual employees are to be instructed by the support contractor regarding the sensitivity of the official contract files;
(3) The support contractor performing these services be barred from providing any other supplies and/or services, or
competing to do so, to NAVSEA for the period of performance of its contract and for an additional three years thereafter
unless otherwise provided by law or regulation; and,
(4) In addition to any other rights the contractor may have, it is a third party beneficiary who has the right of direct action against the
support contractor, or any person to whom the support contractor has released or disclosed protected information, for the unauthorized
duplication, release, or disclosure of such protected information.
(c) Execution of this contract by the contractor is considered consent to NAVSEA's permitting access to any information, irrespective
of restrictive markings or the nature of the information submitted, by its file room management support contractor for the limited
purpose of executing its file room support contract responsibilities.
(d) NAVSEA may, without further notice, enter into contracts with other contractors for these services. Contractors should enter into
separate non-disclosure agreements with the file room contractor. Contact the Procuring Contracting Officer for contractor specifics.
However, any such agreement will not be considered a prerequisite before information submitted is stored in the file room or
otherwise encumber the government.
(End of Text)

Description: THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL. THIS IS A NOTICE OF THE GOVERNMENT'S INTENT TO ISSUE A SOLE SOURCE CONTRACT TO TSI INCORPORATED TO ASSIST THE U.S. DEPARTMENT OF LABOR'S (DOL), MINE SAFETY AND HEALTH ADMINISTRATION (MSHA), MINE SAFETY AND HEALTH ENFORCEMENT. This effort is to procure TSI Incorporated Quest Edge 8M Noise Dosimeters (Part Number: TSI 5EG8M-BT-D) and Microphones (Part Number: MIC-EG8) that TSI Incorporated has created specifically for MSHA. The TSI Incorporated Quest Edge 8M Noise Dosimeter and Microphone are the only products for this requirement that have received MSHA approval as intrinsically safe for use in underground coal mines. This is a sole source notice published for informational purposes only and not a request for competitive proposals. Therefore, no solicitation documents exist for this requirement. However, all responsible parties interested in responding to this notice are invited to submit a capability statement by Friday, 05/15/2026, 5:00 pm ET, that provides sufficient details for consideration by the Government, via email to: proietto.ryan.v@dol.gov and jackson.alicia.m@dol.gov. The determination not to compete the contract based on the responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. All information submitted should support the offeror's capability to provide the products required and shall be furnished at no cost or obligation to the Government. Responses must be in writing and must provide clear and concise documentation indicating an offeror's bona fide capability to provide these products. The Government reserves the right to cancel this requirement.

matters.title: Special Notice to Sole Source Purchase of Supply BLS Gas Flow Controller
matters.text:
Federal notice (Special Notice), DEPT OF DEFENSE.DEPT OF THE ARMY.W2R2 USA ENGR R & D CTR
Title: Special Notice to Sole Source Purchase of Supply BLS Gas Flow Controller
Solicitation number: W912HZ26Z1BTT
PSC: 3655; NAICS: 333998
Description: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Engineer Research and Development Center (ERDC) Geotechnical and Structures Laboratory (GSL), Structural Mechanics Branch (SMB) intends to award a sole source basis in accordance RFO FAR 13.101(b) to Stumptown Research & Development LLC, 104 Eastside Drive, Suite 110, Black Mountain, NC 28711-8208, as the sole manufacturer and only responsible source that can provide a 8-ft x 8-ft Blast Load Simulator (BLS-8). This acquisition is being conducted under RFO FAR Part 13, Simplified Procedures for Noncommercial Acquisitions. The Structural Mechanics Branch (SMB) of the Geotechnical and Structures Laboratory (GSL) of the US Army Engineer Research and Development Center (ERDC) currently conducts R&D by operating an 8-ft x 8-ft Blast Load Simulator (BLS-8) and an Advanced Blast Simulator (ABLS-12) that are used to evaluate structural targets subjected to shock waves produced by either compressed or combustible gasses. Items included in this acquisition are: One (1) combustible Gas System Flow Controller for the BLS-8. The Stumptown Research and Development, LLC Compressed Gas Driven Simulator must include: the ability to adhere to the same specifications as the existing combustible BLS Gas System Flow Controller. The components must consist of one main Valve Rack and one Driver Valve Rack. The main Valve Rack must house the flow controllers, flame arresters, driver isolation valves, and the driver. The Driver valve rack must house the spring return isolation valves, venturi evacuation pump, and electric match connection. The gas delivery system must be controlled with a provided Control Unit, which is equipped with an Emergency Shut Off (E-Stop) switch and performs multiple operations simultaneously. The intended procurement will be classified under North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) 333998 - All Other Miscellaneous General Purpose Machinery Manufacturing, with a size standard of 700 employees. This notice of intent is not a request for competitive quotes and no solicitation document exists for this requirement. However, parties interested in responding to this notice shall submit capable quotes, including price, sufficient to determine capability in providing the brand-name supply. All capability statements received by the closing date of this publication of this synopsis will be considered by the Government. A determination by the Government not to compete based on responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. This announcement fulfills the synopsis requirements under RFO FAR 5.101(a). USACE ERDC intends to release a solicitation no sooner than thirty (30) days after publishing this synopsis. This Special Notice of Intent (NOI) is not a request for competitive quotes. Meaningful submissions received in response to this notice will be considered solely for the purpose of determining whether a competitive procurement is in the best interest of the Government. If no meaningful, written submissions are received by the date listed below, which reflects at least fifteen (15) days after the publication of this notice, the solicitation will be issued as a sole source requirement to Stumptown Research and Development, LLC. Capability statements shall be submitted only by e-mail as a Microsoft Office Word, Microsoft Office Excel, or Adobe PDF attachment to Shinita.M.Jordan@usace.army.mil and Sonia.J.Boyd@usace.army.mil. Statements are due by 3:00pm Central Time, Friday, 05 June 2026. No phone calls will be accepted.

Description: The Government hereby submits a notice of intent to award a sole source Firm-Fixed-Price contract to Sysmex America, INC. for commercial-off-the-shelf (COTS) Cost-Per-Result-Reportable (CPRR) Automated Hematology Analyzer System. The contract will consist of a base year and four (4) option years, and one (1) Optional six (6) Month Option; the period of performance for the base year is 01July2026 - 30June2027. Sysmex America, INC.'s XN-9100-202 is the only source available that utilizes fluorescent flow cytometry, which analyzes RNA and DNA content and intracellular cellular structures rather than relying solely on impedance and light scatter. This technology provides superior differentiation of white blood cell populations and improves identification of immature and abnormal cells, including blasts, atypical lymphocytes, and immature granulocytes. These capabilities support higher flagging accuracy, reduced manual smear reviews, and earlier clinical decision-making, directly impacting patient care quality and safety. Another feature is the RU 20 reagent dilution unit that has reduced diluent changes, inventory and storage. The RU is unique to Sysmex and offered by no other vendor. These features not only reduce the manual workload on minimal undermanned laboratory staff and minimal storage area needed, but increases, accuracy, efficiency, and readiness for regulatory audits within space constraints due to delays in renovation for NMCP�s laboratory. The total estimated value is $1,891,450.00. Market research has determined that Sysmex America, INC. has a strategically sourced Federal Supply Schedule contract V797D-40235 for CPRR Automated Hematology Analyzer System which is valid through 31August2029. Responses to this notice must demonstrate clear and convincing evidence that competition would be advantageous to the Government, would not be cost or time prohibitive, and would not hinder the mission objective of Naval Medical Center Portsmouth. The determination not to compete this proposed contract action is solely within the discretion of the Government. Information received will normally be considered for the purposes of determining whether to conduct a competitive procurement. The Government will not be responsible for any costs incurred by responding to this notice. This is not a request for quote or proposals. attachments.name: Draft SOW for NOI CPRR Hematology.docx
attachments.text:
PART 1
1.0 GENERAL INFORMATION

1.1 This is a supply contract to provide Hematology Automation Line with Testing Agreement. The requirement is a lease of a complete Hematology Automation Line capable of providing complete blood cell counts (CBC) with advanced RBC and Body Fluid Software Applications, & Differential Remote Review Software Teams Edition (5 concurrent licenses) in a Cost-Per-Reportable-Result Agreement, Consumables (reagents) and Maintenance Support Services for Naval Medical Center Portsmouth.

1.2 Description of services/introduction: The contractor shall provide all personnel, equipment, supplies, facilities, transportation, tools, materials, supervision, and other items and non-personal services necessary to perform installation, validation, and implementation of the complete Hematology Automation Line as defined in this Statement of Work (SOW) except for those items specified as government furnished property and services. The contractor shall perform to the standards in this SOW.

1.3 Background: NMCP is a Level II Trauma Center and the primary military medical facility for the Hampton Roads region. The Hematology laboratory services:
Oncology inpatients receiving active myelosuppressive chemotherapy regimens
Bone marrow transplant (BMT) patients in engraftment monitoring periods
Immunocompromised active-duty personnel and beneficiaries
ICU patients that at risk for sepsis, where early neutrophil left-shift detection is a life-critical
finding
Patients with suspected or confirmed hematologic malignancies (AML, MDS, CLL, ALL) requiring diagnostic-quality automated differentials

These patient populations present with blood samples that are fundamentally different from routine outpatient specimens. They contain low cell counts, dysplastic morphology, treatment-related artifacts, and abnormal cell distributions that stress the limitations of standard impedance-based technology. 

To provide the expected standard of care for those who receive their healthcare services at Naval Medical Center Portsmouth (NMCP); there must be capability of providing certain in-house laboratory tests that are ordered on a routine basis. A Complete Blood Count (CBC) is one such test. The CBC is a test panel that is requested by a credentialed provider which provides information about the cells in a patient's blood. A clinical laboratory scientist/technician performs the requested testing and provides the requesting provider with results of the patient’s CBC. The CBC includes a white blood cell count, red blood cell count, hemoglobin, hematocrit, red blood cell indices (information on red blood cell size and hemoglobin content), a platelet count as well as a white blood cell differential (neutrophils, lymphocytes, monocytes, basophils, immature granulocytes, and eosinophils are enumerated). Due to the large CBC workload experienced daily, CBC analyzer automation is necessary to ensure consistent, standardized and timely CBC test results are provided to the ordering providers. 



1.4 Objectives: The Naval Medical Center Portsmouth (NMCP) and its affiliated Branch Health Clinics (BHCs) are responsible for providing the U.S. Navy, other military branches, and their military families with reliable quality health care. In addition to maintaining status as one of the nation’s premier care providers, NMCP is responsible for preparing for deployable support of operational forces, as well as shaping the future of military medicine through education, training and research. The requirement is for a reliable analyzer capable of automated identification and enumeration of pathologic cell populations specifically immature granulocytes (IG), blast cells, abnormal lymphocytes, and platelets within a high-acuity oncology and immunocompromised patient population, at a throughput and accuracy level that supports real-time clinical decision-making without excess manual review delays. 

NMCP’s patient population requires an analyzer capable of:

High sensitivity/specificity detection and flagging of abnormal cells, including blasts, variant lymphocytes, and immature granulocytes.
Reliable automated differential performance in pathologic samples, not only normal samples
Accurate reticulocyte and immature reticulocyte fraction (IRF) quantification
Reduction in false-negative flags that would otherwise require additional manual review and delay clinical decision-making
Capability to determine true platelet count in the presence of certain disease states.

The vendor shall supply a lease agreement for a complete Hematology Automated System capable of providing complete blood cell counts (CBC) with advanced RBC and Body Fluid Software Applications, direct platelet detection technology & Differential Remote Review Software Teams Edition (5 concurrent licenses) in Cost-Per-Reportable-Result Agreement, Consumables (reagents) and Maintenance Support Services for Naval Medical Center Portsmouth.

1.5 Scope: The requirement is for a lease of duplicate Hematology analyzers incased within its own automation line to also include Advanced RBC and Body Fluid Software Applications, &Teams Edition (5 concurrent licenses) in Cost-Per-Reportable-Result (CPRR) Agreement, Consumables (reagents) and Maintenance Support Services for Naval Medical Center Portsmouth. All analyzer and accessories technology, testing methodologies, quality control, consumables, spare parts used in routine user maintenance, and reagents used onboard the analyzers will be approved by and compliant with the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) requirements to market and deliver medical products for use in the United States of America, even should delivery be requested outside of the United States. The claims made for the product shall comply with the regulations of the FDA with respect to products for marketing and delivery of a medical product for use in the United States of America, even should delivery be requested outside of the United States. The equipment and reagents shall be in compliance with OSHA requirements. Services include all list in Part 5. The contractor shall accomplish all items listed in Parts 3 and 4.

RFO 6.103-1(b) One responsible source. Agencies may contract without providing for full and
open competition when the supplies or services required by the agency are available from only
one responsible source and no other type of supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements.
5. Rationale Justifying Use of Authority Cited:
The Sysmex XN-9100-202 utilizes fluorescent flow cytometry, which analyzes RNA and DNA
content and intracellular cellular structures rather than relying solely on impedance and light
scatter. This technology provides superior differentiation of white blood cell populations and
improves identification of immature and abnormal cells, including blasts, atypical lymphocytes,
and immature granulocytes. These capabilities support higher flagging accuracy, reduced manual
smear reviews, and earlier clinical decision-making, directly impacting patient care quality and
safety. Critically, lower flagging sensitivity in competing impedance-based platforms can
produce false-negative results for blast cells, variant lymphocytes, and other critical findings.
Failure to flag these cells at the instrument level means that pathologic findings may not be
escalated for manual review, resulting in missed or delayed diagnoses at the onset of a disease
risk is clinically
unacceptable. The Sysmex fluorescent flow cytometry methodology minimizes this risk by
providing enumerated Immature Granulocyte (IG) counts and Immature Platelet Fraction (IPF)
on every sample, enabling early identification of hematopoietic abnormalities before they
become clinically apparent through other means.
Another feature for only the Sysmex product, is the RU 20 reagent dilution unit that has reduced
diluent changes, inventory and storage. The RU is unique to Sysmex and offered by no other
vendor. These features not only reduce the manual workload on minimal undermanned
laboratory staff and minimal storage area needed, but increases, accuracy, efficiency, and
laboratory.
Given these clinical and operational imperatives, no other hematology vendor currently offers
the same combination of diagnostic accuracy, workflow automation, data integration, and
platform standardization. Therefore, acquiring Sysmex as a sole source is not only justified but
to high-quality patient care.
6. Efforts to Obtain Competition:
A Request for Information (RFI) was posted to SAM.gov on 10Mar2026 and closed on
25Mar2026. Two vendors responded to RFI- Sysmex America, INC. (OTSB) and Beckman
Coulter, INC. (OTSB).
Sysmex America could meet all the requirements on 24Mar2026.

in their capability statement. On 25Mar2026, Contract Specialist (CS), Lisa Wilk, emailed
Beckman Coulter and asked for clarification that they could meet specific requirements per the
SOW. Beckman Coulter did not respond with their answers until 31Mar2026, which was after
the closing date of the RFI. They stated that certain requirements were unduly restrictive and to
be removed from the SOW.
When the CS spoke with the End User, they stated that these requirements were essential to their

matters.text:
Federal notice (Combined Synopsis/Solicitation), DEPT OF DEFENSE.DEPT OF THE NAVY.NIWC PACIFIC
Title: N6600126Q6142 // RFQ // BRAND NAME AMETEK ORTIC PORTABLE HIGH PURITY GERNAMIUM (HPGe) DETECTORS AND ASSOCIATED ACCESSORIES
Solicitation number: N6600126Q6142
PSC: 5963; NAICS: 334519
Description: This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial products and commercial services prepared in accordance with the format in Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Subpart 12.2 (Overhaul), as supplemented with additional information included in this notice. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation; quotes are being requested and a separate written solicitation will not be issued. This enclosure is an addendum to FAR provision 52.212-1, Instructions to Offerors ? Commercial Products and Commercial Services, which applies to this acquisition. Competitive quotes are being requested under Request for Quote (RFQ) Number N66001-26-Q-6142. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code applicable to this acquisition is 334519, Other Measuring and Controlling Devices and the small business size standard is 600 employees. This procurement is being solicited under Full and Open Competition (Unrestricted). All responsible sources may submit a quote, which shall be considered by the agency.DESCRIPTION OF REQUIREMENTSThe Government is seeking to acquire brand-name Advanced Measurement Technology Inc. (AMETEK) ORTIC Portable High Purity Germanium (HPGe) detectors and associated accessories. To be considered acceptable and eligible for award, quotes must provide all of the items and quantities listed below. The Government will not consider quotes or offers for partial items or quantities. The required items are contained in the RFQ attachments (go to PIEE Solicitation link). The expected delivery date is 160 days after receipt of order. The Government is seeking Free on Board (FOB) Destination pricing to the following shipping address: San Diego, CA. 92110 (full address will be disclosed at time of award).OFFEROR INSTRUCTIONSThe Government intends to award a Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) contract resulting from this solicitation to the responsible offeror whose quotation conforming to the solicitation represents the lowest priced offer that meets the brand name technical requirements as defined in the EVALUATION FACTORS FOR AWARD Section below. A complete quote is necessary to be adequately considered for award. Respond to each item listed below, if the response is None or Not applicable, explicitly state and explain. The Government may consider quotes that fail to address or follow all instructions to be non-responsive and ineligible for contract award. A complete quote includes a response and submission to each of the following:1. General Information: Offeror Business Name, Address, CAGE and Unique Entity ID (ensure Representation and Certifications are up to date in SAM.gov), Business Size on applicable NAICS Code as provided above, Federal Tax ID, Primary Point of Contract (to include telephone and e-mail address) and provide a GSA contract number if some or all items proposed are on the GSA schedule. 2. Technical Documentation:a. Technical Approach or Specifications: Offerors are encouraged to submit product manufacturer specifications, pictures, brochures, and other pertinent technical information of the quoted brand name items to facilitate the evaluation. The quote must address and meet the requirements/specifications as defined under Technical Factor I below.b. Sustainable Acquisitions Information and Certification: The contractor shall comply with all sustainable acquisition policies in an effort to minimize the Governments environmental impact and deliver community benefits through better selection and improved usage of products and services. In accordance FAR Part 23, sustainable acquisition policies apply to both contracts for products and services that require the delivery, use, or furnishing of products/services to the Government. Indicate if any the following sustainable acquisition categories apply to any products or services proposed: Energy Efficient, Water Efficient, Recycled, Bio-Based, Environmentally Preferable, Non-ozone depleting substances, Less Toxic and/or Less GHGs.c. Authorized Source Confirmation: The following product certification statement below applies to ALL line items and each offeror must submit supporting documentation, as needed: To be considered for award, the offeror/contractor is required to submit documentation confirming that they are an authorized source. An Authorized Source is defined as the original manufacturer, a source with the express written authority of the original manufacturer or current design activity, or an authorized aftermarket manufacturer.3. Price Quote: Submit complete pricing for each individual item listed in the DESCRIPTION OF REQUIREMENTS Section above to include the unit of issue, the extended price for each line item and a total price in US Dollars ($). Note: Ensure FOB Destination shipping costs are included in the pricing. EVALUATION FACTORS FOR AWARD: Basis for Award: The Government intends to award a contract to the lowest priced offeror that meets the brand name technical requirements, and who is registered in the System for Award Management (SAM); however, the Government reserves the right to award no contract at all, depending on the quality of quotes submitted and availability of funds. A quote will be considered non-responsive if technical requirements are not met. Technical requirements are defined in Factor I below. Factor I ? Technical: The Government will evaluate the quote and verify if the following specification requirements are met to include all information required for a complete quote as defined in paragraph 2 above: The Government will evaluate the quote and verify specification requirements are met and perform an item risk assessment to determine technical acceptability. This requirement contains supplies that are Brand Name pursuant to FAR 11.105, Items Peculiar to One Manufacturer. To be considered for award, the offeror is required to certify that the product being offered is an original, new, and Trade Agreements Act (TAA) compliant (reference 2(c) above) AMETEK ORTEC product. The Government will only accept the required brand name product as specified in Attachment 01.Factor II ? Price: The Government will evaluate the total price to determine if it is fair and reasonable. Description: This notice is not a request for a quotation. A solicitation document will not be issued and quotations will not be requested. This acquisition is being conducted under the authority of RFO 12.102 The National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST), Physical Measurements Lab (PML), Quantum Nanoelectronics Group requires an Automated 2-dimensional (2D) Material Transfer System to use for transferring and stacking 2D van der Waals crystals. The 2D transfer system provides precise control of motion for manipulating single atomic layer crystals to create quantum devices. The 2D transfer system is used to make low-dimensional van der Waals devices for mission-critical experiments in physics and metrology, quantum information science, and electrical standards dissemination. For air sensitive crystals, we require the transfer system to be located in a glove box and remotely operated with full motorized controls. The 2D transfer system shall provide the highest manipulation resolution and motorization as well as having a needle control for picking up nanowires for our device needs. NIST conducted market research from Market research was conducted from February 2026 to May 2026 and included searches on: Google, GSA, small business dynamic search, and reviewing previous awards for similar items. The results of that market research revealed that only HQ Graphene Systems B.V.(UEI: GE58CCC6PC51) appears to be capable of meeting NIST�s requirements per the following. Through our market research, we found that only HQ Graphene provides an automatic transfer system that meets the critical technical specifications required to meet the NIST mission for fabrication critical quantum devices. 1. Motorized mask tilt (Holmarc is manual) 2. Sample XY travel ranges up to 50mm (Holmarc 25mm) 3. Stamp needs to be able to rotate (Holmarc cannot) 4. Statement of Work

The NIH Department of Transfusion Medicine (DTM) in Bethesda, Maryland, intends to award Quidel-Ortho Clinical Diagnostics, on a sole-source basis, a contract that will provide for procurement of Ortho Vision Analyzer (capital expenditure) and accessories necessary for seamless workflow (Ortho Vision Table, Printer, Validation kit). 

The DTM/TSL laboratory currently uses the Ortho Vision Analyzer to test samples from NIH patients, NIH donors, outside referral samples and special project samples containing highly unique characteristics. 

1.1 Background

DTM uses Quidel-Ortho Clinical Diagnostics, Inc. technology to perform pretransfusion testing for blood grouping and antibody detection. It is a critical instrument in determining red blood cell compatibility for transfusion and offers the option of a fully automated workflow. The system minimizes wait time and reduces human error in support of improved transfusion safety.  

 Scope of Work

The vendor must be able to maintain the Ortho Vision Analyzer and provide warranty repair services to meet the specific diagnostic testing needs of the NIH Clinical Center patients. The vendor must ensure the analyzer maintains a level of reliability, ease of access to samples, large volume capacity with small physical footprint, and compatible with most liquid nitrogen supply cylinders.

Salient Characteristics for 120’+ Boom Lift

A boom lift is a hydraulic aerial work platform that features a platform or bucket at the end of a jointed or telescopic arm (the “boom”). This arm is mounted on a base, which can be stationary, self-propelled, or towable. They are designed to provide both vertical and horizontal reach, making them indispensable for a wide range of tasks where ladders or scaffolding simply aren’t practical or safe.

The aerial lift shall meet the following minimum performance requirements:

Vertical Reach
Must provide a minimum platform height of 120 feet.

Horizontal Outreach
Must provide no less than 70 feet of horizontal outreach under normal operating conditions.

Platform Capacity
Platform shall support a minimum unrestricted capacity of 500 lb, and
A higher restricted capacity (e.g., for limited reach positions) of at least 750–1,000 lb.

Articulating Jib
Boom must include an articulating or telescoping jib capable of providing multi axis positioning adequate for precise placement at extreme height.
Must provide wide range of vertical articulation sufficient for accessing overhead or recessed work areas.

Powertrain
Unit must be diesel powered and capable of reliable operation in outdoor industrial environments.
Engine must provide sufficient horsepower and hydraulic performance to achieve the required lift speed, drive performance, and gradeability.

Tires
Unit must have foam filled, rough terrain tires suitable for jobsite surfaces and stable operation at maximum elevation.
Ground pressure performance shall support safe operation on mixed terrain.

Platform Rotation
Must include platform rotation capability, minimum ≥ 150–180 degrees, to allow operator positioning.

Required Accessories
A cold‑weather package capable of supporting reliable operation in low‑temperature environments (battery warming capability, hydraulic system heating (hydraulic tank heater), engine block heater or equivalent). Must maintain system responsiveness and startability in cold climates.
A platform approximately 36 × 96 inches, or comparable size, capable of supporting two operators plus tools without restricting normal movement.
A self‑closing gate that swings inward to ensure safe entry and exit from the platform.
A bolt‑on or integrated fall‑arrest anchor system compliant with applicable ANSI/OSHA fall‑protection standards, allowing operators to tie off safely while maneuvering on the platform.
An integrated on‑board AC generator system providing:
Standard 110–120V, 60 Hz electrical power routed to the platform for operating electric tools;
A factory‑routed ½‑inch air line from the base to the platform, enabling the use of pneumatic tools at height (external air compressor supplied separately).
The system must provide continuous, reliable power delivery suitable for typical construction and maintenance tasks performed at elevation.

Description: AMENDMENT 0001 Due date extended to 29 May 2026 11:00 am (Pacific). All questions must be received no later than 27 May 2026, 11:00 AM (Pacific) ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- This is a Combined Synopsis/Solicitation for commercial products prepared in accordance with the format in Subpart 12. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation. Quotes are being requested and a separate written solicitation will not be issued. Request for Quotation (RFQ) N5523626Q0075 is issued as a Sole Source requirement. The subject solicitation is being processed using FAR Part 12. The Government intends to solicit and contract with only one source, Fairbanks Morse Defense, LLC for the parts listed on the Product Description under the authority of FAR 12.102 on a sole source basis. Interested parties may identify their interest and capability to respond to the requirement and submit quotes. This notice of intent is not a request for competitive quotes. Determination by the Government not to compete with this proposed contract based upon responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. The applicable North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code is 333618 � Other Engine Equipment Manufacturing. matters.title: Sources Sought for Honeywell Engineering Sustainment Support, Sole Source to Honeywell
matters.text:
Federal notice (Sources Sought), DEPT OF DEFENSE.DEFENSE LOGISTICS AGENCY.DLA AVIATION
Title: Sources Sought for Honeywell Engineering Sustainment Support, Sole Source to Honeywell
Solicitation number: SPE4A626R0238
PSC: 1660; NAICS: 336413
Description: Sources Sought for Honeywell Engineering Sustainment for Sole Source Honeywell Parts Defense Logistics Agency (DLA) Aviation - Richmond is issuing this Sources Sought Notice as a means of conducting market research to identify parties having an interest in and the resources to support this requirement. DISCLAIMER: This Sources Sought Notice is for informational purposes only. The Government intends to solicit and negotiate with only one source under authority of FAR 6.302-1. This is not a request for proposal. It does not constitute a solicitation and shall not be construed as a commitment by the Government. Submission of any information in response to this sources sought is purely voluntary; the Government assumes no financial responsibility for any costs incurred. The purpose of this Sources Sought Notice is to conduct market research to identify parties having an interest in and the resources to support engineering sustainment and program services for sole source Honeywell part-numbered items. The proposed contract action is for engineering and program services, for which the Government intends to solicit and negotiate with only one source under the authority of FAR 6.302. Interested parties may identify their interest and capability to support the objectives by responding to this notice. All responses received by the notice response date will be considered by the Government. A determination by the Government not to compete this proposed contract based upon responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. Information received in response to this notice will normally be considered solely for the purpose of determining whether to conduct a competitive procurement. This notice is for information and planning purposes only and does not constitute a solicitation or commitment by the Government. The contract is anticipated to be a Firm-Fixed Price Contract with yearly renewal options as needed. The objective of this acquisition is to improve acquisition readiness of complex or nonstandard part-numbered items for DLA Aviation customers. This requirement is for all Sole Source Honeywell NSNs, with the following AMC Codes: 3, 4, and 5. The contractor shall provide sustainment engineering support and program services. An analysis will be performed on sole source Boeing parts to include drawing updates, part number versions, etc. Once the review is completed, the contractor shall submit long term contract pricing. If your organization has the potential capacity to perform the services outlined above; please provide the following business information: 1. Organization Name, Physical and/or Mailing Address, CAGE Code, DUNS Number, Number of Employees, Point of Contact (POC), POC Phone Number, PC Email Address, and Web Page URL, if available. 2. Tailored capability statements addressing the particulars of this effort, with appropriate documentation supporting claims of organizational and staff capability. SUBMISSION INSTRUCTIONS: Interested parties who consider themselves qualified to perform the above-listed services are invited to submit a response to this Sources Sought Notice by 3PM, EST., May 26, 2026. All responses under this Sources Sought Notice must be emailed to Chadney.Thompson@dla.mil.

matters.title: Intent to Sole Source- RPS-62 Radar Systems
matters.text:
Federal notice (Special Notice), DEPT OF DEFENSE.DEPT OF THE NAVY.USMC
Title: Intent to Sole Source- RPS-62 Radar Systems
Solicitation number: M67854-26-I-0025
PSC: 5840; NAICS: 334511
Description: Program Manager Ground Based Air Defense (GBAD) within Portfolio Acquisition Executive (PAE) Mission Systems (MS) Marine Corps (MC) intends to negotiate and award on a sole-source basis in accordance with Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 6.103-1 to RADA Technologies, LLC�s (hereafter referred to as RADA), 20511 Seneca Meadows PKWY STE 100 Germantown, Maryland 20876 United States, for the procurement of non-commercial RPS-62 radar systems, software/firmware releases and associated licenses, spares, ancillary components, maintenance and repairs, and engineering services for the Marine Air Defense Integrated System (MADIS) program. The RPS-62 radar system is a readily available solution that has been integrated within the size, weight, and power parameters of the JLTV, to include all electrical and mechanical interfaces. The RPS-62 radar system is also compatible with the MADIS software baseline. The RPS-62 radar system is the only known and currently available solution that satisfies Product Manager Future Weapon Systems� (PdM FWS) requirements. The Government anticipates award of a hybrid Cost-Plus-Fixed Fee/Firm-Fixed-Price contract, with a period of performance of five years. This acquisition is being pursued on a sole source basis under the statutory authority of 10 U.S.C. 3204(a)(1), as implemented by Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 6.103-1(c)(2)(iii) "Only One Responsible Source and No Other Supplies or Services Will Satisfy Agency Requirements.� RADA is the designer, developer, and producer of the RPS-62 radar system. This is not a request for competitive quotes. No formal solicitation package is available. The Government will not be responsible for any cost incurred in responding to this notice; however, interested parties may identify their interest and capability to meet the requirements and past performance data no later than 1000 local time on 11 June 2026. Responses received will be evaluated; however, a determination by the Government not to compete the proposed procurement based upon responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. All responses to this notice shall be submitted to Ms. Natalia Bruno at natalia.bruno@usmc.mil and Mrs. Megan Brady at megan.brady.civ@usmc.mil. Please reference the Notice ID on all responses. Telephone calls will not be accepted.

Federal notice (Combined Synopsis/Solicitation), DEPT OF DEFENSE.DEPT OF THE NAVY.NIWC PACIFIC
Title: N6600126Q6142 // RFQ // BRAND NAME AMETEK ORTIC PORTABLE HIGH PURITY GERNAMIUM (HPGe) DETECTORS AND ASSOCIATED ACCESSORIES
Solicitation number: N6600126Q6142
PSC: 5963; NAICS: 334519
Description: This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial products and commercial services prepared in accordance with the format in Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Subpart 12.2 (Overhaul), as supplemented with additional information included in this notice. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation; quotes are being requested and a separate written solicitation will not be issued. This enclosure is an addendum to FAR provision 52.212-1, Instructions to Offerors ? Commercial Products and Commercial Services, which applies to this acquisition. Competitive quotes are being requested under Request for Quote (RFQ) Number N66001-26-Q-6142. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code applicable to this acquisition is 334519, Other Measuring and Controlling Devices and the small business size standard is 600 employees. This procurement is being solicited under Full and Open Competition (Unrestricted). All responsible sources may submit a quote, which shall be considered by the agency.DESCRIPTION OF REQUIREMENTSThe Government is seeking to acquire brand-name Advanced Measurement Technology Inc. (AMETEK) ORTIC Portable High Purity Germanium (HPGe) detectors and associated accessories. To be considered acceptable and eligible for award, quotes must provide all of the items and quantities listed below. Description: The purpose of this acquisition is to provide HLA typing and antibody screening reagents to the HLA Lab on a regular basis. The Contractor shall manufacture the devices in accordance with the Source control
