right-23812500STATEMENT OF WORK 
Title: IR Spectrometer System, NLIR Model S-MIDWAVE-2050-400-2K-F
LAB: Material Measurements Laboratory, Materials Measurement Science Division, Nanomechanical Properties Group (NPG). 

BACKGROUND INFORMATION
The Nanocalorimetry for Semiconductors and Semiconductor Process Metrology project is developing bespoke sensors, instrument control systems, and calibration and model verifications methods. These sensors measure the thermal properties of thin film semiconductor materials, can perform experiments at time scales applicable to the operations of semiconductor devices, and are being investigated for integration into processing tools for plasma and atomic layer deposition processes. The temperature calibration of nanocalorimeter sensors is critical and relies on the accurate emissivity of platinum thin films of nanocalorimeter sensors while an optical calibration method is used. Infrared (IR) spectrometer allows us to make measurements of emissivity of metal thin films as a function of both temperature and wavelength when the sample is placed on a temperature-controlled stage. This system will be used to measure radiance of metal surfaces including Pt (emissivity of apx 0.22 at 1550 nm) in the temperature range of 100 °C to 600 °C for the wavelengths of 3.0 µm to 5.0 µm. The IR spectrometer specified here is a portable mid IR spectrometer to be able to measure thermal radiance from a small area of metal surfaces of the silicon sensors fabricated at NIST in the temperature range of 100 °C to 600 °C for the wavelengths of 3.0 µm to 5.0 µm. The metal used here could be platinum which has a low emissivity therefore the detector sensitivity requirement is critical for the application here. 
PURPOSE: Advance semiconductor manufacturing by providing reliable material properties for modeling and improved high-yield processing. This investment will assist industry by improved new measurement capabilities that foster the development of next generation devices and help manufacturers with metrology solutions that improve the yield of manufacturing processes. 

SCOPE:
The Contractor shall deliver a quantity of one (1) IR Spectrometer System IR Spectrometer System, NLIR Model S-MIDWAVE-2050-400-2K-F inclusive of FOB Destination delivery terms (or equivalent INCOTERM such as DDP), and one (1) year warranty. 

BRAND NAME ONLY JUSTIFICATION
The detector sensitivity of this IR spectrometer is the key to enable quantifying the emissivity of the metal thin film surface with a low emissivity in the temperature range of 100 °C to 600 °C as a function of wavelength from 3.0 µm to 5.0 µm. The reliable temperature calibration of nanocalorimeter sensors is critical for this project. An optical calibration method is best suitable and applicable for nanocalorimetry, and it relies on the accurate emissivity measurement of metal thin films (heater) of nanocalorimeter sensors. Thus, the sensitivity of the detector must be 130k counts/(ms µw).

MINIMUM REQUIREMENTS
The Contractor shall submit a firm fixed price quotation which offers a supply/system that meets all technical specifications identified below. All items must be new. Used or remanufactured equipment will not be considered for award. Experimental, prototype, or custom items will not be considered. The use of “gray market” components are not authorized for sale in the U.S. by the Contractor is not acceptable. All line items shall be shipped in the original manufacturer’s packaging and include all original documentation and software, when applicable.

Line Item 0001
Description: IR Spectrometer System, NLIR Model S-MIDWAVE-2050-400-2K-F
Quantity: One (1)

Technical Specifications:
Detector Sensitivity: Sensitivity of the detector must be 130k counts/(ms µw).
Minimum Detectable Optical Power: An optical power of 5 pW/nm at the fiber entrance must exceed the dark noise of the spectrometer at an integration time of 100 ms. 
 Spectrometer Speed: The spectrometer must collect the full spectral range at a rate exceeding 250 Hz.
Spectral Range: Spectrometer must include 3.0 µm - 5.0 µm, 
Spectrum Resolution: Resolution must be equal or better than 6 cm-1.
Spot size: Spot size range must be 300 µm - 500 µm
Optical Fiber Coupled – Spectrometer shall be optical fiber coupled and shall include the MWIR light gathering optics and optical fiber. 
Working distance:
the working distance must be between 100 mm and 200 mm. 
System must be capable of collecting light from a bare cleaved or polished fiber placed near the sample surface.
The software to control the instrument must
Allow control of all applicable control parameters (e.g. dwell time, resolution, etc.).
Allow collection of spectra.
Allow saving of spectral data to non-proprietary file types (e.g. text, hdf5).
Run on Window 10 or 11.
If the vendor has an application programing interface (API), it shall be included.
Physical:
Connections from the spectrometer to the control PC must be made via USB or ethernet. 
The system mass must not exceed 10 kg.
Must operate from a NEMA 5-15R (standard US outlet – 120 V, 15 A) with no other facility requirements for compressed gases or cryogens.

Such tests and evaluations, if performed, shall be conducted within the environment that the system is to be operated. Performance Tests:

NIST may choose at its discretion to forego this part of acceptance testing.

A visual inspection of the equipment will be performed by the NIST COR to identify surface defects or any form of indication that any equipment was damaged during transport to NIST.  The Government shall have sole discretion to require repair or replacement of damaged and/or nonconforming supplies at no cost to the Government.  The Government at any time prior to acceptance shall reject the equipment due to defects and/or nonconformance.  The vendor is responsible for latent defects discovered any time after final inspection.  However, the extent of its liability shall be prorated over the useful life of the equipment.

Notice of Intent to Sole Source 
Commercial Supply
Contract Type: Firm Fixed Price
Title: CW UV Laser (Coherent Model OBIS 320nm XT, 40mW)
Notice ID Number: NB305000-26-00682


PURPOSE
This is a notice of intent the Acquisition Management Division (AMD) at the National Institute of Standards and Technology Physical Measurement Lab, Nanoscale Device Characterization Division, Advanced Electronics Group, intends to procure a quantity of one (1) CW UV Laser (Coherent Model OBIS 320nm XT, 40mW) on a sole source basis with Coherent, Inc. using FAR Part 12, Acquisition of Commercial Products and Commercial Services. 

This notice shall not be construed as a Request for Quote. Respondents are advised that the U.S. Government will not pay for information or administrative costs incurred in the response to this notice. All costs associated with responding to the notice will be solely at the interested party’s expense. Not responding to this notice does not preclude participation in any future RFQ or other solicitation (if any are issued). This is a notice of intent to sole source, not a pre-solicitation notice. There is no formal solicitation available at this time. No award will be made as a result of this notice. Respondents will not be notified of the results of this notice, or results of information submitted. 

BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVE
The semiconductor supply chain is global, specialized, and interconnected. Chipmakers do business with thousands of individual suppliers that provide the highly complex materials and tools used to produce semiconductors. To address the lack of full visibility into the semiconductors markets supply chain and R&D ecosystem gaps, NIST will conduct the measurement science or metrology, critical to the development of new materials, packaging, and production methods in chip manufacturing.  
 
To meet project requirements, NIST requires a laser system that is continuous wave (CW) and emits in the ultraviolet (UV) to enable efficient photoemission-based measurements. This acquisition will allow the project to expand its photoemission electron spectroscopy and microscopy metrology capabilities. This acquisition is critical to achieving the project’s goals as it would accelerate measurement throughput to deliver milestones and deliverable. The laser will be used to serve a CHIPS metrology project to investigate uniformity and defects in chip-to-chip bonding in order to develop known good processes. The CW UV laser will be used as a photon source required for electron microscopy and spectroscopy to measure changes in chemical and spatial structure as a result to pre-bonding processes. Because of this, the light has a maximum wavelength for this process to occur and therefore the requirement of light must be in the ultraviolet regime. The laser system consists of a laser unit, electronics to control the laser, and a cooling system. A continuous wave with high power is necessary for the measurements to not be distorted spatially or energetically.

SCOPE
The Contractor shall deliver a quantity of (1) CW UV laser Coherent Model OBIS 320nm XT, 40mW, inclusive of FOB Destination delivery terms (or equivalent INCOTERM) and one year warranty. 

SALIENT CHARACTERISTICS 

Description: Coherent Model OBIS 320nm XT, 40mW
Quantity: One (1)
Laser output drive mode must be continuous wave (CW)
2. Output wavelength of 320 nm
3. Output power of 40 mW
4. Must provide a TEM00 spatial mode at the output of the Laser. The beam quality factor M2 must be less than or equal to 1.1

NOTICE RESPONSE
Interested firms/companies are encouraged to respond to this notice by submitting documentation that clearly demonstrates how the minimum requirements and technical specifications will be met. Response which merely repeat the minimum requirements, and technical specifications without providing demonstration of how the minimum requirements and technical specifications will be met, will not be considered or evaluated by the government. Description: ***THIS IS A COMBINED SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE AND NOTICE OF INTENT TO SOLE SOURCE*** The purpose of this sources sought notice is to conduct market research and identify potential sources of commercial products/services that satisfy the Government�s anticipated needs. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for this acquisition is 334516, Analytical Laboratory Instrument Manufacturing. The Natinal Inistitute of Standars and Technology (NIST) Physical Measurement Laboratory (PML) requires an integrated superconducting magnet power system to replace a failed power supply and energize the Cryomagnetics superconducting magnet in the PML ultra-low-temperature scanning probe facility. The superconducting magnet is used for mission-critical experiments in metrology for quantum information science and electrical standards dissemination. The superconducting magnet power system must be the Cryomagnetics model number 4G-200s for an exact replacement of the current model. The required power system energizes a superconducting magnet, which operates with a dilution refrigerator to produce high magnetic fields at ultra-low temperatures. The replacement for this power supply must be the exact model of the existing Cryomagnetics 4G-200s power supply used with our dilution refrigerators, so that it has the same footprint and connections, and can be interchanged with the existing model to keep critical experiments running at ultra-low temperatures. NIST is seeking information from sources that may be capable of providing a solution that meets all the minimum required technical specifications below: Replica of the existing Cryomagnetics 4G-200s power supply Single output model with output current up to � 200 amperes (� 10 volts up to � 165 amperes, � 8 volts at 200 amperes). 4-quadrant, true bipolar systems featuring smooth sweeps through zero. Five (5) programmable sweep rate ranges. Safety interlocks for persistent switch enable/disable and changing of important magnet parameters and limits. Visual confirmation of current present in leads will alert users to be mindful of safety when operating the power supply, even if line power is off. Display Resolution: 0.1 mA, 1 mV. Output Current Setability: 0.1 mA. Sweep Rate Resolution: 0.1 mA/sec. Persistent Switch Heater 0-125mA 0-12V. AC Input: 220-230V a.c., 50-60 Hz, 10A max. Ethernet: IEEE-802.3 10/100 BASE-T. US vehicles are built to meet American standards, which include specific lighting requirements such as amber turn signals and sealed-beam headlights, as well as odometers that measure in miles. Additionally, European emission standards for Danish cars are generally stricter, influencing engine design and fuel efficiency. CONTROLLED UNCLASSIFIED INFORMATION
Single Source Justification (Simplified Acquisition)
Section A: General Contract Information
Is this a Bridge Action as defined in the AF Bridge Action Reduction Plan? Yes No
Contracting Activity: 4 CONS
Project/Program Name: 916th Bose Proflight Series 2 headsets
Purchase Request / Local ID Number: F3TTWG5031A001
Estimated Contract Cost (including Options): $31,800.90
Section B: Description of the Supplies/Services Required
The 916th Operations Group requires flight headsets made by the Bose Corporation for use on the KC-46; specifically the Bose
ProFlight Series 2 aviation headset must include the following salient characteristics:
1. Cancel noise typical to KC-46 aircraft, with a performance canceling no less than 105 db of sound pressure level.
2. Have a microphone compatible with both high and low impedance systems, such that no interference is created when the
microphone is keyed.
3. Feature in-ear headphones, giving the ability to be operated using the one or two ears, to facilitate cross-cockpit checklist
reading.
4. Have a lightweight fit of 4.5 oz or less
5. Feature necessary 6-pin allowing connection to U-174 Connector
6. Bluetooth must be able to be turned off
7. Use alkaline batteries to ensure operation for at least 45 hours
8. Be FAA TSO and E/TSPC139A certified
Section C: Justification for Soliciting from a Single Source or Brand Name
The Air Force refueling squadrons have conducted over 20 separate flight headset tests to determine the best headset that can
satisfy flight operations for the KC-46. After extensively testing the Bose A30 low impedance, U174, 5 Ohm, Bose ProFlight Series 2
with 6-pin adapter, David Clark Pro-M, David Clark-H-10, David Clark C-17 H-10, Telex 7, Telex 8, and Telex 8+, the only in ear
headset to meet all the requirements was the Bose ProFlight Series 2 with 6-pin adapter. The Bose ProFlight Series 2 was the only
headset that reduced noise typical to KC-46 to allow for clear communication with the crew, air traffic control and receivers. All
other brands produced a side-tone that caused unitelligible communications and Air Traffic Control confusion. Furthermore, over-
ear and on-ear headset styles inhibited the use of 3D glasses during air refueling without causing severe discomfort. While some of
the features were available in other headset models, the Bose ProFlight Series 2 configuration is the only model that contains all of
the required features to support the 916th Operation Group's mission needs.

Section D: Efforts to Obtain Competition
Each iteration of this type of purchase we are required to validate the market place and ensure that there are no other products or

Pro-M, David Clark Pro-S, David Clark H-10, David Clark C-17 H-10, Telex 750, Telex 7, Telex 8, and Telex 8+, the only headset to
meet all the requirements was the Bose ProFlight Series 2 with 6-pin adapter.

4 CONS will continue to monitor if the Air Force allows other approved flushing equipment as well as survey the marketplace for
other commercial providers for this equipment should a similar requirement arise in the future.

I have determined, in accordance with FAR 13.106-1(b)(1), that the circumstances of this contract action deem only a

(cid:20)(cid:17) (cid:39)(cid:72)(cid:86)(cid:70)(cid:85)(cid:76)(cid:83)(cid:87)(cid:76)(cid:82)(cid:81)(cid:82)(cid:73)(cid:49)(cid:72)(cid:72)(cid:71)
Sole source procurement of Ornitella tracking devices to determine the local, regional and annual
movements of migratory shorebirds and short-billed gulls of high conservation concern.
(cid:21)(cid:17) (cid:48)(cid:68)(cid:85)(cid:78)(cid:72)(cid:87)(cid:53)(cid:72)(cid:86)(cid:72)(cid:68)(cid:85)(cid:70)(cid:75)(cid:38)(cid:82)(cid:81)(cid:71)(cid:88)(cid:70)(cid:87)(cid:72)(cid:71)
Vertebrate Systems, LLC is the North American distributor of Ornitella GPS GSM tags that are suitable
for tracking small to medium-sized birds. The OrniTrack-2.8, 6.0, and 10 models, which are 4G solar
powered transmitters (https://www.ornitela.com/) that weigh only 2.8 g, 6 g, and 10 g, respectively, and
are the right size for the small shorebirds and small gulls we wish to track. These tags are capable of
storing 1000s of GPS locations on the tag, with locations accurate to <10m and collected at 15 minute
intervals. These locations are transmitted in <1 second to any 4G LTE Cat-M1 cellular tower when
birds pass by. The devices are fully rechargeable and programmable.
(cid:22)(cid:17) (cid:50)(cid:87)(cid:75)(cid:72)(cid:85)(cid:38)(cid:68)(cid:83)(cid:68)(cid:69)(cid:79)(cid:72)(cid:54)(cid:82)(cid:88)(cid:85)(cid:70)(cid:72)(cid:86)
We researched other vendors that supply telemetry equipment, and located only one other vendor (Cellular
Tracking Technologies or CTT), which makes a comparable tag at similar weights. Their tags, called the flicker
Gen2 model (2.8-3.0 g) and ES-420-UL-10-BKP have similar weights and functionality but are more expensive
to purchase and require a ca. $5/month downloading cost per tag. We and our collaborators have used the
Ornitella tags to successfully track small to medium sized birds for the past four years. We prefer to stay with
the Ornitella tags because we are familiar with the devices, know that they will work, and want to ensure the
data are collected in a consistent way to ensure sound scientific data analyses can be done. Using the same
tags through time ensures that we successfully meet our study objectives and can compare data from multiple
years. Also, the CTT Gen2 tag is relatively new and has only been field tested by one field project in 2025.
Given the complexity of these units, it is always better to let others be the beta tester and to focus on tags that
we know can deliver good data.
(cid:23)(cid:17) (cid:37)(cid:68)(cid:85)(cid:85)(cid:76)(cid:72)(cid:85)(cid:86) (cid:87)(cid:82) (cid:38)(cid:82)(cid:80)(cid:83)(cid:72)(cid:87)(cid:76)(cid:87)(cid:76)(cid:82)(cid:81)
The market will continue to be monitored and surveyed for future purchases under this project to
identify emerging products that may improve our ability to collect high precision and accurate data
without compromising our ability to compare to prior years information.
(cid:24)(cid:17) (cid:38)(cid:82)(cid:81)(cid:87)(cid:85)(cid:68)(cid:70)(cid:87)(cid:82)(cid:85)(cid:10)(cid:86)(cid:52)(cid:88)(cid:68)(cid:79)(cid:76)(cid:73)(cid:76)(cid:70)(cid:68)(cid:87)(cid:76)(cid:82)(cid:81)(cid:86)
Ornitela is a specialized manufacturer of avian GPS/GSM telemetry systems, focused on solutions for
ornithological research and wildlife tracking. The core team combines experienced biologists with expertise in
bird tracking and skilled micro-electronics engineers, enabling them to tailor technical solutions specifically for
the needs of biological research. The company was established to address limitations seen in existing
tracking products — especially where flexibility, customization for moderate order sizes, and cost
competitiveness are needed. Their products are used around the world and trusted by hundreds of research
organizations in over 50 countries for biodiversity monitoring, migration studies, and ecological research.

Federal notice (Combined Synopsis/Solicitation), DEPT OF DEFENSE.DEPT OF THE NAVY.NSWC CRANE
Title: SOLE SOURCE � GREEN HILLS PROBE
Solicitation number: N0016426Q0130
PSC: 6625; NAICS: 334513
Description: Naval Surface Warfare Center (NSWC) Crane has a requirement for Green Hills Probes V4, Adapter and Annual Support. The proposed contract action is for the supplies or services for which the Government intends to solicit and negotiate with Green Hills Software, 30 West Sola Street, Santa Barbara, CA 93101. This is being sole sourced to meet form fit and function with existing systems, which are compliant with Navy information assurance compliance requirements. All responsible sources may submit a capability statement, which shall be considered by the agency. However, a determination by the Government not to compete with this proposed contract based upon responses to this solicitation is solely within the discretion of the Government. Information received will normally be considered solely for the purpose of determining whether to conduct competitive procurement. Contractors must be properly registered in the System for Award Management (SAM). Offerors may obtain information on SAM registration and annual confirmation requirements by calling 866-606-8220 or via the internet at https://sam.gov. This solicitation is being issued pursuant to Simplified Acquisition Procedures. Synopsis exception FAR 5.202(a)(13) applies and Solicitation Number N00164-26-Q-0130 is hereby issued as an attachment hereto. All changes to the requirement that occur prior to the closing date will be posted to Contract Opportunities on https://sam.gov/. It is the responsibility of interested vendors to monitor https://sam.gov/ for any amendments, which may be issued to this solicitation. For changes made after the closing date, only those offerors that provide a quote will be provided any changes/amendments and considered for future discussions and/or award. Offers shall be e-mailed to sandra.e.gunderman.civ@us.navy.mil. All required information must be received on or before 28-APR-2026 � 3:00 PM Eastern Time.

USE OF OTHER THAN FULL AND OPEN COMPETITION FOR AN ACQUISITION
UNDER THE SIMPLIFIED ACQUISITION THRESHOLD
I. BACKGROUND:
1. FAR 13.106-1(b)(1)(i) states for purchases not exceeding the simplified acquisition
threshold, Contracting Officers may solicit from one source if the Contracting Officer determines
that the circumstances of the contract action deem only one source reasonably available (e.g.,
urgency, exclusive licensing agreements, brand-name or industrial mobilization).
2. As required by FAR 13.106-3(b)(3)(i), this memorandum explains the absence of
competition for this acquisition, as only one source will be solicited for this requirement (or for a
portion of the requirement) and the requirement is not expected to exceed the simplified
acquisition threshold.

required source or brand name, and the required delivery date/period of performance.

COMPETITION IS BASED ON THE FOLLOWING (select all that apply):

rights in data, patent rights, copyrights or secret processes in the item or service required.
Explain what rights are restricted, why the restrictive rights make the required item or service
available from only one source, and why another company could not satisfy the Governments
need.

available from the Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM), or there is only one authorized
distributor or technical representative for the OEM.

available from the OEM.

evidence of the exclusive licensing agreement as an attachment to this document. NOTE: If there

impact if requirement is not solicited from only one source.

particular to one manufacturer.

multiple years, availabilities, and engineers, this is the only pump that meets our specific

Salient Characteristics: Cable, Special Purpose, Electrical Drawing: A3206001 PN: 17-1532

1. General
Product: Special Purpose Electrical Cable
Operating Temperature Range: -55°C to +80°C
Applicable Standards:
Dimensions and tolerances per ANSI Y14.5M-1982.
General properties must meet MIL-C-27500, with the exception of jacket wall thickness.
Packaging identification per MIL-STD-130.

2. Component Conductor Details
A. Type A Insulated Conductor (1 Twisted Pair with Shield)
Conductor: Silver-plated copper, 24 AWG.
Conductor Insulation: Extruded ETFE.
Insulation Colors: WHT-BLU.
Twisting: 4 twists per foot, minimum.
Shield: Tin-plated copper, 38 AWG, with 90% minimum coverage.
Distributed Capacitance: 30pF maximum per foot (wire-to-wire).
Characteristic Impedance: 77 ± 7 ohms nominal at 1MHz sinusoidal.
Attenuation: 1.5 dB maximum per 100 feet at 1MHz sinusoidal.

Conductor Insulation: Extruded ETFE.
Insulation Colors:
Pair 1: RED-BLK
Pair 2: YEL-VIO
Twisting: 5 twists per foot, minimum.
C. Type C Insulated Conductor (Single Conductor)
Conductor: Tin-plated copper, 20 AWG.
Conductor Insulation: Extruded ETFE.
Insulation Color: ORN (solid color) per MIL-STD-104.

3. Cable Construction
Filler: Thermoplastic rubber.
Isolator: Clear Mylar, 0.02" thick, 50% minimum overlap.
Overall Shield:
Material: Tin-plated copper braid, 36 AWG.
Coverage: 90% minimum.
Performance: Must meet a requirement of 500 milliohms per meter maximum at 100 MHz.
Separator: Clear Mylar, 0.02" thick, 50% minimum overlap.
Jacket:
Material: Extruded Polyurethane (TPU).
Color: Black, dull finish.
Wall Thickness: 1.00 mm minimum.
Nominal Outer Diameter: 9.7 mm.

4. Material Properties
The cable materials must withstand exposure to fuels, lubricants, solvents, and preservatives.
All materials used shall be non-hygroscopic.
Materials shall not contain nutrients that support fungal growth.
The jacket must be capable of being pushed back 3 inches without damage.

NIST Requirements Document
DCC Bridge, High Resistance bridge, Scanners
I. Background
The National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST), Physical Measurements
Laboratory (PML), Fundamental Electrical Measurement (FEM) group realizes and
maintains the unit of resistance, the Ohm, for the United States. Automated resistance
bridges are used to disseminate the ohm from primary quantum Hall resistance (QHR)
standards to standard resistors across over 20 decades of resistance with low uncertainty to
suppDort our QHR reseaRrch programs , meaAsurement se rviceFs, internatio nal cTomparisons with
other national metrology institutes (NMI), and our measurement services for standard
resistors, high current shunts, and graphene QHR device characterization.
II. Scope
In order to meet the mission indicated above, FEM requires instruments to maintain
functionality and the efficient automation of our resistance measurement services (SP-250
Test no. 51100S through 51141C) and graphene research activities, it has come time to add
several instruments to the direct current comparator resistance bridge systems that serve as
the workhorses for these tests over the range 10-4 Ω to 100 kΩ. Test currents up to 300 A may
be used in the range 10-4 Ω to10-1 Ω for high current resistors or shunts. Ancillary systems,
such as temperature controlled oil an air baths, environmental monitors, thermometers,
resistance scanners, equipment rack, NIST cables and wiring, IEEE 488 to GPIB adapters,
and customized data collection and processing software will remain as part of the system.
Bridge control software has been customized, tested, and used for many years to interface
with NIST Measurement Data Support System (MDSS). Automated control of temperature-
controlled oil and air baths by bridge control software is needed for automated determination
of alpha and beta temperature coefficients of resistors under test. The system of main bridges,
range extenders with reversing switchs, and linear dc power supplies will be augmented with
modern versions, compatible with instruments that remain in the measurement systems of
bridges.

graphene devices, 5 T and 9 T cryostats, NIST breakout boxes, NIST cables and wiring,
matrix scanners, oil baths, air baths) requires an additional direct current comparator bridge
and a binary voltage divider bridge, also compatible with our ancillary systems. A recent
software upgrade adds a feature to remove the built-in software filter (filter option of 0)
which introduced autocorrelations in the measurements. The current reversal algorithm was
modified to perform more suitable statistics to get more information on the time dependent
settling of the resistance standard under calibration. The individual points are accessible

STATEMENT OF WORK/REQUIREMENTS DOCUMENT
Title: Field Standard and Programmable Load Test Set for Accuracy Evaluation of Electric
Vehicle Supply Equipment (EVSE)
I. BACKGROUND INFORMATION
The National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) Office of Weights and Measures
(OWM) within the Physical Measurement Laboratory (PML) requires the purchase of test
equipment that can be used for testing the accuracy of Electric Vehicle Supply Equipment
(EVSE), also known as EV Charging Equipment. The test equipment must possess technical
specifications enabling accuracy evaluation of electric energy delivery, compatible with the
D R A F T
criteria as described in NIST Handbook 44 Specifications, Tolerance, and other Technical
Requirements for Weighing and Measuring Devices; Section 3.40. Electric Vehicle Fueling
Systems. The test equipment must be able to evaluate both alternating current (AC) and direct
current (DC) modes of operations, must include a programmable load emulator, and the
integrated system must be field-ready and easily transportable. A critical training need exists
within the US Weights and Measures system regarding EVSE testing and inspection. Weights
and Measures officials (metrologists, inspectors, and service agents) at the international,
federal, and state levels, along with industry, currently have little access to suitable training for
developing required skills to utilize this type of test equipment to make traceable accurate
measurements as part of testing an EV charging device.
Objective: The procured test equipment will be used in the development and implementation
of EVSE inspection and testing training programs. The targeted audience of the OWM-
developed training modules will be US federal, state, and local weights and measures officials.
International and industry weights and measures officials will benefit as well. These devices
will be integrated into a 5-day EVSE Metrology Course that addresses electricity basics,
electrical metrology concepts, NIST Handbook 44, and hands-on device training inspecting
and training AC and DC EVSE. The system purchased shall be the same system that is
currently being used by all of the weights and measures officials within the United States.
D R A F T
II. SCOPE
The Contractor shall deliver a quantity of one (1) Electric Vehicle Supply Equipment test
system (field standard and programmable load), inclusive of FOB Destination delivery,
warranty and training, compliant with the minimum technical requirements stated below.
III. MINIMUM REQUIREMENTS
The Contractor shall provide a system that meets all technical specifications identified below.
All items must be new. Used or remanufactured equipment will not be considered for award.
Experimental, prototype, or custom items will not be considered. The use of “gray market”
components are not authorized for sale in the U.S. by the Contractor is not acceptable. All line
items shall be shipped in the original manufacturer’s packaging and include all original
documentation and software, when applicable.
1
Line Item 0001: EVSE Field Standard
Description: Metrology field standard for measuring and evaluating energy delivery accuracy of
EVSE
Quantity: 1
A. Technical Specifications
a. The field standard will be capable of testing accuracy of energy delivery using a
transactional mode compatible with NIST OWM Handbook 44 provisions.
b. The field standard will test AC Level 1 and Level 2 EVSE up to 80 A maximum
current and DC fast charge EVSE up to 200 A at 1000 V DC.
c. SAE J1772 (CCS1) and SAE 3400 (Tesla) connectors shall be incorporated and
functional on device.
d. MeasDurement C apaRbilities A F T
i. Voltage
1. AC, up to 3 channels 60 VAC to 350 VAC
2. DC, one channel 60 to 1000 VDC
ii. Current
1. AC, up to 3 channels 0.2 to 80 A
2. DC, one channel 1.0 to 200 A
iii. Power: Active Energy, Reactive Energy, and Apparent Energy
e. Measurement Accuracy

matters.text:
Federal notice (Special Notice), DEPT OF DEFENSE.DEPT OF THE ARMY.W2R2 USA ENGR R & D CTR
Title: Notice of Intent to Sole Source- ElectroForce Apex 1
Solicitation number: W912HZ26N7446
PSC: 3990; NAICS: 334516
Description: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers Research and Development Center (ERDC), Geotechnical and Structures Laboratory (GSL) intends to issue a sole source award to TA Instruments � Waters, LLC. (CAGE Code: 0MJS5) to procure (1) ElectroForce Apex 1 in the areas of Concrete Materials Branch (CMB) research in an ongoing force protection research and development program and efforts on novel additives and polymer synthesis. The mechanical testing system with dynamic mechanical analysis capabilities to support material characterization and processing. This instrument will be used to understand polymeric and composite materials at various strains, frequencies, tensile, and compressive rates. The instrument should be able to characterize polymeric materials up to a peak force of 1,000 N, acceleration of up to 20 g, and have a displacement range and dynamic stroke of 100 mm. Additional requirements include: Tension/torsion grips that are rated to 350�C that can be used to 3000 N, Compression platens 100 mm diameter, and 3- and 4-point bend fixtures with adjustable lower span from 15 to 160 mm. This capability will help support ongoing research in material development. The ability to understand mechanical and viscoelastic properties are important to ensure reliable performance for polymers and building materials for applications ranging from force protection to infrastructure materials The instrument should use TRIOS software package as GSL-CMB researchers are well experience in using this data software for analysis and reporting. The software is used across different instruments and allows data to be leveraged seamlessly across instruments without having to redo comparative analysis across other software. Installation, training, and computer capable of running the software should be included. Instrument support should be through 24 months. The DMA application kit shall be compatible with WinTest. The unique characteristics detailed are critical to the continuation of the GSL�s mission and continued research in the Concrete Materials Branch (CMB). Since alternative methods of field-testing technique will not be deemed acceptable, it is determined that TA Instruments � Waters, LLC. (CAGE Code: 0MJS5) is the only vendor that can provide the ElectroForce Apex 1 that can meet the government�s exact specifications. Therefore, the Government intends to award a Firm-Fixed price contract to TA Instruments � Waters, LLC in accordance with FAR 13.106-1(b)(1)(i). TA Instruments � Waters, LLC is not a small business concern under the applicable NAICS code 334516 (Analytical Laboratory Instrument Manufacturing) with a size standard of 1000 employees. This notice of intent is for information purposes only. This notice is not a request for competitive quotes or proposals. A solicitation will not be issued. However, all responsible sources may submit a capability statement, proposal, or quotation, which shall be considered by the agency. The information submitted must be provided in sufficient detail to demonstrate the vendor�s ability to fulfill this requirement. The contractor must also provide a description of their past experience in fulfilling requirements which are the same or similar to this requirement and references for each. Information received will be considered solely for the purpose of determining whether to conduct a competitive procurement. A determination by the Government not to compete this requirement on a full and open competition basis, based upon responses to this notice, is solely within the discretion of the government. Oral communications are not acceptable in response to this notice. Responses to this requirement may be submitted to Tam Coronel at Tam.M.Coronel@usace.army.mil no later than 4:00PM CST Tuesday, 28 April 2026.

matters.text:
Federal notice (Presolicitation), DEPT OF DEFENSE.DEPT OF THE NAVY.NAVAL UNDERSEA WARFARE CENTER
Title: Notice of Intent to Award a Sole Source Contract and Sources Sought for FMS Vertical Deployment Tube (VDT) Technical and Tooling Package
Solicitation number: N0025326R9001
PSC: 1045; NAICS: 336611
Description: The Naval Undersea Warfare Center (NUWC) Division Keyport intends to award a firm-fixed-price/cost-plus-fixed-fee, sole-source contract to General Dynamics Electric Boat (GDEB) under the authority of 10 U.S.C. 3204(a)(1) as implemented by FAR 6.302-1, �Only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements.� This notice is published for market research purposes to determine if any other sources can satisfy the agency's needs. The Government's minimum needs are for the supplies necessary to prepare for the future manufacturing of VDT components. The required supplies consist of a comprehensive technical and tooling package based on the U.S. VIRGINIA Class program. The contractor shall develop all necessary tooling (fixtures, NDT calibration standards, dies, etc.) and deliver procurement-ready drawings for said tooling. The final supply package shall include a comprehensive list of the tooling with its life expectancy, a detailed cost and schedule for its production, and expected maintenance costs. Additionally, the contractor shall provide preliminary production documents including a manufacturing process plan, and test location and supplied size drawings for each unit. Finally, the contractor shall deliver a documented plan for testing of the units and a comprehensive production schedule for initial production. The basis for restricting competition is to utilize existing design and manufacturing process capabilities and expertise to reduce the need for prototyping units and associated qualification testing and accelerate the timeline for overall VDT component production by leveraging an existing vendor with a Production Readiness Level of 9. This established industrial relationship has resulted in a fully integrated team that is ready to execute this effort without unacceptable delays and substantial duplication of cost. In accordance with Department of Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Procedures, Guidance, and Information (PGI) 206.302-1, the Government is accepting information from companies potentially capable of meeting the requirements as described above. All interested parties must submit a response demonstrating their capability to meet these requirements. To be considered, a response must provide clear and convincing evidence of the contractor's ability to satisfy all the following requirements: Possess immediate, authorized access to the U.S. VIRGINIA Class submarine VPM proprietary design data, tooling manufacturing processes, and testing standards required to adapt this technology for applicable FMS Customer requirements. Demonstrate an existing, validated Production Readiness Level (PRL) of 9 for manufacturing large-scale, HY-80 submarine hull-integrated components. Guarantee the ability to meet an accelerated timeline of contract award by October 2026 and initial production unit delivery within 12 months thereafter, without requiring a multi-year development and qualification period that would result in substantial duplication of cost and unacceptable delays to the Government. A response that fails to provide a detailed and substantiated explanation for all three of these points will be considered non-responsive. Responses should include availability, budgetary cost estimate, and lead time of the solution and any other relevant information deemed necessary to expedite the decision-making process as well as company and product literature, a white paper no longer than 5 pages addressing the requirements above and shall identify other Government contracts with similar efforts for the Government(s) consideration. Responses to the Market Survey shall include the following: Submitter's Name Submitter�s CAGE/UEI Street Address, City, State, Zip Code Business Size Point of Contact (POC) POC Telephone Announcement Number Contractors must be properly registered in the Government System for Award Management database (SAM). Contractors may obtain information on SAM registration and annual confirmation by calling 1-866-606-8220 or via the internet at www.sam.gov. This RFI/sources sought does not constitute an Invitation for Bids (IFB), a Request for Quote (RFQ), or a Request for Proposal (RFP) and it should not be construed as a commitment of any kind by the Government to issue a formal solicitation or ultimately award a contract. The U.S. Government is in no way liable to pay for or reimburse any companies or entities that respond to this announcement. Any costs incurred by interested companies in response to this announcement will NOT be reimbursed. Information may be submitted to the Point of Contact any time prior to the expiration of this announcement. The Point of Contacts for this effort are Shelby Hallman, e-mail: shelby.n.hallman.civ@us.navy.mil, phone: (360) 315-0681 and Kimberly Hammit, e-mail: kimberly.s.hammit.civ@us.navy.mil, phone: (360) 315-3868. The mailing address is: Naval Undersea Warfare Center, Keyport Division, Attention: Shelby Hallman, Code 0252, Bldg 206L, 610 Dowell Street, Keyport, WA 98346-7610. Reference N0025326R9001 in the subject line of e-mails. Submissions in response to this RFI shall be submitted to the NUWC Keyport Contracting POCs by 13:00 Pacific Time 27 April 2026. Responses received after 27 April 2026 may not be considered in the Government�s research. All information marked as proprietary information will be safeguarded to prevent disclosures to non-government personnel and entities. Your interest in the Government�s requirements is appreciated. Reference number N0025326R9001 in all correspondence and communication.

PRE-SOLICITATION NON-COMPETITIVE – 
Notice of Intent to Sole Source

RESPONSE DATE: April 30, 2026 at 4:00 pm EST. 

PRIMARY POINT OF CONTACT:
Jaddua Johnston
jaddua.johnston@mail.nih.gov
Phone: 240-569-0006

INTRODUCTION:
THIS IS A PRE-SOLICITATION NON-COMPETITIVE (NOTICE OF INTENT) SYNOPSIS TO AWARD A CONTRACT WITHOUT PROVIDING FOR FULL OR OPEN COMPETITION (INCLUDING BRAND-NAME). 

The National Center for Advancing Translational Sciences (NCATS), National Institutes of Health (NIH), intends to award a firm-fixed-price contract for the acquisition of a Revvity (PerkinElmer) JANUS G3 automated liquid handling workstation.

NORTH AMERICAN INDUSTRY CLASSIFICATION SYSTEM (NAICS) CODE and SET ASIDE STATUS

NAICS code 621511 - Medical Laboratories @ $41,500,000. This acquisition is NOT set aside for small businesses.

REGULATORY AUTHORITY 

This acquisition will be conducted using FAR Part 12 – Acquisition of Commercial Items in conjunction with FAR Part 13 – Simplified Acquisition Procedures, as applicable. The resultant contract will include all appropriate provisions and clauses in effect through the current Federal Acquisition Circular (FAC)..

STATUTORY AUTHORITY

This acquisition is being conducted under the authority of:
FAR 6.302-1 – Only One Responsible Source and No Other Supplies or Services Will Satisfy Agency Requirements (41 U.S.C. 3304(a)(1))


DESCRIPTION OF REQUIREMENT:
PURPOSE AND OBJECTIVES:

NCATS requires the acquisition of a replacement Revvity (PerkinElmer) JANUS G3 automated liquid handling workstation to replace an existing first-generation JANUS instrument currently in use for approximately 17 years.
The system supports Compound Management operations responsible for preparing and distributing chemical compounds to NCATS researchers and collaborators. The replacement system must integrate seamlessly with existing laboratory infrastructure, automation workflows, and validated protocols.

Purchase Description: (Revvity (PerkinElmer) JANUS G3 automated liquid handler with 8-Tip dispenser and MDT dispenser
 
 
Salient characteristics 
The system must be compatible with existing JANUS accessories and WinPrep protocols currently used by NCATS Compound Management. The system.must include: 
• Revvity (PerkinElmer) JANUS G3 automated liquid handler • 8-Tip dispenser • Modular Dispense Technology (MDT) dispenser • 500 μL syringes • MDT heads: I30 384, I30RC 384, and I50 96 • (2) PlateStak diving boards with associated required accessories • System table • (2) Inheco MultiTEC controllers • (8) CPAC Ultraflat HT 4°C–70°C deck tiles • Microplate tilter • (2) MDT docking stations • Modern computer with required JANUS control software • 115V air compressor • MDT gripper VE assembly • Installation and system setup
 
 
Quantity: 1
 
 
Delivery Date: One-time delivery to NCATS, 9800 Medical Center Drive, Rockville, MD 20850, within 30 days after receipt of order.


PERIOD OF PERFORMANCE: Includes a 180-day parts and labor warranty beginning upon installation and system acceptance.


CONTRACTING WITHOUT PROVIDING FOR FULL OR OPEN COMPETITION (INCLUDING BRAND-NAME) DETERMINATION
The Government’s determination to award this requirement on a non-competitive basis is based on the unique technical requirements of the acquisition and the results of market research conducted in accordance with FAR Part 10.
The required system must be fully compatible with existing Revvity (PerkinElmer) JANUS platform components, including Modular Dispense Technology (MDT) hardware, integrated accessories, and WinPrep software protocols currently used by NCATS Compound Management. These systems are part of an established laboratory automation environment supporting ongoing research operations.
Use of an alternative liquid handling system from another manufacturer would require significant modification or replacement of existing equipment, redevelopment and revalidation of protocols, and retraining of personnel. This would result in substantial duplication of cost to the Government and unacceptable delays to mission-critical research activities.
Market research included a review of commercially available liquid handling systems, outreach to industry vendors, consultation with technical subject matter experts, and review of GSA Advantage, Dynamic Small Business Search, and prior Government acquisitions. While other liquid handling systems are available in the marketplace, none were identified that can meet the Government’s requirement for full compatibility with the existing JANUS-based infrastructure without significant additional cost and operational disruption.
The JANUS G3 system is proprietary to its manufacturer, Revvity, Inc., and must be procured through a vendor capable of providing the required configuration, components, installation, and integration support. Based on market research, Copia Scientific is the only vendor identified that can provide the required system configuration and associated support necessary to meet the Government’s requirements within the required timeframe.
Accordingly, this acquisition is justified under FAR 6.302-1.

STATEMENT OF WORK
Introduction/Background
Central Arkansas Veterans Healthcare System, Nursing Service, is requesting the brand name purchase of the Baxter/Hill-Rom Progressa + ICU Bed System to replace the non-functional/unrepairable beds in our facility.

The Progressa + ICU Bed has specific features to increase patient mobility and surfaces to decrease pressure ulcers that are common in ICU. Although it’s not many, data for CAVHS demonstrate that the ICU has HAPU (Hospital-Acquired Pressure Ulcers) and availability of this technology will support patient care, reduce costs and improve outcomes for the ICU patient, especially ventilator patients and post-surgical patients.

Objective
The Baxter/Hill-Rom Progressa + Bed is designed specifically for Intensive Care Units to increase patient mobility and surfaces to decrease pressure ulcers. It has a Stay-In-Place technology that addresses patient migration to the foot of the bed. This supports back strain to healthcare nurses caring for the patients.

USE OF OTHER THAN FULL AND OPEN COMPETITION FOR AN ACQUISITION

I. BACKGROUND:

acquisition threshold.

4.

Provide estimated shipping and delivery information for the requested supplies (e.g. Expected lead time on delivery). 

*If applicable, VAAR 852.212-71 Gray Market Items, will apply to the potential solicitation.* 

The Mass Spectrometers shall include all system hardware, software, filters, purging bottles, waste containers, uninterruptible power supply (UPS), a nitrogen generator, and any other components required to make the system fully operational upon installation. The contractor will also be required to install the equipment, provide training, and maintain the equipment for the length of the lease. This is a lease to own requirement. The Government will retain the title of the equipment at the end of the contract period.

The following describes the salient characteristics salient characteristics of the Liquid Chromatography Mass Spectrometry (LC/MS) systems.

Mass Analyzer and Performance Requirements.
Triple quadrupole mass spectrometer with a mass range of at least m/z 5–3000.
Capable of scan speeds ≥18,000 Da/sec to support fast chromatographic separations.
Mass resolution options including 0.4 Da, 0.7 Da, 1.2 Da, and 2.5 Da (FWHM) for flexible method development.
Mass accuracy within ±0.1 Da across the majority of operating mass range.
Mass stability with drift <0.1 Da over 24 hours.
Sensitivity and Quantitation Requirements.
Instrument detection limits in the low-femtogram range (<5 fg) for both positive and negative ionization modes.
Signal-to-noise ratios exceeding 850,000:1 for standard sensitivity verification compounds.
Linear dynamic range of at least six orders of magnitude for quantitation.
Ion Source and Ionization Flexibility.
Must support Electrospray Ionization (ESI) and Atmospheric Pressure Chemical Ionization (APCI).
Must offer multimode ionization that enables simultaneous ESI and APCI.
Must be compatible with low-flow nano spray ionization for increased sensitivity.
MRM Throughput and Acquisition Requirements.
Capable of ≥500 MRM transitions per second.
Minimum dwell times of 0.5 ms.
Support for Dynamic MRM (dMRM) and Triggered MRM (tMRM).
Ability to run >30,000 transitions per method.
Polarity and Collision Cell Performance.
Fast polarity switching <25 ms to allow multianalyte methods.
Collision cell clearance time <1 ms to prevent crosstalk in dense MRM methods.
Instrument Intelligence and Automated Maintenance.
Must include predictive maintenance tools such as Early Maintenance Feedback (EMF).
Must have built in autotune and check tune routines requiring no manual parameter adjustments.
Must include automation features such as iReflex that trigger reinjections or extended runs without user intervention.
Maintenance and Uptime Requirements.
System must offer VacShield or equivalent capability allowing ion source and front-end cleaning without breaking instrument vacuum, minimizing downtime.
Total downtime for routine source cleaning must not exceed 30–45 minutes.
Software and Data System Requirements.
Compatible with comprehensive LC/MS data acquisition and quantitation software.
Must support full scan, SIM, product ion scan, precursor ion scan, neutral loss scans, MRM, tMRM, dMRM, and mixed mode acquisition in a single method.
Software must support automated reporting, audit trails, and features compliant with regulated environments (such as 21 CFR Part 11).
Physical and Integration Requirements.
Instrument dimensions approximately 77 cm × 84 cm × 48 cm to fit existing laboratory space.

Delivery and Installation.
The instruments must be delivered and installed in a reasonable timeframe , but not to exceed ninety (90) days after receipt of the contract award. If unseen circumstances arise, the contractor will coordinate with the Government Point of Contact (POC).
Contractor shall install the instruments and all accessories at no additional cost to the Government. 

Instrument Services and Maintenance. The Contractor shall provide an extended warranty and/or service plan for the life of the contract. The plan shall include:
Telephone Support
On-Site hardware troubleshooting and repair
All labor, travel costs, and service parts, including consumables parts required for repair at no additional cost to the Government.

Training. The contractor shall provide the following:
Initial on-site operator training for instruments. 
Initial off-site operator training for two operators.
Applications and Method development assistance.
Handouts and training materials in sufficient quantity for each participant. These are off-the-shelf courses. The contractor shall provide lesson plan, course materials and media (DVD’s, CD’s, videos, etc. if required), and editable procedures at no additional cost.
Additional on-site training as requested by VANTXHCS at no additional charge.

In accordance with FAR 13.106-1(b)(1), “only one source [is] reasonably available” which
states that, “For purchases not exceeding the simplified acquisition threshold. (i)
Contracting officers may solicit from one source if the contracting officer determines that
the circumstances of the contract action deem only one source reasonably available
(e.g., urgency, exclusive licensing agreements, brand-name or industrial mobilization). (ii)

MEMORANDUM FOR 56TH CONTRACTING SQUADRON (56 CONS/PKB)
FROM: 56TH SECURITY FORCES SQUADRON (56 SFS/RA)
SUBJECT: Salient Characteristics for Man-Portable and Vehicle-Mounted RF Drone Detection
System
1. Purpose: This memorandum outlines the minimum essential salient characteristics for a
portable, multi-mission Radio Frequency (RF) based detection system for small
Unmanned Aircraft Systems (sUAS). This system is required to provide dismounted
security patrols and mobile vehicle patrols with immediate, localized drone detection and
alerting capabilities. The identified brand name product that meets these requirements is
theDroneShield RfPatrol™ Immediate Response Kit (NSN: 5865-66-025-4740). An "or
equal" system must meet or exceedall specifications listed below to be considered
technically acceptable.
2. Core System Functional Characteristics:
a. Detection Methodology: The system must be a completely passive, non-emitting
Software Defined Radio (SDR) based sensor. It must not transmit, jam, or
interfere with the RF spectrum.
b. Drone Identification: The system must detect and classify RF Command and
Control (C2) signals, custom protocols, Remote ID signals, and drone video
transmissions. The system's AI/ML engine must be capable of identifying over
150 common drone models.
c. Situational Awareness: Must provide real-time, on-device display of critical
information including, at a minimum, drone model, altitude, speed, and
communication frequency. Must also provide a "DroneLocator" feature to display
the drone and controller's GPS coordinates for compatible models.
d. Data Interface: The system must be capable of outputting detection data via
gRPC, JSON, and Cursor on Target (CoT) XML-based formats to enable
integration with third-party and government battle management systems (e.g.,
TAK software).
3. Handheld Detector (Primary Unit) Technical Specifications:
2
a. Performance:
*(1) Detection Time: Must provide initial detection and alerting inless than 5
seconds.
*(2) Frequency Coverage: Must monitor, at a minimum, the following frequency
ranges: 400MHz – 1004MHz, 1004MHz – 2400MHz, 2363MHz – 2517MHz, and
4800MHz – 6000MHz.
b. Physical and Environmental:
* (1) Weight: Total weight of the handheld unit, including attached battery, must
not exceed 1.2 kg (2.6 lbs).
* (2) Environmental Durability: Must be certified to meet, at a minimum,MIL-
STD-810G/H for operation in harsh environmental conditions (including high/low
temp, vibration, and shock).
* (3) Ingress Protection: The handheld unit must have an Ingress Protection (IP)
rating of IP67, certifying it as dust-tight and submersible in water.
c. Power and Battery:
*(1) Battery Type: Must utilize a rechargeable Lithium-Ion battery that is
compliant with NATO standards and is interchangeable with common military
radio batteries (e.g., PRC-152, PRC-163).
*(2) Operating Time: A single battery must provide a minimum of10 hours of
continuous, uninterrupted operation.
4. Vehicle Integration Kit Specifications:
a. Antenna System:
*(1) Mounting: The kit must include an external, wide-band antenna with
amagnetic mounting system for rapid, non-permanent vehicle attachment.
b. * (2) Frequency Support: The external antenna must support, at a minimum, the
following frequencies: 433MHz, 868MHz, 915MHz, 2.4GHz, 5.2GHz, and
5.8GHz.
5. Immediate Response Kit (Carrying Case and Accessories):
a. Complete Kit: The system must be delivered as a comprehensive "Immediate
Response Kit" housed in a rugged, IP67-rated hard-shell case with custom foam
inserts.
b. Required Accessories: The kit must include, at a minimum: one (1) Handheld
Detection Unit, two (2) NATO-standard rechargeable batteries, a battery pass-
through charger, one (1) Vehicle-Mount Magnetic Antenna Kit, one (1) MOLLE-

Description: COMBINED SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE AND NOTICE OF INTENT TO SOLE SOURCE Announcement Type: Special Notice Announcement Number: NIST-SSN-NOI-26-6800992 Subject: 1552.93 nm Laser System Applicable NAICS: 334513 - Instruments and Related Products Manufacturing for Measuring, Displaying, and Controlling Industrial Process Variables with size standard of 750 employees Applicable PSC: 6685 - Pressure, Temperature, and Humidity Measuring and Controlling Instruments Purpose This is a combined sources sought notice and notice of intent to sole source, not a request for a quotation. NIST is seeking information from sources that may be capable of providing a solution that will achieve the essential requirements included in the �Description� section below. If no alternate sources are identified, the Government intends to negotiate a firm-fixed price purchase order on a sole source basis with NKT Photonics, Inc. (UEI: WJNUYEZ9UT11) located at 23 Drydock Avenue, Boston, MA 02210. This action will be conducted under the authority of FAR RFO Part 12.102(a) and 41 USC 1901, allowing the Contracting Officer (CO) to solicit from one source. Delivery will be required within fifteen weeks after contractor receipt of order. Description The Contractor shall provide one laser system which meets the minimum requirements identified below. Design Wavelength: centered at 1550 nm Tunable range of at least 100 nm Maximum tuning step size 10 pm Stable single frequency operation Must be coupled to polarization maintaining fiber (FC/APC) with an output power (through the fiber) of at least 3 mW Linewidth < 1 kHz Relative Intensity Noise less than -150 dBc / Hz at 1 MHz Include power supply and all communication electronics Includes software control Background The National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) Sensor Science Division is investigating the use of the ruggedized optical-based pressure metrology using NIST-designed Fixed Length Optical Cavity (FLOC) technology. The purpose of this investigation is to provide air data calibration capability for US Air Force calibration laboratories. The FLOC measures pressure by measuring the change in the resonant frequency of an optical cavity that results from a change in the refractive index that occurs when gas is added. NIST owns and uses NKT Photonics Mikro lasers in the prototype system developed for this investigation. NIST intends to duplicate the prototype system so that both a control version and a version into which variables may be incorporated are available for further research efforts. Based on market research conducted between January 2026 and April 2026, including speaking with colleagues, performing internet searches, and speaking with vendors to determine what sources could meet NIST�s minimum requirements, only NKT Photonics, Inc. appears to be capable of meeting the Government's requirements; the NKT Photonics, Inc. lasers in the original prototype are proprietary to this contractor and NKT Photonics, Inc. does not authorize resellers of its equipment. How to Respond to this Notice Interested parties that believe they could satisfy the requirements listed above for NIST may clearly and unambiguously identify their capability to do so in writing by or before the response date for this notice. This is a combined sources sought notice and notice of intent to sole source is not a solicitation. Any questions regarding this notice must be submitted in writing via email to Ms. Lauren Roller, Contract Specialist, at Lauren.Roller@nist.gov. All responses to this notice of intent must be submitted via email to Lauren.Roller@nist.gov so that they are received no later than April 28, 2026 at 11:00 AM Eastern Time. B. 2 – DRAFT - Statement of Work
___________________________________________________

A. BACKGROUND

The Iowa City VA HCS is requesting a training system that is a high-fidelity virtual reality simulator designed to train and assess ophthalmic surgeons in phacoemulsification and cataract surgery techniques under realistic, repeatable conditions. The system consists of both software and hardware capable of simulating cataract and vitreoretinal surgical procedures.

All equipment provided must be Brand Name Only by Haag-Streit. It must be new; and which includes all the software, hardware, and any accessories required to be fully operational. This requirement is also requesting professional installation and clinical education and on-site training.

B. SALIENT CHARACTERISTICS 

Specifications – Brand Name Only

Must be capable of simulating both common and rare ocular procedures.
Must provide both visual and touch feedback to the surgeon.
Must be capable of providing video demonstrations for given procedures.
System must be mobile, allowing for relocation when necessary.
Must have stereoscopic 3D visualization with high-resolution binocular display.
Must have real-time rendering of anterior segment anatomy including cornea, iris, lens, capsule, and zonules.
Must have dynamic tissue behavior with deformation, tearing, and fluid interaction.
Must have realistic lighting, reflections, and shadows simulating an operating microscope.
Must have dual-handed haptic feedback for realistic force sensation.
Simulated resistance for corneal incision, capsulorhexis, lens manipulation, and nuclear fragmentation.
Must support cataract instruments including phaco handpiece, chopper, forceps, irrigation tips, and aspiration tips.
Cataract surgery simulation procedures must include clear corneal incision, viscoelastic injection, continuous curvilinear capsulorhexis, hydrodissection, hydrodelineation, phacoemulsification, cortex removal, and IOL implantation.
Must be capable of simulation of intraoperative complications including posterior capsule rupture, zonular dialysis, and iris prolapse.
Must have automated objective performance evaluation including instrument path length, applied force, time to completion, tissue damage, efficiency, safety scores.
Must track user progress over time.
Must have modular training structure from basic skills to advanced cases.
Must be capable of customizable difficulty levels.
Must have scenario repetition with consistent baseline conditions.
Must have proficiency benchmarks for each user.
Must have software-based updates to expand the procedure libraries.
Must have an integrated operating microscope simulator.
Must have ergonomic surgical headrest and instrument mounts.
Must have foot pedal input for phaco power and fluidics controls.
Warranty Requirements
Manufacturer must offer a (1) one-year minimum warranty that product is free from defects in materials and workmanship. All defects will be replaced or repaired by the manufacturer at no cost to the buyer.
Installation
Installation is TBD by the Contractor. Contractor shall contract the Point-of-Contact within ten (10) business days from issuance of award to schedule installation. 
Training
Clinical Education and On-Site Training is TBD. Contractor shall contact the Point-of-Contact within ten (10) business days from issuance of award to schedule the Clinical Education and On-Site Training.

C. PERIOD OF PERFORMANCE:

TBD


D. TYPE OF CONTRACT 

This is a Firm-Fixed-Priced, one-time supply contract with no option year(s). 

E. POINT-OF-CONTACT (POC)

This contract is assigned a POC and will provide general instructions for administrating the contract. The POC is not authorized to grant permission(s) to change the scope of the project. The POC that is assigned for this contract will ensure that the supplies/services provided by this company are received based on the contractual terms and conditions.

VA Fargo Health Care System

G. DELIVERABLES OR DELIVERY SCHEDULE

The vendor shall deliver the equipment via standard delivery with F.O.B. destination as scheduled. See Section C for delivery schedule period-of-performance. 

The equipment shall be delivered to the following address:

Iowa City VA Health Care System
601 Highway 6 West, 
Iowa City, IA 52246

Before performing any action in a non-contractual nature or is considered out-of-scope, the Contractor shall contact the Point of Contact (POC) and the Contract Officer identifying the reason(s) for change. All changes shall have prior authorization from a VA Contract Officer in the form of a written modification.

Contractors, contractor personnel, subcontractors and subcontractor personnel will be subject to the same federal laws, regulations, standards, VA directives and handbooks, as VA personnel regarding information and information system security and privacy.

The Government shall receive unlimited rights to data/intellectual property first produced and delivered in the performance of this contract or order (hereinafter “contract”) unless expressly stated otherwise in this contract. This includes all rights to source code and all documentation created in support thereof. MEMORANDUM FOR RECORD
SUBJECT: Justification for Other Than Full and Open Competition for an Acquisition
Under the Simplified Acquisition Threshold (SAT) Garden State Fireworks Pyro Gerbs
1. BACKGROUND: This memorandum is prepared in accordance with Revolutionary FAR
Overhaul (RFO) FAR 12.102 Restricting Competition, in support of a sole-source acquisition
as permitted under RFO FAR 12.102(a), as the Contracting Officer has determined that only
one source is reasonably available to satisfy the agency’s requirements.
This document explains the absence of competition for this acquisition, as only one
source, Garden State Fireworks, Inc., will be solicited for this requirement, which is
not expected to exceed the Simplified Acquisition Threshold.
2. DESCRIPTONS OF SUPPLY: 3,500 "Silver Droppy" Gerbs (Pyrotechnics) for nighttime
demonstrations. The effect is a 6" x 0.9" rolled paper tube that emits hundreds of silver
sparks for a duration of 28-32 seconds with an estimate value of . The requested
delivery date is 25 April 2026.
The Gerbs are used during nighttime aerial jumps by the USAPT "Golden Knights"
to provide clear visual cues for parachutists. This enables them to maintain
formation and situational awareness, which is critical for preventing mid-air collisions
and ensuring safe landings.
3. RATIONALE FOR SOLE-SOURCE PROCUREMENT:
a. Unique Capabilities, Safety, and Performance: The pyrotechnics manufactured by
Garden State Fireworks have demonstrated full compatibility with the parachutist
supplemental uniform, a critical safety and cost-efficiency feature. Competing products
evaluated previously have been shown to cause burn-through, which would necessitate
the frequent replacement of expensive safety equipment and introduce unacceptable
risk to personnel.
Controlled by: Army
Controlled by: MICC – Ft Knox
CUI Category: General Procurement and Acquisition
Distribution/Dissemination Control: FED ONLY
POC: Meagan S. Clavel, meagan.s.clavel.civ@army.mil

CUI//SP-PROCURE//FEDCON
CCMI-CSH-KX
SUBJECT: Justification for Other Than Full and Open Competition for an Acquisition
Under the Simplified Acquisition Threshold (SAT) Garden State Fireworks Pyro Gerbs
b. Enhanced Visibility: The burn rate of the GERBs produced by the vendor provides a
level of visibility during aerial nighttime jumps that is unmatched by any other product.
This allows for the formation of clearly identifiable configurations in the air, which directly
contributes to the safety of parachutists by providing clear visual references.
c. Proven Reliability: The Government has exclusively used this vendor's pyrotechnics for
the past eight years. This is a testament to the product's proven performance and
reliability in a high-risk operational environment. No alternative vendor is acceptable, as
competing products have failed to meet these critical performance requirements.
4. MARKET RESEARCH: Market research was conducted on 09 April 2026 to identify
all qualified sources. The research included querying Government databases (FPDS-
NG, GSA, UNICOR, AbilityOne, SBA), performing web-based searches (Google),
and reviewing the System for Award Management (SAM).
The results of the market research confirm that only Garden State Fireworks, Inc. can
meet the Government's unique and critical requirements. A search of the SBA
database under the relevant NAICS code (325998) identified over 2,400 small
businesses; however, a subsequent targeted search for vendors capable of providing
"gerbs" yielded zero results. Required sources under FAR Part 8 (AbilityOne, FPI,
GSA) were also screened and found to be unable to provide the required items.
Based on this research and a history of rigorous testing, Garden State Fireworks, Inc.
is the only source reasonably available to meet the Government's unique
requirement.
5. DETERMINATION OF FAIR AND REASONABLE PRICE: The Contracting Officer
has determined that the anticipated cost to the Government of will be fair
and reasonable. This determination will be based on a comparison of the proposed
price with prices found reasonable on previous purchases and historical contract
awards for the same item.
6. ACTIONS TO OVERCOME BARRIERS TO COMPETITION: The U.S. Army
Parachute Team and the U.S. Army Marketing and Engagement Brigade (MEB) will
continue to monitor the market for new firms that may be capable of meeting the
Government's requirements for future acquisitions.

Description: Notice of Intent to Sole Source HT941026N0037 THIS IS A NOTICE OF INTENT TO AWARD A SOLE SOURCE SUPPLY CONTRACT AND IS NOT A REQUEST FOR COMPETITIVE QUOTES. The Defense Health Agency Contracting Activity (DHACA), Healthcare Operation-West (HCO-W), intends to award a firm fixed price supply purchase for Phadia 250 System, analyzer supplies and reagents for use in the Laboratory Department at Tripler Army Medical Center, HI, in accordance with the Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 12.102-1, Simplified Procedures sole source acquisition FAR 12.102(b), restricting competition, only one source being available to meet the Government�s needs, to: Phadia US Inc. (Thermo Fisher Scientific) 4169 Commercial Ave Portage, MI 49002 The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for this requirement is 334516, Analytical Laboratory Instrument Manufacturing; the business size standard is 1,000 (in employees). The Product Service Code (PSC) is 6632 Analysis Instruments, Medical Laboratory Use. The objective of this sole source award is to procure Phadia 250 System Analyzer, supplies and reagents for Tripler Army Medical Center. ImmunoCAP assays are uniquely standardized and globally recognized for their analytical performance, reproducibility, and long-term consistency. ImmunoCAP provides scaled, reproducible results that closely mirror skin prick testing. The proprietary nature of ImmunoCAP assay design, calibration, and result standardization means that alternative systems cannot produce clinically equivalent or interchangeable results. As a result, no other supplies or services can reasonably satisfy the Government�s requirement to maintain consistent longitudinal patient data and validated diagnostic outcomes across time and locations. The Laboratory Department requires supplies, reagents, and maintenance for the Phadia Analyzer which can perform whole-allergen and allergen component testing. This breadth and depth of capability is not replicated by any other vendor and is essential to supporting the full spectrum of current and emerging clinical requirements relevant to the military health system. Limiting this capability would directly reduce diagnostic readiness and flexibility. This notice of intent is not a request for competitive proposals, and no solicitation document exists for this requirement. Sources interested in responding to this notice are required to submit a capability statement that includes management and technical data and cost information, in sufficient detail and with convincing evidence that clearly demonstrates the capability to provide the required customized implant for Naval Hospital Twentynine Palms. Capability statements shall not exceed six (8.5 x 11 inch) pages using a font size no smaller than 10-point. All capability statements received by the due date of this notice will be considered by the Government. A request for documentation or additional information or submissions that only ask questions will not be considered as an affirmative response. A determination by the Government not to compete based on responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. Information received will be considered solely for the purpose of determining whether to conduct a competitive procurement or to proceed with a sole source purchase order. If a vendor challenges the basis of this requirement, please email capability statements as a Microsoft Word or Adobe PDF attachment to Bobbie Dobberstein at bobbie.s.dobberstein.ctr@health.mil. The closing date for challenges is no later than 1000 Pacific Daylight Time, Wednesday, 25 April 2026. NO TELEPHONE REQUESTS/OFFERS WILL BE HONORED.

matters.text:
Federal notice (Presolicitation), DEPT OF DEFENSE.DEPT OF THE NAVY.NAVAL UNDERSEA WARFARE CENTER
Title: Notice of Intent to Award a Sole Source Contract and Sources Sought for SSN AUKUS Vertical Deployment Tube (VDT) Technical and Tooling Package
Solicitation number: N0025326R9001
PSC: 1045; NAICS: 336611
Description: The Naval Undersea Warfare Center (NUWC) Division Keyport intends to award a firm-fixed-price/cost-plus-fixed-fee, sole-source contract to General Dynamics Electric Boat (GDEB) under the authority of 10 U.S.C. 3204(a)(1) as implemented by FAR 6.302-1, �Only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements.� This notice is published for market research purposes to determine if any other sources can satisfy the agency's needs. The Government's minimum needs are for the supplies necessary to prepare for the future manufacturing of the SSN-A VDT ITH/ITK components. The required supplies consist of a comprehensive technical and tooling package based on the U.S. VIRGINIA Class program, adapted for the United Kingdom's VDT design. The contractor shall develop all necessary tooling (fixtures, NDT calibration standards, dies, etc.) and deliver procurement-ready drawings for said tooling. The final supply package shall include a comprehensive list of the tooling with its life expectancy, a detailed cost and schedule for its production, and expected maintenance costs. Additionally, the contractor shall provide preliminary production documents including a manufacturing process plan, and test location and supplied size drawings for each unit. Finally, the contractor shall deliver a documented plan for the prototype testing, NDT Ultrasonic Testing Scan and Magnetic Particle Test Procedures of the VDT units and a comprehensive production schedule for initial production of ITH/ITK units. The basis for restricting competition is to utilize existing design and manufacturing process capabilities and expertise to reduce the need for prototyping units and associated qualification testing and accelerate the timeline for overall VDT component production by leveraging an existing vendor with a Production Readiness Level of 9. This established industrial relationship has resulted in a fully integrated team that is ready to execute this effort without unacceptable delays and substantial duplication of cost. In accordance with Department of Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Procedures, Guidance, and Information (PGI) 206.302-1, the Government is accepting information from companies potentially capable of meeting the requirements as described above. All interested parties must submit a response demonstrating their capability to meet these requirements. To be considered, a response must provide clear and convincing evidence of the contractor's ability to satisfy all the following requirements: Possess immediate, authorized access to the U.S. VIRGINIA Class submarine VPM proprietary design data, tooling manufacturing processes, and testing standards required to adapt this technology for the SSN-A VDT. Demonstrate an existing, validated Production Readiness Level (PRL) of 9 for manufacturing large-scale, HY-80 submarine hull-integrated components. Guarantee the ability to meet an accelerated timeline of contract award by September 2026 and initial production unit delivery within 12 months thereafter, without requiring a multi-year development and qualification period that would result in substantial duplication of cost and unacceptable delays to the Government. A response that fails to provide a detailed and substantiated explanation for all three of these points will be considered non-responsive. Responses should include availability, budgetary cost estimate, and lead time of the solution and any other relevant information deemed necessary to expedite the decision-making process as well as company and product literature, a white paper no longer than 5 pages addressing the requirements above and shall identify other Government contracts with similar efforts for the Government(s) consideration. Responses to the Market Survey shall include the following: Submitter's Name Submitter�s CAGE/UEI Street Address, City, State, Zip Code Business Size Point of Contact (POC) POC Telephone Announcement Number Contractors must be properly registered in the Government System for Award Management database (SAM). Contractors may obtain information on SAM registration and annual confirmation by calling 1-866-606-8220 or via the internet at www.sam.gov. This RFI/sources sought does not constitute an Invitation for Bids (IFB), a Request for Quote (RFQ), or a Request for Proposal (RFP) and it should not be construed as a commitment of any kind by the Government to issue a formal solicitation or ultimately award a contract. The U.S. Government is in no way liable to pay for or reimburse any companies or entities that respond to this announcement. Any costs incurred by interested companies in response to this announcement will NOT be reimbursed. Information may be submitted to the Point of Contact any time prior to the expiration of this announcement. The Point of Contacts for this effort are Shelby Hallman, e-mail: shelby.n.hallman.civ@us.navy.mil and Kimberly Hammit, e-mail: kimberly.s.hammit.civ@us.navy.mil.
